design:
# Reconciled fix: make end-of-session opening-delta paths truly cache-only

Follow-on to g-fix-end-latency. After that change, `/api/game/end` still took
**9.95s** (server log: `opening_score_delta source=cached_stale compute_ms=9397.03`).
Two independent diagnoses (tmp/p1, tmp/p2) reached the same root cause; this bead
records the reconciliation and the final proposed fix.

## Status / builds on (read first)

g-fix-end-latency is ALREADY COMMITTED as `c5bcbed`
("fix(openings): non-blocking end-of-session delta + reconcile poll"). Its bead is
intentionally still OPEN because that commit did NOT resolve the latency — it set up the
reconcile-poll architecture but left the expensive O(evidence) freshness proof on both
request paths (see root cause below). THIS bead builds directly on top of the committed
`c5bcbed` code: keep its score-delta GET endpoint, route normalization, frontend poll
helper (`src/utils/openingDeltaPoll.ts`), and terminal-site wiring; the Phase 1 work
below revises the backend delta reader on top of them. Do not revert or re-do c5bcbed.

## Root cause (both diagnoses agree; confirmed against code + server.log)

- g-fix-end-latency already removed the synchronous `refresh_now` scheduler wait.
  That was NOT the dominant cost.
- The 9.4s is spent inside the supposedly non-blocking `_delta_items_from_cache`,
  which calls `proven_fresh_opening_scores()` -> `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint()`
  -> `raw_evidence_inputs_digest()` (backend/app/opening_evidence.py:646). That digest
  full-scans and hashes EVERY `session_moves` + `analysis_cache` row for the user. It
  is **O(evidence volume)** and at game-end contended with the in-flight 62-move final
  upload and the background recompute writing concurrently.
- The cost is paid on BOTH request paths, because `compute_opening_score_delta`
  (terminal POST) and `read_opening_score_delta` (poll GET) both route through
  `_delta_items_from_cache`. That is why the poll GETs ballooned in the log:
  2.3 -> 9.3 -> 17.6 -> 14.9 -> 12.3 -> 9.0 -> 5.7 -> 2.3s.
- Same root cause makes the start-path `snapshot_opening_baseline` cost 2.1s
  (`opening_baseline_snapshot source=cached_fresh snapshot_ms=2138.42`) — it calls the
  same fingerprint.

Original g-fix-end-latency premise ("serving the warm cached delta is a cheap read")
was wrong: **proving the cache is fresh is the expensive part, not building the items.**

## Reconciliation of tmp/p1 vs tmp/p2

- Terminal POST: p1-opt1 returns nothing (banner only from poll); p2-part1 returns the
  warm cached items via cheap `list_cached_opening_scores`, marked unverified. TAKE p2 —
  the cost was never building items, only proving freshness, so keep the instant banner.
- Poll GET: p1-opt2 worried that scheduler quiescence can falsely read "fresh". p2-part2
  RESOLVES this: use the scheduler signal only as a cheap NOT-fresh gate, and keep the
  fingerprint as the ONLY thing that can assert is_fresh=true. Cheap AND correct.
- Materialized cursor: p1-opt3 and p2-part3 are the same idea; both flag it largest/
  riskiest and p1 notes it overlaps another agent's in-flight evidence/position_analysis
  refactor. DEFER (Phase 2).

## Final proposed fix

### Phase 1 — make both request paths cheap (THIS bead)

Keep the reconcile-poll infrastructure shipped in c5bcbed (frontend
`src/utils/openingDeltaPoll.ts`, GET `/api/openings/score-delta/{session_id}`,
`OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse`) — both diagnoses agree it is correct and worth keeping.

1. Split cheap item-build from the expensive freshness proof. Refactor
   `_delta_items_from_cache` (backend/app/opening_score_delta.py) so the chain-walk +
   baseline-diff reads rows via `list_cached_opening_scores` (indexed batch+rows, no
   fingerprint). Factor the freshness predicate into `_is_batch_fresh(db, batch, rows)`
   (registry fp + raw-input fp + stale-branch check — the same three conditions
   `proven_fresh_opening_scores` uses today, opening_cache.py:380) so there is one
   source of truth.

2. Terminal POST (`compute_opening_score_delta`) NEVER proves freshness. Build items
   from `list_cached_opening_scores`, enqueue `request_recompute`, return. Log
   `source=cached_unverified` (plus `no_chain` / `skipped_cold`). Reconciled p1-opt1 +
   p2-part1: instant warm banner, zero fingerprint. Fixes the reported 9.95s outright.

3. Poll GET (`read_opening_score_delta`) runs the fingerprint at most once per poll
   session:
   - empty chain -> is_fresh=true (stop, unchanged)
   - no batch (cold) -> is_fresh=false (keep polling)
   - `is_recompute_scheduled(user, color)` true (pending/in-flight) -> is_fresh=false,
     CHEAP, skip the fingerprint  <-- this kills the 9-17s poll GETs
   - only when quiescent -> run `_is_batch_fresh` once to confirm and stop the poll
   The poll deliberately does NOT re-enqueue (avoids pushing the scheduler debounce).
   Convergence is still guaranteed: the `/moves` write path enqueues a recompute
   covering the final plies (backend/app/api/session.py:832) and the terminal POST
   enqueues one too.

Touch points: backend/app/opening_score_delta.py (helper split + both callers),
imports of `is_recompute_scheduled` / `list_cached_opening_scores`. The GET endpoint
(openings.py) and frontend poller are unchanged.

### Observability / tests (extends g-fix-end-latency's existing ask)

- Regression test: `/api/game/end` and `/api/drills/{id}/fail|natural-end` return 200
  with a warm banner while `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` /
  `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` is patched to FAIL IF CALLED (proves the terminal path no
  longer pays the digest), keeping the existing "fail if refresh_now called" assertion.
- Poll test: with a recompute scheduled, GET returns is_fresh=false WITHOUT calling the
  digest; once quiescent it calls the digest exactly once and returns is_fresh per the
  fingerprint verdict.
- Keep `source` + `compute_ms` logging so production api_request duration verifies the
  fix.

### Phase 2 — DEFERRED follow-up (p1-opt3 / p2-part3), separate bead

Materialized evidence-version cursor: bump a per-(user, color) version on evidence
writes, stamp the version the recompute covered onto the batch, make freshness an
indexed `covered_version == current_version` compare. Real long-term fix (also makes the
start-path 2.1s snapshot instant). NOT in this bead because it is the largest change,
needs schema work (model + alembic + conftest `_create_test_schema` per the
hand-written-SQLite-schema rule), and overlaps another agent's in-flight
evidence/position_analysis refactor. Note: `OpeningScoreCursor.latest_generation`
already exists but is a BATCH-generation counter, not an evidence-write version — this
needs a distinct column.

### Secondary — final upload (from tmp/p2 + g-end-delta-hotpath), separate concern

The 62-move final upload took ~9.3s server-side while the client timed out at 4s. It is
a masking issue, not the direct cause. Once the terminal POST is cache-only it stops
doing evidence work, so upload contention no longer inflates `/api/game/end`. The warm
banner at game-end may lag by the still-uploading final plies — exactly what the poll
reconciles, so acceptable. Two candidate fixes for the separate bead:

- (preferred, low-risk) Soft timeout instead of hard abort in
  `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd`: after 4s proceed to the terminal POST but do NOT
  abort the in-flight `/moves` request. Keep the upload promise alive; when it settles
  successfully, start/continue the reconcile poll for that session so a fast terminal
  POST never permanently misses evidence the server is still writing after the old
  client timeout. Frontend test: soft-timeout upload proceeds to endGame, does not abort
  uploadSessionMoves, and starts/continues the poll when the late upload settles.
- (larger) Make the final upload incremental so it never blocks for ~9s.
acceptance_criteria: /api/game/end and /api/drills/{id}/fail|natural-end return 200 in well under 1s with a warm banner; raw_evidence_inputs_digest is never called on the terminal POST path (regression test patches it to fail-if-called); poll GET returns is_fresh=false cheaply while a recompute is scheduled and calls the digest at most once when quiescent; reconcile-poll infra (frontend poller, GET endpoint) preserved.
close_reason: Made terminal POST + poll cache-only; dropped O(evidence) freshness proof from both paths

title: Make end opening delta truly non-blocking
description: Follow-on to g-fix-end-latency. The current implementation removed the old refresh_now wait, but production logs still show /api/game/end spending almost all of its time in opening_score_delta because the replacement path calls proven_fresh_opening_scores. Need keep evidence fingerprint work off terminal request paths and make reconcile polling cheap enough to avoid server-side pileups.
design:
Final proposed fix

Evidence
- backend/server.log shows opening_score_delta source=cached_stale compute_ms=9397.03 immediately before POST /api/game/end 200 9975.367ms. The delta helper consumed almost the full endpoint duration.
- The old scheduler wait was real, but it is no longer the active measured hot path. The current hot path is _delta_items_from_cache calling proven_fresh_opening_scores, which computes opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint over raw evidence and related analysis rows.
- The same problem repeats in the poll endpoint: GET /api/openings/score-delta calls read_opening_score_delta, which calls the same _delta_items_from_cache and can run 9s to 17s while recompute/upload work is active.
- The final full-history upload timed out client-side at roughly 4s, but the server kept processing it for 9.27s. A fast /api/game/end can therefore overlap a still-running /moves upload.

Decision
- Keep the existing reconcile-poll architecture from g-fix-end-latency, but correct the backend hot path. Terminal POSTs must never prove freshness. Polling must avoid repeated raw evidence fingerprints while recompute is pending or in flight.
- Do not rely on scheduler quiescence as a permanent freshness proof. It is a cheap active-work guard only. The durable freshness solution is a materialized evidence cursor/version stored with each opening-score batch.

Immediate implementation
1. Make compute_opening_score_delta truly cache-only.
   - Replace the proven_fresh_opening_scores call inside _delta_items_from_cache for terminal use with list_cached_opening_scores or a targeted latest-batch read for the played opening keys.
   - No refresh_now, no load_cached_rows, no proven_fresh_opening_scores, no opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint on terminal POSTs.
   - Warm cache: return best-effort items immediately with source cached_unverified or cached_warm_unverified.
   - Cold cache: return [] and source skipped_cold.
   - Always enqueue request_recompute after the cheap read so the cache converges for polling.
   - Log source, row/read timing, chain length, and compute_ms.

2. Split delta building from freshness proving.
   - Keep a private builder that accepts cached rows and builds OpeningScoreDeltaItem from the played chain and session opening_score_baseline.
   - Terminal path calls the cheap latest-batch reader only.
   - Poll path can reuse the builder but must decide freshness separately.

3. Make GET /api/openings/score-delta cheap while work is active.
   - Check is_recompute_scheduled(user_id, player_color) first.
   - If true, return latest cached items with is_fresh=false without running proven_fresh_opening_scores or the raw evidence fingerprint.
   - If false and there is no durable freshness cursor yet, either run the expensive proof only as a quiescent fallback or return is_fresh=false with bounded attempts on the frontend. Prefer adding the cursor in this bead if scope allows.

4. Fix the final-upload race.
   - Change uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd semantics from hard abort to soft timeout: after 4s, proceed to terminal POST, but do not abort the /moves request.
   - Keep the upload promise alive. When it settles successfully, ensure the reconcile poll is started or continued for that session.
   - This prevents a fast terminal POST from permanently missing evidence that the server is still writing after the old client timeout.

Durable freshness cursor option
- Add an opening evidence version/cursor per user_id/player_color, bumped by every write surface that can affect raw_evidence_inputs_digest: session_moves upserts, analysis cache/position analysis inputs that can satisfy fallback, blunders/ghost targets, and blunder reviews/SRS.
- Store covered_evidence_version on OpeningScoreBatch when recompute starts or when its matching raw input snapshot is captured.
- Poll freshness becomes indexed comparison: latest_batch.covered_evidence_version == current_evidence_version, plus registry fingerprint and branch-key checks.
- The worker can keep using raw_evidence_inputs_fingerprint as the correctness gate if desired, but request paths should not scan all raw evidence.

Tests
- Backend regression: patch app.opening_cache.opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint and app.opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now to raise; /api/game/end, /api/drills/{id}/fail, and natural-end still return 200 and terminal delta compute does not call either function.
- Backend unit: warm terminal delta returns items from cached rows and logs cached_unverified; cold terminal delta returns []; request_recompute called once.
- Backend poll: pending/in-flight scheduler returns is_fresh=false and does not call opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint; quiescent fresh path behaves as designed.
- Frontend: soft-timeout upload proceeds to endGame, does not abort uploadSessionMoves, and starts/continues poll when late upload settles. Existing poll helper tests should cover no stale write after sessionId changes.

Recommendation for current g-fix-end-latency change
- Do not commit it as complete in its current state. It still leaves the measured 9.95s server-side latency.
- Do not throw it away wholesale either. The useful parts are the new score-delta GET endpoint, route normalization, frontend poll helper, and terminal-site wiring. Keep those and revise the backend delta reader plus final-upload timeout behavior before committing.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal endpoints do not call refresh_now, proven_fresh_opening_scores, or opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint; /api/game/end returns without opening delta fingerprint work; poll GET avoids fingerprint work while recompute is scheduled; final upload timeout is soft rather than aborting server work; backend and frontend regression tests cover the behavior.

title: Fix ending latency
description:
Both /api/drills/<session_id>/fail and /api/game/end are taking more than five seconds after g-xanz. Investigate the regression, identify the slow path, and fix the endpoint completion latency.

Investigation findings (2026-06-26)

Observed regression surface:
- g-xanz (173f1b5) wired opening-score deltas into terminal response paths.
- /api/game/end calls compute_opening_score_delta after the game-end commit/refresh in app/api/game.py:791.
- /api/drills/{session_id}/fail calls compute_opening_score_delta in the response return path in app/api/drills.py:341. Drill natural-end also uses the same helper at app/api/drills.py:507.
- Abandon skips the helper; off-route route-check skips deltas and is not part of this latency issue.

Root cause:
- compute_opening_score_delta still performs a synchronous scheduler wait: app/opening_score_delta.py:167 calls opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now(session.user_id, player_color) with no timeout override.
- refresh_now defaults to timeout=5.0 and waits until a covering recompute finishes/quiesces or the deadline expires (app/opening_score_scheduler.py:143-178). When the opening-score worker is busy, stale, cold, or slow, the request blocks for the full 5s before continuing.
- The helper treats that recompute as best-effort. It ignores a False return and serves cached rows anyway; test_opening_score_delta.py::test_delta_serves_cached_when_final_refresh_fails already codifies that cached-after fallback is acceptable.
- There is a second possible blocking wait: compute_opening_score_delta then calls load_cached_rows (app/opening_score_delta.py:180). On a cold/no-batch cache, load_cached_rows calls refresh_now again with the same default 5s timeout (app/opening_cache.py:371-374). Warm users can pay one 5s wait; cold terminal paths can pay a second wait before returning.
- g-fix-start-latency (cff5b60) fixed only snapshot_opening_baseline on the start path by using proven_fresh_opening_scores and never touching the scheduler. It did not change the end delta helper, so the g-xanz end-path wait remains.

Secondary factor:
- g-xanz frontend terminal flows also added uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd with FINAL_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS=4000 before /api/game/end and /api/drills/{id}/fail. That can add user-perceived end time before the POST starts, but it does not explain server-side api_request duration for the terminal endpoints themselves.

Recommended fix direction:
- Make end-of-session opening-score delta non-blocking on the HTTP response path. Do not call refresh_now from compute_opening_score_delta, and do not call load_cached_rows in a way that can cold-block.
- Prefer a non-blocking read helper for the delta path: inspect/list the latest cached batch directly, optionally prove freshness with the same fingerprints as proven_fresh_opening_scores. If the cache cannot be proven fresh after the final move upload, return no opening_score_changes (or a conservative after-only result) instead of waiting.
- If a recompute should still happen, enqueue it with request_recompute as background work only. The banner delta is supplementary and should degrade rather than hold the terminal action hostage.
- Add endpoint-level regression coverage for /api/game/end and /api/drills/{session_id}/fail that patches app.opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now to fail the test if called, while still returning 200 and preserving the existing abandon/off-route skip behavior.
- Add/keep observability for delta source and timing (for example: cached_fresh, skipped_stale, skipped_cold, no_chain, failed plus compute_ms) so production api_request duration can verify the fix.
design:
# g-fix-end-latency — non-blocking end delta + reconcile poll

## Context

After g-xanz (173f1b5), the terminal endpoints `/api/game/end`, `/api/drills/{id}/fail`,
and `/api/drills/{id}/natural-end` take >5s. Root cause: `compute_opening_score_delta`
(`backend/app/opening_score_delta.py:145`) forces a synchronous `refresh_now(...)` (default
**5s** timeout, `opening_score_scheduler.py:143`) so the "after" scores reflect the just-played
session, then calls `load_cached_rows` which on a **cold** cache calls `refresh_now` *again*
(another 5s). Warm users pay up to 5s; cold users up to 10s. The wait exists only to freshen a
**supplementary** banner; it holds the whole terminal action hostage.

g-fix-start-latency (cff5b60) already fixed the *start* path the right way: it reads the latest
cached batch directly via `proven_fresh_opening_scores` (`opening_cache.py:380`) — a non-blocking
freshness verdict that never touches the scheduler.

**Chosen approach (user's design):** make the end path non-blocking by serving the **warm cached
delta immediately** (zero scheduler wait), enqueue a background recompute, and have the **frontend
poll a new GET endpoint** for the provably-fresh delta, updating the banner in place once it lands.
The banner appears instantly (possibly lagging by the final plies) and self-corrects within a few
seconds.

**Best-effort warm "after" (Finding 2 — corrected).** `opening_score` is a **0–100 mastery
score**, not a monotonic counter: the just-played plies are fresh evidence that can move a score in
**either direction** (a clean line nudges it up; a misplay or a newly-revealed gap nudges it down).
So a slightly-stale warm "after" can transiently **over- or under-state** the eventual fresh delta —
the earlier "can only under-report" framing was wrong. The correctness guarantee is *not*
directional; it is that **warm-stale is best-effort and is corrected by polling**: once the poll's
`is_fresh=true` lands, the banner is overwritten with the provably-fresh value, erasing any transient
over/under-statement. (The start fix keeps the baseline fresh-or-NULL, which prevents the baseline
from being a *second* source of staleness, but it does not make the "after" directional.)

The poll runs after **every** terminal set; the GET's `is_fresh` flag tells the frontend when to
stop — distinguishing "no opening crossed / already fresh" (stop after one GET) from "cold, batch
still building" (keep polling until the banner pops in).

## Backend changes

### 1. `backend/app/opening_score_delta.py` — non-blocking helper + a poll reader

Factor the chain-walk + baseline-diff into a private core; **keep `compute_opening_score_delta`'s
`-> list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem]` signature unchanged** so the three POST call sites and the existing
list-asserting unit tests are untouched.

- **`_delta_items_from_cache(db, session) -> tuple[list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem], bool, str]`** (private, no scheduler)
  - Walk the chain via `played_opening_chain(_session_played_fens(db, session.id), get_opening_roots())`. Empty chain → `([], True, "no_chain")` (**`is_fresh=True` so the poll stops — nothing will ever appear**).
  - `batch, rows, is_fresh = proven_fresh_opening_scores(db, session.user_id, session.player_color)`.
  - `batch is None` (cold) → `([], False, "skipped_cold")` (**`is_fresh=False` so the poll keeps going until a batch builds**; no all-`None` banner meanwhile).
  - Else build items as today (current lines 192–219: baseline parse, before/after/delta/is_new) from `rows` keyed by `opening_key`. Return `(items, is_fresh, "cached_fresh" | "cached_stale")`. **Items are returned for any warm batch regardless of `is_fresh`** — `is_fresh` only drives the poll-stop signal, never gates the items.
- **`compute_opening_score_delta(db, session) -> list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem]`** (POST / immediate) — same signature, now:
  - call `_delta_items_from_cache`; **enqueue background** `request_recompute(session.user_id, session.player_color)` (lazy import from `app.opening_score_scheduler`, mirroring today's lazy import) so the cache converges (cold builds first batch, stale refreshes) for the poll. **Never** call `refresh_now`; **drop** the `load_cached_rows` import/use.
  - keep the outer try/except (never raises → `[]`). Log `source` + `compute_ms` in the **message string** (root formatter prints `%(message)s` only — same pattern as `snapshot_opening_baseline:124`). Return the items.
- **`read_opening_score_delta(db, session) -> tuple[list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem], bool]`** (new, GET poll) — call `_delta_items_from_cache`, return `(items, is_fresh)`. **No enqueue, no scheduler** (re-enqueuing each poll would push the 1.5s `quiet_window` debounce forward and *delay* convergence). Best-effort: exception → `([], False)`.

### 2. `backend/app/api/openings.py` — new poll endpoint (router prefix `/api/openings`, `:53`)

```python
class OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse(BaseModel):
    opening_score_changes: list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem] | None = None
    is_fresh: bool

@router.get("/score-delta/{session_id}", response_model=OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse)
def get_opening_score_delta(session_id: uuid.UUID, db=Depends(get_db), user=Depends(get_current_user)):
    session = db.query(GameSession).filter(GameSession.id == session_id).first()
    if session is None: raise HTTPException(404, "Session not found")
    if session.user_id != user.user_id: raise HTTPException(403, "Not authorized")
    items, is_fresh = read_opening_score_delta(db, session)
    return OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse(opening_score_changes=items or None, is_fresh=is_fresh)
```

One shared endpoint serves **both** game and drill sessions (both are `GameSession`; same
`player_color` / `opening_score_baseline`). Mounting on the openings router sits it next to the
existing non-blocking `GET /api/openings/tree/status` poll (`openings.py:1363`) and reuses its
`get_current_user` auth. Inline ownership check mirrors `game.py:684`.

### 3. POST call sites — no change

`game.py:791`, `drills.py:341`, `drills.py:507` keep calling `compute_opening_score_delta(...)`
(now non-blocking). Abandon-skip (`game.py:793`) and off-route route-check skip untouched.

## Frontend changes

### 4. `src/utils/api.ts` — client fn + type + route normalization (Finding 3)

`OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse { opening_score_changes: OpeningScoreDeltaItem[] | null; is_fresh: boolean }`
and `getOpeningScoreDelta(sessionId, { signal })` → `GET /api/openings/score-delta/{sessionId}`,
copying `getOpeningTreeStatus` (`api.ts:1449`) verbatim (`requestJson` + `getAuthHeaders`).

**Route normalization (Finding 3).** `normalizeApiPath` (`api.ts:93`) maps known dynamic routes to
their **exact** backend template via `API_ROUTE_TEMPLATES` (`api.ts:75`); anything unrecognized
falls through to the generic `{id}` rule. Add the new route so the poll GET's
`api_request_client.route` joins the server `api_request.route` in the latency dashboard instead of
being mislabeled `/api/openings/score-delta/{id}`:

```ts
[new RegExp(`^/api/openings/score-delta/${UUID_SOURCE}$`, 'i'), '/api/openings/score-delta/{session_id}'],
```

### 5. `src/utils/openingDeltaPoll.ts` — shared reconcile-poll helper

New small module (imported by both lifecycle hook and ChessGame, since the terminal sets live in
both). Bounded loop, **per-request `AbortSignal.timeout`** so a hung GET can't stall it (the app
already uses `AbortSignal.timeout`, e.g. `useChessGameLifecycle.ts:230`):

```ts
const DELTA_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 1500;        // ≈ scheduler quiet_window
const DELTA_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 15;         // ≈ 22s ceiling
const DELTA_POLL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 4000;
export async function pollFreshOpeningDelta(sessionId: string) {
  for (let i = 0; i < DELTA_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS; i++) {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, DELTA_POLL_INTERVAL_MS));
    if (useGameStore.getState().sessionId !== sessionId) return;            // superseded by new game
    let res;
    try { res = await getOpeningScoreDelta(sessionId, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(DELTA_POLL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS) }); }
    catch { continue; }                                                     // timeout/transient → retry
    if (useGameStore.getState().sessionId !== sessionId) return;
    if (res.is_fresh) { useGameStore.getState().setOpeningScoreChanges(res.opening_score_changes ?? null); return; }
  }
}
```

Cancellation reuses the existing `getState().sessionId !== <ended id>` guard the terminal handlers
already use — starting a new game flips `sessionId` (and resets `openingScoreChanges` → null at
`useChessGameLifecycle.ts:567/709`, `ChessGame.tsx:655`), so a late poll bails and can't repopulate
a stale banner. The bounded loop + per-request timeout bound total work even if the user lingers.

### 6. Fire the poll at **all five** terminal set sites (unconditional — Finding 1)

After each existing `setOpeningScoreChanges(<terminal response>...)`, add `void pollFreshOpeningDelta(<that site's session id>)`:

| Site | Path | Session id |
|---|---|---|
| `useChessGameLifecycle.ts:299` | drill natural-end | `finalizingSessionId` |
| `useChessGameLifecycle.ts:343` | game end | `finalizingSessionId` |
| `useChessGameLifecycle.ts:453` | revert→resign continuation | `store.sessionId!` (the id passed to `endGame` at `:438`) |
| `useChessGameLifecycle.ts:889` | resign | `finalizingSessionId` |
| `ChessGame.tsx:1130` | drill accuracy fail (`/api/drills/{id}/fail`) | `sessionId` param |

Polling is unconditional (not gated on a non-null immediate value), so cold users who crossed an
opening still get the banner once the batch builds; the GET's `is_fresh` stops it after one request
when there's no chain or the cache is already fresh. The existing `setOpeningScoreChanges` setter
(`useGameStore.ts:213`) drives `GameOpeningLineage.tsx` — no rendering changes; the value updates.

## Tests

**`backend/test_opening_score_delta.py`:**
- Update the autouse `_stub_scheduler` (`:37`) comment — the end path no longer calls `refresh_now`; keep the `request_recompute` stub (now load-bearing — the immediate compute enqueues it).
- Replace `test_delta_serves_cached_when_final_refresh_fails` (`:295`, premise gone) with `test_delta_does_not_call_refresh_now` (patch `refresh_now` as `Mock`, assert **not called**, warm delta still returned).
- Add: `test_delta_enqueues_background_recompute` (request_recompute called once); `test_delta_empty_when_cold_no_batch`; `test_delta_logs_source_and_compute_ms` (caplog, mirrors `:251`).
- Existing list-asserting delta tests (`:379`–`:479`) keep passing — `compute_opening_score_delta` still returns the items list from the same seeded warm batch (now via `proven_fresh_opening_scores`, which reads the same `list_cached_opening_scores` path; `is_fresh` doesn't gate items).
- `read_opening_score_delta` units: fresh→`(items, True)`, stale→`(items, False)`, **cold→`([], False)`**, **no-chain→`([], True)`**, and **never touches the scheduler** (`refresh_now` + `request_recompute` as `Mock`, assert not called).
- **Endpoint regression (bead-requested):** patch `app.opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now` with `side_effect=AssertionError(...)`; assert `/api/game/end`, `/api/drills/{id}/fail`, `/api/drills/{id}/natural-end` return **200** and never call it. Keep `test_game_end_abandon_skips...` (`:738`) + off-route skip tests green.
- New GET endpoint tests: 200 with `is_fresh` true/false shapes; 404 (unknown id), 403 (wrong owner); non-blocking (no `refresh_now`).

No new DB tables → no schema/conftest changes.

**Frontend — three suites touched. Existing terminal-path suites must mock the new poll helper (Finding 1):**

The poll fires from terminal paths that two existing suites already exercise, and both mock
`../utils/api` in incompatible ways for the new `getOpeningScoreDelta` import:
- `useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts:21` **fully replaces** `../utils/api` (no `importOriginal`), so it
  does **not** export `getOpeningScoreDelta` — letting the real `pollFreshOpeningDelta` run would
  call an `undefined` helper (TypeError) and spin real timers.
- `ChessGame.test.tsx:38` spreads `importOriginal` over `../utils/api`, so the **real**
  `getOpeningScoreDelta` would fire a live network GET in those tests.

Fix in both suites: **`vi.mock("../utils/openingDeltaPoll", () => ({ pollFreshOpeningDelta: pollFreshOpeningDeltaMock }))`** so the helper is a spy (no timers, no network), then **assert the poll fires with the correct session id at every terminal site:**
- `useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts` — assert `pollFreshOpeningDeltaMock` called with the finalizing
  id at the **four** lifecycle sites: drill natural-end (`finalizingSessionId`), game end
  (`finalizingSessionId`), revert→resign continuation (`store.sessionId`), resign
  (`finalizingSessionId`). `beforeEach` clears the mock.
- `ChessGame.test.tsx` — assert `pollFreshOpeningDeltaMock` called with the `sessionId` param at the
  drill accuracy-fail site (`ChessGame.tsx:1130`).

**`src/utils/openingDeltaPoll.test.ts`** (new — exercises the *real* helper, mocking
`getOpeningScoreDelta` from `../utils/api` + **fake timers** via `vi.useFakeTimers`, mirroring
`useGameStore.test.ts` store patterns):
- stops on first `is_fresh=true` and writes `opening_score_changes` to the store;
- keeps polling while `is_fresh=false`, then applies the fresh value once it flips;
- **stale-then-fresh reconcile (Finding 2):** seed the store with an immediate warm/stale
  `openingScoreChanges`, drive the poll to return a *different* fresh value, assert the store ends on
  the **fresh** value (transient over/under-statement is overwritten — proves "corrected by
  polling");
- bails when `sessionId` changes mid-poll (no stale write);
- respects the `DELTA_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS` ceiling;
- a timed-out GET (`AbortSignal.timeout`) is caught and retried, not fatal.

**`src/utils/api.timing.test.ts`** (Finding 3): add a `normalizeApiPath` case in the existing
`describe('normalizeApiPath')` block (`:79`):
`normalizeApiPath(\`/api/openings/score-delta/${uuid}\`)` → `'/api/openings/score-delta/{session_id}'`
(and confirm a static sibling / unknown UUID still falls back to `{id}`).

## Verification

1. `cd backend && pytest test_opening_score_delta.py -q` (rerun named file in isolation — pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load).
2. Manual: start a game, play an opening, end it — banner shows immediately (no multi-second hang) and the delta updates in place within a few seconds. Repeat for drill accuracy-fail, drill natural-end, and resign.
3. Server logs: terminal-route `duration_ms` (HTTPLoggingMiddleware) back under the regression threshold; `opening_score_delta source=cached_stale|cached_fresh|skipped_cold compute_ms=…` confirms the path.
4. Frontend, **non-watch** (Finding 4 — `npm run test` maps to `vitest` *watch* mode at `package.json:14`): run `npm run test:run` (or targeted `npx vitest run src/utils/openingDeltaPoll.test.ts src/utils/api.timing.test.ts src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx`). Then `tsc -b && vite build` (pre-push gate runs the whole tree — `tsc -b` is stricter than `--noEmit`).
notes:
Implemented (2026-06-27), pending review — NOT committed.

Backend:
- opening_score_delta.py: factored _delta_items_from_cache (private, no scheduler); compute_opening_score_delta now serves the warm cached delta immediately, enqueues background request_recompute, logs source+compute_ms; dropped refresh_now + load_cached_rows. Added read_opening_score_delta (poll reader, no enqueue/scheduler).
- api/openings.py: new GET /api/openings/score-delta/{session_id} (OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse) with inline 404/403 ownership; shared by game+drill sessions.
- POST call sites unchanged.

Frontend:
- utils/api.ts: getOpeningScoreDelta + OpeningScoreDeltaPollResponse type + route-normalization template.
- utils/openingDeltaPoll.ts: pollFreshOpeningDelta (bounded loop, 1.5s interval, 15 attempts, per-request AbortSignal.timeout, sessionId guard).
- Wired void pollFreshOpeningDelta at all 5 terminal sites (4 in useChessGameLifecycle, 1 in ChessGame drill accuracy-fail).

Tests (all green):
- backend test_opening_score_delta.py: 43 passed (new compute/read units, endpoint non-block regressions, GET endpoint 200/404/403/non-blocking).
- frontend: openingDeltaPoll.test.ts (6), api.timing.test.ts (+2), useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts (4 poll assertions), ChessGame.test.tsx (1 poll assertion) — 160 passed across the 4 suites.
- tsc -b && vite build pass. Backend related suites: 180 + 103 passed.
close_reason: Verified implemented: c5bcbed added non-blocking terminal delta + poll, 1908236 removed residual hot-path freshness digest via g-xmhv; targeted backend/frontend tests and npm run build pass.

title: Fix game/drill start latency from opening baseline refresh
description:
## Problem
Since g-xanz, POST /api/game/start and POST /api/drills/start can take over 6 seconds, causing visible delay before a game or drill begins.

## Root Cause
g-xanz added per-session opening score baselines at session creation. Both start endpoints now synchronously snapshot opening scores before inserting the GameSession:
- app/api/game.py:631 calls snapshot_opening_baseline before creating the normal session.
- app/api/drills.py:266 calls snapshot_opening_baseline before creating the drill session.
- app/opening_score_delta.py:56 snapshot_opening_baseline calls refresh_now(user_id, player_color) before reading cached scores.
- app/opening_score_scheduler.py:143 refresh_now blocks until the single opening-score scheduler reaches quiescence, bounded by the default 5.0 second timeout.

When the scheduler has changed inputs, queued work, or a recompute that cannot finish within 5 seconds, start waits out that timeout. The endpoint then continues with opening_score_baseline = NULL. That matches the observed >6s delay: 5s refresh_now budget plus normal request overhead.

## Production Evidence
Investigated against Railway DB postgresql://postgres:***@nozomi.proxy.rlwy.net:23621/railway on 2026-06-26. The schema includes game_sessions.opening_score_baseline.

Since 2026-06-25 00:00 UTC for user_id=14:
- black: 38 starts, 1 baselined, 37 skipped/null baseline, 97.4% skipped.
- white: 22 starts, 1 baselined, 21 skipped/null baseline, 95.5% skipped.

A null baseline in this code path means snapshot_opening_baseline returned None, most commonly because refresh_now returned False after timeout/failure/shutdown.

Evidence volume for user_id=14 is large:
- black: 47,206 session_moves with fen_before across 1,599 sessions.
- white: 49,274 session_moves with fen_before across 1,252 sessions.

Latest retained opening batches for user_id=14:
- black generation 17220 at 2026-06-26 04:47:59 UTC: 355 opening rows, 8,321 position rows, 8,323 edge rows.
- white generation 16104 at 2026-06-26 05:40:02 UTC: 77 opening rows, 7,914 position rows, 7,990 edge rows.

DB read latency does not explain the 6s delay:
- EXPLAIN ANALYZE for the raw session row query was ~24ms for black and ~30ms for white.
- pg_stat_activity/pg_locks showed no relevant DB lock waits during investigation.

## Impact
Every new game and drill start now depends on opening-score scheduler freshness. Heavy users or stale/changing evidence pay a blocking 5s wait even though opening-score deltas are supplementary UI. This makes starting play feel broken and also usually fails to capture the baseline anyway.

## Constraints
No code changes were made during investigation. Preserve g-xanz's end-of-session delta behavior where practical, but game/drill start latency must take priority over optional opening-score delta precision.

## Proposed Fix

Remove the synchronous `refresh_now` from the session-start hot path. Start
endpoints must create sessions immediately and treat opening-score baseline
capture as a non-blocking, best-effort read. Crucially, do this WITHOUT
re-introducing the misattribution g-xanz's refresh-before-read was designed to
prevent — use the scheduler's existing non-blocking freshness probe instead of
serving whatever happens to be cached.

### Why "just read the stale cache" is not safe

The naive fix (snapshot the latest cached rows even if stale) trades a latency
bug for a silent correctness bug, and it bites the exact heavy users this issue
targets:

- A heavy user's PREVIOUS session-end `refresh_now` (in
  `compute_opening_score_delta`) also times out, leaving pending evidence
  un-recomputed.
- So at the NEXT start the cached batch genuinely IS stale.
- The end-of-session delta then diffs that stale `before` against a fresh
  `after` and over-attributes prior sessions' gains to the just-ended one.

For light users the cache is usually fresh (their prior end-refresh landed), so
they rarely hit this — it is specifically the heavy-user path where "use
whatever's cached" is wrong. Rejecting the blocking wait does not, by itself,
make the cached fallback correct.

### Middle path: probe freshness, never block

The scheduler already exposes `is_recompute_scheduled(user_id, player_color)`
(facade in `opening_score_scheduler.py`, backed by
`OpeningScoreScheduler.is_scheduled`) — a non-mutating, non-blocking probe built
for cheap freshness checks (it backs `/api/openings/tree/status`). It returns
True iff a recompute for the key is pending OR in-flight. Use it:

1. Add a helper such as `snapshot_opening_baseline_cached(db, user_id, player_color)`:
   - Read the latest batch via `list_cached_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)`
     directly. This function (opening_cache.py:322) does NOT touch the scheduler
     at all — no `refresh_now`, no `request_recompute`, no enqueue, no wait.
   - Call `is_recompute_scheduled(user_id, player_color)` (non-blocking).
   - If a recompute is pending/in-flight → the cached batch may be stale →
     return None (baseline NULL → end delta omitted). Do NOT persist a
     possibly-misattributing baseline.
   - Else (cache is current) → return `json.dumps({row.opening_key: row.opening_score ...})`,
     i.e. a confident baseline, or `"{}"` when the user has no batch yet (valid
     empty baseline; first openings later read as new).
   - Never call `refresh_now`. Never enqueue. Never block. Keep the existing
     best-effort try/except + `db.rollback()` guard so a read failure degrades to
     None rather than poisoning the caller's session-create transaction.

2. Point both start endpoints at the new helper:
   - `app/api/game.py:634` (start_game)
   - `app/api/drills.py:268` (start_drill)
   Leave the rest of each handler unchanged.

This is strictly better than both the "pragmatic" (always-stale) and "strict"
(blocking-freshness) options originally sketched: light users get a confident
baseline (better coverage than today's ~95% NULL), heavy users with stale caches
get NULL instead of a misattributed delta, and nobody blocks on the scheduler.
The strict option was only rejected because it implied a blocking wait — the
`is_recompute_scheduled` probe gives the freshness signal without one.

Note the probe has a benign race: a recompute could be enqueued the instant after
the probe returns False, or finish the instant after it returns True. That is
acceptable here — the baseline is supplementary and the window is sub-second; the
probe's job is to catch the common, durable stale state (a heavy user's
timed-out prior refresh leaving work parked), not to be transactionally exact.

### Keep end-of-session recompute separate (out of scope, same root cause)

`compute_opening_score_delta` (opening_score_delta.py:125) still uses best-effort
`refresh_now` and stays as-is: it runs AFTER play and powers the banner, and on
timeout/False it already serves the cached/partial delta. Note this means the
game/drill END endpoints (`game.py:794`, `drills.py:341`, `drills.py:507`) still
expose heavy users to the same up-to-5s `refresh_now` wait — the team already
side-steps it for ABANDON (`game.py:790`). That is the same root cause as this
bug but is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE here; file a follow-up if game-end latency
also proves painful.

### On the original "double blocking" concern (downgraded)

The originally-flagged double-blocking (`snapshot_opening_baseline` → `refresh_now`,
then `load_cached_rows` → `refresh_now` again on cold cache) is real but minor: the
second `refresh_now` only fires on a cold/no-batch cache, where it is fast. Routing
the start path through `list_cached_opening_scores` (which never touches the
scheduler) moots it entirely, so no special handling is needed beyond using that
function instead of `load_cached_rows`.

### Observability — land WITH the fix, not "optional"

The latency attribution in this investigation is strong but circumstantial (5s
timeout matching the >6s delay, ~95% NULL baselines, fast DB reads); no direct
timing was captured. Ship a cheap timing/source log alongside the fix so the
before/after is provable rather than inferred:

- Log start-endpoint duration separately from any opening recompute duration.
- Emit a baseline-source property: `cached_fresh`, `skipped_stale` (probe said
  pending/in-flight), `empty_batch`, or `failed`. This makes a future regression
  (or a surprising stale-rate) obvious and confirms the fix landed.

## Expected Outcome

POST /api/game/start and POST /api/drills/start return without waiting on the
opening-score scheduler. The start-latency regression disappears. Baseline
coverage improves for the common (fresh-cache) case while heavy/stale-cache users
get a NULL baseline (delta omitted) instead of a misattributed delta — graceful
degradation, not a new correctness bug.
design:
# Plan: g-fix-start-latency — non-blocking, freshness-proven opening baseline at session start

## Context

Since **g-xanz**, `POST /api/game/start` and `POST /api/drills/start` can take **>6s**:
both snapshot a per-session opening-score baseline before inserting the
`GameSession`, and that path forces a synchronous `refresh_now(...)` which **blocks
up to its 5s timeout** waiting on the single opening-score scheduler. Production
evidence (Railway, user_id=14): ~95–97% of starts end with a NULL baseline anyway,
so today's path pays the wait AND usually fails to capture a baseline.

The fix must make start non-blocking **without** serving a known-stale baseline (a
stale `before` diffed against a fresh `after` at session end over-attributes prior
sessions' gains — the exact bug g-xanz's refresh-before-read prevented).

**Review correction (this revision):** an earlier draft gated freshness on the
scheduler probe `is_recompute_scheduled()` alone. That is **insufficient** — it only
reports in-memory pending/in-flight work; it does not prove the cached batch is
current after a restart, an out-of-process evidence change, registry drift, or a
legacy/NULL `inputs_fingerprint`. This revision gates on the **same cheap,
overlay-free fingerprint the recompute gate already uses**, and drops the probe.

**Outcome:** start creates the session immediately; baseline capture is a
non-blocking, best-effort read that returns a confident baseline **only when the
cached batch is provably current**, and NULL otherwise — graceful degradation, not a
new correctness bug, with maximum coverage for genuinely-fresh users.

## Verified current state (code @ 2026-06-26)

- `app/api/game.py:634` `start_game` and `app/api/drills.py:268` `start_drill` →
  `snapshot_opening_baseline(db, user_id, player_color)`. **Only two callers** (grep `app/`).
- `app/opening_score_delta.py:56` `snapshot_opening_baseline` currently: lazy-imports
  `refresh_now`; `if not refresh_now(...): return None` (**the 5s block**); else
  `load_cached_rows(...)` (which itself enqueues `request_recompute`, and on a cold
  cache calls `refresh_now` again) → `json.dumps({opening_key: opening_score})`;
  `except` → `db.rollback()` + None.
- **Real freshness gate** = `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` (opening_cache.py:1028).
  For an existing batch it serves it unchanged iff (1084-1099):
  `batch.registry_fingerprint == opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(graph, roots)`
  **and** `batch.inputs_fingerprint == opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint(db,…)`
  **and not** `_batch_has_stale_branch_keys(rows)` (decay aside).
  - `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` (opening_cache.py:112) is **cheap SQL, no
    overlay, no scheduler** — and already folds the registry/config/version fingerprint,
    so an `inputs_fingerprint` match subsumes the registry check. Legacy batches have
    `inputs_fingerprint = None` → never matches → correctly treated as stale.
- `list_cached_opening_scores` (opening_cache.py:322) → `(batch, rows)`, plain SQL,
  **never touches the scheduler**; `UserOpeningScore` has `.opening_key`/`.opening_score`.
  Returns `(None, [])` for **both** no-evidence and cold-cache-with-evidence.
- `has_opening_evidence` (opening_cache.py:777) — cheap (`limit=1`) existence probe to
  distinguish those two cold cases.
- `compute_opening_score_delta` (opening_score_delta.py:125, end-of-session) keeps its
  best-effort `refresh_now` → **out of scope, unchanged**. With a NULL baseline it
  still emits **after-only** items (`before=None`, `delta=None`, `is_new=False`,
  line 176) — the opening still appears, only the numeric before/delta is omitted.
- Observability: `HTTPLoggingMiddleware` already logs per-request `duration_ms` by route
  (http_logging.py:273) → start-endpoint duration is captured. **But** the root
  formatter prints only `%(message)s` (logging_config.py:20) → any new fields must be
  **in the message string**, not `extra=`.

## The change

### 1. New non-blocking freshness helper — `app/opening_cache.py`

Add a read-only helper next to the read cluster (`load_cached_rows`), reusing the
gate's fingerprint primitives so freshness logic stays co-located with the canonical
gate:

```python
def proven_fresh_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color):
    """Non-blocking freshness verdict — NEVER touches the scheduler.

    Returns (batch, rows, is_fresh). is_fresh is True only when a batch exists AND
    recompute_opening_scores_if_needed would serve it UNCHANGED: registry fingerprint
    matches, raw-input fingerprint matches, no stale branch keys. (Time-decay
    staleness is intentionally ignored — it perturbs scores by a small wall-clock
    amount, not by un-folded evidence; skipping on it would gut baseline coverage.)

    Mirrors the fast-path conditions in recompute_opening_scores_if_needed; if that
    gate's freshness conditions change, update this helper too.
    """
    batch, rows = list_cached_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)
    if batch is None:
        return None, [], False
    registry_fp = opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(get_opening_graph(), get_opening_roots())
    raw_fp = opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint(db, user_id, player_color)
    is_fresh = (
        batch.registry_fingerprint == registry_fp
        and batch.inputs_fingerprint == raw_fp
        and not _batch_has_stale_branch_keys(rows)
    )
    return batch, rows, is_fresh
```

Cost: one batch+rows read plus the cheap raw digest (the ~2.6s overlay is never
built). Worst case (heaviest user, ~50k session_moves) is a few hundred ms of DB read
+ hashing — vs the current up-to-5s block. No scheduler, no lock waits.

**Drift note (accepted tradeoff):** this duplicates the gate's freshness predicate
rather than refactoring the hot gate to share it. The cross-reference comment + the
opening_cache tests below lock the behavior; extracting a shared predicate is a
possible follow-up but is deliberately avoided here to keep the change contained.

### 2. Rewrite `snapshot_opening_baseline` in place — `app/opening_score_delta.py`

Rewrite in place (no parallel function): both endpoints already import this symbol,
there are no other callers, and a parallel function would leave the blocking version
as dead code.

```python
def snapshot_opening_baseline(db, user_id, player_color) -> str | None:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    source = "failed"
    try:
        batch, rows, is_fresh = proven_fresh_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)
        if batch is None:
            # Distinguish brand-new user (no evidence -> valid empty baseline) from a
            # cold cache that still has evidence (can't prove a baseline -> skip, else
            # session-end falsely marks every existing opening "new").
            if has_opening_evidence(db, user_id, player_color):
                source = "skipped_cold"
                return None
            source = "empty_no_evidence"
            return "{}"
        if not is_fresh:
            source = "skipped_stale"
            return None
        source = "cached_fresh"
        return json.dumps({row.opening_key: row.opening_score for row in rows})
    except Exception:  # best-effort: never block/poison the session-create commit
        source = "failed"
        try:
            db.rollback()
        except Exception:
            pass
        logger.warning(
            "opening_baseline_snapshot source=failed user_id=%s color=%s",
            user_id, player_color, exc_info=True,
        )
        return None
    finally:
        # Fields IN THE MESSAGE (root formatter prints %(message)s only).
        logger.info(
            "opening_baseline_snapshot user_id=%s color=%s source=%s snapshot_ms=%.2f",
            user_id, player_color, source, (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0,
        )
```

- Never imports/calls `refresh_now`, `request_recompute`, `is_recompute_scheduled`, or
  `load_cached_rows`. → no blocking, no enqueue, no weak probe.
- Source signal ∈ `{cached_fresh, skipped_stale, skipped_cold, empty_no_evidence, failed}`
  (finer than the bead's 4: splits the cold cache so post-restart staleness is visible
  separately from genuinely-new users). `snapshot_ms` proves the snapshot is fast;
  route `duration_ms` (middleware) proves end-to-end start latency dropped.
- Imports: add `proven_fresh_opening_scores`, `has_opening_evidence` from
  `app.opening_cache`; add `import time`. Keep `load_cached_rows` (still used by
  `compute_opening_score_delta`). Update the docstring to the new contract.

### 3 & 4. Start endpoints + end-of-session delta — no change

Endpoints keep calling `snapshot_opening_baseline` and inherit the non-blocking
behavior (middleware already logs duration). `compute_opening_score_delta` is
untouched; with a NULL baseline it degrades to after-only items (not an omitted item).

## Tests

**`test_opening_cache.py` — `proven_fresh_opening_scores`** (addresses reviewer's
"cold-with-evidence" and "stale-fingerprint-with-no-scheduled-work"):
- fresh batch (matching registry + raw fingerprints) → `is_fresh True`.
- evidence mutated (insert/alter a session_move so the raw digest changes) → `False`.
- registry drift (batch.registry_fingerprint set to a non-current value) → `False`.
- legacy `inputs_fingerprint = None` → `False`.
- stale branch keys present → `False`.
- no batch → `(None, [], False)`.

**`test_opening_score_delta.py`:**
- Helper `_make_batch` must seed **matching** `registry_fingerprint =
  opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(get_opening_graph(), get_opening_roots())` and
  `inputs_fingerprint = opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint(db, user_id, color)` so
  the freshness check passes for the happy-path (no-evidence test users → deterministic
  empty digest). Add a `fresh=False` variant (e.g. `inputs_fingerprint=None`) for stale
  tests.
- DELETE `test_snapshot_forces_refresh_before_reading`; `test_snapshot_skips_when_refresh_fails`
  (old blocking contract).
- KEEP/ADJUST `test_snapshot_returns_json_score_map`, `test_game_start_populates_baseline`,
  `test_drill_start_populates_baseline` (seed fresh fingerprints).
- `test_snapshot_empty_map_when_no_batch` → rename/clarify: no batch **and no evidence**
  → `"{}"` (source `empty_no_evidence`).
- ADD `test_snapshot_skips_cold_cache_with_evidence`: seed session_moves but NO batch →
  `None` (source `skipped_cold`). **(finding 2)**
- ADD `test_snapshot_skips_when_batch_stale`: batch with non-matching `inputs_fingerprint`,
  no scheduler activity → `None` (source `skipped_stale`). **(finding 1)**
- ADD `test_snapshot_does_not_call_refresh_now`: patch `app.opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now`
  as a Mock; fresh batch → returns map AND `refresh_now.assert_not_called()`. (AC 1/2/7)
- ADD `test_game_start_does_not_block_on_scheduler` / `..._drill_...`: same at the
  endpoint level (201, baseline set, refresh_now not called).
- UPDATE `test_snapshot_none_on_failure`, `test_snapshot_rolls_back_on_failure`,
  `test_game_start_succeeds_when_baseline_snapshot_fails`: patch target →
  `app.opening_score_delta.proven_fresh_opening_scores` (was `load_cached_rows`). (finding 6/AC 6)
- ADD `test_snapshot_logs_source_signal` (`caplog`): assert the message text contains
  `source=cached_fresh` and `source=skipped_stale` on the respective paths. **(finding 4 / AC 10)**
- `compute_opening_score_delta` tests unchanged (still pass; AC 8) — confirms after-only
  degradation under NULL baseline **(finding 5)**.

## Verification

- `cd backend && python -m pytest test_opening_score_delta.py test_opening_cache.py -q`
- Regression: `python -m pytest test_opening_score_scheduler.py -q`
- Project memory: full pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load — re-run any failing
  file in isolation before trusting a failure.
- Post-deploy: route `duration_ms` for both start endpoints falls well below the old
  >6s; `opening_baseline_snapshot source=…` distribution shows `cached_fresh`/
  `empty_no_evidence` dominating, with `skipped_stale`/`skipped_cold` flagging the
  genuinely-stale heavy-user / post-restart paths and **no 5s waits**.

## Revised acceptance criteria (supersede the bead's probe-based wording)

1–2,7. Neither start endpoint synchronously calls `refresh_now` / blocks on the scheduler.
3. Start reads via `list_cached_opening_scores` (inside `proven_fresh_opening_scores`); never `load_cached_rows` / never enqueues.
4. A confident baseline is persisted **only when the cached batch is provably current**
   (registry + raw-input fingerprints match, no stale branch keys); otherwise NULL
   (`skipped_stale`). A NULL baseline degrades to **after-only** delta items at session
   end (numeric before/delta omitted), not an omitted opening.
5. Cold cache **with** evidence → NULL (`skipped_cold`); no batch **and no** evidence → `"{}"`.
6. Start stays 201 when the cache read fails (rollback → NULL).
8. End-of-session deltas still work with a baseline and degrade gracefully when NULL.
9. Tests cover no-block-on-start (refresh_now Mock asserted not-called), stale-fingerprint-skip, and cold-with-evidence-skip.
10. A `source` signal (`cached_fresh|skipped_stale|skipped_cold|empty_no_evidence|failed`) + `snapshot_ms` are logged **in the message string**; start duration via existing middleware.

## Scope / files

- `backend/app/opening_cache.py` — add `proven_fresh_opening_scores` (+ tests).
- `backend/app/opening_score_delta.py` — rewrite `snapshot_opening_baseline` (imports, docstring, message-string log).
- `backend/test_opening_cache.py`, `backend/test_opening_score_delta.py` — tests above.
- **No change** to `game.py`, `drills.py`, the scheduler, or `compute_opening_score_delta`.
- Commit the beads ledger with the code (one commit); commit directly to master (project rules).
acceptance_criteria:
1. POST /api/game/start does not synchronously call opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now (and never blocks on the scheduler).
2. POST /api/drills/start does not synchronously call opening_score_scheduler.refresh_now (and never blocks on the scheduler).
3. Start path reads the latest batch via list_cached_opening_scores directly (not load_cached_rows) so it never enqueues or waits on scheduler work.
4. When is_recompute_scheduled is True at start (pending/in-flight evidence), the baseline is persisted NULL and the end-of-session delta is omitted — no stale 'before' is captured (no misattribution).
5. When no recompute is scheduled, a confident baseline is persisted (or '{}' for a user with no batch yet).
6. Start endpoints remain successful when the opening-score cache is missing, stale, or failing.
7. Heavy users do not pay the 5s refresh_now timeout before a game/drill begins.
8. End-of-session opening_score_changes still work when a baseline is available and degrade gracefully when it is NULL.
9. Tests cover the no-refresh/no-block-on-start regression for both game and drill starts, including a monkeypatched refresh_now that would sleep/raise and must not be reached, and a probe-returns-True path that yields a NULL baseline.
10. A baseline-source signal (cached_fresh | skipped_stale | empty_batch | failed) and start-endpoint duration are logged, landing WITH the fix so the latency improvement is provable, not inferred.

title: /api/openings/tree: bound observed-edge prefetch to visible parents (Option B, supersedes g-a6k2 whole-batch load)
description: g-a6k2 collapsed the per-parent observed-edge N+1 into ONE whole-batch read (lookup_observed_edges_for_batch), which fixed the 35-round-trip blowup but introduced a new bottleneck for high-history users: the eager load now pulls the user's ENTIRE edge history. On user_id=14 server.log shows observed_edge_rows=7872 (white)/8259 (black) and ~1.2s of UNTIMED latency in _OpeningTreeBuilder.__init__ (the load sits between the rollback and builder_total timing stages, so it is invisible in the timing log). Only ~35 parents are actually visible per request. Option B (deferred in g-a6k2 as 'only worth it if a batch can have a very large total edge set' — it can) fetches edges ONLY for the visible parents via a bounded WHERE batch_id=? AND parent_fen IN (...) prefetch: line positions (wave 1) then their column children/frontier (wave 2). 2 round-trips, ~tens of rows instead of ~8000. Also fixes the instrumentation gap (time the prefetch). Full data-flow analysis, 2-wave proof, implementation, edge cases, and tests in the design field.
design:
# `/api/openings/tree`: bound the observed-edge prefetch to visible parents (Option B)

## Why we're doing this (context from g-a6k2)

`g-a6k2` diagnosed `/api/openings/tree` taking 6–10s as an **N+1**: the tree
builder fired one `lookup_observed_edges_for_parent` SELECT per visited parent
(`observed_edge_queries=35`), and against the remote Railway Postgres (~150ms
RTT) that serialized into `structural_columns_ms≈5243`.

The g-a6k2 fix was **Option A**: eager-load the *whole* batch once
(`lookup_observed_edges_for_batch(db, batch_id)` → `dict[parent_fen, list[EdgeEvidence]]`)
in `_OpeningTreeBuilder.__init__`, then read `_observed_children` from memory.
That worked for what it measured:

```
observed_edge_queries: 35 → 1
structural_columns_ms: 5243 → 25–48
```

**But it revealed a deeper problem.** After Option A the page is still ~2.1–2.9s,
and the time is *not in any timed stage*. Arithmetic on a warm line
(`total_ms=2241`):

| stage                | ms   |
|----------------------|------|
| ensure_cache         | 402  |
| rollback             | 133  |
| builder_total (incl. structural 39 + position_rows 146 + move_evals 145 + root_eval 142) | 475 |
| **sum of timed stages** | **~1010** |
| **total_ms**         | **2241** |
| **unaccounted**      | **~1230** |

The only untimed DB call between `request_started` and `total_ms` is the new
`lookup_observed_edges_for_batch` in `__init__`. And the smoking gun is in the
log itself:

```
observed_edge_rows=7872   (white)
observed_edge_rows=8259   (black)
```

The g-a6k2 evidence user had **39** edge rows. user_id=14 has **~8000**. Option A
trades 35 small round-trips for **one round-trip that transfers ~8000 rows and
instantiates ~8000 ORM objects** across the 150ms-RTT remote link — a consistent
~1.1–1.2s regardless of node count (20 vs 50 nodes ⇒ same gap, because the cost
is the fixed full-history load, not per-node work).

This is exactly the case g-a6k2 deferred: *"Option B — batch the discovered set …
only worth it if a batch can have a very large total edge set."* It can. So we
implement Option B now.

> Note: this is amplified by the remote dev DB. In prod (co-located DB, ~1ms RTT)
> the 8000-row load is ~tens of ms and the whole endpoint is sub-second. Option B
> still matters in prod for high-history users (it bounds rows *and* round-trips),
> and it makes the dev experience usable without re-pointing the DB.

## Goal

Fetch observed edges for **only the visible parents** (bounded by nodes on screen,
~tens of rows) in a **bounded number of round-trips** (2, independent of node
count), and **time the load** so it can never hide again.

## Data-flow analysis: which positions trigger `_observed_children`?

Call graph (verified):
- `_observed_children` ← only `_structural_children`.
- `_structural_children` ← `_column_children`, and Pass-1 `build()` (line ~1211,
  on **line positions**).
- `_column_children` ← Pass-1 `build()` (line ~1214, line positions),
  `_terminal_reason_for_position` (pos[k], a line position),
  `_terminal_reason_for_child` (line ~1066, on **frontier children**).
- `_terminal_reason_for_child` ← Pass-1 per column node (line ~1274).

`resolve_line` / `_resolve_moves` / `_bfs_book_path` do **not** read observed
edges — the canonical line is a pure board + book computation, fixed *before* any
observed lookup. So the prefetch can run after replay, before Pass 1.

Therefore the complete set of FENs for which `_observed_children` is ever called
in one request is exactly:

1. **Line positions** `pos_norm[0..k]` — the canonical line.
2. **Frontier children** — `child.child_fen` for every child in
   `_column_children(pos_norm[i])`, for each `i` in `0..k`.

It is **two levels deep, no more**: `_terminal_reason_for_child` probes a frontier
child via `_column_children(child_norm)` (needs the child's *own* observed edges =
wave 2), but only tests truthiness ("does this child have any column children?").
It never displays the child's children, so grandchildren's observed edges are
never read. ⇒ **2 waves suffice.**

### The injected off-tree move is already a line position
Pass 1 injects a `selected_uci` node when `selected_uci not in column`
(g-obh5 off-tree navigation, lines ~1216–1230). `selected_uci = line[i]` for
`i < k`, and pushing `line[i]` on `boards[i]` yields `boards[i+1]` ⇒ its
`child_fen == pos_norm[i+1]`, **already in wave 1**. So the injected child needs
no special prefetch handling. (Its `_terminal_reason_for_child` call with
`is_navigable=True` then probes `_column_children(pos_norm[i+1])`, whose edges
wave 1 loaded.)

### Why 2 waves and not 1
Wave 2's set depends on wave 1's *results*: off-book **observed** children of a
line position become frontier nodes, and we can't know them without first reading
that line position's edges. So the frontier is only knowable after wave 1. (A
1-query variant could over-fetch by predicting the frontier from book children
alone and doing a tiny wave 2 only for off-book observed frontier — not worth the
complexity; the saving is one 150ms RTT. Keep the clean 2-wave.)

## Implementation

### 1. New bounded lookup in `app/opening_cache.py`
Add alongside the existing helpers (reuse `_edge_evidence_from_row` from g-a6k2):

```python
def lookup_observed_edges_for_parents(
    db: Session,
    batch_id: int,
    parent_fens: Iterable[str],
) -> dict[str, list[EdgeEvidence]]:
    """Observed edges for a specific set of parents in one batch, indexed by
    normalized parent FEN. Bounded by the visible node set (line ∪ frontier), so
    it fetches ~tens of rows instead of the whole batch. Parents with no edges are
    absent (callers use .get(fen, [])). Uses the
    idx_opening_position_edges_batch_parent index via parent_fen IN (...).
    """
    fens = {f for f in parent_fens}
    if not fens:
        return {}
    edges_by_parent: dict[str, list[EdgeEvidence]] = {}
    # Chunk the IN-list defensively (SQLite ~999 param cap). The set is small by
    # construction (visible nodes), so this is usually a single chunk.
    for chunk in _chunked(sorted(fens), 900):
        rows = (
            db.query(OpeningPositionEdge)
            .filter(
                OpeningPositionEdge.batch_id == batch_id,
                OpeningPositionEdge.parent_fen.in_(chunk),
            )
            .all()
        )
        for row in rows:
            edges_by_parent.setdefault(row.parent_fen, []).append(
                _edge_evidence_from_row(row)
            )
    return edges_by_parent
```

Remove `lookup_observed_edges_for_batch` (added in g-a6k2) — Option B supersedes
it and nothing else uses it. Keep `lookup_observed_edges_for_parent` (still
unit-tested; used as the defensive straggler fallback below).

### 2. Move the load out of `__init__` into `build()` (`app/api/openings.py`)
`__init__` reverts to initializing an empty cache + counters (it no longer has the
data it needs — `pos_norm` is computed in `build()`):

```python
self._observed_cache: dict[str, list[EdgeEvidence]] = {}
self._observed_edge_query_count = 0   # batch IN-queries issued (waves)
self._observed_edge_row_count = 0
self._observed_straggler_count = 0    # per-parent fallbacks (asserted 0)
```

Add a 2-wave prefetch, called in `build()` **after** the replay loop (we now have
`pos_norm[0..k]`) and **before** Pass 1, wrapped in a new timed stage:

```python
def _prefetch_observed_edges(self, pos_norm: list[str], k: int) -> None:
    """Bounded prefetch: load observed edges for exactly the parents the build
    will visit — line positions (wave 1) then their column children/frontier
    (wave 2) — in 2 IN-queries, independent of node count. No-op when batch_id
    is None (book-only)."""
    if self.batch_id is None:
        return
    # Wave 1: line positions.
    line_fens = set(pos_norm[: k + 1])
    self._load_observed(line_fens)
    # Wave 2: frontier = all column children of every line position. _column_children
    # is now a cache hit for the line positions, so no extra queries here. Some
    # frontier FENs ARE line positions (the on-line child pos_norm[i+1]) — harmless,
    # _load_observed skips already-cached parents.
    frontier: set[str] = set()
    for norm_i in line_fens:
        for child in self._column_children(norm_i).values():
            frontier.add(child.child_fen)
    self._load_observed(frontier)

def _load_observed(self, fens: set[str]) -> None:
    """One IN-query for the not-yet-cached subset of fens; populate the cache so
    every fen has an entry (absent parents → [])."""
    missing = {f for f in fens if f not in self._observed_cache}
    if not missing:
        return
    loaded = lookup_observed_edges_for_parents(self.db, self.batch_id, missing)
    for f in missing:
        edges = loaded.get(f, [])
        self._observed_cache[f] = edges
        self._observed_edge_row_count += len(edges)
    self._observed_edge_query_count += 1
```

In `build()`:
```python
stage_started = time.perf_counter()
self._prefetch_observed_edges(pos_norm, k)
_record_timing(timings, "observed_prefetch_ms", stage_started)
```
Add `observed_prefetch_ms` to the timing-log format string + `_timing_ms` call so
the load is visible (closing the instrumentation gap that hid Option A's cost).

### 3. `_observed_children`: cache read + defensive straggler fallback
Prefetch should cover every visited parent. A miss means the prefetch
under-collected — fall back to a single point query so the tree stays correct,
and COUNT it so the regression is observable (and asserted zero in tests):

```python
def _observed_children(self, norm_fen: str) -> list[EdgeEvidence]:
    hit = self._observed_cache.get(norm_fen)
    if hit is None:
        if self.batch_id is None:
            hit = []
        else:
            # Defensive: prefetch should have loaded this. A miss = under-collection;
            # serve correctly via a point query and flag the straggler.
            hit = lookup_observed_edges_for_parent(self.db, self.batch_id, norm_fen)
            self._observed_straggler_count += 1
            self._observed_edge_query_count += 1
            self._observed_edge_row_count += len(hit)
        self._observed_cache[norm_fen] = hit
    return hit
```

Surface `observed_straggler_count` in the timing log too (should always be 0).

## Edge cases
- **`batch_id is None`** (cold / no-evidence): prefetch no-ops, cache empty, every
  `_observed_children` returns `[]` ⇒ book-only tree, **zero** edge queries.
- **Empty parent set** (e.g. start position with no line): `_load_observed({})`
  is a no-op; wave 1 has `pos_norm[0]`, so never truly empty.
- **Off-book observed frontier**: covered — wave 2 derives the frontier from the
  *post-wave-1* `_column_children`, which includes observed off-book children.
- **IN-list size**: bounded by visible nodes (~tens); chunk at 900 defensively for
  SQLite's param cap (tests run on SQLite). Postgres is unaffected.
- **Transposed/synthetic edges**: unchanged — board-legality guard in Pass 1 still
  filters illegal listed moves; prefetch only changes *how* edges are loaded.

## Tests

### `test_opening_cache.py`
- `test_lookup_observed_edges_for_parents_*`: returns edges only for the requested
  parents (not the whole batch); absent parent omitted; empty input → `{}`;
  quality zeroed; chunking path exercised (>900 parents → still one merged map).
- Remove/replace the `lookup_observed_edges_for_batch` test added in g-a6k2.

### `test_tree_api.py`

- **Bounded queries**: a warm read with observed edges issues **exactly 2**

- **Timing**: assert `observed_prefetch_ms` and `observed_straggler_count` appear

## Acceptance criteria
- `/tree` issues a **bounded** number of observed-edge queries — **2** IN-queries
  on the warm path (1 per wave), **0** on the cold/no-evidence path — regardless
  of node/column count.
- `_observed_straggler_count == 0` across the test matrix (prefetch is complete:
  line ∪ frontier ∪ terminal-probe child parents, incl. off-book observed frontier

- Observed-edge rows fetched are bounded by the visible node set (~tens), **not**

- Tree contents unchanged vs Option A (same moves, names, terminal reasons, evals).
- `structural_columns_ms` stays ~tens of ms; on the remote dev DB the prefetch is

## Relationship to g-a6k2
Supersedes the Option A mechanism (`lookup_observed_edges_for_batch` whole-batch
load) with the bounded Option B prefetch. g-a6k2's other artifacts stay:
`_edge_evidence_from_row` helper, `lookup_observed_edges_for_parent` (now the
