title: /api/openings/tree slow (6-10s): N+1 observed-edge queries × remote DB RTT
description: GET /api/openings/tree takes 6-10s on the /openings page. Root cause: the tree builder issues one observed-edge SELECT per visited parent position (_OpeningTreeBuilder._observed_children -> lookup_observed_edges_for_parent), an N+1 pattern. server.log shows observed_edge_queries=35 for a 34-node/2-column response returning only 39 rows, and structural_columns_ms=5243 dominates the ~7s total. The server is pointed at a remote Railway Postgres (~150ms RTT/query), so structural_ms / query_count is a near-constant ~150ms (one round-trip) across every logged request. cache_state=warm_fresh every time, so it is NOT the scoring/overlay/scheduler path. A pure-graph simulation of the identical node work runs in 30ms. Fix: collapse the per-parent reads into a single batch query (load all batch edges once, index by parent_fen in memory). Full diagnosis, evidence table, and fix options in the design field.
design:
# `/api/openings/tree` is latency-bound on N+1 observed-edge queries

## Symptom
`GET /api/openings/tree` takes 6–10s on the `/openings` page. Confirmed from
`backend/server.log` (user_id=14):

```
total_ms=6982 cache_state=warm_fresh ensure_cache_ms=487 rollback_ms=133
structural_columns_ms=5243  ← dominates
position_rows_ms=143 move_evals_ms=215 root_eval_ms=137 builder_total_ms=5743
raw_columns=2 raw_nodes=34 observed_edge_queries=35 observed_edge_rows=39
```

## Root cause
Two compounding factors:

1. **N+1 observed-edge lookups.** `_OpeningTreeBuilder._observed_children`
   (`backend/app/api/openings.py:935`) fires one separate
   `lookup_observed_edges_for_parent` SELECT per visited parent position
   (`backend/app/opening_cache.py:554` — `SELECT … FROM opening_position_edges
   WHERE batch_id=? AND parent_fen=?`, one round-trip, memoized per FEN in
   `_observed_cache`). The timing field `observed_edge_queries` counts these:
   **35 separate queries** for a response of only 34 nodes / 2 columns returning
   **39 total rows**. Deeper lines hit 42+.

2. **Server is pointed at a REMOTE Railway Postgres**
   (`nozomi.proxy.rlwy.net:23621/railway`, found in the running uvicorn process
   env `DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL`; `.env` only carries POSTHOG keys so
   `resolve_database_url()` would otherwise pick local). Every query pays full
   network RTT (~135–150ms). Every single-query stage in the log confirms the
   RTT: `rollback_ms=133`, `position_rows_ms=143`, `root_eval_ms=135`.

**Math (structural_ms ÷ query_count ≈ constant ~150ms = one round-trip):**

| request            | observed_edge_queries | structural_columns_ms | ms/query |
|--------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|----------|
| white d2d4         | 35                    | 5244                  | 150      |
| white b2b4         | 37                    | 5550                  | 150      |
| white b2b4 b7b5    | 42                    | 6153                  | 147      |
| black b2b4 b7b5    | 32                    | 4848                  | 151      |

So ~35 serialized round-trips × ~150ms ≈ 5s. It is NOT heavy computation: a
pure-graph simulation of the identical node-building work (book fan-out +
`is_middlegame_position` over the same 34 nodes, no DB) runs in **30ms**.
`get_node`/`get_root` are O(1) dict lookups; `is_middlegame_position` is
~0.022ms.

## What it is NOT
- NOT the scoring/overlay/scheduler path. `cache_state=warm_fresh` every time;
  the cheap raw-inputs fingerprint gate (`opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint`)
  is in place and the recompute runs in the background. `ensure_cache_ms≈400ms`.
- NOT `position_rows`/`move_evals`/`root_eval` — those are already single batched
  queries (~135–215ms each, i.e. ~1 RTT).

## Why it matters even in prod
Largely a dev artifact: with the app co-located with the DB (~1ms RTT) the 35
queries total ~35ms and the page is fast. But the N+1 is a real latent bug — the
endpoint's latency scales as (visible parents × RTT), so any latency or a deeper
line degrades it. The per-parent design was chosen to keep the read "bounded by
visible nodes," which bounds row COUNT but not the number of round-trips.

## Proposed fix
Collapse the per-parent observed-edge reads into a SINGLE query. Total edge rows
per (batch) are tiny (39–74 here), so the simplest, lowest-risk option:

**Option A (preferred) — eager-load the batch once, index in memory.**
- Add `lookup_observed_edges_for_batch(db, batch_id) -> dict[str, list[EdgeEvidence]]`
  in `opening_cache.py`: one `SELECT … WHERE batch_id=?`, grouped by `parent_fen`.
- In `_OpeningTreeBuilder.__init__`, load that map once (when `batch_id is not
  None`) and have `_observed_children` read from it (`.get(norm_fen, [])`) instead
  of issuing a per-parent query. Drop/￫retain `_observed_edge_query_count` as 1.
- Keeps the post-`db.rollback()` safety (still keyed only on the scalar
  `batch_id`; no ORM batch row read).

**Option B — batch the discovered set.** Pre-walk to collect the parent FENs
(line ∪ frontier), then one `… WHERE batch_id=? AND parent_fen IN (…)`. More
faithful to "bounded by visible nodes" but requires two passes; only worth it if
a batch can have a very large total edge set.

Given observed_edge_rows is small (tens), Option A is simplest and turns 35
round-trips into 1 — structural stage ~5s → ~150ms.

## Tests
- Update `backend/test_tree_api.py`: assert exactly ONE observed-edge query is
  issued per `/tree` request regardless of node count (patch/count the lookup),
  and that tree contents are unchanged (same observed moves surfaced).
- Verify `batch_id is None` (cold/no-evidence) still yields a book-only tree with
  zero edge queries.

## Note
Do NOT chase this by querying the remote prod DB. Reproduce locally by pointing
the dev server at a local Postgres; the N+1 is visible in `observed_edge_queries`
regardless of latency.
acceptance_criteria: /tree issues exactly one observed-edge query per request regardless of node/column count; the single batch load is timed as observed_edges_ms (its own stage, also inside builder_total_ms) so the DB round-trip is never an unaccounted gap in total_ms; structural_columns_ms is now the in-memory column build (~tens of ms); tree contents unchanged (same observed moves surfaced); cold/no-evidence batch still yields book-only tree with zero edge queries.
notes: Review (P2): the batch load originally sat in __init__, untimed — only reflected in total_ms, not structural_columns_ms/builder_total_ms. Fixed by moving it into _load_observed_edges(), called from build() as the timed observed_edges_ms stage (now also captured by builder_total_ms). Added observed_edges_ms to the timing-log format + test_tree_timing_log_can_be_forced. Review (P3): updated stale 'bounded per-parent'/'read lazily' comments at the module header, class docstring, and route. NOTE: observed_edges_ms exposes that high-history users (user_id=14: observed_edge_rows~7872) pay ~1.2s on the remote dev DB for the whole-batch load — this is the new bottleneck addressed by g-0qe6 (Option B, bounded prefetch).
close_reason: Option A landed: collapsed the per-parent observed-edge N+1 into one batch load (lookup_observed_edges_for_batch), now timed as observed_edges_ms. observed_edge_queries 35->1, structural_columns_ms 5243->~tens of ms. Follow-up g-0qe6 bounds the load to visible parents (the whole-batch read is heavy for high-history users).

title: Batch opening tree observed-edge reads
description:
The /openings page calls GET /api/openings/tree and recent backend/server.log entries show 5.9-7.6s server responses for normal warm-cache requests. The timing logs show cache_state=warm_fresh, so this is not cold bootstrap or refresh_now. The dominant stage is structural_columns_ms: 4.8-6.2s of each request.

Evidence from backend/server.log:
- player_color=white&move=d2d4: total_ms=6982.426, structural_columns_ms=5243.956, observed_edge_queries=35, observed_edge_rows=39.
- player_color=white&move=b2b4: total_ms=6705.581, structural_columns_ms=5549.907, observed_edge_queries=37, observed_edge_rows=66.
- player_color=white&move=b2b4&move=b7b5: total_ms=7313.099, structural_columns_ms=6152.609, observed_edge_queries=42, observed_edge_rows=74.
- player_color=black&move=b2b4&move=b7b5: total_ms=5864.855, structural_columns_ms=4848.138, observed_edge_queries=32, observed_edge_rows=44.

Root cause: _OpeningTreeBuilder._observed_children lazily calls lookup_observed_edges_for_parent one parent at a time. The structural pass also calls terminal checks for child positions, and _terminal_reason_for_child can call _column_children(child_norm), which triggers more parent lookups. In this environment each DB round trip is roughly 135ms, so 32-42 sequential observed-edge queries explain most of the 6-10s latency.
design:
Proposed fix: replace the N+1 observed-edge reads in /api/openings/tree with bounded batched reads while preserving current tree semantics.

Implementation shape:
1. Add backend/app/opening_cache.py helper lookup_observed_edges_for_parents(db, batch_id, parent_fens) -> dict[str, list[EdgeEvidence]]. It should query OpeningPositionEdge once with batch_id == batch_id and parent_fen IN (...), using the existing batch/parent index, then group rows by parent_fen. Include empty lists for requested parents with no rows.
2. Update _OpeningTreeBuilder so observed-edge SQL is prefetched in bounded passes. After resolving/replaying the canonical line, prefetch line parents pos_norm[0:k+1]. During structural column construction, collect child positions that need terminal probing, batch-prefetch those parents before terminal reason derivation, and make _observed_children hit only the in-memory _observed_cache for prefetched parents.
3. Keep lookup_observed_edges_for_parent only as a fallback or migrate tests away from it. The timing field observed_edge_queries should count actual SQL round trips; expected warm reads should drop from 32-42 to about 2.
4. No schema change should be required. The data already lives in opening_position_edges. This is a read-path batching change, not a scoring/cache invalidation change.

Expected result: structural_columns_ms should drop from ~5-6s to low hundreds of ms. Total request time should then be dominated by ensure_cache_ms, position_rows_ms, move_evals_ms, and root_eval_ms, likely near ~1s rather than 6-10s on the same DB.

Test coverage:
- Unit test lookup_observed_edges_for_parents groups rows correctly and returns empty lists for missing parents.
- Tree warm read test asserts bounded observed-edge SQL batches instead of repeated per-parent helper calls.
- Existing behavior remains unchanged for observed moves, book moves, off-tree selected moves, terminal reasons, metrics hydration, evals, and sorting.
- Timing/log expectations should reflect the reduced observed_edge_queries count.
close_reason: Duplicate of g-a6k2 (same N+1 observed-edge root cause, same server.log evidence). g-a6k2 is the canonical issue: superior diagnosis (remote Railway Postgres RTT root cause + dev-artifact caveat + 30ms pure-graph compute proof), tighter acceptance criteria (exactly 1 query), and already documents this ticket's batch-the-discovered-set approach as its Option B. The terminal-probe/_column_children note unique to this ticket was ported into g-a6k2's notes.

title: Ghost steering dies mid-game: in-progress session counts as its own opportunity_since_review
description: find_ghost_move stops steering toward a due blunder partway through a game. _compute_blunder_opportunity_events creates a BlunderOpportunityEvent for the CURRENT in-progress session as soon as it touches an ancestor of the blunder. That single event flips srs_priority from time-based (~84) to opportunity-based: calculate_opportunity_overdue(opportunities_since_review=1, pass_streak=0) = 1/1.0 = exactly 1.0. ghost_eligible requires priority > 1.0 (intentional, see test_srs_priority.py), so the blunder becomes ineligible and find_ghost_move returns None -> Maia fallback -> no steering -> no review toast. Breaks e2e screenshot test 'play > fresh board + review toast' (opponent plays f5 instead of Bc5). Fix: exclude the current session from the opportunity counters used by find_ghost_move (the active game shouldn't count as a missed opportunity against the blunder it is steering toward).

The persisted opening score cache only helps position metrics later in builder.build, so warm tree reads still scale with full user history. Cold users can also pay refresh_now and score recompute work. In dev, React StrictMode may duplicate the initial fetch, making the request-path work appear worse. Target behavior: warm tree reads should be bounded by visible line/frontier size plus indexed cached read-model lookups, not by historical game count.
design:
# Plan: serve /api/openings/tree from cached tree evidence (g-tree-fast-cache)

## Problem (confirmed by code + measurements)
`GET /api/openings/tree` calls `overlay_evidence(db, user_id, color, graph)` on every
request (`backend/app/api/openings.py:1396`). That rebuilds the FULL evidence overlay:
loads all normal/drill `session_moves`, reconstructs every session board line, runs the
Lichess phase divider, normalizes FENs, and consults `analysis_cache`. Measured cost:
`overlay_ms ≈ 22000–25000` of a `total_ms ≈ 22000–26000` request, scaling with historical
game count (overlay_nodes=3394, overlay_edges=7600). Everything else is already cheap:
`builder_total_ms≈130`, `position_rows_ms≈60–80`, `move_evals_ms≈25`.

## Key insight (the change is small in surface area)
The tree builder consumes the overlay through EXACTLY ONE field. `_OpeningTreeBuilder.__init__`
(openings.py:904-906) reads only `overlay.edges` to build `_observed_by_parent`. It never
reads `overlay.nodes`, ghost targets, reviews, quality, or telemetry (the only other
`overlay.*` refs are route-level timing logs at 1398-1400). So the tree needs only the
**observed EDGES**, and per edge only: `uci`, `child_fen`, `traversal_count`
(→`encounter_count`), `live_attempts` (→`user_choice_count` + `is_prepared`), `live_passes`
(→`is_prepared`). That's it.

Observed-edge access pattern in the builder (drives the read shape):
- `_structural_children(norm)` reads `_observed_by_parent.get(norm)`.
- It is called for every line position `pos_norm[0..k]` AND, via
  `_terminal_reason_for_child → _column_children(child_norm)` (openings.py:1027), for every
  rendered FRONTIER child one ply beyond the line.
- So the builder needs observed edges only for {line positions} ∪ {rendered frontier
  children} — exactly the bead's "bounded by visible line/frontier size." Line depth is
  capped at `MAX_TREE_PLY=80`.

## We extend an existing pipeline rather than build new machinery
A fingerprint-gated, scheduler-driven recompute already persists per-(user,color) read
models, keyed by an `OpeningScoreBatch`:
- `recompute_opening_scores()` (opening_cache.py:525) builds the overlay ONCE and writes
  `opening_score_batches` + `user_opening_scores` + `opening_position_scores` in one txn.
  The overlay (`overlay.edges`) is already in memory there.
- Freshness is gated by `batch.inputs_fingerprint` (raw-row digest via
  `raw_evidence_inputs_digest`) and `batch.registry_fingerprint`
  (`opening_score_inputs_fingerprint`). Matching fingerprints ⇒ overlay provably identical ⇒
  serve cached without rebuild (`recompute_opening_scores_if_needed`, opening_cache.py:787).
- Reads already trigger stale-while-revalidate via the in-process coalescing
  `opening_score_scheduler` (`refresh_now` cold / `request_recompute` warm).
- The tree position metrics are ALREADY served warm from `opening_position_scores` via
  `load_tree_position_rows` (openings.py:1233).

So the only thing still rebuilt on the hot path is the overlay's EDGES. We persist those in
the SAME batch and read them on the hot path. No new scheduler, no new fingerprint logic.

---

## Design

### 1. New persisted read model: `opening_position_edges`
Mirror `opening_position_scores` exactly (batch-scoped, cascade, dual index).

Columns:
- `id` BIGINT PK autoincrement
- `batch_id` BIGINT FK → `opening_score_batches.id` ON DELETE CASCADE, NOT NULL
- `user_id` BIGINT NOT NULL
- `player_color` VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL  (+ CHECK in ('white','black'))
- `parent_fen` TEXT NOT NULL    -- normalized 4-field
- `child_fen` TEXT NOT NULL     -- normalized 4-field
- `uci` TEXT NOT NULL
- `traversal_count` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
- `live_attempts` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
- `live_passes` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
- `live_fails` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0   -- EdgeEvidence parity; not read by tree
- `computed_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

Constraints / indexes:
- `UNIQUE(batch_id, parent_fen, child_fen)`  -- mirrors EdgeEvidence key (parent_fen, child_fen)
- `INDEX idx_opening_position_edges_batch_parent (batch_id, parent_fen)`  -- powers the bounded read
- `INDEX idx_opening_position_edges_user_color (user_id, player_color)`   -- parity/admin

Quality (`quality_sum`/`quality_count`) is deliberately OMITTED: the tree never reads it and
the scorer builds its own in-memory overlay during recompute. Reconstruct EdgeEvidence with
`quality_sum=0.0, quality_count=0` (tree ignores both). Note in a comment that if the scorer
ever reads from this table, quality columns must be added.

Add in all THREE places (project rule — SQLite test schema is hand-written):
- `backend/app/models.py`: new `OpeningPositionEdge(Base)` model next to `OpeningPositionScore`
  (models.py:379-453), same `BIGINT_SQLITE`, CheckConstraint, ForeignKeyConstraint(ondelete=
  "CASCADE"), UniqueConstraint, two Index() entries.
- `backend/alembic/versions/20260616_01_create_opening_position_edges.py`:
  `revision="20260616_01"`, `down_revision="20260615_02"` (current head). Copy the body style
  of `20260615_01_create_opening_position_scores.py` (bigint_sqlite variant, create_table with
  CheckConstraint + ForeignKeyConstraint + UniqueConstraint, two create_index). Implement
  `downgrade()` with `op.drop_table`.
- `backend/conftest.py` `_create_test_schema`: add `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
  opening_position_edges (... UNIQUE(batch_id,parent_fen,child_fen), FOREIGN KEY(batch_id)
  REFERENCES opening_score_batches(id) ON DELETE CASCADE)` alongside the other cache tables
  (~conftest.py:286-305). PRAGMA foreign_keys is already ON in conftest:39 and db.py:18-26.

### 2. Persist edges during recompute (write side)
In `recompute_opening_scores` (opening_cache.py:525), the overlay is already built/scored.
Inside the existing `try:` block (after the `OpeningPositionScore` add_all, before
`db.commit()`), add an `add_all` writing one `OpeningPositionEdge` per `overlay.edges.values()`:
`parent_fen=edge.parent_fen, child_fen=edge.child_fen, uci=edge.uci, traversal_count,
live_attempts, live_passes, live_fails, batch_id=batch.id, user_id, player_color, computed_at`.
This rides the same transaction and the same retention/cascade as scores (≈7600 rows in the
measured case; comparable to the position-score insert already logged there). Add a
`logger.info` row-count line mirroring the existing position-score staging log.

### 3. Read edges on the hot path (read side)
New reader in `opening_cache.py`:
```
def lookup_observed_edges_for_parent(db, batch_id, parent_fen) -> list[EdgeEvidence]:
    # SELECT ... FROM opening_position_edges
    # WHERE batch_id=:b AND parent_fen=:p   (index idx_opening_position_edges_batch_parent)
    # -> [EdgeEvidence(parent_fen, child_fen, uci, traversal_count, live_attempts,
    #                  live_passes, live_fails, quality_sum=0.0, quality_count=0), ...]
```
Lazy + memoized point queries are the right shape because the frontier (child FENs) is only
known after observed edges for line positions are loaded; the builder discovers exactly the
parents it needs as it walks.

Refactor `_OpeningTreeBuilder` (openings.py:879-906):
- Constructor takes scalars `batch_id: int | None` and `batch_computed_at: datetime | None`
  instead of `overlay: EvidenceOverlay` (Finding #2 — no ORM row held across the rollback).
- Replace the eager `self._observed_by_parent` dict with:
  ```
  self._observed_cache: dict[str, list[EdgeEvidence]] = {}
  def _observed_children(self, parent_fen) -> list[EdgeEvidence]:
      hit = self._observed_cache.get(parent_fen)
      if hit is None:
          hit = (lookup_observed_edges_for_parent(self.db, self.batch_id, parent_fen)
                 if self.batch_id is not None else [])
          self._observed_cache[parent_fen] = hit
      return hit
  ```
- `_structural_children` (openings.py:938) calls `self._observed_children(norm_fen)` instead of
  `self._observed_by_parent.get(norm_fen, ())`. No other builder logic changes — structural
  shape, ordering, hydration, and sort are byte-for-byte identical given identical edges.
- `build()` reads positions via `lookup_position_scores_for_batch(self.db, self.batch_id,
  position_fens)` (no scheduler re-trigger) and sets `TreeResponse.batch_computed_at =
  self.batch_computed_at` (the pre-rollback scalar).

### 4. Single scheduler trigger in the route — BLOCK on a batch that lacks the edge read model
Extract the stale-while-revalidate trigger out of `load_tree_position_rows` so it fires ONCE,
and **distinguish "warm-fresh" (edges present) from "warm-stale / cold" (edge read model
absent)**. A pre-`edges-v1` batch exists but has ZERO `opening_position_edges`, so plain
stale-while-revalidate (`request_recompute` + serve) would render a book-only tree and silently
hide observed moves until a later read (Finding #1). Because `edges-v1` is folded into the
registry fingerprint (§5), a batch built before this deploy ALWAYS mismatches the current
registry fingerprint — that mismatch is exactly "edge read model may be missing," so on the
TREE path we upgrade registry/schema drift from background-revalidate to a BLOCKING refresh:

```
TREE_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT = 30.0  # generous: a heavy user's one-time post-deploy bootstrap pays
                               # the full overlay rebuild once, inline, so edges exist before serving.

def ensure_tree_cache(db, user_id, player_color, graph, roots) -> tuple[int | None, datetime | None]:
    current_registry = opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(graph, roots)
    batch = get_latest_opening_score_batch(db, user_id, player_color)
    warm_fresh = batch is not None and batch.registry_fingerprint == current_registry
    if warm_fresh:
        request_recompute(user_id, player_color)   # edges present; background revalidate evidence/decay
    else:
        # cold (no batch) OR registry/schema drift (e.g. predates edges-v1 => no edge rows):
        # block so the served tree has its observed edges. refresh_now is serialized through the
        # scheduler's single writer thread, so we do NOT call recompute on the request thread.
        refresh_now(user_id, player_color, timeout=TREE_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT)
        batch = get_latest_opening_score_batch(db, user_id, player_color)
    # Snapshot scalars BEFORE the caller's db.rollback() expires the ORM row (Finding #2).
    if batch is None:
        return None, None
    return batch.id, batch.computed_at
```
- If `refresh_now` still times out for a pathologically heavy user, the re-fetched batch may
  still be registry-stale (no edges). That is a rare one-time degraded read; `_observed_children`
  returns `[]` (book-only) for that single request, the background recompute finishes, and the
  next read is correct+fast. Log a WARNING (`tree_cache_bootstrap_timeout`) so it is visible.
  Trade-off accepted vs. silently serving a wrong tree on every warm read.
- Refactor `load_tree_position_rows` (opening_cache.py:422) into `ensure_tree_cache` +
  `lookup_position_scores_for_batch(db, batch_id, fens)` (its only caller is the tree builder,
  openings.py:1233). The new `_for_batch` reader takes a `batch_id: int` (not the ORM row) so the
  builder reuses the SAME batch the route resolved — no extra `get_latest_opening_score_batch`
  round-trip and no reliance on a possibly-expired ORM object.

### 4a. Finding #2 — never read an ORM batch field after `db.rollback()`
`SessionLocal` sets `expire_on_commit=False` (db.py:29), but **`db.rollback()` expires ALL
instances regardless** of that flag, so a later `batch.id` / `batch.computed_at` access during
`build()` would fire a surprise refresh SELECT (and could raise if the row were pruned
concurrently). Therefore the route captures `batch_id` and `batch_computed_at` as plain scalars
from `ensure_tree_cache` BEFORE the rollback, and the builder holds only those scalars (an
immutable `_TreeCacheCtx(batch_id, computed_at)`), never the ORM row. `batch_computed_at`
feeds `TreeResponse.batch_computed_at` (openings.py:1299); `batch_id` feeds the edge/position
lookups.

New `get_opening_tree` flow (openings.py:1369), with overlay_evidence REMOVED:
```
graph = get_opening_graph(); roots = get_opening_roots()
batch_id, batch_computed_at = ensure_tree_cache(db, user.user_id, player_color, graph, roots)  # only scheduler trigger
db.rollback()                                                # release conn before structural pass (unchanged intent)
builder = _OpeningTreeBuilder(db, graph, roots, batch_id, batch_computed_at, player_color, user.user_id)
response = builder.build(move, opening, timings=timings)     # edges via lazy point queries; positions via batch_id
```
Timing logs: replace `overlay_ms`/`overlay_nodes`/`overlay_edges`/`excluded_sessions` with
`ensure_cache_ms`, `cache_state` (`warm_fresh` | `bootstrapped` | `book_only`), and a new
`observed_edge_query_count`/`observed_edge_row_count` counter incremented inside
`_observed_children`. Keep `position_rows_ms`, `move_evals_ms`, `root_eval_ms`, `total_ms` and
the slow-request log. (The instrumentation scaffolding from the current uncommitted WIP diff
stays; only the overlay-specific fields change.)

### 5. Cache invalidation / migration of existing batches
Pre-existing batches have NO edge rows; a warm read against one would render book-only (wrong —
observed moves vanish). We cannot distinguish "no edges because user has none" from "old batch."
Force a one-time self-healing recompute by folding a new version token into the REGISTRY
fingerprint so every existing batch reports `registry_drift` and recomputes on first read:
- Add `OPENING_SCORE_CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION = "edges-v1"` and fold it into
  `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint` (opening_cache.py:81). Document it as "bump when the set of
  persisted batch read-model tables/columns changes."
- Effect: first read per (user,color) after deploy recomputes once, materializing edges. On the
  `/tree` path this is a BLOCKING bootstrap whenever the latest batch is registry-stale (§4,
  Finding #1) so observed moves are never hidden; the card-grid `/openings` path keeps its
  existing background revalidate (stale SCORES are tolerable there, unlike missing tree edges).
  The scheduler coalesces the thundering herd; this is the normal cost of a registry bump. No
  data backfill script required.
- The registry-fingerprint mismatch is therefore a single shared signal: it drives both the
  `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` recompute decision AND the `ensure_tree_cache`
  block-vs-serve decision, so they cannot disagree about whether a batch has edges.
- No change to `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` or `raw_evidence_inputs_digest`: evidence
  derivation is unchanged; `session_moves` already fully determine the edges, so the existing
  `inputs_fingerprint` correctly invalidates edges whenever they could change.

### 6. Cold / no-evidence path
`ensure_tree_cache` returns `(None, None)` when the user has no evidence (`refresh_now` →
`recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` returns None, no batch written). Builder gets
`batch_id=None` → `_observed_children` returns `[]` → book-only structural tree (matches existing
`test_tree_null_evidence_serves_structural_book_tree`). Cold WITH evidence: `refresh_now` runs
the single bounded bootstrap (same as today), materializing batch + edges + positions before
build.

### 7. SPEC.md (living design doc) update — required (Finding #3)
This adds a persisted read model and changes the `/api/openings/tree` hot path, so SPEC.md must
be updated alongside the code:
- Add **§5.7.5 `opening_position_edges` (Observed Tree Edges)** immediately after §5.7.4
  `opening_position_scores` (SPEC.md:567-604). Mirror that section's prose + `CREATE TABLE`
  block + index list + the generation-retention/cascade note. State that it is the sibling
  read model that supplies the OBSERVED move edges (structural shape + `traversal_count` /
  `live_attempts` / `live_passes` counters) the tree builder needs, persisted under the **same**
  `opening_score_batches` generation, keyed by `(batch_id, parent_fen, child_fen)`.
- In the same area (or §5.7 preamble), note that `/api/openings/tree` now serves observed
  edges from this table via bounded per-parent indexed lookups and **no longer rebuilds
  `overlay_evidence` on the request path**; warm-fresh batches serve immediately while a batch
  predating the read-model schema version blocks for a one-time bootstrap.
- Add `opening_position_edges` to the §5.7 table list / §5 Table of Contents if those enumerate
  the cache tables.

---

## Considered & rejected
- **JSON-blob of all edges on the batch row**: one read, but forces O(total edges≈7600)
  parse per request and loses the indexed by-parent bounded read. Rejected.
- **Load ALL batch edges in one query** (drop-in `EvidenceOverlay` shim, zero builder change):
  simplest, ~50–150ms for 7600 rows, but O(total observed edges), not "proportional to rendered
  nodes." Kept as a documented fallback if per-parent point-query latency ever disappoints; the
  lazy loader is preferred because it meets the bead's bounded-by-line/frontier target.
- **Pre-compute candidate parents up front + one IN-query**: frontier children depend on the
  edges themselves (chicken-and-egg one ply deep), so it can't be done purely from board/graph
  replay. Lazy memoized point-queries sidestep this cleanly.

## Risks / dependencies
- **g-9zoe appears already resolved — verify and close/update, NOT a blocker (Finding #5).**
  The new CASCADE FK needs `foreign_keys=ON` wherever batches are pruned. `app/db.py:18-26`
  now registers the SQLite connect-listener pragma on the main engine, and
  `opening_score_scheduler` runs the recompute on `app.db.SessionLocal`
  (opening_score_scheduler.py:44,71) — i.e. the same pragma-enabled engine — and conftest:39
  sets it for tests. So the orphan/rowid-collision failure mode g-9zoe tracks should no longer
  reproduce. Action: confirm with a cascade test (below) and, if green, close or update g-9zoe
  rather than blocking this work on it.
- **N+1 point queries**: bounded by visible line + frontier (≤ ~MAX_TREE_PLY line positions +
  their rendered children), each a sub-ms indexed lookup. If prod network RTT makes this matter,
  switch to the all-batch-edges fallback (one query). Instrument `observed_edge_query_count`.
- **Insert volume on recompute**: ≈7600 edge rows per batch, off the hot path (worker / cold
  bootstrap), same retention (keep 2) and cascade as position scores.

---

## Test coverage (bead acceptance)
Conftest: add `opening_position_edges` DDL.

`test_opening_cache.py` (write side):
- `recompute_opening_scores` persists one `OpeningPositionEdge` per `overlay.edges` with correct
  counters; row count matches `len(overlay.edges)`.
- Retention prune + FK cascade deletes edge rows with their batch (assert no orphans; exercises
  the PRAGMA/g-9zoe path).
- Registry bump (`edges-v1`) makes a pre-existing edgeless batch recompute (`registry_drift`).

`test_tree_api.py` (read side — migrate fixtures):
- Replace `patch("app.api.openings.overlay_evidence", return_value=overlay)` (lines 167, 695)
  with a patch of `app.api.openings.lookup_observed_edges_for_parent` that serves
  `overlay._observed_by_parent[parent_fen]` from the in-memory `_overlay(...)` fixtures. Keeps
  every existing structural/ordering/terminal assertion intact with minimal churn.
- WARM read does NOT call `overlay_evidence` (spy `patch(... overlay_evidence)` and assert
  `not called`) and issues only bounded per-parent edge lookups (assert
  `observed_edge_query_count` is bounded by line+frontier, not total edges).
- Observed off-book edge appears navigable from cache (port `test_tree_observed_off_book_edge_appears_navigable`).
- Observed in-book edge sets both flags from cache (port `test_tree_observed_in_book_edge_sets_both_flags`).
- User-turn ordering by `user_choice_count` and opponent-turn ordering by `encounter_count`
  driven by cached `live_attempts`/`traversal_count` (port lines 596/609).
- No-data / book-only when `batch is None` (port `test_tree_null_evidence_serves_structural_book_tree`).
- Stale/missing cache: missing batch → `refresh_now` materializes then serves; warm-fresh batch
  (registry matches) → `request_recompute` queued, cached edges served immediately without
  blocking.
- **Finding #1 regression — legacy edgeless batch does not serve book-only.** Seed a batch whose
  `registry_fingerprint` predates `edges-v1` (no `opening_position_edges` rows) plus
  `session_moves` that yield observed edges; assert `ensure_tree_cache` BLOCKS via `refresh_now`
  (not background) and the served tree includes the observed moves (not book-only). Also assert
  the WARM-fresh path does NOT block.
- **Finding #2 regression — no surprise query after rollback.** With a real persisted batch,
  assert the response `batch_computed_at` is populated and that `build()` issues no implicit
  ORM-refresh SELECT for the batch row after `db.rollback()` (e.g. the builder never holds the
  ORM `OpeningScoreBatch`; drive via the scalar `_TreeCacheCtx`).

`test_tree_api.py::test_tree_end_to_end_real_lookups` (line 668): convert to persist a real
batch + real edge rows (via `recompute_opening_scores` or a small `_persist_overlay_as_batch`
helper) and assert the route serves from cache with overlay_evidence un-called.

Run named modules in isolation (pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load), from `backend`
with the venv activated and a valid TMPDIR per AGENTS.md:
```
cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && \
TMPDIR=/Users/mvargas/src/ghostreplay/backend/.tmp \
pytest -p no:randomly test_opening_cache.py test_tree_api.py test_opening_score_scheduler.py
```

## Out of scope
Frontend unchanged (response shape, sorting, field names all preserved). The `/score` endpoint
(openings.py:610) keeps its own `overlay_evidence` call. StrictMode double-fetch dedup is a
separate frontend concern, not required here.
acceptance_criteria: Warm /api/openings/tree requests with an existing cache do not call overlay_evidence or reconstruct session board lines. Runtime for warm root and one-move tree requests is proportional to rendered nodes and indexed DB lookups, not total session_moves. Cold/no-cache behavior is explicit and covered by tests. Existing API response shape and sorting semantics remain unchanged. Tests cover warm cached tree evidence, stale/missing cache behavior, observed off-book edges, user/opponent sort counters, and no-data/book-only tree responses.

title: Non-blocking /opening reader: serve cached, recompute in background (Approach A)
description:
The /opening page is slow on every read — plain reloads AND every navigation down the opening tree — because all three read endpoints (/children, /families/scores, /families/{family}/scores) funnel through _load_cached_rows, which calls a BLOCKING refresh_now on every load. g-6zhp removed the ~2.6s python-chess overlay build on cache hits, but the read still pays the blocking scheduler round-trip plus the O(all session_moves) raw_evidence_inputs_digest each time.

Fix (Approach A): make the reader non-blocking (stale-while-revalidate). Serve the cached batch immediately and schedule a coalesced BACKGROUND recompute; the existing g-6zhp gate does the real content-based freshness check off the request path and rebuilds only when evidence changed. The only blocking path left is cold cache (no batch yet).

Approach B (block only when a recompute is genuinely owed, via a durable dirty cursor) was designed in full but REJECTED after four review rounds / ten findings — it requires a separate, exhaustively-covered, durable freshness signal (silent-staleness failure mode), and its read-your-writes is a multi-second block anyway. Full B design + rejection reasoning archived in docs/plans/g-v2tk-approach-b-rejected.md.

This bead now holds the description + reasoning for Approach A. The detailed implementation plan and tests are deferred to a later session. $'\n'
design:
APPROACH A — non-blocking reader. The detailed implementation plan is now included
below (it was previously deferred). Rejected alternative (Approach B, durable dirty
cursor) and its full rejection reasoning are archived in
docs/plans/g-v2tk-approach-b-rejected.md.

WHAT APPROACH A IS
------------------
Non-blocking, stale-while-revalidate reader. On a WARM cache, the reader serves the
currently-cached batch immediately and never blocks; it schedules a coalesced
BACKGROUND recompute via the existing debounced scheduler (request_recompute). The
existing g-6zhp gate (recompute_opening_scores_if_needed) runs the real,
content-based freshness check — raw evidence digest plus the registry-drift / decay
/ stale-branch-key gates — on the background worker thread, OFF the request path, and
rebuilds the batch only when evidence actually changed. The only synchronous
(blocking) path that remains is the COLD cache case (no batch yet), which must
compute an initial batch once.

Contrast with today: the reader currently calls refresh_now unconditionally, which
blocks the request thread on the scheduler round-trip plus the O(all session_moves)
raw_evidence_inputs_digest on every load. That is the cause of the slow plain reloads
and the slow navigation down the opening tree (all read endpoints funnel through the
same reader, and the cached batch is identical across navigations, so the per-click
blocking flush is pure redundancy). Approach A removes that blocking entirely for
warm reads.

WHY A OVER B (the rejected durable-cursor approach)
---------------------------------------------------
1. Silent-staleness failure mode. B is only correct if EVERY evidence-write surface
   bumps the durable signal. Miss one — including a future evidence source someone
   forgets to wire — and B serves wrong scores with no signal. The review already
   caught two missed surfaces (blunder creation, out-of-process scripts).
2. A sidesteps the whole class. A's background recompute reads REAL evidence via the
   content digest, so any evidence change is caught automatically — new/future
   sources, process restart, and out-of-process script writers all included. No
   write-surface audit, no durable cursor, no migration, no scheduler freshness
   machinery.
3. B's read-your-writes is a multi-second block anyway (~2.6s, bounded by the 5s
   refresh_now timeout). A shows prior scores instantly and converges on the next
   navigation — the better UX for a derived analytics metric.
4. The motivating feature doesn't need it. The planned "after a drill, show how it
   affected your opening score" screen is read-your-writes, but it should get a
   DEDICATED scoped/incremental endpoint, not force the generic reader synchronous.

THE ONE REAL TRADE-OFF A ACCEPTS
--------------------------------
Eventual consistency for post-write reads. After an evidence write (drill move,
blunder, review) the /opening read shows the previous batch until the background
recompute completes (debounce ~1.5s + recompute) and the client refetches. The
frontend does not poll today, so "refetches" effectively means the next navigation or
reload. Acceptable for a derived analytics metric. Registry drift after a deploy
converges the same way: first post-deploy warm read serves the old-registry batch,
the second is fresh.

WHY A IS CORRECT WITHOUT NEW MACHINERY
--------------------------------------
The background recompute reads real evidence via the content digest, so freshness,
durability, and write-surface coverage are all handled by the existing g-6zhp gate:
- New/future evidence sources: caught (digest reads the actual rows).
- Process restart: caught (next read schedules a background recompute).
- Out-of-process script writers: caught on the next read.
request_recompute on every warm read is load-bearing (NOT redundant): it is the
trigger that lets the gate catch evidence changes with no write-path enqueue
(out-of-process scripts, post-restart first read). Rapid navigation coalesces to
~one background recompute per 1.5s quiet window; the per-run cost on an unchanged
warm cache is just digest + fingerprint queries (no overlay), off the request path.

==========================================================================
DETAILED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (Approach A)
==========================================================================

SCOPE DECISION (confirmed with user): include the 4th read path,
get_session_openings in backend/app/api/session.py (~832), which has the identical
blocking refresh_now + list_cached pattern. All four opening read paths convert.

STEP 0 — persist this plan to the g-v2tk design field (done).

NEW SHARED READER — backend/app/opening_cache.py
------------------------------------------------
Add load_cached_rows here (natural home: it owns list_cached_opening_scores and
already imports opening_aggregate). Use a LAZY import of the scheduler funcs inside
the function body — opening_cache is imported BY opening_score_scheduler, so a
module-level import would cycle (scheduler -> opening_cache -> scheduler).

    def load_cached_rows(db, user_id, player_color):
        """Stale-while-revalidate reader.
        WARM (batch exists): serve cached batch + schedule coalesced BACKGROUND
        recompute (non-blocking). COLD (no batch): compute once synchronously.
        The g-6zhp gate inside the scheduler worker does the real content-based
        freshness check off the request path.
        """
        from app.opening_score_scheduler import refresh_now, request_recompute  # lazy: breaks cycle
        batch, rows = list_cached_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)
        if batch is None:
            refresh_now(user_id, player_color)            # COLD: bounded blocking compute
            batch, rows = list_cached_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)
        else:
            request_recompute(user_id, player_color)       # WARM: non-blocking convergence
        return batch, _snapshot_cached_rows(rows)

Extend the existing `from app.opening_aggregate import _batch_has_stale_branch_keys`
to also import `_snapshot_cached_rows, CachedOpeningScoreRow` (both already live

DATA-FLOW / CORRECTNESS NOTES

  endpoints already need) and ZERO request-thread work beyond enqueuing — no
  refresh_now, no digest, no overlay. This is the win.
- Cold path: one cheap get_latest_opening_score_batch (None, no row fetch), then

title: Build tree position-score read model
description: Implement the generation-scoped direct position-score read model for the opening tree. The persisted model is keyed by batch_id and normalized_fen and stores direct metrics for scoreable positions plus connected observed off-book positions; the tree read path covers static in-book positions by normalizing lookup FENs and treating absent in-graph rows as no-data without running compute_root_score once per visible card.
design:
Research spike result (2026-06-15), revised after review: choose full generation precompute for direct position metrics, but do NOT materialize static in-book no-data rows by default.

Algorithm:
- Keep `user_opening_scores` on its named-root contract. Add a sibling generation-scoped position read model under the same `opening_score_batches` generation/fingerprints, keyed by `(batch_id, normalized_fen)`, for direct tree-node metrics.
- Persist only rows that the database actually needs: positions with mastery evidence at or below the FEN (`has_mastery_below` / `has_evidence`) plus connected observed off-book positions. Static in-book positions with no evidence below are already represented by `OpeningGraph`; the API can return no-data for an in-graph FEN that is absent from the position batch. Do not write one row per book-domain FEN unless the build bead first measures row count, insert time, storage, and retention cost and justifies full structural materialization against the static-graph alternative.
- Build one `_SharedCalculator(player_color, graph, overlay, roots, RootCalcConfig(), computed_at)` per recompute. Use the existing seed set (`graph.root_fen` plus all named root keys). Its domain already walks `_structural_children`, which unions reference book children with observed overlay edges and applies the SCC cut before scoring.
- Add a rootcalc API such as `compute_position_scores(...)` or a calculator method that iterates the selected scorer domain, calls `_calc(fen, False)` and `_calc(fen, True)` for scoreable FENs, and derives direct `opening_score`, `confidence`, `coverage`, and `weighted_depth` from the same formulas as `_base_root_score`. Because `_metrics` is keyed by `(fen, perfect)`, this is still one shared memoized traversal: at most two metric records per reachable FEN, not one root walk per visible card.
- Extract the metadata aggregation currently embedded in `_base_root_score` into a helper usable by both named-root rows and arbitrary position rows: structural reachable set -> `sample_size` as summed `quality_count`, `game_count` as unioned `session_ids`, and `last_practiced_at` as max live/review touch. Branch summaries remain named-root-only unless a later UI asks for per-position branch cards.
- Score visibility must be gated by mastery evidence below the FEN, regardless of side to move. A no-evidence user-turn row must not surface the alpha/beta prior, and a no-evidence opponent-turn leaf must not surface `_calc`'s perfect-looking `(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)` result. No evidence below means no-data.

Fallback, lookup, and invalidation:
- Primary path is full batch precompute of the selected rows. Tree API reads direct rows from the latest batch and must not call `compute_root_score` once per visible card.
- API inputs may be raw FENs from the tree UI. Normalize every incoming FEN before lookup; otherwise transpositions and halfmove/fullmove differences silently miss rows.
- If a normalized FEN is in `OpeningGraph` but absent from the latest position batch, return no-data from the API layer. This is the expected representation for static in-book no-evidence nodes.
- If a normalized FEN is not in `OpeningGraph` and absent from the latest position batch, treat it as outside the current connected observed scorer domain and return no-data. If fingerprints drifted, serve stale/no-data for that request and let the existing scheduler recompute a new generation.
- A lazy exact-FEN computation is acceptable only as a non-persisted debug/development fallback, or if it reserves a fresh generation with the matching raw-input fingerprint; otherwise it can persist rows against stale inputs and break cache invalidation.
- Existing invalidation surfaces remain sufficient: `opening_score_batches.registry_fingerprint`, `inputs_fingerprint`, `SCORE_MODEL_VERSION`, `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION`, divider/quality versions, and raw evidence digest. Adding position rows should reuse the same generation so named and direct metrics cannot disagree.

Required schema/cache changes:
- Add a position-score table with `batch_id` as a foreign key to `opening_score_batches(id)` using `ON DELETE CASCADE`, matching `user_opening_scores`. `prune_old_opening_score_batches` must therefore prune position rows through the same generation-retention path; otherwise direct rows leak unbounded across recomputes.
- Index for the read path should include `(batch_id, normalized_fen)` and any query shape the tree API uses. Keep `normalized_fen` explicit in the model name/column contract.
- Row-volume guardrail: record persisted row count per recompute. If the implementation elects to persist all structural rows anyway, measure and document rows per batch, insert duration, storage per batch, and keep=2 retention impact for both colors before landing.

Required `opening_rootcalc` changes:
- Add a `PositionScore`/direct-row DTO and a public `compute_position_scores` path that exposes selected direct scorer rows without requiring `roots.get_root(opening_key)`.
- Share one calculator instance between named-root row generation and position-row generation, so the named rows, synthetic repertoire row, and direct FEN rows reuse the same `_metrics`, SCC cut, weights, and reachable caches.
- Factor root metadata aggregation out of `_base_root_score`; keep transposition-safe reachable-set semantics for sample and distinct-game counts.
- Add telemetry for `domain_count`, `scoreable_position_count`, `observed_off_book_row_count`, metric key counts, reachable membership count, persisted row count, insert duration, and timings so the batch builder can log drift if user evidence grows beyond the measured range.

Required `opening_evidence` changes:
- No production blocker found in the current overlay semantics. `_collect_session_moves` already records phase-valid book exits and follows observed continuations after book boundary; `overlay.edges` endpoints are enough for `_structural_children` to stitch off-book nodes into the child graph.
- Add a small helper or explicit contract for observed scorer positions: derive them from `overlay.edges` endpoints that are not in `OpeningGraph`, plus any overlay node reachable through those edges. The calculator should not need `OpeningGraphNode` instances for off-book FENs; `active_color(fen)` is enough.
- Do not seed disconnected off-book blunders/reviews. `_collect_ghost_targets` and `_collect_reviews` currently ignore off-book positions unless they already exist in overlay nodes; keep that behavior for this build. If manual off-book targets with no observed path must become scoreable later, that requires a separate path-materialization design.

Off-book scorer seed semantics:
- Start seeds stay as book root plus named roots. Phase-valid observed off-book positions enter the scoring domain only by reachable `overlay.edges`: book boundary exit -> observed continuation -> further observed continuation until the phase-filtered move rows stop. This keeps direct rows aligned with navigable tree data and avoids disconnected FEN rows.
- Connected observed off-book positions should get persisted direct rows so the API can distinguish navigable observed off-book nodes from arbitrary unknown FENs. Metrics remain no-data unless quality exists at or below that connected subtree.

Sizing evidence from the spike:
- Local benchmark against the real cached graph on 2026-06-15: graph load about 1.0s; `graph_nodes=15,511`, `graph_edges=15,870`, `named_roots=11,274`.
- Baseline sparse overlay: calculator domain `15,202`; setup `2.96s`; forcing direct actual+perfect metrics for every domain FEN `0.59s`; memo keys `30,404`; current reachable metadata pass `0.43s`; reachable-cache memberships `248,880`.
- Synthetic observed-overlay stress with 1,200 legal observed edges and 1,102 off-book domain FENs: domain `16,304`; setup `3.16s`; full direct metric pass `0.56s`; reachable memberships `271,751`.
- Tracemalloc around calculator-side caches for the synthetic observed run peaked at about `36.8 MB` after graph/roots load. Tracemalloc inflated timings (`init 10.64s`, metrics `1.51s`, reachable `0.40s`), so use the non-traced timing run for CPU sizing and the traced run for memory sizing.
- The previous spike did not measure database row-volume/write/storage cost for 15k structural rows per batch. This review changes the default persistence strategy to avoid that cost. If full structural materialization is reintroduced, it must be benchmarked explicitly before build acceptance.
- Complexity: metric generation is `O(V + E)` per actual/perfect pass with memoization and the existing SCC cut, so roughly `2 * domain_fens` metric entries. Metadata via current reachable-set caching is `O(sum(|reachable(fen)|))`; measured membership counts are far below an `O(V^2)` danger zone for the current 15.5k-book-node graph plus 1.2k observed-edge stress. The build bead should add logging/guardrails, but full metric precompute is comfortably sized for the current product scale; persistence should stay sparse unless proven otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Adds schema/model/repository support for the position-score read model; computes rows from one shared traversal or the approved lazy fallback; persists only evidence-bearing score rows plus connected observed off-book rows unless full structural materialization is separately benchmarked and justified; handles observed off-book scorer domains; preserves distinct game count semantics; cascades position rows through opening_score_batches retention; normalizes raw API FENs before lookup; backend tests cover direct metrics, null evidence/no-data gating, transpositions, phase-boundary inclusion, absent in-graph rows, and no per-child independent root scoring; SPEC.md documents the read-model contract.
close_reason: Implemented generation-scoped direct position-score read model: opening_position_scores table + migration, compute_position_scores shared-calculator path, observed off-book handling, normalized-FEN lookup, batch-retention cascade, SPEC.md contract. Full backend suite green (1009 passed).

title: Fix drill stalls from stale async work
description: Drill mode can get stuck on Waiting for opponent while stale async analysis/upload work from prior drill sessions continues to POST /session/{id}/moves for minutes. Investigate the drill opponent/session lifecycle, guard stale results, and prevent old sessions from mutating or blocking current gameplay.
design: Trace data flow from drill start/restart through opponent move selection, analysis outcomes, and session move upload. Add session/generation guards where async results can outlive their initiating session. Keep stale backend/upload responses from applying to the active board or UI, and add focused tests around drill restart/stale request behavior rather than layout-specific assertions.
notes: Review follow-up: confirmed natural-end intentionally discards any resolved but unsent upload tail for unconverted drills; added an explicit lifecycle comment. Broadened backend late-upload guard from abandoned-only to abandoned OR any ended non-converted drill, so natural-end late uploads keep raw move upserts but skip graph/opportunity/cache/recompute side effects. title: Fix slow /opening load: cheap SQL freshness gate for opening-score cache
description:
## Problem

Every `/opening` page load is much slower under opening-score v2. The page makes one `GET /api/openings/children` call; the reader (`_load_cached_rows`, app/api/openings.py:230) calls `refresh_now(user_id, player_color)`, which BLOCKS the request (up to ~5s) while the scheduler worker runs `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` (app/opening_cache.py:472).

## Root cause

To answer "did anything change since the cached batch?", `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` computes a CONTENT fingerprint that is hashed over the FULLY BUILT evidence overlay:

    overlay = overlay_evidence(...)                      # built UNCONDITIONALLY (line ~490)
    fingerprint = opening_score_evidence_fingerprint(overlay, ...)   # line ~491
    ...
    if not drift and not stale_branch_keys and batch.inputs_fingerprint == fingerprint:
        return batch                                     # cache hit — but overlay already built

So the overlay is rebuilt on EVERY load, even when nothing changed and we are about to serve the cached batch.

In v2 the overlay build is expensive: `overlay_evidence` now reconstructs every session's board line with python-chess and runs the exact Lichess phase divider per session (app/opening_evidence.py:290-311: `reconstruct_board_sequence` + `divide`), plus `_uci_from_san` re-parsing in passes 2/3. v1 did NONE of this — it only counted `eval_delta` pass/fail from SQL rows (python-chess was used lazily only for book-exit moves).

## Evidence (measured)

Just the `reconstruct_board_sequence + divide` step, 200 sessions x 30 plies: ~2598 ms (~13 ms/session). Real cost is higher (uci_from_san, normalize_fen, quality). For a user with a couple hundred analyzed games, every `/opening` load blocks ~2.6s+ purely to recompute a fingerprint and conclude "nothing changed."

Confirmed regression boundary: pre-v2 `overlay_evidence` (509ab64^) had no per-session board reconstruction or divider; v2 added both, and they run on the read path because the freshness check requires the built overlay and `refresh_now` blocks on it.

## Fix (chosen approach)

Replace the overlay-OUTPUT content fingerprint with a cheap raw-INPUT SQL fingerprint computed without python-chess. Build the overlay only when that digest actually differs. Preserves exact synchronous read-your-writes freshness; unchanged loads drop from ~2.6s to ~10ms. Non-blocking-reader (stale-while-revalidate) is explicitly deferred — revisit only if true post-write recomputes are still too slow for UX.

Scope is contained to app/opening_cache.py (+ a digest helper). The `inputs_fingerprint` column already exists (models.py:365) so NO migration is needed.

Parent epic: g-opening-score-v2.
design:
## Design: cheap SQL freshness gate

### Principle
`overlay_evidence` is a pure deterministic function of a fixed set of raw DB rows + graph/roots/config/version constants. Same inputs -> identical overlay -> identical scores. Therefore "did anything change?" can be answered by hashing the INPUTS to the derivation (cheap SQL, zero board work) instead of the OUTPUT of the derivation (which today forces the ~2.6s python-chess replay first). If the input hash matches the value stored on the batch AND the registry fingerprint matches, the overlay is provably identical, so we serve the cached batch and never build the overlay.

### New helper: `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint(db, user_id, player_color) -> str`
Hashes a canonical, deterministically ORDERED projection of exactly the raw rows `overlay_evidence` reads, and nothing else. No python-chess, no overlay. Pull scalar columns and sha256 in Python (dialect-agnostic; the expensive part was always the board replay, not the SQL fetch or hashing — a few ms for thousands of rows).

Tables/columns to digest (traced against app/opening_evidence.py):
1. session_moves JOIN game_sessions (_build_move_rows:262) — session_id, move_number, color, fen_before, fen_after, move_san, eval_delta, eval_cp, best_move_eval_cp, started_at; filters: gs.user_id, gs.player_color, sm.fen_before IS NOT NULL, gs.session_mode IN ('normal','drill'). This is the SAME query the overlay already runs — we hash scalar columns and stop instead of replaying boards.
2. analysis_cache (the fallback, _apply_cache_fallbacks:368) — fen_before, move_uci, played_eval, played_eval_mate, best_eval, best_eval_mate; restricted to fen_before values appearing in THIS user's session moves that lack primary evals (eval_cp IS NULL OR best_move_eval_cp IS NULL). Bounded join, NOT the whole global cache table. Broader scoping is safe (worst case: an unnecessary rebuild, still correct) — never narrower (would miss a change).
3. blunders JOIN positions (_collect_ghost_targets:471) — p.fen_raw; same user/color/mode filter (note OR (source_session_id IS NULL AND p.active_color=:color)).
4. blunder_reviews JOIN blunders JOIN positions (_collect_reviews:499) — p.fen_raw, br.passed, br.reviewed_at; same filter.

Determinism: ORDER BY a stable key (or sort the projected tuples) before hashing.

### CRITICAL: explicit evidence-logic version (caveat from review)
A raw-row hash is blind to SEMANTIC changes in the derivation code that change the derived overlay WITHOUT changing any raw row — e.g. PASS_THRESHOLD (app/opening_evidence.py:44; feeds edge.live_passes -> `_prepared_children` selection/weights), fallback PRECEDENCE/ordering in `_apply_cache_fallbacks`, `normalize_fen` behavior, how the divider/phase filter is applied in `_build_move_rows` / `is_opening_premove`, and the digest's own column set/filters. The current overlay-output hash catches these implicitly because the derived counters change; the raw-input hash will NOT.

Mitigation: introduce `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION = "raw-v1"` in app/opening_evidence.py (next to the logic it tracks) and fold it into the raw fingerprint. The raw fingerprint is composed as:

    raw_fp = sha256( opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(graph, roots)   # registry/config/scoring/divider/quality versions (existing)
                     + "|" + OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION          # evidence-derivation logic version (NEW)
                     + "|" + <ordered raw-row projection> )

Document a BUMP DISCIPLINE comment on the constant: bump `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` on ANY change to evidence-derivation semantics, including: PASS_THRESHOLD; quality-source precedence/ordering; normalization behavior; phase-filter / divider application; the SQL projection or filters in the digest; or the set of columns the overlay consumes. (DIVIDER_VERSION, QUALITY_VERSION, TAU_WC, TAU_CP, SCORE_MODEL_VERSION already live in `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint` and remain there.)

Note: some semantic surfaces are ALREADY covered by `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint` (divider version, quality params, model version). `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` covers the residual opening_evidence.py logic those constants do not, plus the digest contract itself.

### Wiring in recompute_opening_scores_if_needed (app/opening_cache.py:472)
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    graph = get_opening_graph(); roots = get_opening_roots()
    registry_fp = opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(graph, roots)
    raw_fp = opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint(db, user_id, player_color)   # NEW: cheap, no overlay
    batch, rows = list_cached_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)

    if batch is None:
        if not has_opening_evidence(db, user_id, player_color):
            return None
        overlay = overlay_evidence(db, user_id, player_color, graph)           # build only on miss
        return recompute_opening_scores(..., overlay=overlay, inputs_fingerprint=raw_fp, computed_at=now)

    registry_drift = batch.registry_fingerprint != registry_fp
    stale_branch_keys = _batch_has_stale_branch_keys(rows)
    if not registry_drift and not stale_branch_keys and batch.inputs_fingerprint == raw_fp:
        if not <stale_for_decay(batch, now)>:
            return batch                                                       # FAST PATH — overlay never built

    overlay = overlay_evidence(db, user_id, player_color, graph)               # change/drift/stale path only
    return recompute_opening_scores(..., overlay=overlay, inputs_fingerprint=raw_fp, computed_at=now)

Key changes vs. today:
- Do NOT call overlay_evidence at the top unconditionally. Compute raw_fp first; build overlay only on the non-fast paths.
- `recompute_opening_scores` (app/opening_cache.py:361): its default `inputs_fingerprint` (currently `opening_score_evidence_fingerprint(overlay, graph, roots)` at line 379) switches to the raw digest, so direct callers (`ensure_opening_scores`, line 468) stay consistent. Pass raw_fp explicitly from the if_needed path.
- Keep the existing time-decay recompute (OPENING_SCORE_DECAY_RECOMPUTE_INTERVAL, once/day) — it intentionally re-ages confidence/coverage even when raw inputs are unchanged. The gate does not change that.
- `opening_score_evidence_fingerprint` (the overlay-output hash, line 68) becomes unused by the hot path; remove it or retain only if a test references it (prefer remove + update tests).
- No change to the scheduler or `refresh_now`. On the fast path the worker returns quickly, so `refresh_now` returns True fast.
- The debug-only POST `/api/openings/score` (compute_opening_score, api/openings.py:557) builds the overlay directly and is not on the hot path — leave it.

### Drift-safety note
The digest's projection + filters MUST exactly mirror what `overlay_evidence` consumes. To reduce drift risk, keep the digest query in the same module as / adjacent to the overlay queries (or share the column list), and the bump discipline above treats "overlay consumed columns changed" as a version bump trigger.

### Correctness argument
raw_fp unchanged AND registry_fp unchanged  =>  inputs unchanged  =>  overlay unchanged  =>  scores unchanged. The fast path can never serve stale scores. When evidence actually changes, raw_fp differs and we rebuild + recompute exactly as today (read-your-writes preserved). A digest false-negative (digest changes when nothing relevant did) only causes an unnecessary rebuild (still correct); the design avoids false-positives (missing a real change) by covering all inputs + the logic version.

### Rollout / migration
No schema migration — reuse the text `inputs_fingerprint` column (models.py:365). On first read after deploy, the stored value (old overlay-hash format) will not match the new raw digest -> exactly one self-healing recompute per (user, color) -> fast thereafter. Same self-heal mechanism the version bumps already rely on; introducing OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION="raw-v1" doubles as the transition marker.

### Test plan
- raw_fp flips (=> recompute) on each input change: in-place eval_delta mutation; in-place eval_cp/best_move_eval_cp mutation; new session_move; new blunder_review; new ghost target; a consulted analysis_cache row appearing/changing.
- raw_fp flips when OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION changes (semantic-version guard).
- raw_fp flips when registry/config/divider/quality versions change (still covered).
- Fast path does NOT build the overlay: patch/spy `overlay_evidence` and assert it is NOT called when nothing changed; assert it IS called on a real change / cache miss / registry drift / stale-branch-keys / decay-stale.
- Determinism: raw_fp stable across repeated calls and independent of row return order.
- analysis_cache scoping: a cache row for an UNrelated fen (not in this user's null-eval session positions) does not need to flip raw_fp (acceptable either way, but assert relevant ones do).
- End-to-end: two consecutive `/api/openings/children` calls with no evidence change — second serves cached batch without rebuilding overlay (timing or spy assertion).
- Run backend focused tests for opening_cache + opening_evidence + openings API; rerun named files in isolation if the pre-push suite flakes under parallel load.
acceptance_criteria:
- A cheap `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` exists that computes a freshness digest from raw DB rows with NO python-chess / no overlay build.
- The digest covers all overlay inputs: session_moves(+game_sessions), the analysis_cache fallback subset, blunders/positions ghost targets, blunder_reviews.
- An explicit `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` (e.g. "raw-v1") is folded into the stored fingerprint, with a documented bump-discipline covering PASS_THRESHOLD, fallback precedence, normalization, phase-filter application, and the digest column/filter contract.
- `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` does NOT build the overlay on the cache-hit fast path; it builds it only on cache miss, registry drift, stale branch keys, raw-digest change, or decay-staleness.
- Synchronous read-your-writes freshness is preserved: a real evidence change still triggers rebuild + recompute on the next read.
- No DB migration (reuse inputs_fingerprint); first read after deploy self-heals with one recompute per (user,color).
- Unchanged `/opening` loads no longer pay the per-session board-reconstruction/divider cost (verified by spying overlay_evidence and/or timing).
- Tests pass: raw_fp flips on each input + version change; fast path skips overlay; backend focused opening tests green.
close_reason: Implemented cheap SQL raw-input freshness digest; fast path skips overlay build on cache hit. Tests + SPEC updated. Commit e0ebd5f.

title: Exactly-once context-correct recording & SRS via outcome channel (F4)
description: Split from g-cache-first-resolve (Finding F4 + Outcome channel API). Under buffered cache-first resolution, a cache batch can resolve two indices synchronously, overwriting lastAnalysis twice before the React recording effect runs — skipping an intermediate blunder and mis-pairing context. Replace the lastAnalysis-driven recording/SRS/alert effects with a typed AnalysisOutcome channel: SRS immediate, recording via a terminal-aware ordered frontier (reusing shouldRecordBlunder), blunder alert microtask-coalesced latest-only. Decision state stays in React refs (durable relocation is g-h94q).
design:
# g-hpw4 — Execution Plan: Exactly-once outcome channel for recording & SRS

## Context

Scope-A (`g-cache-first-resolve`, closed) made one indexed `AnalysisResult` authoritative,
buffering worker output behind cache resolution. But the React recording/SRS/alert consumers
still read a single latest-only `lastAnalysis` value plus one mutable
`pendingAnalysisContextRef` (`AnalysisEffects.tsx:63,75-116,222,238`;
`useChessGameController.ts:237`). Under buffered cache-first resolution a single cache batch
can resolve two indices **synchronously**, overwriting `lastAnalysis` twice before any React
effect runs — so an intermediate player blunder is skipped and the surviving value is paired
with the wrong move's context (Finding F4). This bead replaces those effects with a typed
`AnalysisOutcome` channel and a terminal-aware ordered recording frontier, keyed by
`requestId`, so recording/SRS/alert are each exactly-once and context-correct.

**The full design (semantics, every finding, every edge case) is the authoritative spec:**
`docs/plans/g-outcome-recording.md`. This file is the ordered execution sequence for it.
Decision state stays in React refs; durable relocation/reducer/outbox/backend idempotency are
deferred to **g-h94q** (which this blocks).

Verified against current code: emission points (`analyzeMove:388`, `resolveAnalysisResult:824`,
`releaseFallback:774`, `failRequest:802`), `latestRequestIds:182`, `sessionGeneration:202`,
`activeSessionId:201`, the `analysisResolvedListeners` fan-out (`:212,223,855,1096`), and the
consumer registration (`useChessGameController.ts:145,221,237`) all exist as the doc assumes.

## Approach

Build the coordinator channel first (additive, alongside the legacy listener), migrate the React
consumer onto it, then **remove the legacy `lastAnalysis` recording/SRS/alert path** so nothing
double-fires. Land it in testable layers; run named vitest files in isolation (pre-push suite is
flaky under parallel load).

### Step 1 — Coordinator: AnalysisOutcome channel (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`)
- Add the `AnalysisOutcome`/`AnalysisOutcomeStatus` types and a single `emitOutcome` fan-out
  stamping current `generation`/`sessionId` (+ forward-compat `seq`, undrained here).
- `addAnalysisOutcomeListener` / private `emitOutcome`; **delete** `analysisResolvedListeners` +
  `addAnalysisResolvedListener` (`:212,223,855,1096`) — one channel, no dual fan-out.
- Wire emission points: `analyzeMove`→`scheduled` (with `previousRequestId`), `resolveAnalysisResult`
  →`resolved` (carries `result`), `releaseFallback` reject + `failRequest`→`failed`,
  same-generation termination (restart/fatal/`clearAnalysis`)→`failed` per unresolved index.
- `markSkipped(moveIndex, requestId)`→`skipped`, guarded against double emission.

### Step 2 — Coordinator: supersession lineage + lifecycle APIs
- Add `lastRequestIdByMoveIndex: Map<number,string>` (L3): set on every `scheduled` and in
  `markSkipped`; **preserved** across same-generation `failed` cleanup; cleared on
  session reset / revert-prune / `destroy`. Source `previousRequestId` from it (then overwrite).
- `getEpoch()` synchronous `{generation, sessionId}` snapshot (M3).
- `addAnalysisResetListener` / private `emitReset()` — call **synchronously** in
  `startSession`/`clearSession` immediately after the generation bump (`:305-306,346-347`),
  before clearing pending requests (K1/K4). Effects are too late (microtasks run first).
- `pruneFromMoveIndex(k)` outcome/lineage side (M1): for indices `>= k` cancel/clear requests,
  waiters, cache/timer state, analyses, lineage; move pruned ids into a
  `discardedRequestIds: Set` tombstone (N1) that the worker `analysis`/`-started`/`-streaming`
  handlers (`:552,566,593`) check FIRST and drop; clear tombstones on worker replacement.

### Step 3 — Controller registration (`useChessGameController.ts`)
- Key `BlunderContext` + pending SRS by `committed.analysisId` (already H2-shaped at `:221,237`)
  into a `Map<requestId, BlunderContext>` (replacing the single `pendingAnalysisContextRef`).
- Reorder `commitAppliedMove` so context is written **before** the synchronous `markSkipped`
  call when `analyzeMove()` returns `undefined`/synthetic id (K3).
- Mint a stable `srsDecisionId` (uuid) at SRS registration (`:221`), carried across retries
  unchanged (forward-prep for g-h94q; no backend change).

### Step 4 — Consumer rewrite (`AnalysisEffects.tsx`) — the core of the bead
Single `addAnalysisOutcomeListener` subscription in one `useEffect`, seeding `currentGeneration`
from `getEpoch()` at registration (M3), dropping stale-generation outcomes:
- **(a) SRS — immediate:** per `resolved`, run existing `processSrsReview` (`:118`) directly;
  NOT gated by the frontier or `committedDecisionIndex` (I3/N2).
- **(b) Recording — terminal-aware frontier:** slots `{requestId, status}`;
  `nextDecisionIndex` advances across every terminal (`resolved|failed|skipped`), blocks on
  `pending`. Only `resolved` are candidates, run through existing `shouldRecordBlunder`
  (`utils/blunder.ts:56`) + `recordBlunder` with the **snapshotted** context and the
  **snapshotted** `isGameActive && !isPracticeContinuation` composite (Finding 5). `scheduled`
  reopens/rewinds the display frontier + migrates context & pending-SRS old→new id (one-shot,
  delete old); irreversible recording uses a separate monotonic `committedDecisionIndex` that
  never reopens (M2).
- **(c) Alert/audio — latest-only microtask coalesce:** buffer player-blunder outcomes,
  `queueMicrotask(flushAlert)`; flush picks highest moveIndex → one `setBlunderAlert`/flash +
  one `playRandomBlunderAudio`; `alertEpoch` recheck bails on intervening reset (K2).
- `addAnalysisResetListener` handler: clear frontier/context/alert maps, bump `alertEpoch`.
- **Remove** the legacy `lastAnalysis` recording effect (`:75-116`), SRS effects (`:216-235`),
  and alert effects (`:238-`). `lastAnalysis` stays only for board display + variation resolution.

### Step 5 — Revert/reset wiring (`useChessGameLifecycle.ts`)
- Call `coordinator.pruneFromMoveIndex(newHistory.length)` synchronously inside
  `rewindBoardLocally` (~`:348`), next to the existing `prunePendingSrsReviewsFromMoveIndex`.
- Prune-on-revert / clear-on-reset the `Map<requestId, BlunderContext>` (H2).

## Files to modify
- `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` (Steps 1–2)
- `src/hooks/useChessGameController.ts` (Step 3)
- `src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.tsx` (Step 4)
- `src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts` (Step 5)
- Tests: `GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts`, `AnalysisEffects.test.tsx`,
  `useChessGameController.test.ts`, `useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts`, `ChessGame.test.tsx`

## Verification (acceptance criteria 8–10)
Implement the doc's full test matrix (17e, 17e-2, 17f, 17g, 17h, 17h-2..17h-14, 17i, 19, 20).
Highest-signal cases: 17e (batched two-index recording, own context), 17h/17h-2 (latest-only
alert + coalesce boundary), 17h-8/9 (supersession block + retry context migration),
17h-11 (monotonic commit boundary), 20 (consumers migrated OFF `lastAnalysis` — old path
asserted gone, not left alongside). Run each file in isolation:
```
npx vitest run src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts
npx vitest run src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.test.tsx
npx vitest run src/hooks/useChessGameController.test.ts
npx vitest run src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts
npx vitest run src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx
```
Then `npx tsc --noEmit`. Treat a parallel-suite failure as suspect until reproduced in isolation.

## Out of scope → g-h94q
Coordinator-lifetime decision-owner relocation, reducer/outbox, SRS write ordering, on-the-wire
idempotency keys + backend unique-constraint migration, unmount durability/replay.
acceptance_criteria: 8. Regular-game classification/recording and SRS pass/fail consume the single published result exactly once. 9. Session upload and post-game state retain the same best move, delta, and classification that drove live behavior. 10. Tests vary source completion order and assert stable recording and SRS outcomes (tests 17e,17e-2,17f,17g,17h,17h-2..17h-14,17i,19,20). Recording/SRS/alert consumers are migrated OFF the legacy lastAnalysis effect onto addAnalysisOutcomeListener (old path removed, not left alongside).
close_reason: Implemented exactly-once context-correct recording & SRS via typed AnalysisOutcome channel; terminal-aware recording frontier + monotonic commit boundary; microtask-coalesced alert; lineage/tombstone/prune lifecycle. All 172 targeted tests pass, app project typechecks.

title: Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys on main SQLite engine (opening-score batch UNIQUE crash)
description: prune_old_opening_score_batches relies on ON DELETE CASCADE for user_opening_scores.batch_id, but app/db.py never sets PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, so SQLite ignores the cascade. Deleting a batch orphans its score rows; SQLite reuses the freed rowid for a new batch, whose rows then collide on (batch_id, opening_key) -> IntegrityError spam (stuck batch_id=4). Fix: set PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on connect for sqlite, plus clean existing orphan rows.

Cascade fix is effective; safe to close.
