title: Repair analysis cache and verify all outcomes
description:
## Objective
Repair contaminated/incomplete analysis evidence and verify stable end-to-end behavior across drills, regular-game blunder detection/recording, SRS grading, persistence, and post-game review.

## Current Problem
Existing analysis_cache rows may be game-overwritten depth-17 results or incomplete legacy precompute rows. Even after code fixes, they can preserve unstable best moves, deltas, and classifications. That can alter pass/fail at any drill threshold, whether a regular-game mistake is recorded, whether an SRS response passes, and what post-game analysis displays.

## Scope
- Build a safe idempotent/resumable backfill for canonical opening rows after metadata/comparator and canonical-precompute support are deployed.
- Identify legacy/untrusted/incomplete/lower-quality rows through profile metadata and completeness checks; replace or invalidate them explicitly.
- Run canonical precompute for required opening coverage.
- Add integration regressions that vary cache/worker completion order and assert:
  - repeated Polish Opening drill attempts are stable
  - strict, standard, lenient, and custom threshold outcomes are stable
  - regular-game classification and first-auto-record behavior are stable around thresholds
  - SRS pass/fail and pass_streak/review counters are stable and exactly once
  - live result, session_moves, cache lookup, and post-game display agree
- Add metrics/logging for profile selection, canonical hits, incomplete/untrusted rows, fallback use, accepted/rejected writes, and downstream decision category.
- Update SPEC.md analysis-cache, blunder detection/recording, SRS, session analysis, and drill sections.
- Document deployment order and rollback.

## Deployment Order
1. Deploy quality metadata and comparator.
2. Deploy complete canonical opening analysis.
3. Deploy authoritative indexed-move arbitration and deterministic downstream decisions.
4. Regenerate/invalidate legacy rows.
5. Monitor all decision paths.
Regenerating before write protection is active is unsafe.
design: Backfill must support dry-run/count, resumability, and verification without deleting unrelated coverage. Regression tests should control promise/message order rather than real timing and assert behavioral contracts, DB/SRS state, and persistence consistency rather than cosmetic UI details. Include threshold values immediately below, equal to, and above each relevant boundary.

6. SRS pass/fail and scheduling counters are stable and applied exactly once.

title: Define deterministic grading and blunder decisions
description:
## Objective
Make browser fallback analysis reproducible and ensure threshold-based decisions use authoritative eval_delta consistently across drill accuracy, regular-game classification/auto-recording, and SRS pass/fail.

## Current Problem
analysisWorker.ts reuses Stockfish across independent positions with no ucinewgame/isready boundary, so eval is not reproducible within long-lived workers. Unstable output can cross any downstream threshold. Separately, drill and SRS use inconsistent comparators/clamping, classification differs by resolution source (worker win-chance vs legacy delta-band cache fallback), null evals are conflated with passes, and trusted-cache acceptance is too loose.

## Scope (see Design for full plan)
- Per-request engine reset (ucinewgame+isready) once at the start of analyzeMove, never between the 3 related searches; reject/clear the readyok waiter on cancel/error/timeout/terminate.
- TWO separate comparators via shared evalLoss helper: drill `evalLoss > strictnessCp` (boundary passes); recording/SRS `evalLoss >= 50` (inclusive, matches backend). Do NOT merge into one threshold.
- Tri-state grading pass|fail|unavailable; unavailable routes to drill recovery and to a no-op (no post, no delete) for SRS.
- Tighten cache trust: local-build guards require a valid MoveClassification + finite, non-negative eval_delta. The trust decision is backend-computed — the lookup response exposes contract_satisfied + trusted_for_resolution, and frontend isTrustedCacheHit checks trusted_for_resolution===true (no TS reimplementation of the V2 validator; backend owns FEN/POV/delta consistency).
- 0cp passes any threshold regardless of best_move_uci equality.
- Mark non-canonical worker results in the worker message + diagnostics only.

## Non-Goals
- Exactly-once mutation, SRS retry + analysis-ID migration, lastAnalysis->outcome-channel migration -> g-hpw4 (depends on this bead).
- Cache backfill / source arbitration / persistence of profile through uploads -> g-repair-drill-cache.
- Rewriting the win-chance classification model.
design:
# Plan: deterministic grading & blunder decisions (consolidated)

## Core decisions
- TWO comparators, never merged. Backend contract is authoritative; frontend must match it:
  - Drill accuracy:    evalLoss(delta) >  strictnessCp   (boundary value PASSES)
  - Recording / SRS:   evalLoss(delta) >= 50             (inclusive boundary FAILS)
    Pinned: SPEC.md:1012, backend/app/opening_evidence.py:140, backend/test_precompute_thresholds.py:75.
  - Shared code is ONLY the evalLoss clamp + two named helpers — not a single threshold contract.
- Grading is TRI-STATE: pass | fail | unavailable. `unavailable` (null/non-finite eval) is NOT a pass.
- Exactly-once mutation, retry, and analysis-ID migration are OWNED BY g-hpw4, which depends on this bead
  and consumes its helpers. This bead delivers grading semantics + the shared helper surface only.

## A. Engine reset boundary (analysisWorker.ts)
- Per-request readiness handshake, distinct from initialization readiness:
  - awaitRequestReady(): send `ucinewgame` then `isready`; resolve on the next `readyok` via a dedicated
    pending-ready resolver. Do NOT reuse the init engineReady/bootstrap ready signal.
  - Call ONCE at the top of analyzeMove (after analysis-started, before the root runSearch).
    NEVER between the 3 related searches (root best / post-played / post-best).
- Failure & cancellation (see also G):
  - On engine error: reject and clear the pending readyok waiter.
  - Immediately after readyok resolves: throwIfCanceled(request.id).
  - If canceled during reset: never start the root search.
- Clear Hash: undecided; verify necessity via the real-browser smoke test. Default to `ucinewgame` only.
- Preserve drainQueue serial queue, cancel tombstones, analysis-streaming, and session recreation.
- A mocked analysisWorker.test proves command ORDERING only; reproducibility / Clear-Hash necessity
  (acceptance #10) need the real-browser smoke test.

## B. Threshold helpers (analysisUtils.ts) — two comparators
- evalLoss(delta): delta===null || !Number.isFinite(delta) ? null : Math.max(delta, 0)
- failsDrill(delta, strictnessCp): evalLoss !== null && evalLoss >  strictnessCp
- isRecordableFailure(delta):       evalLoss !== null && evalLoss >= RECORDABLE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD_CP (50; KEEP >=)
- Drill grading (ChessGame.tsx:1022-1026) routes through evalLoss/failsDrill.
- SRS grading (AnalysisEffects.tsx:134-135) routes through evalLoss/isRecordableFailure.

## C. Tri-state grading + null semantics
- gradeMove(...) -> 'pass' | 'fail' | 'unavailable' ('unavailable' when evalLoss===null).
- Drill: 'unavailable' -> existing recovery (setDrillRecovery + engineMessage retry/abandon,
  ChessGame.tsx:1011-1016). Do NOT silently continue.
- SRS: check 'unavailable' BEFORE deleting pendingSrsReviewRef (currently deleted at AnalysisEffects.tsx:128).
  On 'unavailable': do NOT delete the entry and do NOT post a review (no false pass/fail).
  Reanalysis + analysis-ID migration to actually retry is OWNED BY g-hpw4 (the map is keyed by terminal
  analysis ID at AnalysisEffects.tsx:123, so a retry yields a new ID — cannot reconnect here).

## D. Classification parity + trusted-cache validation
- classifyMoveAdvanced needs both scores + POV + mover + isBestMove (analysisUtils.ts:331); it cannot be
  rebuilt from delta. Incomplete cache rows must MISS so the worker yields the canonical result.
- DECISION: do NOT reimplement the V2 contract validator in TypeScript. The backend owns FEN parsing,
  side-to-move delta consistency, and eval-triple validation in its single registry
  (backend/app/evidence_contracts.py:75 _validate_resolver_complete_v2). Expose backend-computed booleans
  on the cache-lookup response:
    contract_satisfied      = contract_satisfied(row.evidence_contract_id, serialized_row_data)
    trusted_for_resolution  = _is_authoritative(row)
                              and row.evidence_contract_id == RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2
                              and contract_satisfied
  (Note: evidence_contract_id labels evidence SHAPE; `authoritative`/_is_authoritative verifies PROFILE
  IDENTITY. Both are required for trust, plus contract_satisfied for structural validity.)
- Frontend (analysisUtils.ts):
  - isMoveClassification(x): membership guard over the union
    ('best'|'excellent'|'good'|'inaccuracy'|'mistake'|'blunder') — lightweight runtime type check only.
  - canResolveCachedAnalysis: keep the structural shape checks it needs to BUILD a result
    (isMoveClassification(classification); best_move_uci present; best_line_uci length>1 with [0]===best;
    eval_delta non-null/finite/>=0). These guard local rendering, not trust.
  - isTrustedCacheHit: require row.trusted_for_resolution === true. Do NOT re-derive from
    authoritative + evidence_contract_id + ad-hoc field checks in TS.
  - Keep authoritative, evidence_contract_id, contract_satisfied on the row for diagnostics only.
- Backend + API change: add contract_satisfied and trusted_for_resolution to the lookup response
  (api.ts cached-row type ~api.ts:655-664) and the backend serializer; cover with backend tests.
- 0cp: delta===0 passes every threshold regardless of best_move_uci equality (regression test).
- Out of scope: rewriting the win-chance model; cache backfill / source arbitration = g-repair-drill-cache.

## E. Fallback profile marking — scope-limited
- AnalysisResult (useMoveAnalysis.ts:20) has no source/profile field; uploads discard them
  (sessionUpload.ts:45). Full persistence/coordinator/upload propagation is OUT OF SCOPE.
- Here: mark non-canonical worker results in the worker `analysis` message + runtime diagnostics/log ONLY.
  Persistence propagation noted as a follow-up.

## F. Relationship to g-hpw4
- g-hpw4 (depends on this bead) owns: lastAnalysis-effects -> outcome-channel migration, exactly-once
  mutation, SRS retry + ID migration (docs/plans/g-outcome-recording.md:337).
- This bead exposes finalized helpers + a recordability contract with table tests
  (worker AND cache results, forced-move, move-cap boundaries) for g-hpw4 to consume. No dedup here.

## G. Request-ready waiter cleared from ALL exits
- Single helper rejectRequestReady(err): REJECT and CLEAR the pending readyok waiter.
- Invoked from: cancelAnalysis, handleEngineError, request timeout, and the `terminate` handler.
- Guarantees analysisInFlight cannot remain permanently true if readyok never arrives.

## Tests
- analysisUtils.test.ts: evalLoss/failsDrill/isRecordableFailure below/equal/above for 0,15,35,50.
  Pin drill `>` (50 passes drill@50) and recording `>=` (50 fails) SEPARATELY. Non-finite delta -> null.
- analysisWorker.test.ts: ucinewgame+isready once per request at start, not between searches; readyok
  waiter rejected on engine error; cancel-during-reset (no readyok emitted) settles request and clears
  analysisInFlight; queue drains; streaming preserved.
- ChessGame drill test: delta===strictness passes; delta===0 passes; 'unavailable' -> recovery path.
- AnalysisEffects.test.tsx: SRS 'unavailable' checked before pending-review delete, posts nothing,
  retains entry; 50cp fails. (Exactly-once + retry -> g-hpw4.)
- Frontend cache trust tests: trusted_for_resolution===true -> trusted; false -> not trusted (worker
  fallback), independent of authoritative/evidence_contract_id surface values. Local-build guards:
  arbitrary-string classification or non-finite/negative/null eval_delta -> canResolveCachedAnalysis miss.
- Backend tests: trusted_for_resolution true only when authoritative AND contract_id===resolver-complete-v2
  AND _validate_resolver_complete_v2 passes (finite played/best eval, FEN parses, side-to-move delta
  consistency); each individual failure -> false.
- Real-browser smoke (acc #10): repeated FEN analysis with an intervening position -> identical output.

2. Worker queue cancellation and streaming remain correct, INCLUDING cancel/error/timeout/terminate while awaiting the per-request readyok (the request-ready waiter is rejected and cleared, and analysisInFlight clears).
3. Drill strictness uses evalLoss(delta) > strictnessCp (boundary PASSES) consistently below/equal/above, at every strictness value.
4. delta==0 passes any threshold regardless of best_move_uci equality.
5. Regular-game classification is deterministic; cache rows lacking a VALID classification or a finite, non-negative eval_delta are misses so the worker produces the canonical classifyMoveAdvanced result.
6. Auto-recording uses isRecordableFailure(delta) = evalLoss >= 50 (inclusive, matches backend SPEC.md:1012) and respects forced-move/move-cap rules.

title: Make indexed-move analysis authoritative
description:
## Objective
Replace timing-based first-write-wins with one authoritative indexed-move AnalysisResult that drives all drill, regular-game blunder, recording, SRS, persistence, and post-game outcomes.

## Current Problem
GameAnalysisCoordinator and useMoveAnalysis start local analysis and cache lookup concurrently. resolvedIndices accepts whichever completes first and drops the other. The chosen bestMove, eval_delta, classification, blunder flag, and recordable flag may therefore depend on timing. These fields feed every drill strictness comparison, regular-game feedback/auto-recording, and pending SRS review grading, not only 0cp drill mode.

## Scope
- Start local analysis immediately if needed, but hold its final result while authoritative cache lookup is pending.
- Complete trusted canonical hit: resolve from cache and cancel/discard worker output.
- Miss, incomplete/untrusted profile, failure, or bounded timeout: release buffered fallback or allow it to finish.
- Preserve request ID, move index, session generation, supersession, reset, teardown, and stale-result guards.
- Apply equivalent policy in GameAnalysisCoordinator and useMoveAnalysis; uncached variation analysis remains worker-only.
- Ensure the resolved result is published once and is the single result consumed by drill grading, AnalysisEffects/regular-game classification and recording, pending SRS reviews, session upload, and post-game state.
- Prevent late alternate-source results from triggering duplicate or contradictory downstream effects.
- Expose/log source/profile and decision path for diagnosis.

Sketch:
Model cache status per request: pending, authoritative hit, or fallback released. Buffer worker completion while pending. Cache completion performs one policy decision. Cleanup buffered state on replacement, session change, clearAnalysis, restart, unmount, and destroy. Use one resolution publication point so downstream subscribers cannot observe both sources. Add bounded timeout behavior so analysis-dependent gameplay cannot hang when lookup fails.

## Non-Goals
Do not change cache quality policy, precompute generation, threshold values, or worker reset commands in this step.
design:
FULL PLAN: docs/plans/g-cache-first-resolve.md (in repo; too large for this field).

Scope (post 3-way split): the cache-resolution state machine + worker message protocol (scoped error id) + isTrustedCacheHit trust gate + two timers (dispatch-time cache-response timer + total-analysis hard deadline) + request-scoping/supersession/waiter binding + lifecycle cleanup, mirrored in GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts (gameplay/drill) and useMoveAnalysis.ts (variations). Exposes the emission points (analyzeMove/resolveAnalysisResult/releaseFallback/failRequest) that g-hpw4 hooks the outcome channel into, but builds neither the channel nor the React recording/SRS consumer.

SPLIT OUT (both blocked by this bead):
- g-86pd (F3): useVariationTree.rejectPending + onVariationError reject channel — docs/plans/g-variation-reject.md.
- g-hpw4 (F4): AnalysisOutcome channel, terminal recording frontier, SRS-immediate, microtask alert, BlunderContext keying, pruneFromMoveIndex, lineage map, committedDecisionIndex — docs/plans/g-outcome-recording.md. Blocks g-h94q.
- g-h94q: durable decision-owner / reducer / outbox / SRS ordering / idempotency / backend migration / unmount durability (now blocked by g-hpw4, not this bead).

Key mechanisms in THIS bead: trust gate isTrustedCacheHit(cached)=authoritative===true && canResolveCachedAnalysis(cached); per-request resolutionState buffering worker until cache settles; TWO timers (cache-response started at dispatch + max-batch-age cap; hard total-analysis deadline so waitForAnalysis cannot hang, cache-miss-then-worker-error fails immediately); worker error message gains optional id for request-scoping; request-scoped guards, supersession, waiter requestId binding, settled-request tombstone, fatal-teardown worker epoch invalidation, synchronous reset/prune APIs. Tests 1-13,15,16,17,17b,17c,18 in the doc.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Worker-first then trusted cache-hit publishes only the cache result. 2. Worker-first then miss/incomplete/untrusted/error/timeout publishes only the worker result. 3. Cache-first resolves and cancels the matching worker request. 4. Late/stale results cannot overwrite analysis or retrigger downstream effects. 5. Session changes, superseded indices, resets, and teardown clear buffered state (both timers). 6. GameAnalysisCoordinator and useMoveAnalysis follow the same precedence contract. 7. Drill grading at all strictness values consumes the single published result (no hang; bounded total-analysis deadline). [AC 8-10 moved to g-hpw4.]
notes: Code-review round 4 fix: hook trusted cache-hit path now calls clearActiveAnalysisStateIfCurrent(pending.requestId) after resolveAnalysis, mirroring the coordinator. Previously a trusted cache hit published the authoritative result but left isAnalyzing/analyzingMove set until the discarded worker finished — permanently stuck if the worker stalled (cache resolution already cleared the deadline timer). Added flushCacheLookups dep + regression test (cache hit clears spinner while worker still running). Hook 37 tests; full sweep 222 green, exit 0, tsc clean.

title: Produce canonical opening analysis
description:
## Objective
Generate complete, reproducible canonical opening-analysis rows for every consumer of indexed-move analysis: drills at all strictness levels, regular-game classification and automatic blunder recording, SRS pass/fail, session persistence, and post-game review.

## Current Problem
precompute_openings.py defaults to depth 24 but accepts an arbitrary Stockfish executable from PATH and omits classification and best_line_uci. canResolveCachedAnalysis can therefore reject deeper rows as incomplete, allowing depth-17 fallback analysis to drive any downstream threshold decision. The script also lacks a defined reset boundary between independent positions.

## Scope
- Pin or validate/document Stockfish version/build/network, hash, threads, MultiPV, and search limit under the canonical profile metadata defined by g-guard-cache-writes.
- Reset Stockfish before each independent position using ucinewgame/isready, while keeping root/played/best searches for one result inside the boundary.
- Capture the root best-move PV.
- Persist best_move_uci/SAN, multi-move best_line_uci, played_eval, best_eval, eval_delta, classification, source=precomputed, and full profile metadata.
- Use the shared classification/threshold contract so canonical deltas and classifications are suitable for drill, recording, and SRS decisions.
- Write through the shared quality comparator and permit replacement only according to its profile-succession/completeness rules.
- Add focused tests without requiring a full production precompute.

Design: Use one classification contract shared with gameplay semantics. Capture a primary root PV whose first move equals best_move_uci. Treat rows without the fields required by the authoritative-analysis contract as incomplete. Record immutable canonical profile metadata on every result. Test eval_delta values around drill strictness, recordable-failure, and SRS thresholds to establish that the precompute output is usable by all downstream consumers.

## Non-Goals
Do not backfill production rows or implement frontend/downstream arbitration in this step.
design:
# Plan: g-canonical-precomp — Produce canonical opening analysis

## Context / state inherited from g-guard-cache-writes
The quality-aware pipeline is already in place: `analysis_cache` carries all
provenance/quality columns plus `best_line_uci`, `classification`,
`played_eval_mate` (`backend/app/models.py:280+`); the comparator
(`analysis_cache_policy.py`), the shared writer `write_analysis_cache_rows`
(`analysis_cache_repo.py`), the contract registry (`evidence_contracts.py`), and
the profile registry (`analysis_profiles.py`) all exist. `precompute_openings.py`
already wires `observe_engine_identity -> resolve_profile ->
write_analysis_cache_rows` with `evidence_contract_id=RESOLVER_COMPLETE`.

The script currently **refuses to run**: `assert_can_produce_target_contract`
(`precompute_openings.py:515`, asserted by `test_precompute_capability.py`)
fails because `AnalysisResult` produces neither `best_line_uci` nor a
classification, so it can't satisfy `resolver-complete-v1`
(`required_fields={best_move_uci, best_line_uci}` + classification signal,
`evidence_contracts.py:23-44`).

**This bead makes the script produce genuinely authoritative, resolver-complete
rows.** Non-goals (per bead): no production backfill, no frontend/downstream
arbitration (those are `g-cache-first-resolve` + the repair child).

## 1. Stronger evidence contract: `resolver-complete-v2`
`resolver-complete-v1` accepts `eval_delta` *without* an explicit
`classification` (`_validate_resolver_complete`, `evidence_contracts.py:29-31`),
so a canonical row could pass while classification-dependent consumers get
nothing. Add `resolver-complete-v2`:
- `required_fields = {best_move_uci, best_line_uci, classification, played_eval,
  best_eval, eval_delta}`.
- `validate`: existing PV checks (multi-move line, `line[0] == best_move_uci`)
  **and** a non-null, enum-valid `classification` (one of `best/excellent/good/
  inaccuracy/mistake/blunder`) **and the full eval triple consumers actually
  read (Finding #1)**: finite integer `played_eval` and `best_eval`, and a
  non-negative integer `eval_delta`. A row with `eval_delta=None` would pass the
  old PV-only check yet be useless to drills
  (`session_contracts.py` tiers compare `eval_delta`), to recording, and to SRS
  (`opening_evidence.py:138` skips edges when `eval_delta is None`). Validate
  **delta consistency** too: recompute the side-to-move-relative `best-played`
  from the FEN's active color and assert it equals the stored `eval_delta`
  (clamped `>=0`), so a row can't carry an internally inconsistent delta.
- **The v2 validator must fail closed (Finding #4, this round).** Add
  `fen_before` to v2's `required_fields`/prerequisites, since delta-consistency
  needs the active color. The `validate` must **catch** a malformed/missing FEN
  (e.g. `chess.Board(fen)` raising) and return `False` — never let an exception
  propagate through `contract_satisfied` (`evidence_contracts.py:116`) and crash
  a write/lookup. Tests: missing FEN, malformed FEN, and a row whose
  `eval_delta` was computed with the **wrong** active color (must be rejected).
- `supersedes = {resolver-complete-v1, minimal-played-eval-v1,
  minimal-best-eval-v1}` so a v2 canonical row may upgrade older rows; v1 must
  NOT supersede v2.
- Precompute targets v2. Keep v1 registered (legacy rows already reference it).
- Browser-allowed set (`BROWSER_ALLOWED_CONTRACTS`) is unchanged — browser rows
  do not get v2.

### 1b. Comparator: contract-only successor upgrade (Findings #2/2, #3/3)
The same-profile rule (`analysis_cache_policy.py:126`) only MERGEs when incoming
contributes a populated field existing lacks; otherwise it returns
`SAME_PROFILE_IDEMPOTENT`. So a re-run authoritative row whose contract is a
**strict successor** (v1→v2) but adds no new evidence field would leave the
stored `evidence_contract_id` at v1 forever — the row never advertises the
stronger v2 guarantee even though it satisfies it. Amend Rule 2: when
`existing`/`incoming` are the same authoritative profile, fields agree, and
incoming's contract is a **strict** successor of existing's
(`is_superset_or_successor` and not equal), advance the contract.

**Reuse `Decision.MERGE`, do NOT add a new decision (Finding #3, this round).**
The repository applies only INSERT/REPLACE/MERGE/KEEP
(`analysis_cache_repo.py:299`), and the existing MERGE path already rewrites the
contract id and revalidates the merged row. So represent contract-only
advancement as `Decision.MERGE` with a new **`Reason.SAME_PROFILE_CONTRACT_UPGRADE`**
only — no new `Decision` member, no widening of the apply switch. The change is
narrow: relax the merge guard so "incoming contributes a new field" OR
"incoming contract strictly succeeds existing" both qualify, keeping the
field-agreement + re-validate steps. Equal contract + no new field stays
`SAME_PROFILE_IDEMPOTENT`. Covered by new policy unit tests; existing branches
unchanged.

## 2. Backend classifier ported from `classifyMoveAdvanced` (exact)
Classification lives only in the frontend today
(`src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`); the non-deprecated classifier is the
win-chance model `classifyMoveAdvanced` + `checkMateEvents` (constants
`WIN_CHANCE_MULTIPLIER=-0.00368208`, `CP_CEILING=1000`; drop thresholds
0.30/0.20/0.10/0.02; mate-transition rules at -999/-700 and 999/700).

Create `backend/app/move_classification.py` porting **exactly**:
- `EngineScore` = `{type: 'cp'|'mate', value: int}`.
- `calculate_win_chance(score, pov)`, `check_mate_events(prev, next, score_pov,
  mover)`, `classify_move_advanced(prev, next, score_pov, mover, is_best)`.
- Mirror the worker's POV wiring (`analysisWorker.ts:402`): both post-move
  scores are from the **opponent-to-move** position; `prevScore = postBestScore`,
  `nextScore = postPlayedScore`, `score_pov = opponent-to-move color`,
  `mover = side that played the move`, `is_best = (best == played)`.

Guarantees the user required:
- **Preserve raw `{type, value}`** for the post-best and post-played searches
  (cp vs mate) — see §3 refactor — and feed them to the classifier; do not
  pre-collapse mate to a large cp.
- `eval_delta >= 50` (`RECORDABLE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD_CP`) stays an **independent**
  recording/SRS signal, computed from white-relative cp as today; classification
  does not replace it.
- **No fallback to the deprecated `classifyMove`.** If advanced classification
  cannot be produced (missing post scores), the row is rejected (not written) —
  a canonical row is never persisted with a degraded classifier.
- **Shared golden vectors**: add `backend/tests/fixtures/classification_vectors.json`
  (or a shared path) of `(prevScore, nextScore, scorePov, mover, isBest) ->
  expected` cases covering every threshold boundary + each mate transition, used
  by BOTH a new Python test and a TS test (`analysisUtils.test.ts`) so the two
  implementations cannot drift.

## 3. Search ordering, PV capture, raw scores, terminal handling
`_run_search` (`:139`) returns only `(bestmove, white_cp)` and discards the PV
and the raw score type; the script also searches in played → root → best order
(`:203-211`). Refactor to mirror the frontend exactly:
- **Root-first ordering (Finding #1).** Run the **root/best search first**
  (`analysisWorker.ts:318`: `bestSearch = runSearch(fen, [])`), THEN evaluate the
  played move, THEN the post-best eval if best != played. The current
  played-first order lets TT warmup from the played move bias the root PV — and
  2,988 opening FENs have multiple indexed moves sharing a FEN, so a per-move TT
  bias is real. (The per-position `ucinewgame` in §5 bounds this, but ordering
  must still match the frontend's canonical result.)
- Return `(bestmove, raw_score, white_cp, pv_moves)`: `raw_score` is the
  engine-reported `{type, value}` from the resulting position's POV (for the
  classifier), `white_cp` the white-relative cp (for `played_eval`/`best_eval`/
  `eval_delta` storage), `pv_moves` the parsed `info ... pv <moves>` from the
  last scored info line.
- **Terminal scores (Finding #5).** Port `terminalScoreAfterMove`
  (`analysisWorker.ts:132`): when the position after a move is game-over, do NOT
  search — synthesize `{type:'mate', value:0}` for checkmate, `{type:'cp',
  value:0}` for stalemate/draw. Native Stockfish emits no scored info line after
  mate/stalemate, which would otherwise reject the row or drift the classifier.
- For the root search, keep `pv_moves` as `best_line_uci` (space-joined),
  guaranteeing `best_line_uci[0] == best_move_uci`.
- **Continuation-PV fallback (Finding #5).** Mirror `buildBestLine`
  (`analysisWorker.ts:419`): prefer the root PV when it begins with the final
  best move, but when it is stale/short fall back to
  `[best_move, ...continuation_pv]` where `continuation_pv` is the
  played-eval-search PV when `move == best_move`, else the post-best-search PV.
  Only after this fallback still yields a single-move line is the position
  classified `skipped-no-continuation`. (So the post-best search's PV must also
  be captured, not just its score.)
- **PV-continuation vs. coverage (Finding #5, second half).** A position whose
  best move is mate-in-one has a valid 1-move PV with no continuation. v2 (like
  the frontend's `canResolveCachedAnalysis`, `len > 1`) treats these as
  non-resolvable, so they are **intentionally not cached** — this is consistent
  with frontend behavior, NOT a silent drop. The result accounting in §below
  classifies such positions as a distinct `skipped-no-continuation` bucket
  (expected/benign), separate from genuine failures.
- Compute `classification` from `raw_score` of best vs played searches via §2.
- Persist `played_eval_mate` (exists) and add **`best_eval_mate`** (§7).

## 3b. Fail-closed result accounting + post-write verification (Finding #2)
Today worker exceptions are swallowed, short PVs are dropped, writer decision
reasons are discarded, and `main()` reports the original `total` as "done"
(`:679-694`) even if rows were rejected. Make the run fail-closed:
- Workers record per-position outcome (`ok` / `skipped-no-continuation` /
  `error`) with the exception; an unexpected worker exception aborts the run
  (non-zero exit), it is not logged-and-forgotten.
- `write_analysis_cache_rows` already returns `[(key, Reason)]` — capture it.
  Accepted authoritative outcomes are `NEW_KEY`/`DOMINATES_REPLACE`/
  `LEGACY_REPLACED_BY_AUTH`/`SAME_PROFILE_SUPERSET_MERGE`/
  `SAME_PROFILE_CONTRACT_UPGRADE` (both `Decision.MERGE`),
  **and** `SAME_PROFILE_IDEMPOTENT` (Finding #2:
  an exact re-run is legitimately idempotent). The idempotent case is NOT
  trusted on the reason alone — it is accepted **only** when the post-write
  verification below confirms the already-stored row is the wanted authoritative
  v2 evidence. Any `INVALID_INCOMING_KEEP`/`INCOMPATIBLE_KEEP`/`MERGE_CONFLICT_KEEP`/
  `*_LESS_COMPLETE_KEEP` on a canonical write is a hard error.
- **Post-write verification pass (authoritative gate):** after all batches,
  re-query the expected key set and assert each stores an `identity_verified`,
  effectively-authoritative row whose `evidence_contract_id` is v2 and whose
  evidence matches what this run produced. This is what makes idempotent/upgrade
  results safe. Final summary reports stored / skipped-no-continuation / failed
  counts; exit non-zero on any genuine failure. "Complete" means verified, not
  "loop finished".

## 3c. Engine liveness: deadlines + cancellation (Finding #4)
`_run_search` / the UCI handshake (`:139`,`:188`) do blocking `for line in
proc.stdout` reads that hang forever if Stockfish stalls or dies mid-search —
"fail closed" must cover this. Specify:
- A handshake deadline (await `uciok`/`readyok`) and a per-search deadline
  (wall-clock bound generous relative to depth-24), implemented via a
  reader thread + `queue.get(timeout=...)` or non-blocking poll, since
  `proc.stdout` has no native read timeout.
- **Subprocess-exit detection:** if `proc.poll()` is not None (engine died)
  before `bestmove`, raise rather than block.
- On deadline/exit: terminate the process, mark that position `error`, and —
  consistent with §3b — abort the run (or bounded-retry then abort), never count
  the key as done.
- **Account for queued-but-unprocessed keys:** when a worker aborts, the keys
  still in `work_queue` are reported as `unprocessed`, not silently lost from the
  total. Coverage is `stored + skipped-no-continuation`; anything else fails.
- Tests cover both a **stalled** engine (no output) and an **early exit**
  (process closes stdout) via the fake-Stockfish stub.

## 4. Add fields to `AnalysisResult` + row dict + writer/comparator allowlists
Add `best_line_uci: str | None`, `classification: str | None`,
`best_eval_mate: int | None`, `played_eval_mate: int | None` to the dataclass
(`:68`) and populate in all three producers (`analyze_position`,
`_analyze_batch`, `_worker_thread`). Include them in the `upsert_results` row
dict (`:556`) and set `evidence_contract_id=RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2`.

**`best_eval_mate` must be threaded through the allowlists (Finding #4).** The
shared writer uses an explicit `_EVIDENCE_FIELDS` allowlist
(`analysis_cache_repo.py:108`) and the comparator uses `EVIDENCE_FIELDS`
(`analysis_cache_policy.py:24`); both already include `played_eval_mate` but NOT
`best_eval_mate`, so without adding it the column would be silently dropped on
write and ignored in completeness/merge. Add `best_eval_mate` to **both** lists,
with a writer round-trip test asserting it persists and reads back.

Once `AnalysisResult` exposes `best_line_uci` + `classification`,
`assert_can_produce_target_contract(RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2)` passes — so
`test_precompute_capability.py` is **inverted** to assert success.

## 5. UCI init + reset boundary (Findings #5, #6)
- **One shared initializer (Finding #6).** Current code sends `setoption`
  *before* `uciok` (`:188-196`). Extract a single `_init_engine(proc)`:
  `uci` → await `uciok` → `setoption Hash/Threads/MultiPV` → `isready` → await
  `readyok`, used by `analyze_position`, `_analyze_batch`, `_worker_thread`, and
  `observe_engine_identity` so handshake/options are identical everywhere.
- **Reset boundary.** Send `ucinewgame` + `isready` **once before each
  position's search group**, never between the root/played/best searches of one
  position (acceptance #4).

## 6. Canonical profile: committed manifest, fail-closed (replaces placeholder)
The installed engine is **Stockfish 18 with two embedded networks**, so the id
must reflect the actual artifact: name `canonical-sf18-depth24-v1` (NOT
`-sf17-`). Replace the placeholder `canonical-sf-depth24-v1` **before its first
production run** (safe — no production rows reference it yet). Pin via a
committed manifest `backend/app/canonical_profiles/<id>.json`, loaded into the
registry:
- Release tag + full source commit; versioned artifact URL; archive SHA-256 +
  extracted executable SHA-256; architecture/build target.
- **Both** NNUE identities (`EvalFile` *and* `EvalFileSmall`), with **full**
  64-hex SHA-256 hashes — not the current 16-char truncation
  (`observe_engine_identity:502` does `[:16]`; remove that).

**One reproducible embedded-NNUE algorithm (Finding #2, this round).** The
current code can only hash an external network file (`precompute_openings.py:496`),
but SF18 official binaries **embed** their nets and merely expose default
filenames over UCI — "hash the blob / record a marker" is two algorithms and a
marker can't satisfy the full-SHA requirement. Pin a single scheme:
- The committed manifest carries the **pinned full SHA-256 of each official NNUE
  artifact** (`nn-*.nnue` for `EvalFile` and `EvalFileSmall`), taken once from
  the official Stockfish release source — these are the authoritative network
  content hashes, recorded by humans, not extracted at runtime.
- `observe_engine_identity` at runtime captures only what it can verify
  reproducibly: the **exact executable SHA-256** plus the **default EvalFile /
  EvalFileSmall filenames** reported via UCI. It does NOT attempt to extract or
  hash an embedded blob.
- If an external `EvalFile` path *is* present, hash it in full and require it to
  equal the manifest value.

**Two-phase resolution to avoid the bootstrap contradiction (Finding #1, this
round).** Runtime can observe only filenames, but `eval_file_id`/
`eval_file_small_id` store *full hashes* and participate in exact identity — so
`resolve_profile` can't match observed-vs-profile directly without first copying
the expected hashes into "observed", which is circular. Split the two field
sets:
- **`RESOLUTION_FIELDS`** (runtime-observable only): executable SHA-256
  (`engine_build`), reported `eval_file`/`eval_file_small` **filenames**,
  `engine_version`, `search_limit_*`, `threads`/`hash_mb`/`multipv`,
  `analyzer_protocol_version`. `resolve_profile(observed)` matches on these and
  returns the profile id (or `None` → abort).
- **Phase 2 stamp:** once resolved, the writer stamps the **manifest-derived
  full** `eval_file_id`/`eval_file_small_id` (and `profile_manifest_digest`) from
  the resolved profile onto the row. So the row persists full hashes even though
  runtime never hashed an embedded blob.
- **`IDENTITY_FIELDS`** (read-time `identity_verified` and `_is_authoritative`):
  the full stored hashes are now present, so verification compares stored full
  `eval_file_id`/`eval_file_small_id` against the profile's manifest values
  exactly. Write-time resolution and read-time verification use different field
  sets by design; the Profile carries both the filenames (for resolution) and
  the full hashes (for verification).
- Every explicitly configured UCI option (Hash 128, Threads 1, MultiPV 1, ...),
  search-limit (depth 24), and the per-position reset protocol.
- Manifest schema/version field.

**Bind authority to the analyzer implementation (Finding #3).** Identity today
covers only engine/search metadata (`IDENTITY_FIELDS`,
`analysis_profiles.py:39`), so changing classifier code, score conversion, PV
selection, or reset behavior would still resolve to the same authoritative
profile and silently stamp rows as canonical — a sidecar run manifest cannot
protect individual rows. Add an explicit **`analyzer_protocol_version`** (a
short, manually-bumped version of *this script's* analysis contract: search
ordering, terminal synthesis, score conversion, PV/continuation rule, classifier
port, reset protocol). Persist it as a column, include it in the `Profile` +
`IDENTITY_FIELDS` (so `resolve_profile`/`identity_verified` require it to match),
and store the **profile-manifest digest** on the row as well. The canonical
profile pins the protocol version it expects; any analyzer change that alters
output bumps the version → old rows no longer `identity_verified` against the new
canonical profile (forcing an explicit re-run / `-v2` profile), exactly as an
engine/network change would.

**Active-vs-retired profiles (Finding #1, this round).** Profile authority today
is a single static `authoritative` bool, and verification keys off the row's
*own* profile (`analysis.py:48`, `analysis_profiles.py:110`), so when a canonical
profile is superseded its retained rows would stay `authoritative=True` forever.
Add a separate **`active`** flag on `Profile` (current-for-resolution),
orthogonal to `authoritative`:
- `resolve_profile` resolves **only** `active` profiles — a new producer can
  never stamp a retired profile id.
- The lookup `authoritative` flag (`_is_authoritative`) and the comparator's
  `is_effectively_authoritative` require `active=True` AND `authoritative=True`
  AND identity match — so a retired profile's rows stop qualifying as trusted
  cache hits the moment its successor is marked active.
- Retired profiles stay **registered** (identifiable) and may still appear in a
  successor's `dominates` set, so the successor explicitly replaces them via
  Rule 5. This lets a future canonical `v2` profile retire
  `canonical-sf18-depth24-v1` without leaving stale trusted rows. Touches
  `analysis_profiles.py`, `analysis.py`, and `analysis_cache_policy.py` (shared
  modules) — with policy/lookup unit tests for the retired-but-dominating case.

**Manifest-digest boundary excludes lifecycle fields (Finding #2, this round).**
`profile_manifest_digest` must cover only the **immutable analysis-identity**
bits (engine name/version/build, network filenames + full hashes, search limit,
threads/hash/multipv, `analyzer_protocol_version`) and must **exclude `active`
and `dominates`**. Retirement only flips `active` (and may extend a successor's
`dominates`); if the digest covered those, retiring a profile would change its
digest, so existing rows would fail `identity_verified`, collapse to **effective
legacy** (`effective_profile_id → None`), and Rule 5's successor-`dominates` edge
(which keys off the existing row's profile id) could never fire — bypassing the
explicit successor path this design relies on. With lifecycle fields excluded,
retired rows stay `identity_verified=True` (recognizable for dominance) but
`active=False` (not trusted hits) — exactly the intended state.

**Schema for two full NNUE identities (Finding #3, NNUE half).** `network_id` is
`VARCHAR(128)` (`models.py:308`) — two raw SHA-256 hashes alone need 129 chars
before any filename/label, so they cannot coexist in one column. Add **two
dedicated `Text` columns** `eval_file_id` and `eval_file_small_id` (each holding
`<filename>:<full-sha256>`), rather than overloading `network_id`. This ripples
through:
- `Profile` dataclass + `IDENTITY_FIELDS` (`analysis_profiles.py:40`): replace
  the single `network_id` identity slot with `eval_file_id` + `eval_file_small_id`
  (keep `network_id` only if some legacy consumer needs it; otherwise retire it
  from the identity set).
- `observe_engine_identity`: populate both fields with full hashes.
- `resolve_profile`: exact-match on both.
- Writer `_METADATA_FIELDS` (`analysis_cache_repo.py:95`) + comparator identity
  projection must carry both columns.
- Migration (§7) adds both columns; `conftest.py::_create_test_schema` too.

Required corrections to current code:
- `observe_engine_identity`: full (untruncated) hashes; capture both EvalFile +
  EvalFileSmall; handle embedded nets.
- **Resolve the executable once** (absolute path) and launch that exact path in
  every worker, instead of each worker re-resolving `--stockfish` via PATH.
- **Abort** the canonical run when `resolve_profile()` returns `None` — do not
  silently perform an expensive non-authoritative run. (Removes the
  "off-spec stored as legacy" path for this script; off-spec => hard error.)
- **Immutability:** never modify a profile after production rows exist. Any
  engine/network/search/wrapper change creates `canonical-...-v2` with an
  explicit `dominates` edge over v1. Document this in the registry module.

Also emit a **run manifest** (logged + written to a sidecar file) containing:
profile id, profile-manifest hash, application git commit, opening-book
(eco.json) hash, evidence contract id, worker count, start/end timestamps.

Rows continue storing the profile id **plus** observed executable/network/
settings metadata (already done via `**observed`).

## 7. Migration
New Alembic revision (down_revision = current head) via `batch_alter_table`
adding nullable columns: `best_eval_mate` (Integer); the two NNUE-identity
`Text` columns `eval_file_id`, `eval_file_small_id`; `analyzer_protocol_version`
(String); and `profile_manifest_digest` (String) (Findings #3). Update
`conftest.py::_create_test_schema` to add all of them so existing API tests keep
passing. The new `analyzer_protocol_version` joins `_METADATA_FIELDS` (writer)
and the comparator identity projection. `downgrade()` drops them. (No data
backfill.)

## 8. Tests (`backend/test_*.py` convention)
- `test_move_classification.py`: drives the shared golden vectors; asserts every
  win-chance boundary + mate transition matches the TS values; the TS suite
  consumes the same fixture.
- `test_precompute_pv.py`: a fake-Stockfish subprocess stub emitting canned
  `info ... pv` / `score cp|mate` / `bestmove` lines through `analyze_position`;
  assert `best_line_uci` parsed and starts with `best_move_uci`, classification
  computed from raw scores (cp and mate cases), `best_eval_mate`/
  `played_eval_mate` persisted, and `ucinewgame` issued exactly once per
  position (not per search). Include a forced/no-continuation position skip case.
- `test_precompute_capability.py`: inverted — `assert_can_produce_target_contract`
  now succeeds for the v2 target.
- `test_evidence_contracts.py`: `resolver-complete-v2` validate (rejects missing/
  invalid classification, rejects single-move PV), supersession over v1/minimals,
  v1 does NOT supersede v2.
- Profile/manifest test: manifest loads, full (untruncated) hashes, `resolve_profile`
  matches only on exact identity, run aborts (raises) when resolve returns None.
- **Drill-boundary threshold cases (Finding #6).** Name the actual tiers from
  `session_contracts.py:20` (strict 15 / standard 35 / lenient 50), which fail
  when `eval_delta > threshold`: test `14/15/16`, `34/35/36`, `49/50/51`, plus
  `0/1`. This pins both the drill `>` boundary and its distinction from
  recording/SRS's `>= 50` (`RECORDABLE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD_CP`).
- `test_analysis_cache_repo.py` extension: writer round-trip persisting +
  reading back `best_eval_mate` and the two NNUE-identity columns (Finding #3,#4).
- `test_precompute_pv.py`: root-search-first ordering, terminal mate/stalemate
  synthesis (no engine search), one `ucinewgame` per position, and
  fail-closed accounting (a rejected/short row marks the run failed / exits
  non-zero; mate-in-one no-continuation counts as `skipped-no-continuation`,
  not a failure).

## Review findings addressed
1. **Root-first ordering** — search root before played, mirroring
   `analysisWorker.ts:318`; TT-bias bounded by per-position `ucinewgame` (§3,§5).
2. **Fail-closed runs** — worker exceptions abort; writer `Reason`s asserted
   authoritative; post-write verification of every expected key; non-zero exit
   on genuine failure (§3b).
3. **Two NNUE identities don't fit `VARCHAR(128)`** — dedicated `eval_file_id` +
   `eval_file_small_id` `Text` columns through model/migration/profile/
   IDENTITY_FIELDS/writer/comparator (§6,§7).
4. **`best_eval_mate` would be dropped** — added to writer `_EVIDENCE_FIELDS` +
   comparator `EVIDENCE_FIELDS` with a round-trip test (§4).
5. **Terminal scores + coverage conflict** — port `terminalScoreAfterMove`;
   mate-in-one single-move PVs are intentionally non-cached (consistent with
   frontend `canResolveCachedAnalysis`), bucketed as benign-skipped, not dropped
   errors (§3).
6. **Explicit UCI init** — one shared initializer: `uci`→`uciok`→setoptions→
   `isready`, fixing the setoption-before-uciok ordering (§5).
7. **Artifact correction** — installed binary is Stockfish 18 w/ two embedded
   nets; profile id is `canonical-sf18-depth24-v1`, not `-sf17-` (§6).

### Third-round findings addressed
1. **v2 completeness for all consumers** — v2 now requires finite `played_eval`/
   `best_eval` + non-negative `eval_delta` with FEN-derived delta-consistency, so
   drills/recording/SRS always have the fields they read (§1).
2. **v1→v2 upgrade + idempotent reruns** — comparator gains a contract-only
   successor upgrade; idempotent reruns are an accepted outcome gated on
   post-write authoritative verification, not treated as failure (§1b, §3b).
3. **Authority bound to analyzer impl** — `analyzer_protocol_version` +
   `profile_manifest_digest` persisted per row and in `IDENTITY_FIELDS`, so
   classifier/score/PV/reset changes invalidate identity (§6, §7).
4. **Hung/dead engines** — handshake/search deadlines, subprocess-exit
   detection, worker cancellation, queued-but-unprocessed accounting; stalled +
   early-exit tests (§3c).
5. **Continuation-PV fallback** — mirror `buildBestLine` continuation reuse
   before classifying a row as `skipped-no-continuation` (§3).
6. **Named drill boundaries** — 14/15/16, 34/35/36, 49/50/51, 0/1, capturing the
   drill `>` vs recording/SRS `>=50` distinction (§8).

### Fourth-round findings addressed
1. **Profile evolution invalidates old rows** — new `active` flag separate from
   `authoritative`; lookup + comparator require `active`, `resolve_profile`
   resolves only active profiles; retired profiles stay registered for dominance
   only (§6).
2. **One reproducible embedded-NNUE scheme** — pin full official network SHA-256
   in the manifest; runtime verifies executable SHA + reported EvalFile/
   EvalFileSmall filenames; no runtime blob extraction or marker (§6).
3. **No new `Decision`** — contract-only advancement is `Decision.MERGE` +
   `Reason.SAME_PROFILE_CONTRACT_UPGRADE`, reusing the existing merge/revalidate
   path; apply switch unchanged (§1b).
4. **v2 FEN validator fails closed** — `fen_before` required; malformed/missing
   FEN caught and returns `False`; wrong-active-color delta tested (§1).
5. **Verification refreshed** — runs the changed policy/repo/profile suites and
   all five new columns' migration (§Verification).

### Fifth-round findings addressed
1. **NNUE resolution bootstrap** — two-phase scheme: `RESOLUTION_FIELDS`
   (executable SHA + reported filenames + version/search/settings/protocol) for
   write-time `resolve_profile`, then stamp manifest-derived full hashes; read-time
   `IDENTITY_FIELDS` verify the stored full hashes. No circular hash-copy (§6).
2. **Manifest-digest boundary** — `profile_manifest_digest` covers immutable
   analysis-identity only and excludes `active`/`dominates`, so retirement leaves
   old rows identity-verified-but-inactive and successor dominance still fires
   (§6).

## Acceptance mapping
1. rows satisfy v2 trusted-cache contract (§1,§3,§4); 2. PV starts with best move
+ continuation (§3); 3. played/best/delta/classification follow shared contract,
delta-50 independent (§2); 4. ucinewgame per position only (§5); 5. canonical
profile pinned/validated/recorded via manifest + run manifest (§6); 6. writes go
through the shared comparator, v2 supersession rules (§1); 7. tests cover PV,
metadata, classification, threshold-adjacent deltas, reset boundary, persisted
fields (§8).

## Verification
1. `alembic upgrade head` on scratch SQLite — assert **all five** new columns
   added: `best_eval_mate`, `eval_file_id`, `eval_file_small_id`,
   `analyzer_protocol_version`, `profile_manifest_digest`; `downgrade()` drops
   them.
2. `pytest test_move_classification.py test_precompute_pv.py
   test_precompute_capability.py test_evidence_contracts.py -q`.
3. **Changed shared-module suites** (these modules are amended by §1b/§4/§6, so
   their existing tests must stay green): `pytest test_analysis_cache_policy.py
   test_analysis_cache_repo.py test_analysis_cache_api.py -q`, plus the new
   profile/manifest test (active-vs-retired, embedded-NNUE identity, abort on
   `resolve_profile`→None).
4. TS golden-vector parity test (`npm test analysisUtils`).
5. Rerun named session/precompute/cache suites in isolation (flaky pre-push note).

## Post-approval first step
Persist this plan into the bead `design` field before writing code (project
convention) — done.
acceptance_criteria:

4. Stockfish receives ucinewgame/isready once per independent position, not between related searches.
