title: We need a better way to help the user return to the latest move after a blunder is shown
description:
When a blunder is shown during gameplay we navigate backward from the latest move. This can be confusing for the user and they might not realize the board is not on the latest move and they can't move the pieces on the board. Brainstorm some visual cues to indicate the not-latest-move state. This visual cue should be shown for any time the user navigated away from the latest move.

In g-9y2a we desaturated the color of the board so there is already some visual cue, come up  with more.

From user testing part of the confusion is that the user doesn't know how to return to live play, one idea is to dramatically highlight the "Go to current position" button in MoveList.
design:
# g-1y68 — Help the user return to the latest move after a blunder rewind

## Goal
When a blunder alert rewinds the board (or the user manually scrubs) during a **live**
game, the user is left on a past ply. Two confusions from user testing:
1. **"I don't realize I'm off the latest move"** — the desaturation wash (g-9y2a) is too
   subtle on its own.
2. **"I don't know how to get back to live play"** — the only return control is the tiny
   `⟩⟩` button in the move list, which users don't see.

This bead adds five reinforcing cues on top of the existing wash. Scope here is the design;
do NOT split into subtasks yet.

## Shared signal — already exists, reuse it
`isReviewingPast = isGameActive && displayedIndex < moveHistory.length - 1`
(`ChessGame.tsx:411`). This is the single master gate for every board-side cue below. It is
already threaded into `BoardStage` (`BoardStage.tsx:25,104` and applied at `:335`). Correct
for blunder-rewind, manual nav, and graph clicks (see g-9y2a design for why `displayedIndex`
beats `viewIndex !== null`).

**Return-to-live action:** `handleNavigate(null)` (`ChessGame.tsx:427` → `setViewIndex(null)`).
This is the same path the move list's `⟩⟩` (`handleLatest` → `onNavigate(null)`) already uses.
Firing it sets `viewIndex = null` → `isReviewingPast` flips false → all cues unmount and the
wash clears in one commit.

**Extra data needed for the badge (B1):** `displayedIndex` and `moveHistory.length` — both
already live in `ChessGame` and can be passed to `BoardStage` as `reviewingPly`
(`displayedIndex + 1`, 1-based) and `latestPly` (`moveHistory.length`).

## Board-area layout coordination (`.chessboard-board-area`, `BoardStage.tsx:146`)
Several absolutely-positioned children already share this box: `streak-toast` (top),
`board-notice` (top-left, `:161`), and full-cover overlays (start overlay, revert dialog,
ended scrim, promotion picker). To avoid collisions:
- **B1 reviewing badge → top-center strip.** Keeps clear of the top-left `board-notice`
  slot (a `review-result` ✗ box can still appear off-live via the SRS-fail spotlight, so the
  two must not stack).
- **A1 return-to-live pill → bottom-center**, anchored to the lower board edge (matches the
  familiar chess.com "return to live" placement, away from the top notices and the sibling
  eval bar on the left).
- Both A1 and B1 must be **suppressed while a modal-ish overlay owns the board**:
  `showStartOverlay`, `showEndedScrim`, `isRevertPending` (revert dialog is a centered
  overlay that CAN co-occur since it requires an active game), and `pendingPromotion`.
  Gate inside `BoardStage`, e.g. a local
  `const showReviewingCues = isReviewingPast && !isRevertPending && !pendingPromotion && !showStartOverlay && !showEndedScrim;`
  (start overlay / ended scrim already imply `!isGameActive`, so they can't truly co-occur
  with `isReviewingPast`, but gate defensively).
- Ensure the pill has `pointer-events: auto` (the toast layer above it may be
  `pointer-events: none`) so the click lands.

---

## A1 — Floating "Return to live ⟩⟩" pill on the board  *(primary fix)*
**What:** A prominent primary-colored pill reading `⟩⟩ Return to live`, floating at the
bottom-center of the board while reviewing. Click returns to the latest move. This is the
single strongest fix for confusion #2 because it sits where the user's attention already is.

**Wiring:**
- New `BoardStage` prop `onReturnToLive?: () => void`, wired in `ChessGame.tsx` (the
  `<BoardStage .../>` block ~`:1914`) to `() => handleNavigate(null)`.
- Render inside `.chessboard-board-area`, gated on `showReviewingCues` (above).
- Reuse the `⟩⟩` glyph for continuity with the move-list button (A2).
- On click → `onReturnToLive()` → `viewIndex` null → `isReviewingPast` false → pill unmounts;
  the board un-washes via the existing g-9y2a rule.

**Style/layout:** absolute, `bottom` a few % up from the board's lower edge, centered via
`left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`. z-index above `[data-square]`/arrows but below the
overlay layer (start/revert/ended). Soft entrance (fade+rise) reusing the toast animation
vocabulary; a gentle looping pulse to draw the eye.

---

## A2 — Dramatize the move-list `⟩⟩` button  *(reinforcement, cheap)*
**What:** When reviewing during a live game, the `⟩⟩` ("Go to current position") button in
`MoveList` (`MoveList.tsx:555`) gets a primary fill + pulse/glow, and a small "LIVE" text
label appears beside it. Reinforces A1 for users whose eyes are in the move list.

**Wiring (self-contained in `MoveList.tsx`):** `MoveList` already has `isGameActive` and
derives `isAtLatest` (currentIndex null OR === `moves.length - 1`). Derive locally:
`const emphasizeLatest = isGameActive && !isAtLatest;` — no new prop needed, and it mirrors
`isReviewingPast` exactly. The button is already `disabled` when `isAtLatest`, so emphasis
only shows while the button is actionable. Add a conditional class
`move-nav-button--return-live` and a sibling "LIVE" `<span>` shown only when `emphasizeLatest`.

**Note:** `ChessGame` renders `ConnectedMoveList` (`ChessGame.tsx:2042`); it does NOT use
`HorizontalMoveList`/`ControlsRow` (those are analysis-board only), so A2 touches only
`MoveList.tsx` + CSS.

---

## A3 — Failed-move affordance: shake + inline hint  *(catches the exact confused moment)*
**What:** When the user tries to interact with a piece while reviewing, briefly shake the
board and surface a one-line hint ("You're viewing an earlier move — return to live to
play") with the return action, instead of the current silent no-op. This converts the
"why can't I move?" moment into the answer.

**Key constraint — drag is already disabled:** `allowDragging` is false while `!isViewingLive`
(`ChessGame.tsx:1826`), so pieces don't lift and `onPieceDrop`/`handleDropPiece` will NOT
fire from a drag attempt during review. The reliable interception point is **`handleSquareClick`**
(`ChessGame.tsx:1324`), which react-chessboard still calls with dragging off. It currently
early-returns at `:1337` on `!isViewingLive`. 

**Wiring:** inside `handleSquareClick`, before/within the `!isViewingLive` early return,
detect the specific reviewing case and fire the affordance:
```
if (isReviewingPast) { triggerReviewShake(); return; }
```
Gate on `isReviewingPast` specifically (NOT the broader `!playersTurn`/opponent-thinking
case, which is a different situation and should stay a silent no-op). `triggerReviewShake`
bumps a nonce/boolean passed to `BoardStage` (e.g. `reviewNudge`) that:
- adds a short-lived shake class to `.chessboard-square-measure` (CSS keyframe, ~300ms,
  self-clearing via timeout or `animationend`), and
- optionally flashes/pulses the A1 pill + B1 badge to point at the way out.

**Note on wash filter interaction:** the shake must be a `transform`/`translate` animation on
the `.chessboard-square-measure` wrapper — it must NOT fight the `filter:` wash on
`[data-square]` (g-9y2a, `App.css:4357`). Different property, different element level → safe.

---

## B1 — Persistent "Reviewing · move X of Y" badge  *(names the state)*
**What:** A small persistent badge, top-center of the board area, reading e.g.
`Reviewing — move 14 of 20` for the whole duration of `isReviewingPast`. Directly answers
confusion #1 by *labeling* the state rather than implying it via desaturation. Naturally
hosts / sits above the A1 pill.

**Important — do NOT route through `useBoardNotice`:** that hook owns the single
auto-dismissing notice slot and, by design, returns `null` whenever `!isViewingLive`
(`useBoardNotice.ts:121`). A reviewing badge is by definition shown off-live and must
persist (no auto-dismiss). So render it as a **separate, purely view-derived element** in
`BoardStage`, driven straight off `showReviewingCues` + `reviewingPly`/`latestPly` props —
independent of the `boardNotice` slot. This lets it coexist with a transient off-live
`review-result` box (kept top-left) without either hook's timer touching it.

**Copy/text:** `reviewingPly = displayedIndex + 1`, `latestPly = moveHistory.length`.
`aria-live="polite"`, `role="status"`.

---

## B2 — Distinct board frame while reviewing  *(mode legibility)*
**What:** A distinct (amber) ring around the board while reviewing. A frame reads as "you're
in a different mode" more legibly than a wash and complements the existing desaturation.

**Wiring:** extend the existing `.chessboard-square-measure--reviewing` rule (`App.css:4357`,
applied at `BoardStage.tsx:335`) — no new class/prop needed; it's already toggled by
`isReviewingPast`.

**Critical layout constraint — use `outline`/`box-shadow`, NOT `border`:** the measuring
wrapper sets `line-height: 0` and is used to size the board; adding a `border` would change
its measured box and shift the board. Use `outline` or an inset/offset `box-shadow` ring
(neither affects layout box). Note there is already a `boxShadow` on `boardStyle`
(`BoardStage.tsx:355`) on the inner board — the ring goes on the `--reviewing` wrapper and
should visually read as a frame around, not clash with, that drop shadow.

---

## Coexistence & lifecycle summary
- All five cues rise/fall together with `isReviewingPast` (A2 uses its local mirror
  `emphasizeLatest`). One `handleNavigate(null)` clears every cue in a single commit.
- A1 + B1 are suppressed under modal overlays (revert/promotion/start/ended) — see layout
  coordination.
- A3 is an event-driven nudge layered on top; it only fires on a board click during review.
- The existing g-9y2a wash stays; B2 layers the ring onto the same `--reviewing` rule.

## Accessibility
- B1 badge: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`.
- A1 pill: real `<button>`, focusable, keyboard-activatable; label "Return to live".
- A3 hint: `aria-live="polite"` (not assertive — it's a gentle correction, fired repeatedly
  if the user keeps clicking; avoid a screen-reader storm — consider debouncing announcements).
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for the A1 pulse, A3 shake, and any B1 entrance.

## Test coverage
- `BoardStage.test.tsx` (already covers the `--reviewing` class): add
  - A1 pill renders only when `isReviewingPast` + not under overlays; click calls
    `onReturnToLive`.
  - B1 badge renders "move X of Y" from `reviewingPly`/`latestPly`; absent when not reviewing.
  - B2: `--reviewing` wrapper class present (extends existing assertion).
- `MoveList.test.tsx`: A2 — `move-nav-button--return-live` class + "LIVE" label present when
  `isGameActive && !isAtLatest`; absent when at latest or game over; button still fires
  `onNavigate(null)`.
- `ChessGame.test.tsx`: A3 — a board square click while `isReviewingPast` triggers the shake
  nudge and does NOT attempt a move; a click while live-and-your-turn still moves normally;
  a click while merely waiting-for-opponent (live) does NOT shake.
- Regression: confirm `handleNavigate(null)` from the pill clears wash + all cues.

## Open questions (defer, note only)
- Should A3 also flash A1/B1, or just shake? (Lightest: shake + let the always-present pill
  be the answer.)
- Auto-return-to-live after N seconds idle was considered and rejected for now (too
  aggressive); revisit only if testing still shows users stuck.

title: Opening cards changes

- The move name is the top label in the header,
- The secondary header line is the full list of moves. For example Caro-Kann Defense: Hillbilly Attack's secondary would show "1.e4 c6 2.Bc4". The last move in the list should be highlighted with bold font.

- Move "View in Openings" link into the card

design:
# g-d65n — Opening cards changes

## Context

The opening cards render on three surfaces from two components:

- **`/openings`** — `OpeningTreeNodeCard` in `kind="move"` (horizontal move-tree columns).
- **`/play` & `/history`** — `GameOpeningLineage` → `OpeningTreeNodeCard` in `kind="family"` (the openings a game crossed).

Today the card identity is inconsistent: `/openings` cards lead with the **move** (e.g. `2. Bc4`) and show the name/ECO underneath, while the family cards lead with the **name** and show the ECO underneath. Neither shows the move list that produced the opening. The user wants one consistent card on all surfaces:

- **Header (top label) = opening name**, on every surface.
- **Secondary line = the full list of moves** (e.g. `1.e4 c6 2.Bc4`) with the **last move bold**.
- Compact mode **truncates** both lines; expanded mode **wraps** (no truncation).

Plus, for the `/play` and `/history` family cards: relocate the **"View in Openings"** link *inside* the card; and on `/play`, once a game has ended, offer **Start Drill** and **board navigation** to the opening's position (history parity).

### Decisions confirmed with user
1. **Name on top, everywhere** — including `/openings`. Sibling move-cards in a column may share an inherited name; the **bold last move** in the move list disambiguates them (the column header already shows the move too).
2. **Move list = the player's actual moves** (from session moves), for the family cards — not the canonical book line.

### Review corrections folded in (findings 1–5)
Post-review adjustments are incorporated below: mirror the route-state drill flow instead of resolving `openingFamilies` directly; a stricter `/openings`-root predicate; an indexed lineage walk (not a fragile FEN→index map); authoritative move numbering via a backend `start_ply` (drill-safe); and keep the card router-free via a `footerAction` slot.

---

## Data model changes

### Backend — attach the player's move list + correct numbering
`OpeningLineageItem` has no move sequence today (`opening_key` is a FEN, `path` is ancestor opening-keys). `SessionMove` stores `move_san`, `move_number`, `color`, `fen_after` — the player's SAN moves in play order are directly available.

**`backend/app/opening_roots.py`** — add an *indexed* chain variant so each crossing keeps its own move index (fixes the non-consecutive-repeat fragility; `played_opening_chain` only dedupes consecutive repeats):
- Add `played_opening_chain_indexed(fens_in_move_order) -> list[tuple[OpeningRoot, int]]` doing the same walk but returning `(root, index)` at each boundary crossing. Refactor the existing `played_opening_chain` to derive from it (`[root for root, _ in ...]`) so dedup + normalization stay single-sourced and the 3 existing callers (`opening_roots.py:482`, `opening_score_delta.py:401`, `session.py:1364`) are unaffected.

**`backend/app/api/session.py`** — `get_session_openings` (~L1349–1395):
- Add `moves: list[str]` to the `OpeningLineageItem` pydantic model (~L192) and `start_ply: int` to `SessionOpeningsResponse` (~L206).
- Build the chain via `played_opening_chain_indexed(...)` over `session_moves` (already ordered by `move_number` asc, then white-before-black). For each `(root, idx)`, set `moves=[m.move_san for m in session_moves[: idx + 1]]` — the player's actual SAN prefix up to and including the crossing move.
- `start_ply` = ply of `session_moves[0]`, computed authoritatively from `move_number`/`color`: `ply = (move_number - 1) * 2 + (1 if color == "white" else 2)`. Constant across items (all prefixes start at index 0). This makes numbering correct even if a drill's stored moves don't start at ply 1 — no client-side guess. `start_ply` defaults to `1` when there are no moves.

### Frontend types
- **`src/utils/api.ts`** — add `moves: string[]` to `OpeningLineageItem` (~L1160) and `start_ply: number` to `SessionOpeningsResponse` (~L1174). Document `start_ply` in a comment as **"ply of `moves[0]` (1 = White's move 1)"** so its meaning is unambiguous at the type.

---

## Shared move-list rendering

One helper so both surfaces render identically. **`src/openings/format.ts`** (alongside `formatMoveLabel`):

```ts
export interface MoveListToken { text: string; isLast: boolean }
// startPly: ply of sanMoves[0] (1 = White's move 1). White plies (odd) get an
// "{n}." prefix; Black plies print SAN only. n = ceil(ply / 2).
// Empty input short-circuits: buildMoveListTokens([], startPly) === []
// regardless of startPly (accept `startPly?: number | null`), so the empty
// defensive case (family card with moves: []) stays boring.
export function buildMoveListTokens(sanMoves: string[], startPly?: number | null): MoveListToken[]
```

The card renders tokens inline (space-separated); the `isLast` token is wrapped in `<strong>`. On empty `sanMoves` the card renders no secondary line (see the root/empty handling below). The card owns the call (keeps `GameOpeningLineage`/`treeView` thin). Add to `OpeningTreeNodeView` (`OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx` ~L24): `moveListSan: string[]` and `moveListStartPly: number`.

### Feeding the view-model
- **Family (`/play`, `/history`)** — thread `start_ply` through `useSessionOpenings` (return `{ lineage, playerColor, startPly }`; `src/hooks/useSessionOpenings.ts` ~L20/55) → `GameOpeningLineage` prop → `toNodeView(item, startPly)` sets `moveListSan: item.moves`, `moveListStartPly: startPly`.
- **`/openings`** — in `buildTreeView` (`src/openings/treeView.ts` ~L270): replay `selectionLine` **once** with chess.js for the prefix SAN list (reuse the file's `applyUci`/`replayLine`). Each node's `moveListSan = prefixSan.slice(0, lineIndex).concat(node.view.san)` — no per-node replay, since `node.san` is already present. `moveListStartPly = 1` (tree lines always start at White's move 1). Root/synthesized node → `moveListSan: []`.

---

## `OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx` — the card itself

Unify both `kind`s: header = name, secondary = move list. Preserve `/openings`-only metadata (score/grade, eval, Off-book / Your-move chips).

- **Root predicate (Finding 2)** — "Starting position" is ONLY the `/openings` synthesized root, never a family card (whose `san` is also null and whose `moves` may defensively be `[]`). Guard with: `kind === "move" && node.ply === 0 && node.san === null && node.openingName == null`. Family cards always render name + (possibly empty) move list, never "Starting position".
- **`CompactBody`** (~L261):
  - Primary line: `formatOpeningName(node.openingName)` (truncated) + `score` + `GradeTag` (right). Same for both kinds.
  - Secondary line: move-list tokens (truncated, last bold). `move` kind also keeps the chips (before the list) and `eval` (right, `margin-left:auto`). `family` kind: just the move list (drop the ECO line).
  - Root: "Starting position", no secondary.
- **`ExpandedBody`** (~L326):
  - Header top label (`.tree-node-card__move-label`) = `formatOpeningName(node.openingName)` for **both** kinds (`move` kind switches away from `formatMoveLabel`).
  - New secondary line under the header = move-list tokens (wrapping, last bold). `move` kind keeps chips adjacent; `family` kind has none.
  - Score/eval panel, metrics, terminal note, Start Drill button: unchanged.
- **"View in Openings" into the card (Finding 5)** — keep the card router-free. Add an optional `footerAction?: ReactNode` prop; render it inside the expanded body **above** the full-surface `onCollapse` overlay (same raised z-index as the drill button) with `stopPropagation` so a tap doesn't collapse the card. `OpeningTreeNodeCard` does **not** import `react-router` / build `<a>`.

## `GameOpeningLineage.tsx`
- Accept a `startPly` prop; `toNodeView` sets `moveListSan`/`moveListStartPly`.
- Expanded branch (~L121–143): stop rendering the external `<Link>` sibling; pass `footerAction={<Link to={openingsHref} onClick={stopPropagation}>View in Openings</Link>}` into the card (this component already owns `react-router` `Link`). Keep the `opening_key` href via `buildOpeningsSearchParams`.
- Score-diff badge sibling (g-3gmc, ~L167) unchanged.

## `/openings` — `OpeningsPage.tsx` / `treeView.ts`
- No structural page change. Column headers already show the selected move (`formatMoveLabel`), which now complements the name-led cards.
- Only `treeView.ts` changes: compute `moveListSan` + `moveListStartPly=1`.

---

## `/play` wiring — `ChessGame.tsx`

The lineage in `openingLineageSlot` (~L1894) passes neither `onSelectRoot` nor `onStartDrill` (expand-only during live play — must not move the live board). Gate both new behaviors on **game ended** (`gameResult !== null`):

- **Board navigation (history parity)** — add `handleLineageSelectRoot(item)`: find `idx` in `moveHistory` where `normalize_fen(m.fen) === normalize_fen(item.opening_key)` (`MoveRecord` has `fen`), then `handleNavigate(idx)`. Pass as `onSelectRoot` only when `gameResult !== null`; `undefined` while active.
- **Start Drill (Finding 1)** — add `handleLineageStartDrill(item)` that **mirrors the route-state intercept flow** (ChessGame.tsx:982–1030), NOT direct `openingFamilies` resolution (that list is null post-game until the overlay opens — it's fetched only when `showStartOverlay && isDrillMode`, ChessGame.tsx:1034). Do:
  1. `setIsDrillMode(true)`
  2. `adHocLineRef.current = null`
  3. `pendingDrillSetupRef.current = { openingKey: item.opening_key, playerColor }`
  4. `setShowStartOverlay(true)`
  
  Opening the overlay triggers the `getOpeningRoots()` fetch (L1034 effect); the existing roots-match effect (L1106–1121) then resolves `pendingDrillSetupRef` → `setSelectedDrillOpening`. Pass as `onStartDrill` only when `gameResult !== null`. Do **not** reuse `handleStartDrill` (needs a full `StartDrillDraft`) or `handleShowStartOverlay` alone (doesn't set drill mode / seed the ref).
- Use `playerColor` (not `openingLineagePlayerColor`) for these handlers, matching `/history`.

`/history` already wires `onSelectRoot`/`onStartDrill` — no change beyond the shared card/link/`startPly` updates.

---

## CSS — `src/App.css`

Card line styles ~L10127+ (`.tree-node-card__line*`, `__move`, `__name`, `__move-label`, `__name-line`), family move ~L10473, openings link ~L8501.

- Move-list line, compact: single line, `overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap`. Bold last token via a `--last`/`<strong>` span (weight 600–700).
- Move-list line, expanded: `white-space:normal` (wrap), no ellipsis.
- Name header: compact primary name truncates (`min-width:0` + ellipsis) as the lead; expanded header name wraps.
- Re-home `.opening-lineage-card__openings-link` styling to sit inside the expanded card footer; ensure it's above the collapse overlay (z-index) with a sensible tap target.

---

## Tests

- **Backend** `backend/test_session_openings.py`: assert each item's `moves` = played SAN prefix up to its boundary (e.g. Caro-Kann game → `["e4","c6","Bc4"]` for the Hillbilly Attack item); cover the multi-opening chain so prefixes grow broadest→deepest; assert `start_ply` (1 for a normal game). Add a case exercising the indexed walk (a **non-consecutive repeated root** gets its own crossing prefix, not the first). Add/verify a **drill** case so numbering is proven, not assumed.
- **`OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx`**: header = name on both kinds/variants; secondary renders the move list with the last move in a `<strong>`; compact truncation class vs expanded wrapping; `/openings` root (`kind="move"`, ply 0) shows "Starting position" with no move list; a family card with `moves: []` does **not** show "Starting position". Update the existing ECO-secondary assertion (~L440). `footerAction` renders inside the expanded card and its click doesn't collapse.
- **`treeView.test.ts`**: `moveListSan` correct for the **selected** node and **sibling** nodes in a column (shared prefix + differing last move); `moveListStartPly === 1`; root → `[]`.
- **`GameOpeningLineage.test.tsx`**: "View in Openings" link is now **inside** the expanded card (still `role=link`; ~L108/134/192/224); tapping it doesn't collapse.
- **`OpeningsPage.test.tsx`**: cards lead with the name; move list appears in the card.
- **`ChessGame.test.tsx`**: post-game (`gameResult !== null`) lineage shows Start Drill (mirrors route-state: drill mode on, overlay shown) and navigates the board on select; during active play neither is wired (board doesn't move).
- **`HistoryPage.test.tsx`**: wiring still works with the relocated link.
- **Fixtures/mocks**: add `moves: []` (and `start_ply`/`startPly` where a response is mocked) to **all** `OpeningLineageItem`/`SessionOpeningsResponse` test fixtures, not only the named-lineage tests, so the new required fields typecheck everywhere.

---

## Docs
- **Update `SPEC.md`** after implementation: the opening-card contract (name header + played move list, truncate/wrap) and the `/play` post-game lineage behavior (Start Drill + board navigation) have changed.

---

## Verification (end-to-end)

1. **Backend**: `cd backend && pytest test_session_openings.py test_opening_roots.py -q`.
2. **Frontend units**: `npx vitest run src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx src/components/GameOpeningLineage.test.tsx src/openings/treeView.test.ts src/pages/OpeningsPage.test.tsx src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx` (rerun any flaky file in isolation per project note).
3. **Manual / `/run`**:
   - `/openings`: cards lead with the opening name; secondary shows the move list with the last move bold; narrow columns truncate, expanded wraps.
   - `/history`: a game with a known opening → family cards show name + played move list; "View in Openings" is inside the expanded card and navigates without collapsing; Start Drill + board-jump work.
   - `/play`: mid-game the lineage is expand-only (no board move, no Start Drill); after the game ends, Start Drill opens the pre-seeded drill setup and selecting a card jumps the post-game board to that opening's position.
   - Drill lineage: move numbers are correct (start_ply honored).

---

## Risks / edge cases
- **`/openings` name repetition**: expected per the confirmed design; bold last move + column header disambiguate.
- **Collapse overlay vs. links/buttons**: the in-card `footerAction` link and Start Drill must stay clickable above the full-surface collapse overlay (z-index + `stopPropagation`).
- **Long move lists in expanded mode**: wrapping is intended; confirm the card grows gracefully in the tree column and the history/play footer.
- **Non-consecutive repeated roots**: handled by the indexed walk (each crossing keeps its own prefix); also confirms React keys — if duplicate `opening_key`s can appear in one lineage, keys in `GameOpeningLineage` must include the index.
close_reason: Implemented: name-led opening cards + played move list on all surfaces (/openings, /play, /history); backend moves/start_ply + indexed chain walk; /play post-game Start Drill + board navigation (nav also during play per user); per-occurrence lineage keys/jumps.

title: Move Review Warning onto board
description: Move the Review warning out of the info panel, or wherever it is on mobile layouts, onto the chessboard similar to how the best move streak is shown on top of the chessboard. The warning should show for a few seconds and then get out of the way so the player can play the game. After success or failure show the box with the green checkmark or red x but for a shorter amount of time. Get rid of the warning stack concept that never seemed to work right anyway. Only show one warning box at a time. A new Review Warning message has higher priority than a Review Warning success/fail message. It's OK if we lost the  success/fail message since it's also shown in MoveList.
design:
# g-vdn2 — Move Review Warning onto the board

## Context

The "Review Position" warning ("This position has come back to haunt you…") and its
pass/fail result (green ✓ / red ✗) currently live in a **warning stack** —
`GameWarningStack` in `GameInfoPanel.tsx`, rendered twice: once inside the desktop
info panel (`.chess-warning-stack--panel`) and once below the board on mobile
(`.chess-warning-stack--mobile`, grid-area `notices`). The stack also houses the
engine→ghost "The haunting resumes" rehook toast.

Problems the user wants fixed:
- The warning is off to the side / below the board, not on the board where attention is.
- The pending warning stays up the **entire** time the player sits on the review FEN
  (`isReviewMomentActive`) instead of showing briefly and getting out of the way.
- The pass/fail box also lingers (cleared only on the next move).
- The "stack" can show two boxes at once and "never worked right."

**Goal:** Render a single board-anchored notice (like the bottom-right best-move
**streak toast**), top-left of the board, auto-dismissing after a few seconds.
Delete the warning-stack concept entirely. Show exactly **one** box at a time, with
a new Review warning preempting a showing pass/fail box. Losing the pass/fail box is
acceptable — it's also recorded in the MoveList.

**Decisions confirmed with user:**
- Rehook "haunting resumes" toast → **fold into the single board notice** (lowest
  priority; a Review warning preempts it). Stack is fully removed.
- Position → **top-left** of `.chessboard-board-area` (streak toast stays bottom-right;
  no collision).

## Current implementation (reference)

- `isReviewMomentActive` derived in `ChessGame.tsx:497` (at review FEN, game active,
  player's turn, viewing live, not over) → drives the pending "Review Position" warning.
- `resolvedReview` state (`ChessGame.tsx:227`); set to `{result:"pending"}` when the
  player makes the targeted review move (`useChessGameController.ts:262`), updated to
  `pass`/`fail` when graded (`DecisionOwner.ts:668`), cleared on the next move
  (`useChessGameController.ts:226-227`) — **no timer today**.
- `showRehookToast` state (`ChessGame.tsx:232`), auto-cleared after 3s
  (`ChessGame.tsx:1459-1463`).
- `GameWarningStack` renders both messages (`GameInfoPanel.tsx:155-222`), used in panel
  (`GameInfoPanel.tsx:522`) and mobile (`ChessGame.tsx:1976`).
- Streak toast is the pattern to mimic: rendered in `.chessboard-board-area`
  (`BoardStage.tsx:153-166`), `.streak-toast` CSS absolute bottom-right, z-index 8,
  `blunder-toast-in` 250ms; auto-dismissed after 2400ms (`ChessGame.tsx:1467`).
- `blocksStreakToast` (`ChessGame.tsx:503-511`) already suppresses the streak toast while
  any review/rehook signal is active — **left unchanged** (still derived from the same
  signals; keeps mixed "you blundered" + "best moves" messaging from co-occurring).

## Design: single-slot board notice with a tiny state machine

### New type (`src/components/chess-game/types.ts`, beside `ResolvedReview`)
```ts
export type BoardNotice =
  | { kind: "review-warning"; nonce: number }
  | { kind: "review-result"; result: "pass" | "fail"; nonce: number }
  | { kind: "rehook"; nonce: number };
```
`nonce` is a monotonically increasing counter so re-triggering the same kind restarts
the entrance animation (React `key`) and the dismiss timer.

### New hook `src/hooks/useBoardNotice.ts`
Inputs: `{ isReviewMomentActive, resolvedReview, showRehookNotice, isViewingLive }`.
Output: `BoardNotice | null`.

> **`showRehookNotice` is pre-gated by the caller.** The old stack rendered rehook only
> when `isGameActive && opponentMode === "ghost" && showRehookToast`
> (`GameInfoPanel.tsx:199`). To preserve that, `ChessGame.tsx` computes
> `const showRehookNotice = isGameActive && opponentMode === "ghost" && showRehookToast;`
> and passes it in. The hook does **not** see raw `showRehookToast`/`opponentMode`.

Holds `const [notice, setNotice] = useState<BoardNotice | null>(null)` and a nonce ref.
Trigger semantics (rising-edge via refs holding the previous value):

- **review-warning** — single effect on `[isReviewMomentActive]` handling **both edges**
  (rising/falling via a `prevReviewActiveRef`):
  - false→true: `setNotice({kind:"review-warning", nonce:++})`. Always preempts (highest
    priority). Re-entering the FEN re-fires.
  - true→false: **clear a showing warning** —
    `setNotice(p => p?.kind === "review-warning" ? null : p)`. **This is the High-severity
    fix:** when the player makes the targeted review move, the controller synchronously
    clears the target and flips `resolvedReview` to `pending`
    (`useChessGameController.ts:252,262`) while the grade arrives later
    (`DecisionOwner.ts:668`). `isReviewMomentActive` falls false on that same commit, so the
    stale warning is removed *immediately* (it gets out of the way) instead of lingering for
    the rest of its 4s timer during the grading wait. Also covers navigating away. The 4s
    auto-dismiss remains as the fallback for a player who just sits on the FEN.
- **review-result** — effect on `[resolvedReview, isViewingLive]` (both in deps to satisfy
  `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`; replay is prevented by the key, not by omitting a dep).
  Track a `lastResultKey` ref (`analysisId + result`). When `resolvedReview` is `pass`/`fail`
  and its key `!== lastResultKey`: **always** set `lastResultKey = key` (mark seen), then
  show **only if `isViewingLive`** → `setNotice({kind:"review-result", result, nonce:++})`.
  Correctness from review: a result graded while scrubbed to history
  (`isViewingLive === false`) is marked seen but **never shown**; when `isViewingLive`
  later returns true the effect re-runs but the key already matches → it **skips** (no
  replay). When `resolvedReview?.result === "pending"`, this effect also clears any showing
  warning (`setNotice(p => p?.kind === "review-warning" ? null : p)`) as a belt-and-braces
  guard alongside the falling-edge clear above. **Pending itself is never shown.** (Losing a
  scrubbed result box is acceptable — it's in the MoveList.)
- **rehook** — on `showRehookNotice` false→true (effect on `[showRehookNotice]`): fill the
  slot **only if** current notice is null or already `rehook`
  (`setNotice(prev => prev && prev.kind !== "rehook" ? prev : {kind:"rehook", nonce:++})`).
  Never stomps a review notice.
- **not-live** — effect on `[isViewingLive]`: `if (!isViewingLive) setNotice(null)` so no
  notice lingers off-live.

All effects keep `setNotice` (stable) out of needing deps and use refs for previous-value
tracking, so each effect's dep array is exactly the signal(s) it reads — lint-clean under
`reactHooks.configs.flat.recommended` (`eslint.config.js`).

This yields the required priority: a new Review warning > a showing pass/fail box; rehook
is lowest. (No static priority table needed — warning↔result are strictly sequential per
review because `resolvedReview` is only set *after* the player moves off the warning FEN;
the only cross-conflict the issue names — new warning preempting a result on back-to-back
reviews — is handled by the warning trigger always preempting.)

**Auto-dismiss** — effect on `[notice]`: schedule `setTimeout` by kind, on fire clear only
if nonce still matches (`setNotice(p => p?.nonce === n ? null : p)`):
- review-warning: **4000ms** ("a few seconds")
- review-result: **2000ms** ("shorter amount of time")
- rehook: **3000ms** (matches today's behavior)

**Clear** when `isViewingLive` flips to false (scrubbing history) so notices don't linger
off-live. (`isReviewMomentActive` already includes `isViewingLive`, so its edge won't fire
while scrubbing.)

A focused `useBoardNotice.test.ts` (vitest, `vi.useFakeTimers`) covers, independent of the
heavy ChessGame harness:
- warning rising edge shows; auto-dismiss at 4s; re-entry re-fires.
- **warning clears immediately when `isReviewMomentActive` falls false** (player made the
  review move) — does not wait for the 4s timer.
- pending (`resolvedReview.result === "pending"`) shows nothing and clears any warning.
- result pass/fail shows; auto-dismiss at 2s.
- a new warning preempts a showing result; rehook never stomps a review notice; rehook
  auto-dismiss at 3s.
- a result graded while `isViewingLive === false` is never shown and never replays after
  `isViewingLive` returns to `true`.

### Wiring in `ChessGame.tsx`
- Compute the pre-gated rehook flag:
  `const showRehookNotice = isGameActive && opponentMode === "ghost" && showRehookToast;`
- Call `const boardNotice = useBoardNotice({ isReviewMomentActive, resolvedReview, showRehookNotice, isViewingLive });`
- Pass `boardNotice={boardNotice}` to `<BoardStage>`.
- **Delete** the mobile `<GameWarningStack className="chess-warning-stack--mobile" …/>`
  (`1976-1985`).
- **Remove** the warning/rehook props passed into `<GameInfoPanel>`
  (`isReviewMomentActive`, `resolvedReview`, `isViewingLive`, `showRehookToast`,
  `onDismissRehookToast`, lines `1906-1910`).
- Remove the `{ GameWarningStack }` named import (`55`); keep default `GameInfoPanel`.
- Remove `handleDismissRehookToast` (was only wired to the deleted toast) — verify no other
  callers. Keep `showRehookToast` state + its setter + the existing 3s reset effect
  (`1459-1463`) so the flag re-arms for the next engine→ghost switch; `useBoardNotice`
  consumes its rising edge and owns the *visible* timing.
- Leave `blocksStreakToast` untouched.

### `BoardStage.tsx`
- Add `boardNotice: BoardNotice | null` to `BoardStageProps` + destructure.
- Render one element inside `.chessboard-board-area` (after the streak toast block),
  keyed by `nonce`, mirroring the streak-toast JSX. Reuse the **local** `WarningTriangleIcon`
  already defined in this file (`75-86`). **Note:** that icon currently has
  `className="review-warning-toast__icon"` and is *also* used by the revert/resign warning
  dialogs (`BoardStage.tsx:311,362`) — see the CSS section for the shared-class fix so
  deleting the review-warning rules doesn't strip the dialogs' icon styling.
  `role="alert"` + `aria-live="assertive"` for the
  warning; `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` otherwise:
  - review-warning: triangle icon + "Review Position" + short detail
    ("You've blundered here before.").
  - review-result: large ✓ / ✗ + short label.
  - rehook: "The haunting resumes" / "Steering to past mistake" (existing copy).

  Keep the literal text **"Review Position"** (e2e asserts it).

### CSS (`src/App.css`) + shared icon class (Finding 1)
- **Shared warning-icon class (do this first):** `BoardStage.tsx`'s `WarningTriangleIcon`
  uses `.review-warning-toast__icon` (`App.css:2771-2774`: `flex:0 0 auto; color:
  var(--warning-dark);`) and is also rendered by the revert/resign dialogs
  (`BoardStage.tsx:311,362`). Introduce a neutral shared rule `.warning-triangle-icon`
  with those same declarations, and change `BoardStage.tsx:77` to
  `className="warning-triangle-icon"`. The new board notice reuses the same local icon, so
  it inherits the class for free. This decouples the icon from the deleted review rules.
- **Add** `.board-notice` rules next to `.streak-toast` (~2650): `position:absolute;
  top:0.75rem; left:0.75rem; z-index:8; max-width:min(70%,22rem); pointer-events:none;
  animation:blunder-toast-in 250ms ease-out;` plus per-kind borders/backgrounds reusing
  existing tokens (`--warning`/`--warning-bg`/`--warning-dark`, `--success`,
  `--eval-blunder`, `--status-ghost`, `--overlay-bg`). Keep `@keyframes blunder-toast-in`
  and `review-overlay-in`.
- **Delete** now-dead rules: `.chess-warning-stack`, `.chess-warning-stack--mobile`
  (`2653-2663`), `.rehook-toast*` (`2665-2690`), and `.review-warning-toast*`
  (`2741-2848`) — but **only after** the icon rule has been re-homed as
  `.warning-triangle-icon` (don't leave `BoardStage`'s revert/resign icon unstyled).
  Also delete their media-query blocks: panel `order` (`8049-8051`), the mobile overrides
  (`8258-8294`), and the `notices` grid-area templates (`8461-8473`).
  **Keep** `.review-fail-panel*` (`2693-2738`) — that's the separate `reviewFailModal`
  feature, untouched by this issue.

## Tests to update (selectors/behavior change)

- `src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx` (~18 assertions, `2616-3183`): rewrite
  `.review-warning-toast*` / `.chess-warning-stack .rehook-toast` / "The haunting resumes"
  checks to the new `.board-notice*` DOM, and switch the lingering-presence checks to the
  new timed model (`vi.useFakeTimers` + `advanceTimersByTime`) — warning auto-dismisses at
  4s, result at 2s, and a new warning preempts a showing result.
- `src/components/chess-game/ui/GameInfoPanel.test.tsx` (`39`, `223-245`): remove the

- `e2e/mobile-game-layout.spec.ts` (`59-116`): replace the below-board

- `e2e/game-blunder-ghost-srs.spec.ts` (`126`): `getByText("Review Position")` still works

## Verification

Use non-watch commands and the full frontend gate (`build` runs `tsc -b && vite build`,
so it catches the Vite path that `tsc -b` alone misses):

title: Batch ghost-graph existence checks in _upsert_session_position_graph
description: _upsert_session_position_graph (backend/app/api/session.py:389) does per-move queries: ensure_position runs a Position lookup per FEN and an existing-Move check per move. For a 20-move upload that's ~60 sequential round-trips (~1.2s at 20ms RTT) — the ghost_graph_upsert=1188ms log lines.
design:
# g-wlzj — Batch ghost-graph existence checks in `_upsert_session_position_graph`

## Context

`_upsert_session_position_graph` (`backend/app/api/session.py:410`) teaches the ghost
graph from uploaded game moves. It does **per-move DB round-trips**:

- `ensure_position(fen)` runs a `Position` `.first()` lookup per unique FEN, and a
  `db.flush()` per newly-created position (`session.py:447`, `:463`).
- the main loop runs an existing-`Move` `.first()` check per valid move (`session.py:484`).

For a 20-move upload that's ~60 sequential round-trips. Against the ~20ms-RTT Railway
Postgres this is the `ghost_graph_upsert=1188ms` log line (parent epic g-3dvu). The fix
(matching the already-shipped g-b809 pattern for opportunity events) is to replace the
per-row loops with a small fixed number of **bulk queries** and resolve everything
in-memory.

**Acceptance:** O(1) bulk lookups per upload instead of O(moves) round-trips;
`ghost_graph_upsert` stage drops to ~100ms; graph upsert results identical (same
positions/edges created, identical `GhostGraphUpsertStats`).

## Decision — edge visibility (resolves the flush-invariant question)

The opportunity BFS `_forward_reachable_position_ids` (`session.py:319`) reads `Move`
edges via DB query and runs in the **same transaction** immediately after the graph
upsert (`session.py:763 → 552`). With `autoflush=False` (`app/db.py:40`) it only sees
**flushed** edges. Today the incidental `db.flush()` in `ensure_position` (`session.py:463`)
leaks *most* of this upload's edges into the BFS — but not edges staged after the last
new position. That is flush-order-dependent and undefined.

**Chosen behavior: flush ALL fresh edges before the BFS runs.** Add a single
`db.flush()` at the **end** of `_upsert_session_position_graph`, after all `Move`s are
staged. This:
- matches the forward-reachable docstring's definition (reachability over the full
  forward graph, including this upload's edges);
- is a strict **superset** of current production behavior (today already leaks most
  edges) — smallest behavior change, only newly exposes the tail edges;
- keeps the edge-INSERT cost attributed to the `ghost_graph_upsert` timing stage (not
  misattributed to the compute stage) — consistent with the *purpose* of the comment at
  `session.py:595-601`, which is about timing attribution, not a correctness contract.

**Stale comments to update (all of them, not just `:595`):**
- `session.py:595-601` — no longer "deferred to commit"; edges flush at end of the
  ghost-graph upsert stage.
- `session.py:776-784` — the `evidence_commit` stage no longer "owns the graph-edge
  flush"; it owns the COMMIT (durability) only. Duplicate-edge `IntegrityError`s now
  surface during the Phase 6 flush (the `ghost_graph_upsert` stage), not at
  `evidence_commit`. Update the wording accordingly.
- `scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py:131-133` — its explicit `db.flush()` becomes redundant
  (the upsert now flushes its own edges in Phase 6, so the next session's dedup SELECTs
  already see them). Remove the now-redundant `db.flush()` and its comment (or, if kept,
  re-comment it as a defensive no-op).

A regression test pins the flush behavior (see Verification).

## Current behavior (must be preserved exactly)

Per move, in order:
1. `move_matches_fens(move)` — CPU-only python-chess validation (no DB). Fail → `invalid_moves += 1`, skip.
2. Pass → `valid_moves += 1`.
3. `from_id = ensure_position(fen_before)`, `to_id = ensure_position(fen_after)`. If either `None` → skip (no edge, no counter).
4. `edge_key = (from_id, move_san)`. If in `pending_edges` (in-batch dedup) → `edges_existing += 1`, skip.
5. Else DB check `Move(from_position_id=from_id, move_san=move_san)`. Exists → `edges_existing += 1`, skip.
6. Else stage `db.add(Move(...))`, `pending_edges.add(edge_key)`, `edges_created += 1`.

Invariants to keep:
- `valid_moves` counts every move passing `move_matches_fens`, even if a later id is `None`.
- First-seen `fen_raw`/`active_color` wins for a given hash (normalize_fen strips move
  clocks, so transposed positions share a hash but differ in raw FEN). Order: `fen_before`
  then `fen_after` within each move, in move order.
- A `Move` from a **newly-created** position can never pre-exist this txn → only
  pre-existing from-positions can have existing edges.
- Per valid-move occurrence, exactly one of `edges_created` / `edges_existing` (or neither
  when an id is `None`).

## Plan — core rewrite of `_upsert_session_position_graph` (plus the comment/flush cleanups listed in Files)

Keep the signature, `GhostGraphUpsertStats`, the `pending_edges` set, and the nested
`move_matches_fens` helper. Drop the nested `ensure_position` (inlined into phases).

**Phase 1 — validate + hash (CPU only, no DB).** Iterate `moves` once:
- `move_matches_fens` fail → `invalid_moves += 1`, continue.
- else `valid_moves += 1`.
- Compute `h_before` (and color) then `h_after` (and color), **independently**, each in its
  own `try/except (IndexError, ValueError)`. For EACH that succeeds, record it into
  `hash_meta` (first-seen wins) — this is what guarantees the position is created/counted.
  This exactly mirrors today's unconditional `ensure_position(fen_before)` **then**
  `ensure_position(fen_after)` (both run, each independently creating/counting its position,
  even when the *other* returns `None` and the edge is dropped). Order: before then after.
- Append spec `(h_before, h_after, move.move_san)` to an ordered `valid_specs` list **only
  if both `h_before` and `h_after` succeeded** (else the edge is dropped, but any
  successfully-computed position metadata is still recorded above → same `positions_created`).
- `hash_meta: dict[str, (fen_raw, color)]` preserves insertion order — it is the ordered
  source of truth for both the lookup IN-set and new-position creation order.

**Phase 2 — bulk-fetch existing positions (1 SELECT).** Guard `if hash_meta:`
```python
for pid, fh in (
    db.query(Position.id, Position.fen_hash)
    .filter(Position.user_id == user_id, Position.fen_hash.in_(hash_meta.keys()))
    .all()
):
    hash_to_position_id[fh] = pid
```

**Phase 3 — bulk-create new positions (1 flush).** Iterate `hash_meta` **in insertion
order** (NOT a set — fixes stable-id ordering): for each hash not in
`hash_to_position_id`, build `Position(user_id, fen_hash=h, fen_raw=<first-seen>,
active_color=<first-seen>)`, `db.add`, collect into `new_positions`. One `db.flush()`
assigns all ids (SQLAlchemy 2.x `insertmanyvalues` → batched RETURNING on PG). Then
`hash_to_position_id[h] = pos.id` for each; `positions_created += len(new_positions)`.

**Phase 4 — bulk-fetch existing moves (1 SELECT).** Resolve `from_id`/`to_id` per spec
from `hash_to_position_id` (skip specs with a missing hash — defensive `None`). Collect
`candidate_from_ids = {from_id}` over resolvable specs. Guard `if candidate_from_ids:`
```python
existing_edges = {
    (fid, san)
    for fid, san in db.query(Move.from_position_id, Move.move_san)
    .filter(Move.from_position_id.in_(candidate_from_ids))
    .all()
}
```
(Filter by `from_position_id` only — slight sibling-SAN over-fetch, one round-trip; new
from-ids return nothing.)

**Phase 5 — resolve + stage edges in-memory (no round-trips).** Iterate `valid_specs` in
order; resolve `from_id`/`to_id`; missing → continue. Then exact check order:
- `edge_key in pending_edges` → `edges_existing += 1`, continue.
- `edge_key in existing_edges` → `edges_existing += 1`, continue.
- else `db.add(Move(...))`, `pending_edges.add(edge_key)`, `edges_created += 1`.

**Phase 6 — single `db.flush()`** (per Decision) so all staged edges are visible to the
immediately-following BFS. Return `stats`.

**Round-trips:** ~3 SELECT/flush logical ops (positions SELECT + positions flush + moves
SELECT) plus the final edge flush — independent of move count, vs ~60 today. The SELECT
side is exactly the bead's "O(1) bulk lookups" criterion.

## Why this is safe for both call sites

- **Live path** (`session.py:763`): runs under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(user_id)`
  (`session.py:754`) → no concurrent same-user graph txn → no racing inserts of the same
  `(user_id, fen_hash)`; `uq_positions_user_fen_hash` backstops. Final flush replaces the
  incidental per-position flushes; the caller's commit (`session.py:776`) now only
  finalizes durability.
- **Backfill** (`scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py:120`): calls once per session; Phase 6
  now flushes each call's positions+edges, so a later session's Phase 2/4 SELECTs see the
  prior session's data — same cross-session dedup as today, which is exactly why the
  backfill's own per-session `db.flush()` (line 133) becomes redundant and is removed. No
  lock, same as today.

## Edge cases

- Empty `moves` / no valid moves → `hash_meta` empty (skip Phase 2/3), `candidate_from_ids`
  empty (skip Phase 4), no edges (Phase 6 flush is a no-op). Avoids `IN ()`. Zeroed stats.
- `fen_before == fen_after`: single position, self-edge — identical to today.
- Hash-compute failure on a validated move: practically impossible (both FENs already
  parsed by `move_matches_fens`), but handled to keep the `None`-skip path.

## Files

- `backend/app/api/session.py` — rewrite `_upsert_session_position_graph` body (~410–503);
  add the final `db.flush()` (Phase 6); update the stale comments at `:595-601` and
  `:776-784` (see Decision). No signature/return change. `postgresql_insert` already
  imported but not needed (ORM `add`+`flush` suffices); no new imports expected.
- `backend/scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py` — remove the now-redundant `db.flush()` at
  `:133` and its `:131-132` comment (Phase 6 flushes edges inside the upsert).
- `backend/test_backfill_ghost_graph.py` — add parity + perf-guard tests (below).
- `backend/test_srs_opportunity.py` — add the fresh-edge-visibility regression test
  (reuses its existing `event.listen(..., "before_cursor_execute", ...)` counter pattern,
  e.g. `_count_moves_queries`, `test_srs_opportunity.py:637-669`).

## Verification

Existing (must stay green, unchanged):
- `cd backend && pytest test_backfill_ghost_graph.py -v` — all 5 tests (happy path
  edges=2, incoherent skip, idempotent existing=1, dry-run, user scoping).
- `cd backend && pytest test_srs_opportunity.py -v` — opportunity math/BFS unaffected.

New REQUIRED tests (the perf contract is acceptance, not optional):
1. **O(1) lookups (perf guard).** Add a **NEW SELECT-only** counter — do NOT reuse
   `_MovesTableQueryCounter` (`test_srs_opportunity.py:637`), which counts ANY statement
   touching `moves` and would now also tally Phase 6's `INSERT INTO moves`, breaking the
   `== 2` assertion / asserting the wrong contract. Model it on the
   `before_cursor_execute` + verb-classification pattern already used by
   `_OpportunityEventWriteCounter` (`test_srs_opportunity.py:687-695`): count only
   statements whose leading verb is `select` AND that touch `positions`/`moves`. Run with a
   2-move and a 10-move transposition-free input; assert the SELECT count is **identical
   and == 2** (one positions lookup + one moves lookup) regardless of move count, and **0**
   for empty input. This is the precise "O(1) bulk lookups" criterion (dialect-stable;
   INSERT batching is a PG-only property confirmed via the live `ghost_graph_upsert` log).
2. **In-batch duplicate-edge accounting.** Feed the same `(fen_before, move_san)` edge
   twice in one call; assert `edges_created == 1`, `edges_existing == 1`.
3. **Pre-existing (from_id, move_san) edge.** Seed+commit an edge, then upload the same
   edge; assert `edges_created == 0`, `edges_existing == 1`, no duplicate row.
4. **First-seen fen_raw on hash-equal FENs.** Two raw FENs that normalize to the same hash
   (differing only in halfmove/fullmove clocks) in one batch; assert one Position created
   and its `fen_raw` equals the first-seen raw.
5. **Fresh-edge visibility (pins the Decision).** Combined path where an opponent→player
   edge played THIS upload extends BFS reachability to a not-reached downstream blunder;
   assert the opportunity event IS created (proves Phase 6's flush exposes fresh edges to
   the BFS). Guards against silently reverting to defer-all.

Optional: watch the real `ghost_graph_upsert` log drop from ~1.2s to ~100ms on a live
upload.
acceptance_criteria: O(1) bulk lookups per upload instead of O(moves) round-trips; ghost_graph_upsert stage drops to ~100ms; graph upsert results identical (same positions/edges created).
close_reason: Batched ghost-graph existence checks into fixed bulk queries (6-phase rewrite); O(1) SELECTs per upload, Phase 6 flush exposes fresh edges to BFS. Tests + comments updated.

title: Avoid full opportunity recompute per increment + collapse end-of-session upload burst
description: opportunity_events recomputes ALL blunders on every /moves upload, including 1–2 move increments. At session end the frontend fires two overlapping uploads for the same session (src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts: flushPendingUploads + awaited uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd ~line 221), which serialize on the advisory lock so the last upload pays the sum (14.8s log line).
design:
# g-y90g — Plan: opportunity recompute once per finalize + collapse end-of-session upload burst

## Context: what g-yjtn already changed (re-baseline)

This issue was written against the OLD inline pipeline. Sibling g-yjtn (committed,
2b908b8) already moved the expensive graph/opportunity/analysis-cache/recompute
pipeline OFF the /moves request path into `app/session_evidence_scheduler.py`:

- `POST /moves` now: validate → bulk-upsert `session_moves` → commit → `enqueue_session_evidence(...)` → return. The request is cheap; it no longer holds the advisory lock.
- `SessionEvidenceScheduler` (one daemon thread, single-process) coalesces by `session_id` (debounce `quiet_window=1.5s`, `max_wait=10s`) and dedupes moves by `(move_number,color)` last-write-wins. Its docstring already claims to collapse the end-of-session burst into ONE worker run.

So acceptance #3 (request-path latency = SUM of queued recomputes) is largely solved
ALREADY. What g-y90g still must fix is the REMAINING waste:

1. **Every coalesced worker run still does a FULL opportunity recompute.** During play the coordinator's incremental uploader fires every `INCREMENTAL_UPLOAD_INTERVAL_MS=3000` (> the 1.5s quiet window), so each mid-game upload fires its OWN evidence run, each doing a full `_compute_blunder_opportunity_events` (forward BFS + load ALL user blunders + bulk DELETE/UPSERT). Only the final, complete recompute matters.
2. **Two concurrent `/moves` for the same session at finalize.** At game/drill end the incremental interval-timer auto-flush can run concurrently with the awaited `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` full upload (separate code path, no `uploadInFlight` guard between them).

## Key correctness facts established by tracing the data flow

- **Opportunity counters ARE read mid-game by ghost-move selection** (`game.py` `load_opportunity_counters`, ~line 390) — BUT that read passes `exclude_session_id=session_id`, deliberately excluding the in-progress session's own events (so an early ancestor touch can't flip the very blunder being steered toward to "not overdue" and kill steering). They are otherwise consumed only at session-end / next-drill / analysis-view (`app/srs_opportunity.py`). Net: the CURRENT session's own mid-game opportunity events are never consumed during its own play, so deferring THIS session's opportunity recompute to its final upload changes no mid-game reader's result. (Other sessions' events are already committed; this design never defers a session past its own finalize.)
- **The opening-score delta is INDEPENDENT of opportunity events** (grep: `opening_score_delta.py`/`opening_score_scheduler.py`/`opening_cache.py` never reference `BlunderOpportunityEvent`). The delta reads the ghost graph + opening cache. So gating opportunity does NOT affect `compute_opening_score_delta` correctness/freshness. The graph upsert + `request_recompute` must keep running per upload — they are NOT gated.
- **Opportunity is computed WHILE the session is still active**, by the final pre-terminal `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` (it runs `/moves` BEFORE `endGame`/`naturalEndDrill` flips `status="ended"`). For natural-end/abandoned drills, once ended `_should_run_session_move_evidence(...)` returns False (drill becomes hidden), so a post-end trigger would no-op. → **We must NOT gate opportunity on "session ended"** (that would silently drop opportunity for drills entirely). The correct discriminator is **"is this the final / complete upload"**, which the FRONTEND knows (`uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` vs the incremental uploader). This is the load-bearing reason the design is a request flag, not a backend status check.

## Design — Part A (backend): opportunity recompute only on the final upload

Thread a per-upload boolean `recompute_opportunity` (default **True**) from the
`/moves` request → enqueue → coalesced entry (OR-folded) → worker → gate the
opportunity stage. Default True = a caller that omits it keeps today's behavior
(safe: compute, just slower); only the frontend's internal incremental uploader
opts OUT. This minimizes test churn and keeps the unsafe direction (drop accounting)
opt-in.

Files / symbols:

1. `backend/app/api/session.py`
   - `SessionMovesRequest` (line ~126): add `recompute_opportunity: bool = True`.
   - `upsert_session_moves` (line ~943): pass `recompute_opportunity=request.recompute_opportunity` into BOTH `enqueue_session_evidence(...)` calls (~1029 sqlite/generic path, ~1093 pg path).
   - `_run_session_move_evidence_side_effects` (line ~847): add param `run_opportunity: bool`; forward it into `_run_graph_evidence_txn(...)` via `graph_txn_kwargs`. analysis-cache write + `request_recompute` stay UNCONDITIONAL (outside the gate).
   - `_run_graph_evidence_txn` (line ~761): add param `run_opportunity: bool`; wrap ONLY the `opportunity_events` `_timed_side_effect` block + `_compute_blunder_opportunity_events(...)` call (~817-828) in `if run_opportunity:`. KEEP graph_lock + ghost_graph_upsert + evidence_commit unconditional. The opportunity recompute MUST stay in the SAME txn AFTER the graph upsert (so the forward BFS sees this upload's fresh edges) — preserve ordering; the final upload carries the full move history so its graph upsert includes all final edges.

2. `backend/app/session_evidence_scheduler.py`
   - `_Entry` (line ~56): add field `run_opportunity: bool`.
   - `_enqueue_locked` (line ~94): accept `run_opportunity`; new entry sets it from the arg; existing entry OR-folds: `entry.run_opportunity = entry.run_opportunity or run_opportunity`. (OR is what makes the burst-collapse correct: incremental(False) + final(True) → True → exactly one recompute.)
   - `enqueue` (line ~123): accept `run_opportunity: bool = True`; pass through.
   - `_run_one` (line ~261): pass `run_opportunity=entry.run_opportunity` into `self.run_side_effects(...)`.
   - `enqueue_session_evidence` (line ~318): accept `run_opportunity: bool = True`; forward to `_scheduler.enqueue`.
   - `_default_run_side_effects` (line ~299) already forwards `**kwargs`, so `run_opportunity` reaches `_run_session_move_evidence_side_effects` once that signature accepts it.

3. `backend/conftest.py`
   - `_sync_session_evidence._run_sync` (line ~478): add `run_opportunity: bool = True` to the shim signature and forward into `_run_session_move_evidence_side_effects(...)`. Default True keeps EXISTING endpoint tests (which POST a full move set and assert `BlunderOpportunityEvent`) green without edits.

## Design — Part B (frontend): one `/moves` at finalize + flag the final upload

1. `src/utils/api.ts`
   - `SessionMovesRequest` interface (line ~605): add `recompute_opportunity?: boolean`.
   - `uploadSessionMoves` (line ~866): extend options to `{ signal?: AbortSignal; recomputeOpportunity?: boolean }`; include `recompute_opportunity` in the JSON body only when defined (omitting → backend default True).

2. `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`
   - `flushIncrementalUpload` (line ~1709): pass `recomputeOpportunity: false` in the `uploadSessionMoves(...)` options. This is the ONLY opt-out site — mid-game uploads now do graph + analysis-cache + opening-recompute but SKIP opportunity.

3. `src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts`
   - **Fold the upload-stop INTO `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd`** (line ~221), not into each call site. As its FIRST step (before `buildSessionMoveUploads`), call `coordinator.stopSessionUploads()`, then pass `recomputeOpportunity: true` on the `uploadSessionMoves(...)` call. Rationale: this function is the single "final/complete pre-terminal upload" primitive and is the ONLY thing every terminal path shares — handleGameEnd (normal + drill natural-end), handleResign, AND the post-root drill accuracy-fail path in `ChessGame.tsx` (`stopPostRootDrillForAccuracy`, line ~1123). Folding the stop in makes the invariant "the final full upload is the last `/moves` this client emits" STRUCTURAL, so no terminal call site can forget it (this is exactly the accuracy-fail miss the review caught). `coordinator` is already in this function's closure.
   - Remove the now-redundant `coordinator.stopSessionUploads()` calls that the function makes structural: drill natural-end path ~line 308 and executeRevert ~line 468 become redundant for the FINAL-upload race (executeRevert still needs its own — see below). Leaving them is harmless (idempotent), but prefer removing the natural-end one for clarity.
   - `executeRevert` snapshot upload (line ~440): this path does NOT use `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` (it uploads a pre-revert `snapshotMoveHistory`, not the live `moveHistory`), so it keeps its own upload. Add `coordinator.stopSessionUploads()` BEFORE that `uploadSessionMoves(...)` (inside the `!isPracticeContinuation && isRated` block, ~line 434) and pass `recomputeOpportunity: true` (terminal resign-before-revert). The existing stop at ~line 468 then becomes redundant.
   - `stopSessionUploads()` only touches `uploadState` (disables the interval timer, clears dirty, aborts the in-flight fetch). `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` reads `useGameStore.moveHistory` + `coordinator.store.analysisMap` and calls `uploadSessionMoves` DIRECTLY, so it is unaffected by the disable. All callers are terminal (no resumed play on the same session), so permanent disable until the next `startSession` is correct.
   - The abandon paths (handleNewGame ~542, handleNewDrill ~671) use `flushPendingUploads()` (incremental path → `recomputeOpportunity=false`) + `await endGame("abandon")`. `endGame` is `/api/game/end`, not `/moves`, so there is no concurrent-`/moves` there — leave them. (See accepted-regression note on abandoned-game opportunity below.)

### Scope of the concurrency guarantee (revised per review — P1)

`stopSessionUploads()` is CLIENT-SIDE: it aborts the in-flight fetch and clears
`uploadInFlight`, but a request that has ALREADY reached FastAPI can still finish
committing `session_moves` + enqueuing evidence server-side. So this does NOT give
true server-side mutual exclusion of two `/moves` for one session. What it DOES
guarantee — and what the acceptance is narrowed to — is: **no NEW frontend
incremental upload is generated once finalize begins; the final full upload is the
last `/moves` this client emits.** Any already-dispatched in-flight incremental that
races to the server is HARMLESS because (a) `session_moves` upsert is idempotent
(ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), and (b) the evidence enqueue coalesces by `session_id`
(g-yjtn) — the in-flight one and the final one fold into ONE worker run, and only
the final (`recompute_opportunity=true`) entry's flag drives the single recompute.
This is the intended use of g-yjtn's coalescing and needs no extra plumbing.

OPTIONAL stronger guarantee (only if strict server-side single-flight is wanted):
expose the in-flight incremental upload promise from the coordinator and `await` it
(bounded by the existing 4s budget) BEFORE the final upload instead of aborting it.
Cost: serializes the (now-fast, post-g-yjtn) in-flight request ahead of the final
one, adding its latency to the terminal path. Not recommended given coalescing
already makes the duplicate harmless; listed so the choice is explicit.

## Data-flow walkthrough (finalize, normal game)

1. handleGameEnd: `coordinator.stopSessionUploads()` (kills incremental timer/in-flight).
2. `await uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` → `/moves` with `recompute_opportunity:true`, full history → commit session_moves → `enqueue_session_evidence(run_opportunity=True)`. Any still-pending incremental entry coalesces into the same `session_id` key; OR-fold → `run_opportunity=True`.
3. `await endGame` → status=ended; `compute_opening_score_delta` serves warm/unverified delta + `request_recompute` (opening cache; independent of opportunity).
4. Background worker (~1.5s later): ONE run → advisory lock → graph upsert (full edges) → opportunity recompute (forward BFS over fresh graph + all blunders) → commit → analysis-cache → `request_recompute`.
5. `pollFreshOpeningDelta` reconciles the banner once the opening recompute lands (unchanged).

Result: exactly ONE opportunity recompute at finalize; mid-game uploads do zero; one `/moves` in flight at finalize.

## Accepted regressions / risks (documented, consistent with existing posture)

- **Lost final upload ⇒ no opportunity recompute for the new moves.** If `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` times out (4s bound) or aborts and no `recompute_opportunity=true` upload lands, the session's opportunity events miss the latest moves (mid-game ones were skipped). This extends the scheduler's already-accepted "evidence may be dropped on failure" posture (module docstring). Self-heal: offline `scripts/recompute_srs_opportunities.py`. A backend backstop (terminal endpoint enqueues a flagged recompute) is intentionally NOT added: it cannot work for natural-end/abandoned drills (the post-end `_should_run_session_move_evidence` gate returns False), so it would be an asymmetric, normal-games-only patch.
- **Abandoned games (walk-away → new game) skip opportunity.** The abandon cleanup uses the incremental path (`recompute_opportunity=false`) and mid-game uploads no longer compute opportunity, so a never-finalized abandoned game contributes no opportunity events. Matches its best-effort/discarded-response nature; self-heals via the offline script. If undesirable, the abandon path can fire a flagged final upload (adds latency to "start new game") — left out by default.

## Test coverage

Backend (`backend/`):
- `test_session_evidence_scheduler.py`: (a) OR-fold — enqueue False then True (and True then False) for one `session_id` ⇒ entry `run_opportunity=True`; all-False burst ⇒ False. (b) `_run_one` forwards `run_opportunity` into `run_side_effects`.
- session/opportunity tests: with `run_opportunity=False`, `_run_graph_evidence_txn` does NOT call `_compute_blunder_opportunity_events` (no `BlunderOpportunityEvent` written) but DOES upsert the graph + run analysis-cache + `request_recompute`; with True it writes the event (in-txn, after graph upsert). Add via the conftest shim + an explicit `recompute_opportunity` on the POST body.
- `test_session_api.py`: a `/moves` POST with `recompute_opportunity=false` writes NO opportunity event; default/`true` writes it (guards the new field + default).
- Confirm existing opportunity-asserting endpoint tests stay green under the default-True shim.

Frontend (`src/`):
- `api.test` (or util): `uploadSessionMoves` includes `recompute_opportunity:false` in the body when `recomputeOpportunity:false`, and omits it otherwise.
- `GameAnalysisCoordinator.test`: incremental flush calls `uploadSessionMoves` with `recomputeOpportunity:false`.
- `useChessGameLifecycle.test`: `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` calls `coordinator.stopSessionUploads()` BEFORE its `uploadSessionMoves`, and that upload carries `recomputeOpportunity:true`. Because the stop is folded in, asserting it once on `uploadFullMoveHistoryBeforeEnd` covers handleGameEnd (normal + drill natural-end), handleResign, AND the accuracy-fail path — but still add a focused case per terminal entry point to lock the ordering (stop precedes upload). executeRevert: assert it stops uploads before its snapshot `uploadSessionMoves` and sends `recomputeOpportunity:true`.
- `ChessGame.test` (accuracy-fail / `stopPostRootDrillForAccuracy`): assert no incremental upload is emitted after the accuracy-fail final upload (regression guard for the review's P1 miss — covered structurally via the folded stop, no ChessGame.tsx change needed).

## Acceptance mapping
- "At most one full opportunity recompute per session end" ⇒ Part A (only the OR-folded final entry runs it; mid-game skip).
- "no two concurrent /moves for the same session at end" ⇒ Part B, NARROWED to client-side: no NEW incremental upload after finalize begins; the final full upload is the last `/moves` emitted. Any already-dispatched in-flight request is harmless via g-yjtn coalescing + idempotent upsert. (See "Scope of the concurrency guarantee".)
- "session-end latency no longer the SUM of queued recomputes" ⇒ g-yjtn (off-path) + Part A (mid-game queue no recomputes; one final recompute).

## Out of scope
- Touching graph upsert / analysis-cache cadence (kept per-upload; graph already optimized by g-wlzj).
- The opening-score scheduler / delta poll (unchanged; independent of opportunity).
- g-q6w5 (dev/prod DB target) — separate sibling.
acceptance_criteria: At most one full opportunity recompute per session end; no two concurrent /moves for the same session at end; end-to-end session-end latency no longer the SUM of queued recomputes.
close_reason: Implemented: opportunity recompute gated on recompute_opportunity flag (OR-folded in evidence scheduler) so it runs once at finalize; mid-game incremental uploads skip it; final upload folds in stopSessionUploads + flags recompute. Backend 1395 tests pass; frontend api/coordinator/lifecycle + accuracy guard green. Stale self-heal docs/log updated.
