title: Opening-baseline snapshot pays ~1.3s O(evidence) digest on every game/drill start (residual)
description:
# Opening-baseline snapshot pays ~1.3s O(evidence) digest on every game/drill start (even when fresh)

## Symptom
Even on the happy path with a provably-fresh cache and no concurrent load, capturing the opening-score
baseline at session start costs over a second. From server.log, first drill start of the session:

```
11:19:14 INFO opening_baseline_snapshot user_id=14 color=black source=cached_fresh snapshot_ms=1261.48
11:19:14 INFO POST /api/drills/start 201 1336.046ms ...
```

1261ms of a 1336ms request is the snapshot — and that is the BEST case (fresh, quiescent). This is the
residual floor under the pathological case tracked by the sibling bead (which addresses the 9.6s
recompute-in-flight blow-up via a cheap gate, but leaves this ~1.3s in place).

## Root cause
`snapshot_opening_baseline` (`backend/app/opening_score_delta.py:62`) proves cache freshness by
recomputing `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` (`backend/app/opening_evidence.py:646`) on the request thread.
That digest is O(all of the user's evidence). For user 14 / black:
- 22,416 `session_moves` rows fetched + string-hashed
- 9,387 distinct candidate FENs each normalized via python-chess `normalize_fen` in a Python loop

There is no cheaper way to PROVE freshness with the current design — proving requires re-deriving the
fingerprint and comparing it to the one stored on the batch. So the cost is inherent to the
"only snapshot when PROVABLY fresh" requirement that `g-fix-start-latency` chose.

## Why the conservative requirement exists
`snapshot_opening_baseline`'s contract (g-fix-start-latency): persist a baseline ONLY when the cache is
provably current; otherwise return None and show no end-of-session delta. Diffing a stale "before"
against a fresh "after" would over-attribute prior sessions' gains to the just-ended one. So it refuses
to trust a batch it cannot prove fresh — and proving fresh is the expensive part.

## Options (to be decided in design)
1. Background the snapshot off the request entirely. The baseline must exist before the first drill
   move uploads (so the end-of-session diff has a stable "before"), but the first move POST is itself a
   few seconds out; a fast async task that fills `GameSession.opening_score_baseline` shortly after the
   INSERT may land in time. Risk: race with a very fast first move; needs a defined fallback (treat
   missing baseline as "no delta", which is already the degraded behavior).
2. Accept "latest batch + no recompute scheduled" as a good-enough baseline WITHOUT recomputing the
   fingerprint. Cheaper, but weakens the provably-fresh guarantee the design deliberately chose — a
   batch can be stale even with no recompute scheduled (e.g. out-of-process evidence writes,
   post-restart first read), reintroducing some misattribution risk. Would need product sign-off on the
   accuracy/latency trade.
3. Make `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` itself cheaper / incremental (e.g. a maintained running digest or
   a max(updated_at)+count watermark per (user,color) instead of a full row hash). Largest change;
   benefits every caller of the digest, not just the snapshot.

## Dependency
Do the sibling cheap-gate bug first — it removes the user-visible 10s stalls. This bead is the residual
optimization on top and is lower priority.
design:
# Design: background the opening-baseline snapshot off the start hot path

Implement Option 1 from the issue description: move opening-baseline capture out of the
`POST /api/game/start` and `POST /api/drills/start` request path. Option 3, the cheaper/incremental
freshness signal, remains separate work in `g-jact`; this bead removes the O(evidence) digest from
session start now.

## Goal and acceptance

- `POST /api/game/start` and `POST /api/drills/start` do not invoke `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` on
  the request thread. Start latency should fall from the digest-dominated ~1.3-3.2s range to the
  existing insert/commit cost plus a best-effort scheduler enqueue.
- End-of-session opening-score delta correctness is preserved. A persisted
  `GameSession.opening_score_baseline` is either a proven pre-session snapshot or NULL. NULL degrades
  to "no delta"; it must never store a post-session baseline.

## Race model and correctness rule

Moving capture to a background job creates a race: this session's evidence may arrive before the
worker captures the baseline, and a recompute may fold that evidence into a fresh cached batch. The
session can contribute opening evidence through all of these paths:

1. `POST /api/session/{sid}/moves` inserts `session_moves` and calls `request_recompute`
   (`session.py:945`). These rows are hashed as `SM|` digest inputs (`opening_evidence.py:696`).
2. `POST /api/srs/review` inserts `blunder_reviews(session_id=sid)` and calls `request_recompute`
   (`srs.py:159,189`). These reviews are hashed as `BR|` digest inputs
   (`opening_evidence.py:875`), scoped through the reviewed blunder's color.
3. `POST /api/blunder` records `blunders(source_session_id=sid)` via `_record_target`
   (`blunder.py:316`; constructor field around `:253`, endpoint around `:336`). These targets are
   hashed as `GT|` digest inputs (`opening_evidence.py:858`).

Move uploads are batched by a ~3s timer and also flush after 4 dirty moves
(`src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:73-74`), so reviews or blunder targets can precede any
`session_moves` row. Freshness alone is insufficient: a batch that already includes this session can
still be fresh relative to the current evidence.

Persist a cached batch B as the session baseline only when both predicates hold:

- `_is_batch_fresh(db, B, rows)` is true, so `B.inputs_fingerprint` equals the digest of all current
  evidence.
- `B.computed_at < session.started_at`, strictly before the session start.

Before comparing timestamps, normalize both values to timezone-aware UTC. SQLite test paths and older
rows can return naive datetimes, so treat naive values as UTC, matching the existing guard around
`opening_cache.py:1155-1157`. The predicate is strict `<`: if `computed_at` equals `started_at`, the
batch cannot be proven pre-session from wall-clock values alone and must be rejected with
`source="skipped_post_session_batch"`.

The date guard must run after the cheap cached batch/rows lookup and before `_is_batch_fresh`. If
`not_after` is provided and `batch.computed_at >= not_after`, return
`(None, "skipped_post_session_batch")` without paying the O(evidence) digest.

## Required `computed_at` invariant

The timestamp rule is sound only if `batch.computed_at` is an upper bound on the evidence reads used to
build the batch. Today the recompute paths sample `computed_at` before their reads, which can mis-date
a post-session batch as pre-session. Make this invariant explicit:

- Add `_utcnow()` in `app/opening_cache.py` as a small seam around `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` so tests
  can control timestamp ordering.
- In `recompute_opening_scores`, remove the early default `computed_at = datetime.now(...)`. Resolve
  the fingerprint and overlay first, then set `computed_at = _utcnow()` immediately before
  `_build_cached_scores` when the caller did not provide an explicit value.
- In `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed`, keep the existing `now` used for decay-staleness checks, but
  stop passing `computed_at=now` into `recompute_opening_scores`. Let the writer sample `computed_at`
  after the already-built fingerprint and overlay have been passed in.

This changes `computed_at` from a lower bound to an upper bound for the data reflected in the batch.
The known consumers tolerate the shift: `_build_cached_scores` uses it as the decay as-of value, the
batch stores it, and the stale-decay gate still uses its own `now`.

With this invariant, freshness plus `computed_at < started_at` proves the cached rows cannot contain
any evidence from the session. If session evidence E had committed at or after `started_at` and the
worker observed a fresh batch, E would have to be part of B's fingerprint. But B's fingerprint reads
are bounded by `B.computed_at`, and `B.computed_at < started_at`, contradicting E's commit time. Evidence
that lands between the fingerprint read and overlay read is caught by freshness because the current
digest no longer matches B's stored fingerprint.

This proof is source-agnostic. Future evidence sources added to `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` are
covered as long as they participate in the digest and `computed_at` remains a post-read upper bound.

The rule is deliberately conservative. A recompute that reflects only pre-session evidence but finishes
just after session start is rejected, as is a genuine pre-session batch whose timestamp ties
`started_at` at clock resolution. Both cases lose delta coverage but never write a wrong baseline. The
background worker still has a race window equal to scheduling latency plus digest duration; under
contention it can GIL-serialize behind a recompute for up to the observed ~9.6s. The safe outcome is
NULL/no-delta.

## Defense-in-depth persist

After building a JSON baseline, persist it with a single conditional UPDATE that re-checks for
session-scoped evidence and idempotency:

```sql
UPDATE game_sessions
   SET opening_score_baseline = <json>
 WHERE id = <sid>
   AND status = 'active'
   AND user_id = <captured user_id>
   AND player_color = <captured player_color>
   AND opening_score_baseline IS NULL
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM session_moves WHERE session_id = game_sessions.id)
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blunder_reviews WHERE session_id = game_sessions.id)
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blunders WHERE source_session_id = game_sessions.id)
```

Build this as SQLAlchemy Core against typed ORM columns, not raw `text()` SQL. `game_sessions.id` is
`TEXT` in the SQLite test schema while production Postgres uses UUID; typed columns let SQLAlchemy bind
the UUID correctly on both backends. Bind `status`/`user_id`/`player_color` from the row the job loaded,
so the persisted baseline is the one it captured for:

```python
stmt = (
    update(GameSession)
    .where(GameSession.id == session_id)
    .where(GameSession.status == "active")
    .where(GameSession.user_id == session.user_id)
    .where(GameSession.player_color == session.player_color)
    .where(GameSession.opening_score_baseline.is_(None))
    .where(~select(SessionMove.id).where(SessionMove.session_id == GameSession.id).exists())
    .where(~select(BlunderReview.id).where(BlunderReview.session_id == GameSession.id).exists())
    .where(~select(Blunder.id).where(Blunder.source_session_id == GameSession.id).exists())
    .values(opening_score_baseline=json_str)
)
persisted = db.execute(stmt).rowcount == 1
db.commit()
```

The `status == "active"` predicate closes a real TOCTOU window: a session can transition out of active
between the step-3 read and this UPDATE, and re-checking it here makes the "only baseline an active
session" rule atomic with the write instead of trusting the earlier Python read. The `user_id` /
`player_color` predicates bind the write to the identity the baseline was captured for; because those
columns are immutable in practice they are defense-in-depth, but together with capturing from the row
(not the payload) they guarantee a persisted baseline can never belong to a different user/color than the
session it lands on — even under a mis-routed enqueue.

The timestamp/freshness rule is the primary proof; the `status`/identity and `NOT EXISTS` clauses are a
secondary safety net. `session_moves.session_id` is already indexed. `blunder_reviews.session_id` and
`blunders.source_session_id` are not indexed, so those two checks may table-scan. Accept the scans for
this bead because the UPDATE runs once per session start on the background worker and no migration is
otherwise needed. If they measure as material later, add indexes in a follow-up with its own migration
and test-schema DDL.

`blunder_reviews.session_id` is color-blind, while the digest projection scopes reviews through the
reviewed blunder's color. A cross-color review may therefore make the UPDATE reject a baseline the
primary proof would have allowed. That is acceptable: it loses coverage, not correctness.

## Scheduler architecture

Add `backend/app/opening_baseline_scheduler.py`, modeled on `session_evidence_scheduler.py`:

- A single daemon worker thread.
- In-memory dedupe keyed by `session_id`.
- No debounce; enqueue jobs as immediately due.
- Best-effort facade methods that log and never propagate failures into request handlers.
- Graceful shutdown with drain.
- DI-friendly `session_factory=SessionLocal` and `auto_start` controls.
- Synchronous `run_due()` test surface, matching the existing scheduler test pattern.

Public surface:

- `enqueue_baseline_snapshot(session_id, user_id, player_color)`
- `get_baseline_scheduler()`
- `OpeningBaselineScheduler.start()`
- `OpeningBaselineScheduler.shutdown(drain=True)`
- `OpeningBaselineScheduler.run_due()`

The worker obtains a fresh DB session from `session_factory()`, calls
`run_baseline_snapshot_job(db, session_id, user_id, player_color)`, and closes the DB session in
`finally`. Tests inject `TestingSessionLocal` or the Postgres test factory so `run_due()` writes to the
same database the assertions read.

Use a dedicated scheduler rather than piggybacking on the opening-score scheduler. The keys differ
(`session_id` vs `(user_id, color)`), the baseline worker should not sit behind a long recompute, and
the recompute scheduler stays untouched. The accepted tradeoff is occasional concurrent digest work
with the recompute worker; if a hard kill drops an enqueued baseline before completion, the session
degrades to NULL/no-delta.

## `app/opening_score_delta.py`

Split the current snapshot logic into one pure helper and two best-effort wrappers.

`_capture_baseline_json(db, user_id, player_color, *, not_after: datetime | None,
skip_when_inflight: bool) -> tuple[str | None, str]`:

- Pure helper: no `try/except`, no rollback, no logging, no timing `finally`.
- Reads the cached batch and rows via `list_cached_opening_scores`.
- If no batch exists, returns `"{}"` with `source="empty_no_evidence"` only when
  `has_opening_evidence` is false; otherwise returns `None` with `source="skipped_cold"`.
- If `not_after` is set and the normalized `batch.computed_at >= not_after`, returns
  `None, "skipped_post_session_batch"` before `_is_batch_fresh`.
- If `skip_when_inflight` is true, preserves the existing in-flight-only cheap gate from `g-1iul`.
- Otherwise proves freshness with `_is_batch_fresh`; stale batches return
  `None, "skipped_stale"`.
- Fresh accepted batches return `json.dumps({row.opening_key: row.opening_score for row in rows})`
  with `source="cached_fresh"`.
- Unexpected DB errors raise to the wrapper.

`snapshot_opening_baseline(db, user_id, player_color) -> str | None` remains as a thin best-effort
wrapper for direct tests and any legacy callers. It calls `_capture_baseline_json(..., not_after=None,
skip_when_inflight=True)`, catches errors, rolls back best-effort, returns None on failure, and logs the
existing `opening_baseline_snapshot ... source=... snapshot_ms=...` line. After this change, production
start handlers no longer call it.

`run_baseline_snapshot_job(db, session_id, user_id, player_color) -> str` owns worker behavior and its
own log line, `opening_baseline_job ... source=... snapshot_ms=...`. It must never raise.

The queued `user_id`/`player_color` are UNTRUSTED routing hints, not authoritative capture inputs. The
`GameSession` row already owns `user_id` (`models.py:194`) and `player_color` (`models.py:202`), and
`list_cached_opening_scores` reads the cached batch keyed on `(user_id, player_color)`
(`opening_cache.py:322-344`). A stale or buggy duplicate enqueue carrying the wrong pair would otherwise
make the job capture ANOTHER user's/color's cached scores and persist them onto this session — the
persist UPDATE only guarded `id` + NULL-baseline + no-session-evidence, none of which validate identity.
So the job always captures for the SESSION'S OWN `user_id`/`player_color` read from the row, and uses the
queued copies only for logging and one cheap sanity check. Flow:

1. `db.get(GameSession, session_id)` missing -> `"missing_session"`.
2. Existing `opening_score_baseline` -> `"already_set"` (idempotent).
3. `session.status != "active"` -> `"not_active"` (cheap early-exit; the UPDATE re-checks it atomically).
4. Sanity-check the hints: if `(user_id, player_color) != (session.user_id, session.player_color)`,
   return `"session_mismatch"` without capturing — a mis-routed/stale enqueue; safe-degrade to NULL and
   log it. Correctness does not depend on this check (capture uses the row either way); it exists to
   surface the upstream bug rather than silently do the right thing.
5. Call `_capture_baseline_json(db, session.user_id, session.player_color,
   not_after=session.started_at, skip_when_inflight=False)` — capture inputs come from the ROW, never the
   payload.
6. If the helper returns `None`, leave the baseline NULL and return its source.
7. Persist via the typed conditional UPDATE above, which re-checks `status == "active"` and the same
   `user_id`/`player_color` the row was captured for, so the status/identity pre-checks are atomic with
   the write. `rowcount == 1` returns the helper source; otherwise return
   `"raced_evidence_or_already_set"`.
8. On unexpected errors, guarded `db.rollback()`, return `"failed"`, and do not crash the worker.

The worker passes `skip_when_inflight=False` because it is off the request thread. Correctness comes
from the strict timestamp/freshness proof; the in-flight gate was only to protect synchronous start
latency.

## Start handlers and lifespan

`app/api/game.py` `start_game` and `app/api/drills.py` `start_drill`:

- Remove the synchronous `snapshot_opening_baseline(...)` call.
- Construct `GameSession(opening_score_baseline=None, ...)`.
- After `db.add(session); db.commit(); db.refresh(session)`, call
  `enqueue_baseline_snapshot(session.id, user.user_id, request.player_color.value)` best-effort.
- The endpoint must still return 201 if enqueueing fails.

`app/main.py` lifespan:

- Startup calls `get_baseline_scheduler().start()` best-effort alongside the existing schedulers.
- Shutdown drains the baseline scheduler first. It is a leaf worker: it reads cache state and writes
  the session row but does not enqueue recomputes.

## Documentation and model comments

- Update the `GameSession.opening_score_baseline` comment to say the baseline is captured
  asynchronously shortly after session start and persisted only when the pre-session cached batch is
  provably fresh and dated strictly before `started_at`; otherwise it remains NULL.
- Update the `opening_score_delta.py` module docstring to describe async capture and the
  fresh-and-strictly-before guard.
- Add a short comment near the recompute timestamp sampling explaining that `computed_at` is an
  evidence-read upper bound consumed by the baseline date guard.
- Update `SPEC.md` section 5.7.3 to document `OpeningBaselineScheduler` as the third in-process
  scheduler: session-keyed, no debounce, best-effort, single-process/one-worker assumption, async
  baseline capture, NULL/no-delta fallback.

## No schema, migration, or frontend changes

Reuse nullable `GameSession.opening_score_baseline`. Do not add columns, Alembic migrations, or
`conftest` test-schema DDL for this bead. Start responses never exposed the baseline, and
`compute_opening_score_delta` / `read_opening_score_delta` already tolerate NULL. Do not add a terminal
synchronous fallback; a normal game that already has session evidence cannot safely capture a baseline
at the end, and a zero-move end has no played chain.

## Test plan

Add `backend/test_opening_baseline_scheduler.py`:

1. Fresh batch dated strictly before `started_at`, no session evidence -> baseline JSON is persisted
   with `source="cached_fresh"`.
2. Review race: `blunder_reviews(session_id=sid)` plus a newer batch dated after `started_at` -> NULL
   and `source="skipped_post_session_batch"`.
3. Blunder-target race: `blunders(source_session_id=sid)` plus a newer batch dated after
   `started_at` -> NULL and `source="skipped_post_session_batch"`.
4. Move race: a newer post-session batch after a move -> NULL and
   `source="skipped_post_session_batch"`.
5. Brand-new user with no batch and no evidence -> `"{}"` and `source="empty_no_evidence"`.
6. Already-set baseline -> no-op with `source="already_set"`.
7. Defense-in-depth persist race: after capture returns JSON, insert one of
   `session_moves`, `blunder_reviews`, or `blunders` before the UPDATE -> rowcount 0, baseline remains
   NULL, `source="raced_evidence_or_already_set"`.
8. Cold/stale cache -> NULL with `source="skipped_cold"` or `source="skipped_stale"`.
9. Naive timestamp handling: naive `computed_at` strictly before `started_at` is accepted; naive
   `computed_at` equal to `started_at` is rejected without an aware/naive comparison crash.
10. `run_due()` and `shutdown(drain=True)` drain due work deterministically.
11. Untrusted queued identity: seed the session owner (`session.user_id`/`player_color`) with a fresh
    pre-session batch, and seed a DIFFERENT user/color with their own fresh batch. Enqueue with the
    WRONG `(user_id, player_color)` pair for that session -> baseline stays NULL,
    `source="session_mismatch"`, and the other user's scores are never written onto the session. Then
    enqueue with the CORRECT queued pair -> the session-owner's batch is captured (`source="cached_fresh"`),
    confirming capture keys off the row, not the payload.

Add scheduler/facade lifecycle tests, mirroring `test_session_evidence_scheduler.py`:

- Facade swallows enqueue failure.
- `OpeningBaselineScheduler.enqueue()` swallows auto-start failure.
- `/api/game/start` and `/api/drills/start` still return 201 if the bound
  `enqueue_baseline_snapshot` aliases raise.
- Worker DB sessions close in `finally` when the job fails, and a later enqueue still runs.
- Duplicate enqueues for the same `session_id` coalesce to one job invocation.

Add `backend/test_opening_cache.py` coverage for the `computed_at` invariant:

- Patch `app.opening_cache._utcnow` with a monotonic fake clock.
- Wrap both `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` and `overlay_evidence` to record the clock value
  after each read.
- Assert `batch.computed_at >= max(fingerprint_read_tick, overlay_read_tick)`.
- Cover both direct `recompute_opening_scores(computed_at=None)` and
  `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed`.

Update fixtures in `backend/conftest.py`:

- Extend the `client` fixture to patch `app.main.get_baseline_scheduler` so the FastAPI lifespan does
  not start a real baseline daemon with production `SessionLocal`.
- Extend the Postgres `pg_client` fixture the same way.
- Add an autouse no-op/recorder fixture patching the bound aliases
  `app.api.game.enqueue_baseline_snapshot` and `app.api.drills.enqueue_baseline_snapshot`, matching the
  existing bound-alias stubs for `request_recompute` and `enqueue_session_evidence`.

Update existing endpoint tests in `backend/test_opening_score_delta.py`:

- Tests that used to expect `opening_score_baseline` immediately after `/start` should now assert the
  immediate value is NULL, drain an injected non-autostart
  `OpeningBaselineScheduler(session_factory=TestingSessionLocal)` with `run_due()`, then assert the
  populated JSON.
- Keep the "does not call refresh_now on the start path" assertions.
- Move the failure-injection test from synchronous `/start` snapshotting to the worker job:
  `run_baseline_snapshot_job` swallows the error, leaves the baseline NULL, and does not crash. Keep a
  small endpoint assertion that `/start` returns 201 with NULL when enqueueing is best-effort.

Add acceptance coverage in `backend/test_game_api.py` and `backend/test_drill_api.py`:

- Inject a non-autostart baseline scheduler and spy `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` with a call counter.
  Call `/start`, assert 201 and exactly one queued job, and assert the digest call count is STILL ZERO
  once the response returns. The load-bearing contract is "no digest before the `/start` response," not
  "the digest ran on some other thread": with synchronous `run_due()` the job runs on the caller's
  thread, so thread identity is not a meaningful signal for the worker path.
- Drain the injected scheduler with `run_due()` and assert the digest call count increments (0 -> 1)
  only across that explicit drain — proving the digest moved off the request path onto the drained job.
  A request-thread-id spy MAY additionally record that no digest call carried the request thread's id,
  but the count-across-the-drain-boundary assertion is the one that must hold.
- End-to-end delta: when the worker drains in time, before/after delta is populated; when the date
  guard loses the race, baseline remains NULL and the response degrades to no delta.

## Relationship to `g-jact`

This change moves the expensive freshness proof off the start hot path. `g-jact` can later replace the
O(evidence) digest with a cheap freshness signal for every caller and may allow this background job to
collapse back into a cheap synchronous check.
acceptance_criteria: Session start no longer invokes raw_evidence_inputs_digest synchronously on the request thread; end-of-session opening-score delta correctness preserved (baseline in time, NULL->no-delta degrade, and pre-first-move capture all covered by tests).

title: Honor privacy signals (DNT/GPC) in PostHog init
description:
Split from g-posthog-cors (which is scoped to the reverse-proxy CORS fix). The PostHog frontend init in src/analytics/posthog.ts currently honors no privacy signals (SDK default respect_dnt: false; no GPC handling).

Scope:
- Set respect_dnt: true so the SDK honors navigator.doNotTrack / msDoNotTrack / window.doNotTrack (see node_modules/posthog-js/lib/src/consent.js _getDnt).
- Add a manual pre-init gate for GPC: the SDK does NOT read navigator.globalPrivacyControl, so check it ourselves and either skip init or use opt_out_capturing_by_default when GPC is set.
- Add tests in src/analytics/posthog.test.ts mirroring the existing config-assertion pattern (respect_dnt present; capture is opted out / init skipped when GPC is signaled).

Out of scope: the reverse-proxy CORS work tracked in g-posthog-cors.
design:
Honor privacy signals in PostHog init.

1. DNT (SDK-handled): add respect_dnt: true to posthog.init() config. The SDK's consent.js _getDnt() then opts capture out when navigator.doNotTrack / navigator.msDoNotTrack / window.doNotTrack is yes-like (true/'true'/1/'1'/'yes').

2. GPC (manual pre-init gate): SDK does NOT read navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Added isGpcSignaled() checking navigator.globalPrivacyControl === true (typeof-guarded for non-browser). Wired into initAnalytics early return alongside !token/isDisabled() so GPC skips init entirely — no SDK load, no cookies, no network — leaving enabled=false so all helpers no-op. Chose skip-init over opt_out_capturing_by_default for consistency with the module's existing disabled posture (no consent banner to later opt in).

Tests (posthog.test.ts): added respect_dnt: true to the main config objectContaining assertion; added 'does not initialize when Global Privacy Control is signaled' (stubGlobal navigator {globalPrivacyControl:true} -> init not called, disabled) and 'initializes normally when Global Privacy Control is not asserted' (globalPrivacyControl:false -> init called). Added vi.unstubAllGlobals() to beforeEach/afterEach. All 10 tests pass; tsc --noEmit clean.
close_reason: Implemented DNT (respect_dnt:true) + GPC pre-init gate with tests

metrics to add:

     This is the clearest progress metric for the product’s core loop.

 - Accuracy % instead of ACPL
 - Opening performance

 - Most of the Library section ignores the window selector. Blunders Total,
   Positions Total, Edges Total, and Avg Blunder Loss are all computed all-time
   (stats.py:447-479) — only "New Blunders" respects the 7d/30d/90d toggle. So a
   player switches to "7d," and four of the five Library cards silently don't change.
   That's worse than useless — it's misleading. Same issue with Perfect Streak,

design:
# g-k87r — Audit / rework the Stats page

## Context

The Stats page (`src/pages/StatsPage.tsx` + `GET /api/stats/summary` in
`backend/app/api/stats.py`) accreted a pile of low-signal counters and, worse,
several cards that silently ignore the 7d/30d/90d window selector — they compute
all-time numbers but sit under a window toggle, so switching windows leaves them
unchanged. That is actively misleading. This rework strips the noise, fixes the
window dishonesty, and replaces raw counts with the rate/progress metrics that
actually reflect the product's core loop (blunder → review → retain).

Feasibility is fully confirmed against the current schema — every new metric is
computable from data that is already persisted. No new tables or migrations.

## Design principle: window honesty

Every card obeys one rule: **either it respects the window selector, or it is
explicitly tagged "All-time."** No card silently shows all-time data under a
window toggle. This is the direct fix for the issue's core complaint.

- Window-scoped: Score %, Accuracy %, Mistake-Free Rate, Review Pass Rate,
  Training Conversion, New Blunders, per-color splits, quality distribution.
- All-time (tagged): Review Retention, Blunders Total, Avg Blunder Loss,
  Top Costly Blunders, Openings (from the latest opening-score batch).

### Rate contract (P3)

**Every rate/percentage field is `float | None`, returning `None` when its
denominator is 0** (no decided games, no ended games, no reviewed blunders,
etc.). This applies uniformly to `score_pct`, `accuracy_pct`,
`mistake_free_game_rate`, `retention_pct`, and `review_pass_rate` — no field uses
0 as a "no data" sentinel. The frontend renders `—` for `null` (the existing
`GameReviewStats` accuracy cell already does this). Count fields
(`reviews_total`, `conversions_in_window`, `blunders_total`, etc.) stay plain
ints. Update the `StatsPage` formatters to accept `number | null` accordingly.

**`quality_distribution` is the exception to per-field nullability, handled at
the object level.** Its three buckets (`inaccuracy`, `mistake`, `blunder`) share
one denominator — classified player moves — so they can never diverge: either all
three are defined or none are. A bucket's `0.0` is a *legitimate value when data
exists* (you had classified moves, none of that class), not a "no data" sentinel.
The only undefined case is **zero classified player moves**, which invalidates all
three at once. So the whole object is nullable: `quality_distribution:
Distribution | None`, `None` iff zero classified moves; otherwise each bucket is a
non-null `float` (0.0 allowed). The FE hides the distribution block (or shows a
"no moves yet" placeholder) when the object is `null`, rather than rendering three
`—` rows.

## Data sources (all already persisted)

- **Score %** — `GameSession.result` counts already gathered in `stats.py`.
- **Accuracy %** — reuse `compute_game_accuracy` / `AccuracyMove` /
  `expected_total_moves_from_pgn` from `backend/app/accuracy.py`, aggregated with
  the exact ordered-eval query pattern in `backend/app/api/history.py:102-151`
  (per-session ordered `SessionMove` evals + `GameSession.pgn`). Restrict to
  `status == "ended"` sessions (accuracy is `None` for incomplete games anyway).
- **Mistake-Free Game Rate** — per-session count of player `SessionMove` rows
  with `classification == "blunder"`; a game is "clean" if that count is 0.
- **Review Retention** (renamed from "Blunder Retention" — see note) —
  `Blunder.pass_streak` + `Blunder.last_reviewed_at`. A fail resets `pass_streak`
  to 0 (`srs.py:153`), so `pass_streak >= 1` ⇔ last review passed. Retention =
  retained / reviewed blunders. **This is SRS/review-based, NOT the issue's
  literal "did I avoid it when the position recurred in a new game" (organic)
  metric** — that was the product decision confirmed during planning. Renamed so
  the label is honest about what it measures.
- **Review Pass Rate** — `BlunderReview.passed` / total, windowed by
  `BlunderReview.reviewed_at`. **`BlunderReview` has no `user_id`**
  (`models.py:122`) — every `BlunderReview` query MUST `JOIN Blunder ON
  BlunderReview.blunder_id == Blunder.id` and filter `Blunder.user_id ==
  user.user_id`, or it counts other users' reviews.
- **Training Conversion** — `BlunderReview.pass_streak_after` crossing the
  mastery threshold **N (default 3)** within the window; same
  `JOIN Blunder … user_id` scoping requirement as above.
- **Openings** — reuse `list_cached_opening_scores(db, user_id, player_color)`
  (`backend/app/opening_cache.py:322`, latest batch via
  `get_latest_opening_score_batch`) → `UserOpeningScore` rows
  (`opening_name`, `opening_family`, `player_color`, `opening_score`,
  `sample_size`, `game_count`).

## Backend — `backend/app/api/stats.py`

Reshape `StatsSummaryResponse` (and its nested pydantic models). New shape:

```
window_days, generated_at
games:    { played, score_pct: float|None, wins, losses, draws, avg_moves }
moves:    { accuracy_pct: float|None, mistake_free_game_rate: float|None,
            quality_distribution: { inaccuracy, mistake, blunder } | None }
colors:   { white|black: { games, score_pct: float|None, accuracy_pct: float|None } }
training: { retention_pct: float|None, reviewed_blunders, retained_blunders,
            review_pass_rate: float|None, reviews_total, reviews_passed,
            conversions_in_window, mastery_threshold }
library:  { blunders_total, new_blunders_in_window, avg_blunder_eval_loss_cp,
            top_costly_blunders }
openings: { strongest: [OpeningStat], weakest: [OpeningStat] }
```
(All `*_pct` / rate fields are nullable per the Rate contract above.)
`OpeningStat = { opening_name, opening_family, player_color, opening_score,
sample_size, game_count }`.

Computation details:
- **games.losses** = `checkmate_loss + resign + abandon` (all are losses from the
  player's view — folds the removed Resigns/Abandons cards into the L count so
  W-L-D sums to decided games). **wins** = `checkmate_win`, **draws** = `draw`.
- **games.score_pct** = `(wins + 0.5·draws) / decided_games · 100`, where
  `decided_games = wins + losses + draws`; **`None` when `decided_games == 0`**
  (Rate contract).
- **moves.accuracy_pct** = mean of per-game `compute_game_accuracy` over ended
  sessions in the window that return non-None; `None` if none qualify. Add the
  ordered-eval + PGN query (mirror `history.py`) — this is the one new heavier
  query; scope it to `status == "ended"` sessions only.
- **moves.mistake_free_game_rate** (P2) — denominator is **ended visible
  sessions in the window** (`status == "ended"`), NOT all sessions. The current
  session loop (`stats.py:293,333`) includes `active` sessions; an in-progress
  clean game must not inflate the rate. clean = 0 player-`blunder`
  `SessionMove` rows in that ended session. Rate = clean_ended / ended · 100;
  `None` when `ended == 0`.
- **quality_distribution** keeps only `inaccuracy / mistake / blunder`
  (drop best/excellent/good buckets) as % of classified player moves. Return the
  whole object as `None` when `classified_move_total == 0`; otherwise each bucket
  is a `float` (0.0 permitted). Replaces the current `_safe_rate`→0.0 behavior at
  `stats.py:438-445`.
- **colors** per-side: `games`, `score_pct`, `accuracy_pct` (avg per-game
  accuracy over that color's ended games). Drop avg_cpl / blunders_per_100 /
  raw wins-losses-draws / completed. (P2) **Per-color `score_pct` uses the same
  loss folding as the headline: per-color `losses = checkmate_loss + resign +
  abandon` for that color.** The current per-color accumulator (`stats.py:322-355`)
  only tracks per-color `checkmate_loss` and buckets resign/abandon globally —
  extend `per_color_games` to accumulate resign/abandon per color so the color
  `decided_games`/`score_pct` match the global mapping. `None` when a color has 0
  decided games.
- **training** — all `BlunderReview` queries **JOIN `Blunder` and filter
  `Blunder.user_id == user.user_id`** (`BlunderReview` has no `user_id`,
  `models.py:122`). `reviewed_blunders` = `Blunder` (user-scoped) with
  `last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL`; `retained_blunders` = `Blunder` with
  `pass_streak >= 1`; `retention_pct` = retained/reviewed (`None` when
  reviewed == 0). `reviews_total`/`reviews_passed` = user-scoped `BlunderReview`
  rows (passed) with `reviewed_at` in window; `review_pass_rate` = passed/total
  (`None` when total == 0). `conversions_in_window` = distinct `blunder_id` among
  user-scoped `BlunderReview` rows in window with `pass_streak_after == N` (each
  such row is a fresh N-1→N crossing). `mastery_threshold = N` (new module
  constant, default 3).
- **library**: drop `positions_total` + `edges_total` and their queries. Keep
  `blunders_total`, `new_blunders_in_window` (already windowed),
  `avg_blunder_eval_loss_cp`, `top_costly_blunders` (FE tags the all-time ones).
- **openings**: call `list_cached_opening_scores` for white and black, merge,
  filter to `sample_size >= 3` (drop noise), sort by `opening_score`; strongest =
  top 3, weakest = bottom 3. Empty lists when no batch exists (cold user).

Remove from the response/model: `achievements`, `data_completeness`,
`GamesSummary.{completed,active,resigns,abandons,avg_duration_seconds}`,
`MoveSummary.{player_moves,avg_cpl,mistakes_per_100_moves,blunders_per_100_moves}`.
Delete now-unused helpers (`_perfect_streak_summary` only if unused — see below).

**Keep the standalone `/api/stats/achievements` endpoint and
`_perfect_streak_summary`** — `ChessGame.tsx:873` (`getStatsAchievements`) still
uses personal-best for the in-game streak toast. Only the *summary* response and
the *stats page* drop Perfect Streak.

## Frontend

- **`src/utils/api.ts`** — rewrite `StatsSummaryResponse` and nested interfaces
  (`StatsGamesSummary`, `StatsColorSummary`, `StatsMoveSummary`,
  `StatsMoveQualityDistribution`, `StatsLibrarySummary`) to match; add
  `StatsTrainingSummary` and `StatsOpeningsSummary`/`StatsOpeningStat`; delete
  `StatsDataCompletenessSummary`, `PerfectStreakSummary`/`StatsAchievementsSummary`
  from the *summary* types (leave `getStatsAchievements` + its type — still used).

- **`src/pages/StatsPage.tsx`** — rebuild sections in this order:
  1. **Rating** — existing `<RatingGraph>` (see Elo-default below).
  2. **Results** — Score % (headline) with a `W–L–D` detail line; Played; Avg Moves.
  3. **Accuracy & mistakes** — Accuracy % (headline, colorize with existing
     `accuracyColor` from `src/utils/statColor.ts`); Mistake-Free Game Rate;
     quality distribution (Inaccuracy/Mistake/Blunder only) — hide the block or
     show a "no moves yet" placeholder when `quality_distribution` is `null`.
  4. **By color** — White/Black cards: Games, Score %, Accuracy %.
  5. **Training** — Review Retention (tag "All-time"), Review Pass Rate,
     Training Conversion ("N blunders mastered", using `mastery_threshold`).
  6. **Library** — New Blunders (windowed); Blunders Total, Avg Blunder Loss,
     Top Costly Blunders (each tagged "All-time"). Drop Positions/Edges.
  7. **Openings** — Strongest / Weakest lists from `openings` (tag "All-time");
     hide the section when both lists are empty.
  - Remove `formatDuration`, the `QUALITY_KEYS` good buckets, the Achievements
    and Data Completeness sections, and update `isEmptySummary` (it references
    `library.blunders_total` + `moves.player_moves`; switch to
    `games.played === 0 && library.blunders_total === 0`).
  - **Null handling**: `formatPercent`/`formatAverage` currently take `number`.
    Make the rate cells accept `number | null` and render `—` for `null` (Rate
    contract) — mirror the `accuracy != null ? … : '—'` pattern in
    `GameReviewStats.tsx:136`.

- **`src/components/RatingGraph.tsx`** — "Select Elo by default": initialize
  `visibleSeries` to `{ elo: true, chesscom: false, lichess: false }`
  (currently all three `true`, `RatingGraph.tsx:183-187`). Chess.com/Lichess
  remain available via the existing checkboxes.

## Removals checklist (issue → code)

| Remove | Where |
|---|---|
| Positions Total, Edges Total | stats.py library query + StatsPage Library |
| Data Completeness section | stats.py model + StatsPage section |
| Active, Completed, Resigns, Abandons, Avg Duration | GamesSummary + StatsPage Games |
| Player Moves | MoveSummary + StatsPage |
| Mistakes/100, Blunders/100 as cards | MoveSummary + StatsPage |
| Best / Excellent / Good buckets | MoveQualityDistribution + QUALITY_KEYS |
| Perfect Streak (from page only) | summary model + StatsPage (keep endpoint) |

## Tests

- **`backend/test_stats_api.py`** — rewrite the assertions (they assert exact
  dict shapes at lines ~120-286, 471+). Update the empty-dataset and mixed-data
  fixtures to cover: score_pct math (incl. resign/abandon folded into losses),
  accuracy_pct over ended games, mistake_free_game_rate (**denominator excludes
  active sessions** — add an active clean game and assert it doesn't inflate),
  retention_pct (pass_streak≥1), review_pass_rate + conversions windowing (needs
  `BlunderReview` rows with `pass_streak_after`), and openings top/weakest
  (needs an `OpeningScoreBatch` + `UserOpeningScore` fixture). Add a
  **cross-user isolation test**: seed another user's `BlunderReview` rows and
  assert they don't leak into review_pass_rate / conversions (guards the
  `Blunder.user_id` join). Add **null-denominator cases**: assert every `*_pct`
  field is `null` (not 0) when its denominator is empty, and that
  `quality_distribution` is `null` (not an all-zeros dict — this changes the
  existing empty-summary assertion at `test_stats_api.py:135-148`) when there are
  zero classified player moves, while a games-with-moves-but-no-blunders case
  keeps `blunder: 0.0` non-null. Note: new tables
  used by fixtures must exist in conftest `_create_test_schema` (per project
  memory on hand-written SQLite schema) — `blunder_reviews`, `user_opening_scores`,
  `opening_score_batches` — confirm they're present, add DDL if not.
- **`src/pages/StatsPage.test.tsx`** — rewrite around the new sections/labels;
  update the mock `StatsSummaryResponse` to the new shape.
- Add a `RatingGraph` assertion (or snapshot) that only Elo is visible initially.

## Verification

1. Backend: `cd backend && .venv/bin/pytest test_stats_api.py -q`.
2. Frontend: `npx vitest run src/pages/StatsPage.test.tsx src/components/RatingGraph` (rerun named files in isolation — pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load).
3. Type/build gate: `npx tsc -b` (stricter than `--noEmit`; the pre-push hook runs `tsc -b && vite build` over the whole tree).
4. Manual: run the app, open `/stats`, toggle 7d/30d/90d/All and confirm **every**
   card either changes or is tagged "All-time"; confirm the rating graph shows
   only Elo until Chess.com/Lichess are checked; sanity-check Score %, Accuracy %,
   and the Training numbers against a known account.

## Open notes / decisions locked in

- **Review Retention** (renamed from "Blunder Retention") = SRS-based (% of
  reviewed blunders currently held, `pass_streak≥1`), per user's steer — **not**
  the issue's literal organic "position recurred in a new game, did I avoid it?"
  metric (which would need `BlunderOpportunityEvent` + the matching `SessionMove`
  outcome, `models.py:101` / `session.py:566`). The rename keeps the label honest.
  If organic recurrence is later wanted, it's a separate follow-up bead.
- All rate fields are nullable (`float | None`), `None` on zero denominator; FE
  renders `—`. Count fields stay ints.
- `BlunderReview` has no `user_id` — all its queries join `Blunder` for user
  scoping.
- Mastery threshold **N = 3** (single tunable constant); confirm the value at
  implementation time.
- Openings = reuse `UserOpeningScore` (latest batch) strongest/weakest — no heavy
  per-game opening resolution.
- Commit code + `.beads` ledger together, directly to master, after review
  (per project workflow memory).

# g-ycxb — Keep engine-line vertical space to stop MoveList jitter ## Problem In the analysis board, navigating the MoveList makes the UI jump up then down. The `.analysis-board__engine-lines` strip (the horizontal row of up-to-3 engine lines under the "Engine lines" toggle) disappears for a moment while the engine recalculates for the newly-selected move, collapsing the panel by one strip-row of height, then reappears. ## Root cause `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx:1435` gates the strip on: ``` showEngineArrows && engineLinesDisplay.some(Boolean) ``` Data flow of the transient on navigation: 1. `displayedFen` updates immediately to the new position. 2. `engineInfoFen` still points at the OLD position until the engine emits info for the new FEN (after `ENGINE_EVALUATION_DEBOUNCE_MS` + first depth). 3. Line 559: `activeEngineLines = showEngineArrows && engineInfoFen === displayedFen ? engineLines : []` → `[]` during the gap (correctly avoids showing stale lines). 4. `mergedEngineLines` (memo, line 571) → `[]` in the EMPTY-DISPLAY path; `engineLinesDisplay` (memo, line 615) → `[]`. 5. `engineLinesDisplay.some(Boolean)` is `false` → the whole `.analysis-board__engine-lines` div UNMOUNTS → panel height drops by one strip-row → MoveList below jumps up. When the engine produces lines for the new FEN the div remounts → MoveList jumps back down. That up/down = the jitter. Important scoping of step 4: `mergedEngineLines` does NOT always go empty during the stale-FEN gap. Line 571 only falls back to `activeEngineLines` (`[]` during the gap) when `!useRestrictedSearch || !trustedBest`. When restricted search is active WITH a `trustedBest`, it synthesizes and prepends a cached canonical line, so `mergedEngineLines = [cachedLine]` stays non-empty even during the gap → `.some(Boolean)` is true → the strip never unmounts → no jitter in that path. The jitter is therefore specific to the empty-display path (no restricted search / no trustedBest, or any state where no cached canonical line is synthesized). The fix below is still correct and complete because it reserves the row for ALL empty-display states whenever engine lines are enabled. The strip is laid out horizontally (`display:flex`, 3 buttons `flex:1 1 0`), so it is exactly one row tall; its mount/unmount is a single-row height change. ## Fix (JSX one-liner, reuse existing placeholder mechanism) Drop the `engineLinesDisplay.some(Boolean)` clause so the strip stays mounted whenever engine lines are enabled: `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx:1435` ``` - {showEngineArrows && engineLinesDisplay.some(Boolean) && ( + {showEngineArrows && (
{[0, 1, 2].map((i) => { const line = engineLinesDisplay[i]; return line ? (
)} ``` The inner `[0,1,2].map` already renders an invisible, height-matched placeholder span for every null slot (`line ?

title: Move score diffs next to opening cards
description: Let's move the after game opening score delta next to the opening cards. To the right of each opening card, if the score for the card has changed display the diff from the previous score and the new score. For example "+1 → 47" or "-2 → 62". If the diff is positive color it green. If it is negative red. If diff is 0 do not display anything.
design:
# g-3gmc — Move opening-score diffs next to the opening cards

## Context
Today the post-game opening-score delta (g-xanz) renders as a **standalone list**
(`OpeningScoreDelta`) in two places: the `PostGameBanner` (game + stopped-drill
branches) and `DrillStopActions`. The user wants this signal moved to sit **inline,
to the right of each opening card** in the live/post-game lineage (`GameOpeningLineage`
chips), so the change reads directly against the opening it belongs to. The card
shrinks horizontally to make room for the badge. Format: `+1 → 47` (green) / `-2 → 62`
(red); no visible change shows nothing; a brand-new opening (no prior score) shows
nothing either.

## Data flow (already in place)
- **Cards**: `GameOpeningLineage` (`src/components/GameOpeningLineage.tsx`) renders
  `lineage: OpeningLineageItem[]` (from `useSessionOpenings`), each keyed by
  `opening_key`. Mounted in `ChessGame.tsx` via `openingLineageSlot`
  (`chess-panel__openings`), shown when `(isGameActive || gameResult !== null) &&
  openingLineage.length > 0`.
- **Deltas**: `openingScoreChanges: OpeningScoreDeltaItem[] | null` in `useGameStore`
  (already selected in `ChessGame.tsx:270`), set at terminal events
  (game-end/resign/natural-end drill/accuracy-fail drill) by `useChessGameLifecycle.ts`.
  Each item keyed by `opening_key` with `before/after/delta/is_new`. **Null during
  live play.** Note: `before/after/delta` are **floats** (`opening_score_delta.py:50`),
  and `is_new` can be true while `after` is `null` (`test_opening_score_delta.py:287`).
- **Join**: both lists are broadest→deepest and share `opening_key`. The two coexist
  post-game (the lineage slot stays mounted because `gameResult !== null`, or
  `isGameActive` for stopped drills, while deltas are set). During live play deltas
  are null → no badges, chips render full-width as before.
- **Terminal-refetch gap (must fix)**: the lineage refetches only on
  `(sessionId, refetchKey)` where `refetchKey = moveHistory.length`
  (`ChessGame.tsx:383`) and polls only while `active` (`useSessionOpenings.ts:116`).
  Resign / fast-stop set `openingScoreChanges` **without adding a move and with polling
  already off**, so the lineage can still be empty at terminal. Because the new badge is
  gated on `openingLineage.length > 0`, removing the standalone list would drop the only
  delta surface. Fix: force one lineage refetch at terminal (below). The fetch effect
  (`useSessionOpenings.ts:108-111`) does NOT depend on `active`, so a `refetchKey` bump
  refetches even after polling stops, and lineage + delta share the same backend
  `played_opening_chain`, so the refetch returns the same openings the deltas key on.

## Changes

### 1. `src/components/GameOpeningLineage.tsx` — render the inline badge
- Add prop `scoreChanges?: OpeningScoreDeltaItem[] | null`.
- `const changeByKey = useMemo(() => new Map((scoreChanges ?? []).map(c => [c.opening_key, c])), [scoreChanges])`.
- Per item compute a badge from `changeByKey.get(item.opening_key)`. **Brand-new
  openings show nothing** (user choice), and the **displayed diff is derived from
  ROUNDED endpoints** (scores are floats; the cards display `Math.round`), so a sub-1.0
  wobble never renders a misleading `+0 → 47` / `+1 → 47`:
  ```
  badgeFor(c):
    if (!c || c.is_new) return null                   // brand-new opening → nothing (user choice)
    if (c.before == null || c.after == null) return null  // no before/after → no diff
    const after = Math.round(c.after)
    const diff = after - Math.round(c.before)         // displayed diff, not raw float delta
    if (diff === 0) return null                        // no VISIBLE change → nothing
    return { text: `${diff > 0 ? "+" : ""}${diff} → ${after}`, dir: diff > 0 ? "up" : "down" }
  ```
- Restructure each `<li className="game-opening-lineage__item">` into a **flex row**:
  the existing chip-or-card block stays as the first child (now `flex:1; min-width:0`);
  append the badge `<span className="game-opening-lineage__delta game-opening-lineage__delta--{dir}" aria-label="…">` as the second child. The badge sits to the RIGHT and
  renders in **both** collapsed-chip and expanded-card states (sibling of the card,
  never inside it — per user direction). Give it a descriptive `aria-label`
  (e.g. `"Italian Game score +3, now 44"`).

### 2. `src/components/ChessGame.tsx` — rewire the data + terminal refetch
- In `openingLineageSlot` (~line 1873), pass `scoreChanges={openingScoreChanges}` to
  `<GameOpeningLineage>`.
- Remove `openingScoreChanges={openingScoreChanges}` from `<PostGameBanner>` (~1975)
  and `<DrillStopActions>` (~1991). Keep the store selector at line 270 (now consumed
  by the lineage).
- **Force a terminal lineage refetch** so the cards exist to host badges when a
  resign/fast-stop produced deltas without a new move. Change the hook's `refetchKey`
  (line 383) to bump once when the terminal delta lands:
  `refetchKey: moveHistory.length + (openingScoreChanges ? 1 : 0)`, with a comment
  explaining it. Rationale: during play `openingScoreChanges` is null (flag 0); at
  terminal it flips to non-null (flag +1) while `moveHistory` is frozen, so the key
  strictly increases → exactly one refetch; a new game resets `sessionId` (hook resets)
  and the lifecycle clears `openingScoreChanges` back to null. The fetch effect ignores
  `active`, so this refetches even though polling has stopped.

### 3. `src/components/chess-game/ui/PostGameBanner.tsx` — drop the standalone delta
- Remove `import OpeningScoreDelta`, the `openingScoreChanges` prop (type + destructure),
  and **both** `<OpeningScoreDelta changes={openingScoreChanges} />` usages (game branch
  + stopped-drill branch). Drop the now-unused `OpeningScoreDeltaItem` type import.

### 4. `src/components/chess-game/ui/DrillStopActions.tsx` — drop the standalone delta
- Remove `import OpeningScoreDelta`, the `openingScoreChanges` prop, the
  `<OpeningScoreDelta changes={openingScoreChanges} />` usage, and the unused
  `OpeningScoreDeltaItem` import.

### 5. Delete the now-dead component
- Delete `src/components/chess-game/ui/OpeningScoreDelta.tsx` and
  `OpeningScoreDelta.test.tsx` (no remaining refs after steps 3–4 — the only other
  `OpeningScoreDelta*` references are the `OpeningScoreDeltaItem` **type** in
  `api.ts`/`useGameStore.ts`, which we keep).
- Remove the `.opening-score-delta*` CSS block in `src/App.css` (~lines 5550–5660).

### 6. `src/App.css` — badge styles + flex row (near `.game-opening-lineage`, ~8865)
- Extend `.game-opening-lineage__item` to `display:flex; align-items:center;
  gap:0.4rem;` (keep its `padding-left` depth rule; the panel-only override at
  `.chess-panel__openings .game-opening-lineage__item` ~9079 only tweaks `padding-left`,
  so it stays compatible).
- `.game-opening-lineage__item > .game-opening-chip,
   .game-opening-lineage__item > .opening-family-card { flex:1 1 auto; min-width:0; }`
  so the card shrinks to make room.
- `.game-opening-lineage__delta { flex:0 0 auto; font-size:0.72rem; font-weight:700;
   font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; white-space:nowrap; }`
- `.game-opening-lineage__delta--up { color: var(--success); }`
- `.game-opening-lineage__delta--down { color: var(--error); }`
  (semantic tokens from `src/index.css`.)
- **Narrow-panel (expanded card) tuning**: in `.chess-panel__openings` the expanded
  `opening-family-card--analysis` is already squeezed to ~208px inner width
  (`App.css:9052-9076`: 84px board, capped score/grade type, 2-up metrics). A right-side
  badge subtracts more width, so add a scoped adjustment to keep it inside the 240px
  column — e.g. `align-items:flex-start` on the panel's `…__item` so the small badge
  pins to the card's top-right, and if needed nudge the panel board override (84px→~76px)
  / overview gap. Final pixels decided against a real screenshot (see Verification).

### 7. Tests
- `src/components/GameOpeningLineage.test.tsx`: thread an optional `scoreChanges` through
  the `renderLineage` helper, then add cases:
  - positive (`before:41, after:44`) → badge `+3 → 44`, `--up` class;
  - negative (`before:64, after:62`) → `-2 → 62`, `--down` class;
  - **rounding — no visible change**: `before:41.6, after:42.1` (raw delta +0.5, but
    rounds 42→42) → **no badge** — pins that a sub-1.0 wobble renders nothing;
  - **rounding — boundary cross**: `before:41.4, after:41.6` (rounds 41→42) → `+1 → 42`,
    `--up` — pins that the badge follows the *displayed* (rounded) scores;
  - no matching key → no badge;
  - **`is_new:true`** → **no badge** (covers both `after:30` and `after:null`, since
    brand-new openings render nothing per user choice);
  - badge present in **both** collapsed and expanded states (render expanded, assert the
    badge is still shown and is a sibling, not inside `lineage-board`).
- `src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx`: add ONE integration test in the existing "ChessGame
  opening lineage" suite (~line 3210) that covers BOTH the cross-component wiring (the
  optional `scoreChanges` pass-down at `ChessGame.tsx:1873`) AND the terminal-refetch fix
  (the High finding). Reuse the resign scaffolding in that file: have
  `fetchSessionOpeningsMock` return an **empty** lineage during play, then return a
  matching-key lineage on the terminal refetch, and `endGameMock` resolve
  `opening_score_changes:[{opening_key:"k1", ..., before:41, after:44, delta:3,
  is_new:false}]`. After resign, assert the lineage refetch fired again post-terminal and
  the `+3 → 44` badge appears next to the chip — directly exercising "deltas arrive before
  lineage exists."
- `src/components/chess-game/ui/PostGameBanner.test.tsx`: remove the two "renders
  opening-score deltas…" tests (~208, ~222) and the `openingChange` helper +
  `OpeningScoreDeltaItem` import if now unused; keep the rating-delta assertions.
- `src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx` (stopped drill): add ONE more integration test for
  the **stopped-drill** path, since DrillStopActions (`ChessGame.tsx:1987`) loses its
  `OpeningScoreDelta`. Reuse the existing accuracy-fail drill scaffolding (the suite that
  drives `drillState:"failed"` via `failDrillMock`, ~lines 660–805): with the drill
  stopped (`isGameActive && isStoppedDrill && !gameResult`, so the lineage slot is shown)
  and `openingScoreChanges` landed, assert the `+N → M` badge appears in
  `GameOpeningLineage` (and not in the now-delta-less DrillStopActions).
- Delete `OpeningScoreDelta.test.tsx` (step 5).
- `DrillStopActions.test.tsx`: no delta assertions today (confirmed) and the prop is

title: add alternate board colors to non-live moves
description: We want alternate board colors in the game board when the game is live and the user is not on the latest move, either because they navigated away or a blunder alert navigated backwards. Copy the what-if board colors from the analysis board but a noticeably less desaturated.
design:
# g-9y2a — Alternate board colors when reviewing a past move during a live game

## Goal
While a game is **live** (`isGameActive === true`) and the user is **not on the latest
move** (navigated back manually, or a blunder alert / drill-fail jumped backward), wash
out the board squares so the position reads as "you're looking at history, not the live
board." Reuse the analysis board's what-if wash, but **noticeably less desaturated**
(retain more color — this is a lighter touch than the full what-if treatment).

## Why this is the right trigger
`src/components/ChessGame.tsx` already derives the position-on-board signal:
- `displayedIndex` (memo at line 362) = `viewIndex === null ? moveHistory.length - 1 : viewIndex`.
  This is the single source of truth for *which ply is rendered on the board*, normalizing
  the live (`null`) case to the last ply.
- "Not on the latest move" is therefore exactly `displayedIndex < moveHistory.length - 1`.
- So the trigger is:
  `const isReviewingPast = isGameActive && displayedIndex < moveHistory.length - 1;`
  No wash post-game (isGameActive false) — matches "when the game is live."

### Why NOT `viewIndex !== null`
`viewIndex !== null` is the obvious-looking signal but is wrong: `viewIndex` can be a
**non-null latest index**, which would wash the board while it still shows the latest
position. Concretely:
- `ConnectedAnalysisGraph` (AnalysisConnectors.tsx:138) forwards clicks to `handleNavigate`
  with NO normalization, and `AnalysisGraph.handleClick` (AnalysisGraph.tsx:231) emits a
  numeric index for *every* click including the rightmost point. `handleNavigate` stores it
  directly via `setViewIndex(index)` (ChessGame.tsx:426). MoveList, by contrast, DOES
  normalize latest→null (MoveList.tsx:217) — so the invariant holds for the move list but
  not for the graph.
- The blunder rewind sets `setViewIndex(startIndex)` where `startIndex` =
  `displayedIndexRef.current` (ChessGame.tsx:1449); when the user was live that is the
  latest index, briefly making `viewIndex` a non-null latest before it steps back 125ms
  later.

`displayedIndex < moveHistory.length - 1` is correct in all of these regardless of whether
any caller normalizes: graph-latest-click → displayedIndex = last → no wash; blunder-rewind
brief window → displayedIndex = last → no wash until the board actually steps back; and when
trailing moves are unanalyzed (graph's rightmost point < last ply) it still correctly washes
because you really are off the latest move (a "graph-latest→null" normalization would get
that subtle case wrong).

## Precedent: the analysis what-if wash (g-vf6b)
`src/App.css` ~line 4340:
```css
.analysis-board__board-frame--variation [data-square] {
    filter: saturate(0.55) brightness(1.06) contrast(0.95);
    transition: filter 0.2s ease;
}
```
Key lesson from g-vf6b: scope the filter to `[data-square]` only — NOT the whole board
frame — so move arrows (react-chessboard SVG overlay, a sibling of the squares) and any
badges keep full saturation/contrast. saturate/brightness/contrast are per-pixel point
filters, so per-square filtering is visually identical to filtering the whole board, with
no seams. The game board renders blunder arrows via the Chessboard `arrows` prop (same SVG
overlay), so the identical `[data-square]` scoping keeps those vivid here too.

## Implementation

### 1. `src/components/chess-game/ui/BoardStage.tsx`
The live board is rendered here, with `<Chessboard>` wrapped by
`<div ref={boardSquareRef} className="chessboard-square-measure">` (line ~329). This is the
direct analog of AnalysisBoard's `--variation` frame.
- Add a prop: `isReviewingPast?: boolean;` (default `false`) to `BoardStageProps` and the
  destructured param list.
- Toggle a modifier class on the measure wrapper:
  ```tsx
  className={`chessboard-square-measure${isReviewingPast ? " chessboard-square-measure--reviewing" : ""}`}
  ```
  Keep the existing `ref={boardSquareRef}` (the SrsFailSpotlight target) untouched.

### 2. `src/components/ChessGame.tsx`
- Derive the flag near `isViewingLive` (line 405), reusing the existing `displayedIndex`
  memo (line 362) and `moveHistory`:
  `const isReviewingPast = isGameActive && displayedIndex < moveHistory.length - 1;`
- Pass it to `<BoardStage ... isReviewingPast={isReviewingPast} />` (the prop block at
  lines ~1908-1957).

### 3. `src/App.css`
Add, next to / cross-referencing the what-if rule (~line 4340), a lighter wash scoped the
same way:
```css
/* Reviewing a past move during a LIVE game: a lighter cousin of the what-if wash
   (.analysis-board__board-frame--variation) — same per-square [data-square] scoping so
   blunder arrows stay vivid, but noticeably LESS desaturated so the live game still reads
   as in-progress, not a disabled hypothetical. */
.chessboard-square-measure--reviewing [data-square] {
    filter: saturate(0.78) brightness(1.03) contrast(0.97);
    transition: filter 0.2s ease;
}
```
Filter values are tunable — what-if uses `saturate(0.55)`; `~0.78` is the "noticeably less
desaturated" target (visibly washed, clearly milder than analysis). Final number to be
eyeballed in the running app; brightness/contrast nudged toward 1.0 for the same reason.

## Behavior notes / edge cases
- `viewIndex === -1` / `displayedIndex === -1` (before move 1) → `-1 < length-1` true (when
  ≥1 move exists) → wash applies. Correct: user is off the latest move.
- `moveHistory.length === 0` → `displayedIndex === -1`, `-1 < -1` false → no wash. Correct:
  nothing to review at game start.
- Graph click on the latest move → `displayedIndex = length-1` → no wash. (This is the case
  `viewIndex !== null` would have gotten wrong.)
- Blunder-rewind brief window (line 1449 sets viewIndex to the latest index for ~125ms before
  stepping back) → `displayedIndex = length-1` → no wash until the board actually steps to a
  past ply. Correct.
- Drills are live games (isGameActive true) → wash applies there too. Consistent.
- Live→past fades the wash in via the 0.2s transition; past→live fades it out.
- Last-move highlight tints live on `[data-square]` and get washed too — desired, matches
  the what-if precedent (highlights are part of the position, not a vivid overlay).
- Blunder arrows / flash / board notices are siblings of the squares (or full overlays), so
  the `[data-square]` scope leaves them at full vibrancy.

## Tests
Mirror the AnalysisBoard variation-class test (jsdom can't assert CSS `filter`; assert the
class contract the selector hangs off):
- `src/components/chess-game/ui/BoardStage.test.tsx` (react-chessboard is already mocked, so
  add `isReviewingPast` to nothing in `makeProps` — it defaults false):
  - `it("washes the board when reviewing a past move")`: render with
    `isReviewingPast`, assert `container.querySelector(".chessboard-square-measure--reviewing")`
    is present.
  - `it("does not wash the board on the live position")`: render with default props, assert
    that selector is null but `.chessboard-square-measure` exists.
- Optional (only if cheap with the existing harness): a ChessGame-level assertion that the
  derived prop follows `isGameActive && displayedIndex < moveHistory.length - 1` — in
  particular that a latest-ply view (incl. a non-null latest `viewIndex` from a graph click)
  does NOT wash. The derivation is a one-liner; the BoardStage class-toggle test is the
  meaningful guard, so skip if ChessGame's test setup makes viewIndex navigation expensive.

## Out of scope (but noted)
- No change to the analysis/what-if wash itself.
- No new store state — purely derived from existing `displayedIndex` + `isGameActive`.
- No change to which moves are navigable or to arrows/badges.
- **Pre-existing, separate from this issue:** because the graph path does NOT normalize a
  latest click to `null` (unlike MoveList), clicking the rightmost graph point leaves
  `viewIndex` non-null at the latest ply, which makes `isViewingLive` (line 405) false and
  blocks piece dragging even though the latest position is shown. This plan's
  `displayedIndex`-based wash is immune to that, so it is NOT a blocker here. If we want the
  graph to behave like the move list (and restore can-move on a latest click), normalize in
  `handleNavigate`: `setViewIndex(index !== null && index === moveHistory.length - 1 ? null : index)`.
  Recommend a separate bead for that consistency fix rather than bundling it into g-9y2a.

## Files touched
- `src/components/chess-game/ui/BoardStage.tsx` (prop + class toggle)
- `src/components/ChessGame.tsx` (derive + pass prop)
- `src/App.css` (new `.chessboard-square-measure--reviewing [data-square]` rule)
- `src/components/chess-game/ui/BoardStage.test.tsx` (class-toggle guard)

title: Off-tree board move: loading spinner belongs inside the frontier column, not a new column
description: On /openings, dropping a legal off-tree move on the board (g-obh5 third move type) shows a separate appended loading column with a spinner while the refetch is in flight. But the new move's card actually settles INTO the existing deepest (frontier) column as a selected/expanded sibling — so the separate loading column is misleading and the frontier column renders unselected during loading. Fix: for the off-tree append case, do not render the standalone append column; render the loading spinner + label below the existing cards in that frontier column (the column the new card will land in).
design:
# Plan: off-tree board move — loading spinner inside the frontier column (g-42md)

## Problem / data flow

`/openings` is server-built + URL-driven. A board drop calls `handlePieceDrop`
(`OpeningsPage.tsx`): an in-tree frontier move selects its existing node; any
other legal move calls `selectLine(view.selectionLine.concat(uci))` (the g-obh5
third type). That rewrites the `move=` URL → `useOpeningsTree` enters **Step 3**
(extend, displayed present):

- `divergence = commonPrefix(displayed.line, requestedLine)` = N (old length).
- `selectionLine = requestedLine.slice(0, divergence+1)` = the full new line (N+1).
- `loadedThroughPly = divergence` = N; `appendStatus = "loading"`.

`buildTreeView` then renders api columns with `ply <= N` from the OLD response.
The deepest column is `lineIndex = N` (the old frontier, children of position N).
Its `selectedUci = selectionLine[N] = uci`, but `uci` is off-tree → **not among
its nodes** → that column has **no selected node** (renders unselected, header
"—"). The page also appends a standalone `openings-tree-append--loading` column
(display index `view.columns.length`) with a spinner + "—" header.

When the refetch settles, the backend injects `uci` into the position-N column
(`openings.py` build loop, `selected_uci not in column` → inject) as a
selected+expanded user-selected node. So the new card lands in the **existing**
position-N column (now showing the old siblings + the new selected card), and a
genuinely-new column N+1 (the next frontier) appears.

**Bug:** during loading we draw a spurious extra column for the spinner, while the
column the card actually lands in renders unselected with no loading affordance.

## Desired behavior (user directive)

Do NOT create the separate append column for the off-tree case. Render the
spinner + "Loading…" label BELOW the existing cards inside the frontier column
(the deepest rendered moves column — the one the new card will settle into).
In-tree forward selection (the selected card already renders in the deepest
column; the append column = the next frontier) is UNCHANGED.

## Detection

In `OpeningsPage` (where `columns`/`selectionLine` are already derived for the
connector plumbing), compute:

```ts
const lastColumn = columns?.[columns.length - 1] ?? null;
const offTreeLoading =
  appendStatus === "loading" &&
  lastColumn?.kind === "moves" &&
  selectionLine[lastColumn.lineIndex] !== undefined && // a move is selected at this ply
  !lastColumn.nodes.some((n) => n.isSelected);         // …but it's not in this column → off-tree
const showAppendColumn = appendStatus === "loading" && !offTreeLoading;
```

This correctly distinguishes:
- in-tree frontier selection / forward nav (deepest column HAS the selected node) → append column kept;
- color switch / empty frontier (`selectionLine[lineIndex]` undefined) → append column kept;
- off-tree drop (selected move present in line but not in the column) → spinner inside column.
- Graceful fallback: if the off-tree move's column does not exist in the displayed
  response (deepest position had no frontier column), `lastColumn` is a column whose
  own selected move IS present → `offTreeLoading=false` → append column fallback.

## Changes

1. **`src/pages/OpeningsPage.tsx`**
   - Compute `offTreeLoading` / `showAppendColumn` near the connector plumbing.
   - `connectorColumnCount = columnCount + (showAppendColumn ? 1 : 0)` (was
     `appendStatus === "loading" ? 1 : 0`). Connector-safe: the deepest column has
     no selected node, so `useTreeConnectors` already draws an `unconnected`
     dangling stub from the prior selected card toward it (same as a normal
     frontier); removing the +1 only drops the already-empty append-column pair.
   - Gate the standalone append-loading column JSX on `showAppendColumn`.
   - Pass `showLoadingFooter={offTreeLoading && index === cols.length - 1}` to the
     deepest `TreeColumnView`.

2. **`TreeColumnView`** — add optional `showLoadingFooter?: boolean`; when true,
   render a footer (spinner + "Loading…") AFTER the node `.map`, still inside the
   `__nodes` scroller (so it sits below the cards and scrolls with them). Reuse the
   existing `openings-tree-append__spinner` / `__label` classes in a new
   `openings-tree-column__loading-footer` wrapper.

3. **`src/App.css`** — add `.openings-tree-column__loading-footer` (centered,
   small top padding / hairline separator above the spinner row).

## Why the network call is still required (answer to the open question)

We cannot skip `GET /api/openings/tree` for an off-tree move:
- **Transposition** — an off-book move can transpose into a known book/observed
  position (backend resolves by normalized FEN). The frontend has no copy of the
  opening graph or observed-edge read model, so it can't know the position is
  novel, nor surface its name/eco/metrics.
- **Next frontier** — the new position's children (book + observed) come only from
  the backend; the frontend can't enumerate book moves locally.
- **Eval cache** — the backend may hold a cached engine eval for the new move
  (`analysis_cache`), shown on the card.
- **Canonical line / terminal reason** — truncation (illegal/cycle/over-deep),
  `selected_is_terminal`, etc. are backend-computed.

Future enhancement (not this bead): render the off-tree card OPTIMISTICALLY (SAN
from local chess.js replay, blank metrics — the expected end state for a novel
position) so only the NEXT column shows a spinner, then reconcile with the
refetch. Bigger change; deferred.

## Tests

- `OpeningsPage.test.tsx`: new case — off-tree drop with a PENDING refetch asserts
  the loading footer renders inside the frontier column and NO
  `.openings-tree-append--loading` column exists; then resolves and asserts the
  settled expanded "Your move" card. Keep the existing immediate-resolve off-tree
  test.
- Existing "Loading…" assertions (in-tree click, color switch) stay green
  (those are not off-tree → append column retained).
notes: Implemented: offTreeLoading detection in OpeningsPage; spinner footer inside the frontier column (TreeColumnView showLoadingFooter); append column gated on showAppendColumn; connectorColumnCount drops the +1 in the off-tree case. Added OpeningsPage test (pending off-tree drop → footer in frontier column, no append column). 27 OpeningsPage + 28 treeView/hook tests green. Not committed (awaiting review).

title: End-of-game/drill opening-score delta
description: After a game or drill ends, recompute opening scores and show how the played openings' scores changed (before -> after delta), alongside the rating-delta in PostGameBanner for games, and in the same banner for drills (where there is no rating delta). Requires a per-session baseline snapshot of opening scores at session start and a synchronous recompute at end.
design:
# g-xanz — End-of-game/drill opening-score delta

Parent: g-bs4s. After a game or drill ends, recompute opening scores and show how
the **played openings'** scores changed (before → after), in `PostGameBanner`
where the rating-delta lives. Depends on g-8nke landing first (shares the lineage
model).

## The core problem: where does "before" come from?
Opening scores are CUMULATIVE over all evidence, and live games upload moves
incrementally — each upload already feeds `request_recompute` DURING the game. So
at game end the cached score already reflects most of this game; there is no
"pre-game" score left to diff against unless we snapshot it up front.

**Solution: per-session baseline snapshot at session start.**
1. When a game/drill session is created (before any of its moves are uploaded),
   snapshot the user's current opening scores for that `player_color` into a
   session-scoped baseline: a JSON map `{opening_key: score}`. Bounded by the
   number of opening roots the user has (dozens–low hundreds).
2. At session end, force a synchronous recompute (`refresh_now(user, color,
   timeout)`), read the played-opening chain + fresh scores, and diff each played
   opening's `after` against `baseline[opening_key]` (None ⇒ brand-new opening,
   render as "new" rather than a numeric delta).

### Backend changes
- **Model/schema**: add `opening_score_baseline` (JSON/nullable) to `GameSession`
  (the model used for both games and drills). Per project memory, SQLite test
  schema is hand-written — add the column in the SQLAlchemy model, an Alembic
  migration, AND `conftest._create_test_schema`.
- **Populate baseline at creation**: in the session-create path (game + drill),
  call `load_cached_rows(db, user_id, player_color)` and store
  `{row.opening_key: row.opening_score}`. Keep it cheap/best-effort: on cold cache
  this triggers the bounded initial compute already; wrap so a failure leaves
  baseline null (delta simply omitted) rather than blocking session creation.
- **Compute delta at end**: a shared helper
  `compute_opening_score_delta(db, session, user) -> list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem]`:
  1. `refresh_now(user_id, player_color)` (best-effort; on False serve cached).
  2. `chain = played_opening_chain([m.fen_after ...], get_opening_roots())`
     (same as `get_session_openings`).
  3. `_, rows = load_cached_rows(...)`; `rows_by_key`.
  4. For each root in chain: `after = row.opening_score`,
     `before = baseline.get(opening_key)`,
     `delta = after-before` when both present else None (is_new = before is None).
  5. Return broadest→deepest list of
     `{opening_key, opening_name, before, after, delta, is_new}`.
- **Wire into endpoints**:
  - `POST /api/game/end` (game.py:654) — add
    `opening_score_changes: list[OpeningScoreDeltaItem] | None` to
    `GameEndResponse` (alongside existing `score_changes`).
  - `POST /api/drills/{id}/natural-end` (drills.py:452) and the drill-fail path
    (`checkDrillRoute` → failed) — return the same delta list. Decide a shared
    response field; `DrillSessionContract` may need an `opening_score_changes`
    field, or return a small sidecar. Prefer extending the contract for symmetry.
- Note: `refresh_now` is bounded (default 5s) and best-effort. End-of-game is an
  acceptable place to block briefly; on timeout we still show after-scores (delta
  may be approximate/omitted). Log when baseline is null (older sessions) and
  render after-scores without a delta in that case.

## Frontend changes
- **api.ts**: add `OpeningScoreDeltaItem` type and thread
  `opening_score_changes` onto `GameEndResponse` and the drill end/fail responses.
- **Store**: add `openingScoreChanges` to `useGameStore` (next to `scoreChanges`).
