# g-8nke — Live opening hierarchy in game chess-panel Parent: g-bs4s. Replace the single-line "Opening: ECO Name" text in the live game panel (`GameInfoPanel.tsx:530-539`, the `chess-panel__opening` `

`) with a growing vertical opening-lineage hierarchy, reusing the `/history` analysis-footer components (`GameOpeningLineage` + `OpeningFamilyCard` variant="analysis"). This revision incorporates **review round 2** (findings A–E below) AND the product decision that **clicking a live card must NOT jump the active board away from live play** (unlike the /history footer). Round-1 findings (1–4, 6) are retained where still valid; round-1 finding 5 (board-jump indexing) is now MOOT — see "Live cards are expand-only". ## What the user sees During an active game, the panel shows the "Your Opening Scores" lineage — a broadest→deepest stack of opening cards (King's Pawn → Italian Game → Giuoco Piano …) each with score + grade tag — growing as new opening boundaries are crossed (subject to the analysis/upload lag documented below). Tapping a card expands `OpeningFamilyCard` (coverage / games / confidence) with a "View in Openings" link. **Tapping a card only expands it in place — it does NOT move the live board.** ## Live cards are expand-only (NEW product decision — supersedes round-1 finding 5) In the /history footer, tapping a chip BOTH expands the inline card AND jumps the analysis board to that opening's root (`HistoryPage.handleSelectRoot` → `boardRef.jumpToMove`). In the LIVE panel we must not do that: the board is following live play, and yanking `viewIndex` to an earlier ply mid-game is wrong. **Resolution:** the live lineage renders with **no `onSelectRoot`** — tapping a chip only toggles its expanded card. To allow this without breaking /history: - Make `GameOpeningLineage.onSelectRoot?` **optional** (currently required at `GameOpeningLineage.tsx:14`). - In the chip `onClick` (`GameOpeningLineage.tsx:101-104`), always `setExpandedKey(item.opening_key)` but call `onSelectRoot?.(item)` only when defined. - **Chip wording (finding L2).** The chip's `aria-label` (`:100`) and the adjacent comment currently say "Select … and toggle details" and assume the click selects a root. Make the label conditional: when `onSelectRoot` is provided → `Select ${name} and toggle details` (history parity); when omitted (live expand-only) → `Show ${name} details`. Update the stale comment to match. - Live panel omits the prop → expand-only. `/history` keeps passing `handleSelectRoot` → board-jump (and "Select …" wording) unchanged there. **Consequence:** there is **no board-jump helper** in this bead. The round-1 `resolveOpeningRootViewIndex` helper, the `setViewIndex` wiring, and its `-1`/ initial-FEN semantics (round-2 finding D) are all dropped — the live board is never repositioned from this UI, so the indexing question disappears. `src/components/ chess-game/domain/opening.ts` is NOT modified. ## Data source + live-lag handling (findings A & B — HIGH) Reuse `fetchSessionOpenings(sessionId)` → `{ player_color, lineage: OpeningLineageItem[] }`. No new endpoint. Extract HistoryPage's inline fetch pattern (`HistoryPage.tsx:133-150`) into a shared hook used by both pages. ### Honest staleness model (finding B — corrects the round-1 overclaim) The round-1 claim "staleness window ≤ one poll interval" was **false**. The server builds the lineage **chain** from persisted `SessionMove.fen_after` rows (`backend/app/api/session.py:1235`, via `played_opening_chain(...)`). Those rows reach the server only AFTER each move's analysis resolves and uploads: `GameAnalysisCoordinator` adds the index to `dirtyIndices` **after analysis resolves** (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1381`), then `flushIncrementalUpload` batches/timers the actual `uploadSessionMoves` POST. So a newly crossed opening boundary cannot appear in the panel until: local move → **analysis resolves** for that ply → **incremental upload** persists `fen_after` → next poll tick reads it. The real lag is therefore **analysis-gated + upload-gated + ≤ one poll interval**, NOT one interval. Polling only converges the upload→display gap; it cannot beat analysis+upload. We **document this** (the accepted resolution) rather than build a local boundary engine. > Deferred alternative (NOT in this bead): compute live boundaries locally from > `openingHistoryRef`/openingBook and merge server scores. That requires porting > `played_opening_chain` + the `get_opening_roots()` registry (opening_key / > family / eco / depth / path) to the client — a much larger, higher-risk change. > Filed as a follow-up if instant boundary appearance is wanted. For openings > (crossed in the first ~10–15 plies, whose analysis resolves quickly) the gated > lag is acceptable for a "current scores" display, consistent with the existing > stale-while-revalidate score reader (`session.py:1240`). ### Refetch + bounded poll-while-active (no coordinator changes) - Refetch when `moveHistory.length` changes (`refetchKey`) — picks up already- uploaded plies promptly. - ALSO poll on a fixed modest interval (default ~4000ms) **while `isGameActive`**, so a ply that uploads after its local move event is picked up on the next tick. Stop polling when `!isGameActive`. - **No final refetch on the active→inactive transition** (finding C — MEDIUM, removed). The round-1 plan fired one last fetch "after the coordinator's end-of-game `flushPendingUploads`", but `flushPendingUploads()` does NOT await server completion (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1653` just starts the upload) and game-end calls it fire-and-forget (`useChessGameLifecycle.ts:283`, `.catch(...)`). A refetch at the transition would race the in-flight upload and usually miss it — and the panel is **hidden when inactive anyway** (active-only gate below), so there is nothing to refetch for. Polling simply stops. - Keep the PRIOR lineage on screen during a same-session refetch (replace only when the new result resolves) so the stack never flashes empty between ticks. - Rationale for poll-vs-listener: the coordinator is a delicate invariant-heavy singleton; polling is the lowest-risk option. (A cleaner `onUploadComplete` listener beside `analysisOutcomeListeners` is noted but NOT chosen.) ### New hook: `src/hooks/useSessionOpenings.ts` ```ts export function useSessionOpenings( sessionId: string | null, // null disables fetching entirely (see enabled guard) opts: { refetchKey: number; // bump to force refetch (move count) pollIntervalMs?: number; // when set + active, converge upload→display lag active?: boolean; // gate polling (ChessGame: isGameActive) }, ): { lineage: OpeningLineageItem[]; playerColor: OpeningPlayerColor }; ``` **Enabled / null-session guard (finding M2 — preserve HistoryPage's zero-move skip).** A `null` `sessionId` means "don't fetch" — the effect early-returns and no request fires. HistoryPage today skips `fetchSessionOpenings` while `analysisMoveCount === 0` (`HistoryPage.tsx:134`), and a test asserts it (`HistoryPage.test.tsx:377` — "does not fetch openings when analysis has no moves"). To keep that behavior, HistoryPage passes `analysisMoveCount > 0 ? selectedId : null` as `sessionId` (equivalently an `enabled` flag — chosen form: the `null` sentinel, since the hook already treats `null` as disabled). ChessGame passes the live `sessionId` directly (the active gate handles its empty state). **Polling lifecycle + out-of-order safety (finding H1 — HIGH).** - `active` and `pollIntervalMs` MUST be **effect dependencies** so the effect tears down and re-runs when `isGameActive` flips. Effect dep array: `[sessionId, refetchKey, active, pollIntervalMs]`. On `active → false` the effect cleanup clears the timer, so polling cannot continue after the game ends. - **No overlapping requests.** Schedule the next poll **only after the previous one settles** (sequential `setTimeout` re-arm in the `.then/.finally`, NOT `setInterval`), so a slow tick can't stack on the next. Each tick also **aborts the previous in-flight request** via its `AbortController`. - **Out-of-order guard.** A monotonically increasing request sequence number is captured per fetch; on resolve, commit `setState` only if the response is the latest issued (`seq === latestSeqRef.current`) AND not cancelled AND its `sessionId` still matches. This prevents a slower OLDER response from overwriting a newer/deeper lineage for the same session (abort alone doesn't guarantee ordering across fast `refetchKey` bumps). - Cleanup on unmount / dep-change: set `cancelled = true`, `abort()` the in-flight request, and `clearTimeout` the pending poll. **Loaded-session guard (finding A — HIGH).** The hook must NEVER show a prior game's stack in a new game. Round-1 only said "keep prior lineage during refetch" with no session check; that would leak game A's lineage into game B until B's first fetch resolved. HistoryPage handles this today by clearing on game change (`HistoryPage.tsx:162`). The hook adopts that responsibility for BOTH pages via a single state object stamped with the session it belongs to: ```ts const [state, setState] = useState<{ sessionId: string | null; lineage: OpeningLineageItem[]; playerColor: OpeningPlayerColor; }>({ sessionId: null, lineage: [], playerColor: 'white' }); // Derived guard: prior data is shown ONLY for the same session; a session change // yields [] synchronously (no flash of the previous game), held until the new // session's fetch commits. const lineage = state.sessionId === sessionId ? state.lineage : []; const playerColor = state.sessionId === sessionId ? state.playerColor : 'white'; ``` - Effect keyed on `[sessionId, refetchKey, active, pollIntervalMs]`; early-returns when `sessionId == null`. A sequential poll is re-armed only when `pollIntervalMs && active` (see polling-lifecycle above) — never `setInterval`. - Each fetch uses a fresh `AbortController` (finding 4, round 1), a `cancelled` flag, and a sequence number (guards setState after resolve/unmount and against out-of-order responses). - On resolve, commit `setState({ sessionId, lineage: data.lineage, playerColor: data.player_color })` only if `!cancelled && seq === latestSeq && sessionId` unchanged — so neither a late response for an old session NOR a slow older poll for the current session can overwrite newer data. - Error handling: on error, **keep prior same-session data**; only commit `[]` for the FIRST load of a session that has no prior data (so a transient failure doesn't blank an established stack). A session change already shows `[]` via the derived guard. - HistoryPage adopts it as `useSessionOpenings(analysisMoveCount > 0 ? selectedId : null, { refetchKey: analysisMoveCount })` (no polling — game is finished; the `null` sentinel preserves the zero-move skip that `HistoryPage.test.tsx:377` asserts). Its inline effect (`HistoryPage.tsx:133-150`), the `openingLineage` `useState` (`:39`), and the manual `setOpeningLineage([])` in `handleGameChange` (`:162`) are removed — the hook owns that state and reset. ## Active-game gate + dead-code removal (round-1 finding 3; finding L1) The live lineage renders ONLY while `isGameActive` (same gate as today's `

` at `GameInfoPanel.tsx:530`). There is NO post-game lineage in the panel; post-game opening context + drill entry belong to g-xanz's `PostGameBanner`. When `isGameActive` but the lineage is still empty (before the first boundary appears), render nothing (default) — the prior one-line `Opening: …` fallback is dropped. **Removing the `

` orphans the old opening derivation (finding L1).** Once the `chess-panel__opening` `

Extend to `fetchSessionOpenings(sessionId, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal })`, threading `signal` into `requestJson` exactly like `uploadSessionMoves` (`api.ts:844`). The hook passes a per-fetch `AbortController.signal`; the `cancelled` flag remains as belt-and-suspenders. ## Start Drill hidden in the live panel (round-1 finding 2) `OpeningFamilyCard` renders Start Drill only when `onStartDrill` is provided (`OpeningFamilyCard.tsx:183`, optional at `:32`), but `GameOpeningLineage` currently REQUIRES `onStartDrill` (`:15`) and always forwards a wrapper (`:77`). Add `.game-page .chess-panel__openings { display:none }` beside it so the lineage is hidden on mobile too (parity with today; no compact-row redesign in this bead). ## Wiring summary (live game) - In `ChessGame.tsx`: `const { lineage, playerColor } = useSessionOpenings( sessionId, { refetchKey: moveHistory.length, pollIntervalMs: 4000, active: isGameActive });` then render `GameOpeningLineage` with `lineage` + `playerColor`, **no `onSelectRoot`, no `onStartDrill`** (wrapped in `.chess-panel__openings`, only when `isGameActive`). - Pass it into `GameInfoPanel` as a slot prop `openingLineageSlot?: React.ReactNode` replacing the `chess-panel__opening` `

` (keeps memo'd GameInfoPanel presentational; data/hooks stay in ChessGame). ## Tests - `useSessionOpenings.test`: - refetch on `refetchKey` change; - **poll-while-active converges an upload-lagged fetch** (first fetch returns a shallow lineage, advance timers, second fetch returns deeper); - keep-prior-while-loading within the SAME session (no empty flash); - **session change → lineage immediately `[]`, does NOT show prior session's stack** (finding A), and a late response for the old session can't overwrite the new one; - **out-of-order poll (finding H1):** issue two fetches for the SAME session where the FIRST (shallower) resolves AFTER the second (deeper); assert the final state is the deeper lineage, not clobbered by the slow older response (sequence guard); - **null `sessionId` fires no fetch** (finding M2 — the hook-level analogue of HistoryPage's zero-move skip); - `[]`-only on first error with no prior data; prior data retained on a transient error mid-session; - polling stops when `active=false`; no fetch fired on the active→inactive transition (finding C); flipping `active` false tears down the timer (no further ticks); - abort + cancel on unmount; `playerColor` passthrough. - `GameOpeningLineage.test`: - Start Drill hidden when `onStartDrill` omitted, shown when provided; - **`onSelectRoot` omitted → tapping a chip expands the card but does NOT call any select callback** (live expand-only); when provided, tapping calls it (history parity). - `GameInfoPanel`/`ChessGame` test: lineage slot renders when `isGameActive` + non-empty; hidden when inactive. - **`ChessGame.test.tsx` api-mock (finding M3):** the mock spreads the real module and only overrides listed endpoints (`ChessGame.test.tsx:37-56`), so adding the hook would let `fetchSessionOpenings` fall through to the REAL helper (network) in many existing tests. title: Re-center opening-score v2 grade thresholds onto observed distribution
description: Follow-up to g-score-v2-rollout §7. The June 2026 recalibration run (calibrate_opening_scores_v2, prod DB) shows the score distribution is centered far below the retained A≥85…F<45 scale, so nearly every card grades F/alert and the grade conveys no signal. Re-center the grade + tone boundaries onto the observed percentiles so grades differentiate. User decided: re-center now, and KEEP showing the raw score number (accept 'A at 50').
design:
# g-g5sg — Re-center opening-score v2 grade thresholds

## Origin
Recalibration follow-up to closed bead `g-score-v2-rollout` §7 ("grade-threshold
+ tau decision"). The `format.ts` comment (g-m36y) had retained the original
A≥85…F<45 scale because the first calibration cohort was ~95% one user.

## Calibration evidence (run 2026-06-24, prod Railway DB)
`python -m scripts.calibrate_opening_scores_v2 --database-url=<prod>`

- Candidate pairs 13 | included (≥20 obs) 6 | low-evidence 7.
- Pooled named-root scores (n=450): mean 32.8, p5 18.9, p25 25.0, p50 33.3,
  p75 36.3, p95 54.7. Histogram (0-20/20-40/40-60/60-80/80-100) = [42,328,69,11,0].
- Per-user median summary (n=6): all six pairs' medians 30.6–34.1 (mean 32.6).
  → low center is REAL across users, not a user-14 artifact.
- Still volume-dominated: user 14 = 426/450 pooled rows (94.7%). So central
  tendency is trustworthy; fine 5-band *shape* is one-user-driven (accepted).
- Synthetic hero (__repertoire__) mean 33.6.
- tau_wc=0.20, tau_cp=100. Source mix 99.6% session_eval. Horizon mean 15.3 ply.

## Problem
Under retained A≥85/B≥70/C≥55/D≥45 (alert<45/watch<65): >75% of cards grade F,
~95% D-or-F, 0% reach C+; median card renders red "alert". Grade is a constant.

## Decisions (user, 2026-06-24)
1. Re-center NOW (not hold).
2. KEEP showing the raw score number next to the grade (accept "A at 50").
   formatScore unchanged; grade = relative signal, number = absolute quality.
3. tau retained at 0.20/100 (out of scope here; scope is grade/tone bands only).

## New boundaries (anchored on pooled percentiles)
getPriorityLabel:  A≥50 (~top 7%, p95=54.7) · B≥38 (~p82) · C≥28 (~p40,
  median 33 lands mid-C) · D≥22 (~p12) · F<22 (~bottom 12%).
getPriorityTone:   alert<25 (~bottom p25, genuinely weak) · watch<38 (~p25–p82)
  · steady≥38.
Resulting pooled grade mix ≈ A 7% / B 11% / C 42% / D 28% / F 12%; median = C.

## Files
- `src/openings/format.ts` — getPriorityLabel + getPriorityTone boundaries;
  rewrite the lines 36-40 comment to cite this run (g-g5sg) + docs section.
- `src/openings/format.test.ts` — already exists (the §7 "create it" note is
  stale). Update getPriorityLabel / getPriorityTone / getGradeToken /
  getGradeText boundary fixtures + the header comment.
- `src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx` — childView score 72 now grades
  A (was B): update the two "Grade B" assertions (~L86-87, L250) → "Grade A";
  update the it.each grade table (L335-340) to new representative scores
  [90→A, 42→B, 32→C, 24→D, 10→F]. (File has an unrelated 1-line uncommitted
  deletion from another agent at ~L207 — leave it.)
- `docs/openingscore_final.md` — update "Calibration Outcome (v2)" with the
  2026-06-24 run + new thresholds + rationale; note tau retained.

## Out of scope
tau change; formatScore display change; the raw-number rescale option (rejected).

## Verify

title: Allow chessboard to add non-tree moves
description: Currently the /openings tree shows two types of moves, opening book moves and moves played by the player. Add a third type of move, moves selected on the chessboard. Currently the chessboard doesn't allow you to make moves that are not in the tree, relax that so any legal move can be made on the board. If the move is not currently in the tree add it to the tree.
design:
# Plan: Allow chessboard to add non-tree moves (g-obh5)

## Goal & decided scope

On `/openings`, the board currently only accepts moves that already exist in the
tree (book moves + the player's observed moves). Relax this so **any legal move**
can be played on the board. A legal move that is not in the tree becomes a third
move type — a **user-selected move** — rendered as a navigable node.

Decisions (confirmed with user):
- **Persistence: ephemeral / URL-scoped.** The selected move is navigable only
  while it is part of the current explored line (encoded in the URL `move=`
  params). It survives a reload of that URL and deeper exploration, but vanishes
  once it leaves the line. No new DB table, no recompute integration.
- **Data: null/empty when uncached.** A brand-new position has no
  `opening_position_scores` row and usually no `analysis_cache` eval, so
  score/coverage/games/confidence/eval render blank. Whatever the eval cache
  happens to hold is still shown (existing lookup is by `(parent_full_fen, uci)`).
  On-demand analysis is explicitly out of scope (future bead).

## Architecture recap (why a backend change is required)

The tree is **server-built and URL-driven**. The board never mutates the tree
locally: every move (node click or board drop) rewrites the URL `move=` line via
`selectLine` → `useOpeningsTree` refetches `GET /api/openings/tree` → the backend
returns the full column model → `buildTreeView` renders it. So a non-tree move
must be accepted by the backend's line resolver, or the refetch will truncate it
and the board will snap back.

Backend gate today (`backend/app/api/openings.py`):
- `_resolve_moves` (1074-1107) truncates the line at the first move that is not in
  `_structural_children(parent)` (line 1096) or that makes the position a leaf
  (line 1094).
- `_structural_children` = observed edges ∪ book edges whose child is not a
  middlegame position. A legal-but-unknown move is not in this set → truncated.
- Columns are built from `_column_children` (structural ∪ display-only middlegame
  book boundaries). Boundary nodes are `is_navigable=False`,
  `terminal_reason="opening_boundary"`.

## Backend changes (`backend/app/api/openings.py`)

### 1. Accept any legal move in `_resolve_moves` (1074-1107)
Replace the structural-membership gate with a legality gate. Keep every other
guard (malformed UCI → 422, max ply, true game-over, illegal move, cycle/
repetition via the `visited` normalized-FEN set).

```python
parent_norm = normalize_fen(board.fen())
if board.is_checkmate() or board.is_stalemate():
    break                                   # no legal continuations exist
if move not in board.legal_moves:
    break                                   # keep illegal-move truncation
board.push(move)
child_norm = normalize_fen(board.fen())
if child_norm in visited:                   # keep cycle guard
    board.pop(); break
visited.add(child_norm)
line.append(token)
```
Remove the `_is_leaf(...)` break (1094) and the `token not in _structural_children`
break (1096). Net effect: a legal move past the book/observed frontier is now kept
in the canonical line instead of being dropped. Cycles, illegality, and max-ply
(MAX_TREE_PLY=80) still bound abuse.

NOTE: `_is_leaf` is `checkmate or stalemate or not _column_children`. Replacing it
with the explicit checkmate/stalemate test is deliberate: a position past the book
boundary has no column children but *does* have legal moves, and we now want to
allow exploring them.

### 2. Inject the selected off-tree move into its parent column (build, 1208-1264)
**Critical: the build loop has its OWN leaf gate that must be replaced too.**
Line 1211 `if self._is_leaf(board_i, norm_i): continue` runs *before* any column
iteration. `_is_leaf` is `checkmate or stalemate or not _column_children`. For a
*second* consecutive off-tree move the parent position (the first off-tree
position) has no `_column_children`, so the loop would `continue` and never render
a node, request an eval, or load metrics for that selected move — even though
`_resolve_moves` kept it in the canonical line. Result: board shows the move, tree
has no node for it. So replace the build-time skip exactly like the resolver gate:
skip immediately only on true game-over, build the local column (injecting the
selected move), and `continue` only when the column ends up empty.

```python
for i in range(k + 1):
    board_i = boards[i]
    norm_i = pos_norm[i]
    if board_i.is_checkmate() or board_i.is_stalemate():
        continue                              # genuinely no children
    structural = self._structural_children(norm_i)
    column = dict(self._column_children(norm_i))   # local copy, not the cache
    selected_uci = line[i] if i < k else None
    if selected_uci is not None and selected_uci not in column:
        move = chess.Move.from_uci(selected_uci)   # pre-validated legal
        board_i.push(move); child_full = board_i.fen(); board_i.pop()
        column[selected_uci] = _ChildEdge(
            uci=selected_uci, child_fen=normalize_fen(child_full),
            in_book=False, is_observed=False, edge=None,
        )
    if not column:
        continue            # leaf with nothing selected (only at i == k) — no reveal column
    raw_nodes: list[_RawNode] = []
    for uci, child in column.items():
        ...
        is_user_selected = uci == selected_uci and uci not in structural
        is_navigable = uci in structural or is_user_selected
```
This preserves the old "no reveal column for a terminal deepest position" behavior
(`column` empty and `selected_uci is None` at `i == k` → `continue`), while a first
*and* second off-tree move both render because their parent column is non-empty
after injection. A chain of N off-tree moves now renders N nodes, each with its own
eval request and (usually null) metrics.

Two cases both resolve correctly:
- **Fully off-tree move** (not in book, not observed): injected above, not in
  `structural` → `is_user_selected=True`, forced navigable.
- **Display-only boundary move the user chose to cross** (in book, middlegame,
  already in `column` as non-navigable): `uci not in structural` → also becomes
  `is_user_selected=True` and forced navigable *for this line only*. When the same
  boundary move is NOT the selected move it stays `is_navigable=False` exactly as
  today (the existing boundary test still passes).

`terminal_reason` is computed unchanged via `_terminal_reason_for_child` with the
forced `is_navigable=True`; an off-tree move into a quiet position →
`"no_children"`, into a middlegame → `"opening_boundary"`. The card renders
terminal but the board still accepts a further legal move (relaxed `_resolve_moves`
keeps extending the line — a chain of selected moves is supported, including a
transposition back into the book, which naturally re-expands children).

### 3. Thread a `is_user_selected` discriminator end-to-end
- `_ChildEdge` (839): no change needed (we compute `is_user_selected` in the loop).
- `_RawNode` (856): add `is_user_selected: bool`.
- Populate it in the `_RawNode(...)` construction (1235) from the loop variable.
- `TreeNode` Pydantic model (786): add `is_user_selected: bool`.
- `_hydrate_node` (1358): pass `is_user_selected=rn.is_user_selected`.

`is_user_selected` is distinct from `in_book`/`is_observed`: a selected move is
`in_book=False, is_observed=False, is_user_selected=True` (or, for a crossed
boundary, `in_book=True, is_user_selected=True`). The frontend treats
`is_user_selected` as the strongest discriminator (third type wins over book).

## Frontend changes

### 4. Relax the board drop gate — `src/pages/OpeningsPage.tsx` `handlePieceDrop` (339-363)
Keep the legality check (`resolveDrop`) and `isSettled` guard. After the existing
in-tree lookup, fall through to extend the line for any legal move:

```ts
const uci = resolveDrop(view.board.fen, sourceSquare, targetSquare);
if (!uci) return false;                       // illegal → snap back (unchanged)
const frontier = view.columns.find(c => c.kind === "moves"
    && c.lineIndex === view.selectionLine.length);
const target = frontier?.nodes.find(n => n.uci === uci && n.isNavigable);
if (target) { selectLine(target.selectLine); return true; }   // in-tree path
selectLine(view.selectionLine.concat(uci));   // off-tree: extend the line
return true;
```
`selectLine(newLine)` already pushes `?move=...` history and the hook refetches.
The optimistic board state (piece stays because we returned `true`) reconciles
with the new `view.board.fen` once the refetch settles — identical to existing
in-tree drops. Works even when there is no frontier column (the selected position
was a leaf): we no longer require a matching node.

The `opening_explored` capture in `selectLine` (308) covers this automatically.

### 4b. Prevent URL-scoped selected nodes from leaking through the cache
`is_user_selected` nodes are **line-scoped**: the backend only emits one as the
selected move of its column. But `useOpeningsTree` can render a *deeper* cached
response for a *shorter* prefix without refetching, and `buildTreeView` maps every
visible column node regardless of whether the selected move still matches. Two
leak paths:
- **Step-2 prefix no-fetch** (`src/hooks/useOpeningsTree.ts:183`): direct-load
  `a2a3,a7a6`, then back to `a2a3`. The cached deep response is reused with
  `loadedThroughPly = 1`, so the frontier column (children of `a2a3`) still renders
  `a7a6` as a navigable selected sibling though it left the line. For a *selected
  boundary* move this also leaves a formerly forced-navigable boundary navigable.
- **Step-3 provisional frame** (`useOpeningsTree.ts` ~210): even if we force a
  refetch, the provisional render uses `loadedThroughPly = divergence`, which still
  shows the stale node for one frame until the exact response lands.

Two-part fix (both needed — refetch fixes metrics/freshness, the invariant fixes
the provisional frame):

1. **Refetch exact prefixes when the displayed response carries selected nodes**
   (reviewer's preference). In the Step-2 guard, add a condition that bails out of
   the no-fetch path when `displayed.response` contains any `is_user_selected`
   node (a cheap `columns.some(c => c.nodes.some(n => n.is_user_selected))`,
   memoized per response). Then back-nav falls through to Step 3 → exact fetch,
   whose column for `a2a3` contains only structural children (`a7a6` is neither
   selected nor structural there, so it is absent). Can be narrowed later to "a
   selected node at ply ≥ requested length" if cache efficiency matters; the broad
   form is correct and simple.
2. **Enforce the line-scope invariant in `buildTreeView`**
   (`src/openings/treeView.ts:289`). When mapping a column's nodes, treat a node
   with `is_user_selected === true && node.uci !== selectedUci` as **stale and
   omit it** (it only legitimately exists as the selected move of its own column).
   This is a local invariant — "a selected move is a node only while selected" —
   not a reconstruction of backend structural semantics, and it closes the
   provisional-frame and any exact-cache-of-deeper edge cases the refetch misses.

### 5. Wire type — `src/utils/api.ts` `TreeNode` (~1388)
Add `is_user_selected: boolean;` mirroring the backend field.

### 6. Display model — `src/openings/treeView.ts`
- `DisplayNode` (36): add `isUserSelected: boolean`.
- `buildTreeView` node map (290-307): `isUserSelected: node.is_user_selected`.
- Root node (264-279): `isUserSelected: false`.
- `OpeningTreeNodeView` (card view, in `OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx` 24-50): add
  `isUserSelected: boolean`; map it in `nodeToView` (113-130) and
  `synthesizeRootView` (139-163, `false`).

### 7. Card chip — `src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx`
Today `CompactBody`/`ExpandedBody` show `OffBookChip` when `!isRoot && !inBook`.
Split the third type out so it is not mislabeled "Off book" (which means the
player's own off-book *game* line):
- `isUserSelected` → render a new `SelectedMoveChip` ("Explored" / "Your move" —
  pick label in implementation; a clickable info popover like `OffBookChip`
  explaining "a move you played on the board; not from the book or your games").
- `!inBook && !isUserSelected` → existing `OffBookChip` (player's off-book games).
- `inBook` → no chip (unchanged).
Refactor `OffBookChip` into a small shared popover-chip so the new chip reuses the
fixed-position popover plumbing (115-195) rather than duplicating it.

### 8. Connector distinction — `src/openings/treeView.ts` + `OpeningsPage.tsx`
Connectors currently encode only width (`encounterCount`) and reserve dashing for
off-screen clamping. Add a color axis for move type so the third type reads on the
graph, not just the card:
- Extend `ConnectorStyle` with `variant: "book" | "observed" | "selected"` derived
  in `connectorStyle(node)` from the selected child (`isObserved` → observed,
  `isUserSelected` → selected, else book).
- **Recolor via `color` on the `<g>`, not `stroke` on the path.** The stroke
  (`stroke="currentColor"`, 549/588) AND the clamp tips (`fill="currentColor"`,
  562/595/600) all key off `currentColor`, so only setting `stroke` would leave the
  clamp triangles default-colored. Set the variant color as the `color` CSS
  property on the wrapping `<g>` (e.g. a class `openings-tree-connector-group--selected`
  or inline `style={{ color: var }}`); stroke + tip fills then inherit together.
  Keep `stroke="currentColor"` as-is.
- **Arrowheads need a per-variant marker.** The arrowhead is defined once in
  `<defs>` (497-506) with `fill="currentColor"`; inside a `<marker>`, `currentColor`
  resolves against the marker's own computed color (inherited from `<defs>`), NOT
  the referencing path's `<g>` color — so the group-color trick does not recolor
  it. Add a second marker `id="openings-tree-arrowhead--selected"` with the
  selected fill, and reference it via `markerEnd` (552-556, 591) when
  `variant === "selected"`. (book/observed keep the existing marker.)
- Add the CSS var + chip styles in `src/App.css` (near the existing
  `.tree-node-card__off-book` / `.openings-tree-connector` rules).

### 9. Legend — `src/components/OpeningsMetricsLegend.tsx`
The current legend explains Score/Coverage/Confidence only. Add a short
"Move types" section (or a sibling legend) describing the three connectors/chips:
Book move, Your games (observed), Selected on board. Match the colors chosen in
step 8.

### 10. SPEC.md update (required — the spec contradicts the new behavior)
Two passages describe the *old* contract and must change in the same commit:
- **`SPEC.md:2388`** — "board-drop → tree sync (accept only a navigable move in
  the rendered frontier column, else snap back)". Rewrite to: accept **any legal
  board drag**; an in-tree frontier move selects its node, any other legal move
  extends the line as a **user-selected (third type) move**; only illegal drags
  snap back. Note the ephemeral/URL-scoped lifetime and the line-scope invariant.
- **`SPEC.md:2389`** — connector style legend ("dashed = book-only (`in_book &&
  !is_observed`), solid = observed, thickness = …"). Add the third type: a
  **selected** edge variant (distinct color via the `<g>` `color` + dedicated
  arrowhead marker) and mention the move-type legend addition.

## Scope note — promotions
"Any legal move" means any legal board **drag under the existing queen-promotion
policy**: `resolveDrop` (`src/openings/treeView.ts:236`, `promotion: "q"`)
hardcodes queen, matching the board's drag default. Underpromotions are not
reachable by drag here (as today). If literal underpromotion exploration matters,
file a follow-up bead for a promotion picker; it is out of scope for g-obh5.

## Tests

### Backend (`backend/test_tree_api.py`)
- **Update** `test_tree_stale_move_truncates_to_canonical` (389): `1.e4 1...d5` no
  longer truncates — assert `canonical_line == ["e2e4", "d7d5"]`, the d5 node has
  `is_user_selected True`, `is_navigable True`, `in_book False`, `is_observed
  False`, and null metrics.
- **Update** `test_tree_stale_url_into_boundary_truncates` (468): selecting the
  boundary `b8c6` now keeps it — `canonical_line` retains `b8c6`, node is
  `is_navigable True`, `is_user_selected True`.
- **Keep passing (regression):** `test_tree_middlegame_book_child_is_terminal_boundary`
  (450) — `b8c6` as an *unselected* sibling stays `is_navigable False`,
  `terminal_reason "opening_boundary"`, `is_user_selected False`.
- **Keep passing:** `test_tree_cycle_truncates` (399) and the illegal-edge
  truncation (552) — cycle + legality guards preserved.
- **New:** a chain of two selected moves (off-tree → off-tree) stays in the line;
  a selected move that transposes back into the book re-expands book children.

### Frontend
- `treeView.test.ts`: `buildTreeView` maps `is_user_selected` → `isUserSelected`;
  root is `false`; `connectorStyle` returns the right `variant`. **Plus the
  line-scope invariant (step 4b.2):** given a response whose frontier column holds
  an `is_user_selected` node whose uci ≠ the column's `selectedUci`, that node is
  omitted from the built column (and the matching selected one is kept).
- `useOpeningsTree.test.ts` (cache-leak, step 4b.1): direct-load `a2a3,a7a6` then
  navigate back to `a2a3` — assert it does **not** reuse the deeper response via
  the no-fetch prefix path (a refetch is issued / `getOpeningTree` called for the
  exact prefix), so `a7a6` no longer renders as a child of `a2a3`.
- `OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx` (already dirty in working tree — coordinate):
  selected move renders `SelectedMoveChip`, off-book renders `OffBookChip`, book
  renders neither; compact + expanded variants.
- `OpeningsPage` drop test — **must update, not optional.**
  `src/pages/OpeningsPage.test.tsx:462` (`"syncs a navigable board drop to the tree
  and rejects off-tree drops"`) currently drops `a2a3` and asserts `rejected ===
  false`, `location()` unchanged, and `captureEventMock` not called (478-480). That
  is exactly the behavior we are reversing. Rewrite the off-tree half to: mock a
  follow-up `getOpeningTree` response for the `a2a3` position, assert `onPieceDrop`
  returns `true`, `location()` becomes `/openings?color=white&move=a2a3`, and
  `opening_explored` is captured with `to_key: "a2a3"`. Rename the test
  (e.g. "...and extends the line for legal off-tree drops"). Keep an
  **illegal**-drop assertion (e.g. `e2→e5` is illegal → `resolveDrop` returns null
  → `false`, location unchanged) so the legality guard stays covered. The navigable
  `e2→e4` half (482-506) stays as-is.

## Risk / sequencing notes
- The two updated backend tests are **deliberate behavior changes**, not
  regressions — call them out in the commit message.
- Pre-push hook builds the whole tree with `tsc -b` (stricter than `--noEmit`);
  ensure the new fields are non-optional everywhere they're constructed (root,
  synth root, mocks/fixtures in tests) or `tsc` will fail on missing props.
- Eval cache may still hit for a transposition (selected move reaching a known
  full FEN), so don't assert evals are always null in tests — only for genuinely
  novel positions.
- Order: backend (1-3) → wire type (5) → display/card/connector/legend (4,6-9) →
  tests. Single commit (code + beads ledger) per workspace rules; commit only
  after user review.
close_reason: Chessboard accepts any legal move; off-tree moves become navigable user-selected (third type) nodes. Code-review findings addressed (SPEC/api/openings comments + move-type legend). Follow-up g-42md (loading footer) also done.

title: show eval for all /openings cards
description: off book cards currently don't show an eval score. But these moves should all be in the backend analysis cache. Can we get the eval from there?
design:
# g-a0ix — Show eval for all /openings cards (incl. off-book)

## Decision (user, 2026-06-24)
Show off-book evals **identically to on-book — no "approximate" marker**. Backend-only
change; wire types, `treeView.ts`, and `OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx` are untouched.

## Root cause
Off-book cards are player game-moves analyzed in the browser. Their evals **are** in
`analysis_cache` (`source="game"`, `analysis_profile_id="browser-game-v1"`) with a real
`played_eval`/`played_eval_mate`, but `lookup_move_evals` (backend/app/tree_eval.py:76)
drops them at the **move trust gate** (`_move_trusted`, line 108 exact + line 137
normalized) because browser-game is non-authoritative. The node gets `eval_cp=None`,
`_hydrate_node` (backend/app/api/openings.py:1358, eval at :1390) sets null, the card
renders "—".

### Data grounding (production DB, read-only probe)
- analysis_cache: 20,755 rows; every row has both `played_eval` and `best_eval`.
- move-trusted: 16,181. Untrusted: 4,574 — almost all `('game','browser-game-v1',
  'resolver-complete-v1')` (4,351), plus minimal-played-eval-v1 (59) and bare game (164).
- A *trusted* position-grain fallback (`resolve_trusted_positions` on each node's child
  FEN) would recover only **27 / 4,574 (0.6%)** — confirmed by pushing each untrusted
  move and resolving the resulting normalized FEN. So trusted-only fallback is a
  non-solution; we must surface the untrusted browser `played_eval` directly.
- Browser evals are real Stockfish evals (different engine/depth than canonical
  `canonical-sf18-depth24-linux-v1`), legitimate for display.

## Data flow (unchanged except step 2)
analysis_cache → `lookup_move_evals(db, [(parent_full_fen, uci)])` → `MoveEval{cp,mate}`
→ `_hydrate_node` → `TreeNode.eval_cp/eval_mate` → wire → `nodeToView` → card
`formatWhiteEval`. Evals are white-relative throughout; browser `played_eval` is stored
white-relative too, so the convention is preserved with no sign work.

## Implementation — backend/app/tree_eval.py ONLY

Add an **untrusted played-eval fallback tier**, strictly below the trusted tiers, in
`lookup_move_evals`. Trusted authoritative evals are still preferred whenever present
(on-book cards keep their depth-24 numbers); untrusted browser evals fill the gaps.

Tier precedence per request (first hit wins):
1. exact `(fen_before, uci)`, move-trusted  (current)
2. normalized `(normalized_fen_before, uci)`, move-trusted  (current)
3. **NEW** exact `(fen_before, uci)`, untrusted (any non-None played_eval)
4. **NEW** normalized `(normalized_fen_before, uci)`, untrusted, ranked by
   `_move_sort_key` (mate first, source_rank, lowest id)

No new DB round-trips: both the exact query (line 97) and the normalized `fallback_rows`
query (line 125) already return untrusted rows — we currently `continue`-discard them at
line 137. Retain them into a separate `untrusted_by_norm` map instead, and keep the
exact untrusted row reachable via the existing `exact_map`.

Code shape:
- In the per-request exact loop (line 106): when the exact row is untrusted or yields no
  usable eval, still record `(fen,uci)` for normalized lookup as today (the untrusted
  exact row stays in `exact_map` for tier 3).
- In the `fallback_rows` loop (line 135): split survivors with a usable `_played_eval`
  into `trusted_by_norm` (current behavior) and `untrusted_by_norm` (new) instead of
  dropping untrusted.
- In the resolution loop (line 143): trusted normalized (tier 2) → else exact untrusted
  via `exact_map.get((fen,uci))` (tier 3) → else `untrusted_by_norm` min by
  `_move_sort_key` (tier 4).

`_move_sort_key` already orders precomputed>game>other; it's reused unchanged for the
untrusted survivors. **Update its docstring** (tree_eval.py:67) — it currently says
"Ranks an already move-trusted candidate list (trust filtering precedes this)", which is
no longer true: it now also ranks untrusted fallback survivors. `MoveEval` is unchanged
(no `approximate` field, per decision).

### Scope of "untrusted" (REVIEW FINDING — broader than browser)
The move trust gate excludes more than browser-game rows, so tiers 3-4 surface **ANY
untrusted row carrying a usable `played_eval`**, not just `browser-game-v1`. In current
prod data the untrusted set is `('game','browser-game-v1','resolver-complete-v1')` 4351,
`('game', None, None)` 164, and `('game','browser-game-v1','minimal-played-eval-v1')` 59
— but the logic is source-agnostic: a `minimal-played-eval-v1`, a bare `source=None`
game row, or any other/unknown source also qualifies. Ranking across untrusted survivors
uses `_move_sort_key` → `source_rank` (analysis_trust.py:38: `precomputed:0, game:1,
other:2`), so a precomputed-but-untrusted row would outrank a game row, etc. This is
**intended** ("any cached eval we have, best-source first"); it must be stated in the
docstring and pinned by a test that seeds a non-browser untrusted source.

## Sort-order behavior (REVIEW FINDING — accepted, must test)
`eval_cp`/`eval_mate` are not display-only: `_eval_favorability` (openings.py:1416) feeds
`_sort_key`'s secondary `eval_key` (openings.py:1445), which breaks **play-frequency
ties** so the column's engine-best move floats up. Off-book siblings usually tie on the
primary key (`encounter_count`/`user_choice_count` = 0), so once untrusted browser evals
hydrate, off-book cards **will reorder by eval**.

Decision: **accept this** — it is the natural extension of "treat off-book evals
identically to on-book". Off-book columns now order by engine eval just like on-book
columns (best reply floats up), and card order stays consistent with the displayed
number. We deliberately do NOT split a separate "trusted-only sort eval" vs "display
eval" (that would show a number inconsistent with the card's position and add a parallel

title: what-if colors should only be the board not the arrows
description: What-if (variation) mode applies a CSS filter to the whole board frame, so the desaturation/contrast reduction leaks onto the move arrows and eval-icon badge — not just the squares. Fix: scope the wash-out filter to the square layer only so arrows/badges keep full saturation. See design field for the full plan.
design:
# g-vf6b — What-if wash-out should desaturate only the board, not the arrows/badges

## Problem (root cause)

What-if (variation) mode applies a single CSS `filter` to the whole board
container, so the desaturation/contrast reduction leaks onto the move arrows and
the eval-icon badge, not just the squares.

Current CSS (`src/App.css:4342`):

```css
.analysis-board__board-frame--variation {
    filter: saturate(0.55) brightness(1.06) contrast(0.95);
    transition: filter 0.2s ease;
}
```

The class lives on the frame `<div>` in `AnalysisBoard.tsx:1361` (added when
`isInVariation`, i.e. `selectedVarNodeId != null`, see `AnalysisBoard.tsx:306`).
A CSS `filter` on a parent applies to its entire rendered subtree.

## DOM structure (verified against react-chessboard 5.8.6 dist)

```
.analysis-board__board-frame(--variation)        <- filter currently here
└─ <Chessboard> (renders a Fragment, no own wrapper div)
   ├─ <div id="{chessboardId}-main-board">        <- "the board" container
   │   ├─ <div id="…-square-a8" data-square="a8" data-column="a" data-row="8">   ┐ 64 square
   │   │    └─ <div style={squareStyles[sq]}>      <- highlight tint + piece     │ divs, each
   │   │         └─ <div data-piece> <svg piece/>                                │ with
   │   ├─ … (63 more square divs) …                                             ┘ data-square
   │   └─ <svg style="position:absolute;z-index:20;pointer-events:none">  <- ARROWS (direct
   │                                                  child of board div, NO class/id)
   └─ <DragOverlay> … </DragOverlay>               <- active-drag clone, sibling of board div
└─ {boardEvalIcon && <div class="board-eval-icons">…}   <- eval badge, sibling of board div
```

Key facts that drive the fix:
- The arrows `<svg>` (react-chessboard `Arrows`, dist line ~4417) is rendered
  **inside** the board div, as a sibling of the square divs. It has **no
  className/id** — the only stable hooks are "direct `<svg>` child of the
  `…-board` div" or its inline `z-index:20`.
- Every square is a `<div>` carrying `data-square` / `data-column` / `data-row`
  (Square component, dist line ~4573/4580). `data-square` is a documented
  react-chessboard data attribute used for drag/drop targeting → the most stable
  hook we have.
- Pieces and per-square highlight tints (`squareStyles`) are **descendants** of
  the square div → they wash out together with the board (correct: they are
  "the board").
- The eval-icon badge (`.board-eval-icons`, `AnalysisBoard.tsx:1388`) is a
  sibling of the board div, not a descendant of any square.

## Chosen approach: scope the filter to the square layer

Move the wash-out from the frame onto the square elements only. Because
`saturate`/`brightness`/`contrast` are **per-pixel point operations** (unlike
spatial filters such as `blur`/`drop-shadow`), applying them to each of the 64
squares independently is visually identical to filtering the board as one group
— no seams, no boundary artifacts, no double-application. The arrows `<svg>`
(sibling of the squares) and the eval badge (sibling of the board div) are left
untouched at full saturation/contrast, sitting visually on top (arrows are
`z-index:20`).

### Edit — `src/App.css` (replace the block at 4340–4345)

```css
/* What-if (variation) mode: wash out only the board squares (and the pieces +
   highlight tints nested inside them) so the position reads as a hypothetical,
   while move arrows and the eval-icon badge keep full saturation/contrast for
   legibility. saturate/brightness/contrast are per-pixel point filters, so
   filtering each square independently is identical to filtering the whole board
   — no seams. Depends on react-chessboard tagging every square with
   data-square; if a future upgrade drops it the wash simply stops (squares show
   full color) rather than breaking layout. */
.analysis-board__board-frame--variation [data-square] {
    filter: saturate(0.55) brightness(1.06) contrast(0.95);
    transition: filter 0.2s ease;
}
```

Net diff: change the selector from `.analysis-board__board-frame--variation` to
`.analysis-board__board-frame--variation [data-square]`; keep the same filter
values and transition; update the comment. No TSX change required — the
`--variation` class stays on the frame as the scoping ancestor.

### What changes visually
- Squares + pieces + last-move/best-move highlight tints: washed (unchanged from
  today — still reads as hypothetical).
- Move arrows: now full saturation/contrast (the reported regression — fixed).
- Eval-icon badge: now full saturation/contrast (consistent with arrows; it is
  an informational overlay, same class as arrows conceptually). Acceptable / a
  legibility win. Noted as an intentional side effect, not scope creep.
- Active-drag piece clone (DragOverlay): already outside the squares, so it
  shows full color mid-drag — a pre-existing, inconsequential detail; unchanged.

## Alternatives considered (rejected)

- **Counter-filter the overlays** — keep the filter on the frame, then neutralize
  it on the arrows (`…-board > svg`) and `.board-eval-icons`. Rejected: inverse
  `saturate/brightness/contrast` math is imprecise (clamping is not invertible),
  and it still depends on the same library-internal structure while being
  strictly more complex.
- **Recolor squares via `lightSquareStyle`/`darkSquareStyle` props instead of a
  filter** — would not wash the piece SVGs (fixed-color), so it can't reproduce
  the current washed look without a piece filter anyway; more code, more
  invasive. Rejected.
- **Fork react-chessboard to lift arrows out of the board div** — heavy, owns an
  upgrade burden. Rejected. The library nests arrows inside the board, so *any*
  fix must reach into that structure; `[data-square]` is the least-bad,
  gracefully-degrading hook.
- **Selector `…-board > div` instead of `[data-square]`** — also works (squares
  are the only div children; arrows is the svg child) and avoids the data
  attribute, but is a less semantic, equally library-internal assumption. Keep
  `[data-square]` as primary; this is the fallback if the attribute is ever
  dropped.

## Test coverage

react-chessboard is **mocked** in `AnalysisBoard.test.tsx:111` (the mock only
captures `options`; it renders no real squares), and jsdom does not apply
external-stylesheet `filter` values — so the per-square desaturation itself
cannot be asserted in a unit test. Plan:

1. **Unit (React contract the CSS hangs off of):** add a test in
   `AnalysisBoard.test.tsx` asserting the frame div carries
   `analysis-board__board-frame--variation` when in a variation
   (`mockSelectedVarNodeId` set) and **omits** it on the main line
   (`mockSelectedVarNodeId = null`). The frame div is our own element (not the
   mocked Chessboard), so it is queryable. This guards the scoping ancestor that
   the CSS selector depends on. No existing test covers this.
2. **Manual / visual verification (the actual fix):** open Analysis → enter
   what-if by dragging a piece → confirm the squares/pieces wash out while the
   engine/best-move arrows and the eval badge stay vivid and high-contrast; exit
   what-if and confirm everything returns to full color with the 0.2s fade.
   Screenshot before/after for the bead.

## Files touched
- `src/App.css` — 1 selector + comment (block at 4340–4345).
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx` — +1 test for the `--variation` class
  toggle (optional but recommended).
- No change to `AnalysisBoard.tsx`.

## Risks
- **Library-internal selector** (`[data-square]`): a react-chessboard major
  upgrade could rename/drop it. Failure mode is graceful (no wash, full color) —
  not a layout break. Mitigated by the inline CSS comment documenting the
  dependency.
- **Per-element transition** on 64 squares vs 1 frame: negligible — point
  filters are GPU-composited; 64 simultaneous filter transitions are cheap.
close_reason: Scoped the what-if wash-out filter to the square layer ([data-square]) so move arrows and the eval-icon badge keep full saturation/contrast; squares/pieces still wash out.

title: debug logs dont have network
description: The in-app debug overlay (g-0oow: debugLog.ts + DebugOverlay.tsx) captures console.* and uncaught errors but NOT network traffic. Network telemetry goes only to PostHog (reportApiRequest), so on-device debugging has meant hand-exporting .har files. Add network requests to the debug log via a window.fetch monkeypatch (mirrors the existing console-patch pattern; covers api.ts + AuthContext + openingBook). Metadata-only MVP (method/URL/status/duration/request-id); body capture is split to g-bsg9 behind redaction. Full plan in design.
design:
# Debug overlay: capture network (metadata-only MVP)

## Problem
The in-app debug overlay (g-0oow: `src/utils/debugLog.ts` + `src/components/DebugOverlay.tsx`)
captures `console.*` and uncaught errors into a localStorage-backed ring buffer, viewable
on-device via the overlay (mobile/devtools-closed). It does NOT capture HTTP traffic.
Network telemetry exists but goes only to PostHog (`reportApiRequest`, `src/utils/api.ts:151`),
not the on-device overlay — which is why debugging has required hand-exporting `.har` files
(see `tmp/*.har`). This bead adds network requests to the debug log.

Scope of THIS bead: **metadata-only** (method, URL, status, duration, request-id). Capturing
request/response bodies is the follow-up **g-bsg9** (blocked on the redaction work flagged in
the `debugLog.ts` RELEASE BLOCKER header) — bodies + `Authorization` headers must NOT be
persisted to localStorage without redaction.

## Capture point: monkeypatch `window.fetch` (NOT the api.ts client)
The app issues fetches from three places, only one of which is the central client:
- `src/utils/api.ts` (`requestJson`, fetch at `:321`) — the bulk of API calls
- `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:129` — direct `fetch`
- `src/openings/openingBook.ts:115` — direct `fetch`
Plus PostHog's own egress (also via `fetch`).

Hooking `reportApiRequest` (Option B) would be ~5 lines and reuse already-computed timing, but
would miss auth + opening-book traffic. So patch global `fetch` instead — this mirrors the
existing console-patch pattern exactly and gives full coverage. `debugLog.ts` is a standalone
no-React module (so it can install before app mount), which is the right home for the patch.

## Data model (`src/utils/debugLog.ts`)
Extend the existing single entry type (minimal churn — the overlay already renders by `level`
and filters/copies off `args`):

```ts
export type LogLevel = 'log' | 'warn' | 'error' | 'info' | 'debug' | 'net'

// Console interception must stay typed to ONLY the console methods. Adding 'net'
// to LogLevel otherwise breaks `console[level]` (`debugLog.ts:215`) and the
// `originalConsole: Partial<Record<LogLevel, …>>` map (`:190`) — TS can no longer
// prove `level` is a real console key. Split it out and retype both:
export type ConsoleLogLevel = Exclude<LogLevel, 'net'>   // 'log'|'warn'|'error'|'info'|'debug'

export type NetErrorKind = 'http' | 'network' | 'timeout' | 'abort'

export interface NetMeta {
  method: string            // upper-cased
  url: string               // path+search, origin stripped for readability
  status: number            // 0 when the request never got a response
  ok: boolean
  durationMs: number
  errorKind?: NetErrorKind  // present only on failures
  requestId?: string | null // X-Request-ID echo, correlates with server logs
}

export interface LogEntry {
  id: number
  ts: number
  level: LogLevel
  args: string              // human one-liner; keeps text-filter + Copy working unchanged
  net?: NetMeta             // present only when level === 'net'
}
```

`args` for a net entry is a readable summary so the existing text filter (`DebugOverlay.tsx:43`)
and Copy-all (`:58`) keep working with zero changes:
- success: `GET /api/openings/tree?player_color=white 200 (143ms) #a1b2c3`
- failure: `POST /api/game/end 500 (812ms) [http] #d4e5f6`
- never-answered: `GET /api/history 0 (30002ms) [timeout]`

`hydrate()` (`:168`) already filters entries on `typeof e.args === 'string'` — `net` rides
along in the JSON and is forward/backward compatible (older persisted blobs simply lack it;
the overlay guards `e.net?`).

**Console-typing fix (required by the `'net'` addition).** Introduce
`ConsoleLogLevel = Exclude<LogLevel, 'net'>` and retype `CONSOLE_METHODS: ConsoleLogLevel[]`
(`:28`) and `originalConsole: Partial<Record<ConsoleLogLevel, …>>` (`:190`). The
`CONSOLE_METHODS` loop body (`:215`) then keeps proving `console[level]` / `originalConsole[level]`
are valid keys. `push()` and `isImmediateLevel()` still take the wider `LogLevel` (net entries flow
through `push`/`pushNet`), so only the console-iteration types narrow.

## Fetch patch semantics (fold into existing install/uninstall)
Add `installFetchCapture()`/`uninstallFetchCapture()` invoked from inside the existing
`installConsoleCapture()` / `uninstallConsoleCapture()` (`:208` / `:233`), guarded by the SAME
`__grPatched` flag so double-install wraps once and the test teardown
(`src/test/setup.ts` afterEach → `uninstallConsoleCapture`) restores `window.fetch` too.
No change needed at the `main.tsx:13` call site.

```ts
let originalFetch: typeof fetch | null = null

function installFetchCapture(): void {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined' || typeof window.fetch !== 'function') return
  originalFetch = window.fetch          // store the RAW, UNBOUND ref (NOT .bind()) so
                                        // uninstall can restore the EXACT original identity
  // Assigning to window.fetch gives the arrow the `typeof fetch` contextual type, so
  // `input: RequestInfo | URL` and `init?: RequestInit` come for free — no annotations/casts.
  window.fetch = async (input, init) => {
    const method = (
      init?.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')
    ).toUpperCase()
    const rawUrl =
      typeof input === 'string' ? input
      : input instanceof URL ? input.href
      : input.url
    const start = performance.now()      // monotonic for duration
    try {
      // .call(window) because we stored the raw unbound fn; bare invocation would
      // throw "Illegal invocation" (fetch requires `this === window`). NO `input as
      // RequestInfo` cast: the wrapper's `typeof fetch` contextual type keeps `input`
      // as `RequestInfo | URL`, and `.call` preserves it via `Parameters<typeof fetch>`
      // (casting would narrow URL inputs away).
      const res = await originalFetch!.call(window, input, init)
      pushNet({
        method,
        url: displayUrl(rawUrl),
        status: res.status,
        ok: res.ok,
        durationMs: performance.now() - start,
        errorKind: res.ok ? undefined : 'http',
        requestId: readRequestIdHeader(res),
      })
      return res                         // pass-through UNTOUCHED — body never read
    } catch (err) {
      pushNet({
        method,
        url: displayUrl(rawUrl),
        status: 0,
        ok: false,
        durationMs: performance.now() - start,
        errorKind: classifyFetchError(err),  // 'timeout' | 'abort' | 'network'
      })
      throw err
    }
  }
}
```

`uninstallFetchCapture()`: if `originalFetch`, set `window.fetch = originalFetch; originalFetch = null`.
This restores the exact pre-install function identity — the reason we store the raw unbound ref
rather than a `.bind()` copy (a bound copy would fail an identity assertion in the restore test).

### Critical correctness points (traced)
1. **Body is never consumed.** Metadata-only ⇒ we never touch `res.body`/`res.json()`/`res.text()`,
   so NO `clone()` is required and the app's stream is intact. (Body capture in g-bsg9 MUST clone
   first — that is the whole reason it's a separate, gated bead.)
2. **No recursion.** The wrapper calls only `originalFetch`; `pushNet` touches in-memory buffer +
   localStorage only (no fetch). PostHog egress is captured (it's just more `fetch`) but cannot loop.
   Optional denylist: skip URLs whose host matches the PostHog host to cut noise — left OUT of the
   MVP to keep it simple; note as a tuning follow-up if the overlay gets noisy.
3. **Immediate vs debounced persist.** `pushNet` sets
   `immediate = !ok && errorKind !== 'abort'` so genuine failures / never-answered requests survive a
   reload (same rationale as `isImmediateLevel` for error/warn at `:192`), while successes AND aborts
   take the debounced path (`schedulePersist`, `:156`). Aborts are deliberately EXCLUDED from
   immediate flush even though they carry `ok:false`: superseded openings/session fetches are routine
   UI churn, not real failures, so flushing each to localStorage would be wasteful. (This resolves
   the earlier contradiction between "immediate = !ok" and "aborts are non-immediate".)
4. **Abort handling — judgment call.** `api.ts` deliberately SKIPS reporting aborts to PostHog
   (`isAbortError`, `:142`) because a superseded fetch isn't a round-trip outcome. For the *debug*
   overlay an aborted request IS useful to see (e.g. a cancelled tree/openings fetch), so we DO
   record it — as `status:0, errorKind:'abort'`, non-immediate persist, visually de-emphasized.
   `classifyFetchError`: `name === 'TimeoutError'` → `'timeout'`; `name === 'AbortError'` →
   `'abort'`; else `'network'` (reuse the logic shape from `classifyNetworkError`/`isAbortError`).
5. **`displayUrl(raw)`** — strip noise for OUR origins but PRESERVE the host for third-party egress,
   so PostHog/external calls stay distinguishable from same-origin paths (we intentionally capture
   them). Resolve `const u = new URL(raw, window.location.origin)` (catch → return `raw`); if
   `u.origin` is in the strippable set, return `u.pathname + u.search`, else return
   `u.host + u.pathname + u.search`. **Strippable set** = `window.location.origin` (covers prod,
   where the API base is same-origin `/api`) ∪ the dev API-base origin. The dev origin is derived
   inline — NOT by importing `api.ts` (debugLog must stay standalone and install before analytics,

6. **`readRequestIdHeader(res)`**: guard `typeof res.headers?.get === 'function'` then

7. **SSR / test guard.** `typeof window !== 'undefined' && typeof window.fetch === 'function'`.

## Overlay changes (`src/components/DebugOverlay.tsx`)
- Add `'net'` to `LEVELS` (`:11`) → a NET filter chip appears; toggling/filtering work via the
  existing `levelFilter`/`toggleLevel` machinery with no other logic change.

- No change to `copyAll`/text-filter (they read `e.args`, which we populate).

```css
.debug-entry--net          { color: #4fd0e0; }      /* teal — distinct from log/warn/error */
.debug-entry--net-fail     { color: #ef6b6b; }      /* reuse error red for failed requests */
```

## Capture granularity: physical attempts vs logical request (resolves open question)
The fetch wrapper logs every PHYSICAL fetch attempt; `api.ts`'s `reportApiRequest`
(`src/utils/api.ts:151`, called once after the retry loop, `:312`+) logs one FINAL LOGICAL request.
This divergence is intentional and complementary, and the overlay's wire-level view is the right
behavior for network debugging:
- **Retries** — `requestJson` retries (e.g. `getNextOpponentMove` `retries:2`, `api.ts:1211`) issue
  N physical fetches, so the overlay shows N net rows (e.g. `500`, `500`, `200`). PostHog still
  records the single logical outcome; the overlay deliberately shows each attempt on the wire.
- **Parse failures** — a `200` with invalid JSON logs as a net SUCCESS (`status:200, ok:true`): the
  wrapper never reads the body, so it cannot know the JSON parse failed. This differs from analytics'
  `error_kind:'parse'` path (`api.ts:344`), and is correct for a *network* overlay — the HTTP
  response WAS 200; the parse error surfaces separately via the console-capture path as a thrown
  error. Body-aware classification is out of scope (it needs body reads → g-bsg9).

## Test coverage
### `src/utils/debugLog.test.ts` — new `describe('fetch capture')`
- Pushes a net entry on success: stub `window.fetch` to resolve a `Response`/double with
  `status:200, ok:true, headers.get('x-request-id')`; assert one entry `level:'net'`,

- **Body not consumed**: stub returns a real `new Response('{"a":1}')`; after the wrapped call,

- Failure `status >= 400`: `ok:false`, `errorKind:'http'`, and entry persisted IMMEDIATELY
  (assert `localStorage` written without advancing the debounce timer — pattern already used in
  this file with `vi.useFakeTimers`).
- Rejected fetch (network error) → `status:0, errorKind:'network'`, entry pushed, error re-thrown.
- Abort (`AbortError`) → `status:0, errorKind:'abort'`, non-immediate; re-thrown.
- Timeout (`name:'TimeoutError'`) → `errorKind:'timeout'`.
- Idempotent: double `installConsoleCapture()` wraps `window.fetch` once (one entry per call).
- `uninstallConsoleCapture()` restores `window.fetch` to the EXACT original reference: capture the
  ref BEFORE install, assert `window.fetch === ref` after uninstall (passes only because we store the
  raw unbound fn, not a `.bind()` copy).
- **Retry visibility (physical attempts)**: stub `window.fetch` to return `500, 500, 200` and call
  `getNextOpponentMove` (`retries:2`); assert THREE net rows (`500/500/200`) — proves each physical
  attempt logs while PostHog records one logical request. (Use 500, which is retryable per
  `ApiError`'s default.)
  **TIMER NOTE**: this file's `beforeEach` calls `vi.useFakeTimers()`, but `requestJson`'s retry path
  sleeps via `setTimeout` (`delay()`, `api.ts:261`, called at `:327`/`:377` — 200ms then 400ms).
  Under fake timers the awaited promise HANGS unless the timers are driven. For this one test either
  (a) `vi.useRealTimers()` at the top — total wait ~600ms, and afterEach already restores real timers
  so nothing leaks — or (b) keep fake timers and interleave `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(200)`

- **Parse-failure stays a 200**: stub `window.fetch` → `200` with body `'not json'`; assert the net

- **Cross-origin host preserved**: a fetch to `https://us.i.posthog.com/e` logs `args` containing
  the host (`us.i.posthog.com/e`); a same-origin `/api/...` and the dev API base
  (`VITE_API_URL` / `localhost:8000`) log path-only (`/api/...`).
- **Console typing guard**: `tsc -b` must stay green (the pre-push gate builds the whole tree) —
  `CONSOLE_METHODS`/`originalConsole` use `ConsoleLogLevel`, so adding `'net'` to `LogLevel` does not

Note `src/test/setup.ts` afterEach already calls `uninstallConsoleCapture()` + clears storage,

title: Drill bug: Not best move shown as best.
description:
The captured network logs in tmp/6.22.17-51.cleaned.har show a Horwitz Defense drill that ended after moves 1.d4 e6 2.Nf3 d5.
The move 2..d5 was shown as Best in MoveList even though /api/analysis/lookup said Nf6 was the best move.
design:
# g-jfdj — Drill bug: non-best move shown as Best

## Root cause
Repro: Horwitz Defense drill `1.d4 e6 2.Nf3 d5`. For the position after `1.d4 e6 2.Nf3`,
`/api/analysis/lookup` for move `d7d5` returned:
- `position_trusted=true`, trusted `best_move_uci=g8f6` / `best_move_san=Nf6`
- the exact move row `move_trusted=false`, `classification=best` (from browser-game-v1 evidence)

The frontend published-cache gate correctly releases this mixed/untrusted hit to the worker.
A worker/cache fallback then publishes `d7d5` classified `best`. The terminal-resolve
reconciliation helper `promoteToTrustedBest` (src/workers/analysisUtils.ts:424) is the only
place that consults trusted-position truth, and it ONLY promotes (played == trustedBest →
'best'). It **no-ops when `classification === 'best'`** — so a fallback that wrongly calls a
NON-trusted-best move 'best' is published and uploaded unchanged. Result: MoveList shows the
best-move star on `d5` and the session upload writes `classification=best` / `best_move_uci=d7d5`,
even though trusted position truth says `Nf6` is best.

Both render and upload read straight from the published `AnalysisResult`
(MoveRow.tsx keys the star on `classification === 'best'`; sessionUpload.ts:52-60 pulls
`bestMove`/`bestEval`/`delta`/`classification` directly). So a single fix in the shared
reconcile helper fixes BOTH paths.

## Decision (confirmed with user)
When trusted position says played ≠ best but the fallback graded it `best`, demote to the
**'excellent' floor** — non-best, no fabricated eval loss, no false blunder.

## Fix: make the helper reconcile bestness BOTH ways
File: `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts` — replace the body of the helper (currently
`promoteToTrustedBest`). Rename to `reconcileTrustedBest` since it is no longer promotion-only
(update its export, both imports/call sites, and test `describe`).

```ts
export const reconcileTrustedBest = (
  result: AnalysisResult,
  trustedBestUci: string,
): AnalysisResult => {
  // Direction 1 — PROMOTION: played IS the trusted best → it is best (loss 0).
  if (result.move === trustedBestUci) {
    if (result.classification === 'best') return result
    return {
      ...result,
      classification: 'best',
      bestMove: trustedBestUci,
      bestLine: [trustedBestUci],
      bestEval: result.playedEval, // loss 0 by definition; eval magnitude preserved
      delta: 0,
      blunder: false,
      recordable: false,
    }
  }
  // played is NOT the trusted best.
  // Direction 2 — already non-best: nothing the position grain can correct without
  // inventing an eval loss; leave the move/worker grain untouched (the Bf4 case).
  if (result.classification !== 'best') return result
  // Direction 3 — DEMOTION: a fallback wrongly called a non-best move 'best'. The
  // trusted position grain says the best move is elsewhere. Demote to the 'excellent'
  // floor and point bestMove/bestLine at the trusted best. No trusted eval loss exists
  // (move grain is untrusted, mixing it with the position eval would be invented), so
  // delta and bestEval are nulled rather than fabricated. playedEval magnitude is kept.
  return {
    ...result,
    classification: 'excellent',
    bestMove: trustedBestUci,
    bestLine: [trustedBestUci],
    bestEval: null,
    delta: null,
    blunder: false,
    recordable: false,
  }
}
```

Key property: the change is **purely additive** to the existing two no-op cases —
- already-best + played==trusted → still returns input (Direction 1 early return)
- non-best + played!=trusted → still no-op (Direction 2, the existing "Bf4 case")
Only the new third case (played!=trusted AND classification=='best') changes behavior.

## Call sites (rename only; logic already correct)
- `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:21` import, `:1352` call inside
  `resolveAnalysisResult` — truth read from `this.drillTruth`, guarded by
  `truth.requestId === result.id`. No logic change; `published` now also gets demoted.
- `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts:6` import, `:196` call inside `resolveAnalysis` — truth
  from `exactBestTruth`, same requestId guard. Update the stale comment at :185-192
  (it claims the helper "is a no-op unless the played move equals the trusted best").

## Downstream (no code change — verified)
- `MoveRow.tsx`: star/celebrate keyed on `classification === 'best'` → 'excellent' shows
  the excellent icon, no star. ✓
- `sessionUpload.ts:52-60,145-155`: `classification` ← 'excellent', `eval_delta` ← null,
  `best_move_eval_cp` ← null, `best_move_uci/san` ← g8f6/Nf6 (san re-derived via
  `parseUciToSan` from the corrected `bestMove`). Upload schema already accepts null
  classification/delta (`?? null`). ✓
- Backend lookup correctly separates position vs move grain; no backend change.

## Tests
1. `src/workers/analysisUtils.test.ts` (`reconcileTrustedBest` pure helper, ~line 1092):
   - keep the two existing no-op tests (rename describe).
   - ADD: "demotes a wrongly-'best' fallback when played is not the trusted best (d5 vs Nf6)" —
     input `{ ...base, move: 'd7d5', classification: 'best' }`, call with `'g8f6'`; expect
     `classification: 'excellent'`, `bestMove: 'g8f6'`, `bestLine: ['g8f6']`, `delta: null`,
     `bestEval: null`, `blunder: false`, `playedEval` preserved.
2. `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts` (the trusted-best describe, ~line 668):
   mirror the existing "Bf4 case" but with a fallback that classifies the move `best`.
   NOTE: the local `sendWorker` helper (line 621) DEFAULTS `classification: 'excellent'`
   and `bestLine: ['g1f3','d7d5']`, so the override MUST include `classification: 'best'`
   or the demotion branch is never exercised. Set `bestLine: ['d7d5']` too so the test
   proves it is replaced with `['g8f6']`:
   lookup row `move d7d5`, `best_move_uci='g8f6'`, `position_trusted=true`,
   `move_trusted=false`;
   `sendWorker(requestId, { move:'d7d5', bestMove:'d7d5', bestLine:['d7d5'], classification:'best', delta:0 })`.
   Assert `analysisMap.get(idx)` has `classification==='excellent'`, `bestMove==='g8f6'`,
   `bestLine` deep-equals `['g8f6']`, not `d7d5`/`best`.
3. `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.test.ts` (g-49e2 describe, ~line 1445): mirror the c4/Bf4
   cases for the demotion path — exactBestTruth bestUci `g8f6`, resolved result move `d7d5`
   classified `best`; assert the store receives `classification:'excellent'`, `bestMove:'g8f6'`.

## Out of scope
- Correcting `bestMove` for already-non-best results whose worker `bestMove` disagrees with
  trusted (Direction 2 no-op): doing so would require nulling an existing coherent
  delta/bestEval pair — a separate concern, not this bug.
- Backend session-upload writer: lookup grain handling is already correct; the guarded
  writer should not replace canonical evidence. No change here.

## Explicit assumptions (kept by design)
- `bestLine: [trustedBestUci]` is a best-move HINT, not a complete trusted PV. Backend
  trusted-position contracts reject one-move PVs, but session uploads store it as
  untrusted metadata, so a one-element line is acceptable here.
- `delta: null` means SRS / `recordable` grading is unavailable for the demoted result —
  intended, and consistent with the "do not fabricate eval loss" decision.

## Verification (non-watch; repo uses a solution tsconfig with project references)
- `npm run test:run -- src/workers/analysisUtils.test.ts src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.test.ts`
  (`test:run` = `vitest run`; plain `npm run test` is watch mode. Rerun any failure in
  isolation — pre-push vitest suite is flaky under parallel load).
- `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) or `npx tsc -b` for the rename — NOT
  `tsc --noEmit`, which ignores the project references.
notes: Investigation 2026-06-23: tmp/6.22.17-51.cleaned.har shows /api/analysis/lookup for the position after 1.d4 e6 2.Nf3 with move d7d5 returned position_trusted=true and trusted position best_move_uci=g8f6 / best_move_san=Nf6, while the exact move row was move_trusted=false and classification=best from browser-game-v1 evidence. The frontend published cache gate correctly releases this mixed/untrusted hit to the worker. The likely bug is in the trusted-position side channel handling: GameAnalysisCoordinator.resolveAnalysisResult and useMoveAnalysis.resolveAnalysis only call promoteToTrustedBest. That helper promotes played==trustedBest to best, but no-ops for played!=trustedBest and also no-ops when the fallback result is already classified best. Therefore a worker/browser fallback that says d7d5 is best is published and uploaded unchanged, causing MoveList/session upload to show d5 as best even though trusted position truth says Nf6. Fix direction: extend/replace the helper so trusted position truth reconciles bestness both ways: preserve promotion when played==trustedBest, but when played!=trustedBest prevent a published classification of best and set bestMove/bestLine to the trusted best without inventing a trusted eval loss. Add regression coverage in GameAnalysisCoordinator.test and useMoveAnalysis.test for non-best fallback classified best (d7d5 vs g8f6). Backend lookup appears to be separating position and move grains correctly; session upload may insert the wrong browser-game-v1 row only where no stronger cache key exists, but the guarded writer should not replace canonical evidence.
close_reason: Rewrote promoteToTrustedBest as reconcileTrustedBest: demotes wrongly-'best' non-best fallbacks to excellent with trusted bestMove/bestLine; added regression tests in all 3 suites

description:

title: Part B: rewrite _compute_blunder_opportunity_events as forward BFS
description:
Part B of epic g-zuym (see g-zuym for the full master plan). This is the real fix.

Replace the O(blunders × depth) reverse-per-blunder loop in _compute_blunder_opportunity_events (session.py:391) with a single forward BFS.

Equivalence: a session position S makes blunder position B opportunity_only iff S is an opponent-color ancestor of B within 8 reverse plies. Reversing the arrow: B reachable from S by <=8 forward move-edges AND S opponent-color AND S != B.
- opp_source = session positions whose active_color == opponent_color.
- Forward BFS from opp_source following Move.from_position_id -> Move.to_position_id, up to 8 plies (to_position_id WHERE from_position_id IN frontier — uses PK leading column, already indexed; 8 queries total regardless of blunder count). Collect forward_reachable.
- For each user blunder (single load, pure set membership, NO DB query in loop): reached = blunder.position_id in session_position_ids; opportunity_only = blunder.position_id in forward_reachable; opportunity = reached or opportunity_only.
- Existing delete-stale + _upsert_opportunity_event + occurred_at + commit tail unchanged.

Implementation notes:
- Extend session-position query (session.py:419) to also select Position.active_color.
- Add helper _forward_reachable_position_ids(db, *, user_id, start_ids, radius_ply) mirroring BFS shape of _reverse_ancestor_position_ids but forward and seeded from a set.
- EXPLICIT USER SCOPING: moves has no user_id; positions do (models.py:62). Each BFS level must constrain reached to_position_ids to this user — join/filter Position.user_id == user_id on frontier expansion to prevent cross-user graph leakage by construction.
- _reverse_ancestor_position_ids becomes unused; remove it (grep confirms only caller is _compute_blunder_opportunity_events).
- Both upload paths (sqlite session.py:646, pg session.py:697) call the same function, both benefit.
close_reason: Rewrote _compute_blunder_opportunity_events as single forward BFS; retained user-scoped reverse helper for offline recompute script + added smoke/equivalence/cross-user tests
