title: openings tree: eval as secondary column sort by side-to-move favorability
description: In /openings, column cards sort primarily by play frequency (observed/user_choice_count on user turns, encounter_count on opponent turns). Add engine eval as the secondary sort key, breaking play-frequency ties by favorability to the COLUMN'S SIDE TO MOVE: a White-to-move column ranks the highest white-relative eval first; a Black-to-move column ranks the lowest (most-negative) eval first — i.e. the best move FOR THAT COLUMN floats up, independent of the repertoire color. Mate dominates cp; nodes with no eval (incl. a white-relative mate-0, which carries no recoverable winner) sort last. opening_score stays as a tertiary tiebreak. Implemented in _OpeningTreeBuilder._sort_key/_eval_favorability (backend/app/api/openings.py), keyed to active_color(column_fen) (passed in as side_to_move) rather than self.player_color. Frontend renders backend node order and white-relative evals unchanged.
design:
# g-qb4s — secondary eval sort by the column's side to move

## Contract (redirected)

Per-column secondary sort key is **engine eval, most favorable to the column's
side to move first** — the best move *for that column* floats up. Direction is
keyed to the position's side to move (`active_color(column_fen)`), NOT the
repertoire/selected color:

- **White-to-move column** → highest white-relative eval first.
- **Black-to-move column** → lowest (most-negative) white-relative eval first.

This is the redirection from the original implementation, which keyed the flip
to `self.player_color` (the selected/repertoire side). Because the side to move
is a property of the position, the eval tie-break is now **color-independent**:
the same column sorts its evals identically for a white and a black repertoire.
The only columns whose order changes vs. the old behavior are **opponent-turn**
columns (where active color ≠ player color); user-turn columns are unaffected
(active color == player color there).

## Sort key ordering (unchanged structure)

1. Play frequency (PRIMARY): user turn → `(not is_observed, -user_choice_count)`;
   opponent turn → `(encounter_count <= 0, -encounter_count)`.
2. Eval favorability (SECONDARY, this bead): `(favorability is None, -favorability)`
   — unknown last, else most-favorable-to-side-to-move first.
3. `opening_score` (TERTIARY): ascending, null last.
4. Deterministic destination/source/promotion/UCI tail → total order.

Eval NEVER overrides play frequency (it is strictly the secondary key).

## `_eval_favorability(node, side_to_move)`

Mirrors `opening_quality._white_cp`:
- prefer `eval_cp`;
- else a non-zero mate via `mate_to_cp` (a closer mate dominates any cp);
- else (no cp and mate is None or 0) → `None` (sorts last).

A white-relative **mate-0** has no recoverable winner (perspective sign-flip
`mate * sign` zeroes it; `tree_eval._played_eval` collapses mate rows to
mate-only so the disambiguating cp never reaches here) → treated as unknown.

The stored eval is white-relative, so: `white_cp if side_to_move == "white"
else -white_cp`. White column ranks highest white-relative first; Black column
ranks lowest/most-negative first.

## Implementation (backend-only)

`backend/app/api/openings.py`, Pass-2 column loop:
```python
side_to_move = active_color(norm_i)
user_turn = side_to_move == self.player_color
nodes.sort(key=lambda node: self._sort_key(node, user_turn, side_to_move))
```
`_sort_key(node, user_turn, side_to_move)` → `_eval_favorability(node, side_to_move)`.

Frontend is unchanged: cards render white-relative evals as-is (g-qb4s already
removed the frontend perspective flip in `treeView.ts`); only backend column
order changes.

## Tests (`backend/test_tree_api.py`)

Organized by the column's side to move:
- `_white_branch_graph()` helper: 1.e4 e5 with two white book replies (Nf3, Bc4)
  so E4E5 is a white-to-move branch with a play-frequency tie (the shared
  `_make_graph` only branches at black-to-move nodes E4/NF3).
- `test_tree_eval_breaks_ties_white_to_move_column` — White column: +50 > -30.
- `test_tree_eval_breaks_ties_black_to_move_column` — Black column (E4): -30 first.
- `test_tree_eval_tie_break_keys_on_column_side_not_repertoire_color` — same
  black-to-move column sorts identically for white & black repertoires.
- `test_tree_eval_mate_dominates_centipawns_white_to_move` / `_black_to_move`.
- `test_tree_eval_unknown_sorts_after_scored_in_tie_break` — scored (even if
  bad for the side to move) beats unknown.
- `test_tree_eval_mate_zero_winner_is_unknown` — mate-0 sorts last, both colors.
- `test_tree_eval_does_not_override_play_frequency` — kept (eval is secondary).

## SPEC.md

§13.3 tree-page-semantics + node-hydration: "selected-side favorability" →
"the column's side-to-move favorability". §13.x **Sorting**: rewrite the eval
clause to "most favorable to the column's side to move first … keyed to the side
to move rather than the repertoire color". **Color specificity**: primary
play-frequency key still color-specific; secondary eval tie-break is keyed to a
position property, hence color-independent.

Note: tree_eval.eval_for_perspective now has NO production caller (only its own docstring + test_tree_eval.py reference it) since g-qb4s removed the frontend flip; left in place (has tests) — flagged for a possible future dead-code removal, out of scope here.

title: Show best-move star in AnalysisBoard when played move matches trusted position best
description: The post-game AnalysisBoard renders move icons from classification but is fed by src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts, which shares the published-path trust gate yet has NO exact-best truth channel. For a move-untrusted cache row whose played move equals the trusted best_move_uci (the c4 / browser-game-v1 case), it falls back to the worker, which classifies the move 'excellent', so AnalysisBoard shows the '!' icon instead of the best-move star. Same root cause as g-move-best-icon, which fixed only the live ChessGame MoveList (GameAnalysisCoordinator path); the coordinator-side fix does not reach the AnalysisBoard hook.
design:
## Same root cause as g-move-best-icon, different consumer

`g-move-best-icon` fixed the LIVE MoveList (ChessGame -> `GameAnalysisCoordinator`). The post-game `AnalysisBoard` renders move icons from the SAME classification field (`AnalysisBoard.tsx` ~380/964/1325, `AnalysisBoard.helpers.ts` ~92 -> `CLASSIFICATION_ICON[classification]`) but is fed by a DIFFERENT resolution path: `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts`.

`useMoveAnalysis.flushCacheLookups` (~line 337) has the identical published-path gate (`isTrustedPositionHit && isTrustedMoveHit && hasCpEvalLoss`). For a move-untrusted row whose played move equals the trusted `best_move_uci` (the c4 / `browser-game-v1` case), `move_trusted` is false, so it `releaseFallback`s to the worker, and the worker (shallower, blind to the canonical best move) classifies it `excellent`. AnalysisBoard then shows the `!` icon instead of the best-move star — the exact bug g-move-best-icon fixed for the live board.

Crucially, `useMoveAnalysis` has NO drill-truth side channel (that lives only on the coordinator), so the coordinator-side fix does not reach AnalysisBoard.

## Approach

1. Lift the pure helper `promoteToTrustedBest(result, trustedBestUci)` out of `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` into a shared module (candidate: `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`, alongside the trust guards; it operates on `AnalysisResult` which is a type-only import from `useMoveAnalysis.ts`, no runtime cycle). Update the coordinator import + its test import. This is a pure move — no behavior change for g-move-best-icon.

2. In `useMoveAnalysis`, add a per-moveIndex exact-best truth record (mirrors the coordinator's `drillTruth` but minimal — only `best_move_uci` is needed here; no eval-loss/grade machinery). Record it in the cache `.then` when `isTrustedExactBestHit(cached)` is true, BEFORE `releaseFallback`, keyed/guarded by the same requestId the resolution state uses. Clear it on the same supersession/reset paths that clear the resolution state so a stale record never promotes a later request.

3. At the single publish point in `useMoveAnalysis` (`resolveAnalysis(moveIndex, result)`), apply `promoteToTrustedBest(result, truth.best_move_uci)` when an exact-best record matches `result.id` and `result.move`. This covers both the cache-publish path (`fromCachedAnalysis`) and the worker-fallback path, same as the coordinator.

## Notes / scope

- The eval-magnitude behavior is identical to g-move-best-icon: only best-ness facts are rewritten (`classification: 'best'`, `bestMove`/`bestLine`/`bestEval` collapsed onto the played move, `delta: 0`); `playedEval` is preserved. No foreign position eval is pulled in.
- AnalysisBoard's separate engine-line panel ordering bug is `g-54h5`, NOT this bead. This bead is only the move-list/board icon classification.
- Verify the DrillAnalysisSnapshot surface (`sessionUpload.ts` `buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot`) and the session-loaded AnalysisBoard both benefit, since both flow through `useMoveAnalysis` resolution.

## Tests

- New focused tests in `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.test.ts` mirroring the coordinator's g-move-best-icon tests: worker-fallback c4 scenario promotes to `best`; Bf4 (non-best) stays `excellent`.
- If the helper moves to `analysisUtils.ts`, move/keep its pure unit tests there.
acceptance_criteria: In AnalysisBoard, a move whose played UCI equals the trusted best_move_uci renders the best-move star even when its (untrusted/worker) classification is 'excellent'. Non-best moves keep their classification icon. The promoteToTrustedBest helper is shared between the coordinator and useMoveAnalysis (single source). Focused useMoveAnalysis tests pass; existing g-move-best-icon coordinator tests still pass.
close_reason: Implemented: shared promoteToTrustedBest in neutral analysisUtils + exact-best truth side channel in useMoveAnalysis so AnalysisBoard shows the best-move star; AnalysisResult/MoveClassification extracted to src/types/analysis.ts to break the workers->hooks layering cycle.

title: Show best-move icon when played move matches position best
description: MoveList currently shows the classification icon for an excellent move even when lookup evidence says the played move equals best_move_uci. The UI should show the best-move star for matching moves while retaining classification icons for non-best moves.
design:
## Root cause (grain split)

At FEN `rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3P4/5N2/PPP1PPPP/RNBQKB1R w KQkq - 0 3`:
- Bf4 row: `precomputed` canonical, `move_trusted: true`, best_move=c2c4, classification=excellent. Bf4 != best, so `!` is CORRECT.
- c4 row: `browser-game-v1`, `move_trusted: false`, `position_trusted: true`, best_move=c2c4, classification=excellent. c4 == best, so it SHOULD show the star but shows `!`.

The c4 row fails the published-path gate in `GameAnalysisCoordinator.flushCacheLookups` (`isTrustedMoveHit` requires `move_trusted`), so it `releaseFallback`s to the WORKER. The worker's shallower search does not recognize c4 as best, so it publishes `classification: 'excellent'` with a different `bestMove`. Meanwhile the drill GRADE is correct because it reads the trusted-position drill-truth side channel (recorded at line ~1447 via `isTrustedExactBestHit`), not the worker classification. The MoveList icon (`MoveRow` -> `CLASSIFICATION_ICON[move.classification]`) reads the worker classification -> `!`.

So display classification and drill grade come from different channels; only the display side ignores the trusted position truth.

## Fix

Single injection at the one publish choke point `GameAnalysisCoordinator.resolveAnalysisResult` (both cache-publish and worker-fallback paths pass through it; drill-truth is always recorded before it on every terminal path). New exported pure helper `promoteToTrustedBest(result, trustedBestUci)`:

- No-op if `result.classification === 'best'` or `result.move !== trustedBestUci`.
- Otherwise the trusted position grain names the played move as the exact best move, so normalize the published result to a coherent loss-0 best move:
  - `classification: 'best'`, `bestMove: trustedBestUci`, `bestLine: [trustedBestUci]`, `bestEval: result.playedEval`, `delta: 0`, `blunder: false`, `recordable: false`.
  - Eval MAGNITUDES (playedEval/mate) are left as the worker/move grain produced them; everything rewritten is derivable from the played move + its own playedEval (no foreign/untrusted position eval is pulled in). `delta: 0` is correct by definition (playing the trusted best move has exactly 0 loss).

`resolveAnalysisResult` reads `this.drillTruth.get(moveIndex)` (guarded by `truth.requestId === result.id`; supersession clears stale records) and publishes `promoteToTrustedBest(...)` to the store, waiters, and the resolved outcome.

## Why this is the right grain

"Is the played move the best move?" is a POSITION-grain question; the trusted position grain answers it. The icon (and best bling / perfect-streak, which also key on `classification === 'best'`) should reflect that answer regardless of a stale/untrusted move-grain or worker classification. This mirrors how the drill grade already uses the trusted position grain.

## Side effects (intended)
- Best-move bling (`AnalysisEffects`) and perfect-streak (`perfectStreak.ts`) now fire for a played exact-best move that the worker under-rated. Correct: best move == perfect.
- `sessionUpload` now uploads coherent best-* evidence (best_move == played, delta 0) instead of the worker's wrong best move. Strictly better; still `browser-game-v1` untrusted.
- Strictness>0 drill worker-fallback for an exact-best move with null `positionEvalLossCp` now PASSES (delta 0) instead of grading from noisy worker delta. Pre-existing latent bug; the fix is a correctness improvement and only affects exact-best moves.

## Scope
- Live ChessGame MoveList path only (`GameAnalysisCoordinator`). The post-game `AnalysisBoard` (`useMoveAnalysis`) shares the gate but has no drill-truth channel; out of scope for this bead.

## Tests (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts`)
- Worker-fallback c4 scenario (position_trusted, move_untrusted, played == best_move_uci, worker says excellent w/ different bestMove) -> published `classification === 'best'`, `bestMove === 'c2c4'`.
- Bf4 scenario (played != best_move_uci) -> classification stays `'excellent'`.
- Pure-helper unit tests for `promoteToTrustedBest` (match, no-match, already-best no-op).
acceptance_criteria: A MoveList entry whose played UCI equals bestMove/best_move_uci renders the best-move star icon even if its classification is excellent. Non-best excellent moves continue to render the excellent icon. Relevant focused tests pass.

title: Make every /openings card drillable (remove boundary-root gate)
description: Today only registered boundary-root cards show a Start Drill button (frontend gates on drill_opening_key, which the backend sets only for name-change boundary roots). Cards still display an inherited opening name, so users see named cards with no drill option. Make every card drillable: in-book targets keep the transposition-tolerant book BFS; off-book targets drill the exact played line (strict). All card drills SEND the target FEN + full UCI line; the backend persists the line only for ad-hoc/non-root targets (validated by replay, metadata synthesized to match the card), while registered-root targets keep legacy behavior (line ignored, drill_line NULL, metadata from the root). Full plan in design field.
design:
# Plan: Make every `/openings` card drillable

## Context

**Problem.** On the `/openings` tree, only some cards show a "Start Drill" button. This is by design, not a render bug: the frontend gate (`OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx:114`, `showDrill = node.drillOpeningKey != null`) reflects the backend's `drill_opening_key`, non-null **only for registered "boundary roots"** — positions where the opening *name changes* from its parent (`opening_roots.py:231-249`). The card's **displayed name** is resolved far more broadly: every graph position gets a name, and a position without its own name *inherits* the deepest named ancestor's name (`openings.py:1188-1200`). Same data (`eco.byPosition.json` → `OpeningGraph`), two filters — so a deep card shows "Sicilian, Najdorf" but has no drill key, hence no button.

**Goal.** Every expanded **move** card offers Start Drill. A drill = "navigate from the start position to the card's target position, staying on route."

**Key enabler.** Two graphs exist: the **book graph** (`get_opening_graph()`) and the richer **constructed /openings graph** that also includes the user's played moves via `opening_position_edges` (`models.py:575-640`, stitched in `opening_evidence.py:430-491`). So even an *off-book* leaf has a known played line. The tree response already carries `canonical_line` + each node's `uci`/`ply`/`child_fen`, and `treeView.ts:286` already computes each card's full UCI line as `DisplayNode.selectLine`.

**Agreed semantics (final):**
1. Route mode branches on whether the **target** is in the book graph (`graph.has_position(target)`):
   - **In-book target** (all named cards currently missing the button): keep today's transposition-tolerant book BFS (`get_drill_route_map`). No behavior change for existing drills.
   - **Off-book target**: build a **strict line route** from the exact played line. On-route = following that exact line; success = reaching the target. **Strict the whole way.**
2. **Ad-hoc / non-root card drills** send the target FEN + full UCI line (in-book *and* off-book) and the backend persists the line. **Registered-root targets keep legacy behavior** (line ignored, `drill_line` NULL). The line is needed for metadata (inherited name) regardless of route mode; route mode still branches on `has_position(target)`.
3. Backend validates the line by replay (legality + reaches the claimed FEN). No "verify against stored edges" step.
4. Metadata (name/family/eco/depth) for non-root targets is synthesized to **match the card**: deepest named book node along the line (`derive_family` for family), `depth = len(line)`.
5. The existing overlay / `getOpeningRoots()` picker flow (registered roots only) keeps working unchanged.

> Incorporates review of g-6aik: (1) root-card gate, (2) in-book always-send-line, (3) ad-hoc preselect independent of `getOpeningRoots()`, (4) hardened backend validation, (5) reuse existing UCI-line storage helpers, (6) SPEC update.

---

## Backend changes

### 1. `backend/app/drill_steering.py` — strict-line route map

- Extend `DrillRouteMap` (`:19`) with `forward_moves: dict[str, list[DrillRouteMove]] | None = None`. `None` → book BFS map (unchanged). A dict → line map, keyed by normalized FEN → one-element list with the single on-route next move.
- New `build_line_route_map(line_ucis) -> DrillRouteMap`: replay from `chess.Board()`, normalizing each position; `plies_by_fen[positions[i]] = len(line) - i`; `forward_moves[positions[i]] = [DrillRouteMove(line[i], san, positions[i+1], len(line)-(i+1))]`. **Duplicate-position policy:** set each FEN key only on first occurrence, so a line revisiting a position stays deterministic from the top. Do **not** cache line maps in `_ROUTE_CACHE` (build fresh; lines are ≤80 plies).
- Branch the two helpers on `forward_moves` **before** touching `graph` (off-book positions have no graph node):
  - `route_preserving_moves` (`:90`): `if route_map.forward_moves is not None: return list(route_map.forward_moves.get(normalize_fen(fen), []))`.
  - `route_move_for_uci` (`:122`): `if route_map.forward_moves is not None:` return the matching move from `forward_moves.get(fen, [])` else `None`.
- Shared selector (so the two endpoints never diverge; no DB/HTTP coupling):
  ```python
  def route_map_for_target(graph, target_fen, drill_line):  # drill_line: list[str] | None
      if graph.has_position(normalize_fen(target_fen)):
          return get_drill_route_map(graph, target_fen)
      if not drill_line:
          return DrillRouteMap(normalize_fen(target_fen), {})  # caller raises 400 on empty
      return build_line_route_map(drill_line)
  ```

### 2. `backend/app/api/drills.py`

- **`DrillStartRequest`** (`:45`): add `line: list[str] | None = None`. `opening_key` now means "target FEN OR registered root key".
- **`start_drill`** (`:162`): replace the hard `_root_or_404` gate (`:168`) with:
  - `root = get_opening_roots().get_root(request.opening_key)`.
  - `root is not None` → registered-root path exactly as today (`drill_opening_key=request.opening_key`, `drill_line=None`); ignore any `line`.
  - else (ad-hoc card drill) — **a line is required**:
    - **Validation (hardened, all → controlled 422, never a 500):**
      - `if not request.line:` → `404 "Unknown opening root"` (genuinely unidentifiable; legacy picker never produces this).
      - `if len(request.line) > MAX_TREE_PLY:` → `422` (import `MAX_TREE_PLY` from `app.api.openings`; if that introduces an import cycle, define a local `DRILL_MAX_LINE_PLY = 80` with a comment).
      - Replay each UCI: `chess.Move.from_uci(uci)` in `try/except ValueError` → `422`; `if move not in board.legal_moves` → `422`. (UCI item length is validated implicitly by `from_uci`.)
      - Wrap the target `normalize_fen(request.opening_key)` in `try/except ValueError` → `422` (arbitrary keys must not 500).
      - `if normalize_fen(final_board.fen()) != normalized_target:` → `422 "Drill line does not reach the target position"`.
    - Persist `drill_opening_key=normalized_target`, `drill_line=encode_uci_line(request.line)` (reuse `app.models.encode_uci_line`, the space-joined convention — **not** JSON). Routing branches later on `has_position`.
- **route-check** (`:288`): `route_map = route_map_for_target(graph, session.drill_opening_key, decode_uci_line(session.drill_line))`; keep the `if not route_map.plies_by_fen: 400` guard (message → "Drill route is unavailable"). Rest of `check_drill_route` (`:293-356`) unchanged.
- **`_contract`** (`:137`) — `DrillSessionContract` (`:89`) returns non-null `opening_name`/`opening_family`, so a line is mandatory for ad-hoc:
  - `root` present → root metadata (unchanged).
  - elif `drill_line` present → replay `decode_uci_line(...)`, walk book-graph nodes, keep deepest `node.name`/`node.eco` (same inheritance as `openings.py:1188-1200`); then **set the fallback name BEFORE deriving family** (so `derive_family` is never called on `None`): `display_name = name or "Custom line"`; `family = derive_family(display_name)`; `eco` may be null; `depth = len(line)`; `key = session.drill_opening_key` (already normalized).
  - else → `404`. **No graph-node-only fallback** (every ad-hoc session has a line, so the in-book-no-line branch from the earlier draft is removed — it would have yielded a non-inherited / possibly null name).
  - `opening_key` in the contract MUST be the normalized target FEN (echoed back on every route-check, stored client-side as `drillOpeningKey`).
- Imports to add: `chess`, `encode_uci_line`, `decode_uci_line`, `derive_family`, `build_line_route_map`, `route_map_for_target`, `MAX_TREE_PLY`.

### 3. `backend/app/api/game.py` — opponent steering (CRITICAL)

`:878-913` (`is_active_preroot_drill`) builds the route map the same way to pick the opponent's reply. Replace `get_drill_route_map(graph, session.drill_opening_key)` (`:882`) with `route_map_for_target(graph, session.drill_opening_key, decode_uci_line(session.drill_line))`; keep the empty-map 400 guard. Without this, off-book drills are unplayable. Downstream (`is_target`, `route_preserving_moves`, `target_fen`, `plies_to_target`) works for line maps unchanged.

### 4. `backend/app/models.py` — persist the line

After `drill_opening_key` (`:206`): `drill_line: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)` — space-joined UCI string via `encode_uci_line`/`decode_uci_line` (`:23-35`). NULL for registered-root drills. No check constraint.

---

## Frontend changes

### 5. `src/openings/treeView.ts`

- Add `childFen: string | null` to `DisplayNode`. Set `childFen: node.child_fen` in the API-node map (`:275-291`); `childFen: null` for the synthesized root (`:250-265`). Reuse existing `selectLine` (`:286`) as each card's full UCI line.

### 6. Gate + payload (fixes the root-card bug)

The synthesized root **is** expanded when no move is selected (`treeView.ts:256`, `isExpanded: k === 0`). So the page must **not** wire `onStartDrill` for it.

- `OpeningsPage.tsx` `TreeColumnView` (`:104-113`): wire `onStartDrill` **only when `node.childFen != null`** (equivalently `column.kind === "moves"`) — never for the root:
  ```ts
  onStartDrill={ node.childFen != null
    ? () => onStartDrill({ targetFen: node.childFen!, line: node.selectLine,
                           displayName: node.view.openingName, eco: node.view.eco })
    : undefined }
  ```
  Prop type → `(p: { targetFen: string; line: string[]; displayName: string | null; eco: string | null }) => void`.
- `OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx:114`: `const showDrill = onStartDrill != null;` (root passes `undefined` → no button).
- `OpeningsPage.startDrill` (`:280`): `navigate("/play", { state: { drillSetup: { ...p, playerColor } } })`.

### 7. `src/components/ChessGame.tsx` — ad-hoc preselect independent of `getOpeningRoots()`

The roots fetch can be loading or fail (`:953-974`); on failure it currently calls `setSelectedDrillOpening(null)` (`:967`), and the match effect waits for `openingFamilies` (`:1014`). An ad-hoc card drill already carries everything it needs, so it must not depend on the roots list:

- **Set the synthetic selection in the intercept effect** (`:940-951`), not the openingFamilies-gated effect: when `drillSetup.targetFen` is present, `setSelectedDrillOpening({ opening_key: targetFen, opening_name: displayName ?? "Custom line", opening_family: "", eco: eco ?? null, depth: line?.length ?? 0 })`, store the line in a new `adHocLineRef`, and **clear `pendingDrillSetupRef.current`** (the ad-hoc path is fully handled here). Extend the nav-state type with optional `targetFen`/`line`/`displayName`/`eco` (keep `openingKey?` for the legacy path).
- **Apply the nav `playerColor` in the intercept effect** for the ad-hoc path — the registered-root flow applies color later in the openingFamilies match effect (`:1022-1023`), which ad-hoc skips: `setDrillPlayerColor(drillSetup.playerColor === "black" ? "black" : "white")`.
- **Guard the localStorage prefill** (`:976-1011`) so it does not overwrite the pending nav color: the prefill currently calls `setDrillPlayerColor(prefs.playerColor)` (`:995-1000`). Set a `navColorRef` in the intercept effect and have the prefill skip its `setDrillPlayerColor` (and reset the ref) when `navColorRef.current` is true. (Intercept runs before prefill in the overlay-open commit, so without this the sticky color clobbers the nav color.)
- **Don't clear an ad-hoc selection on roots-fetch failure** (`:967`): only `setSelectedDrillOpening(null)` when `adHocLineRef.current == null` (i.e. not an ad-hoc drill).
- **Keep the legacy match effect** (`:1014-1025`) for the registered-root path, but skip it when `adHocLineRef.current != null`.
- `handleStartDrill` (`:1566`): pass `line: adHocLineRef.current ?? undefined` into `handleNewDrill`. Reset `adHocLineRef` (and clear the synthetic selection) whenever the user picks from `OpeningPicker`, so a stale line can't attach to a root drill.

### 8. `src/components/chess-game/ui/OpeningPicker.tsx` — label priority

`triggerLabel` (`:268-274`) currently shows loading/failed **before** the selected label, and the trigger is `disabled` on `isLoading || loadFailed` (`:286`). Reorder so a selection wins:
```ts
const triggerLabel = selectedOpening ? rootLabel(selectedOpening)
  : isLoading ? "Loading openings..." : loadFailed ? "Failed to load openings" : "Select opening";
```
So an ad-hoc drill shows its synthesized name even if the roots list is still loading or failed. (The trigger may stay disabled when `loadFailed` — the user simply can't *switch* openings — but Start Drill stays enabled because `DrillSetupPanel.tsx:151` gates on `selectedOpening`.)

### 9. `src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts` + `src/utils/api.ts`

- `handleNewDrill` options (`:594`) + `startDrill({...})` call (`:626`): thread `line?: string[]`.
- `DrillStartRequest` TS type (`api.ts:408`): add `line?: string[]`.

---

title: Replace analysis wall-clock timeout with per-request inactivity watchdog
description:
Indexed move analysis currently has a no-hang guard that starts a fixed 30s wall-clock timer when analyzeMove schedules a request. The guard prevents waitForAnalysis and drill grading from hanging forever when the worker never emits a result, but total elapsed time is not a reliable liveness signal.

A single depth-17 browser Stockfish move analysis may run up to three searches: root best-move search, post-played search, and, when played != best, post-best search. The older 8s guard falsely killed the reported 20...Qf6 case at about 8.8s; raising the guard to 30s adds headroom, but it is still an arbitrary total-time ceiling that can kill a slow but progressing analysis.

Replace the fixed total-elapsed deadline with a per-request inactivity watchdog. A request should fail only after it has produced no observable activity for the watchdog window. Any activity for that request should reset the watchdog so slow, progressing root/post-played/post-best searches can complete while truly silent or hung workers still fail promptly.
design:
# Plan — Replace analysis wall-clock deadline with per-request inactivity watchdog

## Problem / current behavior
Indexed move analysis arms a fixed `ANALYSIS_TOTAL_DEADLINE_MS = 30_000` wall-clock timer at
`analyzeMove` (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:879`, `ResolutionEntry.deadlineTimer`), fired as
`failRequest(idx, id, 'deadline')`. It is a total-elapsed ceiling: it cannot tell a slow-but-
progressing analysis from a hung one. A depth-17 move runs up to 3 searches (root, post-played,
post-best); the root phase alone can exceed 8s. The legacy `useMoveAnalysis.ts` mirrors this for
indexed requests and also gives variation (what-if) requests their own fixed deadline
(`variationDeadlineTimers`).

Key gap: the worker only surfaces progress during the **post-played** search (`analysis-streaming`
from that search's `onInfo`). The **root** and **post-best** searches emit NO observable activity,
so a tightened inactivity window can't see them — the root search would look "silent" for its whole
(possibly >8s) duration. We must surface root/post-best liveness explicitly.

Also note (per bead): `lastStreamingUpdateMs` is GLOBAL display throttling, not per-request
liveness — it must NOT drive the watchdog.

## Goal
A request fails only after producing no observable activity for an inactivity window; any activity
for that request resets the window. Slow-but-progressing searches survive; truly silent/hung workers
fail well under 30s (UX: drill `waitForAnalysis` recovery doesn't stall). Fully REPLACE the fixed
total deadline (no absolute ceiling retained).

## Design

### Constants
`ANALYSIS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000` (replaces the 30_000 total deadline in BOTH files).
Rationale: comfortably above Stockfish's intra-search info cadence (it emits periodic depth-bearing
`info` lines roughly every ≤3s even within a long iteration) plus the per-request reset round-trip,
while cutting silent-worker failure from 30s → 8s. Single tunable; validate via the real-browser
smoke test and raise to 10s only if real info cadence proves sparse.

`ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` (NEW — boot backstop, distinct from the inactivity window; see
"Engine-boot strategy" below). Generous: comfortably above real WASM cold-boot, below the old 30s.

### New worker liveness signal (root/post-best coverage)
Add response variant: `{ type: 'analysis-progress'; id: string }`.
- NO `depth` field (review finding 3). `parseUciInfoLine` returns non-null for depth **or** score
  **or** pv (`parseInfo.ts:4`), so a score/pv-only line carries no depth; a `depth` field would be a
  misleading `0` on those lines. The watchdog needs only "something happened for `id`", and the
  full engine line (with depth) is already available via the existing `log` messages for debugging.
- Emitted at the **engine-line level** (NOT via `onInfo`) so it covers ALL THREE searches including
  the root, keyed by `activeAnalysisId`, throttled in the worker. Liveness-only; it never drives the
  streaming-eval display (`analysis-streaming` keeps that role for the post-played phase).

### Watchdog reset model (hybrid: per-request + serial-worker liveness)
Per-request timer keyed by requestId on the `ResolutionEntry`, plus a `started` flag.
- Armed at `analyzeMove` (scheduling), `started=false`.
- `noteActivity(requestId)` is called on each worker message and is **self-guarding** — it does
  NOTHING unless `requestId` is a LIVE, CURRENT request (review finding 1):
  `requestIdToMoveIndex.get(id) === idx` AND `resolutionState.get(idx)?.requestId === id` AND
  `latestRequestIds.get(idx) === id` AND `!resolvedIndices.has(idx)`. A superseded id (entry now
  owned by the replacement), a failed id (entry deleted, tombstone retained), a resolved id, or a
  discarded id all fail this gate and are inert. For a live request it:
  1. Per-request: set `entry.started = true` and re-arm ITS watchdog (its own activity).
  2. Serial-worker liveness: `bumpQueuedWatchdogs()` — re-arm the watchdog of every still-pending
     entry that has NOT started yet (queued behind the active request). The worker is a single serial
     engine, so a LIVE active request's progress proves it is alive and draining toward those queued
     requests. (Stale activity never reaches this step, so a superseded/failed request's late
     progress can no longer keep queued work alive — review finding 1.)
- A **started** request is reset ONLY by its own activity → if it goes silent it fails after one
  window (correct: it is the worker's serial focus and is hung).
- A **queued** (not-started) request is reset by any LIVE worker liveness → it fails only if the
  WHOLE worker goes silent. Prevents false-killing a request waiting behind a legitimately slow but
  progressing earlier search.
- `ready` calls `bumpQueuedWatchdogs()` directly (no id) to (re)arm everything once the engine is live.

### Engine-boot strategy (review round 2, finding 1)
The inactivity window (8s) and engine boot have OPPOSITE tuning needs: boot must tolerate a slow cold
WASM start, inactivity must be tight. Arming the 8s timer at scheduling would false-fail the FIRST
request if boot stays silent for >8s (the `ready`-rearm only helps when `ready` arrives < 8s). So
decouple them:
- Track `engineReady` (coordinator boolean, NOT the store status): `false` on worker (re)creation,
  `true` in the `ready` handler.
- The inactivity watchdog is a POST-ready concept. `analyzeMove`'s INITIAL arm only fires when
  `engineReady` is true; a request scheduled while booting gets NO inactivity timer yet and is armed
  when `ready` arrives (`ready → bumpQueuedWatchdogs()`). (`noteActivity` re-arms are unconditional —
  activity only ever follows `ready`.)
- A single coordinator `bootWatchdogTimer` (`ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20s`) bounds a silent/hung
  boot: started on worker creation, cleared on `ready`, and on fire calls `handleFatalError('Analysis
  engine failed to start')` (rejects all waiters + tears down — same as a boot error, so drill
  `waitForAnalysis` recovery still settles instead of hanging). This preserves today's boot
  robustness (old 30s deadline doubled as the boot guard) while the 8s inactivity window targets hung
  SEARCHES only.

Why this beats the alternatives:
- Pure "from scheduling, own-activity-only": false-kills queued requests (no activity while waiting
  their turn behind a long search).
- Pure "arm only on analysis-started": leaves queued requests unprotected if the worker wedges
  mid-search and never reaches them — a regression vs today's per-request fixed deadline.
The hybrid keeps both properties: never false-kill a progressing/queued request; always drain a
genuinely silent worker. The self-guard keeps stale messages inert (bead: "stale worker messages
cannot revive or fail a newer request").

## Exact changes

### 1. `src/workers/analysisMessages.ts`
- Add to `AnalysisWorkerResponse`: `| { type: 'analysis-progress'; id: string }` with a doc comment:
  per-search liveness ping from any active search's info lines (root/post-played/post-best),
  worker-throttled; distinct from `analysis-streaming` (display-only, post-played); consumed solely
  to reset the per-request inactivity watchdog. Carries no eval/depth.

### 2. `src/workers/analysisWorker.ts`
- Add `const PROGRESS_THROTTLE_MS = 250;` and module state
  `let lastProgressPostMs = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;`.
- In `analyzeMove`, immediately after posting `analysis-started`, set
  `lastProgressPostMs = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` so the first info line of each new request emits a
  progress ping promptly. Use `Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` (NOT `0`) — under fake timers `Date.now()`
  starts at 0, so `0` would make `now - lastProgressPostMs === 0 < 250` and suppress the very first
  ping, weakening the root-phase liveness test (review round 2, finding 2).
- In `handleEngineLine`, inside the existing `if (info && activeSearch) { ... }` branch, add (guarded
  by `activeAnalysisId`), BEFORE the existing score/pv handling:
  ```
  if (activeAnalysisId) {
    const now = Date.now();
    if (now - lastProgressPostMs >= PROGRESS_THROTTLE_MS) {
      lastProgressPostMs = now;
      ctx.postMessage({ type: 'analysis-progress', id: activeAnalysisId } satisfies AnalysisWorkerResponse);
    }
  }
  ```
  Fires for any non-null parsed info line (depth/score/pv) during any of the 3 searches → continuous
  liveness even within a long iteration (no `info.depth` filter, per finding 3).
- Phase-boundary pings (review round 3, finding 1): info lines only cover the INSIDE of a search;
  the per-request reset and the gaps BETWEEN searches emit no info, so a `bestmove` arriving just
  before the window followed by a slow next-phase first-info could false-kill a live request. Emit an
  UNTHROTTLED `analysis-progress` (low volume — these are 1 + ≤3 per request) at the two phase
  boundaries, keyed by `activeAnalysisId` and only when it is set and NOT in `canceledAnalyses`:
  - In the `readyok` handler, inside the per-request reset branch (the `if (!waiter.done)` block,
    `analysisWorker.ts:260`) — a completed LIVE reset, before the root search.
  - In the `bestmove` handler, right after `current.resolve(...)` (`analysisWorker.ts:286`) — each
    search-phase completion (root / post-played / post-best).
  Do NOT touch `lastProgressPostMs` here (these are separate, unthrottled). The init-handshake
  `readyok` (`analysisWorker.ts:266`) is NOT a per-request boundary and emits no progress.
- In the `terminate` request handler, reset `lastProgressPostMs = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` (tidy).

### 3. `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`
- Remove `ANALYSIS_TOTAL_DEADLINE_MS`; add `ANALYSIS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000` and
  `ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` (docs).
- `ResolutionEntry`: rename `deadlineTimer` → `watchdogTimer`; add `started?: boolean`.
- New fields: `private engineReady = false`; `private bootWatchdogTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null`.
- `ensureWorker()`: after creating the worker, `this.engineReady = false`, clear any existing
  `bootWatchdogTimer`, and start `bootWatchdogTimer = setTimeout(() => { this.bootWatchdogTimer = null;
  this.handleFatalError('Analysis engine failed to start') }, ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS)`.
- `terminateWorker()`: `this.engineReady = false`; clear + null `bootWatchdogTimer`.
  `destroy()`: also clear `bootWatchdogTimer`.
- New `private armWatchdog(moveIndex, entry)`: clear `entry.watchdogTimer`; set it to
  `setTimeout(() => this.failRequest(moveIndex, entry.requestId, 'inactivity'), ANALYSIS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS)`.
- New `private bumpQueuedWatchdogs()`: for every entry in `resolutionState` with `!entry.started`
  and `!resolvedIndices.has(idx)`, `armWatchdog(idx, entry)`.
- New `private noteActivity(requestId)`: the SELF-GUARDED reset described above — returns early
  unless `requestId` is the live current owner of its index; otherwise sets `entry.started = true`,
  `armWatchdog(idx, entry)`, then `bumpQueuedWatchdogs()`.
- `analyzeMove` (indexed branch): create the entry `{ requestId: id, cacheStatus: 'pending' }`, then
  `if (this.engineReady) this.armWatchdog(moveIndex, entry)` — pre-ready requests are armed later by
  `ready → bumpQueuedWatchdogs()` (boot strategy).
- `failRequest`: change `reason: 'deadline' | 'worker-error'` → `'inactivity' | 'worker-error'`;
  update the closing `console.log` text. Keep the default error text `'analysis timed out'` so
  existing `/timed out/i` assertions and recovery messaging hold.
- Rename all `entry.deadlineTimer` → `entry.watchdogTimer` at every clear site:
  `pruneFromMoveIndex` (443), `analyzeMove` supersession (862), `clearAllResolutionState` (951),
  `clearAnalysis` (997), `failRequest` (1319), `resolveAnalysisResult` (1359).
- `releaseFallback`: unchanged behavior (still does NOT clear the watchdog — a released request still
  awaiting a silent worker stays protected); update its comment from "total-analysis deadline" to
  "inactivity watchdog".
- `handleWorkerMessage`:
  - `case 'ready'`: FIRST add `if (s.status === 'error') break` (review round 3, finding 3 — a stray
    late `ready`, e.g. after the new boot-timeout fatal path, must not flip 'error' back to 'ready',
    re-arm watchdogs, or clear the boot guard on a dead worker; this mirrors the guard the other late-
    message cases already use, and `terminateWorker`'s listener removal isolates a replaced worker so
    no separate generation check is needed). THEN set `this.engineReady = true`, clear+null
    `bootWatchdogTimer`, `setStatus('ready')`, `bumpQueuedWatchdogs()`.
  - `case 'analysis-started'`: after the existing discard/status/ownership gates, `noteActivity(message.id)`.
  - `case 'analysis-streaming'`: after the existing gates, `noteActivity(message.id)`.
  - NEW `case 'analysis-progress'`: drop if `status === 'error'` or
    `discardedRequestIds.has(message.id)`; else `noteActivity(message.id)` (which self-guards against
    stale/superseded/resolved ids); `break`.
  - `case 'analysis'`: after the discard/status guards (before buffering/resolving), `noteActivity(message.id)`.
  - `case 'error'` (scoped): after the entry/ownership/resolved guards, `noteActivity(message.id)`.

### 4. `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts` (mirror — indexed AND variation)
- Replace `ANALYSIS_TOTAL_DEADLINE_MS` → `ANALYSIS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000`; add
  `ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000`.
- `ResolutionEntry`: `deadlineTimer` → `watchdogTimer`; add `started?: boolean`.
- Boot strategy mirror: add `engineReadyRef` (false on mount/worker-create, true in the `ready`
  case) and a `bootWatchdogTimer` ref started in the worker `useEffect` (cleared on `ready`, on
  fatal error, and in the effect cleanup); on fire it runs the hook's fatal teardown (the
  unscoped-error branch: status 'error', reject/clear, free pending variations, terminate worker).
  Initial arming of BOTH indexed and variation watchdogs in `analyzeMove` is gated on
  `engineReadyRef.current`; pre-ready requests are armed by the `ready` case (`noteWorkerLiveness()`).
- Indexed: add `armWatchdog(moveIndex, requestId)` and a self-guarded `noteActivity(requestId)`
  mirroring the coordinator (same live-current gate via `latestRequestIds`/`requestIdToMoveIndex`/
  `resolvedIndices`). Keep the `if (mountToken.current !== token) return` guard inside watchdog
  setTimeout callbacks.
- Variations (review finding 2 — fully specified, matching the indexed hybrid):
  - Rename `variationDeadlineTimers` → `variationWatchdogTimers`.
  - Add `variationStarted: useRef<Set<string>>`.
  - `analyzeMove` (variation branch): arm a variation watchdog with the inactivity window instead of
    the fixed deadline; `started` defaults false.
  - On a variation's **own** activity (its `analysis-started`, `analysis-streaming` streamVar branch,
    or `analysis-progress`): `variationStarted.add(id)` and re-arm its watchdog.
  - Global liveness re-arms only NOT-started variations (id ∉ `variationStarted`) — a STARTED
    variation that goes silent still fails after its window even while other work progresses
    (consistent with the indexed model; this is the explicit decision finding 2 asked for).
  - **Terminal cleanup is preserved**: the existing variation teardown in the `analysis` case
    (`useMoveAnalysis.ts:526`) and the scoped-`error` case (619) still `clearVariationTimer(id)` +
    delete `pendingVariationPlies` + `setVariationStreamingEval(null)`; ADD `variationStarted.delete(id)`
    there and at every other variation-clear site (`failVariation`, `clearAnalysis`, fatal-error,
    unmount). No variation watchdog or `started` entry outlives its request.
- Unify the global liveness into a single `noteWorkerLiveness()` (bump queued indexed entries + bump
  not-started variations). `noteActivity(id)` is SELF-GUARDED exactly like the coordinator's (review
  round 3, finding 2): it RETURNS EARLY — doing nothing, NOT calling `noteWorkerLiveness()` — unless
  `id` is either (a) a live current indexed request (`requestIdToMoveIndex.get(id) === idx` &&
  `resolutionState.get(idx)?.requestId === id` && `latestRequestIds.get(idx) === id` &&
  `!resolvedIndices.has(idx)`) or (b) a still-pending variation (`pendingVariationPlies.current.has(id)`).
  For (a) mark the indexed entry `started` + re-arm it; for (b) `variationStarted.add(id)` + re-arm its
  watchdog; THEN `noteWorkerLiveness()`. This is essential because variation ids are deleted on
  terminal/timeout paths (`useMoveAnalysis.ts:251` `clearVariationTimer`, `:266` `failVariation`,
  `:526` the `analysis` case, scoped `error`): a late `analysis-progress` for a deleted variation must
  be inert and must NOT re-arm unrelated queued indexed/variation requests.
- `handleMessage`:
  - `case 'ready'`: KEEP the existing `if (s.status === 'error') break` guard FIRST
    (`useMoveAnalysis.ts:462`, review round 3 finding 3), THEN set `engineReadyRef.current = true`,
    clear `bootWatchdogTimer`, `setStatus('ready')`, `noteWorkerLiveness()`.
  - `analysis-started`: `noteActivity` (routes to indexed or variation own-re-arm).
  - `analysis-streaming`: `noteActivity` in the indexed branch; variation own-re-arm in the
    `streamVar` branch.
  - NEW `case 'analysis-progress'`: `noteActivity(message.id)`; `break`.
  - `analysis`: `noteActivity` before buffer/resolve (indexed); variation terminal cleanup unchanged.
  - `error` (scoped): `noteActivity` after guards (indexed); variation terminal cleanup unchanged.
- Rename indexed `deadlineTimer` clear sites (200, 239, 411, 725, 757) → `watchdogTimer`.

## Tests

### `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts`
NOTE: the inactivity watchdog is now armed only once the engine is ready, so every watchdog test
posts a `ready` worker message (`handleWorkerMessage({ data: { type: 'ready' } })`) after
`startSession` (before/after `analyzeMove`) to arm it. Audit any existing test that advances timers by
≥ `ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS` (20s) in 'booting' status without a `ready` — only the two rewritten
tests below do, and both now post `ready` (clearing the boot timer), so there is no collateral
boot-watchdog fatal.
- Rewrite "total-analysis deadline rejects a stalled worker..." (1432) → "inactivity watchdog rejects
  a silent worker": advance 200 (cache miss → released, no buffered worker), advance
  `ANALYSIS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` with no activity → `rejects /timed out/i`, `resolutionState.size === 0`.
- Rewrite "keeps a slow-but-finite worker analysis alive past the old 8s deadline" (1445) →
  "a progressing search survives past the window; only silence kills it": schedule, advance 200
  (release), then loop posting `analysis-progress(id)` every < window while advancing total > 2×window;
  assert entry still pending and `analysisMap` empty throughout; then `postWorker(id)` → resolves.
- NEW "a queued request is not failed while the worker progresses another (serial liveness)":
  schedule idx0 and idx1; post `analysis-started(id0)` + periodic `analysis-progress(id0)` spanning
  > window; assert idx1's entry persists (not failed); resolve idx0; then started+progress+analysis
  for idx1 → idx1 resolves.
- NEW "a started request that goes silent fails after one window": schedule idx0, advance 200
  (release), post `analysis-started(id0)`, advance window with no further activity → waiter rejects
  /timed out/, entry gone.
- NEW (review finding 4) "stale progress does NOT extend a queued watchdog": post `ready`; schedule
  idx1 (B, queued/not-started). Make a stale id A (e.g. schedule idx0 then supersede it, or fail it).
  Advance to just before B's window, deliver `analysis-progress(A-stale)`, advance past B's ORIGINAL
  window → B fails at its original window (the stale ping did not re-arm it). Control: the "queued not
  failed" test above proves a LIVE ping DOES re-arm — together they pin the self-guard.
- NEW (review round 2, finding 1) "a request scheduled before `ready` is not failed during a slow
  boot": `startSession` (status booting, engine not ready), `analyzeMove(idx0)` (no watchdog armed),
  advance > `ANALYSIS_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` but < `ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS` → entry still pending,
  `analysisMap` empty, status not 'error'. Then post `ready` (arms it) + progress/`analysis` → resolves.
- NEW (review round 2, finding 1) "a silent boot fails via the boot watchdog": `startSession`,
  `analyzeMove(idx0)`, `waitForAnalysis(0)`, advance `ANALYSIS_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS` with NO `ready` →
  status 'error' and the waiter rejects (no hang).

### `src/workers/analysisWorker.test.ts`
- NEW "emits analysis-progress during the root search (root-phase liveness)": run the ready
  handshake, send `analyze-move`, auto-answer the reset readyok, then drive
  `engineMessageHandler('info depth 5 score cp 20 pv e2e4')` BEFORE any `bestmove` → assert
  `postMessageMock` called with `{ type: 'analysis-progress', id }`. Proves the previously-silent
  root phase now surfaces activity.
- NEW (review round 3, finding 1) "emits analysis-progress on bestmove (phase-boundary liveness)":
  drive the root search's `bestmove` and assert a `{ type: 'analysis-progress', id }` ping is posted
  even with no surrounding info line. (Optionally also assert the per-request reset `readyok` pings.)
- NEW (optional, fake timers) throttle: two rapid info lines → one progress; advance >250ms +
  another info → second progress.
- Confirm existing worker tests are unaffected (they use specific `toHaveBeenCalledWith` /
  `not.toHaveBeenCalledWith` matchers, so extra progress messages don't break them).

### `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.test.ts`
- Update variation-timeout test (380): silence for the new window still fires `onVariationError`;
  fix the comment/`30_000` → new constant.
- NEW: a progressing variation (periodic `analysis-progress`/`analysis-streaming`) survives past the
  window. NEW: a started-but-silent variation still fails after its window even while an indexed
  request progresses (pins the finding-2 decision). NEW: an indexed watchdog is reset by `analysis-progress`.
- NEW (review round 3, finding 2) "stale variation progress does NOT extend queued work": start a
  variation, drive it to a terminal/timeout so its id is deleted from `pendingVariationPlies`, then
  with a separate queued indexed request (or queued variation) present, deliver a late
  `analysis-progress(deleted-variation-id)` and assert the queued request is NOT re-armed (it fails
  at its original window). Pins the hook's self-guard.
- NEW (review round 2, finding 3) "a QUEUED variation survives behind a progressing indexed request":
  post `ready`; `analyzeMove` an indexed move (idx0) and a variation (not started); drive idx0's
  `analysis-started` + periodic `analysis-progress(id0)` spanning > the inactivity window while the
  variation stays silent/not-started; assert `onVariationError` is NOT called during that span (the
  not-started variation is kept alive by global serial-worker liveness). Then start + resolve the
  variation. Distinct from the started-but-silent variation test, which asserts the opposite.

## Validation
- `npx tsc -b` — strict; the new `analysis-progress` variant forces a handled `case` in BOTH the
  coordinator and hook switches (`message satisfies never`).
- Targeted vitest, run in isolation (pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load):
  `GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts`, `useMoveAnalysis.test.ts`, `analysisWorker.test.ts`.
- Real-browser Stockfish smoke test (per the worker's pinned-version contract): confirm a slow root
  search keeps progress flowing so the 8s window is never tripped; raise to 10s only if real info
  cadence proves sparse.

## Risks / decisions
- Full replacement of the fixed deadline — no absolute ceiling retained (per bead). The serial-worker
  liveness reset means a perpetually-busy worker can keep a queued request alive a long time; that is
  the DESIRED behavior (queued ≠ hung).
- 8s window is a single tunable. First-request engine boot is fully decoupled (Engine-boot strategy):
  the inactivity timer is armed only post-`ready`, and a separate 20s boot backstop bounds a hung
  boot — so a slow-but-progressing boot never false-fails and a silent boot still fails (not hangs).
- Worker→coordinator message volume bounded by the 250ms worker-side progress throttle.
- `lastStreamingUpdateMs` remains display-only and never touches the watchdog.

## Review refinements (from g-analysis-watchdog review)
1. Stale progress can't keep queued work alive: `noteActivity` is self-guarded to the live current
   request, so a superseded/failed/resolved/discarded id never reaches `bumpQueuedWatchdogs`.
2. Variation watchdog fully specified: `variationWatchdogTimers` + `variationStarted`, started/queued
   split matching indexed, terminal cleanup preserved on final `analysis` and scoped `error` (plus a
   `variationStarted.delete` at every clear site); a started variation is NOT re-armed by unrelated
   global liveness.
3. Progress contract matches the parser: `analysis-progress` carries no `depth`; emitted on any
   non-null `parseUciInfoLine` (depth/score/pv) — no misleading `depth: 0`.
4. Stale-progress test added (coordinator) asserting a queued watchdog is not extended by a
   stale/superseded request's late `analysis-progress`.

## Review refinements (round 2)
1. Engine boot decoupled from the inactivity window: `engineReady` gate (arm only post-`ready`) +
   a 20s `bootWatchdogTimer` backstop (fatal on a silent boot). No pre-`ready` false-fail; a hung
   boot fails rather than hangs. Mirrored in the hook (`engineReadyRef` + boot timer). New coordinator
   tests for slow-boot-survives and silent-boot-fails; watchdog tests now post `ready` to arm.
2. `lastProgressPostMs` initializes and resets to `Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` (not `0`) so the first
   progress ping always fires, including under fake timers where `Date.now()` starts at 0.
3. Hook test added for a QUEUED variation surviving behind a progressing indexed request (pins the
   "global liveness re-arms not-started variations" branch).

## Review refinements (round 3)
1. Worker liveness no longer misses non-info progress: unthrottled `analysis-progress` pings at the
   two phase boundaries — live per-request reset `readyok` and each `bestmove` — keyed by
   `activeAnalysisId`, skipped when canceled. Covers the bestmove-just-before-window gap. Worker test
   added for bestmove-phase liveness.
2. Hook `noteActivity` is now explicitly self-guarded: it returns early (no own re-arm, no
   `noteWorkerLiveness()`) unless the id is a live current indexed request OR a still-pending
   variation — so a late progress for a deleted/terminal variation can't re-arm unrelated queued
   work. Hook stale-progress test added.
3. Both `ready` handlers keep the fatal-error guard FIRST (`if status === 'error' break`) before the
   new engineReady/boot-timer/bump logic, so a stray late `ready` (incl. after the boot-timeout fatal
   path) can't revive a dead worker. Worker-replacement listener removal makes a generation check
   unnecessary.

title: Position analysis Phase 6: drill grading semantics (strictness-0 + CP eval-loss + mate fallback)
description:
Sub-task of epic **g-position-analysis** — Phase 6 of the master plan (see the parent epic's DESIGN → "Drill Semantics And g-l02q Ordering" and "Eval-Loss Ownership And Mate Handling"; the full plan stays in the parent).

## Goal

Update drill grading so strictness-0 exact-best depends only on trusted position truth, and threshold/eval-loss grading derives loss per grain from trusted position best eval + trusted move played eval.

## Work

1. **Strictness 0 exact-best**: compare the played move to `position_analysis.best_move_uci` only. With canonical winner `c2c4`, c4 passes and Bf4 fails, independent of whether a trusted move row exists. Missing/untrusted move evidence must NOT block a strictness-0 verdict when the position row is trusted.
2. **Intentional ordering change in `gradeDrillMove`** (`src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`): today it returns `unavailable` when `evalLoss(delta) === null` BEFORE checking `strictnessCp <= 0`. The g-l02q comment in `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` relies on that ordering to avoid false-passing when `best_move_uci` is null and `bestMove` falls back to the played move. Under the split, run the best-move check against trusted position evidence independent of move-eval availability, and update the g-l02q reasoning so implementers do not preserve the old ordering by accident.
3. **Threshold / eval-loss (CP-only this phase)**: derive loss at read time from `position_analysis.best_eval` + trusted move `played_eval`, using the same side-to-move-relative + clamp-to-zero rule as the current v2 validator:
   - White to move: `max(best_eval - played_eval, 0)`
   - Black to move: `max(played_eval - best_eval, 0)` (white-relative CP).
4. **Mate handling**: CP-vs-mate, mate-vs-CP, and mate-vs-mate do NOT derive a numeric eval loss in this migration — return unavailable or fall back to local worker recompute for threshold grading. Exact-best and tree ranking may still use trusted position `best_move_uci` / `best_eval_mate`.
5. If `analysis_cache.eval_delta` is retained, document it as a canonical-run snapshot with metadata proving it was computed against the same position row/profile. Browser snapshots must not drive strict position outcomes.

## Acceptance

Strictness-0 exact-best compares against trusted `position_analysis.best_move_uci` only and is not blocked by missing/untrusted move evidence. `gradeDrillMove` ordering is intentionally changed and the g-l02q reasoning updated. Threshold grading derives CP-only loss from trusted position + move evidence. Mate-bearing rows fall back/unavailable for threshold grading. Tests cover strictness-0 with missing trusted move evidence, CP-only derivation, and mate fallback behavior.
design:
# Phase 6 — Drill grading semantics (strictness-0 + CP eval-loss + mate fallback)

## Chosen architecture (per owner direction): split cache use BY CONSUMER PURPOSE

Do NOT relax the shared cache-hit gate. The normal published `AnalysisResult` path stays
strict and keeps feeding regular-game blunder detection, SRS, uploads, and the review
board. Strictness-0 exact-best AND the Phase-6 threshold loss read a SEPARATE, drill-only
side channel ("drill truth"), populated only from CACHE evidence.

```
canPublishAnalysisResult = trusted position && trusted move evidence && usable CP loss
canGradeStrictness0      = trusted position best_move_uci exists   (NO PV requirement)
canDeriveThresholdLossCP = trusted position CP best_eval && trusted move CP played_eval
                           && both grains pure-CP (no mate fields) && SAME search strength
                           -> computed on the BACKEND, never on the frontend
```

Hard rule: a position-only hit must NOT call `resolveAnalysisResult`, emit an
`AnalysisOutcome`, mark uploads dirty, or cancel the worker. It only fulfills drill truth.

## Incorporated review findings

**v2:** (1) narrow `isTrustedExactBestHit` (vs PV-requiring `isTrustedPositionHit`,
`analysisUtils.ts:307,:346`); (2) requestId/generation-bound side-channel waiters (vs
`AnalysisWaiter` `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:74,:750`); (3) lifecycle clearing in
per-index `pruneFromMoveIndex` (`:386`) + `clearAnalysis` (`:757`) + global resets;
(4) keep the published result on the co-computed snapshot (`eval_delta` +
`classification`), derive drill loss out-of-band; (5) ChessGame cutover tests
(`ChessGame.test.tsx:137,:3739`).

**v3:** (6) never mix canonical position eval with local-worker played eval — derive only
from trusted-cache grains.

**v4 (threshold loss moves to the BACKEND — resolves the three new findings):**
7. **Don't depend on the worker when the cache is sufficient.** A split move row can be
   trusted-CP yet carry no publishable `eval_delta` (post-split move-complete rows don't
   satisfy v2's cross-grain `eval_delta` invariant), so the published gate
   (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1190` `hasCpEvalLoss`) releases to the worker. The drill
   threshold must NOT wait on that worker: `waitForDrillGrade` waits for DRILL TRUTH
   first and only falls back to `waitForAnalysis` when no cache loss exists.
8. **Mate-bearing rows must fall back even when a CP field is also present.** Producers
   store mate AND a mate->CP conversion in the same row
   (`precompute_openings.py:304,:474`), so "finite CP" alone is insufficient. The loss is
   emitted ONLY when BOTH grains have null mate fields.
9. **Profile compatibility must be proven.** `TrustedPosition` drops profile identity
   (`position_analysis_repo.py:270`) and the lookup's `analysis_profile_id` is move-row
   metadata; there are multiple active authoritative profiles
   (`analysis_profiles.py:372` AUTHORITATIVE_PROFILE_PRIORITY). Subtracting evals across
   different-strength profiles is invalid. The backend computes the loss ONLY when
   `compare_search_strength(position_profile, move_profile) == EQUAL`
   (`analysis_profiles.py:388`; `engine_build` is intentionally NOT strength-invariant, so
   the two canonical profiles stay comparable).
   Consequence: the frontend no longer does eval arithmetic, so the `moverColor` param is
   dropped (perspective + sign live in the backend, mirroring `precompute_openings.py:474`).

**v5 (fast-settlement preamble — don't copy waitForAnalysis's pending reject):**
10. `resolveAnalysisResult` deletes `pendingMoveIndices`/`pendingMeta`/`resolutionState`
    on any terminal resolution (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1102-1105`) but leaves
    `latestRequestIds` intact and never touches `drillTruth`. A cache/worker result can
    settle BEFORE `waitForDrillGrade` is even called. So `waitForDrillGrade` must NOT
    mirror `waitForAnalysis`'s `!pendingMoveIndices.has(requestId)` reject (`:744-745`) —
    that would reject although `drillTruth` (and `analysisMap`) hold the data. Custom
    preamble: capture `latestRequestIds` + `generation`, read already-settled `drillTruth`
    first, and delegate the worker branch to `waitForAnalysis` (whose own `analysisMap`
    fast path `:733-735` returns settled results). Reject ONLY when there is no current
    request AND no settled data — and that reject is delegated to `waitForAnalysis`.

**v6 (SPEC scope + backend PV semantics):**
11. **SPEC narrative deferred to g-position-analysis.8.** SPEC §6.4.6 "Analysis cache
    race" (`SPEC.md:1158`) still describes the pre-trust-gate behavior ("resolves
    immediately" when `classification`/`eval_delta` present) and the old `GET
    /api/analysis-cache` shape — already stale post Phase 4/5, and Phase 6 changes it
    again (drill-truth side channel beside the published path, position-only lookup hits,
    `position_eval_loss_cp`). Phase 6 does NOT rewrite SPEC prose; it defers to
    g-position-analysis.8 (the SPEC phase) and enumerates the Phase-6 items there so they
    are not lost. Step 6 below is an inline CODE-COMMENT note on `eval_delta`, not a SPEC
    edit.
12. **"No PV requirement" is FRONTEND-only.** `isTrustedExactBestHit` deliberately does
    NOT re-check the PV that `isTrustedPositionHit`/`canResolvePositionAnalysis` check —
    drill exact-best only compares the played move to `best_move_uci`. This is NOT a
    relaxation of backend trust: `position_trusted` REMAINS gated on position-complete-v1,
    which REQUIRES a multi-move PV (`evidence_contracts.py:120` `_validate_position_
    complete` -> `_pv_first_equals_best`). A `position_trusted` row already guarantees a
    valid PV server-side; do NOT weaken `_validate_position_complete`.

---

## Verified current state (file:line)

- Drill grade call site `ChessGame.tsx:1090/:1115`; `unavailable`->recovery (`:1120`);
  `fail`->`stopPostRootDrillForAccuracy` (`:1129`) reads only `analysis.bestMove` (`:1061`).
- `gradeDrillMove` (`analysisUtils.ts:223`) gates `evalLoss(delta)===null` BEFORE
  `strictnessCp<=0` (`:232-234`).
- Published gate (`GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1190-1209`): cache-resolve iff
  `isTrustedPositionHit && isTrustedMoveHit && hasCpEvalLoss`; else `releaseFallback`; on
  resolve cancels worker (`:1223`). `fromCachedAnalysis:174` -> `delta=cached.eval_delta`
  (`:185`), `classification`/`blunder`/`recordable` (`:186-192`), `bestMove =
  cached.best_move_uci ?? move` (`:201`).
- Waiters request-bound (`:74,:732-754`); `rejectAnalysisWaiters` (`:461`); per-index
  reject in `pruneFromMoveIndex` (`:410`).
- Backend `/api/analysis/lookup` (`analysis.py:169-205`) emits only when an exact
  `(fen,move_uci)` row exists; position-only suppressed (`:170-173`); `move_san` required
  (`:42`); resolver batched (`position_analysis_repo.py:353`); `TrustedPosition` carries
  best_* only, no profile (`:270`). Suppression pinned by `test_analysis_cache_api.py:888`.
- Loss formula (mover-relative, clamped, white-relative inputs):
  `precompute_openings.py:474` `delta = best-played (white) | played-best (black); max(.,0)`.

---

## Changes

### 1. Backend — position-only hits + backend-derived threshold loss

`backend/app/position_analysis_repo.py`:
- Add `analysis_profile_id: str | None` to `TrustedPosition` (`:270`); populate it in the
  builder (`:344`) from the storage winner row / the legacy-v2 projection row's profile.

`backend/app/api/analysis.py`:
- `CachedAnalysisResult.move_san`: `str` -> `str | None = None` (`:42`).
- Add `position_eval_loss_cp: int | None = None` (mover-relative, clamped >=0, backend-
  computed trusted CP loss; null unless all guards pass).
- `lookup_analysis`: normalize ALL requested FENs (not only `:161`'s move-row subset);
  single batched `resolve_trusted_positions` (no N+1).
- Emission loop (`:169`): `row = row_map.get(...)`, `tp = resolved.get(norm)`:
  - `row is not None` -> emit as today PLUS compute `position_eval_loss_cp` when ALL hold:
    - `move_trusted` (already computed) AND `tp is not None` (position_trusted);
    - pure CP both grains: `tp.best_eval is not None and tp.best_eval_mate is None and
      row.played_eval is not None and row.played_eval_mate is None` (finding #8);
    - strength-compatible: `pp = get_profile(tp.analysis_profile_id)`, `mp =
      get_profile(row.analysis_profile_id)`; both non-None and
      `compare_search_strength(pp, mp) == EQUAL` (finding #9);
    - then `mover = 'white' if fen.split()[1]=='w' else 'black'`;
      `loss = tp.best_eval - row.played_eval if mover=='white' else row.played_eval -
      tp.best_eval`; `position_eval_loss_cp = max(loss, 0)`. Else `None`.
  - `row is None and tp is not None` -> POSITION-ONLY: position fields from `tp`,
    `position_trusted=True`, `position_eval_loss_cp=None`; move grain null/untrusted
    (`move_san=None`, `played_eval=None`, `played_eval_mate=None`, `eval_delta=None`,
    `classification=None`, `move_trusted=False`, `authoritative/contract_satisfied/
    trusted_for_resolution=False`).
  - both None -> skip.
- Keep slow-log accounting (`:209`).

### 2. Frontend wire type (`src/utils/api.ts`)

- `CachedAnalysis.move_san: string` -> `string | null` (`:875`).
- Add `position_eval_loss_cp: number | null` (POSITION+MOVE-grain backend-derived trusted
  CP loss; null when un-derivable). Doc-block note.

### 3. Frontend guards (`src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`)

- New `isTrustedExactBestHit(input) = input.position_trusted === true &&
  input.best_move_uci != null`. FRONTEND-only looser guard (finding #12): no PV RE-check,
  because backend `position_trusted` (position-complete-v1) already guarantees the PV.
  Comment it so nobody "tightens" it to `isTrustedPositionHit` or relaxes backend trust.
- `gradeDrillMove` reorder (`:223`):
  ```ts
  if (strictnessCp <= 0) return isBestMove ? 'pass' : 'fail'   // caller supplies TRUSTED isBestMove
  if (evalLoss(delta) === null) return 'unavailable'
  return failsDrill(delta, strictnessCp) ? 'fail' : 'pass'
  ```
  Rewrite `:228-231`: trust of `isBestMove` is the caller's contract (`waitForDrillGrade`).

### 4. Coordinator — drill-truth side channel + `waitForDrillGrade`
   (`src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`)

State (request-bound):
```ts
type DrillTruth = { best_move_uci: string; positionEvalLossCp: number | null }
private drillTruth = new Map<number, { requestId: string; truth: DrillTruth | null }>()
private drillTruthWaiters = new Map<number, Set<DrillTruthWaiter>>()
// DrillTruthWaiter = { generation; requestId; resolve(t: DrillTruth | null); reject(e) }
```
Record present = settled for that requestId (`truth` set, or `null` = no trusted position).

Populate (cache `.then` loop, `:1179`, BEFORE the published gate `:1190`):
- `if (cached && isTrustedExactBestHit(cached))` record `{requestId: pending.requestId,
  truth: {best_move_uci: cached.best_move_uci, positionEvalLossCp:
  cached.position_eval_loss_cp ?? null}}`; fulfill matching waiters. Pure side-channel
  write — must NOT touch resolutionState/resolvedIndices/worker/uploads/outcomes; the
  existing published gate runs unchanged after.

Settle (so a waiter never hangs): at every cache-settlement point set `null` for the
requestId if absent + drain waiters — full-resolve (`:1220`), `releaseFallback` (`:1044`:
untrusted/cache-miss/cache-error `:1240`/cache-timeout `:1167`). Guard on
`sessionGeneration` (`:1177`).

Public method (NO moverColor — finding #9):
```ts
waitForDrillGrade(moveIndex, playedMoveUci, strictnessCp): Promise<DrillGrade>
// DrillGrade = { grade: MoveGrade; bestMove: string | null; source: 'position' | 'worker' }
```
CUSTOM preamble (NOT a mirror of `waitForAnalysis` — finding #10): `const generation =
this.sessionGeneration`; `const requestId = this.latestRequestIds.get(moveIndex)` (may
still be set after a terminal resolution; may be undefined after prune/clear). Do NOT
reject on missing pending state here — `drillTruth`/`analysisMap` may already hold the
result. Then DRILL TRUTH FIRST for BOTH branches (finding #7):
- `const t = await waitForDrillTruth(moveIndex, requestId, generation)`.
- `strictnessCp <= 0`:
  - `t` present -> `{ grade: gradeDrillMove(null, 0, playedMoveUci === t.best_move_uci),
    bestMove: t.best_move_uci, source: 'position' }`.
  - `t` null -> worker fallback (below).
- `strictnessCp > 0`:
  - `t && t.positionEvalLossCp != null` -> `{ grade:
    gradeDrillMove(t.positionEvalLossCp, strictnessCp, playedMoveUci === t.best_move_uci),
    bestMove: t.best_move_uci, source: 'position' }`. (No worker dependency; mate/cross-
    profile already excluded by the backend -> positionEvalLossCp null.)
  - else -> worker fallback (below).
- worker fallback: `const a = await waitForAnalysis(moveIndex)`; `{ grade:
  gradeDrillMove(a.delta, strictnessCp, a.bestMove === playedMoveUci), bestMove:
  a.bestMove, source: 'worker' }`. `waitForAnalysis` returns a SETTLED result via its own
  `analysisMap` fast path (`:733-735`) and rejects only when nothing is
  scheduled/pending — so the only reject path fires when there is no current request AND
  no settled data (handled by ChessGame's try/catch -> recovery).
- `waitForDrillTruth(idx, requestId, generation)` (settled-aware):
  - `const rec = this.drillTruth.get(idx)`: if present, resolve immediately with
    `rec.truth` (FAST PATH; supersession/clear remove stale records, so a present record
    is always current — no requestId match needed here).
  - else if `requestId` is undefined (nothing pending, nothing settled): resolve `null`
    (caller falls back to `waitForAnalysis`).
  - else: register a `(generation, requestId)`-bound waiter (settle/reject by requestId;
    a DIFFERENT settling/superseding requestId rejects it).

`fromCachedAnalysis` (`:201`): drop `?? move` — the published gate guarantees
`best_move_uci` non-null; use it directly; NEVER let `bestMove ?? playedMove` reach a
published result. Update g-l02q comment (`:197-200`). Published `delta`/`classification`
UNCHANGED.

Lifecycle (finding #3): add `rejectDrillTruthWaiters(error)` (mirrors `:461`) + per-
`(idx,requestId)` rejection; clear `drillTruth` + drain waiters in `pruneFromMoveIndex`
(`:386`, "Analysis reverted"), `clearAnalysis` (`:757`, "Analysis cleared"),
`clearAllResolutionState` (`:722`), session change (`:527`), session cleared (`:572`),
worker restart (`:708`), destroy (`:1400`), supersession in `analyzeMove` (`:639-644`).

### 5. ChessGame call site (`src/components/ChessGame.tsx`)

- Replace `waitForAnalysis` + `gradeDrillMove` (`:1090,:1115`) with `const drill = await
  coordinator.waitForDrillGrade(result.moveIndex, result.moveUci, threshold)` in the same
  try/catch -> recovery. Route on `drill.grade` as today.
- `stopPostRootDrillForAccuracy` (`:1045`): take `bestMove: string | null` instead of the
  full `analysis`; build `suggestionUcis` from it (`:1061`).
- Drill-recovery `waitForAnalysis(failedMoveIndex)` (`:754`) stays `waitForAnalysis`.

### 6. eval_delta documentation (work item 5) — inline code comment only

Document `analysis_cache.eval_delta` (in code, at `fromCachedAnalysis` and the gate) as a
canonical-run snapshot for blunder/SRS/display; the DRILL threshold loss is the
backend-derived `position_eval_loss_cp` (trusted, same-strength, CP-only), never a
browser/worker snapshot. SPEC.md prose is NOT edited here — deferred to
g-position-analysis.8 (finding #11).

---

## Invariants / guardrails

- Position-only hits never publish.
- Threshold loss is BACKEND-derived only from same-strength, pure-CP, trusted position +
  trusted move grains; null otherwise. Frontend does no eval arithmetic.
- Drill threshold never waits on the worker when a cache loss exists (drill-truth-first).
- Drill truth + waiters are `(moveIndex, requestId, generation)`-bound.
- `bestMove` for strictness-0 is trusted position truth or an honest worker best move —
  never `?? playedMove`.
- Published `AnalysisResult` stays internally consistent (snapshot delta + classification
  co-computed); Phase 6 does not derive delta into it.
- Drill truth never outlives its session/request; `waitForDrillGrade` cannot hang.
- `waitForDrillGrade` works whether called before OR after settlement: a present
  `drillTruth` record is always current (supersession/clear remove stale ones), and the
  worker branch reuses `waitForAnalysis`'s settled fast path; it rejects only when there
  is no current request and no settled data.

---

## Test plan

Backend (`backend/test_analysis_cache_api.py`):
- Replace `test_lookup_position_only_no_move_row_suppressed` (`:888`) ->
  `..._emits_position_grain` (position_trusted True, best_* set, move grain null,
  `position_eval_loss_cp` None).
- Keep `test_lookup_move_only_untrusted_position_null` (`:865`) + both-grains (`:838`).
- `position_eval_loss_cp`: emitted for trusted pos CP + trusted move CP SAME profile
  (white and black to move, sign correct); NULL when (a) either grain has a mate field
  set even though CP is present (finding #8), (b) profiles `compare_search_strength !=
  EQUAL` (finding #9), (c) move untrusted, (d) position-only (no move row).
- Batch [position-only, move+position, miss] -> correct shapes; single resolver call.

Frontend `src/workers/analysisUtils.test.ts` (`:507`):
- `isTrustedExactBestHit` true with no PV; false when untrusted/null best.
- `gradeDrillMove(null,0,true)='pass'`, `(null,0,false)='fail'`, `(NaN,0,true)='pass'`;
  existing finite-delta (`:516-520`) + threshold (`:508-513`) stay green.

Frontend `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts`:
- strictness-0, POSITION-ONLY hit: pass/fail by best move; ASSERT no published result / no
  outcome / worker not cancelled / uploads not dirtied.
- strictness-0, no trusted position: worker fallback; drill truth settles null (no hang).
- strictness>0, drill truth with `positionEvalLossCp` set: grades from it, `source:
  'position'`, WITHOUT awaiting the worker (finding #7 — e.g. published path released to
  worker due to missing `eval_delta`, drill grade still resolves from cache).
- strictness>0, `positionEvalLossCp` null (mate/cross-profile/untrusted move): worker
  fallback uses `a.delta`.
- **Fast settlement (finding #10): call `waitForDrillGrade` AFTER the cache/worker result
  has already settled (pending state torn down). It must still grade — from settled
  `drillTruth` (position source) or from the `analysisMap` result via `waitForAnalysis`
  (worker source) — and must NOT reject "not pending".**
- Published path: position-only -> releaseFallback (worker publishes) + drill truth
  recorded; full-trust -> publishes from cache + records drill truth; published
  delta/classification unchanged.
- Race/lifecycle: re-`analyzeMove` same index rejects the old drill-truth waiter;
  `pruneFromMoveIndex(k)` + `clearAnalysis` clear/drain drill truth + reject waiters.

Frontend `src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx`:
- Add `waitForDrillGrade` to `mockCoordinator` (`:135`); migrate post-root grading sites
  (`:3739` matrix; `:565,:760,:857,:1392`) to it; keep `waitForAnalysis` for recovery
  (`:754`). New: strictness-0 `{grade:'fail', bestMove:'c2c4', source:'position'}` ->
  `suggestionUcis: ['c2c4']`; `{grade:'pass', source:'position'}` -> advances.

---

## Sequencing (separable commits, all within Phase 6)

1. Backend: un-suppress position-only + `TrustedPosition.analysis_profile_id` +
   `position_eval_loss_cp` (strength/mate-guarded) + `move_san` optional + backend tests.
2. `isTrustedExactBestHit` + `gradeDrillMove` reorder + unit tests.
3. Wire type (`position_eval_loss_cp`) + drill-truth side channel + `waitForDrillGrade`
   (both strictness branches) + lifecycle clearing + ChessGame cutover + coordinator/

(strictness-0 and strictness>0 now share the same drill-truth-first path, so the prior
4th commit folds into commit 3; the only remaining backend dependency is commit 1.)

---

## Out of scope / deferred

Phase 7 (consumer audit):
- `useMoveAnalysis.ts` / review board: gate + `fromCachedAnalysis` left strict/unchanged.
- SRS/recordable trusted-loss derivation on the published path (kept on snapshot).

Phase 8 / g-position-analysis.8 (SPEC) — record these Phase-6 deltas in that bead so the
stale doc is knowingly tracked (finding #11):
- SPEC §6.4.6 "Analysis cache race" (`SPEC.md:1158`): rewrite for the trust-gated
  published path + the drill-only truth side channel; fix `GET /api/analysis-cache` ->

- `/api/analysis/lookup` shape: position-only hits (trusted position, no move row) +

- Eval-loss ownership: drill threshold loss is backend-derived `position_eval_loss_cp`;
