title: Position analysis Phase 5: frontend wire types + grain-specific cache guards
description:
Sub-task of epic **g-position-analysis** — Phase 5 of the master plan (see the parent epic's DESIGN → "Wire And Frontend Contract"; the full plan stays in the parent).

## Goal

Update frontend wire types and cache guards as plumbing for the new split payload. No frontend module should treat one cached move row as both position truth and move truth.

## Work

1. `src/utils/api.ts` — `CachedAnalysis`: represent separate position and move payloads (or explicitly mark transitional flattened fields as merged/deprecated). Replace `trusted_for_resolution` with `position_trusted` and `move_trusted`.
2. `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts` — split `canResolveCachedAnalysis` into position and move guards:
   - PV guard (`best_move_uci` + multi-move `best_line_uci`) belongs to the position payload.
   - classification/eval-loss guard belongs to the move payload.
   - `isTrustedCacheHit` becomes grain-specific or is removed.
3. `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` and `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts` — preserve the existing protection that untrusted `analysis/lookup` rows do not drive live drill grading, but stop deriving `bestMove` from a move row once the split payload exists. Exact-best uses the trusted position payload; move payloads provide played-move facts.
4. `src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts` — stop building untrusted `PositionAnalysis` best-move seeds from upload rows without a trust signal.
5. Migrate frontend tests that manufacture `trusted_for_resolution: true` to the new grain-specific trust fields.

Note: `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx` ordering itself is tracked by **g-54h5**; this phase only needs to deliver `position_trusted` to it.

## Acceptance

`src/utils/api.ts`, `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`, `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`, `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts`, and `sessionUpload.ts` no longer treat one cached move row as both position and move truth. `trusted_for_resolution` is replaced by `position_trusted` / `move_trusted`. Tests updated to the new trust fields.
design:
# Phase 5 — Frontend wire types + grain-specific cache guards

Plumbing for the position/move grain split. No frontend module may treat one
cached move row as both position truth and move truth. Replace the single
`trusted_for_resolution` gate with independent `position_trusted` / `move_trusted`
decisions, and separate backend TRUST from the frontend's transitional CP-only
grading usability. This phase is type/guard plumbing only — drill grading
semantics (strictness-0 from position alone, CP eval-loss derivation, mate
fallback) AND position-only lookup consumption are Phase 6; AnalysisBoard
trust-gating is g-54h5; SPEC.md is Phase 8.

## Starting state (already delivered by Phase 4, commit a14c880)

Backend already emits the split shape; the frontend just hasn't consumed it.

- `/api/analysis/lookup` `CachedAnalysisResult` returns:
  - POSITION grain (resolver-derived by NORMALIZED FEN, `null` when no trusted
    position — NEVER copied from the move row): `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`,
    `best_line_uci`, `best_eval` (white-relative), `best_eval_mate`.
  - MOVE grain (exact `(fen, move_uci)` row): `played_eval`, `played_eval_mate`,
    `eval_delta`, `classification`, `move_san`.
  - Flags: `position_trusted` (trusted position resolved → drives `best_*`),
    `move_trusted` (move row passes the move-grain gate).
  - `trusted_for_resolution` kept unchanged transitionally.
  - A result is emitted ONLY when an exact `(fen, move_uci)` move row exists;
    position-only hits (storage row, no move row) are intentionally suppressed
    (`analysis.py` loop; pinned by `test_lookup_position_only_no_move_row_suppressed`,
    which asserts `results == {}`). Un-suppressing this is NOT a Phase 5 task — see
    Out of scope.
- `/api/session/{id}/analysis` `PositionAnalysis` carries a REQUIRED
  `position_trusted: bool`, keyed by full `fen_before`; `best_move_eval_cp` is
  side-to-move-relative.

IMPORTANT backend semantics (drive the guard design below):
- `move-complete-v1` (`evidence_contracts.py _validate_move_complete`) requires an
  enum-valid `classification` AND a usable played eval that may be CP
  (`played_eval`) OR mate (`played_eval_mate`). It DELIBERATELY does NOT require
  `eval_delta`. So `move_trusted === true` is possible with `eval_delta` null
  (mate-only rows) — proven by `test_lookup_move_complete_mate_only_contract_satisfied`.
- The current frontend grades drills from a CP `delta` only (`gradeDrillMove`,
  `evalLoss`). A mate-only row has no CP delta, so the live path must still fall
  back to the worker for those rows until Phase 6 adds mate-aware grading. That
  "can I grade from a cached CP delta right now?" check is SEPARATE from move trust.

The frontend is still on the legacy single flag: `api.ts CachedAnalysis` lacks
`best_eval_mate`/`position_trusted`/`move_trusted`; `PositionAnalysis` lacks
`position_trusted`; `analysisUtils` has one `canResolveCachedAnalysis` (which
conflates structure with a CP-delta requirement) + `isTrustedCacheHit`; both
live-drill consumers (`GameAnalysisCoordinator`, `useMoveAnalysis`) gate on
`isTrustedCacheHit`.

## Data-flow recap (what each consumer does today)

- Live drill cache path (identical in both `flushCacheLookups`): `lookupAnalysisCache`
  → per row `if (!cached || !isTrustedCacheHit(cached)) releaseFallback(...)`, else
  `fromCachedAnalysis` resolves + cancels the worker. A cache row replaces the
  worker only when the gate passes; otherwise the worker result wins. This
  "untrusted rows do not drive live grading" protection MUST be preserved, AND the
  current effect (mate-only / delta-less rows fall back to the worker) MUST be
  preserved.
- `fromCachedAnalysis` builds the combined `AnalysisResult`:
  `bestMove: cached.best_move_uci ?? move`, `bestEval` from `cached.best_eval`,
  `playedEval`/`playedEvalMate` from move grain, `delta`/`classification` move grain.
- `AnalysisBoard.tsx` reads `positionAnalysis?.[displayedFen]` →
  `best_move_uci`/`best_line_uci`/`best_move_eval_cp`; does NOT read
  `position_trusted` yet (g-54h5). Fed by backend `analysis.position_analysis`
  (GameAnalysisPage/HistoryPage/BlundersPage) and local `snapshot.positionAnalysis`
  (DrillAnalysisPage).
- `sessionUpload.buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot` constructs `PositionAnalysis` seeds
  from LOCAL worker results — untrusted-as-position-truth, no backend trust signal.

## Changes

### 1. `src/utils/api.ts`
- `CachedAnalysis`: add `best_eval_mate: number | null`; add
  `position_trusted: boolean` and `move_trusted: boolean`; re-doc the flattened
  best-* fields as POSITION grain (resolver-derived, null when untrusted); mark
  `trusted_for_resolution?: boolean` `@deprecated` (backend still emits it; the
  frontend STOPS reading it).
- `PositionAnalysis`: add REQUIRED `position_trusted: boolean` (matches the backend
  pydantic model, never defaulted).

### 2. `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`
Separate THREE concerns: backend trust (the two flags), structural renderability
(grain guards mirroring the backend grain contracts), and the transitional
CP-only grading usability gate.
- Split `canResolveCachedAnalysis` (remove it) into two STRUCTURE guards:
  - `canResolvePositionAnalysis({ best_move_uci, best_line_uci })`: `best_move_uci`
    present AND `Array.isArray(best_line_uci)` AND `length > 1` AND
    `best_line_uci[0] === best_move_uci`. (PV = position grain.)
  - `canResolveMoveAnalysis({ classification, played_eval, played_eval_mate })`:
    `isMoveClassification` AND (finite `played_eval` OR finite `played_eval_mate`).
    Mirrors `move-complete-v1`. DOES NOT require `eval_delta` (Finding 2 fix).
- Grain trust guards (backend owns trust; frontend re-checks structure only):
  - `isTrustedPositionHit({ position_trusted, best_move_uci, best_line_uci })` =
    `position_trusted === true && canResolvePositionAnalysis(...)`.
  - `isTrustedMoveHit({ move_trusted, classification, played_eval, played_eval_mate })`
    = `move_trusted === true && canResolveMoveAnalysis(...)`. NOTE: this is now
    correctly TRUE for a move-trusted mate-only row (no `eval_delta`).
  - Remove `isTrustedCacheHit`.
- Transitional CP-only usability gate (NOT trust): `hasCpEvalLoss({ eval_delta })`
  = `Number.isFinite(eval_delta) && eval_delta >= 0`. Documented explicitly as the
  CP-only limitation the live path needs to grade a drill from a cached delta
  today; Phase 6 replaces it with a mate-aware eval-loss model. (Preserves the old
  guard's finite-non-negative-delta rejection, which `evalLoss` alone does not —
  `evalLoss(-1)` returns 0, not null.)
- Leave `gradeDrillMove` / `evalLoss` / `failsDrill` UNCHANGED; add a one-line
  comment marking the strictness-0 ordering as Phase 6 territory (epic g-l02q note)
  so it isn't "fixed" here by accident.

### 3. `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` and `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts`
(Same edit to both — duplicate cache logic.)
- Imports: drop `isTrustedCacheHit`; add `isTrustedPositionHit`, `isTrustedMoveHit`,
  `hasCpEvalLoss`.
- Cache gate in `flushCacheLookups`: replace
  `if (!cached || !isTrustedCacheHit(cached))` with
  `if (!cached || !isTrustedPositionHit(cached) || !isTrustedMoveHit(cached) || !hasCpEvalLoss(cached))`.
  Rationale, mapped to the three concerns:
  - `isTrustedPositionHit` — trusted, renderable best move/PV (so `bestMove`/PV are
    grain-correct and exact-best is meaningful).
  - `isTrustedMoveHit` — trusted, renderable played evidence (classification + a
    played eval of either kind).
  - `hasCpEvalLoss` — TRANSITIONAL: the current grader needs a CP delta; mate-only
    rows lack one and must fall back to the worker until Phase 6. Removing this line
    is the Phase 6 change, not Phase 5.
  This preserves today's behavior exactly: move-trusted-but-position-untrusted
  (null best) → fails position guard → worker; position-trusted-but-move-untrusted
  → fails move guard → worker; move-trusted mate-only → fails `hasCpEvalLoss` →
  worker. Keep the `cached ? 'untrusted' : 'cache-miss'` ReleaseReason.
- `fromCachedAnalysis`: `best_move_uci` is now guaranteed non-null here (position
  guard). Keep `bestMove: cached.best_move_uci ?? move` defensively but REWRITE the
  stale g-l02q comment — under the grain gate the position best move is always
  present, so the old "null best → unavailable recovery" reasoning no longer
  applies; the fallback is purely defensive. Do NOT thread `best_eval_mate` into
  `AnalysisResult` (no field; mate-aware grading is Phase 6).

### 4. `src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts`
- `buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot`: set `position_trusted: false` on locally-built
  `PositionAnalysis` seeds (local worker results are not a backend trusted-position
  winner). Document that whether AnalysisBoard re-searches on this is g-54h5's call;
  this phase only delivers the honest flag.

### 5. Tests
- `src/workers/analysisUtils.test.ts`:
  - Replace `canResolveCachedAnalysis` describe with `canResolvePositionAnalysis`
    (best_move + multi-move PV; PV[0]≠best, single-move PV, null PV, null best).
  - New `canResolveMoveAnalysis` describe: classification valid/invalid/null;
    played_eval finite; played_eval_mate-only (accepted); BOTH played evals null
    (rejected). Assert it does NOT require `eval_delta` (Finding 2).
  - New `hasCpEvalLoss` describe: null/Infinity/NaN/negative → false; 0 and
    positive finite → true. (Takes over the old delta-rejection cases.)
  - Replace `isTrustedCacheHit` describe with `isTrustedPositionHit` /
    `isTrustedMoveHit`: include `move_trusted:true` + `played_eval_mate` set +
    `eval_delta:null` → `isTrustedMoveHit === true` (Finding 2). Drop all
    `trusted_for_resolution` fixtures.
- `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts` (13 refs) and
  `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.test.ts` (4 refs): migrate every mocked
  `CachedAnalysis` with `trusted_for_resolution: true` to set `position_trusted` +
  `move_trusted` (and a usable played eval; `best_eval_mate` where needed). Add
  cases proving the split:
  (a) `position_trusted:true, move_trusted:false` → worker fallback ('untrusted');
  (b) `move_trusted:true, position_trusted:false`/null best → worker fallback;
  (c) `move_trusted:true` mate-only (`eval_delta:null`, `played_eval_mate` set) →
      worker fallback via `hasCpEvalLoss` (CP-only limitation, Finding 2);
  (d) all three pass → cache resolves and cancels the worker.
- `PositionAnalysis` object literals gain the now-REQUIRED `position_trusted`.
  Known constructors (confirm full set via `tsc --noEmit`):
  `AnalysisBoard.test.tsx`, `DrillAnalysisPage.test.tsx`, `GameAnalysisPage.test.tsx`,
  `ChessGame.test.tsx`, `chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.test.ts`,
  `chess-game/domain/domain.test.ts`, `utils/api.test.ts`.
- `sessionUpload.test.ts`: assert snapshot `positionAnalysis` entries carry
  `position_trusted: false`.

### 6. Backend doc-only correction (behavior-neutral, optional but recommended)
Phase 5 does NOT un-suppress position-only hits, so the "until Phase 5" markers are
now stale. Update the comment at the `analysis.py` lookup loop and the docstring of
`test_lookup_position_only_no_move_row_suppressed` to reference Phase 6 (where
strictness-0-from-position-only needs them). Keep the suppression behavior and the
`results == {}` assertion unchanged. No other backend change.

## Out of scope (explicit)
- Un-suppressing position-only lookup hits (backend emission + frontend consumption)
  → Phase 6 (g-position-analysis.6): strictness-0 exact-best from a trusted position
  with no exact move row is what actually needs it. (Finding 1.)
- `gradeDrillMove` ordering / strictness-0-from-position-only / CP eval-loss
  derivation / mate-aware grading (removing `hasCpEvalLoss` from the gate) → Phase 6.
- AnalysisBoard reading/gating on `position_trusted` (restricted-search skip) → g-54h5.
- Removing the backend `trusted_for_resolution` field → later cleanup.
- SPEC.md grain documentation → Phase 8.

## Acceptance
- `api.ts`, `analysisUtils.ts`, `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`, `useMoveAnalysis.ts`,
  `sessionUpload.ts` no longer treat one cached move row as both position and move
  truth. The frontend no longer reads `trusted_for_resolution`; trust is the pair
  `position_trusted` / `move_trusted`, kept distinct from the transitional CP-only
  grading usability gate. Tests migrated, including a move-trusted mate-only case.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (catches every required-field / removed-export break).
- `npx vitest run src/workers/analysisUtils.test.ts src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.test.ts src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.test.ts`
  (rerun named files in isolation — the full pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load).
- If the optional backend doc-fix is included: `cd backend && python -m pytest test_analysis_cache_api.py -k position_only` to confirm the suppression test still passes.
close_reason: Phase 5 implemented: frontend wire types split into position/move grains, grain-specific cache guards (isTrustedPositionHit/isTrustedMoveHit/hasCpEvalLoss) replace isTrustedCacheHit; sessionUpload seeds position_trusted=false; backend doc-only Phase-5/legacy-comment fixes. tsc + vitest + backend tests green. Reviewed.

title: Position analysis Phase 4: cut over backend payload consumers (analysis/lookup, tree_eval, session)
description:
Sub-task of epic **g-position-analysis** — Phase 4 of the master plan (see the parent epic's DESIGN → "Consumer Cutover And Audit" and "Wire And Frontend Contract"; the full plan stays in the parent).

## Goal

Cut over the payload-producing backend consumers so responses carry **separate** trusted position evidence and trusted move evidence sourced from `position_analysis` (or an explicitly trusted legacy v2 projection during transition). **This is the phase g-54h5 depends on.**

## Work

1. `/api/analysis/lookup` (or replacement endpoint) in `backend/app/api/analysis.py`:
   - Resolve trusted position facts by `normalized_fen`; keep exact `(fen_before, move_uci)` lookup for move evidence.
   - Replace/wrap `_trust_flags(row)` with grain-specific `position_trusted` / `move_trusted` helpers. Keep diagnostics (`authoritative`, `contract_satisfied`, `evidence_contract_id`) per grain.
   - Stop returning one flattened object whose best-move/PV, played-eval/classification, and trust flag all come from a single move row. If flattened `CachedAnalysis` fields remain temporarily, derive them by merging position + move payloads, never copied from one `analysis_cache` row.
2. `backend/app/tree_eval.py` (HIGH PRIORITY — verified live non-trust-gated consumer). Source root best eval, mate ranking, and best move from `position_analysis` / trusted legacy projection. Must explicitly cover:
   - `lookup_root_eval`
   - `lookup_move_evals` — currently reads `analysis_cache` via `normalized_fen_before` fallback with NO trust filter; must stop reading raw position facts without trust/contract filtering.
   - `_root_sort_key` and `_move_sort_key` — preserve forced-mate-ahead-of-CP ranking via stored `best_eval_mate`.
3. `backend/app/api/session.py` session drill-review export (HIGH PRIORITY — verified live non-trust-gated consumer). Stop presenting duplicated `SessionMove.best_move_uci` as authoritative. **Bridge the grains explicitly**: look up storage rows with `normalize_fen(move.fen_before)`, then emit the `position_analysis: dict[str, PositionAnalysis]` response keyed by the ORIGINAL full `move.fen_before`. Carry `position_trusted`; mark legacy/untrusted seeds false. Do not return a normalized-FEN keyed storage map directly.

## Acceptance

`/api/analysis/lookup`, `tree_eval.py` (all four functions above), and session export return separate trusted position and move evidence. Position lookup uses normalized FEN; move evidence stays `(fen_before, move_uci)`-keyed. Session export preserves full-FEN response keys while sourcing storage by normalized FEN, and carries `position_trusted`. Tests cover tree_eval rejecting untrusted position roots (incl. `lookup_move_evals`), session export carrying `position_trusted` with full-FEN keys, mate-ranking preservation, and lookup transposition behavior.
design:
# g-position-analysis.4 — Cut over backend payload consumers

## Context

`analysis_cache` is keyed by `(fen_before, move_uci)` but each row also carries
position-level facts (`best_move_uci`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`,
`best_eval_mate`). Those are properties of the position, not the played move, so
sibling rows for different played moves can disagree, and a low-trust browser row
can redefine the position best in any consumer that doesn't apply the backend
trust contract.

Phases 1–3 already built the fix's storage layer:
- **Phase 1** — `position_analysis` storage table (`PositionAnalysisRow`,
  single winner per `normalized_fen`) + `position_analysis_conflicts`;
  grain-specific contracts `position-complete-v1` / `move-complete-v1` and legacy
  `resolver-complete-v2` projection helpers in `evidence_contracts.py`.
- **Phase 2** — backfill (`position_analysis_backfill.py`) that stamps winners
  `source="precomputed"`, `evidence_contract_id="position-complete-v1"`,
  `source_cache_id=<cache row id>`.
- **Phase 3** — write policy (`decide_position_analysis_replacement` /
  `write_position_analysis_row`): native writes use `position-complete-v1`,
  browser-game rows structurally rejected before any dominance comparison.

**Phase 4 cuts over the read/payload-producing consumers** so responses carry
*separate* trusted position evidence (sourced from `position_analysis` or a
trusted legacy v2 projection) and trusted move evidence (sourced from
`analysis_cache`, the correct grain for played-move facts). This is the phase
`g-54h5` depends on.

The two verified live, non-trust-gated consumers are front-loaded:
`backend/app/tree_eval.py` and `backend/app/api/session.py`. `/api/analysis/lookup`
is already trust-gated on the frontend, so its change is additive/non-breaking.

### Red-baseline tests this phase flips (in `backend/test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py`)
Three `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` tests document the bugs today; Phase 4
makes them pass, after which their `xfail` markers must be removed:
1. `test_lookup_move_evals_untrusted_normalized_fallback` — untrusted browser
   played-eval must NOT drive the normalized fallback; expect `None`.
2. `test_root_eval_gul4p_untrusted_sibling_does_not_surface` — untrusted browser
   sibling must NOT win the root eval; trusted canonical `best_eval` (35) wins.
3. `test_session_position_analysis_untrusted_seed_marked_untrusted` — export must
   expose `position_trusted is False` for an untrusted seed.
Plus update the green characterization test
`test_session_position_analysis_current_shape` (currently asserts
`"position_trusted" not in entry`) to assert the new field's presence.
Keep `test_lookup_move_evals_trusted_canonical_still_resolves` green (guards
against over-correction: canonical eval must still resolve).

## Out of scope (later phases / beads)
- Frontend wire types & cache guards (`src/utils/api.ts`,
  `analysisUtils.ts`, `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`, `useMoveAnalysis.ts`,
  `sessionUpload.ts`) → **Phase 5 (g-position-analysis.5)**.
- Drill grading semantics (strictness-0, CP eval-loss derivation, mate
  fallback) → **Phase 6**.
- Mate-aware loss model → Phase 6 (this phase is CP-only; mate is *stored* and
  used for ranking/exact-best only).
- `AnalysisBoard.tsx` line ordering → **g-54h5**.
- Deprecating legacy `resolver-complete-v2` → later follow-up.

---

## Step 0 — Shared building blocks (new code consumed by all three consumers)

### 0a. Grain-specific trust helpers — new module `backend/app/analysis_trust.py`
DB-free, operate on plain dicts (mirrors `position_analysis_policy._effectively_authoritative`,
which is already dict-based). Avoids an import cycle with the API/repo modules.

**⚠ Gate by the EXPECTED contract, not the row's declared contract.** Calling
`contract_satisfied(data["evidence_contract_id"], data)` validates whatever the
row *claims*, so an authoritative `move-complete-v1` row would wrongly read as
`position_trusted` (and vice-versa). The grain must require its own contract id
explicitly — exactly the pattern already in `analysis.py:88`
(`evidence_contract_id == RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2 and satisfied`).

```
def position_trust_flags(data: dict) -> tuple[bool, bool, bool]:
    """(authoritative, contract_satisfied, position_trusted) for a position-grain row."""
    authoritative = _effectively_authoritative(data)        # profile authoritative+active + IDENTITY_FIELDS match
    cid = data.get("evidence_contract_id")
    satisfied = (
        (cid == POSITION_COMPLETE and contract_satisfied(POSITION_COMPLETE, data))   # native position row
        or legacy_v2_satisfies_position(data)                                        # legacy v2 projection (checks cid == v2 internally)
    )
    return authoritative, satisfied, (authoritative and satisfied)

def move_trust_flags(data: dict) -> tuple[bool, bool, bool]:
    """(authoritative, contract_satisfied, move_trusted) for a move-grain row."""
    authoritative = _effectively_authoritative(data)
    cid = data.get("evidence_contract_id")
    satisfied = (
        (cid == MOVE_COMPLETE and contract_satisfied(MOVE_COMPLETE, data))           # native move row
        or legacy_v2_satisfies_move(data)                                            # legacy v2 projection
    )
    return authoritative, satisfied, (authoritative and satisfied)
```

`legacy_v2_satisfies_position` / `_move` already fail closed unless
`evidence_contract_id == resolver-complete-v2` (internal `_is_declared_v2`), so a
cross-grain native row cannot sneak through either branch.

Reuse, don't re-implement:
- `_effectively_authoritative` already exists in `position_analysis_policy.py:117`
  (dict-based, identical gate to `analysis.py:_is_authoritative`). Hoist it into
  `analysis_trust.py` (or import it) so all callers share one definition.
- `contract_satisfied`, `legacy_v2_satisfies_position`, `legacy_v2_satisfies_move`,
  `POSITION_COMPLETE`, `MOVE_COMPLETE`, `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2` from
  `evidence_contracts.py`.
- `IDENTITY_FIELDS`, `get_profile` from `analysis_profiles.py`.

Also move the **shared deterministic source preference** here:
`source_rank(source) -> int` (precomputed=0, game=1, other=2). It currently lives
as `_SOURCE_RANK` / `_OTHER_SOURCE_RANK` / `_source_rank` in `tree_eval.py:28-43`.
Both the repo's legacy-position ranking and `tree_eval`'s move ranking need it;
hosting it in this neutral module keeps the dependency arrows one-directional
(see the import-cycle note in 0c).

**Validation note (verified against the contract validators):** for a
canonical/legacy `resolver-complete-v2` `analysis_cache` row, `contract_satisfied`
for `position-complete-v1`/`move-complete-v1` returns False (wrong contract id),
but `legacy_v2_satisfies_*` returns True via projection — so trusted canonical v2
rows stay trusted at both grains during migration. Browser
`resolver-complete-v1`/non-authoritative rows fail both branches → untrusted.

Provide thin row→dict projectors (or reuse existing ones):
- Position dict keys needed by validators: `best_move_uci`, `best_line_uci`,
  `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`, `evidence_contract_id`, `analysis_profile_id`,
  + IDENTITY_FIELDS. `position_analysis_repo._row_to_dict` (`:94`) already covers
  storage rows; add an `analysis_cache`→position-dict projector for the legacy path.
- Move dict keys: `played_eval`, `played_eval_mate`, `classification`,
  `eval_delta`, `evidence_contract_id`, `analysis_profile_id`, + IDENTITY_FIELDS.

### 0b. Position read helpers — add to `backend/app/position_analysis_repo.py`
There is currently **no read helper** (only `_load_existing` at `:120`, which uses
`FOR UPDATE` and is for the write path). Add read-only (no lock) helpers:
```
def get_position_analysis(db, normalized_fen: str) -> PositionAnalysisRow | None
def get_position_analyses(db, normalized_fens: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, PositionAnalysisRow]  # batch IN()
```
Batch variant is required so `tree_eval`/`session`/`lookup` don't N+1.

### 0c. Single trusted-position resolver — `resolve_trusted_position` (shared by all 3 consumers)
The phase goal allows position evidence to come from `position_analysis` **or a
trusted legacy v2 projection during transition**. To avoid re-implementing that
two-tier logic in tree_eval, session, and analysis, add one resolver (in
`position_analysis_repo.py`) that all three call:

```
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrustedPosition:
    best_move_uci: str
    best_move_san: str | None
    best_line_uci: list[str] | None
    best_eval: int | None        # white-relative
    best_eval_mate: int | None   # white-relative

def resolve_trusted_position(db, normalized_fen: str) -> TrustedPosition | None:
    # 1. Storage first: get_position_analysis(db, norm); use it iff position_trust_flags(_row_to_dict(row)).position_trusted
    # 2. Trusted legacy fallback: SELECT analysis_cache WHERE normalized_fen_before == norm;
    #    keep only rows where position_trust_flags(cache_row_as_position_dict(r)).position_trusted;
    #    rank survivors with _legacy_position_sort_key (repo-local); take the winner's position facts.
    # 3. else None
```

It returns a payload **only when trusted** (so a `None` result tells the caller to
take its own untrusted fallback). This resolver is the single place that honors:
- **Finding 4** — the legacy fallback ranks **all** trusted rows at the
  `normalized_fen` grain (one `normalized_fen_before == norm` query). It does
  **not** prefer exact full-FEN rows first (today's `tree_eval.py:167-179`
  behavior), which could otherwise miss a trusted mate/stronger row at a
  clock-variant of the same normalized position.
- **Finding 2** — session export can reuse the exact same trusted legacy-v2
  fallback, not just the storage table.

**⚠ Import-cycle avoidance (Finding):** `resolve_trusted_position` must NOT import
`tree_eval._root_sort_key` — `tree_eval` will import this resolver, and the reverse
edge would form `position_analysis_repo → tree_eval → position_analysis_repo`.
Today `position_analysis_repo.py` has no dependency on tree code. So:
- Define the position-grain ranking as a **repo-local** `_legacy_position_sort_key(row)`
  in `position_analysis_repo.py` (same tuple as today's `_root_sort_key`:
  mate-first via `best_eval_mate`, then canonical best-move row
  `move_uci == best_move_uci`, then `source_rank(source)`, then `id`).
- It uses `source_rank` imported from the neutral `analysis_trust` module (0a).
- `tree_eval` **stops owning** the position sort key (`_root_sort_key` is deleted),
  keeping only `_move_sort_key` for the move grain.

Resulting dependency arrows (acyclic): `analysis_trust` ← `position_analysis_repo`
← `tree_eval`; `analysis_trust` ← `tree_eval`; `analysis_trust` imports only
`evidence_contracts` + `analysis_profiles`.

---

## Step 1 — `backend/app/tree_eval.py` (HIGH PRIORITY)

Consumed by the openings tree builder (`backend/app/api/openings.py:1288,1296` →
`TreeResponse.root_eval_cp/_mate`, `TreeNode.eval_cp/_mate`).

### `lookup_root_eval(session, starting_fen)` — position grain
Becomes a thin wrapper over `resolve_trusted_position`:
1. `norm = normalize_fen(starting_fen)`; `tp = resolve_trusted_position(session, norm)`.
2. If `tp` is None → return `None`. Else return `MoveEval` from `tp.best_eval` /
   `tp.best_eval_mate`.

Drops today's exact-FEN-first preference for the position grain (Finding 4) — the
resolver ranks all trusted rows at the normalized grain. Turns
`test_root_eval_gul4p_…` green: browser `c2c4` sibling (resolver-complete-v1,
non-authoritative) is filtered out; trusted canonical `c1f4` row (v2,
authoritative, `best_eval=35`) survives → returns 35.

### `lookup_move_evals(session, requests)` — move grain (stays on `analysis_cache`)
Played-eval is genuinely move-grain, so the table is correct; add the missing
trust filter:
1. Step-1 exact `(fen_before, move_uci)` hit: accept the row's `played_eval` only
   if `move_trust_flags(...).move_trusted`.
2. Step-2 normalized fallback: when grouping `fallback_rows` into
   `by_norm_move`, **drop rows that aren't move-trusted** before ranking with
   `_move_sort_key`.

Turns `test_lookup_move_evals_untrusted_normalized_fallback` green (lone browser
row → `None`); keeps `…_trusted_canonical_still_resolves` green (canonical 18 wins
over browser 77).

### Sort keys
- `_root_sort_key` is **removed** from `tree_eval` — position-grain ranking now
  lives in `position_analysis_repo._legacy_position_sort_key` (see 0c, import-cycle
  fix). `lookup_root_eval` no longer needs it (thin wrapper over the resolver).
- `_move_sort_key` **stays** in `tree_eval` for the move grain; it now ranks an
  already-`move_trusted`-filtered candidate list and uses `source_rank` imported
  from `analysis_trust` (the local `_SOURCE_RANK`/`_source_rank` helpers move to
  that neutral module). Mate-first ordering (`played_eval_mate`) unchanged; add a
  comment that trust filtering precedes ranking. Re-assert mate-ranking by test.

### Imports
Add `resolve_trusted_position` (repo) and `move_trust_flags` + `source_rank`
(`analysis_trust`). `normalize_fen` already imported. `lookup_root_eval` no longer
references `_root_sort_key` or `_best_eval`-on-cache-rows directly (resolver owns it).

---

## Step 2 — `backend/app/api/session.py` drill-review export (HIGH PRIORITY)

Endpoint: `get_session_analysis` (`GET /{session_id}/analysis`, `:712`). Current
build (`:786-794`) keys the `position_analysis: dict[str, PositionAnalysis]`
response by full `move.fen_before` and copies fields straight off `SessionMove`.

### Model change
Add `position_trusted: bool` to the `PositionAnalysis` pydantic model
(`session.py:127`). Set explicitly per entry (no silent default that hides
untrusted seeds).

### Build change — bridge the grains
**Finding 2 fix — the emit gate must no longer depend on `SessionMove.best_move_uci`.**
Today (`session.py:788`) an entry is only built when `move.best_move_uci` is set.
After cutover, a *trusted storage/legacy* best move must be emitted for **any move
with `fen_before`**, even when `SessionMove.best_move_uci` is None. Only the
untrusted fallback seed path still requires `SessionMove.best_move_uci`.

For each `move` with `fen_before` (de-duped by full `fen_before`, first wins):
1. `tp = resolve_trusted_position(db, normalize_fen(move.fen_before))` — storage
   first, then trusted legacy v2 projection (the same resolver as tree_eval, so
   session honors the legacy fallback too, not just the storage table).
2. **If `tp` is not None:** emit `PositionAnalysis` from `tp`
   (`best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, sign-converted eval), with
   `position_trusted=True`, **keyed by the original full `move.fen_before`** —
   regardless of whether `SessionMove.best_move_uci` is set.
3. **Else if `move.best_move_uci` is set:** emit the legacy `SessionMove` seed
   fields, with `position_trusted=False`.
4. **Else:** no entry (no usable best move at any trust level).

Batch the resolver lookups (collect distinct norms first) to avoid N+1.

### ⚠ Eval orientation (correctness-critical, verified)
`position_analysis.best_eval` and `analysis_cache.best_eval` are **white-relative**
(`models.py:325,390`), so `tp.best_eval` is white-relative. But the session wire
field `best_move_eval_cp` is **side-to-move-relative** (`session.py:130`, and the
inbound conversion at `:468,487` uses `* sign`). When sourcing the eval from `tp`,
convert: `sign = +1 if active_color(move.fen_before) == "white" else -1`;
`best_move_eval_cp = tp.best_eval * sign`. `active_color` is already imported
(`session.py:26`). The `SessionMove` fallback path needs no conversion (already
side-to-move-relative). (Mate: `tp.best_eval_mate` is white-relative too; it is
not part of the session wire model today, so it stays unused here — Phase 6.)

Turns `test_session_position_analysis_untrusted_seed_marked_untrusted` green: the
browser seed has no trusted `position_analysis` row (browser rows can't enter
storage) → falls back to `SessionMove` seed `e2e4`, `position_trusted=False`. Keep
the response keyed by full FEN — never return the normalized-keyed storage map.

### Imports
Add `get_position_analyses` (repo) and `position_trust_flags` (`analysis_trust`);
`normalize_fen`/`active_color` already imported.

---

## Step 3 — `backend/app/api/analysis.py` `/api/analysis/lookup` (additive, non-breaking)

Already frontend-trust-gated, so this is additive so the frontend keeps working
until Phase 5. The endpoint (`:108`) currently flattens one `analysis_cache` row
into `CachedAnalysisResult` and exposes a single `trusted_for_resolution`.

**Finding 3 — result-shape decision: position-only hits are intentionally
suppressed until Phase 5.** The current response (`:38`) requires `move_san` and a
result is only emitted when an exact `(fen_before, move_uci)` move row exists. The
frontend still consumes that flattened shape until Phase 5, so this phase does
**not** introduce a nested/nullable position-only payload. Instead, each emitted
result (still gated on an exact move row) is *enriched* with separately-resolved
position evidence + grain trust flags. A position-only hit (storage row but no
move row) is **not** surfaced; this is documented and deferred to Phase 5 when the
frontend can consume the split shape.

Changes:
1. Keep the exact `(fen_before, move_uci)` query for **move evidence**
   (`move_san`, `played_eval`, `played_eval_mate`, `eval_delta`, `classification`)
   and keep emitting a result only when that move row exists.
2. For each emitted result, resolve position evidence separately via
   `resolve_trusted_position(db, normalize_fen(position.fen))` (storage + trusted
   legacy v2 fallback — same resolver as tree_eval/session). Note `best_eval`
   here stays **white-relative** (the current lookup already returns white-relative
   `row.best_eval`), so **no sign conversion** in this endpoint.
3. Replace `_trust_flags` with grain-specific results: add `position_trusted`
   (True iff the resolver returned a payload) and `move_trusted`
   (`move_trust_flags` on the move row), plus per-grain `authoritative` /
   `contract_satisfied` / `evidence_contract_id` diagnostics, to the response.
4. Flattened best-move fields (`best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`,
   `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`) are **derived from the resolver payload**
   (null when untrusted), never copied from the move row.
5. **Keep `trusted_for_resolution`** on the response with its current semantics
   (authoritative + v2 + satisfied on the move row) so Phase-5-pending frontend
   code is unaffected; Phase 5 removes it.

`CachedAnalysisResult` (`:38`) gains `position_trusted`, `move_trusted`, and
position/move diagnostic fields. Reuse `decode_uci_line`.

---

## Step 4 — Tests

In `backend/` (pytest; suite lives flat in `backend/`, e.g.
`backend/test_tree_eval.py`, `backend/test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py`):

**Flip the red baseline** (`test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py`):
- Remove `xfail` from the three tests above; keep their dual assertions
  (untrusted value absent AND correct trusted outcome present).
- Update `test_session_position_analysis_current_shape` to assert
  `position_trusted` is present (`is False` for the untrusted seed).

**New trust-helper coverage** (`test_analysis_trust.py`, new) — **cross-grain
negatives (Finding 1):**
- An authoritative `move-complete-v1` row reads `position_trusted=False`.
- An authoritative `position-complete-v1` row reads `move_trusted=False`.
- A trusted legacy `resolver-complete-v2` row reads True at **both** grains.
- A browser `resolver-complete-v1` / non-authoritative row reads False at both.

**New `tree_eval` coverage** (`test_tree_eval.py`):
- Storage hit: a trusted `position_analysis` row drives `lookup_root_eval` even
  when `analysis_cache` siblings disagree.
- Storage miss → trusted legacy projection path used; untrusted siblings excluded.
- **Finding 4:** a trusted stronger/mate row at a *clock-variant* (same normalized
  FEN, different full FEN) is selected even though an exact-FEN trusted row also
  exists — i.e. normalized-grain ranking, not exact-first.
- Mate ranking preserved among trusted rows (root + move sort keys): a
  `best_eval_mate` / `played_eval_mate` trusted row outranks a CP-only trusted row.
- `lookup_move_evals` trust filter on both exact and normalized paths.

**New `session` coverage:**
- Trusted storage row present → `position_trusted=True`, response keyed by full
  `fen_before`, best move sourced from storage, **eval sign-converted** to
  side-to-move-relative.
- **Finding 2a:** trusted storage row present but `SessionMove.best_move_uci is
  None` → entry is still emitted from storage (`position_trusted=True`).
- **Finding 2b:** no storage row, but a trusted legacy `resolver-complete-v2`
  `analysis_cache` row at the normalized FEN → entry emitted via the legacy
  fallback, `position_trusted=True`.

**New `analysis.py` lookup coverage** (Finding 3 cases):
- Both grains hit: position resolved by normalized FEN (transposition), move by
  exact `(fen_before, move_uci)`; `position_trusted` / `move_trusted` independent;
  flattened best-move derived from the position payload, not the move row.
- Move-only (untrusted/no position) → result emitted, `position_trusted=False`,
  flattened best-move fields null.
- Position-only (storage row, no move row) → **no result emitted** (documented
  suppression until Phase 5).
- `trusted_for_resolution` legacy field still behaves as today.

**Run isolation note:** the full vitest/pytest suite is flaky under parallel
pre-push load — rerun any failing file in isolation before trusting a failure.

1. `cd backend && pytest test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py test_tree_eval.py -q`

2. `cd backend && pytest test_session*.py test_analysis*.py -q` — session export and

3. Targeted run of the new tests for each consumer in isolation (flaky-suite rule).
4. Spot-check the openings tree endpoint and a drill-review session response in the

title: Position analysis Phase 3: position write policy + move-complete contract on writes
description:
Sub-task of epic **g-position-analysis** — Phase 3 of the master plan (see the parent epic's DESIGN → "Position Write Policy" and "Contract And Trust Migration"; the full plan stays in the parent).

## Goal

Route all new position writes through a dominance/supersession policy so trusted position truth is protected on write, not only filtered at read time. Ensure post-split move-grain writes stop claiming the cross-grain v2 contract.

## Work

1. Add a position write policy mirroring `decide_analysis_cache_replacement` in `backend/app/analysis_cache_policy.py`:
   - Reject invalid contract claims.
   - Non-authoritative browser-game evidence cannot insert or replace trusted position truth when canonical coverage exists.
   - Same-profile authoritative supersets may merge when the contract explicitly allows it.
   - Authoritative successors may replace weaker rows when dominance is explicit.
2. Keep lower-trust browser evidence as move diagnostics in `analysis_cache` only; it must never become position truth via `position_analysis`.
3. New post-split move-grain writes must use the **move-complete** contract, NEVER `resolver-complete-v2` — v2 validates the cross-grain `eval_delta == f(best_eval, played_eval)` invariant that a move-only row can no longer satisfy.
4. Enforce browser-rejection structurally on write (constraint + policy), not as a read-time filter alone.

## Acceptance

Position writes route through the new policy; browser-game writes cannot insert or replace trusted position rows; post-split move writes never claim `resolver-complete-v2`. Tests cover write-side browser rejection for trusted position rows and grain-specific contract validation on write.

## Interlock with g-mk1d

Phase 3 must keep the position write policy and move-cache diagnostic policy separate.

For position_analysis, browser-game evidence remains ineligible before any strength comparison: non-authoritative browser rows cannot insert or replace trusted position truth, even after g-mk1d records dynamic browser search metadata.

For analysis_cache move diagnostics, do not preserve same-browser-profile idempotency as a permanent invariant. g-mk1d will extend the move-cache replacement policy so comparable stronger browser rows can replace weaker browser rows for the same (fen_before, move_uci), while canonical authoritative rows still dominate browser rows and browser rows still cannot replace canonical rows. Phase 3 tests and wording should avoid flattening all non-authoritative rows into one unordered bucket.
