title: Position analysis Phase 2: backfill canonical position winners from AnalysisCache
description:
Sub-task of epic **g-position-analysis** — Phase 2 of the master plan (see the parent epic's DESIGN → "Backfill And Repair" and "Phased Implementation"; the full plan stays in the parent). The concrete Phase-2 build plan lives in this bead's DESIGN field.

## Goal

Backfill canonical position winners into `position_analysis` from existing `AnalysisCache` rows, choosing exactly one winner per `normalized_fen` with explicit dominance logic, and persisting best-move/mate disagreements to `position_analysis_conflicts`.

## Work

1. Source position facts from existing `AnalysisCache` rows (NOT from `OpeningPositionScore`, which is batch-scoped aggregate win-rate data with no engine fields). `AnalysisCache` already has `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`, and indexed `normalized_fen_before`.
2. Resolve target `normalized_fen` from `normalized_fen_before` when present; for null/legacy rows compute `normalize_fen(fen_before)` before grouping.
3. **Group first, then pick one winner per group.** Do NOT iterate cache rows relying on `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` / unique-constraint ordering — the DB conflict clause has no dominance logic and would make result order part of correctness.
4. Candidate eligibility: **effectively authoritative** (profile `authoritative and active` AND all `IDENTITY_FIELDS` columns match) AND **legacy-v2 position-complete** (declared `resolver-complete-v2` whose `project_v2_to_position` projection passes `_validate_position_complete`). This excludes browser-game / JeffML (non-authoritative) and v1/legacy rows; the g-ul4p browser sibling is filtered out before grouping.
5. Winner selection ranks candidates by a **guarded search-strength comparison** (`compare_search_strength`: `engine_version` then `search_limit_value`, only when scoring-semantics fields — nets, multipv, analyzer protocol, engine_name, search_limit_type — all match), then by a deterministic preference order (profile priority preferring the linux precompute profile, then `cache_id`). Strictly-stronger search always wins through the guarded comparator; equal-strength / incomparable candidates resolve by the deterministic preference order. Raw `search_limit_value` is never used as a sort key outside the comparator.
6. Emit exactly one write decision per `normalized_fen` group. **Idempotent / re-runnable:** conditional no-op when the recomputed winner equals the stored row (so `updated_at` does not churn), and backfill **never overwrites a natively-written position row** (`source_cache_id IS NULL`, i.e. a future Phase-3 live write) — it only owns rows it backfilled.
7. On **best-move or mate-winner** disagreement among eligible candidates, persist an **append-only** `position_analysis_conflicts` row (deduped by a deterministic content signature, never by deleting prior rows) with candidate detail and per-axis disagreement columns; `policy_reason` is `selected_dominant` (strength resolved it) or `conflict_best_known_kept` (equal-strength deterministic tiebreak). A winner is **always** selected — there is no quarantine path. PV-continuation and CP-only `best_eval` differences are captured in the audit columns when such a conflict fires, but are NOT themselves conflict triggers.

## Acceptance

Backfill groups by `normalized_fen` before writing, selects exactly one canonical winner per group with explicit strength-then-deterministic dominance rules, emits one write decision per group, and records **best-move and mate-winner** disagreements in **append-only** `position_analysis_conflicts` (with candidate + per-axis detail including mate; PV/eval differences captured only as audit detail when a best-move/mate conflict fires, not as standalone triggers). Never uses `OpeningPositionScore` as an engine-truth source. Reruns are idempotent (unchanged winners no-op; conflicts dedupe by signature) and backfill never overwrites a natively-written position row (`source_cache_id IS NULL`). Tests cover group-then-pick winner selection, the g-ul4p mixed-row case (browser filtered out → clean canonical winner, no conflict), the equal-strength best-move tiebreak (linux preferred), a CP-only difference producing NO conflict, rerun idempotency, and native-row protection.
design:
# g-position-analysis.2 — Phase 2: backfill canonical position winners

## Context

`analysis_cache` is keyed by `(fen_before, move_uci)` but also stores position-level
facts (`best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`,
`best_eval_mate`). Those facts are properties of the *position*, not the played
move, so they are duplicated across sibling rows and a lower-trust row can appear to
redefine a position's best move (the g-ul4p bug).

Phase 1 (closed, commit `fd7e904`) built the foundation: the `position_analysis`
(single winner per `normalized_fen`) and `position_analysis_conflicts` tables in all
three schema locations; the `position-complete-v1` / `move-complete-v1` grain
contracts; and legacy-v2 → grain projection helpers (`legacy_v2_satisfies_position`,
etc.). **Nothing writes those tables yet.**

Phase 2 is the **backfill**: read existing `AnalysisCache` rows, group candidates by
`normalized_fen`, pick exactly one canonical winner per group with explicit dominance
logic, write it into `position_analysis`, and record best-move/mate disagreements in
`position_analysis_conflicts`. **Group first, then pick** — never rely on
`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` ordering for the winner. **Never** use `OpeningPositionScore`
as an engine-truth source (batch-scoped aggregate win-rate data, no engine fields).

## Decisions locked with the user

1. **Strength comparison is a reusable profile helper** in `app/analysis_profiles.py`
   (engine_version, then search_limit_value), guarded for comparability. Move-grain
   `analysis_cache_policy` left unchanged.
2. **Equal-strength best-move ties → deterministic tiebreak + keep** (prefer the linux
   precompute profile), record the conflict with `policy_reason="conflict_best_known_kept"`.
   No quarantine path.
3. **Conflict-recording scope = best-move / mate-winner disagreement only.** Benign
   `best_eval` cp jitter (same best move) and PV-continuation-only differences do NOT
   write a conflict row.
4. **Browser dynamic-depth is a separate follow-up bead**, out of Phase 2 scope.

## Review fixes incorporated (from user review of v1)

- **(High) Rerun idempotency:** updates are now **conditional** — no-op when the
  recomputed winner-stamp equals the stored row (so `updated_at` does not churn).
- **(High) Conflict append-only:** keep `position_analysis_conflicts` **append-only**
  (per `models.py:434` / `SPEC.md`); achieve idempotency by **content-signature dedupe**
  (skip insert when an identical conflict row already exists for the FEN), NOT by
  deleting prior rows.
- **(Med) `compare_search_strength` comparability:** require equality of all
  scoring-semantics fields (nets, multipv, analyzer protocol, engine_name,
  search_limit_type) before ranking by version/value; else INCOMPARABLE.
- **(Med) No raw `search_limit_value` in the sort:** depth/value ranking lives ONLY
  inside the guarded comparator; the deterministic tiebreak uses profile-priority then
  cache id only.
- **(Med) Conflict scope alignment:** narrow trigger made explicit and the Phase-2 bead
  acceptance wording is updated to match (best-move/mate), reconciled against the
  parent epic's broader phrasing.
- **(Hardening, adopted) Protect native rows:** backfill only owns rows it wrote
  (`source_cache_id IS NOT NULL`); it never overwrites a row a future Phase-3 live write
  produced.

## Design

### Eligibility (which `analysis_cache` rows become candidates)

Eligible iff **both**: (a) effectively authoritative — `analysis_profile_id` resolves
to an `authoritative and active` profile AND every `IDENTITY_FIELDS` column matches it
(reuse `api/analysis.py:_is_authoritative` / `analysis_cache_repo._identity_verified`);
and (b) `legacy_v2_satisfies_position(row_dict)` (declared `resolver-complete-v2` AND
`project_v2_to_position` passes `_validate_position_complete`). This excludes
browser-game / JeffML (non-authoritative) and legacy/v1 rows. **The g-ul4p browser
sibling is filtered out before grouping** → that group has one eligible canonical
candidate → clean winner, no conflict.

### Grouping key

`normalized_fen_before` when present (canonical rows always have it); else
`normalize_fen(fen_before)` (`app/fen.py`); skip + count unparseable FENs.

### `compare_search_strength` (new, in `app/analysis_profiles.py`)

```
class StrengthComparison(Enum): A_STRONGER; B_STRONGER; EQUAL; INCOMPARABLE
_STRENGTH_INVARIANT_FIELDS = (engine_name, eval_file_id, eval_file_small_id,
                              multipv, analyzer_protocol_version, search_limit_type)
def compare_search_strength(a: Profile, b: Profile) -> StrengthComparison
```
- **INCOMPARABLE** unless every `_STRENGTH_INVARIANT_FIELDS` value is equal (same
  scoring semantics: same nets, same multipv, same analyzer protocol, same engine,
  same limit *type*). This prevents calling a depth-30-on-a-different-net run "stronger"
  than the canonical depth-24 run. (`engine_build` is deliberately NOT invariant — the
  two canonical profiles differ only by platform binary and stay comparable.)
- Then compare `engine_version` (parse leading int; non-numeric & unequal →
  INCOMPARABLE), then `search_limit_value` (higher = stronger). Equal on both → EQUAL.
- Today's two canonical profiles → EQUAL (both v18/depth-24); a future depth-30 canonical
  run on the same net auto-wins without editing `dominates`. Add
  `AUTHORITATIVE_PROFILE_PRIORITY = ("canonical-sf18-depth24-linux-v1",
  "canonical-sf18-depth24-v1")` for the equal-strength tiebreak.
- Extend `test_analysis_profiles.py`: stronger depth → A_STRONGER; equal → EQUAL;
  differing net / multipv / protocol / limit-type → INCOMPARABLE.

### `app/position_analysis_policy.py` (new — pure, no DB)

Phase-2 position-grain primitives (Phase 3 will *extend* this same module with the live
write decision `decide_position_analysis_replacement`):

- `PositionCandidate` dataclass: `cache_id`, `normalized_fen`, position facts,
  representative `fen`, profile id, contract id, and the metadata block to stamp.
- `is_eligible_position_candidate(row_dict) -> bool`.
- `position_signature(c) -> (best_move_uci, mate_winner)` — the conflict-relevant axes
  (`mate_winner` encodes mate sign / mate-vs-cp). NOTE: PV-continuation and CP-only eval
  differences are intentionally NOT in the signature (decision #3).
- `select_position_winner(candidates) -> WinnerSelection`:
  1. **Preference order** (deterministic tiebreak only): `AUTHORITATIVE_PROFILE_PRIORITY`
     index, then higher `cache_id`. **No raw `search_limit_value` in this sort.**
  2. Fold to winner: `winner = first`; promote to `next` **only** when
     `compare_search_strength(next.profile, winner.profile) == A_STRONGER`. EQUAL /
     WEAKER / INCOMPARABLE keep the preference-earlier winner. (Strictly-stronger always
     wins through the guarded comparator; ties/incomparable resolve by preference order
     → deterministic.)
  3. `is_conflict` = more than one distinct `position_signature` among candidates.
  4. `policy_reason`: `selected_dominant` when the winner is strictly stronger
     (`A_STRONGER`) than every other distinct-best-move candidate; else
     `conflict_best_known_kept`.
- `position_conflict_axes(candidates) -> dict`: `candidate_cache_ids` (sorted),
  `candidate_summaries`, and per-axis distinct-value lists
  (`best_move_disagreement`, `pv_disagreement`, `best_eval_disagreement`,
  `best_eval_mate_disagreement`), each `None` when that axis agreed. These columns are
  filled for audit **when a conflict fires**, but the trigger is best-move/mate only.
- `conflict_signature(axes, policy_reason) -> str`: deterministic JSON over
  `candidate_cache_ids` + per-axis columns + `policy_reason`, for append-only dedupe.
- Tests (`test_position_analysis_policy.py`): single candidate (no conflict); siblings
  agreeing on best move / different played moves (one winner, no conflict); stronger
  search wins (`selected_dominant`); equal-strength best-move disagreement → linux
  preferred + `conflict_best_known_kept`; **CP-only difference → winner, NO conflict**;
  conflict axes populate only the differing axes.

### `app/position_analysis_backfill.py` (new — orchestration, importable + tested)

Mirrors `scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py` (importable logic, dry-run, stats, progress).

- SQL pre-filter: `evidence_contract_id == "resolver-complete-v2"`,
  `analysis_profile_id` in the authoritative-active set, `best_move_uci IS NOT NULL`,
  `best_line_uci IS NOT NULL`, ordered by `normalized_fen_before`; Python applies full
  `is_eligible_position_candidate` and groups; NULL `normalized_fen_before` handled via
  `normalize_fen(fen_before)`.
- Per group: `select_position_winner` → build the **winner-stamp** dict (position facts +
  metadata, `source_cache_id = winner.cache_id`, `source = "precomputed"`,
  `evidence_contract_id = "position-complete-v1"` — the stored row genuinely satisfies
  the position contract; legacy-v2 provenance kept via `source_cache_id`). Re-validate
  `_validate_position_complete` before persisting (defensive).
- **ORM upsert with ownership guard + conditional no-op:**
  - Query existing `position_analysis` by `normalized_fen`.
  - **No existing row** → INSERT (`winners_inserted++`).
  - **Existing row with `source_cache_id IS NULL`** (a future Phase-3 native write) →
    **leave untouched** (`skipped_existing_protected++`); backfill never clobbers a
    natively-written winner.
  - **Existing backfill-owned row** (`source_cache_id IS NOT NULL`) → compare the
    winner-stamp field-set to the stored row; **equal → no-op** (`winners_unchanged++`,
    so `updated_at` does not churn); **different → ORM update** (`winners_updated++`,
    `updated_at` advances legitimately via `onupdate`). Deterministic recompute always
    yields the strongest available winner, so updates only move forward.
- **Conflicts (append-only + content-signature dedupe):** on `is_conflict`, build axes +
  `conflict_signature`; query existing conflict rows for that `normalized_fen`; insert a
  new `PositionAnalysisConflict` (with `position_analysis_id` = winner id) **only when no
  existing row matches the signature** (`conflicts_recorded++` / else
  `conflicts_skipped_duplicate++`). No deletes — append-only contract preserved.
- `dry_run`: single rollback at end, log stats. `PositionBackfillStats`:
  `groups_scanned`, `candidates_eligible`, `winners_inserted`, `winners_updated`,
  `winners_unchanged`, `skipped_existing_protected`, `conflicts_recorded`,
  `conflicts_skipped_duplicate`, `skipped_no_eligible`, `skipped_unparseable_fen`.

### `scripts/backfill_position_analysis.py` (new — thin CLI)

Mirrors `scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py`: `sys.path` bootstrap, `_safe_database_url`
print, argparse `--dry-run`, `--limit`, `--normalized-fen` (targeted single-position
repair, e.g. g-ul4p), `--batch-size`, `--progress-every`; opens `SessionLocal`, calls
`backfill_position_analysis(db, ...)`, prints stats.

### Acceptance reconciliation (decision #3)

Update the Phase-2 bead's ACCEPTANCE wording from "records conflicting … best-move/PV/
eval/mate candidates" to **"records best-move and mate-winner disagreements (with
candidate detail; PV/eval differences captured in the audit columns when a best-move or
mate conflict fires, but not themselves triggers)"** — and note that the parent epic's
broader phrasing is satisfied at the architecturally-meaningful best-move/mate grain.
`position-complete-v1` only requires PV-first == best (`evidence_contracts.py:65`), so
PV-continuation and CP-only differences are intentionally not standalone conflicts.

## Files

- **New:** `backend/app/position_analysis_policy.py`,
  `backend/app/position_analysis_backfill.py`,
  `backend/scripts/backfill_position_analysis.py`,
  `backend/test_position_analysis_policy.py`,
  `backend/test_position_analysis_backfill.py`.
- **Edit:** `backend/app/analysis_profiles.py` (`StrengthComparison`,
  `compare_search_strength`, `_STRENGTH_INVARIANT_FIELDS`, `AUTHORITATIVE_PROFILE_PRIORITY`);
  `backend/test_analysis_profiles.py`.
- **Reuse (no edit):** `legacy_v2_satisfies_position` / `_validate_position_complete`
  (`evidence_contracts.py`), `_is_authoritative` (`api/analysis.py`),
  `IDENTITY_FIELDS` / `get_profile` (`analysis_profiles.py`), `normalize_fen` (`fen.py`),
  `encode_uci_line`/`decode_uci_line` + `PositionAnalysisRow` / `PositionAnalysisConflict`
  (`models.py`).
- **Beads:** update Phase-2 acceptance (above); create follow-up bead for browser
  `search_limit_value` gap + dynamic per-device browser depth.

## Verification

- `cd backend && .venv/bin/pytest test_position_analysis_policy.py
  test_position_analysis_backfill.py test_analysis_profiles.py test_evidence_contracts.py
  test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py` — new suites pass; Phase-1 xfail consumer tests
  still `xfailed` (Phase 2 does not touch read paths). Run files in isolation (pre-push
  suite is flaky under parallel load).
- **g-ul4p:** seed canonical `c1f4`/best-`c2c4` + browser `c2c4`/best-`c1f4` → backfill
  writes `position_analysis.best_move_uci="c2c4"`, browser drives nothing, NO conflict row.
- **Rerun idempotency:** run backfill twice on the same sqlite DB → second run reports
  `winners_unchanged == groups`, `winners_updated == 0`, `conflicts_recorded == 0`
  (`conflicts_skipped_duplicate` > 0 where conflicts existed), and `updated_at` unchanged.
- **Native-row protection:** pre-insert a `position_analysis` row with
  `source_cache_id = NULL`; backfill leaves it untouched (`skipped_existing_protected`).
- **Dry-run:** `python scripts/backfill_position_analysis.py --dry-run` writes nothing.

## Commit (after user review — no commit without review)

Stage path-by-path (multi-agent workspace rule): the two `app/` modules, the script,
`analysis_profiles.py`, the test files. Commit the beads ledger change (acceptance edit,
close `g-position-analysis.2`, new follow-up bead) in the **same** commit as the code,
direct to `master`.
close_reason: Phase 2 backfill implemented: group-then-pick canonical position winners, guarded strength comparator, append-only signature-deduped conflicts, idempotent reruns, native-row protection, dry-run-only --limit. Review findings addressed.

title: Position analysis Phase 1: storage tables + grain-specific contracts + consumer-bug tests
description:
Sub-task of epic **g-position-analysis** — Phase 1 of the master plan (see the parent epic's DESIGN → "Phased Implementation"; the full plan stays in the parent and is the source of truth).

## Goal

Lay the foundation for separating trusted position truth from move evidence: add the storage tables and grain-specific trust/contract helpers, while keeping the existing canonical reads trusted during the transition. End the phase with failing/red tests that pin the live non-trust-gated consumers so later phases start from the verified bug.

## Work

1. Add `position_analysis` table (single winner per `normalized_fen`) in all three schema locations:
   - SQLAlchemy model in `backend/app/models.py`
   - Alembic migration
   - Hand-written SQLite test schema in `backend/conftest.py` (`_create_test_schema`)
   Required columns: `id`, `normalized_fen` (UNIQUE, `uq_position_analysis_normalized_fen`), representative `fen` (provenance/sample only), `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate` (first-class, NOT conditional), `source`, `analysis_profile_id`, engine/build/search-depth metadata, `evidence_contract_id`, provenance/debug fields, timestamps.
2. Add `position_analysis_conflicts` table in the same three locations: `normalized_fen`, selected `position_analysis_id` (nullable), disagreeing candidate cache-row ids/summaries, disagreement fields (`best_move`, `pv`, `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`), policy reason, timestamps. This is a real storage sink — do not rely on logs/comments.
3. Introduce grain-specific contracts in `backend/app/evidence_contracts.py`:
   - **Position-complete contract**: requires `best_move_uci`, a multi-move `best_line_uci` whose first move equals best move, and either finite CP `best_eval` or explicit `best_eval_mate`.
   - **Move-complete contract**: requires `played_eval` or explicit played-mate, enum-valid `classification`, and a retained eval-loss snapshot only if documented as tied to the same canonical position winner.
   - Keep `resolver-complete-v2` registered as a LEGACY read/projection contract. Do NOT remove it or make it fail — that would mass-untrust existing canonical rows mid-migration.
4. Add legacy-v2 projection helpers so existing authoritative `analysis_cache` v2 rows can project into both grain-specific trust decisions during transition.
5. Add tests that pin the live non-trust-gated consumers so later phases have a red baseline:
   - `backend/app/tree_eval.py` including `lookup_move_evals` (untrusted normalized-fallback reads)
   - session drill-review export in `backend/app/api/session.py`
   - the mixed canonical/browser sibling-row case from g-ul4p

## Naming boundary

`position_analysis` (new storage table, keyed by `normalized_fen`) collides by name with the existing `position_analysis: dict[str, PositionAnalysis]` session response field / pydantic model (keyed by full `fen_before`). These are different grains. Keep the boundary explicit in naming and adapters; a storage row must never be returned as the session map directly.
design:
## Phase 1 Implementation Plan — storage tables + grain-specific contracts + consumer-bug tests

Source of truth for the overall architecture is the parent epic g-position-analysis DESIGN. This is the concrete Phase-1 build plan.

### Scope boundary (what Phase 1 does NOT do)

- Do NOT modify `backend/app/api/analysis.py` `_trust_flags`, `backend/app/tree_eval.py`, or `backend/app/api/session.py` consumer logic. Read-path cutover is Phase 4; trust-flag split is Phase 4/5. Phase 1 only builds the storage + contract + projection primitives those phases consume, and pins the current bug with red-baseline tests.
- Do NOT implement the position write policy (Phase 3) or backfill (Phase 2). The `position_analysis_conflicts` table is created but only written by Phase 2.
- Keep `resolver-complete-v2` registered and unchanged so existing authoritative canonical rows stay trusted during transition.

### 1. `position_analysis` storage table (3 schema locations)

ORM class name: `PositionAnalysisRow` (table `position_analysis`). Name is deliberately distinct from the `PositionAnalysis` pydantic model + `position_analysis: dict[str, PositionAnalysis]` response field in `backend/app/api/session.py`. Those are full-FEN-keyed session wire grain; this is normalized-FEN-keyed storage grain. Storage rows must never be returned as the session map directly.

Locations:
- `backend/app/models.py` — SQLAlchemy model using `BIGINT_SQLITE` for id, mirroring `AnalysisCache` column conventions/comments.
- New Alembic migration `backend/alembic/versions/20260617_01_create_position_analysis.py`, `revision = "20260617_01"`, `down_revision = "20260616_01"` (current single head). Use `op.create_table` with `sa.BigInteger().with_variant(sa.Integer(), "sqlite")` for bigint cols, exactly like `20260616_01_create_opening_position_edges.py`.
- `backend/conftest.py` — hand-written SQLite DDL in `_create_test_schema`, plus `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS position_analysis` in `_reset_test_schema` (drop before analysis_cache; order is irrelevant since no FK).

Columns:
- Identity/key: `id` PK autoincrement; `normalized_fen` Text NOT NULL with `UniqueConstraint("normalized_fen", name="uq_position_analysis_normalized_fen")`; `fen` Text NOT NULL (representative/provenance sample from the winning run — NOT used for lookup or uniqueness).
- Position facts: `best_move_uci` String(5) NOT NULL (a stored winner without a best move is meaningless); `best_move_san` String(10) nullable; `best_line_uci` Text nullable; `best_eval` Integer nullable; `best_eval_mate` Integer nullable, white-relative mate count. `best_eval_mate` is first-class/unconditional — omitting it would silently lose forced-mate preference when Phase 4 cuts `_root_sort_key`/`_move_sort_key` over.
- Evidence metadata (mirror AnalysisCache): `source` String(20) NOT NULL server_default 'precomputed'; `analysis_profile_id` String(64); `engine_name` String(64); `engine_version` String(64); `engine_build` String(128); `network_id` String(128); `search_limit_type` String(16); `search_limit_value` Integer; `threads` Integer; `hash_mb` Integer; `multipv` Integer; `eval_file_id` Text; `eval_file_small_id` Text; `analyzer_protocol_version` String(64); `profile_manifest_digest` String(64); `evidence_contract_id` String(64).
- Provenance/debug: `source_cache_id` BIGINT_SQLITE nullable (the `analysis_cache.id` the winner was projected/backfilled from; audit trail for Phase 2).
- Timestamps: `created_at` DateTime(tz) server_default func.now() NOT NULL; `updated_at` DateTime(tz) server_default func.now() onupdate func.now() NOT NULL (position winners are replaced over time, unlike append-only cache rows).
- **`updated_at` write-path caveat (review finding 4):** ORM `onupdate=func.now()` fires only on ORM-flush UPDATE and Core `update()`. It does NOT fire on `insert().on_conflict_do_update()` / bulk upserts, which is how Phase 2 backfill and Phase 3 winner-replacement will likely write. Phase 1 documents the requirement in a model comment: any Core upsert/replacement path MUST set `updated_at` explicitly in its conflict-update set (or we add a DB trigger / `server_onupdate`) so winner-replacement audit time is not silently stale. No Phase-1 code writes this table, so this is a documented contract for Phases 2/3, not Phase-1 logic.

### 2. `position_analysis_conflicts` storage table (3 schema locations)

ORM class `PositionAnalysisConflict` (table `position_analysis_conflicts`). Real storage sink for backfill disagreements — never logs/comments. Same 3 locations + `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS position_analysis_conflicts` in `_reset_test_schema`.

Columns:
- `id` PK; `normalized_fen` Text NOT NULL with `Index("idx_position_analysis_conflicts_norm", "normalized_fen")` (non-unique — append-only audit, many records possible per fen over recomputes).
- `position_analysis_id` BIGINT_SQLITE nullable (the selected winner when one was chosen; plain nullable bigint, no FK, to keep backfill/delete ordering simple in both Postgres and the FK-off SQLite test schema).
- Candidate detail: `candidate_cache_ids` Text (JSON array of `analysis_cache.id`); `candidate_summaries` Text (JSON array of `{cache_id, source, profile, contract, best_move_uci, best_line_uci, best_eval, best_eval_mate}`).
- Per-axis disagreement (JSON array of distinct candidate values, NULL when that axis agreed): `best_move_disagreement`, `pv_disagreement`, `best_eval_disagreement`, `best_eval_mate_disagreement`. Per-axis columns (not one blob) so Phase 2 audits can filter by axis; mate disagreement is captured first-class.
- `policy_reason` String(64) (e.g. `selected_dominant`, `conflict_quarantine`, `conflict_best_known_kept`).
- `created_at` DateTime(tz) server_default func.now() NOT NULL (no `updated_at`; append-only).

### 3. Grain-specific evidence contracts (`backend/app/evidence_contracts.py`, additive)

Keep `resolver-complete-v2` and the whole existing registry/supersedes graph untouched (it governs `analysis_cache` write policy; disturbing it would mass-untrust canonical rows).

Note on `Contract.required_fields` (review finding 2): verified that nothing in the codebase reads `Contract.required_fields` — `contract_satisfied` is driven solely by `Contract.validate`. The field is declarative documentation, so it must HONESTLY describe always-required fields; OR-disjunctions belong in `validate`, not `required_fields`. Add a one-line test in `test_evidence_contracts.py` asserting this is informational-only (e.g. that a contract whose `required_fields` lists a field still validates a row populating the alternative), so a future reader does not wire `required_fields` into logic expecting it to be exhaustive.

Add two contracts, each `supersedes=frozenset()` (independent of the resolver family — legacy projection is handled by the helpers in section 4, not by registry supersession):

- `POSITION_COMPLETE = "position-complete-v1"`:
  - `required_fields = frozenset({"best_move_uci", "best_line_uci"})` (both are unconditionally required; the best_eval/best_eval_mate disjunction is validator-enforced, NOT listed here).
  - `validate = _validate_position_complete(data)`: `_pv_first_equals_best(data)` (existing helper: best_move present, multi-move `best_line_uci`, `line[0] == best_move_uci`) AND (`_is_finite_int(best_eval)` OR `_is_finite_int(best_eval_mate)`). No `fen_before`/`eval_delta`/board construction — position grain carries no played-move delta.

- `MOVE_COMPLETE = "move-complete-v1"`:
  - `required_fields = frozenset({"classification"})` (the only unconditionally-required field; played_eval is NOT always required because played-mate is an accepted alternative). Changed from the earlier `{"played_eval"}` plan, which mis-described the contract. A code comment states the played_eval-OR-played_eval_mate disjunction is enforced by `validate`.
  - `validate = _validate_move_complete(data)`: (`_is_finite_int(played_eval)` OR `_is_finite_int(played_eval_mate)`) AND `classification in VALID_CLASSIFICATIONS`. Deliberately does NOT validate `eval_delta == f(best_eval, played_eval)` — a move-only row has no `best_eval`, which is exactly why post-split move rows cannot use v2. Snapshot-provenance ("eval-loss snapshot retained only if tied to the same canonical position winner") is a write-time concern deferred to Phase 3, documented in a code comment here.

Export the new constants and include them in `_CONTRACTS` so `get_contract`/`contract_satisfied` resolve them. Do NOT add them to `BROWSER_ALLOWED_CONTRACTS`.

### 4. Legacy-v2 projection helpers (`evidence_contracts.py`, library-only, unwired in Phase 1)

Let an existing authoritative `analysis_cache` v2 row project into both grain-specific trust decisions during transition, before backfill exists:

- `project_v2_to_position(data) -> dict`: `{best_move_uci, best_line_uci, best_eval, best_eval_mate}` pulled from a cache-row dict.
- `project_v2_to_move(data) -> dict`: `{played_eval, played_eval_mate, classification, eval_delta}`.
- `legacy_v2_satisfies_position(data) -> bool`: `_validate_position_complete(project_v2_to_position(data))`.
- `legacy_v2_satisfies_move(data) -> bool`: `_validate_move_complete(project_v2_to_move(data))`.

Note: `project_v2_to_move` needs `played_eval_mate`, which `analysis.py._row_contract_data` does not currently include — when Phase 4/5 wires these helpers it must extend that projection. Phase 1 only defines + unit-tests the helpers; nothing imports them yet.

### 5. Red-baseline consumer-bug tests — `backend/test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py`

Mechanism (decided): `@pytest.mark.xfail(reason="g-position-analysis Phase 4 cutover — untrusted row currently drives result", strict=True)`. CI/pre-push stays green now (expected-fail); when a later phase fixes the consumer the test xpasses and strict-mode FAILS it, forcing the implementer to drop the marker and assert for real.

**Authoring rules (the xfail must actually xfail TODAY, not XPASS):**
- All references to not-yet-existing API live INSIDE test function bodies — never at module import — so an AttributeError is caught as xfail rather than breaking collection.
- Use DIRECT attribute access for future fields, never `getattr(obj, "field", default)` (review finding 1). `getattr(entry, "position_trusted", False) is False` returns `True` TODAY (default kicks in) → the test passes → strict-xfail turns that into an XPASS failure, breaking the suite immediately. Instead assert `entry.position_trusted is False`: today `PositionAnalysis` (session.py:127) has no such field, so attribute access raises AttributeError → xfailed; after Phase 4 marks untrusted seeds `position_trusted=False`, the assert passes → XPASS → strict-fail tripwire.

Per the trust-gate≠correctness rule, every test asserts BOTH (a) the untrusted value did not drive the result AND (b) the positive correct/unavailable outcome — never merely "result != browser value."

**Trusted vs untrusted row construction (review finding 3):** green companion tests that must pass before AND after cutover have to seed FULL canonical identity, not just `source="precomputed"`. Post-cutover trust uses `_is_authoritative` (analysis.py:88) = profile authoritative+active AND every `IDENTITY_FIELDS` column matches `get_profile(CANONICAL_PROFILE_ID)`. Mirror the existing `_canonical_v2_seed_values()` helper (test_analysis_cache_api.py:709): stamp `analysis_profile_id = CANONICAL_PROFILE_ID`, all `IDENTITY_FIELDS` from `get_profile(CANONICAL_PROFILE_ID)`, and `evidence_contract_id = "resolver-complete-v2"`. Untrusted rows in the xfail tests use `analysis_profile_id = "browser-game-v1"` + `evidence_contract_id = "resolver-complete-v1"` (non-authoritative, identity will not match). Factor a local `_trusted_canonical_values()` / `_untrusted_browser_values()` helper in the new test module so every test seeds consistently.

Tests:

1. `lookup_move_evals` untrusted normalized-fallback read (`tree_eval.py`):
   - xfail: insert ONLY an untrusted browser row supplying a `played_eval` for `(normalized_fen, move_uci)`; assert `lookup_move_evals` returns `None` for that request (no trusted eval) — currently it returns the browser eval via the unfiltered normalized fallback.
   - companion green test: with a FULL-identity trusted canonical row present, `lookup_move_evals` returns the canonical eval (passes now and after cutover — guards against over-correction). Today tree_eval picks canonical only via `_source_rank`; after cutover it must pick it via trust, which the full-identity seed guarantees.

2. g-ul4p mixed canonical/browser sibling case (`tree_eval` root/move ranking):
   - Reproduce FEN `rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3P4/5N2/PPP1PPPP/RNBQKB1R w KQkq - 0 3` with the two documented sibling rows: a canonical `c1f4` row whose best move is `c2c4` (stamp full canonical identity, profile `canonical-sf18-depth24-linux-v1`, contract `resolver-complete-v2`); a browser `c2c4` row whose best move is `c1f4` (browser-game-v1, resolver-complete-v1).
   - xfail: assert root best-move/eval resolves from the canonical row (`c2c4`), independent of the browser sibling — currently `_root_sort_key` has no authoritative/contract/trust filter so the browser row can surface.

3. Session `position_analysis` export seed (`session.py`):
   - Build a session whose SessionMove best-move seed comes from an untrusted/legacy source.
   - xfail: `assert entry.position_trusted is False` (direct access — AttributeError today → xfailed; aligns with the epic's "carry position_trusted ... or mark legacy/untrusted seeds false").
   - companion green characterization test: assert the CURRENT shape (entry present, `best_move_uci` from the seed, no trust signal) so Phase 4 can see exactly what changes.

### 6. Contract + projection unit tests — extend `backend/test_evidence_contracts.py`

Green now (these are pure library additions, not consumer bugs):
- `position-complete-v1`: accepts a valid position row (PV first == best, finite best_eval); accepts mate-only (`best_eval_mate` set, `best_eval` None); rejects single-move PV; rejects PV whose first move != best_move; rejects no eval at all.
- `move-complete-v1`: accepts finite `played_eval` + valid classification; accepts played-mate + valid classification; rejects invalid/missing classification; rejects no played eval/mate; confirms it does NOT require/validate `eval_delta`.
- `required_fields` is informational-only: a `move-complete-v1` row carrying `played_eval_mate` (not `played_eval`) still passes `contract_satisfied`, documenting that `required_fields` is not consulted by validation (review finding 2).
- Projection: a valid v2 cache-row dict satisfies both `legacy_v2_satisfies_position` and `legacy_v2_satisfies_move`; a v2 row missing the PV fails position projection; a v2 row with bad classification fails move projection.
- `resolver-complete-v2` regression: existing v2 tests still pass (registry untouched).

### 7. Verification

- Run targeted files in isolation (pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load): `cd backend && .venv/bin/pytest test_evidence_contracts.py test_position_analysis_consumer_bugs.py test_session_api.py test_tree_eval.py` (per the repo's standard invocation). Confirm the new consumer-bug tests report `xfailed` (NOT `xpassed`/`error` — an XPASS means an authoring-rule violation per finding 1), contract/projection unit tests pass, and no existing test regresses.
- Alembic round-trip: `alembic upgrade head` then `alembic downgrade -1` on a scratch DB to confirm the new migration's up/down both work and that head stays single.
- Confirm `conftest._create_test_schema` parity: the three schema locations agree on columns/constraints for both new tables (per the project's hand-written-SQLite-schema rule).

### Commit

Per project convention: commit directly to master, but only after user review (no commit without review). Stage path-by-path (multi-agent workspace rule): the new migration, `models.py`, `conftest.py`, `evidence_contracts.py`, and the two test files. Commit the beads ledger separately.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: storage tables + grain contracts + red-baseline consumer-bug tests; reviewed and approved

title: Tree cold-cache: non-blocking bootstrap + UI initialization state
description:
Follow-up to g-tree-fast-cache. On a cold or registry-stale read, GET /api/openings/tree currently BLOCKS in ensure_tree_cache -> refresh_now for the one-time ~22-25s bootstrap, then returns the built tree. The slow wait IS the request, so the UI can only show a generic long spinner with no specific messaging. The cache_state signal (warm_fresh / bootstrapped / book_only / bootstrap_timeout) is computed but never leaves the backend (it only goes into the timings dict + log line; TreeResponse does not carry it).

Goal: let the UI detect a cold cache and show an explicit one-time 'Setting up your opening tree...' state instead of a silent 22s spinner, by flipping the cold path from blocking to non-blocking + poll.

Cost model recap (why this is rare): the blocking bootstrap fires only when there is no current-registry batch for (user, player_color) -- i.e. genuinely first open per color, or the first read after a registry-changing deploy (schema/model/divider/quality version bump, config, or book/roots change). Playing new games does NOT trigger it (that changes the raw-inputs digest -> background revalidate, non-blocking).
design:
Tree cold-cache: non-blocking bootstrap + UI initialization state (g-k4z2)

CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (refines the original A/B design with the decisions
made after reading the code).

== Backend ==

1. New helper `resolve_tree_cache_state(db, user_id, player_color, graph, roots) -> str`
   in `app/opening_cache.py`, next to `ensure_tree_cache`. CHEAP probe — NO overlay
   build, NO refresh_now (never blocks). Returns "warm" | "building" | "cold".
   Logic (reuses existing primitives):
     current_registry = opening_score_inputs_fingerprint(graph, roots)
     batch = get_latest_opening_score_batch(db, user_id, player_color)
     a) batch present AND registry_fingerprint == current_registry  -> "warm"
     b) batch is None AND not has_opening_evidence(...)              -> "warm"
        (a no-evidence/no-batch user's tree is correctly book-only and /tree is
        FAST — recompute_opening_scores_if_needed returns None without writing a
        batch for them, so polling would otherwise NEVER flip to warm. Reporting
        warm lets the UI load /tree directly.)
     c) otherwise a recompute WILL produce a current-registry batch
        (cold-with-evidence, or registry/schema drift — both write a batch):
          already = is_recompute_scheduled(user_id, player_color)   # non-mutating
          if not already: request_recompute(user_id, player_color)  # BACKGROUND
          return "building" if already else "cold"
        Firing only when not already scheduled avoids redundant coalesced
        re-enqueues; a failed/missing recompute auto-retries on the next poll.

2. New scheduler primitive `OpeningScoreScheduler.is_scheduled(user_id, color)` +
   module facade `is_recompute_scheduled(...)` in `app/opening_score_scheduler.py`:
   non-mutating `key in _pending or key in _inflight` under the lock. Facade
   swallows/logs like the other facades.

3. New route `GET /api/openings/tree/status?player_color=` in `app/api/openings.py`:
   resolves graph+roots, calls resolve_tree_cache_state, returns
   `TreeStatusResponse{ player_color, state }`. No db.rollback (read-only, no heavy
   work after).

4. Part A: add `cache_state: str = "warm_fresh"` to `TreeResponse`; the /tree route
   sets `response.cache_state = cache_state` after build (value already computed at
   the ensure_tree_cache call). Lets a DIRECT /tree caller still see a degraded
   book_only/bootstrap_timeout tree. The /tree blocking cold branch is LEFT AS-IS
   (it stays the correctness fallback for direct/legacy callers so a book-only tree
   is never served silently); the UI simply never triggers it because it gates on
   status=warm first.

== Frontend ==

5. `src/utils/api.ts`: add `TreeCacheState = "warm"|"building"|"cold"`,
   `TreeStatusResponse`, and `getOpeningTreeStatus(playerColor, {signal})`. Add
   optional `cache_state?: string` to the `TreeResponse` interface.

6. `src/hooks/useOpeningsTree.ts`: gate the /tree fetch behind cache warmth.
   - PageStatus gains "initializing".
   - `warmColorsRef: Set<color>` memoizes confirmed-warm colors for the session
     (warm stays warm until a deploy/page reload), so the status probe runs at most
     once per color — warm reads are unchanged (one extra cheap probe on first load
     of each color, behaviorally identical otherwise).
   - The effect keeps the existing synchronous provisional/loading setRender, then:
       if warmColorsRef has color: runFetch()  (today's getOpeningTree path)
       else: ensureWarm(color, signal, version).then(warm => { if current&&warm:
              warmColorsRef.add(color); runFetch() }).catch(pageOrAppendError)
   - ensureWarm polls getOpeningTreeStatus every STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS (2000ms),
     respecting the AbortSignal + versionRef guard. warm -> true (NO initializing
     render is ever shown for a warm/no-evidence user => no flash). building/cold ->
     setRender an "initializing" state (response:null => OpeningsPage shows the
     setup screen) and wait one interval. After ATTEMPT_CAP (~25 => ~50s) throw a
     retry-able "still being set up" error.
   - delay(ms, signal) rejects AbortError on abort; isAbortError already silences it.

7. `src/pages/OpeningsPage.tsx`: add a `pageStatus === "initializing"` branch BEFORE
   the generic `!view` loading branch — "Setting up your opening tree (one-time)…"
   with a short sub-message + reuse the board/column skeleton. Optionally surface
   `view`/response cache_state === "bootstrap_timeout" as a retry note (secondary).

== Tests ==
- backend test_tree_api.py: status warm (current-registry batch), warm (no batch +
  no evidence), cold (no batch + evidence, idle scheduler -> request_recompute fired
  once), building (is_recompute_scheduled True -> not re-fired). Assert overlay_evidence
  NOT called and refresh_now NOT called in all (no blocking bootstrap / no overlay).
- backend test_opening_score_scheduler.py: is_scheduled True while pending/inflight,
  False when idle.
- frontend: useOpeningsTree/OpeningsPage — existing tests get a default
  getOpeningTreeStatus mock => "warm" (behaviorally unchanged). New tests: building
  then warm shows the initializing screen then loads the tree; warm path shows no
  initializing flash and issues one /tree fetch.
acceptance_criteria: Cold (user, color) first open shows an explicit 'initializing' UI state, not a silent 22s spinner. Status check does NOT trigger the blocking bootstrap (no overlay rebuild). Warm reads unchanged (still serve cached + background revalidate). bootstrap_timeout surfaces to the UI as a retry-able state. Tests: status endpoint returns cold/building/warm correctly without building overlay; warm path still no overlay rebuild.
notes:
Review fixes (still pending review, NOT committed):
(1) Setup-flow failures now surface as retry-able PAGE errors, not append errors. Root cause: onReject branched on displayedRef, so a poll timeout/failure after a previous tree was shown took the append-error path and left the initializing screen pinned with no Retry + polling stopped. Fix: dedicated setSetupError/onSetupError (always response:null page error); ensureWarm chain catches via onSetupError. New hook test covers the cold color-switch timeout.
(2) ensure_tree_cache now short-circuits no-batch/no-evidence to book_only WITHOUT refresh_now (TREE_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=30s, so the old path could block behind the single scheduler worker). Mirrors resolve_tree_cache_state. Updated test_ensure_tree_cache_no_evidence_returns_book_only (refresh_now NOT called) and the no-batch timeout test (now seeds evidence via has_opening_evidence patch).
(3) Hook now handles response.cache_state==='bootstrap_timeout': drops the warm memo and surfaces a retry-able setup state instead of caching/rendering the degraded book-only tree as ready. New hook test covers it.
All green: full backend (1332), tsc -b, eslint, hook (6) + page (28) vitest.
close_reason: Implemented non-blocking cold-cache bootstrap + UI initializing state: GET /api/openings/tree/status probe (resolve_tree_cache_state), scheduler is_scheduled, cache_state on TreeResponse, no-evidence short-circuit in ensure_tree_cache, and a frontend per-color status-poll gate with a 'Setting up…' screen + retry-able bootstrap_timeout handling. Review approved.

title: Separate trusted position analysis from move evidence
description:
## Problem

`analysis_cache` is keyed by `(fen_before, move_uci)`. That is the correct grain for played-move evidence: played eval, eval-loss snapshots, classification, recording evidence, and SRS evidence are facts about one specific move from one specific position.

The same row also stores `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, and `best_eval`. Those are position-level facts. They should not vary by which move was played. Because they are duplicated across sibling `(fen_before, move_uci)` rows, mixed-source coverage can let a lower-trust browser row appear to redefine the best move for the whole position in consumers that do not apply the backend trust contract.

`g-ul4p` exposed the data shape. For FEN `rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3P4/5N2/PPP1PPPP/RNBQKB1R w KQkq - 0 3`, production has sibling rows for different played moves:

- `c1f4` / Bf4: canonical `precomputed`, profile `canonical-sf18-depth24-linux-v1`, contract `resolver-complete-v2`, best move `c2c4`, `eval_delta=0`.
- `c2c4` / c4: browser-game row, profile `browser-game-v1`, contract `resolver-complete-v1`, best move `c1f4`, `eval_delta=0`.

These rows do not conflict under the current unique constraint because the played moves differ. The architectural bug is the row grain: a move row carries independent position-best truth.

Important correction: the live `/api/analysis/lookup` drill path is already trust-gated today. `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` and `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts` both require `isTrustedCacheHit(cached)` before converting a cached row into a worker result. `backend/app/api/analysis.py` only marks `trusted_for_resolution` true for effectively authoritative `resolver-complete-v2` rows that satisfy the contract. A `browser-game-v1` / `resolver-complete-v1` row cannot pass that gate, so at the `g-ul4p` position the stale browser row does not directly grade live drill strictness. The fallback worker may still diverge from canonical precompute, but that is different from untrusted cache evidence driving the verdict.

The current live non-trust-gated consumers are higher priority:

- `backend/app/tree_eval.py`: `lookup_root_eval` and move/root ranking (`_root_sort_key`, `_move_sort_key`) choose among `analysis_cache` rows by mate/source/id and best-move-row preference, with no authoritative/profile/contract/trust filter. A browser row's `best_eval` or `played_eval` can surface in the opening tree.
- `backend/app/api/session.py`: the drill-review `position_analysis` response is built directly from `SessionMove.best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_move_eval_cp`, and `best_line_uci` with no trust signal. This is the payload consumed by `src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts` and `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`, and it is the surface related to `g-54h5`.

The first implementation slice must therefore prioritize trusted position payload production and cutover for `tree_eval.py` and session drill-review export. The frontend lookup trust split and drill grading rewrite are still needed, but they are plumbing for the new payload shape and future strictness semantics, not the currently verified cache-trust bypass.

## Existing Architecture To Preserve

Do not assume `analysis_cache` already stores many rows per cache key and chooses trust at read time. Today it does the opposite:

- `AnalysisCache` is unique on `(fen_before, move_uci)`.
- `decide_analysis_cache_replacement` lives in `backend/app/analysis_cache_policy.py` and resolves conflicts at write time using incoming validity, effective profile identity, authoritative dominance, and evidence-contract supersession.
- Browser-game rows can write new `(fen_before, move_uci)` keys, but non-authoritative rows cannot replace authoritative rows for the same key.

The position-level fix should reuse this proven write-time dominance/supersession model instead of introducing read-time profile selection unless a later design explicitly chooses that larger migration.

## Architecture Decision

Add a single-winner `position_analysis` table keyed by `normalized_fen`, with profile/contract/engine fields stored as metadata on the winning row, not as part of the default unique key.

This table stores the canonical position winner after the same kind of dominance/supersession policy used by `analysis_cache`. It must structurally enforce that browser-game writes never insert or replace trusted position truth when canonical coverage exists.

Reject for this bead: a multi-row position table keyed by `(normalized_fen, profile, contract)` plus read-time trusted-row selection. That would require new selector logic in every lookup path and duplicates the trust decision that the cache policy already centralizes.

## Grain And Keys

Position analysis is keyed on `normalized_fen`, not full `fen`.

Reasons:

- `tree_eval.py` already treats best-move/best-eval truth as normalized-grain data via `normalized_fen_before` fallback.
- `normalize_fen` drops move clocks and canonicalizes en passant, so best move is well-defined at this grain.
- `opening_position_scores` is batch-scoped aggregate win-rate data and has no engine fields, so it does not replace this table. The new table is for engine position truth, not opening aggregate stats.

Store full `fen` only as a representative/provenance sample from the winning analysis run. The initial schema must include `UniqueConstraint("normalized_fen", name="uq_position_analysis_normalized_fen")`.

Keep `analysis_cache.fen_before` as the move-grain name. Drop `position_fen` aliases from the move-table design unless a separate compatibility adapter needs one.

## Related Work And g-54h5

`g-54h5` is blocked because the analysis-board engine-line panel seeds line 1 from session/client `PositionAnalysis` without a trust signal, excludes that move from live search, then prepends the stale/untrusted cached line without re-ranking. That is the same duplicated best-move truth problem in a display consumer.

This bead must produce a trusted position payload that `g-54h5` can consume. The `g-54h5` implementation can then skip live search only when the cached seed is `position_trusted`, and otherwise fall back to full MultiPV search or re-rank searched alternatives. This bead does not need to fix the panel ordering itself, but it must provide the trust surface needed by that fix.

## Tracking Note

Keep this as one task for now. Do not convert it to an epic or create phase sub-beads in this rewrite. The implementation phases in the design are intentionally written so each phase can become a child bead later. When that split happens, `g-54h5` should depend on the payload-producing phases only, roughly Phases 1-4, rather than waiting for the frontend drill rewrite and broad cleanup phases.
design:
## Target Data Flow

1. Canonical precompute analyzes a position and writes the storage table `position_analysis(normalized_fen)` through a position-level dominance/supersession policy.
2. The stored position row keeps representative `fen`, `normalized_fen`, best-move/PV/best-eval facts, profile/engine/search/contract metadata, source provenance, and timestamps. Profile/contract identify the winning evidence; they are not part of the default unique key.
3. Canonical played-move analysis writes `analysis_cache(fen_before, move_uci)` as move evidence only: `move_san`, `played_eval`, mate equivalent, classification, source/profile/contract metadata, and optionally a verified canonical eval-loss snapshot.
4. Browser-game uploads may write move diagnostics for new move keys, subject to the existing move-row replacement policy. Browser-game uploads must not insert or replace trusted `position_analysis` rows unless a future explicit product decision creates a separate non-authoritative diagnostic table.
5. Read paths first resolve trusted position facts by `normalized_fen`, then resolve trusted move facts for the requested played move. Strict exact-best checks compare the played move to the trusted position row. Threshold checks derive loss from trusted position `best_eval` plus trusted move `played_eval` only when both are finite CP values.
6. Session drill-review export keeps its existing wire grain during migration: `backend/app/api/session.py` exposes `position_analysis: dict[str, PositionAnalysis]` keyed by full `fen_before`. Phase 4 must bridge the grains explicitly by looking up the storage row with `normalize_fen(move.fen_before)`, then emitting the session response keyed by the original full `move.fen_before`.

## Core Invariants

- `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`, and `best_eval_mate` are properties of `normalized_fen`, not of `(fen_before, move_uci)`.
- `analysis_cache` remains a single winning row per `(fen_before, move_uci)` and continues to use write-time replacement decisions.
- The storage table `position_analysis` is a single winning row per `normalized_fen` with `UniqueConstraint("normalized_fen")`.
- Full `fen` on the storage `position_analysis` row is provenance/sample data only. Lookups and uniqueness use `normalized_fen`.
- The name `position_analysis` is intentionally reused for the new storage table, while `session.py` already has a `position_analysis` response field and a `PositionAnalysis` pydantic model. These are different grains. Storage is normalized-FEN keyed; session wire output remains full-FEN keyed until the wire contract changes. Implementation must keep this boundary explicit in naming and adapters so a storage row is never returned as the session map directly.
- Trust is computed per grain. A trusted position row and a trusted move row can have different contracts because post-split rows no longer satisfy the old mixed-grain `resolver-complete-v2` contract.
- `resolver-complete-v2` remains a legacy read/projection contract during migration. New move-grain writes after the split must use the move-complete contract, never `resolver-complete-v2`, because v2 validates the cross-grain `eval_delta == f(best_eval, played_eval)` invariant and a move-only row can no longer satisfy it.
- Browser-game data cannot define strict position truth. Enforce this on write through the position policy, not only by filtering at read time.

## Schema

Add `position_analysis` in all three schema locations used by this repo:

- SQLAlchemy model in `backend/app/models.py`.
- Alembic migration.
- Hand-written SQLite test schema in `backend/conftest.py`.

Required columns include at least:

- Identity/key: `id`, `normalized_fen` unique, representative `fen`.
- Position facts: `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`, and `best_eval_mate`.
- Evidence metadata: `source`, `analysis_profile_id`, engine/build/search depth metadata, `evidence_contract_id`, timestamps.
- Provenance/debug metadata needed by the replacement policy and audits.

`best_eval_mate` is first-class, not conditional. Exact-best can use `best_move_uci` without mate-aware numeric loss, but `backend/app/tree_eval.py` already ranks mate-bearing rows ahead of CP rows in `_root_sort_key` and `_move_sort_key`. Omitting mate from the position row would silently lose forced-mate preference during the tree-eval cutover.

Add a real storage sink for backfill disagreements: `position_analysis_conflicts`. This table should also be added in `models.py`, Alembic, and `conftest.py`. It should record `normalized_fen`, selected `position_analysis_id` when available, disagreeing candidate cache row ids or summaries, disagreement fields (`best_move`, `pv`, `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`), policy reason, and timestamps. Do not rely on logs or comments as the conflict sink.

## Backfill And Repair

Backfill must source position facts from existing `AnalysisCache` rows, not from `OpeningPositionScore`. `AnalysisCache` already has the required position columns (`best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`) and an indexed `normalized_fen_before` column. Use `normalized_fen_before` for grouping when present; for null or legacy rows, compute `normalize_fen(fen_before)` before grouping.

Backfill must group first, then pick one winner per `normalized_fen`. Do not iterate cache rows and rely on `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` or unique-constraint ordering to choose a winner; the database conflict clause has no dominance logic and would make result order part of correctness.

Algorithm shape:

1. Source candidates from authoritative, contract-satisfied canonical evidence. During transition, eligible legacy v2 `analysis_cache` rows can provide both position and move facts.
2. Resolve the target `normalized_fen` from `normalized_fen_before` or `normalize_fen(fen_before)`.
3. Group candidates in memory or in an equivalent deterministic query by `normalized_fen`.
4. For each group, select the strongest canonical candidate using the same dominance concepts as `analysis_cache`: effective authoritative profile, contract successor/superset, profile-defined search strength/depth, and validity of position facts.
5. Emit exactly one `position_analysis` upsert/insert decision per `normalized_fen` group.
6. When candidates disagree on best move/PV/eval/mate, persist a `position_analysis_conflicts` row with enough candidate detail for audit/repair. Keep the selected best-known row only when the policy can justify it; otherwise quarantine or skip that group deliberately.

## Contract And Trust Migration

Keep `resolver-complete-v2` registered in `backend/app/evidence_contracts.py` as a legacy read contract throughout the payload-producing phases. Existing authoritative `analysis_cache` rows stamped v2 must continue to confer legacy position-grain and move-grain trust until backfill and read-path cutover are complete. Removing v2 or changing it to fail because no split row can satisfy it would mass-untrust existing canonical rows mid-migration.

Introduce grain-specific contracts:

- Position-complete contract: requires `best_move_uci`, a multi-move `best_line_uci` whose first move equals the best move, and either finite CP `best_eval` or an explicit `best_eval_mate` representation accepted for exact-best usage and tree ranking.
- Move-complete contract: requires `played_eval` or explicit played-mate representation, enum-valid `classification`, and any retained move-grain eval-loss snapshot only if that snapshot is documented as tied to the same canonical position winner.

Replace the read contract surface with grain-specific trust flags:

- `position_trusted`: the position row is effectively authoritative, uses the current position-complete contract or eligible legacy v2 projection, and satisfies that position contract.
- `move_trusted`: the move row is effectively authoritative, uses the current move-complete contract or eligible legacy v2 projection, and satisfies that move contract.

Backend work:

- Replace or wrap `backend/app/api/analysis.py` `_trust_flags(row)` with position and move trust helpers. Legacy `analysis_cache` v2 rows may project into both grain-specific trust decisions only during the transition.
- Keep diagnostic fields (`authoritative`, `contract_satisfied`, `evidence_contract_id`) per grain so callers can explain why a payload is or is not trusted.
- Once `position_analysis` read paths are fully cut over and backfill is verified, create a separate follow-up to deprecate legacy v2 semantics. Do not do that deprecation inside the early split phases.

## Position Write Policy

Route position writes through a new policy that mirrors `decide_analysis_cache_replacement` in `backend/app/analysis_cache_policy.py`:

- Reject invalid contract claims.
- Non-authoritative browser-game evidence cannot insert or replace trusted position truth.
- Same-profile authoritative supersets can merge when the contract explicitly allows it.
- Authoritative successors can replace weaker rows when dominance is explicit.
- Lower-trust browser evidence can remain move diagnostics in `analysis_cache`; it must not become position truth through `position_analysis`.

## Wire And Frontend Contract

`/api/analysis/lookup`, session drill-review export, and any compatibility adapter must stop returning or constructing one flattened object whose best-move/PV, played-eval/classification, and trust flag all come from a single move row.

Required response shape change, or equivalent compatibility layer:

- Position payload keyed by normalized FEN for canonical lookup surfaces: `best_move_uci`, `best_move_san`, `best_line_uci`, `best_eval`, `best_eval_mate`, `position_trusted`, and position evidence metadata.
- Session drill-review compatibility payload keyed by full `fen_before`: build each entry by resolving `normalize_fen(move.fen_before)` against the storage table, then emit the result under the original full FEN key expected by `position_analysis: dict[str, PositionAnalysis]` consumers.
- Move payload keyed by `(fen_before, move_uci)` unless a normalized fallback is deliberately proven correct for move semantics: `move_san`, `played_eval`, played mate field, `classification`, optional verified eval-loss snapshot, `move_trusted`, and move evidence metadata.
- If old flattened `CachedAnalysis` fields remain temporarily, they must be derived by merging position fields from the position payload and move fields from the move payload. They must not be copied from one `analysis_cache` row.

Frontend edits are plumbing for this new payload shape:

- `src/utils/api.ts` `CachedAnalysis`: represent separate position and move payloads, or explicitly mark transitional flattened fields as merged/deprecated, and replace `trusted_for_resolution` with `position_trusted` and `move_trusted`.
- `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`: split `canResolveCachedAnalysis` into position and move guards. The PV guard (`best_move_uci` + multi-move `best_line_uci`) belongs to the position payload. The classification/eval-loss guard belongs to the move payload. `isTrustedCacheHit` must become grain-specific or be removed.
- `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` and `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts`: preserve the existing protection that untrusted `analysis/lookup` rows do not drive live drill grading, but stop deriving `bestMove` from a move row once the split payload exists. Exact-best results must use the trusted position payload; move payloads provide played-move facts.
- Frontend tests that manufacture `trusted_for_resolution: true` must be migrated to the new grain-specific trust fields.

## Drill Semantics And g-l02q Ordering

Strictness 0 exact-best should depend only on a trusted position row. Compare the played move to `position_analysis.best_move_uci`. With canonical position winner `c2c4`, playing c4 passes and Bf4 fails, independent of whether a trusted move row exists for the played move.

Missing or untrusted move evidence must not block a strictness-0 exact-best verdict when the position row is trusted.

Record the current ordering interaction: `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts` `gradeDrillMove` returns `unavailable` when `evalLoss(delta) === null` before checking `strictnessCp <= 0`. The `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts` g-l02q comment relies on that current ordering to avoid false-passing when `best_move_uci` is null and `bestMove` falls back to the played move. Under the new split semantics, strictness 0 must run the best-move check against the trusted position row independent of move-eval availability. Threshold/eval-loss grading still depends on trusted move evidence.

## Eval-Loss Ownership And Mate Handling

Preferred design: derive drill eval loss at read time from `position_analysis.best_eval` plus trusted move `played_eval`, using the same side-to-move-relative and clamp-to-zero rule as the current v2 validator.

That derivation is CP-only for this bead. The existing v2 validator requires finite integer `played_eval` and `best_eval`, so mate-bearing rows currently fail v2 and fall back to local worker analysis. Preserve that behavior unless this bead explicitly implements and tests a mate-aware loss model. Still store `best_eval_mate` on the position row so exact-best and tree ranking retain mate awareness.

Required rule:

- CP vs CP: derive `max(best_eval - played_eval, 0)` when white to move and `max(played_eval - best_eval, 0)` when black to move, using white-relative CP values.
- Mate vs CP, CP vs mate, and mate vs mate: do not derive a numeric eval loss in this migration. Return unavailable or fall back to local worker recompute for threshold grading. Exact-best and tree ranking may still use the trusted position `best_move_uci` / `best_eval_mate`.

If implementation keeps `analysis_cache.eval_delta`, document it as a canonical-run snapshot and store enough metadata to prove it was computed against the same position row/profile. Browser snapshots must not drive strict position outcomes.

## Consumer Cutover And Audit

Known consumers that must be migrated or explicitly deferred with follow-up beads:

- `backend/app/tree_eval.py`: high priority. Source root position best eval, mate ranking, and best move from `position_analysis`, or from an explicitly trusted legacy projection during transition. This includes `lookup_root_eval`, `lookup_move_evals`, `_root_sort_key`, and `_move_sort_key`. `lookup_move_evals` currently reads `analysis_cache` through the `normalized_fen_before` fallback with no trust filter, so it is part of the same untrusted-read surface and must not remain on raw `analysis_cache` position facts.
- `backend/app/api/session.py` and `session_moves`: high priority. Stop presenting duplicated `SessionMove.best_move_uci` as authoritative position analysis. Session drill-review export must carry `position_trusted`, must look up storage position facts by `normalize_fen(move.fen_before)`, and must emit the compatibility map keyed by the original full `fen_before`, or mark legacy/untrusted seeds false.
- `backend/app/api/analysis.py`: split response data or add a new endpoint; use normalized FEN for position lookup and keep exact move-key lookup for move evidence.
- `src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts`: stop building untrusted `PositionAnalysis` best-move seeds from upload rows without a trust signal.
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`: tracked by `g-54h5`; it must receive `position_trusted` so it only skips live search for trusted canonical seeds, and otherwise runs full search or re-ranks alternatives.
- `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`, `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts`, and drill grading paths: update after the payload exists so strictness 0 and eval-loss thresholds consume trusted position facts separately from trusted move facts.

## Phased Implementation

Keep this issue as one task for now. Each phase below is intended to become a sub-bead later.

Phase 1: Add `position_analysis`, `position_analysis_conflicts`, grain-specific contract helpers, and legacy v2 projection helpers. Keep v2 registered and keep existing canonical reads trusted during transition. Add tests that pin the actual non-trust-gated consumers (`tree_eval.py` including `lookup_move_evals`, and session export) so the work starts from the live bug.

Phase 2: Backfill canonical position winners from existing `AnalysisCache` rows by grouping candidates per `normalized_fen`, using `normalized_fen_before` where available, selecting one winner with dominance logic, and recording conflicts in `position_analysis_conflicts`.

Phase 3: Route new position writes through the position replacement policy. Ensure browser-game writes cannot insert or replace trusted position truth, and ensure post-split move-grain writes use the move-complete contract rather than `resolver-complete-v2`.

Phase 4: Cut over payload-producing backend consumers: `/api/analysis/lookup` or replacement endpoint, `backend/app/tree_eval.py`, and `backend/app/api/session.py`. These responses must carry separate trusted position evidence and trusted move evidence. For session export, explicitly bridge the grains by looking up `normalize_fen(move.fen_before)` and emitting `position_analysis` keyed by the original full `move.fen_before`. This phase is the part `g-54h5` should depend on when phases become sub-beads.

Phase 5: Update frontend wire types and cache guards: `src/utils/api.ts`, `src/workers/analysisUtils.ts`, `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`, `src/hooks/useMoveAnalysis.ts`, `sessionUpload.ts`, and related tests. Replace `trusted_for_resolution` with `position_trusted` and `move_trusted`.

Phase 6: Update drill grading semantics. Strictness 0 exact-best uses only trusted position best move and runs independent of move eval availability; threshold/eval-loss uses trusted position CP best eval plus trusted move CP played eval, with mate-bearing rows falling back/unavailable unless a mate-aware model is implemented.

Phase 7: Complete the remaining best-move/best-eval consumer audit and create follow-up beads for any intentionally deferred readers.

Phase 8: Update `SPEC.md` to document position-vs-move grains, normalized-FEN storage keying, full-FEN session response compatibility, grain-specific trust contracts, eval-loss ownership, required mate storage, legacy v2 transition/deprecation rules, conflict storage, and the write-side dominance guarantee.

title: conflicting best moves in drill
description:
tmp/drillhar.json5 has the network logs of two drill sessions I played with the same opening and strictness set to 0 cp loss allowed.
Once the opening root was reached I played Bf4 at which point the drill ends because /api/analysis/lookup says the best move is c4.
In the second session once the opening route was reached I played C4 at which point the job and again because says the best move is Bf4.
Investigate this bug.
notes:
Investigation 2026-06-16: Queried the provided Railway DB. For FEN rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/3P4/5N2/PPP1PPPP/RNBQKB1R w KQkq - 0 3, analysis_cache has mixed-source rows:
- c1f4/Bf4: id 40295, source=precomputed, profile=canonical-sf18-depth24-linux-v1, contract=resolver-complete-v2, best_move=c2c4, played_eval=44, best_eval=35, eval_delta=0, trusted by lookup.
- c2c4/c4: id 142255, source=game, profile=browser-game-v1, contract=resolver-complete-v1, best_move=c1f4, played_eval=42, best_eval=30, eval_delta=0, untrusted by lookup.
- c1g5/Bg5: canonical v2, best_move=c2c4, eval_delta=14.
No normalized/transposed canonical c2c4 row exists for the same 4-field position. This matches tmp/drillhar.json5 and explains the contradictory exact-best failures: both disputed moves are 0cp loss but carry opposite best_move_uci from different analysis profiles.
close_reason: Closed

title: Investigate slow next opponent move calls
description: Investigate occasional long latency in POST /api/game/next-opponent-move, especially when concurrent POST /api/analysis/lookup calls appear to take the same duration. Identify a plausible shared blocking bug or add targeted logging to narrow future occurrences.
design: Plan: trace POST /api/game/next-opponent-move across session/FEN validation, ghost recursive CTE/SRS scoring, and backend Maia fallback. This lets a future slow pair distinguish DB query time, endpoint thread execution time, remote Maia latency, and analytics overhead without logging secrets or raw request bodies.

### Phase 7 — Network timing
- In `requestJson` (`src/utils/api.ts:196-224`) measure `performance.now()` around the request. Capture success **only AFTER `response.json()` resolves**; if the parse throws, capture with `error_kind: 'parse'` (don't report bad JSON as success). Restructure: `const parsed = await response.json()` inside the ok-branch, capture success, then return `parsed`.
- `api_request_client` props: `route` (`normalizeApiPath(url)`), `method`, `status` (or `0` for network error), `ok`, `duration_ms`, `attempts`, `error_kind` (`http`/`network`/`timeout`/`parse`). One event per logical request (final outcome), NOT per retry.
- Apply same capture to the 3 AuthContext raw fetches (apiLogin :109, apiClaim :131, apiRegister :155) — prefer routing them through `requestJson` / a thin shared timing wrapper to avoid duplicating retry semantics.
- Add `normalizeApiPath()` (strip base URL; replace UUIDs + bare numeric segments with `{id}`, e.g. `/api/drills/7f..-../fail` → `/api/drills/{id}/fail`) in `src/utils/api.ts` or `src/analytics/`.

### Tests (Phase 10, frontend subset)
- `normalizeApiPath()` unit tests (UUIDs, numeric ids, query strings, base-url stripping).
- `requestJson` emits exactly one `api_request_client` per logical request (mock singleton); no emit when disabled.
- Pre-push runs the full vitest suite and is flaky under parallel load — re-run any failing file in isolation before trusting a failure.

### Phase 1 — Dependencies, config, hygiene (backend)
- `backend/requirements.txt`: add `posthog>=3.25,<4` (instance API: `Posthog(project_api_key, host=...)`; capture signature `client.capture(event, distinct_id=…, properties=…)`; no feature-flag poller without a personal key). Verify `client.shutdown()` exists in the installed version.
- `.gitignore`: add `.env`, `backend/.env`, `.env.*` with `!.env.example` (the `.env`/`backend/.env` files are currently NOT gitignored).
- New `backend/.env.example`: document `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`, `POSTHOG_HOST`, `POSTHOG_DISABLED`.

### Phase 2 — Backend client module (`backend/app/posthog_client.py`)
- `get_client()` → process-singleton `Posthog` from `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`/`POSTHOG_HOST`. Returns `None` when token missing or `POSTHOG_DISABLED=true` → all helpers no-op. Disable logic lives HERE (not an SDK kwarg).
- `capture(distinct_id, event, properties=None)` wrapper → internally `client.capture(event, distinct_id=…, properties=…)`. Swallows ALL exceptions (analytics must never break a request); skips when disabled; anon fallback distinct_id `"anon"`.
- `shutdown()` → `client.shutdown()` (flush + join sender thread); guard with getattr/try-except. Do NOT rely on a bare `flush()`.
- Wire `shutdown()` into `backend/app/main.py` lifespan `finally` (before `engine.dispose()`), swallowing errors like the existing scheduler teardown.

### Phase 3 — Per-request capture (PRIMARY deliverable)
- In `HTTPLoggingMiddleware.__call__` `finally` (after `duration_ms`, `backend/app/http_logging.py:191-220`), emit `api_request`.
- Props: `route` (template from `scope["route"].path`), `method`, `status_code`, `duration_ms`, `ok` (status<400), `status_class` (2xx/4xx/5xx), `request_id`. distinct_id = `str(user_id)` else `"anon"`.
- Skip OPTIONS, `/health*`, `/`, static/docs (reuse existing exemption shape).
- Wrap in try/except so analytics failure never alters the response.
- Fallback route label (`"unmatched"`) when `scope["route"]` unset (404 / early short-circuit) so cardinality stays bounded.

### Phase 11 (this child) — Dashboard that unblocks g-e8wz
- Build PostHog insights: per-`route` p50/p95/p99/max of `api_request.duration_ms`, request count, `status_class` error rate — call out `/api/srs/review` and `/api/session/{id}/moves`. This dashboard IS the g-e8wz unblock artifact.

### Tests (Phase 10, backend subset)
- `posthog_client`: disabled when no token (`get_client()` is None, helpers no-op); `capture` swallows exceptions from a faulty client (monkeypatched to raise) without propagating.
- Route-template extraction: parametrized route → captured `route` is the template, not the concrete path; 404 → fallback.
- Middleware never alters the response when capture raises.
- `backend/conftest.py`: add `os.environ.setdefault("POSTHOG_DISABLED", "true")` (or leave token unset) so suite never emits.

### Privacy (Phase 9, backend)
- Never send bodies/passwords/tokens. Existing log redaction unaffected.
