title: Fix PostHog browser CORS failures
description:
Investigate and fix browser CORS/network failures after adding PostHog analytics, including local dev behavior.

Scope: reverse-proxy CORS fix only. Privacy-signal handling (DNT/GPC) is split out to g-rff5 (depends on this bead). Full step-by-step plan lives in the DESIGN field.

Investigation:
# Fix PostHog browser CORS failures

## Symptom
Browser dev console shows a batch of PostHog requests blocked with **"CORS Failed"**
(requests to `https://us.i.posthog.com` and `https://us-assets.i.posthog.com`).

## Root cause: COEP cross-origin isolation, not cookies
The app is **cross-origin isolated** — it sends `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`
(+ `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`), required so the Stockfish WASM engine can use
`SharedArrayBuffer`.

- Dev/preview: `vite.config.ts` `server.headers` / `preview.headers`.
- Prod / unsupported browsers: `public/coi-serviceworker.js` injects the same headers.

Under `require-corp`, **every cross-origin subresource response** must explicitly opt in — either
pass CORS, or return `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`. PostHog's ingestion + asset
endpoints don't return headers that satisfy COEP, so the browser drops the requests. The
"CORS Failed" message is the COEP wall, not a normal CORS/cookie issue.

This is the **same root cause already documented in `src/analytics/featurebase.ts`** (its widget /
iframe can't load under `require-corp`, hence the link-out). See also project memory
"COEP blocks third-party embeds".

## Why first-party cookies will NOT fix it
First-party cookie settings (PostHog `persistence` / `cross_subdomain_cookie`) only change *where the
SDK stores its distinct-id cookie* (our domain vs PostHog's). The network call to `us.i.posthog.com`
is still **cross-origin** and still hits the same `require-corp` wall. Cookie scoping is irrelevant to
a COEP resource-policy block — so this approach is rejected.

## Fix: reverse proxy (make PostHog same-origin)
Proxying makes ingestion/asset requests **same-origin** (e.g. `/ingest/*` on our domain →
forwarded to PostHog). Same-origin requests are exempt from both CORS and COEP's resource-policy
check entirely. We already use this exact pattern: `vercel.json` rewrites `/api/*` → Railway backend.
Side benefit: also dodges ad blockers.

### Correctness requirements (verified against the installed SDK)
With `api_host: '/ingest'` the SDK enters the **CUSTOM** region
(`node_modules/posthog-js/lib/src/utils/request-router.js:71`) and simply prefixes `/ingest` onto
every path. THREE distinct PostHog path families then appear under `/ingest/*`, and they do NOT all
live on the same upstream host:

| SDK request | Path under proxy | Real upstream host |
|---|---|---|
| events / flags / decide (`'api'` target) | `/ingest/e/`, `/ingest/flags/…` | `us.i.posthog.com` |
| array/recorder/toolbar scripts (`'assets'`, `/static/`) | `/ingest/static/…` | `us-assets.i.posthog.com` |
| remote config (`'assets'`, `/array/<token>/config[.js]`) | `/ingest/array/…` | `us-assets.i.posthog.com` |

1. **Proxy BOTH ingestion AND the static-assets host.** Asset scripts load under COEP too, so they
   must also be same-origin.
2. **Remote config (`/array/<token>/config.js`) routes to the ASSETS host**, not ingestion
   (`remote-config.js:35`, `external-scripts-loader.js:86`). So `/ingest/array/*` needs its own rule
   to `us-assets` BEFORE the broad `/ingest/*` rule — otherwise the broad rule mis-routes it to
   `us.i.posthog.com`.
3. **Rewrite order is first-match-wins.** Both `us-assets` rules (`/ingest/static/*`,
   `/ingest/array/*`) must come before the broad `/ingest/*` rule, and all three must come before
   the SPA catch-all `"/(.*)" → "/index.html"`.
4. **`ui_host` must be conditional.** When unset the SDK derives the UI host by replacing
   `.i.posthog.com` → `.posthog.com` (`request-router.js:44-57`) — fine for an absolute host
   (`eu.i.posthog.com` → `eu.posthog.com`) but broken for `/ingest`. So set
   `ui_host: 'https://us.posthog.com'` ONLY when proxying, never unconditionally (an unconditional
   value would hijack EU/self-hosted overrides).

## Implementation summary

### 1. `vercel.json` — three rewrites before the catch-all
```jsonc
{ "source": "/ingest/static/:path*", "destination": "https://us-assets.i.posthog.com/static/:path*" },
{ "source": "/ingest/array/:path*",  "destination": "https://us-assets.i.posthog.com/array/:path*" },
{ "source": "/ingest/:path*",        "destination": "https://us.i.posthog.com/:path*" }
```

### 2. `src/analytics/posthog.ts` — point the SDK at the proxy
```ts
const apiHost = import.meta.env.VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST || DEFAULT_HOST  // DEFAULT_HOST = '/ingest'
posthog.init(token, {
  api_host: apiHost,
  ...(apiHost.startsWith('/') ? { ui_host: 'https://us.posthog.com' } : {}),  // proxy only
  // …existing options…
})
```

### 3. `vite.config.ts` — shared dev + preview proxy (us-assets rules first; first-match-wins)
Define once, apply to BOTH `server.proxy` and `preview.proxy`. `preview.proxy` is
MANDATORY: the new `/ingest` default + the preview server's COEP headers
(`vite.config.ts:34`) would otherwise route `/ingest/*` to the static preview server
(404 / broken analytics). Vite 7.3.1 supports it (`PreviewOptions extends CommonServerOptions`).
```ts
const posthogProxy = {
  '/ingest/static': { target: 'https://us-assets.i.posthog.com', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (p) => p.replace(/^\/ingest/, '') },
  '/ingest/array':  { target: 'https://us-assets.i.posthog.com', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (p) => p.replace(/^\/ingest/, '') },
  '/ingest':        { target: 'https://us.i.posthog.com',        changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (p) => p.replace(/^\/ingest/, '') },
}
// server.proxy: { '/api': { … }, ...posthogProxy }
// preview:      { headers: { …COEP… }, proxy: { ...posthogProxy } }
```

### 4. Env — files AND hosted
- `.env.example` + local `.env`: set `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=/ingest` (a pinned absolute host
  overrides the new default and bypasses the proxy).
- **Hosted (Vercel):** `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` is build-time inlined — a project env var still set
  to `https://us.i.posthog.com` silently bypasses the proxy in prod. Audit and remove/repoint it.

### 5. Tests
- `src/analytics/posthog.test.ts`: default-host test expects `api_host: '/ingest'` AND
  `ui_host: 'https://us.posthog.com'`; EU-override test asserts `api_host` is the absolute host
  and `ui_host` is NOT set to the proxy value.
- New `src/analytics/vercel-rewrites.test.ts`: read repo-root `vercel.json` and assert rewrite ORDER —
  both `us-assets` rules (`/ingest/static/*`, `/ingest/array/*`) before broad `/ingest/*`, all three
  before the SPA catch-all `/(.*)`, with correct destinations. (Ordering is the most fragile part.)

## Verification
- `npx vitest run src/analytics/posthog.test.ts src/analytics/vercel-rewrites.test.ts` passes.
- `tsc -b` / build confirms `ui_host` typechecks.
- `npm run dev` with a token + `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=/ingest`: `crossOriginIsolated === true`
  (Stockfish unaffected); Network tab shows `/ingest/*`, `/ingest/static/*` AND
  `/ingest/array/<token>/config*` all same-origin / 200 / no "CORS Failed"; events land in PostHog.
- `npm run build && npm run preview` with a token: same Network-tab parity (proves `preview.proxy`).
- Prod: after deploy + hosted-env audit, repeat the Network check (verify `/ingest/array/*` 200).

## Rejected alternative
First-party cookies — does not address the cross-origin COEP block (see above).
design:
# Plan: PostHog reverse proxy (g-posthog-cors)

## Context
PostHog browser requests to `us.i.posthog.com` / `us-assets.i.posthog.com` are
dropped with "CORS Failed". Root cause is **COEP, not cookies**: the app is
cross-origin isolated (`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`, needed for
the Stockfish WASM `SharedArrayBuffer`). Under `require-corp` every cross-origin
subresource must explicitly opt in via CORS or `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`,
and PostHog's ingestion/asset endpoints don't, so the browser drops them.

**Fix:** route PostHog through a same-origin reverse proxy (`/ingest/*` on our
domain → forwarded to PostHog). Same-origin requests are exempt from both CORS
and the COEP resource-policy check. We already use this exact pattern
(`vercel.json` rewrites `/api/*` → Railway; `vite.config.ts` `server.proxy`
forwards `/api`). Side benefit: dodges ad blockers. First-party cookie tweaks
are rejected — they don't touch the cross-origin COEP wall.

**Scope:** reverse-proxy CORS fix only. Privacy-signal handling (DNT/GPC) is
split out to **g-rff5** (depends on this bead) per the decision to keep this
diff focused.

### Routing facts (verified against the installed SDK)
PostHog's `RequestRouter` (`node_modules/posthog-js/lib/src/utils/request-router.js`)
resolves endpoints by *target*. With `api_host: '/ingest'` the SDK enters the
**CUSTOM** region (`request-router.js:71`), so it just prefixes `/ingest` onto
every path. Three distinct PostHog path families therefore appear under
`/ingest/*`, and they do NOT all live on the same upstream host:

| SDK request | Path under proxy | Real upstream host |
|---|---|---|
| events / flags / decide (`'api'` target) | `/ingest/e/`, `/ingest/flags/…` | `us.i.posthog.com` |
| array/recorder/toolbar scripts (`'assets'`, `/static/`) | `/ingest/static/…` | `us-assets.i.posthog.com` |
| **remote config** (`'assets'`, `/array/<token>/config[.js]`) | `/ingest/array/…` | `us-assets.i.posthog.com` |

The third row is the subtle one: remote config loads via
`endpointFor('assets', '/array/<token>/config.js')`
(`remote-config.js:35`, `external-scripts-loader.js:86`), which for the default
region resolves to **`us-assets`**, not the ingestion host. So `/ingest/array/*`
needs its own rewrite to `us-assets` placed **before** the broad `/ingest/*`
rule — otherwise the broad rule mis-routes remote config to `us.i.posthog.com`.

`ui_host` (`request-router.js:44-57`): when unset, the SDK derives the UI host by
replacing `.i.posthog.com` → `.posthog.com`. That works for an absolute host
(`eu.i.posthog.com` → `eu.posthog.com`) but produces garbage for `/ingest`. So
`ui_host` must be set **only when proxying**, not unconditionally.

## Changes

### 1. `vercel.json` — three rewrites BEFORE the SPA catch-all
Insert after the `/api/:match*` rewrite, before `"/(.*)" → "/index.html"`. Order
matters (Vercel = first match wins): the two `us-assets` rules before the broad
ingestion rule, all three before the catch-all.
```jsonc
{ "source": "/ingest/static/:path*", "destination": "https://us-assets.i.posthog.com/static/:path*" },
{ "source": "/ingest/array/:path*",  "destination": "https://us-assets.i.posthog.com/array/:path*" },
{ "source": "/ingest/:path*",        "destination": "https://us.i.posthog.com/:path*" }
```

### 2. `src/analytics/posthog.ts` — point the SDK at the proxy
- Change `DEFAULT_HOST` from `'https://us.i.posthog.com'` to `'/ingest'`.
- Keep the env override (`VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST || DEFAULT_HOST`) so a
  self-hosted/EU instance can still opt out; default is now the same-origin proxy.
- Add `ui_host` **conditionally** — only when the resolved host is the
  same-origin proxy (an absolute host lets the SDK derive its own UI host):
  ```ts
  const apiHost = import.meta.env.VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST || DEFAULT_HOST
  posthog.init(token, {
    api_host: apiHost,
    ...(apiHost.startsWith('/') ? { ui_host: 'https://us.posthog.com' } : {}),
    // …existing options…
  })
  ```
  (If a self-hosted instance ever needs a custom UI host too, add an optional
  `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_UI_HOST` later — not needed now.)

### 3. `vite.config.ts` — dev AND preview proxy (shared)
Define the three rules once and apply to **both** `server.proxy` and
`preview.proxy`. `preview.proxy` is **mandatory, not optional**: this change makes
`/ingest` the default `api_host`, and the preview server already emits COEP
(`preview.headers`, `vite.config.ts:34`), so `npm run preview` with a token would
otherwise route `/ingest/*` to the static preview server (404 / broken analytics)
instead of PostHog. Vite 7.3.1 supports it — `PreviewOptions extends
CommonServerOptions`, which includes `proxy` (`node_modules/vite/dist/node/index.d.ts`).
```ts
const posthogProxy = {
  '/ingest/static': { target: 'https://us-assets.i.posthog.com', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (p) => p.replace(/^\/ingest/, '') },
  '/ingest/array':  { target: 'https://us-assets.i.posthog.com', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (p) => p.replace(/^\/ingest/, '') },
  '/ingest':        { target: 'https://us.i.posthog.com',        changeOrigin: true, rewrite: (p) => p.replace(/^\/ingest/, '') },
}
// server.proxy: { '/api': { … }, ...posthogProxy }
// preview:      { headers: { …COEP… }, proxy: { ...posthogProxy } }
```
`us-assets` rules first (Vite proxy = first-match-wins on object key order, and
object spread preserves it); `changeOrigin: true` so SNI/Host matches the
upstream; rewrite strips `/ingest` so `/ingest/static/array.js` →
`us-assets…/static/array.js`, `/ingest/array/<t>/config.js` →
`us-assets…/array/<t>/config.js`, `/ingest/e/` → `us.i.posthog.com/e/`.
(Preview's existing `/api` gap is pre-existing and out of scope.)

### 4. Env files
- `.env.example`: change `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=https://us.i.posthog.com` →
  `/ingest`; update its comment to say it now defaults to the same-origin proxy.
- Local `.env`: same change (currently pins `https://us.i.posthog.com`, which
  would override the new default and bypass the dev proxy).
- **Hosted env (deployment, not a file):** `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` is
  **build-time** (Vite inlines `import.meta.env.*`). If the Vercel project has
  `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=https://us.i.posthog.com` set, it will override
  `/ingest` at build and silently bypass the proxy in prod. Audit the Vercel
  project env vars and remove/repoint that var to `/ingest` (or unset it) as
  part of the deploy. This is the real-world gotcha, not just the local files.

### 5. Tests
**`src/analytics/posthog.test.ts` — adjust expectations**
- "defaults the host when VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST is unset": expect
  `api_host: '/ingest'` and `ui_host: 'https://us.posthog.com'`.
- The env-override test (`eu.i.posthog.com`): assert it sets that `api_host` and
  does **not** set `ui_host` to the proxy value (e.g. assert
  `initMock.mock.calls[0][1].ui_host` is undefined) — locks in the conditional.

**New: `src/analytics/vercel-rewrites.test.ts` — Vercel rewrite-order contract**
The rewrite ordering is the most fragile part and nothing else guards it. Add a
tiny test that reads repo-root `vercel.json` (import the JSON, or
`readFileSync(new URL('../../vercel.json', import.meta.url))` — `node:fs`/`node:path`
sidestep the bare `fs`/`path` vitest aliases). Locate each rewrite's index in
`rewrites` and assert:
- all three PostHog rules exist with correct destinations (`/ingest/static/*` and
  `/ingest/array/*` → `us-assets…`; `/ingest/:path*` → `us.i.posthog.com`);
- `idx('/ingest/static/:path*') < idx('/ingest/:path*')` AND
  `idx('/ingest/array/:path*') < idx('/ingest/:path*')` (assets before broad);
- all three `< idx('/(.*)')` (the SPA catch-all, `vercel.json:2`).
Lives under `src/` to match vitest `include: ['src/**']`.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run src/analytics/posthog.test.ts src/analytics/vercel-rewrites.test.ts`
  — config + init assertions pass (rewrite-order contract included).
- `tsc -b` / `npm run build` — confirms `ui_host` typechecks (init uses
  `OnlyValidKeys<PostHogConfig>`; an invalid key fails the build gate).
- `npm run dev` with a real token + `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST=/ingest`:
  - DevTools console: `crossOriginIsolated === true` (Stockfish unaffected).
  - Network tab: PostHog calls hit `/ingest/*` (events/flags), `/ingest/static/*`
    (array/recorder scripts) **and** `/ingest/array/<token>/config*` (remote
    config) — all same-origin, all 200, no "CORS Failed".
  - Events land in the PostHog project; toolbar/links resolve via `ui_host`.
- `npm run build && npm run preview` with a token: same Network-tab parity —
  `/ingest/*` and `/ingest/array/*` same-origin / 200 (proves `preview.proxy`).
- Prod: after deploy (and after auditing the hosted env var), repeat the
  Network-tab check on the Vercel domain — verify `/ingest/array/*` in particular
  returns 200 (the rule most likely to be missed).

## Rejected alternative
First-party cookies (`persistence` / `cross_subdomain_cookie`) — only change
where the SDK stores its distinct-id; the network call stays cross-origin and
hits the same COEP wall.

## Follow-up (separate bead)
**g-rff5** — Honor privacy signals (DNT/GPC): `respect_dnt: true` plus a manual
pre-init GPC gate (the SDK reads DNT but not `navigator.globalPrivacyControl`).
close_reason: Implemented PostHog same-origin reverse proxy (/ingest) to fix COEP CORS failures: vercel.json rewrites (us-assets rules before broad ingestion, all before SPA catch-all), conditional ui_host in posthog.ts, shared dev+preview vite proxy, env default /ingest, plus posthog + vercel-rewrites order tests. Note: Vercel hosted env var VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST must be unset/repointed to /ingest before deploy.

title: engine line arrow widths using patched ~/src/react-chessboard
description:
Add arrow width as a new visual channel using react-chessboard's arrowWidthDenominator.
For arrow width I want not only for bad moves to be thinner but good moves to be wider. I'm thinking the way to do this is to make the width proportional to the average of the 3 evals.
 arrowWidthDenominator's scale should go from 2 to 20 with a midpoint of 6. Though I'm not sure how to map eval to this scale.
Disparity between the top 3 engine lines is usually <1cp, in those cases the widths should be similar. But occasionally there is a huge discrepancy, such as when taking advantage of an opponent's blunder. The goal is to really emphasize those game changing moves with wider arrows.

title: sometimes the 2nd engine line is the best one
description:
## Symptom

In the analysis board engine-line panel, the 2nd engine line sometimes shows a
better eval than the 1st line. Line 1 is supposed to be the best move, so a
higher-scoring line 2 is a visible contradiction.

## Root cause

The engine-line panel has an optimization that reuses the game's stored best
move to skip re-searching it (`src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx:496-571`):

1. `cachedBest = positionAnalysis[displayedFen]` (line 497) — the stored best
   move for the displayed position.
2. `searchmoves` = every legal move EXCEPT `cachedBest.best_move_uci`
   (lines 500-512), handed to the engine with `multipv: 2` (line 524). The
   cached best move is therefore NEVER re-evaluated by the live engine.
3. Merge: `return [cachedLine, ...activeEngineLines]` (line 571) — the cached
   move is force-prepended as line 1 with its STORED eval, and the merged list
   is never re-ranked by eval.

Two defects fall out of this:

- **Un-trust-gated seed (shared root cause with `g-position-analysis` / the
  drill bug `g-ul4p`).** The `PositionAnalysis` payload carries best move /
  eval / line but NO trust signal (`src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts:152-157`).
  The consumer cannot tell whether the seeded best move came from canonical deep
  analysis or a low-trust browser-game pass. If the seed is wrong or stale, the
  board pins it as line 1 without verification — the same "best-move truth stored
  redundantly, source-dependent, read without a trust gate" anti-pattern that
  `g-position-analysis` is fixing. Seed sources are the server session response
  (`backend/app/api/session.py:786`, from `SessionMove.best_move_uci`) and the
  client drill snapshot (`sessionUpload.ts:152`); neither is trust-gated.

- **Prepend-without-rerank + depth mismatch (specific to this panel).** Because
  `cachedBest` is excluded from the search AND force-prepended, the true best
  move (when it differs) is still searched, scores higher, and is displayed as
  line 2 BELOW the cached line 1 — exactly this bead's symptom. Also,
  `best_move_eval_cp` is never recomputed at `ENGINE_SEARCH_DEPTH` while the
  searchmove lines are, so the panel compares evals from different depths/sources
  (the code only reconciles side-to-move sign at lines 551-552, not depth/provenance).

## Severity

Display-only (engine arrows + line panel) — does not affect drill pass/fail
grading. But more user-visible than the drill bug because of the contradictory
line ordering.

## Why blocked by g-position-analysis

The durable fix needs a trusted, single-source best move for a position.
`g-position-analysis` introduces a trust-gated `position_analysis` store
(single canonical winner per `normalized_fen`, carrying `trusted_for_resolution`).
Once that exists, `PositionAnalysis` can thread a trust flag and this path can:

1. Short-circuit the search ONLY when the seed is the trusted canonical best;
   otherwise fall through to the full `multipv: 3` search (existing `else` at
   line 526) instead of pinning an unverified move.
2. Stop treating index 0 as gospel — re-rank by eval, or refuse to prepend, when
   the cached move is not verified >= the searched alternatives.

This bead is one of the best-move consumers that `g-position-analysis`'s
consumer audit should enumerate (alongside drill grading and `tree_eval.py`).

## Acceptance

- Line 1 of the engine panel is always >= every other displayed line by eval
  (no "line 2 is better than line 1").
- The cached best move is only trusted to skip live search when it comes from
  the trusted canonical position source; untrusted/missing seeds fall back to a
  full search.
- Eval comparisons within the panel are at a consistent depth/source, or clearly
  marked when not.
design:
# g-54h5 — Fix "2nd engine line is sometimes the best one"

## Status of the blocker

`g-position-analysis.4` (the depended-on phase) is **closed**, and the trust
surface it promised is already live end-to-end:

- `backend/app/api/session.py:808-833` — bridges grains by `normalize_fen(move.fen_before)`,
  emits `PositionAnalysis(..., position_trusted=True)` when a trusted
  `position_analysis` row exists, `position_trusted=False` for legacy
  `SessionMove.best_move_uci` seeds.
- `src/utils/api.ts:1086-1100` — `PositionAnalysis.position_trusted: boolean`
  (required, never defaulted).
- `src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts:151-161` — local drill
  snapshots set `position_trusted: false` (worker results are not a backend
  trusted winner).

So this bead is now a **pure frontend fix** in `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`.
The panel still reads the seed (`cachedBest`) without ever consulting
`position_trusted`, and force-prepends it without re-ranking — the two defects in
the bead description.

## Current data flow (the bug, precisely)

`src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`:

1. `cachedBest = positionAnalysis?.[displayedFen] ?? null` (497) — used
   unconditionally; `position_trusted` ignored.
2. `searchmoves` (500-512) — every legal move EXCEPT `cachedBest.best_move_uci`.
3. effect (515-531) — if `cachedBest && searchmoves` → `evaluatePosition(..., {multipv:2, searchmoves})`
   (best move excluded from live search); else `{multipv:3}` full.
4. `useRestrictedSearch` (534-539) — true when `cachedBest && searchmoves`.
5. `mergedEngineLines` (553-572) — when restricted, returns
   `[cachedLine, ...activeEngineLines]`, where `cachedLine` carries the STORED
   `best_move_eval_cp` (canonical depth, ~24) and `depth: undefined`. **No
   re-rank.** `activeEngineLines` are live at `ENGINE_SEARCH_DEPTH = 21` (34).
6. Everything downstream keys off array order: `buildEngineArrows`
   (`AnalysisBoard.helpers.ts:35-64`, index 0 = best/blue), `buildEngineLinePreview`
   (sourceSlot = display index, 578), `liveEngineEvalCp` (`mergedEngineLines[0]`,
   805-812), panel render (`i===0 ? opacity 1`, 1372-1410).

Two defects fall out:

- **Un-trust-gated seed.** An untrusted/stale `position_trusted:false` seed
  (browser-game row or local drill snapshot) is pinned as line 1 with no
  verification.
- **Prepend-without-rerank + depth/source mismatch.** When the live engine scores
  a non-best move higher than the cached stored eval (depth/source mismatch, or a
  bad seed), that move is searched, scores higher, and lands at index >= 1 BELOW
  the cached line 1 → the visible "line 2 better than line 1".

## Fix (concentrated in AnalysisBoard.tsx; matches the bead's own two steps)

### Edit 1 — Trust-gate the seed

After line 497 derive a gated seed; route ALL skip/prepend consumers through it:

```ts
const cachedBest = positionAnalysis?.[displayedFen] ?? null;

// Only a TRUSTED canonical position winner with a comparable cp eval may drive
// the search-skip optimization and the line-1 prepend (g-54h5). Untrusted seeds
// (browser-game rows, local drill-snapshot worker results) or seeds without a
// comparable cp eval fall through to a full multipv search so the live engine
// ranks every move at one depth.
const trustedBest =
  cachedBest &&
  cachedBest.position_trusted === true &&
  cachedBest.best_move_eval_cp != null
    ? cachedBest
    : null;
```

Replace `cachedBest` with `trustedBest` in: `searchmoves` (501, 507), the search
branch (523), `useRestrictedSearch` (534-539), and `mergedEngineLines` (555,
561-566). When `trustedBest` is null → `searchmoves` undefined → effect runs full
`multipv:3` → no merge → `activeEngineLines` (engine-sorted) returned as-is → no
contradiction possible.

Why also require `best_move_eval_cp != null`: a trusted seed without a comparable
cp eval can't be ranked against searched cp lines for the re-rank guarantee below;
falling back to full search keeps the panel internally consistent.

**Known limitation (Finding 2) — mate-only trusted winners.** Backend trusted
positions can be mate-only: `position_analysis_repo` stores `best_eval=None` with
`best_eval_mate` set, and `session.py:818` emits
`best_move_eval_cp = tp.best_eval * sign if tp.best_eval is not None else None` —
so a mate-only trusted winner arrives with `position_trusted=True` but
`best_move_eval_cp=None`. The wire `PositionAnalysis` (`src/utils/api.ts:1086`,
backend `session.py:128-137`) carries **no `best_eval_mate` field**, so the gate
above routes those trusted mate winners into full live `multipv:3` search. That is
defensible — live search still finds the mate and ranks it consistently — but it
means **trusted canonical mate winners are not skip-optimized or displayed with
the canonical PV by this panel until the wire payload grows mate-eval support.**
Follow-up (separate bead, not this one): add `best_move_eval_mate` to the wire
`PositionAnalysis` (backend pydantic + `api.ts` + `session.py` trusted branch +
`sessionUpload.ts`), build `cachedLine.score` as `{type:"mate"}` when present, and
widen the gate to `best_move_eval_cp != null || best_move_eval_mate != null`.
`scoreToNum`/`mateToCp` already rank mate above cp, so Edit 2's sort needs no
change once the mate eval is threaded.

### Edit 2 — Re-rank merged lines so line 1 >= every other line

Export `scoreToNum` from `src/components/AnalysisBoard.helpers.ts:29`
(`const` → `export const`; it already maps mate→cp via `mateToCp`, so mate
correctly outranks cp). Import it into AnalysisBoard.tsx. In the merge branch of
`mergedEngineLines`, replace `return [cachedLine, ...activeEngineLines]` with a
stable descending sort by a single consistent eval:

```ts
const merged = [cachedLine, ...activeEngineLines];
// Re-rank by one consistent eval so displayed line 1 is always >= every other
// line (g-54h5). Stable: ties keep the trusted cached line first (canonical best
// preserved when live merely matches it). A higher searched line (depth/source
// mismatch) sorts above the cached line instead of "line 2 better than line 1".
return merged
  .map((line, i) => ({ line, i, n: scoreToNum(line.score) }))
  .sort((a, b) => {
    if (a.n === b.n) return a.i - b.i;   // stable tiebreak (keeps cached first)
    if (a.n === null) return 1;          // null eval sinks to the bottom
    if (b.n === null) return -1;
    return b.n - a.n;                    // higher eval first
  })
  .map((x) => x.line);
```

The sort lives ONLY in the restricted/merge branch; the early return for the
full-search path is untouched (engine already returns sorted lines).

Because the sort happens in `mergedEngineLines`, every downstream consumer sees
the same order: `buildEngineArrows` colors the true best blue, `buildEngineLinePreview`
keeps `sourceSlot === display index` (so popup selection/`aria-pressed` stay
correct), `liveEngineEvalCp` reads the genuine best, and panel opacity follows.

### Edit 3 — Mark the canonical line's provenance (acceptance #3, required)

Edits 1-2 fix the *ordering* contradiction, but the panel still displays the
cached canonical eval (deeper search) next to live `ENGINE_SEARCH_DEPTH = 21`
evals as if directly comparable. Finding 1 is correct: that is a mixed-source
comparison and acceptance #3 demands it be same-source **or clearly marked**.
Rather than drop the canonical deep-eval display the author built, mark it:

1. `EngineLinePreview` type (`AnalysisBoard.tsx:89`) — add
   `source: "canonical" | "live"`.
2. `buildEngineLinePreview` (115-187) — add a `canonical: boolean` param; set
   `source: canonical ? "canonical" : "live"` on the returned object.
3. `engineLinesDisplay` map (575-581) — compute
   `const canonical = !!trustedBest && line.pv?.[0] === trustedBest.best_move_uci;`
   and pass it in. This identifies the cached line wherever Edit 2's sort placed
   it. It is unambiguous: `trustedBest.best_move_uci` is excluded from
   `searchmoves`, so no live line shares that first move; in the full-search path
   `trustedBest` is null → `canonical` is always false (nothing was prepended).
4. Compact panel button (1392-1397) — when `line.source === "canonical"`, render a
   marker glyph **`C`** in a muted `.analysis-board__engine-source` span with
   `title`/`aria-label` **"Canonical deep analysis"**. This is what makes the
   mixed-source eval "clearly marked".
5. Popup (1463-1467) — the canonical line already has `depth: undefined` → `depth`
   0 → the existing `selectedEngineLine.depth > 0` chip (`d{depth}`) is hidden.
   Replace that branch so `source === "canonical"` renders a chip reading
   **`Canonical`** instead of the `d21` chip, making the contrast explicit where
   the live lines show their depth.
6. `src/App.css` — add the `.analysis-board__engine-source` rule (small, muted;
   matches existing `.analysis-board__engine-*` styling).

Alternatives considered and rejected: (a) drop the optimization so every line is
live depth-21 and no marker is needed — discards the canonical deep eval the
author built and re-searches the best move; (b) show the canonical move with no
eval number — loses the eval the panel exists to show. The marker is the
lightest change that keeps the feature and satisfies #3.

## Tests (`src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx`)

Existing trusted-path tests (515-841: `searchmoves: expect.not.arrayContaining([...])`,
prepend, popup) keep passing — the skip optimization is preserved for
`position_trusted:true` + finite cp seeds.

Add:

1. **Untrusted seed → full search.** Render with `position_trusted:false`; assert
   `evaluatePosition` called with `multipv:3` and NO `searchmoves` (best move NOT
   excluded). Inverse of the existing 785-814 test.
2. **Re-rank fixes the symptom — assert the reordered MOVE, not just numbers
   (Finding 3).** Trusted seed whose `best_move_uci` is e.g. `g1f3` (Nf3) with low
   cached `best_move_eval_cp` (10); inject a live searched line `b1c3` (Nc3) with
   higher eval (50). After the fix assert ALL of:
   - "Show engine line 1"'s rendered move (`.analysis-board__engine-pv` text) is
     `Nc3` (the live line), and its eval is `+0.5`;
   - "Show engine line 2"'s rendered move is `Nf3` (the cached line), eval `+0.1`;
   - the canonical `source` marker is now on **line 2** (the cached line actually
     moved slots — catches a future impl that reorders numbers but leaves the
     wrong line/arrow first);
   - downstream consumer follows: line 1's PV drives the best (blue) arrow — assert
     via the canonical marker placement above and, if board arrows are queryable in
     the test harness, that the best-move arrow source square matches `b1` (Nc3).
   Asserting only the eval numbers would pass even if the wrong line stayed first
   with swapped formatting — hence the move-text + marker-placement assertions.
3. **Trusted seed with higher eval stays line 1.** Cached `g1f3` eval 80 >
   searched `b1c3` eval 20 → line 1 move is `Nf3`, the canonical marker is on
   line 1 (guards against over-rotating the sort).
4. **Null-eval trusted seed → full search.** `best_move_eval_cp:null`,
   `position_trusted:true` → `multipv:3`, no `searchmoves`.

Run: `npx vitest run src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx src/components/buildEngineArrows.test.ts`.
(Per project memory: the full pre-push vitest run is flaky under parallel load —
rerun named files in isolation before trusting a failure.)

## Files

- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx` — trust gate + re-rank + provenance marking
  (core).
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.helpers.ts` — `export const scoreToNum`.
- `src/App.css` — `.analysis-board__engine-source` marker style.
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx` — 4 new tests (move-text + marker-
  placement assertions per Finding 3).

## Follow-up bead (filed: g-jsac)

`g-jsac` — "Thread best_move_eval_mate through wire PositionAnalysis so trusted
mate winners are used by the engine-line panel" (depends on g-54h5, child of the
g-position-analysis epic). Covers the mate-only-trusted-winner limitation under
Edit 1: backend pydantic + `session.py` trusted branch, `api.ts`,
`sessionUpload.ts`, and widening the Edit-1 gate. Edit-2 sort and Edit-3 marker
need no change (mate-ready via `scoreToNum`/`mateToCp`; marker keys off move
identity).

## Out of scope

- The played-vs-best green/red `arrows` (748-785) read `move.best_move_san`
  (AnalysisMove move-grain), a different surface — not this bead.
- Backend/type/payload plumbing — already delivered by g-position-analysis
  Phase 4 (verified present).

## Considered alternative (rejected)

Drop the skip optimization entirely (always full `multipv:3`). Simplest possible
consistency, but discards the canonical deep best-line display the author
deliberately built, and the bead explicitly prescribes "skip only when trusted +
re-rank/refuse-to-prepend otherwise" — which Edits 1-2 implement.
close_reason: Trust-gate the cached best seed (position_trusted + finite cp), re-rank merged engine lines so line 1 is always >= every other line, and mark the canonical deep-analysis line's provenance. Frontend-only fix in AnalysisBoard. 6 new tests.

title: drill again should still randomize opponent
description: When clicking the Again button after a drill has ended it currently plays another drill with the exact same drill settings. Let's change it so the opponent difficulty is randomized using the same randomization algorithm that the new game popup uses
design:
# g-ncvm — Drill restart re-randomizes opponent difficulty

## Goal
The instant **Again** button (and "Another drill" / "New Drill"), and the **gear**
"Change drill settings" overlay, currently reuse the previous drill's exact engine
difficulty (`engineElo`). Change both so opponent difficulty is re-randomized using the
same algorithm the New Game popup uses: `sampleEloBin(playerRating)`. Opening, side, and
strictness stay fixed — only difficulty is resampled.

Paths in this plan are relative to the FRONTEND repo root: `/Users/mvargas/src/ghostreplay`.

## Current behavior (data flow)
- All instant-restart buttons route to `handleAgainDrill` in `src/components/ChessGame.tsx`:
  - PostGameBanner `onNewDrill={handleAgainDrill}` (`src/components/ChessGame.tsx:1970`)
  - DrillStopActions `onAnotherDrill={handleAgainDrill}` (`src/components/ChessGame.tsx:1992`)
  The gear next to each routes to `handleAgainSettings` (the manual setup overlay).
- `handleAgainDrill` (`src/components/ChessGame.tsx:1675`) reads the live store and passes
  `engineElo: s.engineElo` straight into `handleNewDrill` → exact replay of difficulty.
- `handleAgainSettings` (`src/components/ChessGame.tsx:1632`) seeds the overlay with
  `setEngineElo(s.engineElo)` (line 1643) → overlay shows the previous difficulty.
- `handleNewDrill` (`src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts:634`) calls
  `startDrill({ engine_elo: options.engineElo, ... })` and `s.setEngineElo(options.engineElo)`,
  so whatever elo is passed becomes the new drill's elo AND updates the store (drives avatar/label).

## The algorithm to reuse (New Game popup)
- `sampleEloBin(userElo, sigma=125)` in `src/components/chess-game/elo.ts` — Gaussian-weighted
  sample over `MAIA_ELO_BINS` using `Math.random()`. (With `Math.random()===0` the loop returns
  `MAIA_ELO_BINS[0]` regardless of `userElo`.)
- New Game uses it as `sampleEloBin(store.playerRating)`:
  - On overlay open: `handleShowStartOverlay` (`src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts:1002`)
  - On idle rating fetch (mount): (`src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts:200-201`) — this effect
    deliberately SKIPS resampling when a drill is in the store (`drillState !== null`), which is
    why the elo is currently retained across a reviewed-return Again.

## Change — frontend only (no backend/store/API change; `startDrill` already accepts engine_elo)

### 1. `src/components/ChessGame.tsx`
- Add `sampleEloBin` to the existing elo import:
  `import { eloStakes } from "./chess-game/elo";`

title: Implement openings tree workspace layout
description: Implement the production desktop and narrow responsive layout for the openings tree workspace after the page data flow exists. This owns viewport-bounded sizing, independent column scrolling, horizontal tree scrolling, connector rendering, and mobile stacking.
design:
# g-tree-layout — Openings tree workspace layout

## Context

`g-tree-page-state` (commit `3584a0c`) shipped the `/openings` horizontal move-tree
**data flow** with deliberately minimal, unpolished CSS: a flex board + a single
`overflow-x:auto` row of `overflow-y:auto` columns, no connectors, no viewport
bounding, no responsive stacking. This bead (`g-tree-layout`) owns the
**production viewport layout**: viewport-bounded sizing, independent per-column
vertical scroll + horizontal tree scroll (no whole-tree vertical scroll), a
square sticky board that does not drive column height, measured SVG connectors
along the selected path (dashed book-only / solid observed / encounter-count
thickness), and the `<=720px` stacked mobile layout — plus screenshots covering
desktop and narrow.

The connector technique is already proven in `src/pages/TreePrototypePage.tsx`
(the `useLayoutEffect` measurement loop + bezier rendering). We port that into
the production page, restrict it to the **selected path** (the production model
already exposes per-column selection), and drive style from real edge metadata
instead of mock data. The `OpeningTreeNodeCard` component and the page state
machine are done and **unchanged** in behavior — this is layout + connectors.

Sizing values are dictated by the bead design and are treated as the contract.

### Revisions from review
1. `selectionKey` = full UCI line, not depth — same-depth sibling switches re-aim.
2. Hook returns **geometry only**; styles applied at render → live `in_book` /
   `is_observed` / `encounter_count` always reach the DOM (no styleKey needed).
3. Dash reserved strictly for book-only; clamped endpoints use opacity + tip glyph,
   never dashing — keeps "dashed book-only / solid observed" unambiguous.
4. Screenshots gate on the settled selected state (expanded card + connector path
   count + append-loading gone) before capture; click the compact card button.
5. Unit test asserts `stroke-dasharray` + `stroke-width` from known fixture metadata
   (behavioral data→style contract), not just SVG presence.

## Sibling-bead scope boundaries (do NOT touch)
- `g-tree-cleanup`: deletes legacy `.openings-shell*` / `.openings-grid` CSS,
  `OpeningFamilyCard`, `/tree-prototype` route. We leave all of that alone.
- `g-tree-drill-links`: drill correctness / lineage migration. Start Drill nav
  already works; untouched.

---

## 1. `src/openings/treeView.ts` — thread connector metadata (pure, unit-tested)

Connectors need per-edge style from the **child** node (the edge identity is the
child). Add three fields to `DisplayNode` and populate from the API `TreeNode`
(`in_book`, `is_observed`, `encounter_count` already exist on `api.ts:1338`):

```ts
export interface DisplayNode {
  ... existing ...
  /** Reference opening-book edge. */
  inBook: boolean;
  /** Edge traversed in the user's real sessions → solid connector. */
  isObserved: boolean;
  /** Times the user reached this edge → connector thickness. */
  encounterCount: number;
}
```
- In `buildTreeView`, set them from `node.in_book` / `node.is_observed` /
  `node.encounter_count` for api columns; root node defaults `false/false/0`
  (the root is only ever a connector *parent*, never a styled child).

Add a pure style helper (this is what satisfies "without measuring every
sibling" — style derives from one selected child node, not the whole column):

```ts
export interface ConnectorStyle { dashed: boolean; width: number; }

/** Edge style for the selected child of a column. null → neutral frontier
 *  pointer (solid, base width). dashed = book-only theory not yet played;
 *  solid = observed. Width clamps log2(encounters) into [2,6]. */
export function connectorStyle(node: DisplayNode | null): ConnectorStyle {
  if (!node) return { dashed: false, width: 2 };
  const dashed = node.inBook && !node.isObserved;
  const width = Math.max(2, Math.min(6, 2 + Math.log2(node.encounterCount + 1)));
  return { dashed, width };
}
```

## 2. `src/openings/useTreeConnectors.ts` — NEW measurement hook (GEOMETRY ONLY)

Extract the prototype's `useLayoutEffect` measurement loop into a reusable hook so
`OpeningsPage` stays readable. The hook is the only DOM-measuring code. It returns
**pure geometry** — NO style. Style is applied at render time (§3), so a same-line
refetch or color switch that changes only edge metadata (`in_book`/`is_observed`/
`encounter_count`) re-renders correct connectors **without a re-measure**, and the
measure key needs to track only what moves the lines, not what colors them
(addresses review findings 1 & 2).

Signature:
```ts
useTreeConnectors({
  canvasRef,        // RefObject<HTMLDivElement> — the positioned frame
  scrollRef,        // RefObject<HTMLDivElement> — the overflow-x scroller
  columnEls,        // Map<number, HTMLElement>  keyed by display-col idx
  selectedNodeEls,  // Map<number, HTMLElement>  selected node per col
  columnCount,      // # display columns (add/remove → re-measure)
  selectionKey,     // FULL selected line (sibling switch at same depth → re-measure)
}): Connector[]
```
- `Connector = { x1,y1,x2,y2, off:-1|0|1, off2:-1|0|1 }` — geometry only (port the
  prototype type unchanged; do NOT bake dashed/width here).
- For each adjacent display-column pair `(i, i+1)` where `columnEls[i]` AND
  `selectedNodeEls[i]` AND `columnEls[i+1]` exist:
  - origin `x1 = colR(i).right - canvasR.left`; `y1` = selected-node center,
    **clamped to column i's visible band** (`off = ±1` when scrolled out) — exactly
    the prototype clamp.
  - target `x2 = colR(i+1).left - canvasR.left`; `y2` = `selectedNodeEls[i+1]`
    center clamped to col i+1's band, or col i+1's vertical midpoint when there is
    no selected child yet (frontier replies column).
- Connector geometry `i` is index-aligned with style `i` because both derive from
  the same `view.columns` adjacency (pair `(i, i+1)`).
- **`selectionKey` is the full line, NOT a depth count**:
  `playerColor + "\0" + view.selectionLine.join("\0")` — a same-depth sibling
  selection (`src/pages/OpeningsPage.test.tsx:349` flow) changes which node is
  selected without changing `columnCount`, and must re-aim the lines.
- Re-measure on: mount, `selectionKey`/`columnCount` change, `window resize`,
  `scrollRef` scroll **with `capture:true`** (so per-column vertical scrolls fire),
  and a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas. All via a single rAF-coalesced `schedule()`.
- **jsdom guards**: `if (typeof ResizeObserver !== 'undefined')` before observing
  (vitest jsdom lacks it); `getBoundingClientRect` returning zeros is harmless
  (zero-length paths still render with their style attributes). Use `useLayoutEffect`.

Refs are attached **only to selected nodes** (`selectedNodeEls`), never to
siblings — we never measure non-selected cards.

## 3. `src/pages/OpeningsPage.tsx` — restructure workspace + render connectors

DOM restructure (split the single scroller into scroller → positioned canvas so
the SVG overlay survives both scroll axes, mirroring the prototype):

```
.openings-tree-workspace                 board + tree, bounded height (desktop)
  .openings-tree-board                    sticky, square, clamp width
    <Chessboard/>                         (unchanged options)
  .openings-tree-scroll                   overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:hidden; min-width:0
    .openings-tree-canvas                 position:relative; display:flex; gap:32px; width:max-content
      <svg.openings-tree-connectors>      pointer-events:none; overflow:visible
      TreeColumnView * N                  (each = an independent vertical scroller)
      <frontier append placeholder>       loading/error (unchanged markup, lives in canvas)
```
- Replace `.openings-tree-columns` with `.openings-tree-scroll` > `.openings-tree-canvas`.
  Keep the loading-skeleton block structurally similar (skeleton columns inside a
  canvas-like wrapper so the skeleton still renders).
- `TreeColumnView` gains a `columnIndex` prop (the `view.columns.map` index) and
  ref-setter callbacks `registerColumn(idx, el)` / `registerSelectedNode(idx, el)`.
  - attach `registerColumn` to the column root (keep `data-testid="tree-column"`).
  - mark active column: `const isActive = column.nodes.some(n => n.isExpanded)` →
    add `openings-tree-column--active`.
  - wrap **only the selected node's** card in a plain `<div ref={el => registerSelectedNode(columnIndex, el)}>`
    (card has `width:100%`, so the wrapper box == card box; layout unchanged).
- Page owns stable memoized `Map`s `columnEls` / `selectedNodeEls` (same pattern as
  prototype `useMemo(() => new Map(), [])`) + `canvasRef` + `scrollRef`.
- Compute connector styles from the model (pure, no DOM) every render — NOT inside
  the measure hook, so live metadata always reaches the DOM (review finding 2):
  `const styles = columns.slice(0, -1).map((_, i) => connectorStyle(columns[i+1].nodes.find(n => n.isSelected) ?? null))`.
- Call `useTreeConnectors(...)` for geometry → render `<svg>` zipping geometry with
  `styles[i]` at render time (bezier + arrowhead + clamp-tip glyphs ported from the
  prototype). Each path:
  - the curve carries `className="openings-tree-connector"` (the contract the unit
    test + e2e wait query); the `<svg>` wrapper is `.openings-tree-connectors`.
  - `stroke="currentColor"`, `strokeWidth={styles[i].width}`.
  - `strokeDasharray={styles[i].dashed ? "5 4" : undefined}` — **dash is reserved
    strictly for book-only**; it does NOT change when an endpoint is clamped
    offscreen (review finding 3 — keeps "dashed book-only / solid observed"
    unambiguous).
  - offscreen/clamped endpoints are signaled by **opacity + the clamp-tip glyph
    only** (e.g. `opacity={(c.off || c.off2) ? 0.5 : 0.9}`), never by toggling dash.
  - marker `fill="currentColor"`. SVG color via CSS (`color: var(--brand-primary)`),
    so connectors are theme-aware.
- **Autoscroll** (small effect, keyed on `selectionKey`): scroll the active display
  column (`columnEls.get(view.selectionLine.length)`) into the scroller so the
  expanded column sits near the left and the next compact column peeks:
  `scrollRef.current.scrollLeft = activeEl.offsetLeft - inset`. Defensive no-op if
  refs missing (also covers jsdom). This delivers the "next column peeks" criterion.

No change to selection / drop / perspective / canonicalization / Start Drill / the
five states — those already pass tests.

## 4. `src/App.css` — production layout (`.openings-tree*`)

Rewrite the `.openings-tree-workspace` / `-board` / column rules (lines ~7186–7244)
and add the new scroller/canvas/connector rules. Sizing per the bead contract:

Desktop:
- `.openings-tree-workspace { display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.5rem); }`  (16–24px board↔tree gap)
- `.openings-tree-board { width: clamp(280px, 30vw, 380px); aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; flex: 0 0 auto; position: sticky; top: 1rem; }`
  — square + sticky; ≤380px < 420px band min, so the board never dictates column height.
- `.openings-tree-scroll { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; padding-bottom: .5rem; }`  ("tree minmax(0,1fr)" + explicit overflow on both axes)
- `.openings-tree-canvas { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 2rem; width: max-content; }`  (32px inter-column gap; `width:max-content` so the SVG spans the full scroll width)
- `.openings-tree-column { flex: 0 0 9.25rem; width: 9.25rem; /* 148px compact */ display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:.3rem; max-height: clamp(420px, calc(100dvh - 13rem), 56rem); overflow-y: auto; overflow-x: hidden; }`
  — independent per-column vertical scroll, viewport-bounded with a 420px usable
  minimum; `overflow-x:hidden` pinned (prevents spurious per-column h-scrollbars).
- `.openings-tree-column--active { flex-basis: 14.5rem; width: 14.5rem; /* 232px */ }`
- `.openings-tree-connectors { position:absolute; inset:0; width:100%; height:100%; overflow:visible; pointer-events:none; z-index:5; color: var(--brand-primary); }`
- Keep `.openings-tree-board--skeleton` (give the skeleton wrapper the clamp width
  + `aspect-ratio`) and `.openings-tree-column--skeleton` working.

Narrow (`@media (max-width: 720px)`), per the bead:
- `.openings-tree-workspace { flex-direction: column; }`  (board above tree)
- `.openings-tree-board { width: min(100%, 360px); position: static; }`  (un-stick; normal page scroll)
- `.openings-tree-column { min-height: 17.5rem; /* 280px */ max-height: 45dvh; }`  (tree band)
- horizontal scroll + 148px columns keep one next column peeking; the whole page
  scrolls vertically normally (workspace height is content-driven here).

13rem chrome estimate in the desktop `calc` is intentionally generous (nav logo is
`clamp(72px,10vw,112px)` + app-shell padding + header); the `clamp` 420px floor
guarantees usability on short viewports regardless of the estimate's slack. This
avoids fragile global height surgery on the shared `.app-shell`.

## 5. Tests

- `src/openings/treeView.test.ts` (extend): assert `buildTreeView` populates
  `inBook/isObserved/encounterCount` on api `DisplayNode`s and defaults them on the
  root; table-test `connectorStyle` (null → neutral; book-only → dashed; observed →
  solid; width clamps at low/high encounter counts).
- `src/pages/OpeningsPage.test.tsx` (keep green; add data→style assertion): existing
  selectors (`tree-column`, `.tree-node-card__move/score/--expanded`, board test-id,
  Loading…, Retry, Black/White, Start Drill) are all preserved by the restructure.
  Add a **non-geometry** assertion that proves `connectorStyle` reaches DOM
  attributes (review finding 5): mock a tree whose selected edge has known metadata,
  select that line, and assert the rendered connector `<path>` carries the expected
  `stroke-dasharray` + `stroke-width`:
  - a **book-only** selected child (`in_book:true, is_observed:false, encounter_count:0`)
    → `path` has `stroke-dasharray="5 4"` and `stroke-width="2"`.
  - an **observed** selected child (`is_observed:true`, e.g. `encounter_count:7`)
    → no `stroke-dasharray` and `stroke-width` ≈ `connectorStyle` (`2+log2(8)=5`).
  This works even with zero jsdom geometry because styles are applied at render time,
  not measured. (Keep the `path` count ≥ 1 check as part of this.)
- `e2e/screenshots/pages.screens.spec.ts` (rewrite the `openings` describe): the
  current block targets the **deleted grid** (`.openings-shell`, `.openings-state--empty`,
  `/api/openings/children`) and is stale. Rewrite for the tree page using
  `**/api/openings/tree**` and the new states, captured across `viewportsFor("openings")`
  (defaults to ALL_VIEWPORTS — already includes desktop 1440×900 and `<=720`
  mobile 390×844 / mobileShort 360×640, satisfying the criterion):
  - `loading` → `stallRoute('**/api/openings/tree**')`, wait `.openings-state--loading`.
  - `populated` (due user) → wait `.openings-tree-workspace`, capture.
  - `selected-line` → click a **compact card button** (`button.tree-node-card--compact`,

  Reuse `prepareDeterministicPage`, `loginAs`, `captureAcrossViewports`, the slow-

## 6. `SPEC.md` §13.3

design:
# g-tree-page-state — Replace openings grid with tree data flow

## Context

`/openings` currently renders the legacy named-root **card grid** (`OpeningsPage.tsx`,
~580 lines: hero stats, breadcrumbs, `OpeningFamilyCard` grid, drill-down via
`getOpeningChildren`). The epic **g-d5cu** replaces that body with the
chesstree.net-style **horizontal selected-branch move tree** synced to a board.

Everything around the page is already built and merged:
- **Backend** `GET /api/openings/tree` (`backend/app/api/openings.py:1276`) — fully
  hydrates one column per position along a canonical UCI line in a single request
  (structural graph + observed overlay + persisted position metrics + analysis-cache
  evals). Returns `canonical_line`, `selected_fen/ply`, terminal info, `drill_opening_key`,
  `root_eval_cp/mate`, and `columns[].nodes[]` (white-relative evals).
- **Route helpers** `src/openings/route.ts` — `buildOpeningsSearchParams`,
  `parseOpeningsSearchParams`, `buildCanonicalReplacement` (tree URL = `color` + repeated
  `move=<uci>`; legacy `opening=<fen>` honored when no `move`).
- **Card** `src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx` — presentational compact/expanded
  variants over an `OpeningTreeNodeView`; owns its select button + Start Drill button.
  Eval fields are **perspective-relative** (page must flip white-relative API values).
- **Format helpers** `src/openings/format.ts` — `formatMoveLabel`, `formatTerminalReason`,
  `formatOpeningName`, `getGradeToken/Text/PriorityLabel`, `formatScore/Percent/Games`.

**This bead is the data-flow wiring**: API client + a narrow hook + a pure view
transform + a rewritten page that fetches the tree, renders board+columns of the
existing card, handles selection/board-sync/perspective/canonicalization/caching/
stale-guards/recovery states. **Detailed viewport layout is explicitly out of scope**
(sibling **g-tree-layout**): no SVG connectors, no `clamp()`/`dvh` viewport-bounding, no
responsive stacking, no sticky board. Build only minimal functional CSS so columns and
board render and behaviors are testable.

### Scope boundaries vs sibling beads
- **g-tree-layout** (blocked by this): SVG connectors, viewport sizing, column widths,
  mobile stacking, sticky board, Playwright screenshots. → I add only minimal CSS.
- **g-tree-drill-links** (blocked by this): drill correctness + GameOpeningLineage/session
  link migration. → I wire the *basic* Start Drill nav (`drill_opening_key` → `/play`),
  leave `GameOpeningLineage` on its legacy `buildOpeningsSearchParams` path untouched.
- **g-tree-cleanup**: deletes the dead grid CSS (`openings-shell*`, `openings-grid`),
  `OpeningFamilyCard` if unused, and the `/tree-prototype` route. → I stop importing the
  old code but do **not** delete it here.

---

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/utils/api.ts` | **Add** `TreeNode`, `TreeColumn`, `TreeResponse` interfaces + `getOpeningTree({playerColor, moves, opening?})`. Mirror existing `getOpeningChildren` shape; build `player_color` + repeated `move` + optional `opening`. |
| `src/openings/treeView.ts` | **New** pure module: white→perspective eval flip, `TreeNode→OpeningTreeNodeView`, synthesize root view, build display-column model, replay UCI line → board full-FEN + last-move squares, drop→uci resolver. No React. |
| `src/hooks/useOpeningsTree.ts` | **New** narrow data-flow hook: request lifecycle, response cache, stale-guard, page-vs-append status. Chess instances/effects stay outside any store (no Zustand). |
| `src/pages/OpeningsPage.tsx` | **Rewrite**: parse URL via route helper, drive the hook, render board + columns of `OpeningTreeNodeCard`, wire selection / board-drop / perspective / canonicalization / Start Drill / the 5 states. |
| `src/App.css` | **Add** minimal `.openings-tree*` workspace/column/board CSS (functional, not polished). Leave legacy `openings-shell*`/`openings-grid` for g-tree-cleanup. |
| `src/pages/OpeningsPage.test.tsx` | **Rewrite** for the tree model (mock `getOpeningTree` + `react-chessboard`). |
| `src/openings/treeView.test.ts` | **New** unit tests for the pure transforms. |
| `SPEC.md` §13.3 | Update page semantics from grid/hero to the tree page (data flow, states, board sync). |

---

## Data model & view transform (`treeView.ts`, pure + unit-tested)

The transform is **`buildTreeView(response, { selectionLine, loadedThroughPly,
isExactResponseLine }, color)`**. Selection/expansion derive from `selectionLine`, *not* the
response's baked `is_selected`/`selected_uci` — this is what lets a longer cached/displayed
response be **clipped** and re-rendered correctly (back-nav with no refetch; provisional
sibling/divergent views; see the hook).

**Two explicit depths (finding 3), never conflated:**
- **`loadedThroughPly`** caps which response columns are *rendered*: only `columns[ply] where
  ply <= loadedThroughPly`. Everything deeper is dropped; the page draws the loading/error
  **frontier placeholder** beyond it. (Settled render: `loadedThroughPly =
  selectionLine.length`, the deepest selected position's children column. Provisional render:
  `loadedThroughPly = d` = the divergence.)
- **`selectionLine`** drives which node is *selected/expanded* per column. The caller
  guarantees `selectionLine.length - 1 <= loadedThroughPly`, so the expanded node always sits
  in a rendered column — a deep stale URL can never expand a ply we don't render.

**`isExactResponseLine`** = `selectionLine` deep-equals `response.canonical_line`. When
**false** (any clipped/provisional view), the transform **must not read response-level
selected fields** (`selected_fen`, `selected_is_terminal`, `selected_terminal_reason`,
`drill_opening_key`) — those still describe the deeper *fetched* line, not the clipped one
(finding 2). Board/terminal/drill for a clipped view come from per-node data + the replayed
effective line instead. (`root_eval_cp/mate` is the start-position eval, line-independent, so
it is exempt and always usable.)

The backend column model: **`columns[i]`** has `position_fen = pos[i]`, `ply = i`,
`nodes = moves out of pos[i]`. `k = selectionLine.length` for the view being rendered.

**Rendering rule** ("only the deepest selected node is expanded"): the selected path is
`root → line[0] node in col0 → … → line[k-1] node in col(k-1)`. The **deepest** on-path
node is `line[k-1]` in `columns[k-1]`; it renders **expanded**. All other on-path nodes
render compact+highlighted; everything else compact. At `k === 0` there is no selected
api node — the **synthesized root card** is the expanded "current position".

Display columns = `[rootColumn, ...apiColumns]` (mirrors the prototype's leading Start
column, dropped from the API shape):
- **rootColumn**: one synthesized node `{ply:0, san:null, score/coverage/gameCount/
  confidence:null, evalCp/Mate: flip(root_eval_cp/mate)}`. `isTerminal`/`terminalReason`/
  `drillOpeningKey` are taken from the response **only when `isExactResponseLine && k===0`**
  (i.e. the response was actually fetched for root) — **else `false`/`null`** (finding 2: a
  deeper response's drill/terminal must not leak onto the clipped root). Expanded iff
  `k === 0`, else compact+highlighted (on path). Selecting it → `newLine = []`.
- **apiColumn i** (`columns[i]` with `ply <= loadedThroughPly`, `lineIndex = column.ply`):
  each `TreeNode → view` (perspective flip on eval). `isSelected = node.uci ===
  selectionLine[column.ply]` (derived, not baked); expanded iff `column.ply === k-1 &&
  isSelected`. Selecting a node → `newLine = selectionLine.slice(0, column.ply).concat(node.uci)`.

The expanded node in `columns[k-1]` has `child_fen === selected_fen`, so it already
carries the **selected position's** score/coverage/games/confidence + the eval of the
move that reached it, and its `terminal_reason` reflects pos[k] terminality — no extra
response field needed.

**Board** (`replayLine(selectionLine)` via chess.js from the start position — always the
**effective** line, never `response.selected_fen` which may describe a deeper fetched line):
full FEN of pos[k] + `{from,to}` of `selectionLine[k-1]` for last-move highlight. Orientation
= `playerColor` (flips immediately on perspective switch, before the refetch resolves).
**Drop → uci** (`resolveDrop(selectedFullFen, from, to)`): `new
Chess(fen).move({from,to,promotion:'q'})`; uci = `from+to+(move.promotion ?? '')`;
return `null` if illegal. The page accepts the drop only when the children column of pos[k]
is actually rendered (settled, `loadedThroughPly === k`) **and** the uci matches a
**navigable** node (`is_navigable`) there; mid-fetch/provisional and terminal positions
reject all drops.

**Perspective flip** helper: `cp → (color==='black' ? -cp : cp)`, same for mate; nulls
pass through. Applied when building every view (nodes + root).

---

## Hook state machine (`useOpeningsTree.ts`)

Input: the parsed route `{playerColor, moves, opening}`. Output: `{view, pageStatus,
appendStatus, error, canonicalLine, isSettled, retry}`.

**Two keys, deliberately different (finding 2):**
- **requestKey** (cache *lookup*, drives whether we fetch): `\`${color}\n${moves.length ?
  'm:' + moves.join(' ') : 'o:' + (opening ?? '')}\``. A legacy `opening=<fen>` link gets a
  *distinct* key from root (empty line), so a cached root can never short-circuit the
  backend FEN→line resolution the SPEC requires (`SPEC.md:2334`, `openings.py:1069`).
- **canonicalKey** (cache *store*): `\`${color}\nm:${response.canonical_line.join(' ')}\``.
  Identical to the requestKey of an already-canonical `move=` URL, so backtracking to a prefix
  hits this.

State held in the hook:
- `cacheRef: Map<string, TreeResponse>` — a resolved response is stored under **both** its
  canonicalKey and the requestKey that fetched it.
- `displayed` (state): last successfully-rendered `TreeResponse` + the **`displayedLine`**
  it was fetched for. Kept on screen during transitions.
- `versionRef`: monotonic counter; an in-flight resolution is dropped unless its captured
  version is still current (stale guard, as today). An `AbortController` per request aborts
  the prior in-flight fetch (finding 4); the version guard backstops a late settle.

`isSettled`/`canonicalLine` describe **the view actually rendered for the current route**,
which is settled in exactly two cases: an **exact-line response** for the current route
(step 1 cache hit / step 4 resolve → `canonicalLine = response.canonical_line`), or a
**prefix clip of a same-color superset** (step 2 → `canonicalLine = requestedLine`). In both
the rendered columns are correct and canonical for the current route. They are
`false`/`null` only while a fetch is **pending** (step 3) and stale `displayed` columns
remain on screen as a placeholder. The page canonicalizes **only when `isSettled`**
(round-1 finding 1), so a stale response kept during a refetch can never rewrite a
freshly-selected `?move=e2e4` URL back to `[]`.

Per route change (effect keyed on color + `JSON.stringify(moves)` + opening + retry nonce):
1. **Exact cache hit** on requestKey → displayed = cached, settled, `pageStatus='ready'`,
   `appendStatus='idle'`. No network.
2. **Prefix no-fetch path — gated on `opening == null` AND same color AND requestedLine ⊆
   displayedLine.** All three guards are required:
   - **`opening == null`** (round-3 finding 1): a legacy `opening=<fen>` link has `moves=[]`,
     and `[]` is a prefix of *any* displayed line — without this guard a same-color displayed
     response would let `[]` take the no-fetch path and skip the backend FEN→line resolution
     (`SPEC.md:2334`). A legacy `opening=` link therefore only short-circuits on an **exact
     `o:<fen>` requestKey hit** (step 1); otherwise it falls through to step 3 (fetch).
   - **`displayed.player_color === playerColor`** (round-2 finding 1): else White→Black at the
     same line (esp. root `[]`) would reuse white-specific metrics/sort as black
     (`SPEC.md:2351`).
   - **prefix** (`requestedLine.length <= d`, `d = commonPrefix(displayedLine, requestedLine)`):
     the displayed response is a **superset**.

   When all hold: `buildTreeView(displayed, {selectionLine: requestedLine, loadedThroughPly:
   requestedLine.length, isExactResponseLine: false}, color)` renders fully (no fetch). Deeper
   columns drop immediately (round-1 finding 3). **The hook exposes `canonicalLine =
   requestedLine` and `isSettled = true`** (round-3 finding 2) — *not*
   `displayed.canonical_line`; a prefix of a canonical navigable line is itself canonical, and
   returning the deeper displayed line would let the page canonicalize the URL back to the
   deeper line (e.g. back-nav `e2e4,c7c5 → e2e4` snapping forward again). `isExactResponseLine`
   stays `false` here (a strict prefix ≠ the response's line), keeping response-level
   `selected_*`/root-synth fields suppressed per round-2 finding 6.
3. **Otherwise** (extend / sibling / divergent / **color-switch**) → bump version, capture it,
   open an AbortController. **Provisional view** = `buildTreeView(displayed, {selectionLine:
   requestedLine.slice(0, d+1), loadedThroughPly: d, isExactResponseLine: false}, color)` —
   render displayed columns `ply <= d`, mark+expand the divergence node at ply `d`, **drop all
   columns `ply > d`** (sibling/truncate never leave stale deeper columns — finding 3) — **plus
   a single loading-placeholder column** at the frontier. On a color-switch the board
   orientation flips immediately and the stale-color columns stay only as a visual placeholder
   (never settled, so no canonicalization off the wrong-color response). If `displayed ===
   null` → `pageStatus='loading'` (page skeleton); else `appendStatus='loading'`. Fire
   `getOpeningTree({...route}, {signal})`.
4. **Resolve** (version current): store under canonicalKey + requestKey; displayed =
   response; settled (`selectionLine = response.canonical_line`, `loadedThroughPly =
   canonical_line.length`, `isExactResponseLine = true` — so a backend **truncation** of a
   stale/invalid line renders the canonical line, not the requested one); `pageStatus='ready'`,
   `appendStatus='idle'`. Page then canonicalizes the URL to `canonical_line`.
5. **Reject** (version current, not an `AbortError`): `displayed === null` →
   `pageStatus='error'` (page retry); else `appendStatus='error'` (the frontier placeholder
   becomes inline error+Retry; displayed columns untouched).

`retry()` bumps a retry nonce in the effect deps to refetch the current route.

---

## Page behaviors (`OpeningsPage.tsx`)

- **Parse**: `parseOpeningsSearchParams(searchParams)` → `{playerColor, moves, opening}`.
  Feed to the hook.
- **Canonicalize**: **only when `isSettled`** (the rendered view is settled for the current
  route — round-1 finding 1), `buildCanonicalReplacement(searchParams, playerColor, canonicalLine)`;
  if non-null → `setSearchParams(replacement, {replace:true})`. Rewrites legacy `opening=` →
  `move=` line, truncates invalid/stale lines, normalizes `color`, drops junk. Returns null
  when already canonical (no loop). Gating on `isSettled` prevents a stale displayed
  response (kept visible during a refetch) from rewriting the URL backward.
- **Render**: compact header + a single segmented **"Playing as: White | Black"** control
  (the only color selector). Below it the workspace: board (left) + horizontally-scrolling
  display columns (right). Each column = vertical list of `OpeningTreeNodeCard` (compact),
  with the deepest selected node expanded. Append column renders a loading placeholder or
  inline error+Retry when `appendStatus !== 'idle'`.
- **Select**: clicking a node → compute `newLine` (rule above) →
  `setSearchParams(buildOpeningsSearchParams({playerColor, moves: newLine}))` (push, so
  history Back works). Truncation falls out of `slice` + a shorter line.
- **Board drop**: `resolveDrop` → match navigable node in deepest column → select (extend
  line). No match (legal but off-tree, or illegal) → return `false` (board snaps back),
  so board and tree cannot diverge.
- **Perspective switch**: click other color → `setSearchParams(buildOpeningsSearchParams(
  {playerColor: other, moves: currentLine}))`. Line preserved; hook refetches (color in
  key); board orientation flips; backend canonicalizes if an observed-only continuation
  is unavailable for the new side. Existing columns stay visible during refetch (displayed
  != null → append path).
- **Start Drill**: expanded card's `onStartDrill` (shown only when node `drillOpeningKey`
  != null) → `navigate('/play', {state:{drillSetup:{openingKey: drillOpeningKey,
  playerColor}}})` (existing `ChessGame.tsx:941` contract). Correctness deepening is
  g-tree-drill-links.

### The five distinct states
1. **Initial loading** — `pageStatus==='loading' && !displayed` → board/workspace skeleton.
2. **No-data** — response renders normally (book tree, null scores → "—"/no-data grade,
   fully navigable) **plus** a subtle banner when `batch_computed_at === null`
   ("No games for {color} yet — showing the reference opening book"). Not an empty page.
3. **Page error** — `pageStatus==='error' && !displayed` → page-level message + Retry.
4. **Missing eval** — per node, handled by the card (em dash); never an error or a
   browser engine search.
5. **Child-column retry** — `appendStatus==='error'` → inline error + Retry in the
   appending right-most column; existing columns untouched.

---

## API client (`src/utils/api.ts`)

```ts
export interface TreeNode { parent_fen; child_fen; uci; san; ply; opening_name;
  eco; in_book; is_navigable; is_observed; is_prepared; user_choice_count;
  encounter_count; opening_score; confidence; coverage; sample_size; game_count;
  last_practiced_at; eval_cp; eval_mate; terminal_reason; drill_opening_key;
  is_selected } // null-types per the pydantic model in openings.py
export interface TreeColumn { position_fen; ply; selected_uci; nodes: TreeNode[] }
export interface TreeResponse { player_color; canonical_line; selected_fen;
  selected_ply; selected_is_terminal; selected_terminal_reason; drill_opening_key;
  root_eval_cp; root_eval_mate; columns: TreeColumn[]; batch_computed_at; model_version }

export const getOpeningTree = async (
  { playerColor, moves, opening },
  options?: { signal?: AbortSignal },   // finding 4: real abort, not decorative
) => {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ player_color: playerColor })
  for (const m of moves ?? []) params.append('move', m)
  if (opening && !(moves?.length)) params.set('opening', opening)
  return requestJson<TreeResponse>(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/openings/tree?${params}`,
    { method:'GET', headers:getAuthHeaders(), signal: options?.signal },
    { fallbackMessage:'Failed to load openings' })
}
```

`requestJson` forwards `init.signal` to `fetch` (`src/utils/api.ts:186`); the
`options?: { signal? }` shape mirrors `uploadSessionMoves` (`src/utils/api.ts:673`).

---

## Minimal CSS (`src/App.css`)

Functional only — g-tree-layout polishes. `.openings-tree-workspace` (flex row, board +
tree), `.openings-tree-board` (fixed ~`min(360px, …)` width — no `clamp`/sticky),
`.openings-tree-columns` (`display:flex; overflow-x:auto`), `.openings-tree-column`
(flex column, own `overflow-y:auto`, pinned `overflow-x:hidden` to avoid spurious
scrollbars — borrow the prototype's pin), `.openings-tree-append--loading/--error`. No
SVG connector layer.

---

## Tests

**`treeView.test.ts`** (pure): display-column build (root prepend, deepest-expanded,
on-path highlight, `lineIndex` selection math incl. truncation), eval perspective flip,
root synth at `k===0` (terminal/drill propagation), `replayLine` board FEN + last-move,
`resolveDrop` (legal-navigable vs legal-off-tree vs illegal, promotion uci).

**`OpeningsPage.test.tsx`** (behavioral; mock `getOpeningTree` + `react-chessboard` as in
the current file, `MemoryRouter` + `LocationProbe`). Covers the bead's required matrix:
- selection + truncation (sibling in a mid column → URL line truncates+pushes; assert the
  deeper columns **drop immediately**, before the refetch resolves — finding 3)
- **legacy-link never short-circuits (round-1 finding 2 + round-3 finding 1)**: with a
  same-color response already **displayed** (root *and* a deep line), navigate to
  `?opening=<fen>`; assert `getOpeningTree` **is called** with `opening` (the `[]`-prefix path
  does not skip it) and the URL canonicalizes to the resolved `move=` line
- **prefix back-nav does not snap forward (round-3 finding 2)**: from a settled
  `move=e2e4&move=c7c5`, navigate to `move=e2e4`; assert the URL **stays** `…move=e2e4` (not
  rewritten back to the deeper line) and no refetch fires
- **no backward canonicalization (finding 1)**: with a root response displayed, select
  `move=e2e4` while its fetch is still pending; assert the URL stays `…&move=e2e4` (the
  stale root response does not rewrite it to `[]`)
- board→tree sync (navigable drop → URL extends, board `data-position` follows; off-tree
  legal drop → rejected, URL unchanged)
- URL restoration (deep `move` line renders columns) + canonicalization (non-canonical
  line → URL replaced to `canonical_line`; legacy `opening=` → rewritten to `move`)
- perspective switch (→ `color=black`, line preserved, board `data-orientation` flips,
  **refetch fires even at the same line incl. root** and color-specific metrics re-hydrate —
  finding 5)
- clipped-view field isolation (finding 6): from a deep line whose selected node is
  drillable/terminal, back-nav to root → root card shows **no** drill/terminal (not the deeper
  line's), with no refetch
- depth separation (finding 7): a deep stale `move=` URL over a shallow displayed response
  renders columns only through the divergence and expands only the divergence node (no leaked
  deeper columns)
- compact vs expanded (only deepest selected node expanded)
- loading/error recovery (initial skeleton; page error + Retry refetches; append error +
  column Retry while existing columns stay)
- no-data navigation (null-metric book tree still navigable; banner on
  `batch_computed_at===null`)
- stale guard (response settling during a color switch is ignored)
- drill nav (Start Drill present iff `drill_opening_key`; navigates to `/play` with
  `drillSetup`)

Per epic: **no** connector coordinates, pixel layout, or cosmetic-copy assertions.

---

## Verification

1. `npm run test -- src/pages/OpeningsPage.test.tsx src/openings/treeView.test.ts`
   (rerun named files in isolation — pre-push vitest is flaky under parallel load).
2. `npm run build` (production type-check + bundle).
3. Manual (`/run` or dev server): load `/openings`, click through columns (board syncs),
   drag a book move on the board (selects) and an off-tree legal move (rejected), toggle
   Playing as White/Black (orientation flips, line preserved), reload a deep link, paste a
   stale/legacy `opening=` link (canonicalizes), Start Drill from a named root.

---

## Review fixes incorporated

**Round 1**
1. **Backward canonicalization (High)** → hook exposes `isSettled`/`canonicalLine` scoped to
   the current requestKey; page canonicalizes only when settled. Regression test added.
2. **Legacy `opening=` cache bypass (High)** → distinct **requestKey** (`o:<fen>` vs root's
   empty line) forces the backend resolution; store under canonicalKey too. Regression test added.
3. **Append too broad for sibling/truncate (Medium)** → divergence-clipped provisional view:
   render displayed columns `ply <= d`, drop everything deeper *immediately*, placeholder only
   at the frontier; prefix requests render fully with no fetch. Column-drop test added.
4. **Decorative abort (Low)** → `getOpeningTree(route, { signal })` threads `signal` into the
   `fetch` init (matches `uploadSessionMoves`).

**Round 2**
5. **Prefix shortcut color guard (High)** → step 2's no-fetch path also requires
   `displayed.player_color === playerColor`; a color switch always routes through the fetch
   path. Test: White→Black at the same line refetches and re-hydrates color-specific metrics.
6. **Clipped views must not read response-level selected fields (Medium)** → `isExactResponseLine`
   gates `selected_fen`/`selected_terminal_reason`/`drill_opening_key`; clipped board/terminal/
   drill derive from the replayed effective line + per-node data. Test: back-nav to root after a
   deep drillable/terminal line shows no drill/terminal on the root card.
7. **Conflated render vs selection depth (Medium)** → `buildTreeView` takes explicit
   `loadedThroughPly` (rendered columns) separate from `selectionLine` (selected/expanded node),
   with `selectionLine.length-1 <= loadedThroughPly` enforced. Test: a deep stale URL over a
   shallow displayed response renders only through `d` and expands only the divergence node.
8. **Minor** → canonicalKey example typo (`${m:}`) fixed to `m:${canonical_line.join(' ')}`.

**Round 3**
9. **Legacy `opening=` bypassed by the prefix shortcut (High)** → step 2's no-fetch path now
   also requires `opening == null`; a legacy `opening=<fen>` (with `moves=[]`, a prefix of
   everything) only short-circuits on an exact `o:<fen>` requestKey hit, else it fetches so the
   backend resolves the FEN→line. Test generalized to a displayed-response (not just cache) case.
10. **Prefix-branch `canonicalLine` (Medium)** → step 2 explicitly exposes `canonicalLine =
    requestedLine` (not `displayed.canonical_line`), so a back-nav to a prefix can't
    canonicalize the URL forward to the deeper line. Test added.

## Known limitations / deliberate follow-ups

- **Root card score**: the `/tree` response carries metrics only on child nodes, so the
  start-position ("whole repertoire") expanded card shows score `—` + root eval. Surfacing
  a whole-repertoire score is a backend response change — defer (not in this bead's
  acceptance). Flag for a follow-up bead if the user wants the old hero number back.
- **Promotion**: board drops assume queen promotion (mirrors the prototype); navigable
  underpromotion uci still selectable via the tree node.
- Legacy CSS / `OpeningFamilyCard` / `/tree-prototype` removal → g-tree-cleanup.
