title: Extract reusable opening tree node cards
description:
Build production presentational cards for tree nodes, derived from the prototype but shaped for reuse. Compact and expanded variants show the active perspective's metrics without embedding a chessboard or nesting interactive controls.

The cards should look similar to the current opening cards including the showing of colors based on grades. Consider also that the cards will be reused in other surfaces such as game-opening-lineage in analysis-board.
design:
# Plan: Extract reusable opening tree node cards (g-tree-node-cards)

## Context

The `/openings` page is being rebuilt as a chesstree.net-style horizontal move
graph (epic `g-d5cu`). The tree API (`g-tree-api`) and route helpers
(`g-route-tree-url`) already ship. This task builds the **card components** that
render each tree node.

The compact (collapsed) card is the **primary rendering for every non-expanded
node in the tree itself**, and is *also* reused by `GameOpeningLineage` in the
analysis board. The expanded card renders for the single deepest selected node.
The prototype in `src/pages/TreePrototypePage.tsx` proved the look with inline
styles + mock data; we extract production components here.

**Interaction model (decided with the user): self-contained cards.** The card
owns its own interactive elements:
- **Compact** renders its own selection `<button>` (controlled: takes
  `isSelected` + `onSelect`, sets `aria-pressed`). It is the thing you click to
  select/navigate a node.
- **Expanded** is a `<div>` that owns its **Start Drill** button (via
  `onStartDrill`).

The page (`g-tree-page-state`) supplies data + callbacks and remains the source
of truth for *which* node is selected (URL-driven); the card renders the
controls and visual state. The full plan is mirrored in the bead design field.

## 1. Scope and boundary

Pure render + local interaction layer: no data fetching, no Chess instance, no
store, no board, no URL logic. The card owns the selection button and the Start
Drill button, but not the business logic behind them (navigation target, drill
route setup) — those arrive as injected callbacks.

- **Eval perspective flip is NOT here.** API returns white-relative
  `eval_cp`/`eval_mate`; `g-tree-page-state` flips to the selected perspective
  when mapping a `TreeNode` to the card view-model.
- **Column widths / workspace layout (148/232px, gaps, scroll) NOT here** →
  `g-tree-layout`. Card is width-agnostic (`width:100%; min-width:0`).
- **Drill route/setup wiring behind `onStartDrill`, node-selection target behind
  `onSelect`, view-model construction → `g-tree-page-state` / `g-tree-drill-links`.**

## 2. Component API / view-model contract

New `src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx`. One component, two variants, plus
an exported view-model type that `g-tree-page-state` targets:

```ts
export interface OpeningTreeNodeView {
  ply: number;                 // 0 = root; 1 = after White's 1st move
  san: string | null;          // null at root
  openingName: string | null;
  eco: string | null;
  score: number | null;        // 0–100; null = no evidence
  evalCp: number | null;       // PERSPECTIVE-RELATIVE centipawns
  evalMate: number | null;     // PERSPECTIVE-RELATIVE mate-in-N
  coverage: number | null;
  gameCount: number | null;    // DISTINCT sessions (not sample_size)
  confidence: number | null;
  isTerminal: boolean;
  terminalReason: string | null;   // checkmate | stalemate | opening_boundary | no_children
  drillOpeningKey: string | null;  // from API node.drill_opening_key; non-null => drillable root
}

interface OpeningTreeNodeCardProps {
  variant: "compact" | "expanded";
  node: OpeningTreeNodeView;

  // Compact (interactive). When onSelect is given the card renders a <button>.
  onSelect?: () => void;
  isSelected?: boolean;        // selected/on-path highlight + aria-pressed
  // Optional disclosure affordance for the GameOpeningLineage reuse case:
  isExpanded?: boolean;        // when defined, sets aria-expanded
  controlsId?: string;         // when set, sets aria-controls

  // Expanded. Renders one "Start Drill" button when node.drillOpeningKey != null.
  onStartDrill?: () => void;
}
```

Mapping note for page-state (child nodes): copy fields, flip eval
(`evalCp = perspective === "white" ? eval_cp : -eval_cp`, null-safe; same for
`evalMate`), `gameCount = node.game_count`,
`drillOpeningKey = node.drill_opening_key`.

**Root node mapping (for page-state).** The start position is NOT a node in
`columns` — the API exposes it via top-level `TreeResponse` fields
(`root_eval_cp`, `root_eval_mate`, `drill_opening_key`, `selected_is_terminal`,
`selected_terminal_reason`; see `backend/app/api/openings.py:769,1193`). The
root `OpeningTreeNodeView` is therefore synthesized, not copied:

- `ply: 0`, `san: null`, `openingName: null`, `eco: null`.
- `score / coverage / gameCount / confidence`: **forced `null`** — the start
  position is a structural anchor, never a scored move.
- `evalCp / evalMate`: `root_eval_cp` / `root_eval_mate`, perspective-flipped
  (null when the cache has no best-move row).
- `isTerminal: false`, `terminalReason: null` (the start always has children).
- `drillOpeningKey`: top-level `drill_opening_key` only when the root IS the
  selected position (`selected_fen` == start); otherwise `null`. (Start Drill
  renders only on the deepest/expanded card, and the root is expanded only when
  it is the selection, so this stays consistent.)

This mapping note is documentation for `g-tree-page-state`; the card itself just
consumes the resulting view and already handles every null via the rules below.

## 3. Compact variant — self-contained selection button, two lines

Renders `<button type="button" onClick={onSelect} aria-pressed={!!isSelected}>`
(falls back to a static `<div>` if no `onSelect`). Selected state drives a
highlight class AND `aria-pressed`; `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` set only when
those optional props are provided (lineage disclosure). The button contains only
non-interactive spans — no nested controls.

- **Line 1:** `[SAN]` (or "Start" at root) left; right group `[score]` +
  `[grade tag]`. Score via `formatScore`; grade letter via `getPriorityLabel`;
  null score → "—" tag with accessible "No data".
- **Line 2:** `[opening name, ellipsis]` (full text in DOM + `title`) left;
  `[eval]` right via `formatWhiteEval(evalCp, evalMate)`, "" → "—". Name uses
  `formatOpeningName` (see §6): non-root null name → "Unclassified"; the root
  (`san === null`) omits the name slot entirely (line 1 already reads "Start").

Accent: left border `3px solid var(--grade-accent)` (mirrors
`game-opening-chip`). Grade encoded by text AND accent — color never the only
signal.

## 4. Expanded variant — `<div>`, no chessboard, owns Start Drill

1. **Header:** `formatMoveLabel(ply, san)` ("Starting position" / "1. e4" /
   "1… e5") + opening-name line via `formatOpeningName` (non-root null name →
   "Unclassified"; root omits the name line — the "Starting position" header
   stands alone).
2. **Score panel:** "Score" (`formatScore`, large) + grade tag; "Eval"
   (`formatWhiteEval` / "—"). `<dl>/<dt>/<dd>`.
3. **Metrics row:** Coverage (`formatPercent`), Games (`formatGames(gameCount)`,
   distinct sessions — never `sample_size`), Confidence (`formatPercent`).
4. **Terminal note** when `isTerminal` via `formatTerminalReason`.
5. **Start Drill button (owned by the card):** rendered only when
   `node.drillOpeningKey != null` AND `onStartDrill` is provided; one button
   labeled exactly "Start Drill" (no side-specific labels — inherits the global
   perspective via the injected handler). Intermediate / observed off-book /
   non-root nodes omit it. Not nested in a button (the expanded card is a div).

Only the active perspective's metrics; card has no other-side concept.

## 5. Grade tokens (format.ts + CSS)

Add to `src/openings/format.ts`, derived from `getPriorityLabel` so thresholds
stay single-sourced:

```ts
export type GradeToken = "a" | "b" | "c" | "d" | "f" | "none";
export function getGradeToken(score: number | null): GradeToken { /* switch on getPriorityLabel */ }
export function getGradeText(score: number | null): string { /* "Grade A".."Grade F" / "No data" */ }
```

Casing is deliberate: the visible null tag (compact line 1, expanded panel)
shows "—", while `getGradeText(null)` returns the accessible-name string
**"No data"** (sentence case) so it reads naturally beside "Grade A". This is
intentionally distinct from `getPriorityLabel(null)`'s visible **"No Data"**
(`src/openings/format.ts:57`); a test pins both casings so neither drifts.

Six `--grade-accent` CSS modifier classes using the existing palette
(`src/index.css`):

| token | `--grade-accent` |
|-------|------------------|
| a | `var(--color-green-600)` #16a34a |
| b | `var(--color-green-500)` #22c55e |
| c | `var(--color-yellow-600)` #ca8a04 |
| d | `var(--color-orange-500)` #f97316 |
| f | `var(--color-red-500)` #ef4444 |
| none | `var(--text-tertiary)` #7a6f5a |

One visual variable per concept: accent = grade only.

## 6. Eval + helpers

- Reuse `formatWhiteEval(cp, mate)` from `src/components/MoveRow.helpers.ts` as a
  generic signed-eval formatter on perspective-relative inputs; "" → "—".
- `formatMoveLabel(ply, san)`: ply≤0/null → "Starting position"; white
  (`ply%2===1`) → `${ceil(ply/2)}. ${san}`; black → `${ceil(ply/2)}… ${san}`.
- `formatTerminalReason(reason)`: checkmate→"Checkmate", stalemate→"Stalemate",
  opening_boundary→"Opening boundary reached", no_children/unknown→"End of line".
- `formatOpeningName(name)`: `name ?? "Unclassified"`. Used only for non-root
  nodes; the root (`san === null`) omits the name line, so the fallback never
  shows at the root.

## 7. Accessibility

- Compact selection button: `aria-pressed` for selected; optional
  `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` for disclosure reuse.
- Grade tag `aria-label={getGradeText(score)}`; accent decorative
  (`aria-hidden`).
- Full opening name in DOM text (ellipsis is visual only) + `title`.
- Expanded metrics use `<dl>/<dt>/<dd>`; Start Drill is a plain labeled button.

## 8. Files to change

1. `src/openings/format.ts` — add `getGradeToken`, `getGradeText`,
   `formatMoveLabel`, `formatTerminalReason` (+ `GradeToken` type).
2. `src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.tsx` — **new** component + exported
   `OpeningTreeNodeView`; internal `GradeTag` shared by both variants.
3. `src/App.css` — **new** `.tree-node-card*` rules + 6 grade-token classes;
   card width-agnostic.
4. `src/openings/format.test.ts` — extend.
5. `src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx` — **new**.

Reuse unchanged: `formatScore`, `formatPercent`, `formatGames`,
`getPriorityLabel` (format.ts); `formatWhiteEval` (MoveRow.helpers.ts).

## 9. Verification

- `npx vitest run src/openings/format.test.ts src/components/OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx`
  (run named files in isolation per the flaky-pre-push note).
- `npm run build` for type/prod safety.
- Behavior tests only — assert text/roles/labels, never class names, pixels, or
  connector coordinates.

Test coverage:
- **format.test.ts:** `getGradeToken` boundaries match `getPriorityLabel`
  (null→none, <45→f, 45→d, 55→c, 70→b, 85→a); `getGradeText` ("Grade A".."Grade
  F" and null→**"No data"**, pinned alongside `getPriorityLabel(null)`→**"No
  Data"** to lock the deliberate casing split); `formatMoveLabel` (ply 0/1/2/3);
  `formatTerminalReason` (each code + fallback); `formatOpeningName` (passthrough
  + null→"Unclassified").
- **OpeningTreeNodeCard.test.tsx:**
  - compact renders a `button`; clicking fires `onSelect`; `aria-pressed`
    reflects `isSelected`; shows SAN/score/grade/full name/eval; null eval → "—";
    null score → "—" tag + accessible "No data"; non-root null name →
    "Unclassified"; the compact button contains no further `button`/`link` roles.
  - **root** view (ply 0, san null, score/coverage/games/confidence null, eval
    from root_eval): compact shows "Start" + eval and "—" score with no name
    slot; expanded shows "Starting position" header, no name line, "—" metrics,
    eval rendered, no crash on null name.
  - expanded is not a button; renders move-label header, score+grade, eval,
    Coverage, Games (from `gameCount`), Confidence; renders one "Start Drill"
    that fires `onStartDrill` when `drillOpeningKey` set, and omits it when null
    or no handler; no embedded board; terminal note per reason; grade accessible
    name for each band.

## 10. Out of scope / follow-ups

- Migrating `GameOpeningLineage` to this compact card (its data has no SAN/eval
  and its disclosure behavior differs); the optional `isExpanded`/`controlsId`
  props leave the door open, but the migration itself is deferred.
- Column widths/scroll/connectors/workspace sizing → `g-tree-layout`.
- API client types, fetch, eval perspective flip, view-model construction,
  selection target → `g-tree-page-state`. Drill route/setup behind `onStartDrill`
  → `g-tree-drill-links`.
- Relocating `formatWhiteEval` to a shared util.
acceptance_criteria: Compact card shows SAN, score, grade, opening name, and nullable perspective-relative eval; expanded card shows score/grade, eval, coverage, distinct game count, confidence, and terminal status; no card shows both White and Black metrics; no nested interactive controls; frontend behavior tests cover compact/expanded and accessibility state without brittle styling assertions.
close_reason: Implemented reusable OpeningTreeNodeCard (compact + expanded) + format helpers, tests passing, build clean, user-reviewed

title: Migrate openings route helpers to move-line URLs
description: Update the frontend openings route helper and callers from opening/path navigation to the tree URL contract: color plus repeated move parameters, with legacy opening links only passed through for backend canonicalization.
design:
## Goal

Migrate the frontend openings route layer (`src/openings/route.ts`) from the
pre-tree named-grid model (`color` + `opening=<key>` + repeated `path=<key>`) to
the tree URL contract: `color` + repeated `move=<uci>`, with the legacy
`opening=<normalized FEN>` kept as a temporary deep-link entry that the backend
canonicalizes. This is the foundational, frontend-only helper task that
`g-tree-node-cards` and `g-tree-page-state` build on; it deliberately does NOT
rewrite `OpeningsPage` or add the tree API client.

## Established context (verified)

- Backend `GET /api/openings/tree` (g-tree-api, done) already implements the
  server side of this contract: query params `player_color` (required),
  repeated `move=<uci>`, legacy `opening=<normalized FEN>` (used only when
  `move` is empty); it returns `TreeResponse.canonical_line: string[]` (UCI) —
  the deepest valid navigable prefix. Stale/invalid lines truncate; bad UCI or
  bad opening FEN → 422. 80-ply ceiling (`MAX_TREE_PLY`). See SPEC §13.5.
- `opening_key` is a **normalized 4-field FEN** (`opening_roots.py:68`
  "normalized 4-field FEN (durable identity)"), so the legacy `opening=<fen>`
  param and existing `opening_key` links are the same kind of value. Slugs like
  `"polish"` in OpeningsPage tests are fixtures only.
- Current `route.ts` exports `OpeningRoute { playerColor; openingKey?; path? }`
  and `buildOpeningsSearchParams` → emits `color`, `opening=<openingKey>`,
  repeated `path=`. There is no parse helper today; `OpeningsPage` parses
  `searchParams` inline (`color`/`opening`/`path`).
- Callers of `buildOpeningsSearchParams`: `OpeningsPage.tsx` (old grid, 4 sites)
  and `GameOpeningLineage.tsx` (one href). `OpeningFamilyCard` only renders a
  pre-built `openingsHref` string. No other component hand-builds `/openings`
  query strings.
- There is **no** frontend `getOpeningTree` client/types yet — that is
  `g-tree-page-state`, not this task.
- Test harness: vitest. `npm test` (watch) / `npm run test:run` (CI) /
  `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build). Style reference: `format.test.ts`.
- Back-compat constraint: `OpeningsPage.test.tsx`, `GameOpeningLineage.test.tsx`,
  `OpeningFamilyCard.test.tsx` all assert the legacy `opening=`/`path=` URL form
  and the old `getOpeningChildren` call shape. The helper change must keep these
  green (the old grid page is replaced later in g-tree-page-state, removed in
  g-tree-cleanup).

## Design — `src/openings/route.ts`

### Type (additive, backward compatible)

```ts
export type OpeningRoute = {
  playerColor: OpeningPlayerColor;
  moves?: string[];        // NEW: tree line; emits repeated move=<uci>
  opening?: string;        // legacy FEN entry; emits opening=<fen> (used when no moves)
  // --- pre-tree named-grid fields, retained until g-tree-page-state / g-tree-cleanup ---
  openingKey?: string;     // legacy alias of `opening` (old grid still passes this)
  path?: string[];         // legacy named path (old grid only)
};
```

`opening` and `openingKey` both map to the `opening=` query param; `opening`
is the new canonical name, `openingKey` is the retained legacy alias so the old
grid page keeps compiling/working unchanged.

### `buildOpeningsSearchParams(route)` — precedence rules

Three mutually-exclusive modes, checked in order. `path` is scoped to the legacy
`openingKey` (named-grid) mode ONLY — the new `opening` FEN entry never emits
`path` (review finding: a `{ opening, openingKey, path }` mix must not produce
`opening=<fen>&path=...`).

1. Always `params.set("color", route.playerColor)`.
2. **Tree mode** — if `route.moves?.length`: append one `move=<uci>` per entry
   **and return**. The move line is the source of truth; all legacy fields
   ignored (no `opening`, no `path`).
3. **Legacy FEN-entry mode** — else if `route.opening`: `params.set("opening",
   route.opening)` **and return** (no `path`; this is the deep-link FEN entry).
4. **Legacy named-grid mode** — else if `route.openingKey`:
   `params.set("opening", route.openingKey)` and append each `route.path` as
   `path=`.

Result: old grid callers (`{playerColor, openingKey, path}`) produce
byte-identical output to today; new tree callers (`{playerColor, moves}`) get a
clean move line; legacy deep-link callers (`{playerColor, opening: fen}`) get
`color&opening=<fen>` with no stray `path`.

### `parseOpeningsSearchParams(params): ParsedOpeningsRoute`

```ts
export type ParsedOpeningsRoute = {
  playerColor: OpeningPlayerColor;   // normalized: black preserved, everything else -> white
  moves: string[];                   // params.getAll("move")
  opening: string | null;            // params.get("opening") (legacy entry)
};
```

- Color normalization mirrors the existing page rule:
  `rawColor === "black" ? "black" : "white"` (missing/garbage → white).
- `moves` from `getAll("move")` in URL order (preserves repeated params).
- `opening` is the legacy FEN entry, meaningful only when `moves` is empty (the
  consuming page decides; parse just surfaces it).
- Intentionally does NOT surface legacy `path` (the tree contract drops it; the
  old grid page keeps its own inline parse until g-tree-page-state).

### `buildCanonicalReplacement(currentParams, playerColor, canonicalLine): URLSearchParams | null`

Pure helper for the "frontend replaces URLs when the API returns canonical_line"
behavior, mirroring the old page's `canonicalRoute.toString() !== requestedRouteString`
+ `setSearchParams(..., {replace:true})` pattern:

```ts
const canonical = buildOpeningsSearchParams({ playerColor, moves: canonicalLine });
return canonical.toString() === currentParams.toString() ? null : canonical;
```

- Returns `null` when the URL is already canonical (page skips the redundant
  history write).
- Comparing full canonical string vs current string means it also: rewrites a
  legacy `opening=<fen>` link to the resolved `move=` line, strips any stale
  `opening`/`path`/extra `move` params, and normalizes a bad `color`
  (because `playerColor` is already normalized by `parseOpeningsSearchParams`).
- Root line (`canonicalLine === []`) with a bare `color` URL → equal → `null`.

title: Add openings tree API and canonical line resolver
description: Add GET /api/openings/tree for the production horizontal move graph. The endpoint returns hydrated columns for color plus repeated move parameters, validates and truncates stale lines to canonical_line, and serves structural book plus phase-valid observed edges with position metrics and eval data.
design:
# Plan: `g-tree-api` — Openings tree API + canonical line resolver

## Context

Epic `g-d5cu` replaces the `/openings` card-grid with a chesstree.net-style
horizontal move graph. The two scoring dependencies are done:

- `g-tree-score-model` — persisted direct position-score read model
  (`opening_position_scores`, keyed `(batch_id, normalized_fen)`), built in the
  same batch pass as named-root scores via `compute_all_scores(...)`.
- `g-tree-eval-cache` — `app/tree_eval.py` batched eval lookup (exact full-FEN
  wins, indexed normalized fallback), white-relative `MoveEval`.

This bead (backend-only, label `backend`) adds the **read endpoint** that hydrates
one column per selected position along a move line, so a deep link / refresh
renders in a single request. It does **not** touch the frontend (that is
`g-tree-page-state`, `g-tree-node-cards`, `g-tree-layout`) and does **not** build
the route helper (`g-route-tree-url`, which it blocks). `/api/openings/children`
stays during migration.

The endpoint must do **zero per-request scoring**: structural shape comes from the
graph + evidence overlay, metrics from the persisted batch, evals from the cache.

## Endpoint

```
GET /api/openings/tree?player_color=white&move=e2e4&move=c7c5
GET /api/openings/tree?player_color=black&opening=<normalized fen>   # legacy
```

In `backend/app/api/openings.py` (new route on the existing `router`):

```python
@router.get("/tree", response_model=TreeResponse)
def get_opening_tree(
    player_color: Literal["white", "black"] = Query(...),
    move: list[str] = Query([]),            # repeated UCI line (FastAPI repeated param)
    opening: str | None = Query(None),      # legacy normalized-FEN entry
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    user: TokenPayload = Depends(get_current_user),
) -> TreeResponse: ...
```

`Literal[...]` gives automatic 422 for a bad color (matches `/children` at
`openings.py:662`). Repeated `move` uses `move: list[str] = Query([])` exactly like
`path: list[str] = Query([])` at `openings.py:664`.

### Error conventions (decided)
- Malformed UCI in `move` (fails `chess.Move.from_uci`) → **422** (client error;
  do NOT silently truncate a malformed token).
- Well-formed UCI that is not a structural child / past the phase boundary →
  **truncate** to canonical prefix (canonical-URL behavior, like `/children`
  canonicalizes its route). This is the source of `canonical_line`.
- `opening` that fails `normalize_fen` (`chess.Board(...)` raises) → **422**
  (guard the `ValueError`, never let it 500).
- `opening` that parses but is not in the graph / unreachable → resolve to the
  empty line (root), consistent with "legacy/optional." No 404.

## Algorithm

All work uses one `chess.Board` replay (full 6-field FENs for eval keys) plus
normalized 4-field FENs (`app/fen.py::normalize_fen`) for graph/score identity.

### 1. Two child sets (mirror the scorer, then add the boundary ply)
Per parent normalized FEN P (all FENs normalized; book children from
`graph.get_node(P).children`, a `dict[uci -> child_fen]`, `opening_graph.py:236`;
observed from `overlay.edges[(P,·)].uci`):

- **`_structural_children(P)`** = observed children (**always** — phase-authoritative,
  never middlegame-filtered, SPEC.md:2307) ∪ book children whose **child is not
  middlegame**. This mirrors the scorer's `_structural_children`/`_reference_children`
  exactly (`opening_rootcalc.py:292,304`) and is the **navigable/expandable** set. Add
  a parity test against the scorer (finding #2).
- **`_column_children(P)`** = `_structural_children(P)` plus, **only when P is not
  middlegame**, P's middlegame book children (the displayed-but-terminal, **non-navigable**
  boundary). A non-middlegame parent thus shows observed ∪ all book children; a middlegame
  parent — reachable only via an observed continuation — shows exactly its navigable set,
  adding no display-only boundary. This keeps `_column_children ⊇ _structural_children`
  (every navigable move is displayed) with **parity to the scorer's navigable domain**
  (`opening_rootcalc.py:292`). Two graph facts to respect, not assume away: a book edge
  into a middlegame position is **display-only / non-navigable unless also observed** (the
  first middlegame book child is the non-navigable boundary — 605 middlegame graph nodes
  carry book children, so gate on the parent's phase, don't assume the book stops); but per scorer parity a middlegame parent's
  navigable set may still include a **non-middlegame** book child that dipped back below the
  boundary (**67 such non-monotonic parents exist**), and those stay navigable and scored.
  Merge by UCI; `in_book` iff a book edge.

`is_leaf(X)` = checkmate(X) or stalemate(X) or `_column_children(X)` empty (no reveal
column). The two sets have **distinct jobs**: `_structural_children(parent)` gates
whether a move is **navigable** (may enter `canonical_line`); `is_leaf` (via
`_column_children`) decides whether selecting a navigable position **reveals a column**.
Each node carries `is_navigable = uci ∈ _structural_children(parent)`. A node is terminal
(its `terminal_reason` is set) when it cannot reveal a deeper column: mate/stale, OR not
navigable (a display-only middlegame book boundary), OR a navigable dead-end
(`_column_children(child)` empty). So an observed continuation past a board-local
middlegame parent is both shown and navigable, never truncated (finding #2); a
pre-boundary node whose only children are display-only boundary moves is still navigable
and reveals a final column (not terminal); and a book edge into a middlegame position is
display-only / non-navigable unless also observed, though a middlegame position reached
via observed play still exposes the scorer's navigable set (including the 67 non-monotonic
parents).

**Resolve `canonical_line` from `move` params:** seed `visited = {normalize(start)}`,
board at start. For each token, in order:
- `chess.Move.from_uci(token)` → 422 on parse failure.
- Truncate if the parent `is_leaf`; if `token` ∉ `_structural_children(parent)` (the
  navigable set — a boundary/terminal book move is not selectable); if `move ∉
  board.legal_moves` (legality guard **before** `push`, so a corrupt/synthetic overlay
  edge that passed the structural check can't corrupt replay; finding #4); if the child
  norm FEN ∈ `visited` (cycle); or if ply ≥ 80.
- Else `board.push(move)`, add child norm to `visited`, append token to `canonical_line`.

**From `opening` (only when `move` is empty):** normalize (→ 422 on parse failure); if
it equals `graph.root_fen`, line `= []`. Else forward BFS in `OpeningGraph` from
`root_fen` with an explicit **visited normalized-FEN set** (finding #3 — bounds work and
gives stable first-arrival in cyclic/transposed regions), expanding `node.children` in
deterministic UCI tie-break order, depth-bounded to 80; first arrival at the target
gives the UCI path. **Re-validate that path through the same `move` validator** so
legacy and `move` entrypoints never diverge (Bug C). Out-of-graph / unreachable → `[]`.

**Else** (no `move`, no `opening`): line `= []`.

### 2. Replay + identify selected position
Replay `canonical_line` from `chess.Board()` keeping `pos_full[0..k]` and
`pos_norm[0..k]` (k = len(line)), reusing the same legality guard before each `push`.
Selected position = `pos[k]`. Compute `selected_is_terminal = is_leaf(pos[k])` and
`selected_terminal_reason` **directly from `pos[k]`** (checkmate → stalemate → if
`_column_children(pos[k])` empty: opening_boundary when middlegame else
no_children → null), independent of columns (Bug B — covers `k==0` legacy resolving
onto a terminal position).

### 3. Build columns
For `i` in `0..k`: emit a column for `pos[i]` **iff not `is_leaf(pos[i])`**, listing
`_column_children(pos[i])`. For `i < k`, `selected_uci = line[i]` (guaranteed present —
the validator only kept navigable moves); for `i == k`, `selected_uci = null` (the
reveal column). A leaf deepest position yields no column k — the frontend reads the
top-level `selected_*` fields instead of scanning.

Each column lists **one node per edge (by UCI)** — never dedup by `child_fen`; two
UCIs that transpose to the same normalized child are distinct legal moves and stay
distinct (verified `opening_graph.py:236`).

### 4. Hydrate each node
Build a `chess.Board(pos_full[i])` per column for SAN. For each column child
`(uci, child_norm, in_book)` in `_column_children(pos[i])`:
- `parse uci`; if the move is not in `board.legal_moves`, **skip with a guard** — the
  same legality guard used in replay (Gap H / finding #4 — observed UCIs derived from a
  transposed normalized parent could be illegal on this exact full position; never
  500). Book UCIs are always legal (produced by `board.push` at graph build,
  `opening_graph.py:227`).
- `san = board.san(move)`; `ply = i + 1`.
- `opening_name` / `eco` from `graph.get_node(child_norm)`; if name is null, inherit
  the deepest named ancestor seen along this line ("deepest opening name").
- `in_book`; `is_observed = edge exists`; `is_prepared = edge.live_attempts >= 2 or
  edge.live_passes >= 1` (edge-local form; the scoring `_subtree_has_ghost_target`
  arm is a scoring concern, not surfaced per node — documented divergence, Gap G).
- `user_choice_count = edge.live_attempts`, `encounter_count = edge.traversal_count`
  (0 for book-only edges).
- Direct metrics from `position_rows.get(child_norm)` (`CachedPositionScoreRow`):
  `opening_score, confidence, coverage, sample_size, game_count, last_practiced_at`.
  Absent ⇒ no-data (all null / 0). In-book + middlegame children are terminal
  boundary nodes that are **outside the scorer domain**, so their null metrics are
  structural-by-design, not "no evidence" (Bug A — document, do not "fix").
- `eval_cp` / `eval_mate` = **white-relative** `MoveEval` from
  `move_evals[(pos_full[i], uci)]` (acceptance returns white-relative; frontend
  converts via `eval_for_perspective`). Em-dash / null when absent.
- `is_navigable = uci ∈ _structural_children(parent)`; `is_selected` applies only to
  navigable nodes.
- `terminal_reason` (set on every non-expandable node): checkmate → stalemate → (not
  `is_navigable` ⇒ opening_boundary, a display-only middlegame book boundary) →
  (`is_navigable` and `_column_children(child)` empty ⇒ opening_boundary when
  `is_middlegame(child)` else no_children) → null. Precedence matters (Gap I):
  checkmate/stalemate is tested first via the board so a short mate is never mislabeled.
  A boundary book child (middlegame, book-only) is terminal, non-navigable, and outside
  the scorer domain (null metrics).
- `drill_opening_key = roots.get_root(child_norm)` → `opening_key` or null.
- `is_selected = (i < k and uci == line[i])`.

Memoize `is_middlegame_position` per request (Gap — it rebuilds a board + mixedness
each call, `game_phase.py:212`).

### 5. Sort each column's nodes
Parent side-to-move (from `pos[i]` FEN) decides the lens. Engine eval **never**
affects ordering.
- **User turn** (stm == player_color): `is_observed` desc, then `user_choice_count`
  desc, then opening-score asc (mastery; null last), then deterministic tie-break.
- **Opponent turn**: `encounter_count > 0` desc, then `encounter_count` desc, then
  opening-score asc (null last), then deterministic tie-break.
- Deterministic tie-break: destination square (file, rank), source square,
  promotion, then UCI/SAN — yields a total order (distinct UCIs never tie).

Observed edges come from `overlay_evidence(db, user_id, player_color, ...)`, which
filters by user **and color** (`opening_evidence.py:293`), so the column node set and
its metrics are color-specific (finding #1). Eval values are returned **white-relative**
(color-independent); only the frontend **display** perspective differs. The response is
still **not** cacheable across colors because the node set and metrics differ; only the
reference book skeleton is color-independent. The frontend caches by `(player_color,
canonical_line)` (epic); the backend holds no cross-color cache.

### 6. Batched lookups (per the epic "one overlay, one metric lookup per request")
- One `overlay_evidence(db, user.user_id, player_color, graph)` (then `db.rollback()`
  as `/score` does, `openings.py:565`).
- One position-row load via a **new** `opening_cache` helper that mirrors
  `load_cached_rows`' stale-while-revalidate trigger (Bug F — `lookup_position_scores`
  alone schedules nothing, so a cold user's tree would stay empty forever):

  ```python
  def load_tree_position_rows(db, user_id, player_color, fens):
      from app.opening_score_scheduler import refresh_now, request_recompute
      batch = get_latest_opening_score_batch(db, user_id, player_color)
      if batch is None:
          refresh_now(user_id, player_color)        # cold: compute once, sync (bounded)
      else:
          request_recompute(user_id, player_color)  # warm: background coalesced refresh
      return lookup_position_scores(db, user_id, player_color, fens)
  ```
  Recompute runs `compute_all_scores`, which populates `opening_position_scores`
  alongside `user_opening_scores` in the same batch (`opening_cache.py:201`).
- One `lookup_move_evals(db, [(pos_full[i], uci) for every node])`.
- One `lookup_root_eval(db, pos_full[0])` for the column-0 root eval.

Batch metadata: `batch.computed_at` (nullable), `model_version = SCORE_MODEL_VERSION`
(`opening_cache.py:62`).

## Response models (Pydantic, in `openings.py`)

```python
class TreeNode(BaseModel):
    parent_fen: str            # normalized
    child_fen: str             # normalized
    uci: str
    san: str
    ply: int
    opening_name: str | None
    eco: str | None
    in_book: bool
    is_navigable: bool         # uci in _structural_children(parent); gates clicks/drops
    is_observed: bool
    is_prepared: bool
    user_choice_count: int
    encounter_count: int
    opening_score: float | None
    confidence: float | None
    coverage: float | None
    sample_size: int | None
    game_count: int | None
    last_practiced_at: datetime | None
    eval_cp: int | None        # white-relative
    eval_mate: int | None      # white-relative
    terminal_reason: str | None
    drill_opening_key: str | None
    is_selected: bool

class TreeColumn(BaseModel):
    position_fen: str          # normalized
    ply: int
    selected_uci: str | None
    nodes: list[TreeNode]

class TreeResponse(BaseModel):
    player_color: str
    canonical_line: list[str]          # UCI
    selected_fen: str                  # normalized pos[k]
    selected_ply: int
    selected_is_terminal: bool
    selected_terminal_reason: str | None
    drill_opening_key: str | None      # roots.get_root(selected_fen)
    root_eval_cp: int | None           # column-0 start position best_eval (white-rel)
    root_eval_mate: int | None
    columns: list[TreeColumn]
    batch_computed_at: datetime | None
    model_version: str
```

## Files to modify

- `backend/app/api/openings.py` — new `/tree` route, response models, helper
  functions (`_structural_children`, canonical-line validator, legacy-`opening`
  BFS resolver, node/column builders, sort key). Reuse existing imports
  (`get_opening_graph`, `overlay_evidence`, `get_opening_roots`); add
  `tree_eval`, `lookup_position_scores`/new loader, `normalize_fen`,
  `is_middlegame_position`.
- `backend/app/opening_cache.py` — add `load_tree_position_rows(...)` (the
  stale-while-revalidate wrapper over `lookup_position_scores`).
- `backend/test_openings_api.py` (or new `backend/test_tree_api.py`) — tests.
- `SPEC.md` — document the `/api/openings/tree` shape, canonicalization contract,
  and terminal/sort/eval rules (near §13 Opening Weakness Tracking).

No model/migration changes — both dependencies already shipped their schema.

## Tests (cover every acceptance bullet)
- **Graph inclusion/exclusion**: columns contain book ∪ observed edges, not all
  legal moves; a legal-but-unknown move is absent.
- **Phase-boundary terminals**: a book child that is middlegame appears as a terminal
  `opening_boundary` node, is shown but not selectable, and has null metrics.
- **Observed past board-middlegame (finding #2)**: an observed continuation whose
  parent trips the board-local middlegame predicate is NOT truncated and stays
  navigable; parity test: API `_structural_children(P)` == scorer's for sampled P.
- **Boundary navigability (605/67-node cases)**: from a non-middlegame parent, a
  middlegame book child is `is_navigable=false`, terminal `opening_boundary`, null
  metrics, and a stale URL selecting it truncates back. From an observed-reached
  middlegame parent, the column equals the scorer's navigable set and adds no
  display-only boundary — including the 67 non-monotonic parents whose non-middlegame
  book child stays navigable and scored (parity test asserts this).
- **Replay legality guard (finding #4)**: a structurally-listed but board-illegal
  (synthetic/corrupt) observed edge truncates the line / is skipped, never 500s.
- **Color specificity (finding #1)**: switching `player_color` keeps the book skeleton
  and the white-relative eval values identical, while observed nodes, counts, metrics,
  and sort can differ.
- **Legacy BFS visited-set (finding #3)**: a transposed/cyclic target resolves to a
  stable shortest book path.
- **Observed off-book edges**: an off-book continuation from a session shows after
  one traversal with `is_observed`, counts, and (no-data) metrics.
- **Transpositions**: two UCIs to the same normalized child are distinct nodes;
  transposed positions share metrics (same normalized-FEN row).
- **Canonical URLs**: invalid/stale `move` truncates to `canonical_line`; cycle and
  80-ply truncation; legacy `opening=<fen>` resolves to a deterministic shortest
  book path and matches a re-validated `move` line.
- **Null evidence**: no-batch / no-evidence user gets the structural book tree with
  null metrics and still navigates; cold load triggers a compute.
- **Sorting**: user-turn vs opponent-turn relevance order with deterministic
  tie-break; engine eval does not reorder.
- **Eval integration**: exact full-FEN hit; normalized-transposition fallback;
  mate-over-cp; white-relative sign; root `best_eval`; cache miss → null.
- **Drill-root flags**: `drill_opening_key` set only on named-root positions, null
  elsewhere; top-level `drill_opening_key` for the selected FEN.
- **Errors**: malformed UCI → 422; bad `opening` FEN → 422; out-of-graph `opening`
  → empty line; bad color → 422.
- Avoid asserting cosmetic copy or pixel/connector geometry (backend has none).

title: Add tree eval cache lookup and normalized index
description: Add the analysis_cache support needed by opening tree nodes. This owns both the lookup helper and the persistence change for indexed normalized-FEN fallback, independent of the opening score read model.
design:
# g-tree-eval-cache — Tree eval cache lookup + normalized index

## Context

The horizontal opening tree (epic `g-d5cu`) shows an engine evaluation on every
move node. That eval must come from the existing global `analysis_cache` (populated
by opening-book precompute and analyzed player moves) — the tree must **not** launch
browser Stockfish searches when a column opens, and must not duplicate eval storage.

A displayed move node already has the cache key `(parent_fen, move_uci)`. But:

- The tree replays the selected UCI line from the initial board, producing a full
  **six-field** parent FEN. The cache `fen_before` may differ only in halfmove/
  fullmove clocks (transpositions), so an exact match can miss a perfectly good
  eval for the same position.
- `analysis_cache` is keyed/indexed only on full `fen_before`. A normalized-FEN
  fallback today would require a full table scan (15k+ rows), which is unacceptable
  per-request.

This bead owns **both** halves needed before `g-tree-api` can render evals:
1. **Persistence** — an indexed normalized-parent-FEN so fallback is O(index), not a scan.
2. **Lookup helper** — exact-FEN-wins with deterministic normalized fallback, returning
   white-relative cp/mate for the API/frontend to render from the selected perspective.

Scope is backend-only and independent of the opening score read model (`g-tree-score-model`,
already done). It does not build the tree API itself (`g-tree-api`, which this blocks).

## Decision (confirmed)

Storage = **column + index** on `analysis_cache` (not a side table): add
`normalized_fen_before` + a `(normalized_fen_before, move_uci)` index, backfilled via
a Python data migration. Single-table queries, one place to populate (the shared writer).

## Existing code to reuse

- `app/fen.py::normalize_fen(fen)` — the canonical 4-field normalization (EP-aware, uses
  python-chess). Must be the SAME function on both write and lookup sides so stored values
  match query keys. Same function `opening_position_scores` keys on, so transpositions align.
- `app/analysis_cache_repo.py::write_analysis_cache_rows` — the ONE shared writer all
  producers (session upload, precompute, JeffML ingest) route through. Populate the new
  column here so every path stays consistent; no script changes needed.
- `app/models.py::AnalysisCache` (line 301) — model + `__table_args__` to extend.
- `backend/conftest.py::_create_test_schema` (analysis_cache DDL at line 189) — hand-written
  test schema must mirror the new column + index (per project memory: models + alembic + conftest).
- Migration pattern: `alembic/versions/20260604_02_*.py` (add column via `batch_alter_table`);
  current head is `20260615_01_create_opening_position_scores`.
- `app/opening_quality.py::_white_cp` — reference for white-relative cp/mate handling (cache
  values are stored white-relative).

## Implementation

### 1. Model — `app/models.py`
On `AnalysisCache`:
- Add `normalized_fen_before: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)` (nullable — legacy
  rows backfilled by migration; rows whose FEN fails to parse stay NULL).
- Add `Index("idx_analysis_cache_norm_move", "normalized_fen_before", "move_uci")` to
  `__table_args__` (composite, so fallback is `WHERE normalized_fen_before = ? AND move_uci = ?`).

### 2. Migration — new `alembic/versions/20260615_02_add_normalized_fen_before.py`
- `down_revision = "20260615_01"`.
- `upgrade()`: `batch_alter_table` add column `normalized_fen_before` (Text, nullable);
  create the composite index.
- **Backfill** (Python, since `normalize_fen` needs python-chess for EP canonicalization —
  cannot be done in pure SQL like the `active_color` migration): `conn = op.get_bind()`,
  iterate `SELECT id, fen_before FROM analysis_cache` in batches, compute
  `normalize_fen(fen_before)` (import `chess` and inline the normalization, OR import
  `from app.fen import normalize_fen` — app.fen has no import side effects), `UPDATE … SET
  normalized_fen_before = :n WHERE id = :id`. Wrap per-row in try/except → leave NULL +
  count failures (don't abort the whole migration on one bad FEN). ~15k rows, one-time.
- `downgrade()`: drop index, drop column.

### 3. Writer — `app/analysis_cache_repo.py`
- `normalized_fen_before` is **derived** from `fen_before` (part of the immutable key), not
  caller-supplied — keep it OUT of `_WRITABLE_FIELDS`.
- Add a small `_normalized(fen)` helper: `try: return normalize_fen(fen) except Exception: return None`.
- On INSERT only (key never changes on REPLACE/MERGE, so the stored value stays valid),
  **both** insert construction sites must set the derived column — otherwise rows written after
  the migration are unreachable by the normalized fallback (finding #1):
  - SQLite/shared path `_process_row` (Decision.INSERT branch): build the `cols` dict from
    `("fen_before", "move_uci", *_WRITABLE_FIELDS)`, then set
    `cols["normalized_fen_before"] = _normalized(data["fen_before"])` before `AnalysisCache(**cols)`.
  - PostgreSQL path `_process_pg_row` `insert_cols`: set the same key on the dict before the
    `postgresql_insert(...).values(insert_cols)`.

### 4. Lookup helper — new `app/tree_eval.py`
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MoveEval:
    cp: int | None      # white-relative centipawns (None when mate)
    mate: int | None    # white-relative mate distance (None when cp)
```
Source ranking for deterministic fallback: `precomputed=0, game=1, other=2`.

- **`lookup_move_evals(session, requests: Iterable[tuple[str, str]]) -> dict[tuple[str,str], MoveEval | None]`**
  Batched, ≤2 queries total regardless of node count (API requirement: never scan, never
  query per child). Both queries use **composite tuple predicates** so the second key is fully
  used and unrelated moves aren't fetched (finding #2 — `sqlalchemy.tuple_`):
  1. `WHERE tuple_(fen_before, move_uci) IN (requests)` (the unique key). For each request, if
     its exact row has a **usable** played eval (`played_eval_mate` or `played_eval` not null) →
     resolve it. *Exact full-FEN match wins.*
  2. For still-unresolved requests, compute `normalize_fen(full_fen)` per request and query
     `WHERE tuple_(normalized_fen_before, move_uci) IN (distinct (norm, uci) pairs)` (uses the
     composite `idx_analysis_cache_norm_move`). Group candidates by `(normalized_fen_before,
     move_uci)`, keep only rows with a usable played eval, and pick one deterministically by
     **(has_mate, source_rank, id)** — prefer mate data, then precomputed > game > other, then
     stable lowest id.
  3. Each resolved row → `MoveEval`: `played_eval_mate` present → `MoveEval(None, mate)`,
     else `MoveEval(cp, None)` (mate-over-cp). Unresolved → `None`.
  (An exact row that exists but has no usable eval still falls through to normalized fallback —
  this maximizes coverage and matches "null only when the cache has no usable eval".)

- **`lookup_root_eval(session, starting_fen) -> MoveEval | None`**
  For column-0 root, return the position's `best_eval` — the eval under the engine's best move,
  which is a **property of the position**, not of any one row's played move. Requiring
  `move_uci == best_move_uci` would miss valid root evals on game-upload/precompute rows where
  the played move isn't the best move (finding #3, e.g. `api/session.py` and
  `scripts/precompute_openings.py` store `best_eval` on ordinary played-move rows). So: take
  **any** row at the starting FEN with a usable `best_eval`/`best_eval_mate`; rank deterministically
  by **(has_best_mate, is_complete_best_move_row, source_rank, id)** — the complete best-move row
  is *preferred* but not *required*. Exact `fen_before == starting_fen` first, then normalized
  fallback. Return `best_eval_mate` else `best_eval`, else `None`.

- **`eval_for_perspective(ev: MoveEval | None, player_color: str) -> MoveEval | None`**
  Pure helper. White → unchanged; black → negate cp and mate sign (None stays None, cp 0 stays 0).
  Helper returns white-relative; this util lets the API (g-tree-api) or frontend convert. Kept
  here so backend tests cover cp + mate perspective conversion per acceptance.

### 5. Test schema — `backend/conftest.py`
In `_create_test_schema`, add `normalized_fen_before TEXT` to the `analysis_cache` CREATE TABLE
and a matching `CREATE INDEX idx_analysis_cache_norm_move ON analysis_cache(normalized_fen_before, move_uci)`.

### 6. SPEC.md — section 5.6 `analysis_cache`
- **Resync the entire CREATE TABLE block** to match the current model, not just the new column
  (finding #4): the documented block is already stale — missing `played_eval_mate`,
  `best_eval_mate`, `best_line_uci`, `eval_file_id`, `eval_file_small_id`,
  `analyzer_protocol_version`, `profile_manifest_digest`. Add those plus `normalized_fen_before`
  and the `idx_analysis_cache_norm_move` index so §5.6 is accurate.
- Add a "Tree eval lookup contract" subsection: exact full-FEN+UCI wins; indexed normalized-FEN
  transposition fallback; deterministic selection (mate data → precomputed → game → other → id);
  starting-root uses any position `best_eval` (complete best-move row preferred, not required);
  values stored & returned white-relative, converted per-perspective by `eval_for_perspective`;
  null/em-dash only on no usable eval; no per-column browser engine analysis.

## Tests — new `backend/test_tree_eval.py`

Write rows via `write_analysis_cache_rows` (exercises the new column population) plus direct
inserts for fallback-only fixtures. Cover:
- Exact full-FEN+UCI hit returns `played_eval` (cp).
- Exact hit with `played_eval_mate` returns mate (mate-over-cp preference).
- Normalized fallback when no exact row (transposition differing only in clocks).
- Mate-data preference among multiple normalized candidates.
- Source ordering: `precomputed` chosen over `game` over other, same normalized key.
- Stable id tie-break when source + mate equal.
- Starting-root `best_eval` from an ordinary played-move row whose `move_uci != best_move_uci`
  (proves the relaxation, finding #3); complete best-move row preferred when both exist; root mate variant.
- Cache miss → `None`; exact row lacking usable eval falls back to normalized.
- Normalized fallback does not return a different move's eval at the same position (proves the
  composite `(normalized_fen_before, move_uci)` predicate, finding #2).
- Batch `lookup_move_evals` resolves a mix of exact + fallback + miss in ≤2 queries.
- `eval_for_perspective`: white unchanged; black negates cp and mate (None/0 edge cases).

Plus a writer test asserting `write_analysis_cache_rows` populates `normalized_fen_before`
(and that a clock-only-different `fen_before` yields the same normalized value).

## Verification

```bash
cd backend
# migration applies + reverts cleanly
alembic upgrade head && alembic downgrade -1 && alembic upgrade head
# focused suites (rerun named files in isolation if pre-push flakes — project memory)
pytest test_tree_eval.py test_analysis_cache_repo.py -q
```
Manual sanity: insert two cache rows for the same position differing only by move clocks,
confirm `lookup_move_evals` returns the eval via normalized fallback for the clock variant.

## Out of scope
The tree API endpoint and column hydration (`g-tree-api`), frontend rendering, copying evals
into the opening position-score table, and any browser-side engine analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Migration and model updates are included; existing rows are backfilled or queryable through an indexed side table; lookup helper covers exact full-FEN hits, normalized fallback, mate-over-cp preference, source ordering, stable tie-breaking, starting-root best_eval, and cache misses; backend tests cover cp and mate perspective conversion; SPEC.md documents the analysis_cache lookup contract.
close_reason: Implemented normalized_fen_before column+index, backfill migration, tree_eval lookup helpers, tests, and SPEC docs. Verified via pytest (160 passed) and isolated migration up/down.

Example: one Polish Opening game produced sample_size=9 (9 post-root white plies), shown as '9 Games'. Fix: relabel to 'Moves' and rename formatGames->formatCount to remove the misnomer at its source.
design:

title: Run v2 opening-score calibration on production data; confirm or re-center thresholds
description:
Follow-up to g-score-v2-rollout (closed). The calibration tooling shipped, but the threshold/tau decision was RETAINED as data-gated: no local dataset has any quality observations, so the v2 score distribution could not be observed. Run the calibration against real (populated) data and either confirm the retained defaults or re-center.

## Steps
1. Read-only run against production (default = zero writes):
   cd backend && python -m scripts.calibrate_opening_scores_v2 --json > calib.json
2. Inspect: cohort.included_pairs (>0?), named_score_distribution (pooled + per_pair spread), source_mix, horizon, gates (scoring <5s/pair).
3. Optional latency bench on a throwaway DB copy:
   python -m scripts.calibrate_opening_scores_v2 --write-bench --allow-writes --database-url sqlite:///.tmp/opening_calibrate.db
4. Decide:
   - If distribution is well-spread across A-F: confirm retained thresholds (A>=85/B>=70/C>=55/D>=45; tones alert<45, watch<65) and tau_wc=0.20/tau_cp=100.0; record observed medians.
   - If skewed: re-center getPriorityLabel/getPriorityTone in src/openings/format.ts and ADD src/openings/format.test.ts (does not exist today) asserting new boundaries. Any tau change bumps QUALITY_VERSION + docs.
5. Fill exact observed medians + gate numbers into docs/openingscore_final.md 'Calibration Outcome (v2)'.

## Refs
- Script: backend/scripts/calibrate_opening_scores_v2.py ; doc: backend/scripts/CALIBRATE_OPENING_SCORES.md
- Decision rationale: docs/openingscore_final.md 'Calibration Outcome (v2)'
- Thresholds: src/openings/format.ts:36-74

notes:
FINAL: thresholds RETAINED (A>=85,B>=70,C>=55,D>=45,F<45; alert<45,watch<65). Write-bench run completed against ghostreplay_calibrate Postgres copy. Both gates now MEASURED + PASS: scoring median 3.4s/pair (max 3.6) < 5s; cache read 38.96ms over 216 rows < 50ms.

Distribution (n=278): pooled p50 33.3, p95 47.2, mean 32.1; per-user medians 30.8-33.3 (median-of-medians 32.4); synthetic-hero p50 33.9; 4 of 8 pairs included. Still low-skewed (~90% would grade F) BUT ~95% of samples are one user (user 14: 266/278), so re-centring not justified -> retained. Re-centring stays data-gated until distinct populated users exist.

Shipped: src/openings/format.test.ts (pins retained boundaries); docs/openingscore_final.md 'Calibration Outcome (v2)' updated with this run's medians + both gate results. No format.ts change; tau retained; no QUALITY_VERSION bump. All acceptance criteria met.

title: React layer migration onto DecisionOwner
description:
# g-h94q Sub-bead 3 — React layer migration onto DecisionOwner

Split from g-h94q. THIRD of three sub-beads. Wires the `DecisionOwner` (built in sub-bead 2) into the coordinator and React components, removes all decision state from React refs, collapses `AnalysisEffects.tsx`, and updates/deletes the affected component + hook tests. DEPENDS ON sub-bead 2.

This is the step that flips ownership: after this bead, `blunderContextMap`, `pendingSrsMap`, `blunderRecorded`, `frontier`, and `committedDecisionIndex` no longer live on React components.
design:
# g-2m0p — React layer migration onto DecisionOwner

## Context

`g-h94q` is splitting the regular-game recording/SRS decision pipeline off React
component refs onto a coordinator-lifetime `DecisionOwner` service. Sub-bead 2
(`g-4dqj`, **done**) built `DecisionOwner` standalone with 26 unit tests, but
wired it to **nothing** — and built it with UI `callbacks` passed in the
constructor (a test-isolation artifact, not the final design).

This sub-bead (`g-2m0p`) flips ownership. After it:
- `DecisionOwner` is created and owned by the singleton `gameAnalysisCoordinator`
  for the app/coordinator lifetime, fed outcomes/resets internally.
- The recording frontier, `contextMap`, `pendingSrsMap`, `blunderReserved`,
  `committedDecisionIndex` no longer live on any React ref.
- `AnalysisEffects.tsx` collapses (~430 → ~30 lines) to a single
  `registerUICallbacks` **lease** effect + the best-move bling subscription.
- **Durability split (the core invariant):** the durable path (SRS/blunder
  payload creation, outbox state, `drainOutbox`, HTTP retry timers) always runs;
  the transient UI path (`setResolvedReview`, move messages, alert flash/audio,
  `onSrsFail`) runs only while a UI lease is held. Outcomes processed while
  AnalysisEffects is unmounted still POST durably; their UI is suppressed.

## Decisions confirmed with user

1. **Lease-only, no constructor callbacks.** Remove `callbacks` from
   `DecisionOwnerDeps`; construct with durable deps only
   (`new DecisionOwner({ getGameState })`). Add a single active UI lease via
   `registerUICallbacks(callbacks): () => void`. This means `DecisionOwner.test.ts`
   is **in scope** (its `makeOwner` harness must switch to the lease).
2. **Retry test reframed.** Delete ChessGame.test.tsx's "does not retry
   recordBlunder on API failure" (it encodes the old React-ref contract). Retry
   classification already lives in `DecisionOwner.test.ts` (network `TypeError`,
   5xx, 429+Retry-After, non-retryable 4xx→terminal — all present). Optionally add
   a UI-level "duplicate outcome enqueues no second decision" test in ChessGame.

## Review findings folded in (2nd pass)

1. **Lifecycle timing gap** → new `DecisionOwner.cancelPendingSrsReviews(k?)` called
   *before* the awaited work in revert/new-game/new-drill (Phase A.8, Phase D).
2. **Stale test routing** → fakes own a real `DecisionOwner` and route outcomes via
   `handleOutcome`/`handleReset` directly (Phase G header).
3. **Getter naming** → single `coordinator.decisionOwner` getter; AnalysisEffects prop
   narrows to `{ decisionOwner }` (Phase B.2, Phase E).
4. **Durable-before-transient** → reorder `fillSrsSlotByRequestId` durable-first
   (Phase A.7).

---

## Phase A — `DecisionOwner.ts`: constructor → lease

File: `src/services/DecisionOwner.ts`

1. **Deps:** remove `callbacks` from `DecisionOwnerDeps` (keep `getGameState`).
   Keep the exported `DecisionOwnerCallbacks` interface (used by the lease + tests).
2. **State:** replace `private readonly cb` with
   `private uiLease: { leaseId: number; callbacks: DecisionOwnerCallbacks } | null = null`
   and `private uiLeaseSeq = 0`. Constructor stores only `getGameState`.
3. **Lease API:**
   ```ts
   registerUICallbacks(callbacks: DecisionOwnerCallbacks): () => void {
     const leaseId = ++this.uiLeaseSeq
     this.uiLease = { leaseId, callbacks }
     this.bumpUiEpoch()
     return () => {
       if (this.uiLease?.leaseId !== leaseId) return
       this.uiLease = null
       this.bumpUiEpoch()
     }
   }
   ```
4. **Epoch consolidation:** add `private bumpUiEpoch()` that does
   `this.uiEpoch += 1; this.alertEpoch += 1; this.alertBuffer = []; this.alertScheduledEpoch = null`.
   Call it from `registerUICallbacks` + its cleanup, and reuse it inside
   `fullReset`/`partialReset`/`dispose` (which currently inline `uiEpoch += 1` /
   alert resets). This makes a lease change between alert schedule and flush drop
   the flash/audio (unmount suppression), matching the existing reset guard.
5. **Guard every transient UI call** with the active lease. Sites (all currently
   `this.cb.X`): `migrateOnReschedule` setResolvedReview (~:442), `flushAlert`
   setBlunderAlert/setShowFlash/playBlunderAudio (~:560-572), `fillSrsSlotByRequestId`
   setResolvedReview + appendMoveMessage + onSrsFail + playBuzzer (~:610-649).
   Pattern: `const ui = this.uiLease?.callbacks; if (ui) ui.setBlunderAlert(...)`
   or `this.uiLease?.callbacks.appendMoveMessage(...)`. **Durable writes
   (`drainOutbox`/`sendEntry`/POST/retry timers) are already callback-free — do
   not touch them.** `flushAlert` keeps its `epochAtSchedule !== this.alertEpoch`
   guard AND additionally no-ops when no lease.
6. **`PendingSrsReview`** already lacks `analysisId` (controller mints it); keep
   as-is. No `analysisId` field needed on the owner's type.
7. **Durable-before-transient ordering (review finding 4).** In
   `fillSrsSlotByRequestId` (~:610) the current order is UI calls (setResolvedReview,
   appendMoveMessage, onSrsFail, playBuzzer) THEN payload build + `slot.status='pending'`
   + `drainOutbox()`. Reorder so the durable side (compute `passed`/`evalLossCp`,
   set `slot.payload`, `slot.status='pending'`, cancel analysis timer, `drainOutbox()`)
   runs FIRST, then fire the lease-guarded transient UI. A throwing React setState
   then cannot starve the durable POST. (`drainOutbox` is sync up to `sendEntry`'s
   fire-and-forget promise, so this is a safe reordering.)
8. **`cancelPendingSrsReviews(fromMoveIndex?)` (review finding 1).** Add a public
   method that cancels not-yet-resolved SRS reviews — delete `pendingSrsMap` entries
   and terminate outbox SRS slots in `awaiting_analysis`/`awaiting_retry`
   (`markTerminal`, reason `'pruned'`/`'session_reset'`), for `moveIndex >= k` (or
   ALL when `k` is undefined). **Durable resolved slots (`pending`/`in_flight`/
   `awaiting_http_retry`) are untouched.** Factor the shared SRS-prune body so
   `fullReset`/`partialReset` reuse it. This preserves the lifecycle's early-clear
   contract (below) without coupling to a full coordinator prune.

## Phase B — `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`: own + wire the DecisionOwner

File: `src/services/GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts`

1. Import `DecisionOwner` + `DecisionOwnerGameState`. Add private field
   `decisionOwner` constructed in the class field initializer / constructor:
   ```ts
   private readonly decisionOwner = new DecisionOwner({
     getGameState: (): DecisionOwnerGameState => {
       const s = useGameStore.getState()
       return {
         sessionId: s.sessionId, isGameActive: s.isGameActive,
         isPracticeContinuation: s.isPracticeContinuation,
         playerColor: s.playerColor, moveHistory: s.moveHistory,
       }
     },
   })
   ```
   Wire it to the coordinator's own fan-out (reuse existing listener machinery) in
   the constructor:
   ```ts
   this.addAnalysisOutcomeListener((o) => this.decisionOwner.handleOutcome(o))
   this.addAnalysisResetListener((info) => this.decisionOwner.handleReset(info))
   this.decisionOwner.seedGeneration(this.sessionGeneration)
   ```
   (A class without an explicit constructor today — add one, or initialize the
   subscriptions in a small private `initDecisionOwner()` called inline.)
2. **Expose it** via a single getter named **`decisionOwner`** (review finding 3):
   `get decisionOwner(): DecisionOwner { return this.#decisionOwner }` (back the
   field with a private `#decisionOwner`/`_decisionOwner` so the getter name is free).
   The controller and AnalysisEffects reach it through the coordinator they already
   hold. Do NOT add it to `AnalysisOutcomeSource`; instead AnalysisEffects narrows
   its prop to a small host type (Phase E).
3. **`destroy()`** → call `this.decisionOwner.dispose()`.
4. Ordering note: `emitReset()` already fires synchronously before pending state
   is cleared (startSession/clearSession/prune); `handleReset` sets the new
   generation. The listener is added once at construction, so the DecisionOwner
   sees every reset/outcome for the singleton's life. No AnalysisEffects
   subscription remains.

## Phase C — `useChessGameController.ts`: register on the owner

File: `src/hooks/useChessGameController.ts`

- Drop `pendingAnalysisContextRef` and `pendingSrsReviewRef` from options; add the
  coordinator (or a narrow `decisionOwner`) to options instead. `commitAppliedMove`
  replaces `pendingAnalysisContextRef.current.set(analysisId, ctx)` with
  `decisionOwner.registerBlunderContext(analysisId, ctx)`. `applyPlayerMove`
  replaces `pendingSrsReviewRef.current.set(...)` with
  `decisionOwner.registerSrsReview(committed.analysisId, { sessionId, blunderId,
  moveIndex, userMoveSan, srs, srsDecisionId })` (note: owner's `PendingSrsReview`
  has no `analysisId` field — pass the request id as the registration key arg, not
  inside the object).
- Keep the `setResolvedReview({...result:"pending"})` arm — that's UI state owned
  by ChessGame, set directly (still correct; lease will transition it later).
- Update the `useCallback` dep arrays accordingly.

## Phase D — `useChessGameLifecycle.ts`: drop the refs

File: `src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.ts`

- Remove `blunderRecordedRef`, `pendingAnalysisContextRef`, `pendingSrsReviewRef`
  from args. Delete `prunePendingSrsReviewsFromMoveIndex` /
  `prunePendingContextsFromMoveIndex` (DecisionOwner prunes via
  `coordinator.pruneFromMoveIndex` → `handleReset(partialReset)`).
- `rewindBoardLocally`: keep `coordinator.pruneFromMoveIndex(newHistory.length)`
  (this now drives the owner's partial reset); remove the two ref-prune calls.
- **Preserve the early-clear contract (review finding 1).** The current code clears
  pending SRS *before* awaited network work so an analysis resolving during that
  async window cannot POST a review the flow is cancelling
  (`executeRevert` :421 `prunePendingSrsReviewsFromMoveIndex(...)` before
  upload/endGame; `handleNewGame` :525 and `handleNewDrill` :654
  `pendingSrsReviewRef.current.clear()` before abandonDrill/endGame). This is a
  real contract (covered by `useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts:385` "prunes pending SRS
  reviews before rated revert network calls resolve"). Replace each early ref-clear
  with the new owner method **before the await**:
  - `executeRevert`: `coordinator.decisionOwner.cancelPendingSrsReviews(getRewindHistoryLength(snapshotMoveHistory))`
    (replaces line 421). Keep `setResolvedReview(null)`.
  - `handleNewGame` / `handleNewDrill` (the in-active-session pre-await branch):
    `coordinator.decisionOwner.cancelPendingSrsReviews()` (full). Keep
    `setResolvedReview(null)`.
- `handleNewGame` / `handleNewDrill` / `handleReset`: remove the *post-await*
  `pendingAnalysisContextRef.current.clear()`, `pendingSrsReviewRef.current.clear()`,
  `blunderRecordedRef.current = false`. The owner's `fullReset` (driven by
  `coordinator.startSession`/`clearSession` → `emitReset()`) already clears
  contextMap/pendingSrsMap/blunderReserved. **Verify ordering:** these handlers
  call `coordinator.startSession`/`clearSession` which emit the reset
  synchronously — confirm the owner reset lands before any subsequent move
  registration in the same handler (it does: startSession is called before the
  first opponent move is scheduled). Drop the now-unused dep-array entries.

## Phase E — `AnalysisEffects.tsx`: collapse to the lease

File: `src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.tsx` (~430 → ~30 lines)

- New props: `{ coordinator?, appendMoveMessage, setBlunderAlert, setShowFlash,
  setResolvedReview, onSrsFail }` (drop the three refs). The `coordinator` prop type
  narrows to a small host type `{ decisionOwner: DecisionOwner }` (NOT
  `AnalysisOutcomeSource`, which has no owner — review finding 3); defaults to the
  singleton `gameAnalysisCoordinator` (injectable for tests). AnalysisEffects no
  longer registers an outcome/reset listener — the coordinator-owned DecisionOwner
  is the permanent consumer.
- One effect: build the `DecisionOwnerCallbacks` object
  (`appendMoveMessage`, `setBlunderAlert: (a)=>setBlunderAlert(a)`, `setShowFlash`,
  `setResolvedReview`, `onSrsFail`, `playBuzzer`, `playBlunderAudio:
  playRandomBlunderAudio`) and `return coordinator.decisionOwner.registerUICallbacks(cb)`.
  Deps: the callback identities + coordinator.
- **`clearPendingResolvedReview`:** on mount (inside the same lease effect, before
  returning the cleanup), clear any stale `pending` overlay whose decision already
  resolved durably while unmounted:
  `setResolvedReview(prev => prev?.result === "pending" ? null : prev)`. This is
  the "add clearPendingResolvedReview" item — a one-liner so a remount never shows
  a frozen "pending" review.
- Keep the existing best-move bling effect (analysis-store subscription) verbatim.
- Remove all frontier/SRS/alert/processSrsReview/runRecordingDecision/advanceFrontier
  logic and the `recordBlunder`/`reviewSrsBlunder`/`shouldRecordBlunder` imports.

## Phase F — `ChessGame.tsx`: drop refs + prop drilling

File: `src/components/ChessGame.tsx`

- Delete `blunderRecordedRef` (:324), `pendingAnalysisContextRef` (:328),
  `pendingSrsReviewRef` (:335).
- Stop passing them to `useChessGameController` (:568-569), `useChessGameLifecycle`
  (:698-700), and `<AnalysisEffects>` (:1988-1990). Pass the `coordinator` (already
  in scope at :160) to controller/AnalysisEffects where needed.
- The unmount-flush effect (~:731-770) that "lets AnalysisEffects' recording effect
  mount and fire" needs review: recording is now coordinator-owned and runs
  regardless of mount, so that comment/wait may simplify — keep behavior, update the
  comment, don't change the durable flush calls.

## Phase G — Tests

> **Harness routing change (review finding 2).** Today AnalysisEffects registers the
> outcome listener (`AnalysisEffects.tsx:425`) and tests drive outcomes through the
> coordinator's captured listener (`ChessGame.test.tsx:82`). After lease-only,
> AnalysisEffects registers NO listener. Every fake coordinator must instead own a
> **real `DecisionOwner`**, expose it as `.decisionOwner`, and route outcome-driving
> helpers **directly into `decisionOwner.handleOutcome(...)` / `.handleReset(...)`**
> (and the controller's `registerBlunderContext`/`registerSrsReview` target that same
> owner; AnalysisEffects leases UI callbacks onto it). In `ChessGame.test.tsx`, the
> `gameAnalysisStore.subscribe` bridge (~:124) switches from `capturedOutcomeListener(...)`
> to `mockCoordinator.decisionOwner.handleOutcome(...)`.


- **`DecisionOwner.test.ts`** (in scope now): change `makeOwner` to
  `const owner = new DecisionOwner({ getGameState: () => gameState }); owner.registerUICallbacks(callbacks)`;
  return `{ owner, callbacks, gameState }`. All 26 existing assertions then pass
  unchanged. Add 2 lease tests: (a) with **no** lease, a resolved blunder still
  enqueues + POSTs `recordBlunder` (durable) but no `setBlunderAlert`/audio fires;
  (b) releasing the lease before a queued alert flush suppresses the flash/audio
  (epoch guard). Existing retry/idempotency/Retry-After tests already cover the
  outbox. Add (c) `cancelPendingSrsReviews(k?)`: an `awaiting_analysis` SRS slot at
  `moveIndex >= k` becomes `terminal_error` and a subsequent `resolved` posts no
  review, while an already-resolved (`pending`/`in_flight`) slot is untouched.
- **`AnalysisEffects.test.tsx`**: rewrite the harness — render with an injected
  coordinator exposing a real `DecisionOwner` (construct one, expose via
  `decisionOwner`), and drive outcomes through `coordinator.decisionOwner.handleOutcome(...)`
  / `.handleReset(...)` directly (per the routing rule above — the component no longer
  registers a listener). Keep the bling tests verbatim. SRS/alert/resolved-review tests become
  lease tests: the leased callbacks fire on resolved outcomes. The frontier/
  committed-boundary tests (P0 :304, F4 :361, M2 :688) **move to DecisionOwner.test.ts**
  semantics — delete them here (decision logic no longer lives in the component);
  the M2 rewrite (finalized/abandoned failure does NOT record, retried
  rescheduled→resolved DOES) already exists as DecisionOwner provisional-failure
  tests (`:177` block). Add a focused unmount-durability test: resolve a blunder
  with the component unmounted → `recordBlunder` still called, no alert.
- **`AnalysisEffects.analysisStability.test.tsx`**: **DELETE** (its outcome-stability
  matrix is owned by DecisionOwner.test.ts).
- **`useChessGameController.test.ts`**: inject a `DecisionOwner` (or spy with
  `registerBlunderContext`/`registerSrsReview`) via the coordinator. Replace the 5
  ref-map inspections (contexts length :158, pendingSrsReviewRef entries/size :187,
  :259, :301, :324) with spy assertions on `registerBlunderContext` /
  `registerSrsReview` (and "not called" for the no-session cases).
- **`useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts`**: remove the three refs from `setup`; give the
  mock coordinator a real `DecisionOwner` (or a spy exposing `cancelPendingSrsReviews`).
  Replace `pendingSrsReviewRef` size/keys assertions (:378, :458, :519, :940, :981,
  :1030) with assertions that `coordinator.decisionOwner.cancelPendingSrsReviews` was
  called with the right arg (`getRewindHistoryLength` for revert; no-arg for
  new-game/new-drill), seeding pending reviews via `registerSrsReview` instead of the
  ref. Keep `coordinator.pruneFromMoveIndex` assertion (:382) — still valid. The
  "prunes pending SRS before rated revert network calls resolve" test (:385) must
  assert the cancel happens BEFORE the awaited upload/endGame resolve.
- **`ChessGame.test.tsx`**: add the idempotency-key arg to the POST assertions —
  `recordBlunder` gets an 8th arg (`idempotency_key`, `expect.any(String)`) at
  :1831; `reviewSrsBlunder` gets a 6th arg at :2362/:2429/:2580. **Delete** "does
  not retry recordBlunder on API failure" (:2079); optionally replace with a
  duplicate-outcome→single-decision test. Model network failures as `TypeError`,
  not plain `Error`. The coordinator mock must expose a real/spy `decisionOwner`;
  prefer constructing a real `DecisionOwner` with an injected `getGameState` so the
  end-to-end recording/SRS paths exercise the real reducer (per bead: "real
  DecisionOwner, injected getGameState, 6th SRS arg, retry test").

## Verification

```bash
npx vitest run src/services/DecisionOwner.test.ts
npx vitest run src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.test.tsx
npx vitest run src/hooks/useChessGameController.test.ts
npx vitest run src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts
npx vitest run src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx
npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npm run build
```
Project memory: the full vitest suite is flaky under parallel load in the
pre-push hook — rerun named files in isolation before trusting any failure.

Acceptance (inherited): recording/SRS survive AnalysisEffects unmount; the five
decision fields no longer live on React refs; AnalysisEffects ≈30 lines (lease +
bling); tsc + lint + build green.

## Execution notes (post-approval)

This plan is already persisted to the `g-2m0p` design field. Implement Phases A→G
in order; commit only after user review (per project rule), directly to `master`.

Recording and SRS decisions survive AnalysisEffects unmount. 6. blunderContextMap, pendingSrsMap, blunderRecorded, frontier, committedDecisionIndex removed from React component refs and live on DecisionOwner. 7. AnalysisEffects reduced to ~30 lines (UI lease + bling sound). Component + hook tests updated; AnalysisEffects.test.tsx:688 rewritten to new retry-recording semantics; AnalysisEffects.analysisStability.test.tsx deleted; tsc + lint + build green.

title: Backend + API contract: idempotency keys for SRS/blunder POSTs
description:
# g-h94q Sub-bead 1 — Backend + API contract (idempotency keys)

Split from g-h94q (Durable decision-owner). This is the FIRST of three sub-beads and is independently shippable: all idempotency keys are nullable/optional, so the current frontend keeps working unchanged. Covers Phase 0 (backend) + Phase 2 (api.ts) + Phase 2b (blunder.ts util).

## Scope
Backend idempotency for SRS + blunder POSTs, the Alembic migration, conftest DDL, the PG test fixtures + CI workflow, and the frontend API-contract plumbing (`api.ts`, `errorCodeOf`, `RecordBlunderRequest`, `evaluateBlunderCandidate`) that the DecisionOwner (sub-bead 2) will consume.
