title: game settings with sound volume/mute
description: Where should the setting live? Since there's already a gear icon next to the user's rating. We should move that to a more global position and add the sound controls there along with user rating setting.
design:
# g-t0n4 — Game settings panel with sound volume/mute ## Context The game has audio (move, capture, buzzer, "bling"/best-move, end-game win/lose clips, and blunder clips) but no way for the user to mute or adjust volume — every clip plays at full volume unconditionally. Separately, the only existing "settings" affordance is a small gear button buried *inside the rating line* of the game panel (`GameInfoPanel.tsx:297`), which only toggles rating-display type (Elo/Chess.com/Lichess). This task promotes that gear to a single **panel-level settings menu** in the game panel header and expands its popover to hold **sound controls (mute + volume slider)** alongside the existing rating-display setting. Outcome: one discoverable settings menu in the game view controlling both sound and rating display, persisted across sessions. Decisions confirmed with user: - Placement: **game panel header** (not the global AppNav). - Sound UI: **mute toggle + 0–100% volume slider**. ## Source-of-truth contract (resolves divergence risk) Three layers with explicit roles: 1. **In-memory snapshot in `soundSettings.ts`** — the *authoritative runtime value* used by audio playback. Never desyncs from playback even if storage throws. 2. **localStorage** — *persistence only*. Read once at module init to seed the snapshot; written on every change. A write/read failure degrades to defaults but never breaks playback or the UI. 3. **Zustand (`useGameStore`)** — *UI reactive mirror*. The popover reads/writes here. Every setter updates all three in order: snapshot → persist (best-effort) → store. `applyAudioSettings` reads **only the in-memory snapshot** (not localStorage per call), so storage failures can never make playback diverge from the UI. Keys: `ghostreplay_sound_muted` (`"true"`/`"false"`), `ghostreplay_sound_volume` (float string `"0".."1"`). ## Changes ### 1. New module: `src/utils/soundSettings.ts` - Module-level snapshot: `let muted: boolean`, `let volume: number`, seeded by `readSoundMuted()` / `readSoundVolume()` at import time. - `readSoundMuted()` / `readSoundVolume()` — wrap the entire `localStorage.getItem` access in **try/catch** (existence check is insufficient — it can throw). Parse with `Number()`, validate via `Number.isFinite`, **clamp volume to `[0,1]`**, default `false` / `1` on any failure or invalid value. - `writeSoundMuted(m)` / `writeSoundVolume(v)` — clamp/validate then `setItem` in **try/catch** (no-op on failure). - `getSoundMuted()` / `getSoundVolume()` — return the snapshot. - `setSoundMuted(m)` / `setSoundVolume(v)` — clamp/validate, update snapshot, then best-effort persist, and **return the canonical (clamped) value**. Invalid runtime input (`NaN`/non-finite) **retains the previous valid volume** and returns it unchanged. The store setters store this exact return value (see §3) so store and snapshot can never hold different numbers. - `applyAudioSettings(audio)` — wrapped in **try/catch internally** so it can never throw into a caller; sets `audio.muted = getSoundMuted()` and `audio.volume = getSoundVolume()`. This is what protects `buzzerSound.ts` / `blingSound.ts`, whose `.play().catch()` does not guard synchronous pre-play failures. ### 2. Apply settings in **all five** audio paths Call `applyAudioSettings(audio)` immediately before each `audio.play()`: - `src/utils/moveSound.ts` (`playMoveSound`) - `src/utils/buzzerSound.ts` (`playBuzzer`) - `src/utils/blingSound.ts` (`playBling`) - `src/components/chess-game/endGameAudio.ts` (`playEndGameAudio`) - `src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.tsx` — `playRandomBlunderAudio` (`AnalysisEffects.tsx:51`) creates `new Audio(clip)` inline; add the call there too. ### 3. Reactive state in `src/stores/useGameStore.ts` Mirror the `ratingDisplayType` pattern: - State `soundMuted: boolean` (init `getSoundMuted()`), `soundVolume: number` (init `getSoundVolume()`). - Setters resolve the `SetStateAction` via the existing `resolve()` helper, pass the result to the `soundSettings` setter, and store **the value that setter returns** (the canonical/clamped one) — not the raw `resolve()` output — so store and snapshot stay byte-for-byte identical. ### 4. Promote the gear — `src/components/chess-game/ui/GameInfoPanel.tsx` - Remove the inline rating-gear button + inline SVG from inside `.chess-panel__player-rating` (~lines 297–326). - Add a **header row** as the first child of the root `.chess-panel` (`GameInfoPanel.tsx:263`): `
` containing **both** the status `

` (`.chess-status`) **and** the gear+popover (`.panel-settings`) — the status moves into this row rather than the gear getting its own standalone row. The badges (`game-status-badge`, `unrated-badge`, etc.) stay outside the header. The gear button reuses `SettingsGearIcon`. - State renamed `showRatingSettings` → `showSettings`. Popover (`role="dialog"`, `aria-label="Game settings"`) has two sections: - **Sound** (`panel-settings__section`): mute `` (labelled); volume ``. Slider value = `Math.round(soundVolume * 100)`; `onChange` sets `Number(e.target.value)/100`. Slider gets `disabled` + dimmed styling when muted. Include a visible numeric `%` readout, and `aria-label="Volume"` with `aria-valuetext` on the range. - **Rating display**: existing 3-radio group, unchanged, still driven by the `ratingDisplayType` / `onRatingDisplayTypeChange` props. - Sound state comes from `useGameStore` selectors directly (no new props through `ChessGame.tsx`). - **Keyboard / a11y**: gear button has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` + `aria-expanded` bound to `showSettings`; Escape closes and restores focus to the gear; outside-click closes (pointerdown listener on document while open); focus moves into the dialog on open. Follow the existing AppNav drawer focus/Escape handling as the reference pattern. ### 5. Styles — `src/App.css` Reuse the `.rating-settings-*` look but make the anchor panel-aware. The panel is a 240px-ish column ≥1100px and switches to wrapped rows at ≤1099px (`App.css:7464`); `position: relative` currently only exists on the mobile panel, so: - `.panel-header { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 24px; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; }` so status takes remaining width and the gear occupies a fixed 24px track on the right (status keeps existing `.chess-status`). - **Wrapped-row layout (≤1099px)**: `.chess-panel` becomes a wrapping flex row, so the header must claim its own full row — add `.panel-header { width: 100%; flex: 0 0 100%; }` within that breakpoint (or unconditionally — harmless in the grid/column layout). - **Mobile (≤767px game-page)**: `.chess-status` is already `display: none` and the panel arranges items via `order`. A full-width row showing only a gear wastes space, so the gear **joins the compact matchup row**: set `.game-page .panel-header { display: contents; }` so its children become direct flex items of `.chess-panel`; the hidden status drops out and `.game-page .panel-settings { order: 5; margin-left: auto; }` pins the gear to the end of the compact row. - `.panel-settings { position: relative; display: inline-flex; }` (anchor for the popover). - Gear button: keep the 24px `.rating-settings-button` sizing. - Popover: anchor with `right: 0; left: auto;` (not `left: 0`) so it never overflows the narrow column; `min-width: 12rem; max-width: min(16rem, calc(100vw - 2rem));` to fit both the 240px panel and mobile viewport; keep existing `z-index`, shadow, slide style. - `input[type=range]` full-width inside the section; `accent-color: var(--accent)`; dimmed (`opacity`) + `cursor: not-allowed` when disabled. Add a `.panel-settings__section` + section-heading rule. ## Verification ### Unit tests (mirror `moveSound.test.ts` AudioMock + `vi.stubGlobal`) - New `src/utils/soundSettings.test.ts`: - defaults when storage empty; **clamp** out-of-range volume; **`Number.isFinite`** rejection of `NaN`/garbage → default; round-trip write→read. - storage `getItem`/`setItem` that **throw** → no throw, falls back to defaults. - `applyAudioSettings` sets `muted`/`volume` from snapshot; with a throwing audio object it does not propagate. - setters update snapshot so a subsequent `applyAudioSettings` reflects the change. - `moveSound.test.ts` + new `buzzerSound.test.ts` / `blingSound.test.ts` + extend `endGameAudio.test.ts:41`: assert the AudioMock instance receives `muted`/`volume` before play. - **Blunder audio**: export `playRandomBlunderAudio` from `AnalysisEffects.tsx` and add a case to the existing `AnalysisEffects.test.tsx` (already mocks modules + drives the effect) that stubs `Audio` and asserts the constructed instance gets `muted`/`volume` applied before `play()`. Seed the snapshot by stubbing storage / calling the `soundSettings` setters in the test. - New `src/stores/useGameStore.test.ts`: `setSoundMuted`/`setSoundVolume` persist (spy `localStorage.setItem`), update state, store the **canonical clamped** value (out-of- range input → stored value clamped), and invalid input retains the previous volume. - Extend `GameInfoPanel.test.tsx`: open settings via gear; toggle mute calls `setSoundMuted` and disables slider; move slider converts %→0–1 via `setSoundVolume`; `aria-expanded` flips; Escape closes + returns focus; rating radios still switch. ### Build & gates - Targeted: `npx vitest run src/utils/soundSettings.test.ts src/utils/moveSound.test.ts src/utils/buzzerSound.test.ts src/utils/blingSound.test.ts src/components/chess-game/endGameAudio.test.ts src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.test.tsx src/stores/useGameStore.test.ts src/components/chess-game/ui/GameInfoPanel.test.tsx` (rerun named files in isolation if the full suite flakes — project memory). - `npm run lint` and `npm run build` (both must pass). - Manual (`npm run dev`, /play): open the header gear → toggle mute, drag volume → make moves/captures, trigger a buzzer (blunder) and a best move (bling), end a game; confirm audio honors settings. Reload → mute/volume + rating display persist. Confirm rating radios still switch the displayed rating. ### Docs - Update `SPEC.md` (frontend section, §2.1 Gameplay / §3.1 Frontend) to note the persisted game-settings (mute + volume, localStorage-backed, snapshot/store/storage layering) — a user-facing architecture change worth recording. ## Out of scope - Global AppNav settings entry (user chose the game panel header). - Per-clip / per-category volume; one global volume + mute only.
close_reason: Implemented game settings panel: sound mute/volume + rating display, persisted via soundSettings snapshot/store/localStorage layering. All gates pass.

title: add colors for accuracy and acpl
description: Add a color gradient representing bad to good going from red to black midpoint to green for ACPL and Accuracy in the history stats pane
design:
# Plan: Color gradient for Accuracy and ACPL (g-qcdf)

## Context
The history stats pane (`GameReviewStats`) shows **Avg CPL** and **Accuracy**
as plain numbers in `--text-primary`. The bead asks for a red→black→green
gradient so a glance conveys bad (red) / middling (black) / good (green).
ACPL is "lower is better"; Accuracy is "higher is better" — they map to the
gradient in opposite directions.

`GameReviewStats` is **shared by two routes** — `/history` (HistoryPage) and
`/game` (GameAnalysisPage) — so this affects both. (`/drill` /
DrillAnalysisPage uses a separate footer and does **not** render
`GameReviewStats`.) The pane background is **fixed white** (`#fff`,
`src/App.css:1589`), which constrains color choice for contrast.

Chosen ranges (chess-realistic):
- **Accuracy** (higher better): 60% → red, 80% → black, 100% → green
- **Avg CPL** (lower better): 100 → red, 50 → black, 0 → green

## Findings addressed
1. **Missing / in-progress ACPL must not read as green.** `computeSideStats`
   (`src/utils/gameStats.ts:44`) sets `avgCpl = 0` when there are no evaluated
   moves, which would render as "perfect" green. Worse, **during analysis** a
   single analyzed zero-loss move yields `count = 1` and a real green. Fix:
   skip ACPL coloring unless analysis is complete **and** the evaluated count
   is > 0 — reuse the processing flag already passed to the component
   (`accuracyPending`).
2. **Contrast.** Text sits on white at ~15px → WCAG AA needs **4.5:1**. The
   originally proposed `rgb(60,170,80)` green is only 2.98:1. Use darker
   anchors and verify every interpolated color clears 4.5:1.
3. **Tests assert concrete mappings**, not merely "a color exists" (which
   would miss a swapped ACPL/accuracy mapping). Endpoints: ACPL 100/50/0 →
   red/mid/green; accuracy 60/80/100 → red/mid/green.
4. **Tooltip test already passes.** `GameReviewStats.test.tsx` is green (6/6).
   Preserve the existing tooltip assertions; only add new color assertions
   below.

## Implementation

### 1. Track evaluated-move count — `src/utils/gameStats.ts`
- Extend `SideStats` (line 4) with `avgCplCount: number`.
- Initialize `avgCplCount: 0` in `makeSide` (line 17).
- Set `player.avgCplCount = playerDeltaCount` / `opponent.avgCplCount =
  opponentDeltaCount` alongside the existing `avgCpl` assignments (lines 44-45).
- `avgCpl` keeps its current `0`-when-empty value; the count is what gates
  coloring so we don't change the displayed number's behavior elsewhere
  (`useGameReviewStats.ts` consumers untouched).

### 2. Color helper — `src/utils/statColor.ts` (new file)
Pure function interpolating red → near-black → green, with `t` clamped to
`[0,1]` so out-of-range inputs saturate at an endpoint.

```ts
// WCAG-AA anchors on white (#fff): each clears 4.5:1 for ~15px text.
const RED   = [183, 28, 28];   // ~5.9:1
const MID   = [33, 33, 33];    // ~12.6:1 (the "black" midpoint)
const GREEN = [27, 122, 50];   // ~4.8:1 — darker than the rejected 60,170,80

function lerp(a: number[], b: number[], t: number): string  // returns rgb(...)
export function gradientColor(t: number): string  // clamps t; 0=red .5=mid 1=green
export function accuracyColor(pct: number): string { return gradientColor((pct - 60) / 40); }
export function acplColor(cpl: number): string     { return gradientColor((100 - cpl) / 100); }
```
The exact green/red RGB will be confirmed against 4.5:1 during verification;
the midpoint is dark gray (legible on white, not pure black).

### 3. Apply colors — `src/components/GameReviewStats.tsx`
- Import `accuracyColor`, `acplColor`.
- **Avg CPL row** (lines 93-94): for each side, color only when analysis is
  done and there is data:
  `style={ !accuracyPending && side.avgCplCount > 0 ? { color: acplColor(side.avgCpl) } : undefined }`.
  Processing or no evaluated moves → leave default color (no false green).
  (`accuracyPending` is the existing processing flag both pages already pass.)
- **Accuracy row** (lines 120-126): when `accuracy != null`, set
  `style={{ color: accuracyColor(accuracy) }}` on the `--you` value. Leave the
  "computing…" / "—" states uncolored.

Inline `style` overrides `color: var(--text-primary)` from
`.history-stats-pane__value` (App.css:1700) by specificity — no CSS change
needed. Classification value colors (blunder/mistake/inaccuracy) untouched.

### 4. Tests
- **New `src/utils/statColor.test.ts`**: assert `gradientColor` endpoints and
  clamping; assert `acplColor(100)` / `acplColor(50)` / `acplColor(0)` give
  red / mid / green and `accuracyColor(60)` / `(80)` / `(100)` give
  red / mid / green (check R>G for red end, G>R for green end, and the dark
  midpoint). Add a contrast sanity check that each anchor's luminance ratio vs
  white ≥ 4.5.
- **`src/utils/gameStats.test.ts`**: assert `avgCplCount` is 0 when no moves
  carry `eval_delta`, and equals the evaluated count otherwise.
- **`src/components/GameReviewStats.test.tsx`** (keep existing passing
  assertions, incl. the tooltip ones):
  - Assert the Avg CPL value carries a concrete `color` matching `acplColor`
    for a known input, and accuracy carries `accuracyColor`.
  - Assert Avg CPL has **no** inline color when `avgCplCount === 0`, and when
    `accuracyPending` is true (in-progress analysis).

## Verification
- `npm run test:run -- src/utils/statColor.test.ts src/utils/gameStats.test.ts src/components/GameReviewStats.test.tsx`
  (deterministic single run; rerun named files in isolation if the broader
  suite is flaky — see project memory).
- `npm run dev`, open /history (and spot-check /game), select an analyzed game:
  low CPL / high accuracy green, high CPL / low accuracy red, midpoint dark
  gray and legible on the white pane. Confirm a **still-processing** game shows
  no green Avg CPL (stays default until complete).

- `src/utils/statColor.test.ts` (new)

- `src/utils/gameStats.test.ts`

title: engine line UI
description:
Changes to engine lines in the analysis board:
1. Fix the 3rd engine line pv is slightly clipped on the right.
2. The buttons don't look like buttons so users don't know they can click there.
3. Consider adding mouse hover that shows the popup, should improve discoverability in desktop. Though dismiss might be tricky since the popup is interactive when you select the moves in the line. I think the best UX is hover auto-dismisses when the mouse moves outside the popup unless you click anywhere in the popup at which point it perists the same as the current click-to-open behavior where you have to click outside the popup to dismiss it. Should the keyboard handler for move navigation trigger when in hover mode or only when in persist mode?
4. The whole component needs a white background to match other elements on the page.
design:
# Plan: g-lkte — Engine line UI polish

## Context
The analysis board (`src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`) shows up to 3 Stockfish
engine lines as a compact row of buttons in the moves column; clicking one opens
a positioned popup with a mini-board and clickable PV. Four problems remain:

1. The 3rd line's PV text is clipped on the right edge.
2. The line entries don't read as clickable buttons (transparent, borderless).
3. There is no hover affordance, hurting desktop discoverability.
4. The engine area / popup don't sit on a solid card background, so they don't
   match the cream/white surfaces used elsewhere on the page.

The app uses a light cream theme via CSS variables in `src/index.css`
(`--card-bg` = `--bg-primary` = `#f5f0e8`, `--border-color`, `--text-primary`,
etc.). The engine CSS currently relies on dark hex fallbacks that never apply.

## Changes

### 1. Fix 3rd-line PV clipping — `src/App.css`
- `.analysis-board__engine-lines` (line ~1908) is a fixed-gap flex row inside the
  history moves column, which can be as narrow as **200px** (`min-width: 200px`,
  `src/App.css:1290`), not just 230px. Three fixed-width children
  (`engine-eval` 5ch + `engine-pv` 6ch + gaps + `|` separators) plus the new
  per-button borders/padding (~44px of chrome across 3 buttons) overflow and are
  clipped by the column's `overflow: hidden`.
- Fix (intrinsic content must be allowed to shrink — `space-between` alone is
  insufficient):
  - Each `.analysis-board__engine-line` button: `flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0;`.
  - `.analysis-board__engine-pv` span: `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;` with
    `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` (drop the fixed `width: 6ch`).
  - Keep `.analysis-board__engine-eval` intrinsic (it's short) but let the PV
    absorb shrink.
  - Trim row padding (currently `0.1rem 0.5rem 0.25rem`) as needed.
- **Acceptance (verify at BOTH 200px and 230px column widths):** all three
  button borders remain fully visible with no clipping at the container edge.
  PV SAN text MAY ellipsize at narrow widths — that is acceptable; only
  container-edge clipping of the buttons themselves is a failure.

### 2. Make lines look like buttons — `src/App.css`
- `.analysis-board__engine-line` (line ~1923): add a visible resting state —
  `border: 1px solid var(--border-color)`, `background: var(--card-bg)`,
  small `padding: 0.15rem 0.4rem`, keep `border-radius`. Strengthen
  `:hover` / `[aria-pressed="true"]` with a tinted background + border color
  bump so the active line is obvious.
- Remove or rework the `+ .analysis-board__engine-line::before { content: "|" }`
  separator (line ~1918) since discrete buttons no longer need a divider.
- Keep the `--placeholder` variant invisible (`opacity: 0`, no border).

### 3. Hover-to-open with persist-on-click — `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`
**State model (single source of truth to avoid inconsistent paired states):**
Replace the bare `selectedEngineLineIndex` with one combined state, e.g.
`enginePopup: { index: number; mode: "hover" | "persist" } | null`. Derive
`selectedEngineLineIndex`/`selectedEngineLine` from it. A single object prevents
the "index set but mode stale" race.

**Transition rules (must be explicit):**
- Hover a line: if `enginePopup` is `null` or already `hover`, open/replace as
  `{ index, mode: "hover" }`. If currently `persist`, **ignore** the hover —
  a persisted popup is not downgraded by hovering another line. It changes only
  via an explicit click on another line or an outside click.
- Click a line: set `{ index, mode: "persist" }` (works from null or hover).
- Click inside the popup (PV move buttons already have `onClick`, plus a popup
  `onClick`/`onPointerDown` handler): promote `hover` → `persist`.
- Mouse leaves a line button or the popup: start a grace timer (~80ms, stored in
  a ref) that closes **only if** the current mode is still `hover`. Persisted
  popups are never closed by leave.
- Mouse enters the popup or a line: clear any pending grace timer so crossing the
  button→popup gap doesn't flicker.
- Clear the timer ref on persist, on close, and on unmount (effect cleanup).
- Existing outside-`pointerdown` handler (effect ~784) keeps dismissing the
  persisted popup on click-outside — unchanged.
- Touch/click-only users unaffected: click opens directly in `persist`.

**Keyboard handling (BOTH gates required — finding #1):**
The capture-phase arrow handler at `AnalysisBoard.tsx:799-814` drives the popup
PV navigation whenever `selectedEngineLine` is truthy; in hover mode it would
still hijack arrows. Gate it on persisted mode too:
- Effect at ~799: change guard from `if (!selectedEngineLine) return;` to only
  attach the capture listener when `enginePopup?.mode === "persist"` (add to the
  dep array).
- `MoveList` prop at ~1454: `suppressKeyboardNavigation={enginePopup?.mode === "persist"}`.
Result: in `hover` mode arrow keys keep driving the main move list; only after a
click (persist) do arrows navigate the preview and get suppressed for the list.

### 4. Solid card background — `src/App.css` **and** `AnalysisBoard.tsx`
- The header and lines row are **siblings** inside `.analysis-board__moves-col`
  which has a `0.25rem` gap (`src/App.css:1840`, JSX `AnalysisBoard.tsx:1362`).
  Styling each individually leaves a visible seam. Instead **wrap the engine
  header + lines row in a new `.analysis-board__engine-panel` element** (JSX
  change) carrying one `background: var(--card-bg)`, `border`, and `border-radius`.
  This is why item 4 also touches `AnalysisBoard.tsx`, not CSS alone.
- `.analysis-board__engine-popup` (line ~1963): swap
  `background: var(--bg-secondary, #0f172a)` → `var(--card-bg)`, and confirm
  border/text use theme vars so it matches other cards. Keep the existing
  drop shadow (lighten if it looks heavy on the cream theme).
- Audit hardcoded dark hex fallbacks in the engine/popup rules
  (`#0f172a`, `#e2e8f0`, `#94a3b8`, `#64748b`) and ensure the CSS-var primary
  values resolve to the light theme; adjust any that look wrong.

## Files
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx` — combined `enginePopup` state, hover
  handlers + grace timer, gating BOTH the capture keydown effect (~799) and the
  `MoveList` prop (~1454) on persisted mode (item 3), and the engine-panel
  wrapper element (item 4).
- `src/App.css` — engine-line/popup styling, `.analysis-board__engine-panel`
  rules (items 1, 2, 4).
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx` — new behavioral tests (required).

## Verification
- `npm run dev` and open the History page → analysis board on a game with
  engine lines enabled.
- Confirm all 3 button borders stay fully visible with no container-edge
  clipping at narrow (200px) and wide (230px) column widths (resize window).
  PV text ellipsizing at narrow widths is acceptable.
- Confirm lines visibly look like buttons (border/background, clear hover +
  active states).
- Hover a line → popup appears; move mouse into popup → stays open and PV moves
  are clickable; move mouse fully away (without clicking) → popup auto-dismisses.
- While only hovering, arrow keys still navigate the main move list. After
  clicking inside the popup (persist), arrow keys drive the popup/are suppressed
  for the list, and click-outside dismisses it.
- Confirm engine block + popup sit on a cream/white card background matching
  surrounding panels.
- `npx vitest run src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx` — existing tests still
  pass (click persistence at :592, persisted keyboard nav at :755).

**Required new tests** (fake timers for the grace timeout):
- hover a line opens the popup; mouse-leave triggers delayed dismissal after the
  grace window.
- crossing the button→popup gap (leave button, enter popup before timer fires)
  keeps the popup open.
- clicking inside the popup promotes hover → persist (no longer auto-dismisses
  on leave).
- persisted popup ignores leave (stays open) and is dismissed only by
  outside-click; hovering a *different* line does not downgrade it.
- in hover mode, ArrowLeft/Right navigate the main move list (NOT the preview).
- in persist mode, ArrowLeft/Right navigate the preview PV.
close_reason: Engine line UI polish: fixed PV clipping, button styling, hover-to-open with persist-on-click, card background

title: Apply full-game evidence policy to drills
description:
The drill policy was amended on 2026-06-01 to treat continued drills as one full normal game and to allow pre-continue drill moves/uploads/analysis to feed regular evidence paths. Existing backend work from g-drill-contract intentionally filtered drill-prefix rows and unconverted drill rows out of opening evidence, blunder opportunity computation, analysis-cache side effects, automatic blunder capture, stats, achievements, and converted-game summaries. Update the implementation to match the amended policy while keeping uncontinued drills unrated and hidden from history/session-analysis lists.

## Goal

Reverse the old drill-prefix evidence exclusion. Continued drills should behave as one full normal game, and pre-continue drill uploads/analysis should use regular evidence side effects.

## Scope

- Keep RatingHistory blocked for uncontinued drills.
- Keep uncontinued drills hidden from history lists and session-analysis endpoints.
- Stop using `rated_start_ply` or `session_moves.segment` to exclude drill-prefix rows from converted-game history, analysis summaries, CPL, blunder counts, stats, achievements, comparable metrics, and PGN/export behavior.
- Stop suppressing pre-continue drill evidence solely because rows are drill segment or the session is an unconverted drill.
- Allow regular game logic to create blunders and SRS items during drill strictness failures and other pre-continue drill analysis/upload flows.

## Likely audit points

- `backend/app/api/session.py`: upsert session moves, analysis-cache writes, opening score refresh, blunder opportunity computation, session analysis response summaries.
- `backend/app/api/history.py`: converted drill summary aggregation should include full line.
- `backend/app/api/stats.py`: converted drill metrics, perfect streaks, achievements, and comparable counters should include full line where regular games would.
- `backend/app/opening_evidence.py` and `backend/app/opening_cache.py`: live/review evidence and refresh discovery should include drill upload evidence according to regular rules.
- `backend/app/api/blunder.py`: automatic blunder recording should not reject a session only because it is an unconverted drill.
- SRS/blunder-review paths used by drill strictness and target review flow.

## Compatibility

Leaving existing `segment` and `rated_start_ply` fields in place is acceptable. They may still be useful for reconstruction/debugging or legacy clients, but they must not drive exclusion of drill-prefix evidence or summaries under the amended product policy.

## Tests

Add focused backend tests that prove:

- Converted drill analysis and history summaries include pre-continue moves.
- Converted drill stats/comparable metrics include pre-continue moves.
- Pre-continue drill uploads trigger opening evidence and blunder opportunity behavior like normal uploads.
- Drill strictness failure can create normal blunder/SRS evidence.
- Uncontinued drills still create no RatingHistory and remain absent from history/session-analysis lists.

# Implementation Plan — Apply full-game evidence policy to drills

## Policy recap (amended 2026-06-01)
- A continued/converted drill (`drill_state = 'converted'`, the VISIBLE_DRILL_STATE) is ONE full normal game: every move counts, including pre-continue drill-prefix moves, AND its timeline anchors to the drill's actual `started_at` (DECISION 2026-05-31: not conversion time — see Timestamp semantics below).
- Pre-continue drill uploads/analyses feed the SAME regular evidence side effects as normal games (opening evidence, blunder opportunity, analysis-cache, auto-blunder, SRS, stats, achievements, ghost target-selection history).
- Uncontinued drills (`drill_state in active/root_reached/failed/abandoned`) MUST stay: unrated (no RatingHistory) and hidden from history lists and session-analysis endpoints.

## Core mechanism being reversed
`segment` (`normal`/`drill`) on `session_moves` plus `rated_start_ply` on `game_sessions` were the old exclusion levers. `normal_segment_filter()` (= `SessionMove.segment == 'normal'`) and the SQL guards `(gs.session_mode='normal' OR gs.drill_state='converted')` excluded drill-prefix rows and unconverted-drill sessions from evidence/summaries. Per amended policy these levers must NO LONGER drive exclusion. Keep the columns in place (compat/debug) but stop filtering on them.

Key distinction preserved: exclusion of uncontinued drills from *listing/visibility* (`visible_session_filter`, `is_visible_game_session`, RatingHistory gating) STAYS. Only *evidence/summary/aggregation/selection* exclusion is reversed.

## Timestamp semantics (RESOLVED — use started_at)
"One full normal game" applies to the timeline too. Converted drills must anchor recency, stats windows, durations, and SRS-opportunity ordering to `gs.started_at`, NOT `normal_started_at`/conversion time. Touch points:
- `session_contracts.py:48` `normal_play_started_at()` and the `normal_play_started_at_expr()` CASE just below — for converted drills return `started_at` (drop the `coalesce(normal_started_at, started_at)` special-case, or make both branches `started_at`). Audit every caller of these two helpers; some may legitimately still want conversion time (e.g. rating-eligibility windows) — call those out individually if found, otherwise switch to `started_at`.
- `opening_evidence.py:176` the `CASE WHEN gs.drill_state='converted' THEN COALESCE(normal_started_at, started_at) ELSE started_at` → collapse to `gs.started_at` for the `session_ts`.
- `stats.py:292` uses `normal_play_started_at_expr()` for the window cutoff — follows the helper change above.
- SRS opportunity timestamp source (see backend/scripts/recompute_srs_opportunities.py and the SRS write path) — ensure it derives from `started_at` for drills.

## Change set

### 1. backend/app/session_contracts.py
- Adjust `normal_play_started_at` + `normal_play_started_at_expr` per Timestamp semantics above.
- `normal_segment_filter()`: call sites removed below; keep helper or leave unused. `segment_for_move`/`resegment_session_moves` keep writing `segment` (debug/compat), no gating role.

### 2. backend/app/api/session.py
- L256 `_compute_blunder_opportunity_events`: drop `normal_segment_filter()` — full move set (incl. drill prefix) builds `session_hashes`.
- L427/434 upsert path: stop deriving `normal_moves` via `value["segment"] == NORMAL_MOVE_SEGMENT`; trigger `_compute_blunder_opportunity_events` for ALL uploaded moves. Keep writing `segment` on each row. Confirm analysis-cache writes + opening-score refresh here no longer skip drill-prefix rows.
- L542 `normal_summary_filter`: drop `normal_segment_filter()` so session-analysis summary aggregates the full line.
- `rated_start_ply` still returned in SessionAnalysisResponse — leave.

### 3. backend/app/api/history.py
- L73: drop `normal_segment_filter()` (converted-drill CPL/blunder counts span full line). Keep `visible_session_filter` for list membership.

### 4. backend/app/api/stats.py
- L235, L304, L377: drop `normal_segment_filter()` so metrics, perfect/streak counters, achievements, comparable counters include full line.
- L292 window cutoff: follows the `normal_play_started_at_expr` timestamp change (started_at).
- Keep `visible_session_filter` for which sessions are counted.

### 5. backend/app/api/game.py  (ADDED — reviewer High)
- L190 `_same_fen_recent_ghost_moves`: remove `sm.segment = 'normal'` so drill-prefix ghost_path moves are visible to target-selection history. Used at L392 `find_ghost_move` for `_repeat_penalties`. Keep `ORDER BY gs.started_at DESC` (consistent with started_at anchoring).
- Do NOT drop the session guard entirely: pre-root drill ROUTE moves are recorded as `decision_source='ghost_path'` with `target_blunder_id = null`, and including them would let opening-route steering pollute SRS target repeat selection. Correct target shape: include legacy normal ghost rows, and include drill ghost rows ONLY when `sm.target_blunder_id IS NOT NULL` — i.e. `(gs.session_mode = 'normal' OR sm.target_blunder_id IS NOT NULL)`. Keeps drill repeat-penalty contribution scoped to actual SRS-target replays, not route steering.

### 6. backend/app/opening_evidence.py
- Live evidence query (~L176-188): drop `sm.segment='normal'` and broaden `(gs.session_mode='normal' OR gs.drill_state='converted')` to include drill sessions generally (`gs.session_mode IN ('normal','drill')`, i.e. remove the drill exclusion). Collapse the `session_ts` CASE to `gs.started_at`.
- Review/left-join queries (~L290, L319): broaden the drill guard the SAME way BUT preserve `gs.id IS NULL OR ...` so manually-entered blunders (no session) are not dropped. Target shape: `(gs.id IS NULL OR gs.session_mode IN ('normal','drill'))`. Also drop any `sm.segment='normal'` there.

### 7. backend/app/opening_cache.py
- L197/L212 refresh-discovery guards `(gs.session_mode='normal' OR gs.drill_state='converted')`: broaden to include drill sessions so refresh picks up pre-continue evidence. Match the predicate form used in opening_evidence (preserve any `gs.id IS NULL` left-join semantics if present).

### 8. backend/app/api/blunder.py
- L344: remove the `400 "Automatic blunder recording is unavailable for unconverted drills"` rejection. Auto-blunder runs through regular logic for drill sessions, including strictness-failure flows.

### 9. SRS / blunder-review / strictness paths
- Trace drill strictness-failure flow (src DrillStopActions + backend drill endpoints) and target-review flow; confirm they now create normal blunder/SRS evidence and are not short-circuited by unconverted-drill guards. Ensure SRS opportunity timestamps derive from `started_at`.

## Guardrails that MUST remain
- RatingHistory still blocked for uncontinued drills (do not touch rating gating / models constraint).
- `visible_session_filter` / `is_visible_game_session` still hide uncontinued drills from history list + session-analysis endpoints.
- Do not drop `segment` / `rated_start_ply` columns.
- Left-join evidence/review queries keep `gs.id IS NULL` so manual blunders survive the broadening.

## Tests
New / asserted-broadened:
1. Converted drill: session-analysis + history summary include pre-continue moves (blunder/mistake/CPL reflect full line).
2. Converted drill: stats/comparable metrics + achievements include pre-continue moves; window/recency uses `started_at`. Time-order-valid assertion: a drill STARTED outside the window but CONVERTED inside it must NOT count (anchoring to started_at, not conversion time). (Conversion always happens after start, so the reverse case is impossible.)
3. Pre-continue (still-drill) upload: triggers opening evidence rows AND blunder-opportunity events like a normal upload (session.py + opening_cache discovery).
4. Drill strictness failure: records normal blunder + SRS item via regular logic (no 400); SRS opportunity timestamp from started_at.
5. Ghost/repeat target-selection (game.py): drill ghost_path moves with `target_blunder_id IS NOT NULL` contribute to `_repeat_penalties`; assert pre-root drill route moves (`target_blunder_id IS NULL`) do NOT, so route steering can't pollute SRS target repeat selection.
6. Uncontinued drill: creates NO RatingHistory and is absent from history list + session-analysis list endpoints.

Existing old-policy tests to revise (each either updated to new expectation or annotated with explicit rationale):
- `backend/test_opening_evidence.py:306` — old exclusion of drill-prefix/unconverted evidence; update to expect inclusion.
- `backend/test_srs_opportunity.py:232` — SRS timestamp/exclusion behavior; update for started_at + drill inclusion.
- `backend/test_stats_api.py:491` — stats window/segment exclusion; update for full-line + started_at windowing.
- Sweep for other tests asserting `segment='normal'` filtering or conversion-time windows.

## Sequencing
contracts/timestamp helpers → session.py upload+analysis → history.py → stats.py → game.py ghost selection → opening_evidence.py + opening_cache.py → blunder.py + SRS/strictness paths → test revisions + new tests. Run backend pytest (drill, opening_evidence, srs_opportunity, stats, game/ghost modules) after each layer.
acceptance_criteria: Converted drill history, analysis, stats, blunder counts, CPL, achievements, and comparable metrics include the full line; pre-continue drill uploads and analyses feed regular opening evidence, blunder opportunity, auto-blunder, SRS, analysis-cache, streak, and achievement paths; strictness failures can record blunder/SRS evidence through regular logic; uncontinued drills remain unrated and hidden from history/session-analysis lists.

design:
# g-osni — Instant "Again" + gear settings on drill end

## Context

When a drill ends, the user is offered a restart button that today calls
`handleNewDrillSticky`, which **opens the full drill setup overlay** (`DrillSetupPanel`)
and forces re-confirming settings. The bead wants a one-tap restart that immediately
launches a new drill with the **previous drill's exact settings**, plus a small **gear
button** next to it that still opens the setup popup for changing settings.

Two distinct UI surfaces show a drill restart button and BOTH must get the new behavior:
- `DrillStopActions` — shown for **off-route / accuracy** stops (`isStoppedDrill` &&
  `isGameActive` && `!gameResult`), render site `ChessGame.tsx:1713`.
- `PostGameBanner` — shown for **natural-end** drills (gameResult set, so DrillStopActions
  is suppressed). Has two restart buttons ("Another drill" branch ~`PostGameBanner.tsx:58`
  and "New Drill" branch ~`PostGameBanner.tsx:111`), render site `ChessGame.tsx:1692`.

Confirmed with user: when the previous drill used "random" color, Again **reuses the
resolved color**.

## Key design decisions (from review)

- **Restart source = live Zustand drill state, not localStorage.** The store holds the
  just-played drill's *exact* settings: `drillOpeningKey`, `playerColor` (resolved),
  `engineElo`, `drillStrictness`, `drillStrictnessCp` (exact cp from the API response).
  localStorage rounds strictness to 0/25/50 (`useChessGameLifecycle.ts:712`) and would
  restart a 20cp drill at 25cp — so do **not** use it as the restart source.
- **No guessing when `drillStrictnessCp` is null.** Exact replay is impossible without the
  exact cp. New drills always set it; null = legacy/incomplete state. If
  `drillOpeningKey == null` OR `drillStrictnessCp == null`, instant Again instead opens the
  settings overlay (no derived-cp fallback).
- **Fix localStorage persistence to store exact cp.** At `useChessGameLifecycle.ts:709-712`,
  persist `strictnessCp: response.strictness_cp ?? options.strictnessCp` instead of deriving
  0/25/50 from `options.strictness`. This makes the gear/overlay prefill exact too (the
  overlay prefill effect at `ChessGame.tsx:878` reads this prefs blob).
- **Settings/gear path must preserve end state.** The current `handleNewDrillSticky`
  **clears `gameResult` and hides `showPostGamePrompt`** (`ChessGame.tsx:1472/1497`), which
  destroys the post-game banner. Replace it with `handleAgainSettings` that opens the
  overlay **without clearing `gameResult`**, and make `handleCloseStartOverlay` **restore**
  the banner (`setShowPostGamePrompt(true)` when `gameResult != null`) so cancelling returns
  to the natural-end banner.
- **On failure, open the settings overlay via `handleAgainSettings`** (not the old sticky
  handler). `handleNewDrill` only clears `gameResult`/`showPostGamePrompt` *after* startDrill
  succeeds (`useChessGameLifecycle.ts:673/690` run post-success), so on failure the end
  state is intact and `handleAgainSettings` preserves it. `startError` is shown inside the
  overlay (`DrillSetupPanel.tsx:185`).
- **Disable all restart actions while starting.** Gate Again + gear on `isStartingGame`
  (local state in `ChessGame.tsx:152`, already threaded to the hook) to prevent duplicate
  startDrill requests.
- **Remove the dead `selectedOpening` param** from `handleNewDrill` rather than making it
  optional — it is unused in the body.

## Implementation

### 1. `handleNewDrill` signature cleanup (`useChessGameLifecycle.ts`)
- Remove `selectedOpening: OpeningRootItem;` from the options type (~618). It is unused.
- Update the only production caller `handleStartDrill` (`ChessGame.tsx:1444`) and the 3
  lifecycle tests (`useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts:1353/1408/1452`) to drop the field.

### 2a. Persistence fix (`useChessGameLifecycle.ts:709-712`)
Change the persisted `strictnessCp` to the exact value
(`response.strictness_cp ?? options.strictnessCp`) instead of deriving 0/25/50 from
`options.strictness`.

### 2b. Settings/gear handler (`ChessGame.tsx`)
Replace `handleNewDrillSticky` with `handleAgainSettings` that opens the overlay **without
destroying end state**:
- Do **not** call `setGameResult(null)`.
- **Prefill from the live store, not localStorage.** When a just-played drill exists
  (`s.drillOpeningKey != null`), seed the setup-panel state directly from Zustand:
  `setDrillStrictnessCp(s.drillStrictnessCp ?? <existing default>)`,
  `setEngineElo(s.engineElo)`, `setPlayerColorChoice(s.playerColor)`, and
  `pendingDrillSetupRef.current = { openingKey: s.drillOpeningKey, playerColor: s.playerColor }`.
  Store values are exact and always win. Fall back to the existing localStorage-prefill
  effects (`ChessGame.tsx:878`/`905`) **only when no drill state exists**
  (`s.drillOpeningKey == null`).
- `setShowPostGamePrompt(false)` (hide banner while modal open), `setIsDrillMode(true)`,
  `setShowStartOverlay(true)`.
- **Guard the localStorage prefill effect** (`ChessGame.tsx:878`): it currently runs on
  `showStartOverlay` becoming true and would clobber the store-seeded values. Add a
  `skipStickyPrefillRef` set in `handleAgainSettings` (when seeding from store) and have the
  effect early-return + reset the ref when set. Otherwise the localStorage path keeps its
  current behavior.
- Update `handleCloseStartOverlay` (`ChessGame.tsx:1423`) to restore the banner on cancel:
  `setShowStartOverlay(false); if (useGameStore.getState().gameResult) setShowPostGamePrompt(true);`.
  (Successful starts close the overlay via `handleNewDrill`, not this handler, so the banner
  won't wrongly reappear.)

### 2c. Instant-restart handler (`ChessGame.tsx`)
Add `handleAgainDrill` (useCallback):
1. Read `const s = useGameStore.getState()`.
2. If `!s.drillOpeningKey` OR `s.drillStrictness == null` OR `s.drillStrictnessCp == null` →
   `handleAgainSettings()` (open overlay) and return. **No derived-cp guess.**
3. Build params from the store: `openingKey: s.drillOpeningKey`,
   `playerColor: s.playerColor`, `engineElo: s.engineElo`,
   `strictness: s.drillStrictness`, `strictnessCp: s.drillStrictnessCp`.
4. `const result = await handleNewDrill({...})`.
5. On success: `drillFailedMoveIndexRef.current = null; setAnalyzeError(null);` and apply
   opponent move when it's not the player's turn (mirror `handleStartDrill` 1447–1456 using
   `result.fen` / `result.uciHistory`).
6. On failure (`!result`): `handleAgainSettings()` — end state is intact (handleNewDrill
   clears it only post-success), so the natural-end banner is preserved/restorable.
   Do **not** clear `gameResult` anywhere in this handler.

### 3. `DrillStopActions.tsx`
- Add props `onAnotherDrillSettings: () => void` and `disabled?: boolean`.
- Render a gear icon button (⚙, `aria-label="Change drill settings"`, `type="button"`)
  next to **Again** inside `.chess-post-game-actions`.
- Disable Again + gear when `isPreparing || disabled`.

### 4. `PostGameBanner.tsx`
- Add prop `onAnotherDrillSettings?: () => void` (and reuse existing disabled signal or add
  one if needed).
- In BOTH drill branches (~58 "Another drill", ~111 "New Drill"), render a gear button next
  to the restart button wired to `onAnotherDrillSettings`.

### 5. Wire render sites (`ChessGame.tsx`)
- `DrillStopActions` (~1714): `onAnotherDrill={handleAgainDrill}`,
  `onAnotherDrillSettings={handleAgainSettings}`, `disabled={isStartingGame}`.
- `PostGameBanner` (~1692): `onNewDrill={handleAgainDrill}`,
  `onAnotherDrillSettings={handleAgainSettings}` (thread `isStartingGame` for disabling).
- The non-drill "New Game" button keeps `onShowStartOverlay={handleShowStartOverlay}`.

### 6. Styling (`App.css`)
- Add a compact `.chess-button.icon` modifier (square, tighter padding) for the gear if the
  default text-button sizing looks off. Minimal; no icon dependency.

## Tests (required, not optional)

- `DrillStopActions.test.tsx`: gear renders + fires `onAnotherDrillSettings`; Again + gear
  disabled when `disabled`; update `baseProps`.
- `PostGameBanner.test.tsx`: gear renders in both drill branches + fires
  `onAnotherDrillSettings`.
- `ChessGame.test.tsx` integration (follow existing drill test patterns):
  1. Instant Again starts a drill via `startDrill`/`handleNewDrill` **without** opening the
     overlay.
  2. Exact `strictnessCp` and resolved `playerColor` from store are reused (e.g. 20cp stays
     20cp).
  3. Natural-end restart works from `PostGameBanner`.
  4. Opponent-first restart applies the opponent move.
  5. Missing/invalid store settings (`drillStrictnessCp == null`) → overlay fallback, no
     startDrill call.
  6. **Failed natural-end restart** → overlay opens AND `gameResult`/post-game banner is
     preserved; cancelling the overlay restores the natural-end banner.
  7. Duplicate-click prevention: actions disabled while `isStartingGame`.
  8. Gear opens overlay prefilled from the **store**, which wins over conflicting
     localStorage: seed `localStorage` with e.g. 25cp/different opening, set store drill
     state to 20cp/opening X, click gear → overlay shows 20cp/opening X (store values win,
     storage ignored).

## Verification

1. `npm run test -- DrillStopActions PostGameBanner ChessGame` and lifecycle tests.
2. Manual (/run): off-route fail → Again restarts instantly same settings, gear opens
   overlay; natural-end drill → same; previously-random drill reuses color; clear store /
   force a failed start to confirm overlay fallback.
3. Project rule: rerun any failed vitest file in isolation (pre-push hook is flaky).

## Notes
- Per memory: write this full plan to the bead `design` field before exiting plan mode; do
  not commit until the user has reviewed the changes.
notes: Reverted the planned localStorage persistence fix (step 2a). Storing the exact cp instead of tier-nominal (0/25/50) caused leniency drift: the overlay prefill effect restores the slider from localStorage on every open, so a drill nudged to the high end of a tier (e.g. 35cp 'Standard') would restart with a 35cp threshold instead of 25, letting borderline bad moves (delta ~30) no longer stop the drill. The Again/gear feature does not need this persistence change — restart reads the live store, and the gear prefill seeds from the store (guarded against localStorage). Added ChessGame test 'a drill restarted via Again still stops on a post-root bad move' to lock in that restarts preserve accuracy stops.
close_reason: Implemented instant Again + settings gear on drill end; reverted the exact-cp persistence step (caused leniency drift). Styled gear like rating-settings-button, tightly grouped with the restart button.

title: After drill end add analyse button instead of Continue as game
description:
Let's get rid of "Continue as normal game" because this distorts user elo rating since you can drill until you get a strong position and then play and easily win.

Post drill analysis is useful because many times it's not clear why the last played move was wrong and the alternate was better so the player might want to study the position in analyse mode.

Currently the analysis is tied to post-game session uploads.

Use a separate, transient drill-analysis surface. Do not expose unconverted drills through /api/session/:id/analysis, history, or normal game analysis.

Flow (see design field for the full implementation plan):

1. "Analyze" runs a targeted completion barrier while ChessGame + AnalysisEffects are still
   mounted: if the failed move's analysis is still pending (off-route case), await
   waitForAnalysis(failedMoveIndex) only; then snapshot moveHistory, player color, failed
   move index, and the current analysis map into a narrow client store (drillAnalysisStore).
   Plies whose analysis is still unresolved keep null fields.

2. Abandon + finalize the drill via a new lifecycle method (abandonStoppedDrill): unrated,
   hidden, isGameActive/drillState cleared. coordinator.clearSession() lets it idle-shut down.

3. Navigate to /drill-analysis, rendering the existing data-driven
   src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx (no GameReviewStats footer — accuracy isn't available
   for a transient snapshot).

4. Blunder/SRS side effects are flushed BEFORE navigation (barrier), not after — navigating
   unmounts AnalysisEffects, so its automatic blunder-recording React effect would otherwise
   be dropped. Normal evidence uploads are flushed via coordinator.flushPendingUploads().

5. Convert gameplay data to AnalysisBoard's display shapes (AnalysisMove[] + position_analysis)
   reusing the session-upload mapping logic in src/components/chess-game/domain/sessionUpload.ts.

6. Treat the review as ephemeral: refreshing the page expires it (store is not persisted).
   Persistence can be added later through a dedicated drill-analysis endpoint.

This preserves the existing visibility guard in backend/app/api/session.py:698, and the abandon
endpoint already accepts failed drills in backend/app/api/drills.py:371. No conversion, rating,
history entry, or game statistics are created.
design:
# Plan: Replace "Continue as normal game" with "Analyze" (transient drill analysis)

## Goal
Remove the rating-distorting "Continue as normal game" drill-end action. Replace with
"Analyze", opening an ephemeral, in-memory review of the just-played drill moves on a
dedicated /drill-analysis surface. No conversion, rating, history entry, or stats. Drill is
abandoned (unrated, hidden) per g-drill-policy.

## Key design decision (resolves review findings 1-3)
Snapshot/abandon happens while ChessGame + AnalysisEffects are still mounted, with a
**targeted** barrier — NOT a broad wait. By drill-end most analyses are resolved:
- Accuracy failure: continueAfterPlayerMove already `await coordinator.waitForAnalysis(
  result.moveIndex)` before failing (ChessGame.tsx:927) -> failed move resolved.
- Off-route failure: route check (checkDrillRoute, ~ChessGame.tsx:541) runs independently
  of engine analysis, so the failed move's analysis CAN still be pending.
- Earlier plies: can resolve out of order (cache hits), so an occasional earlier ply may be
  unresolved — acceptable, snapshot keeps null fields for those.

handleAnalyzeDrill (async), guarded by an in-flight ref (like isContinuingDrillRef):
  1. failedMoveIndex = drillFailInfo.moveIndex. If analysisStore analysisMap lacks it,
     `await coordinator.waitForAnalysis(failedMoveIndex)` (targeted; resolves immediately if
     already present). Do NOT broadly wait on all pending analyses.
     REJECTION: if waitForAnalysis rejects (session changed / worker error), do NOT abort the
     flow — continue with null analysis for that ply, surface a non-blocking error
     (setEngineMessage "Analysis unavailable; showing partial review."), and proceed. The
     whole handler runs in try/finally that ALWAYS clears the "Preparing analysis…" state
     (isPreparing ref + state), so the button never sticks.
  2. Off-route blunder recording is a React effect in AnalysisEffects
     (src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.tsx:85), so after the failed-move analysis
     resolves, await one commit tick (await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(r))) so
     that effect mounts/starts its fire-and-forget POST (survives later unmount). SRS store
     subscribers run synchronously on resolve, so no extra wait needed for them.
  3. await coordinator.flushPendingUploads() (normal evidence side effects; g-drill-policy:
     no drill-prefix demarcation).
  4. Snapshot from analysisStore.getState().analysisMap + store.moveHistory + playerColor +
     failedMoveIndex into drillAnalysisStore. Plies with still-unresolved analysis keep null
     fields (snapshot never blocks on them).
  5. Abandon + finalize via a NEW lifecycle method (see step 4 note): finishLocalGame is
     closure-private in useChessGameLifecycle (line 163) and not returned, so ChessGame cannot
     call it. Add `abandonStoppedDrill(): Promise<void>` to the hook's return that internally:
     abandonDrill(store.sessionId) -> if sessionId still current: setDrillState(contract.
     drill_state), setIsRated(false), finishLocalGame({type:"abandon"...}, {playEndGameAudio:
     false}). Mirrors the resign-path abandon block (useChessGameLifecycle.ts:789). ChessGame's
     handleAnalyzeDrill awaits this so isGameActive/drillState clear and /play shows no stale
     active drill (finding 3).
  6. coordinator.clearSession() so activeSessionId clears and idle-shutdown can fire
     (coordinator.ts:288/233). Safe: snapshot already copied; clearAll only wipes the live
     analysisStore, not drillAnalysisStore.
  7. navigate("/drill-analysis").
Show a brief "Preparing analysis…" disabled state only while step 1 actually awaits.

## Data shapes (resolves finding 4)
buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot(history, analysesByIndex, startingFen, playerColor, failedMoveIndex):
- moves: AnalysisMove[] — RETAIN EVERY PLY. AnalysisBoard uses array index as the canonical
  move index (src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx:403), so un-analyzed plies get the move's
  san/fen_after with null eval/best/classification fields (never omitted/reordered).
- position_analysis: Record<fen_before, PositionAnalysis> — ONLY analyzed indices contribute
  entries (un-analyzed FENs omitted). Keyed by fen_before, matching server semantics.
- initialMoveIndex = clamp(failedMoveIndex ?? 0, 0, moves.length - 1).
Reuse the existing per-index extraction in sessionUpload.ts (buildUploadForIndex) by factoring
shared field logic so SessionMoveUpload and AnalysisMove stay in sync.

## Steps
### 1. DrillStopActions.tsx
Rename onContinueAsNormal -> onAnalyze; label "Continue as normal game" -> "Analyze"; add
`analyzeEnabled`/`isPreparing` props (disable + "Preparing analysis…" while awaiting; hide
when moveHistory empty). Update DrillStopActions tests.

### 2. sessionUpload.ts
Add buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot (above). Unit-test: every ply present incl. null-analysis
plies; position_analysis keyed by fen_before and omits un-analyzed FENs; san parsing.

### 3. stores/drillAnalysisStore.ts
Narrow non-persisted singleton zustand store (per Zustand-store-design memory):
{ snapshot: { moves, positionAnalysis, playerColor, initialMoveIndex } | null,
  setSnapshot, clear }. Refresh loses it (ephemeral by design).

### 4. useChessGameLifecycle.ts + ChessGame.tsx

title: Fix drill lifecycle after opening root
description:
Correct the behavior introduced by g-drill-postroot. The intended drill lifecycle is:

1. User and ghost play normally until the selected opening root is reached.
2. The drill begins at the opening-root position, not before and not as an indefinite converted normal game.
3. The drill ends when the user makes the first mistake after that opening-root position.
4. After the drill ends, the user is offered the option to continue from the current position as a normal game.

The implementation should revisit frontend drill state transitions, opponent move routing, strictness/mistake handling, and the continue-as-normal-game prompt so these states are distinct and explicit.
design:
Context

 Drill mode currently has its lifecycle inverted vs. the product intent. The earlier
 g-drill-postroot work (437e979) made reaching the opening root the moment the drill
 effectively ends and converts to a normal game, while the "drill" mistake-checking actually
 happens during pre-root steering (and incorrectly fails on global-best accuracy — the
 symptom tracked by g-a20k.1).

 Intended lifecycle (from the bead):

 1. Pre-root — user + ghost play toward the selected root. Mistakes do not end the drill;
 the only pre-root failure is off_route.
 2. Active drill (post-root) — begins exactly when the root is reached. Play continues; the
 user's first post-root mistake (cp loss over drill_strictness_cp) ends the drill.
 3. Ended — that mistake stops the drill and pauses play behind an action surface.
 4. Normal continuation — optional "Continue as normal game" resumes rated play from the
 current position.

 State mapping (reuse existing DrillState, flip the meaning of the mistake paths)

 ┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │          Phase           │ drill_state  │             Mistake handling              │
 ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Pre-root steering        │ active       │ off_route fails; no accuracy check        │
 ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Active drill (post-root) │ root_reached │ first over-threshold player move → failed │
 ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Ended                    │ failed       │ paused; offer "Continue as normal game"   │
 ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ Normal continuation      │ converted    │ normal rated game from current position   │
 └──────────────────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┘

 Today accuracy fires on active (pre-root) and root_reached is a transient "press Continue"
 pause. After this change root_reached is the live drill (play flows, no pause) and the post-root
 mistake is detected client-side, authoritatively.

 Decision: subsume g-a20k.1 (confirmed)

 g-a20k.1 removes the three pre-root accuracy sites (route-check, _maybe_fail_active_drill_on_accuracy,
 the frontend analysis listener). Its fix is implemented-but-uncommitted; the current tree still has all
 three. We fold that removal in here. This dissolves two of the review concerns:

 - No upload-time accuracy check at all → no incremental-batch boundary problem (review #2 moot).
 Post-root detection moves entirely client-side (the worker already analyzes every move; the server
 can't reliably detect deep post-root mistakes on cache misses anyway).
 - Unlike g-a20k.1's "strictness_cp no longer affects anything," here the slider regains meaning
 post-root (it's the post-root mistake threshold) — consistent with the bead's strictness goal.

 Close g-a20k.1 as superseded once this lands.

 ---
 Backend changes

 backend/app/api/game.py — allow opponent moves in root_reached (review #1)

 get_next_opponent_move (~742): the guard treats only active (preroot) or converted as valid,
 so a root_reached drill returns 400 — which would break "play continues after root." Fix:
 - Permit drill_state in ("active", "root_reached") (plus converted); reject only failed/abandoned.
 - Keep the steering branch gated on pre-root active only (~764). root_reached falls through to
 the normal ghost-first / engine selection (the opponent plays normally post-root while the session
 stays a drill). The existing ghost-root transition at ~780–782 (sets root_reached) is unchanged.

 backend/app/api/drills.py

 - check_drill_route (~335–365): remove the pre-root accuracy block (g-a20k.1). Pre-root resolves
 only root_reached / on_route / off_route. is_target → root_reached (~367) stays. Drop now-unused
 threshold/accuracy helpers/imports as g-a20k.1 specified; keep off-route suggestions (unfiltered).
 - /fail (~239) — make it the authoritative post-root stop (review #4). Currently requires
 drill_state == "active" and sets failed with no reason. Change to accept a request body
 a required body { terminal_reason: "accuracy" } and set drill_state = "failed" +
 drill_terminal_reason = "accuracy". Tight contract (review #3/P3): this endpoint is only the
 post-root accuracy stop — it requires terminal_reason == "accuracy" and drill_state == "root_reached";
 reject a missing/other reason (422) and any other state (400). off_route and natural_end keep their
 own server paths (/route-check, /natural-end); /fail no longer accepts the old reasonless
 active failure (that path was unused). This preserves "pre-root mistakes never end the drill." The
 client awaits this on a post-root mistake so the failure is persisted before any /continue — no
 reliance on the (non-awaiting) upload flush. Update failDrill in src/utils/api.ts (currently
 body-less, ~496) to send { terminal_reason: "accuracy" }.
 - /continue (~257) and /natural-end (~425): unchanged. /continue already accepts failed and sets
 converted + is_rated + rated_start_ply = current_ply + resegments — correct for "continue from the
 post-root-mistake position as a normal game." (Post-root drill moves keep the drill segment because
 their ply ≤ rated_start_ply; no segmentation change, no new column.)

 backend/app/api/session.py — remove upload-time accuracy (g-a20k.1; review #2)

 Delete _maybe_fail_active_drill_on_accuracy (~394) and both call sites (~497, ~537) and its import.
 upsert_session_moves no longer mutates drill state. (It may still return drill_state in the response
 for info, but the client no longer drives failure from it — see coordinator change below.)

 ---
 Frontend changes (src/)

 Post-root reply ordering — one shared helper, fail-closed gate (reviews #1, #3)

 Today the opponent move is requested as soon as checkPostPlayerDrillRoute returns true, but mistake
 detection is async — so a bad post-root move can get a reply before the drill stops, pushing the
 "continue" boundary past the mistake. Two duplicated entry points must both be fixed:
 applyPlayerMoveAndAdvance (click, ChessGame.tsx ~885) and the drag/drop path
 (handleDrop/handleDropPiece ~1130–1162, which also calls checkPostPlayerDrillRoute →
 applyOpponentMove). Once allowDragging is unblocked post-root (below), a drag-drop post-root mistake
 could otherwise still get a reply.

 - Extract one shared continueAfterPlayerMove(result) helper that owns all post-player-move
 sequencing, and route both the click path (~885) and the drag/drop path (~1162) through it. No
 caller should call checkPostPlayerDrillRoute/applyOpponentMove/handleGameEnd directly for the
 post-move step. Today both paths also early-out on result.gameOver and skip drill handling — that must
 move inside the helper (see gameOver ordering below).
 - Capture sessionId, result.moveIndex, and the drill phase before awaiting. Inside the helper:
   - pre-root / non-drill (phase ≠ root_reached): await checkPostPlayerDrillRoute (which handles
 off_route failure and the active → root_reached transition; the root-reaching move is exempt from
 post-root accuracy). If it did not stop the drill → then handle gameOver/reply (below).
   - post-root (phase === root_reached): await waitForAnalysis(result.moveIndex); if
 delta > threshold (see threshold resolution below) → run the stop flow, no reply. Else → handle
 gameOver/reply.
 - gameOver ordering (P1): the helper runs drill route/accuracy handling first, and only if the
 drill did not stop does it act on result.gameOver (→ handleGameEnd, which already routes drill
 natural-end for active/root_reached). This prevents a terminal post-root mistake (or a terminal
 pre-root off-route move) from bypassing the drill lifecycle into a normal game end. If the drill stopped,
 do not call handleGameEnd.
 - Add coordinator.waitForAnalysis(moveIndex): Promise<AnalysisResult> to GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts,
 resolving from analysisMap if already present, else one-shot via the resolveAnalysisResult
 listeners (~462). Fail-closed (review #2): no "missing analysis = clean" timeout — the reply is
 withheld until analysis truly resolves. It rejects immediately when no analysis can arrive:
 coordinator status === 'error', or there is no resolved entry and no pending/latestRequestIds
 entry for that moveIndex (the "never scheduled" deadlock — analyzeMove returns undefined when in
 error at GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:302, while commitAppliedMove still invents a fallback id at
 useChessGameController.ts:142); and it rejects on worker error. On rejection the helper surfaces
 a retry/error state and does not reply and does not auto-fail the drill.
 - Stale-session protection (P1): waitForAnalysis captures sessionGeneration and is rejected on
 startSession/clearSession (generation bump) — extend those to reject outstanding waiters. After
 the await, before any fail/reply/message, the helper re-validates: store.sessionId unchanged,
 store.moveHistory[moveIndex]?.uci === result.uci, store.drillState === "root_reached", and not
 isRevertPending. If any check fails, abort silently (no state mutation). The current fire-and-forget
 void (async () => …)() blocks (~885, ~1162) must adopt this guarding.

 Stop flow (post-root mistake) — authoritative + paused

 A helper that: await failDrill(sessionId, "accuracy") (the tightened /fail), then set
 drillState="failed", drillTerminalReason="accuracy", setDrillFailInfo({...}), message.
 DrillStopActions already renders for isStoppedDrill (~1495) with onContinueAsNormal={handleContinueDrill}
 → continueDrill → converted.

 View/continue consistency (P2/P3): while stopped, the displayed board is the position before
 the mistake (viewIndex = moveIndex - 1) with the played-vs-best arrows via drillFailInfo — the
 existing blunder-review teaching pattern. The mistake move itself remains in live game state/history
 (it was played); it is simply not the displayed position until the view returns to live. "Continue as
 normal game" returns the view to live (which includes the mistake move) and resumes play from there;
 continueDrill uses moveHistory.length as rated_start_ply. (Wording fixed so tests/impl agree: the
 displayed board ≠ live position while stopped; continue clears the view back to live.)

 Don't clear teaching state until conversion succeeds (P2): handleContinueDrill (~640) currently
 clears drillFailInfo and viewIndex before convertRootReachedDrill() returns; if /continue
 fails, the drill stays failed but the teaching view/arrows are gone. Reorder: clear drillFailInfo +
 viewIndex only after a successful converted contract; on error, keep (or restore) the teaching
 state so the user can retry continue.

 checkPostPlayerDrillRoute (ChessGame.tsx ~501)

 On route.status === "root_reached": set drillState="root_reached", show a "drill is live" message
 (not "Continue when ready"), and return true so the opponent reply proceeds and play continues
 (no pause). Pre-root off_route failure path unchanged.

 Post-root error recovery — don't strand the game (P1)

 Post-root we disable local fallback (drill-aware), so two failures can leave the game stuck with no
 reply and no Retry, because the current Retry is gated to drillState === "active" (~1334) and rendered
 only in the steering-error UI (~1502):
 - waitForAnalysis rejects (worker error / never-scheduled) after a post-root player move → no reply.
 - Backend opponent move fails after a clean post-root move (onBackendFailure sets a message, no
 fallback) → no reply.

 Add an explicit post-root recovery path:
 - Broaden the retry affordance to also apply when drillState === "root_reached" (extend
 canRetryDrillSteering, or add a parallel canRetryPostRoot, and surface the Retry button in that
 state in the error UI).
 - Retry dispatches by failure kind: opponent-move failure → re-run applyOpponentMove(fen, uciHistory);
 analysis failure → re-schedule analysis for the pending move and re-run the post-root gate
 (continueAfterPlayerMove for that move). Track which recovery is pending so Retry does the right thing.
 - Cover both with tests.

 Failure persistence does not depend on uploads (P2)

 handleContinueDrill awaits coordinator.flushPendingUploads() (useChessGameLifecycle.ts ~949), but
 the coordinator only starts uploadSessionMoves(...).then(...) and returns immediately
 (GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts ~604/~655) — it is not awaitable persistence. The lifecycle stays
 correct because the authoritative failure is the awaited /fail call, and /continue only needs the
 drill in failed (it does not require the terminal move to be uploaded first). Treat the flush as
 best-effort; do not assume the mistake move is persisted before /continue (move data is eventually
 consistent via incremental upload + finalize). If we later need the terminal move guaranteed before
 conversion, change the flush contract to return a real awaited promise — out of scope here.

 Threshold resolution — handle nullable strictness_cp (open question)

 The post-root gate needs a cp threshold, but strictness_cp is nullable in the contract
 (src/utils/api.ts:217) — legacy/tier-only drills have strictness set but strictness_cp = null.
 Decision: mirror the backend resolve_drill_threshold (session_contracts.py:42,
 DRILL_STRICTNESS_TIER_THRESHOLDS = {strict:15, standard:35, lenient:50}): add a small frontend helper
 resolveStrictnessCp(strictnessCp, strictness) that returns strictnessCp ?? tierThreshold(strictness).
 The gate uses that resolved value (never the raw nullable field), so legacy/tier drills are supported.
 (Aligns with g-8iyq, which deprecates the tier field; until then the fallback keeps both working.)

 Ghost-reaches-root (useChessGameController.ts ~396)

 applyGhostMove already sets drillState="root_reached" on drillRoute.status === "root_reached". Update
 its message (drop "Continue when ready"); no pause. The subsequent player move is then gated by the
 post-root branch above — covering the ghost-root acceptance path.

 Remove the pre-root analysis listener (ChessGame.tsx ~550)

 Delete the drillState === "active" accuracy-fail useEffect (g-a20k.1). Post-root detection is now the
 waitForAnalysis gate above.

 Opponent-move drill-awareness after root

 shouldUseLocalFallback (~494): keep drill-aware post-root —
 !(drillOpeningKey && (drillState === "active" || drillState === "root_reached")).

 Coordinator upload handler (GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts ~606)

 Remove the response.drill_state === 'failed' && store.drillState === 'active' transition (the server no
 longer reports accuracy failure; the client drives it). Uploads remain pure move-data sync.

 root_reached is live play, not a pause

 - isRootReachedDrill (~212) and its blocking uses — handleSquareClick (~926), allowDragging (~1355),
 and the dep at ~967 — must no longer block input post-root. Remove !isRootReachedDrill from those
 guards (repurpose/remove the const).
 - BoardStage.tsx (~373–396): remove the drillState === "root_reached" "Continue" overlay
 (onContinueDrill/isContinuingDrill). The continue action lives only in the failed state via
 DrillStopActions. (Optionally drop onContinueDrill from BoardStage props.)
 - handleGameEnd natural-end (useChessGameLifecycle.ts ~270) keeps active | root_reached. Keep.
 - canRetryDrillSteering (~1334) stays gated on active (pre-root steering retry). Keep.

 ---
 Tests

 Backend (backend/test_drill_api.py)

 - route-check: on-route over-threshold pre-root move returns on_route (not failed); off-route still
 failed/off_route; is_target → root_reached.
 - next-opponent-move: a root_reached drill returns a normal ghost/engine move (no 400); failed/
 abandoned still 400.
 - /fail: from root_reached with terminal_reason="accuracy" → failed+accuracy; the same call from
 active is rejected (pre-root accuracy invariant); missing/other terminal_reason → 422; other
 states → 400.
 - /continue from failed → converted with supplied rated_start_ply and resegmentation.
 - Removed: the upload-accuracy tests g-a20k.1 deletes; assert upsert_session_moves no longer changes
 drill state.

 Frontend (ChessGame.test.tsx, GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts)

 - waitForAnalysis: resolves from cache-hit and from late worker resolution; rejects on worker error;
 rejects immediately when in error/never-scheduled (no deadlock, no clean-on-timeout); rejects on
 startSession/clearSession (stale-session). Drag/drop and click both route through the shared
 continueAfterPlayerMove.
 - Player-reaches-root and ghost-reaches-root both set root_reached and continue play (no pause).
 - Post-root: a clean move gets an opponent reply; an over-threshold move triggers failDrill before
 any reply, pauses at the mistake (teaching view), and shows DrillStopActions. A reply is never
 applied if the session changed / move was reverted while analysis was pending.
 - gameOver ordering: a terminal post-root mistake stops the drill (no normal game-end); a terminal
 pre-root off-route move fails off_route (no normal game-end); a terminal clean move → drill natural-end.
 - Threshold fallback: tier-only drill (strictness_cp == null) still detects post-root mistakes via
 resolveStrictnessCp.
 - On waitForAnalysis rejection (worker error): retry/error surfaced, no reply, no drill fail.
 - Post-root recovery (P1): Retry is offered when root_reached and (a) an opponent-move backend
 failure occurred → re-requests the opponent move, or (b) waitForAnalysis rejected → re-runs the gate;
 neither strands the game.
 - Continue failure (P2): if /continue rejects, the drill stays failed with the teaching
 view/arrows preserved (clearing happens only after a converted contract).
 - No analysis listener registered for pre-root accuracy; coordinator upload no longer flips drill state.
 - "Continue as normal game" from failed → converted, clears to live, resumes from current position.

 ---
 Verification (end-to-end)

 1. cd backend && pytest test_drill_api.py (+ touched session tests).
 2. npm run test:run for ChessGame.test.tsx, GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts (NOT npm test — that
 runs Vitest in watch mode); then npm run build (which itself runs tsc -b && vitest run && vite build).
 3. Manual (/run): start a drill on a sideline opening (e.g. 1.b4); play on-route-but-suboptimal pre-root
 moves → drill does not end; reach the root → play continues (no "Continue" pause); make a post-root
 over-threshold move → opponent does not reply, drill stops at the mistake with "Continue as normal
 game"; click it → rated normal play resumes from there. Repeat with the ghost reaching the root.

 Notes / follow-ups

 - Close g-a20k.1 as superseded by this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
Reaching the opening root starts the drill instead of converting immediately to a normal game.
Pre-root moves do not end the drill for mistake purposes.
The first user mistake after the opening root ends the drill.
After the drill ends, the UI offers a continue-normal-game action.
Selecting continue resumes normal game behavior from the current position.
Automated coverage protects player-root and ghost-root paths.
notes:
Requested because the design decision captured in g-drill-postroot was incorrect.

Pre-root route-breaking behavior stays the same: before the opening root is reached, if a user move leaves every valid route/transposition to the selected root, the drill fails with terminal_reason=off_route and shows correction suggestions from the pre-move position. This fix is about the lifecycle after the root is reached.
close_reason: Implemented drill lifecycle after opening root with post-root accuracy stop, route-check/upload accuracy removal, retry recovery, and tests.

title: Add focused drill mode tests
description: Add focused backend and frontend tests for the completed drill mode behavior, emphasizing data flow and critical user outcomes instead of cosmetic UI structure.
design:
Prefer behavior-contract tests. Avoid brittle styling, layout, exact copy, or nav-chrome assertions unless needed to prove a critical outcome.

Policy update from g-drill-policy, amended 2026-06-01:

- Uncontinued drills remain unrated and hidden from history/session-analysis lists.
- Continued drills are one full normal game. Tests should expect history, analysis, CPL, blunder counts, stats, achievements, and comparable user metrics to include the full line, including pre-continue moves.
- Pre-continue drill uploads and analyses should feed regular evidence paths: opening score live attempts, passive blunder opportunity counters, automatic blunder records, SRS item creation/review handling, analysis-cache/upload side effects, streaks, achievements, and comparable user metrics.
- Drill strictness failures should be allowed to create blunder and SRS evidence through regular game logic.
- `rated_start_ply` may exist for compatibility, but tests should not assert that UI or analytics exclude a drill prefix because of it.

Focused coverage should include transposition reaching target root, no-path opening failure, strictness stop before opponent move, hidden abandoned drills, no Elo impact for abandoned drills, continue conversion as a full normal game, regular evidence side effects during pre-continue drill play, and SRS behavior after target root is reached.
