title: Add drill backend session contract
description: Introduce the backend/API contract for drill sessions: selected color, exact opening root, engine difficulty, strictness, unrated mode, drill lifecycle state, and conversion to normal play.
design:
Plan for drill backend session contract

Goal
Introduce a first-class drill session contract that can be created by the drill setup UI, remains unrated and hidden while unconverted, records the selected setup explicitly, and can later convert the same session into normal play with an immutable rated boundary. This bead owns server/session contracts and typed API shape. It does not implement pre-opening steering or full drill UI behavior.

Chosen data model
1. Store drill metadata directly on game_sessions. Do not create a separate drill_sessions table for this bead. The contract needs frequent filtering beside status, user_id, is_rated, engine_elo, and player_color, and direct columns keep existing session ownership/rating code explicit.
2. Add game_sessions.session_mode varchar(10) not null default normal, check in normal|drill.
3. Add game_sessions.drill_state varchar(12) nullable, check null or active|failed|abandoned|converted. Constraint: session_mode=normal requires drill_state is null; session_mode=drill requires drill_state is not null.
4. Add game_sessions.drill_opening_key text nullable. Store only the key durably; opening name, family, ECO, and depth are derived from get_opening_roots at response time so registry corrections do not require data migrations.
5. Add game_sessions.drill_strictness varchar(12) nullable, check null or lenient|standard|strict. Exact UI labels can change later; these enum values are the backend contract.
6. Add game_sessions.normal_started_at timestamp nullable, converted_at timestamp nullable, and rated_start_ply integer nullable with check rated_start_ply >= 0.
7. Constraints for drill conversion: converted drill sessions require normal_started_at, converted_at, rated_start_ply, and is_rated=true. Active, failed, or abandoned drill sessions require is_rated=false and rated_start_ply=null.
8. Preserve existing normal defaults: normal sessions stay session_mode=normal, drill_state=null, is_rated=true unless the existing normal client explicitly ends as practice. Drill creation sets session_mode=drill, drill_state=active, status=active, is_rated=false, blunder_recorded=false, engine_elo/player_color from setup, drill_opening_key, drill_strictness, and rated_start_ply=null.
9. Add session_moves.segment varchar(10) not null default normal, check in drill|normal. Backfill all existing moves to normal. Keep session_moves unique key unchanged: (session_id, move_number, color).
10. Add indexes: idx_game_sessions_user_mode_status on (user_id, session_mode, status), idx_game_sessions_drill_state on (drill_state), and idx_session_moves_session_segment on (session_id, segment). Update SQLAlchemy models, Alembic migration, backend/conftest.py SQLite schema, and test fixture inserts in lockstep.

Ply and segment contract
1. Define ply as zero-based half-moves from the initial board: before any move current_ply=0; after White move 1 current_ply=1; after Black move 1 current_ply=2; after White move N current_ply=2*N-1; after Black move N current_ply=2*N.
2. Map existing session_moves rows to ply deterministically: ply_after = (move_number - 1) * 2 + (1 if color=white else 2). For segmenting a row, compare its ply_after to rated_start_ply.
3. rated_start_ply is the half-move count at the moment Continue as normal is accepted, before any normal-play move is accepted. Rows with ply_after <= rated_start_ply are drill segment. Rows with ply_after > rated_start_ply are normal segment.
4. Before conversion, all uploaded rows for a drill session are segment=drill.
5. After conversion, full-line re-uploads are re-segmented server-side on every upsert using rated_start_ply. The client may send segment for transparency, but the server is authoritative and ignores conflicting segment values.
6. Normal sessions always store segment=normal.
7. Session move upload remains keyed by (session_id, move_number, color). No separate ply column is required for this bead because ply is derived, but helper functions should centralize the calculation.

Create drill API
1. Add POST /api/drills/start. Do not overload /api/game/start; keeping drill creation explicit preserves normal-game compatibility.
2. Request shape: opening_key, player_color, engine_elo, strictness. Validate opening_key against get_opening_roots, player_color via white|black enum, engine_elo with the same bounds accepted by normal game start, and strictness via lenient|standard|strict.
3. Response shape: session_id, mode=drill, drill_state=active, opening_key, opening_name, opening_family, eco, depth, player_color, engine_elo, strictness, is_rated=false, rated_start_ply=null, normal_started_at=null, converted_at=null.
4. Creation does not create positions, moves, blunders, rating history, opening evidence, or analysis-cache entries.

Session identification shape
1. Add a shared DrillSessionContract response model for drill endpoints. If active-play callers need to hydrate by session id, add GET /api/drills/{session_id} with the same response shape.
2. Keep /api/game/start response stable for normal game callers unless downstream UI needs a common GameSessionContract.
3. Any endpoint that returns or consumes active session state must use session_mode, drill_state, is_rated, rated_start_ply, normal_started_at, drill_opening_key, player_color, engine_elo, and strictness from the server rather than relying on frontend-local inference.

Continue as normal contract
1. Add POST /api/drills/{session_id}/continue. Request: current_ply int >= 0, optional pgn/current_fen only if reconstruction requires it later.
2. Server validates ownership, session_mode=drill, status=active, drill_state in active|failed, and not already ended. It must reject normal sessions, abandoned drills, and ended sessions.
3. On success, set drill_state=converted, is_rated=true, normal_started_at=now, converted_at=now, rated_start_ply=current_ply. Keep engine_elo, player_color, drill_opening_key, and drill_strictness immutable.
4. Re-segment any already-uploaded session_moves for that session using the boundary rule. This handles clients that uploaded the drill prefix before conversion.
5. Idempotency: if the drill is already converted and current_ply equals rated_start_ply, return the existing contract. If current_ply differs, return 409.
6. Normal play starts with the next accepted move where ply_after > rated_start_ply.

Fail and abandon drill contract
1. Add POST /api/drills/{session_id}/fail. This is required because failed is an accepted lifecycle state. It validates ownership, session_mode=drill, status=active, drill_state=active, then sets drill_state=failed. It does not end the session, rate the game, write RatingHistory, or create hidden evidence.
2. Add POST /api/drills/{session_id}/abandon. It validates ownership and session_mode=drill. For active or failed unconverted drills, set drill_state=abandoned, status=ended, result=drill_abandon, ended_at=now, is_rated=false. It must never create RatingHistory.
3. Abandon on a converted drill should return 400 instructing callers to use /api/game/end with result=abandon. Converted abandon is a normal-game abandon: preserve session.is_rated=true and create no RatingHistory only because abandon is not in RESULT_SCORES.
4. Another Drill uses the abandon endpoint for the current unconverted drill, then starts a fresh drill.

Harden /api/game/end
1. /api/game/end must not trust request.is_rated for drill sessions.
2. If session_mode=drill and drill_state is active, failed, or abandoned, /api/game/end must reject with 400 and direct the caller to the drill abandon/continue contract. It must not overwrite session.is_rated and must not create RatingHistory.
3. If session_mode=drill and drill_state=converted, /api/game/end may end the session only as the converted normal game. It must force rating eligibility from the stored session state rather than client input: effective_is_rated = session.is_rated and result in rated outcomes. The request.is_rated field must not be allowed to downgrade a converted drill to practice mode.
4. For converted drill abandon through /api/game/end, persist result=abandon while preserving session.is_rated=true. RatingHistory is suppressed by the effective rated-result check, not by downgrading the session.
5. For normal session_mode=normal games, preserve current /api/game/end semantics unless this bead deliberately tightens normal-game practice behavior in tests.
6. Add regression tests proving unconverted drills cannot be rated by posting /api/game/end with is_rated=true, converted drills cannot be made untracked by posting is_rated=false, and converted abandon keeps is_rated=true while creating no RatingHistory.

Server-side filtering and call-site checklist
1. Add shared predicates/helpers, for example is_visible_game_session = session_mode=normal OR drill_state=converted, and normal_segment_move_filter = SessionMove.segment == normal. Use these from API modules instead of repeating ad hoc checks.
2. backend/app/api/history.py: session query must include only ended visible sessions. Summary aggregation must count only segment=normal moves.
3. backend/app/api/stats.py summary session query must exclude unconverted drills from played/completed/active counts. Player move rows, move counts, data completeness, color splits, and blunders-per-100 must use segment=normal only.
4. backend/app/api/stats.py perfect streak helper must count only visible sessions and normal segment player moves.
5. backend/app/api/session.py get_session_analysis must return 404 or hidden for unconverted drills. Converted drills may return full move list for reconstruction, but response must expose rated_start_ply and segment per move, and summaries must use segment=normal only.
6. backend/app/api/session.py upsert_session_moves must set segment server-side and must skip blunder opportunity computation/opening score refresh when the uploaded rows are drill segment only. For mixed converted uploads, evidence computations must consider normal segment rows only.
7. backend/app/opening_evidence.py must ignore drill segment rows and unconverted drill sessions when deriving live attempts, review attempts, last touch, and subtree evidence.
8. backend/app/opening_cache.py user/color discovery and refresh triggers must not treat unconverted drill-only activity as evidence-producing work.
9. backend/app/api/blunder.py automatic blunder recording must reject or no-op for unconverted drills. Explicit SRS review persistence remains allowed during drills per g-drill-policy. Manual capture policy remains unchanged unless a later product bead changes it.
10. backend/scripts/backfill_glicko_ratings.py should naturally ignore unconverted drills by requiring is_rated=true and rated results; add session_mode filtering if needed for clarity.

Validation and errors
1. Unknown opening_key returns 404 Unknown opening root, consistent with openings route behavior.
2. Cross-user drill continue, fail, or abandon returns 403.
3. Continuing a normal session, ended session, abandoned drill, or converted drill with conflicting ply returns 400 or 409 as specified above.
4. Starting a drill with invalid strictness/player_color returns 422 through Pydantic.
5. /api/game/end on unconverted drills returns 400 before mutating the session.

Tests
1. Backend API tests for drill creation: response shape, persisted fields, is_rated=false, session_mode/drill_state, selected color/engine/opening/strictness, auth required, unknown opening rejected.
2. Continue tests: same session converts, rated_start_ply and timestamps set once, existing uploaded rows are re-segmented, repeated matching request is idempotent, conflicting repeated request fails, converted session can later produce one RatingHistory through normal /api/game/end.
3. Fail tests: active drill can become failed, failed drill remains active and continuable, fail does not end/rate/write evidence, invalid transitions fail.
4. Abandon tests: unconverted drill ends with drill_state=abandoned/result=drill_abandon/is_rated=false, no RatingHistory, hidden from history/stats/analysis.
5. /api/game/end guard tests: unconverted drill with is_rated=true is rejected and creates no RatingHistory; converted drill posted with is_rated=false still follows stored converted-game rating rules for rated terminal results; converted drill ended with result=abandon preserves session.is_rated=true and creates no RatingHistory.
6. Ply/segment tests: boundary inclusivity uses ply_after <= rated_start_ply as drill; full-line re-upload after conversion re-segments deterministically; normal sessions default all rows to normal.
7. Filtering tests for each call site: history, stats summary, perfect streak, session analysis, opening_evidence, opening_cache refresh/discovery, and automatic blunder capture.
8. Frontend API type tests only for request/response helpers if this bead touches src/utils/api.ts. Avoid brittle UI tests.

Implementation order
1. Add migration/model/test-schema fields, constraints, indexes, and helper functions for visible session and ply/segment calculation.
2. Add drill API router with start, get, fail, continue, and abandon contracts.
3. Harden /api/game/end before adding positive conversion tests, so unconverted drills cannot leak into rating.
4. Update session move upload to assign segment server-side and re-segment on conversion.
5. Apply shared filtering helpers to history, stats, perfect streak, session analysis, opening evidence/cache, and blunder capture.
6. Update frontend API types/helpers only as needed for downstream setup work.
7. Run focused backend tests: test_game_api.py, test_session_api.py, test_stats_api.py, test_opening_evidence.py, test_opening_cache.py, relevant blunder tests, and new drill contract tests.
acceptance_criteria: API can create and identify drill sessions with explicit selected setup values; drill sessions are unrated from creation; continue-as-normal has a defined immutable rated_start_ply contract; abandoned drill sessions are distinguishable from normal games; /api/game/end rejects unconverted drills and cannot rate them through request.is_rated; converted drills keep session.is_rated=true even when result=abandon and suppress RatingHistory only because abandon is not a rated result; session move segmenting uses the documented ply_after <= rated_start_ply boundary and full-line re-uploads are re-segmented server-side; history, stats, analysis, opening evidence/cache, perfect streaks, and automatic blunder capture use server-side filtering so unconverted drills and drill-prefix rows do not leak into normal-game surfaces or evidence.
notes: Implemented drill backend contract plus review fix for converted-drill timing: stats windows/durations, SRS opportunity occurred_at, and opening evidence live timestamps now use normal_started_at for converted drills and started_at for normal sessions. Verification: 155 focused backend tests pass; git diff --check clean. Alembic SQLite upgrade sanity cannot reach this migration because older 20260203_02 migration uses SQLite-unsupported ALTER check constraints outside batch mode.
close_reason: Implemented drill backend session contract and converted-drill timing boundary fix; focused backend tests pass.

title: Define drill mode product policy
description: Decide the product rules that must be fixed before drill mode implementation: revert and resign behavior, pre-continue data retention, SRS/opening evidence handling, and the exact unrated to rated boundary when a user continues a drill as a normal game.
design:
Drill mode product policy, amended 2026-06-01

State model
- A drill session starts as mode=drill, is_rated=false, hidden from history and analysis lists, and eligible for normal user evidence side effects unless a narrower endpoint explicitly cannot operate before conversion.
- Continue as normal game converts the same board/session into normal play. From that point the whole continued session is treated as one normal game for history, analysis summaries, CPL, blunder counts, stats, achievements, comparable user metrics, and PGN/export surfaces.
- rated_start_ply may remain as a backend reconstruction or legacy contract field if already implemented, but product policy no longer uses it to exclude a drill prefix from normal totals, evidence, analytics, or UI summaries.
- Moves before continue are not a separate product segment once the game is continued. Do not require APIs or UI to mark them as drill context for filtering.

Lifecycle actions
- Revert before continue: local drill rewind only unless the current implementation has already persisted regular game side effects for analyzed/uploaded moves. Do not call normal end_game, do not record resign, do not create RatingHistory, and do not make the session visible in history or analysis lists. Clear pending UI review/analysis state at or after the rewind point where practical; do not delete already-persisted regular evidence without an explicit product decision.
- Revert after the drill has stopped on a drill failure: disable generic revert. The drill-end actions are Another drill and Continue as normal game.
- Revert after continue: use normal rated-game revert semantics. The game is a normal continued game; do not clamp solely to preserve a drill-prefix evidence boundary.
- Resign before continue: product copy should behave as End drill, not a rated resignation. Backend state should be drill abandoned or discarded, with no rating, history-list visibility, or analysis-list visibility. Resign after continue is a normal resignation.
- Abandon before continue, including reset, navigation away, or starting another drill, abandons or discards the drill with no rating, history-list visibility, or analysis-list visibility. Regular evidence already produced by uploads/analysis may remain. Abandon after continue is normal abandonment: visible as a normal-game abandon, with no rating because abandon is not a rated result.
- Another drill abandons the current uncontinued drill, preserves opening, engine, color, and strictness selections client-side as sticky defaults, and starts a fresh drill session.
- Continue as normal game converts the same board/session into normal play. Normal uploads, blunder recording, SRS, analysis, history, and final rating rules apply to the full line.

Rating impact
- Never create RatingHistory for uncontinued drills, drill failure, pre-continue revert, pre-continue resign/end-drill, pre-continue abandon, or Another drill.
- A continued game creates at most one RatingHistory row when it later ends with a rated terminal result: checkmate_win, checkmate_loss, resign, or draw. Abandon remains unrated.
- Rating calculation uses the selected engine difficulty for the converted session. Rating is applied to the continued game as a whole when it ends with a rated result.

History, analysis, and retention
- Uncontinued drills are hidden from history lists and session analysis endpoints. Direct analysis fetch should return hidden/not found until the drill is converted.
- Pre-continue data may be retained for reconstruction, analysis, evidence, and debugging. It does not need to be explicitly segmented for product filtering.
- For continued games, history shows one normal game after it ends. Analysis may show the full move line to reconstruct the board and should summarize the full line as a normal game.
- History summaries, analysis summaries, CPL, blunder counts, stats, achievements, comparable user metrics, and PGN/export surfaces should use the full continued game unless a future surface explicitly introduces a different drill-context view.
- PGN can include the full line for legality and reconstruction. APIs are not required by product policy to expose rated_start_ply for segmentation.

SRS, opening evidence, and evidence side effects
- Passive pre-continue drill moves feed regular evidence paths: opening score live attempts, passive blunder opportunity counters, stats achievements, perfect streaks, automatic blunder library records, user-specific evidence from analysis-cache/upload side effects, and comparable user metrics should behave like regular game logic.
- Explicit SRS review interactions during a drill count. When the UI arms a target_blunder_id and the user answers that reviewed position, persist pass/fail exactly as in a regular game.
- Drill strictness failures may create blunders and SRS items using the regular game logic. Do not suppress them merely because the session is still a drill.
- Opening score review evidence may include explicit drill SRS reviews if the opening score system counts reviews. Live/session-move evidence from the drill prefix is included.
- If pre-continue analyses are uploaded for cache or reconstruction, they should use regular upload/cache/evidence behavior. There is no requirement to mark them as drill segment or filter them out of user evidence paths.

Implementation guardrails
- The backend contract should carry mode, drill_state, selected setup fields, continued_at or normal_started_at, and any existing rated_start_ply field required for compatibility, but filtering must not rely on a drill-prefix exclusion boundary for continued games or evidence side effects.
- Filtering must still be enforced server-side for rating and user-facing history/analysis visibility of uncontinued drills.
- Focused tests should assert uncontinued drills are unrated and hidden from history/analysis lists, continued games summarize and analyze the full line, pre-continue uploads feed normal evidence paths, drill strictness failures can record blunder/SRS evidence through regular game logic, and explicit SRS reviews survive abandon/another drill.
acceptance_criteria: Policy explicitly covers revert, resign, abandon, another drill, continue as normal game, rating impact, history visibility, analysis visibility, and whether pre-continue moves feed hidden evidence or SRS/opening evidence.
close_reason: Product policy recorded in design field and acceptance criteria covered.

title: Epic: chesstree.net style horizontal move graph
description:
Convert /openings's graph display into a chesstree.net style horizontal move graph.

 g-nge9 has the details of the prototype for the UI prototype I built in TreePrototypePage.tsx to test out the UI ideas.

We  need to think through how to convert the existing /openings to the new tree graph.gradient
- The new UI does not have separate black/white repertoire.
- how do we link to an opening?

The prototype did not test out the colors for A-F but we want to keep that concept in the new UI as well as the grades.

The new cards have two states, selected/unselected collapsed/expanded.
The look we use in /history for "Your Opening Scores" might be reusable for collapsed, though I think we need two lines. Let's create a reusable component for the cards.

The new cards don't have a chessboard but we do want to add a new field for eval score. Let's addd eval score to the collapsed card as well.

The prototype shows all legal moves at each node. We should prune that down somehow. Maybe a combination of named nodes and played nodes.

How deep does the graph go? Maybe up to named moves plus played moves (Does that mean you can navigate through your full previously played games?). Another possibility: up to the lichess opening boundary detailed in g-opening-score-v2.
How should the nodes be sorted in a column? Possibilities include, player's opening score descending, player's most played openings, eval score best to worst.
design:
## Product contract

Replace the current card-grid body of `/openings` with the horizontal, selected-branch move graph proven in `TreePrototypePage.tsx`. The route stays `/openings`; the prototype route remains reference-only until the production page has equivalent behavior, then can be removed in the implementation change.

This is one shared move topology, not two separate White and Black opening hierarchies. Scores and evidence must remain side-specific, however, because the same position has different meaning when the user is playing White versus Black. Keep `color=white|black` in the URL and present it above the workspace as one compact global segmented control labeled `Playing as: White | Black`. This is the only White/Black selector in the tree UI. Switching perspective preserves the selected move line and board position, refetches only the user overlay/metrics, flips board orientation, and canonicalizes back to the longest valid shared line if a perspective-only observed continuation is unavailable. Cards show only the active perspective's metrics; do not average White and Black scores, show both scores together, or show a single ambiguous combined score.

## Graph identity and selected-path model

- A displayed move node is an edge identity: `(parent_fen, move_uci, child_fen)`. Use UCI as the stable key and SAN only for display.
- Position identity and score identity use normalized four-field FEN. This keeps transpositions merged for evidence/scoring while the ordered UCI line preserves the route the user actually navigated.
- Column 0 is the starting-position root. Column N+1 contains the interesting moves from the position selected in column N.
- State is one selected root-to-position path. Selecting a move truncates any deeper path and reveals the next column. Only the deepest selected node expands; earlier selected path nodes remain compact and highlighted.
- Tree to board: the board shows the deepest selected position and highlights the edge that reached it.
- Board to tree: a drop succeeds only when its UCI move is present in the current API-provided child set. A legal move outside the opening graph is rejected so the board and tree cannot diverge.
- Checkmate/stalemate or an opening-phase terminal position has no child column and displays a terminal note in the expanded card.

## Which moves appear

Do not enumerate all legal moves. The structural tree is the union of:

1. Reference opening-book edges from `OpeningGraph`.
2. Observed continuation edges from the selected perspective's normal/drill sessions when the move's pre-move position is still in the opening interval.

This makes "named plus played" precise: opening-book paths supply known/named theory, including unnamed intermediate plies, and observed edges retain the user's real off-book continuations. Book edges are shown even with no user evidence. Observed off-book edges are shown after one valid traversal; they do not need to become prepared first.

Use the same Lichess phase horizon implemented by `g-opening-score-v2`:

- For observed games, inclusion follows the exact per-session divider. The move entering the first middlegame position is the final opening move and its resulting node is shown as terminal.
- For reference-only book branches, stop after showing the child that first satisfies the raw middlegame predicate.
- Do not allow navigation through the rest of a previously played game and do not retain the old fixed two-user-decision book extension.
- Keep cycle detection and a defensive 80-ply request limit, but do not impose an arbitrary product depth cap.

The current book has 15,511 positions, 15,870 edges, at most 22 children at a position, and 20 children at the start. The per-column scroll design can therefore show the complete structural sibling set without a result cap for MVP.

## Metrics shown on a node

Every compact and expanded node represents the resulting child position under the perspective selected by the global `Playing as: White | Black` control.

Compact card, two lines:

- Line 1: SAN move, whole-number opening score, and A/B/C/D/F grade.
- Line 2: deepest opening name (ellipsis plus accessible full label) and engine evaluation.

Expanded card, no embedded chessboard:

- Move number plus SAN and opening name.
- Opening score and grade.
- Engine evaluation.
- Coverage, distinct game count, and confidence.
- `Start Drill` when the selected FEN is an existing `OpeningRoots` drill root.
- Terminal/opening-boundary status when applicable.

Neither compact nor expanded cards show both White and Black scores. They show only the score and supporting metrics for the active global perspective.

Use grade text as well as color. Keep grade thresholds behind the existing formatting helper so `g-opening-score-v2` calibration can change thresholds without changing card markup. Add distinct CSS grade tokens for A, B, C, D, F, and no-data rather than collapsing all passing grades into one tone.

`game_count` must mean distinct sessions that reached the scored subtree. Do not label `sample_size` as Games; retain sample size in the API if useful but return a separate distinct game count for this UI.

Engine evaluation is informational and never used for opening score, pruning, or default sorting. Source it from the existing global `analysis_cache`, which is populated both by opening-book precomputation and analyzed player moves. A displayed move node already has the cache key `(parent_fen, move_uci)`: use `played_eval_mate` when present, otherwise `played_eval`, because those fields evaluate the resulting child position after that move. Cache values are stored white-relative; the API may return them white-relative, and the frontend renders them from the selected perspective so positive means favorable for the selected side. For the starting-position root, use `best_eval` from a complete cache row at the starting FEN where `move_uci == best_move_uci`; otherwise show no eval. Replay the selected UCI line from the initial board to retain a full six-field parent FEN for exact cache lookup. Because opening graph identity uses normalized four-field FEN and transpositions can differ only in clocks, the tree cache helper must support an indexed normalized-parent-FEN plus move-UCI fallback rather than scanning `analysis_cache`; exact full-FEN matches win. If multiple normalized fallback rows exist, choose deterministically, preferring a row with mate data, then `source=precomputed`, then `source=game`, then other sources, with stable ID tie-breaking. Return null and render an em dash only when the cache has no usable eval. Do not launch browser Stockfish searches when a column opens and do not copy eval values into the opening position-score table.

## Position-score read model

The tree needs a direct score for intermediate move positions, not only the current 11,274 named boundary roots. It must not run a complete root calculation independently for every visible card or on every click.

After `g-opening-score-v2` supplies direct position-root semantics, add a generation-scoped position-score read model keyed by `(batch_id, normalized_fen)` for every reachable book position and phase-valid observed off-book position. Store direct score, confidence, coverage, sample size, distinct game count and last practiced time. Compute these rows from one shared memoized traversal per user/color generation; named opening cards and arbitrary tree nodes must read the same metric semantics. A separate table/read model is preferred over changing `user_opening_scores` from a named-root contract without an explicit migration.

No-evidence positions remain structural nodes with null score/confidence/coverage and zero games. The skeptical prior must not be presented as observed mastery.

## Sorting

Default to relevance, not engine strength:

- At a user-to-move position: prepared/observed choices first, then `user_choice_count` descending, then scored weaknesses first (`score` ascending, null last).
- At an opponent-to-move position: encountered replies first, then `encounter_count` descending, then scored weaknesses first (`score` ascending, null last).
- Remaining ties/book-only moves sort deterministically by destination file/rank, source square, promotion, then SAN.

This keeps the user's actual repertoire and common replies near the top while surfacing weak branches without allowing one low score from a tiny sample to outrank frequency. Engine eval is not a default sort because it measures the objective position rather than the user's familiarity. A sort menu is out of scope for MVP; add it only after the default is exercised with real data.

## Visual encoding

Keep one visual variable per concept:

- Node/card accent color: opening-score grade.
- Selected-path connector width: log-scaled selected-edge encounter count within the sibling column, clamped to 2-6px.
- Connector style: solid when observed, dashed when book-only.
- Coverage: numeric/progress treatment inside the expanded card, not another connector color.

The connector remains the prototype's measured SVG curve between the selected node and next selected node/column, including clamped off-screen indicators. It must not require measuring every sibling.

## URL and linking contract

The URL is the source of truth for navigation:

- `color=white|black` selects score/evidence perspective.
- Repeated `move=<uci>` parameters encode the exact selected line from the initial position.
- The backend replays and validates the line against the phase-bounded structural graph, truncates at the first invalid move, and returns `canonical_line`; the frontend replaces non-canonical URLs.
- Score identity remains normalized FEN, so transposed positions share metrics even when reached through different `move` lines.

Support existing `opening=<normalized FEN>` links during migration. If no exact UCI line is supplied, resolve a deterministic shortest book path to that FEN with stable UCI tie-breaking, return that canonical line, and rewrite the URL. Exact history-game links should pass the game's actual UCI prefix when `g-isrd` is implemented. Update `buildOpeningsSearchParams` rather than constructing query strings in components.

## Backend API

Add a lazy tree endpoint, e.g. `GET /api/openings/tree?player_color=white&move=e2e4&move=c7c5`.

Return enough data to hydrate a refresh/deep link in one request:

- `player_color`, `canonical_line`, selected FEN, batch timestamp/model version.
- One column for the root and each selected parent along the canonical line.
- Each column's selected UCI and ordered child nodes.
- Each node: parent/result FEN, UCI, SAN, ply, opening name/ECO, book/observed/prepared flags, choice/encounter counts, direct score/confidence/coverage/sample size/game count, white-relative cp/mate eval, terminal reason, and nullable `drill_opening_key`.

Use one evidence overlay and one position-metric lookup per request. Do not call `compute_root_score` once per returned child. The endpoint should serve cached current-generation position rows and structural graph data; stale score refresh follows the existing atomic opening-score batch behavior.

Retain `/api/openings/children` during migration for other callers, then remove it only after `/openings`, session-opening links, and tests no longer depend on it.

## Frontend structure and data flow

- Replace the mock implementation with production components; do not copy the entire prototype into `OpeningsPage` unchanged.
- Add a reusable presentational `OpeningScoreCard`/`OpeningTreeNodeCard` with compact and expanded variants. Interaction wrappers own buttons/links so actions are never nested inside a node button. The compact visual body should be reusable by `GameOpeningLineage`; migrating that caller is in scope only where it does not change its behavior.
- Keep route parsing/canonicalization in `src/openings/route.ts`.
- Keep page request state local or in a narrow openings-tree hook; no broad Zustand store is needed. Chess instances and request effects stay outside stores.
- Cache successful responses by `playerColor + canonicalLine` for instant backtracking. Guard stale requests with an abort/version check as the current page does.
- Selecting a node updates the URL and keeps existing columns visible while the new right-most column loads. Expansion errors render inline in that column with Retry instead of blanking the whole page.
- The tree remains fully operable by node buttons without board dragging. Node controls expose selected/expanded state and grade text to assistive technology.

## Layout and sizing

Desktop/tablet workspace:

- Compact page header and the global `Playing as: White | Black` segmented control above a viewport-bounded workspace; remove the current large hero/card-grid treatment.
- Workspace is a two-column flex/grid: board `clamp(280px, 30vw, 380px)`, gap 16-24px, tree `minmax(0, 1fr)`.
- Compact tree columns are 148px; the active expanded column is 232px; inter-column gap is 32px. The tree scrolls horizontally and auto-reveals a newly added right-most column.
- The workspace fills the remaining `100dvh` after nav/header/padding with a minimum usable height of 420px. Columns stretch to the workspace height; each node list owns vertical overflow. There is no whole-tree vertical scrollbar.
- The board never determines tree column height. Keep it square and sticky at the workspace top if the workspace itself can scroll.

Narrow layout (`<=720px`):

- Stack board above tree, board width `min(100%, 360px)`.
- Tree remains horizontally scrollable with a 280px minimum height and approximately 45dvh maximum visible band; columns keep independent vertical overflow.
- Preserve at least one compact next column peeking beside the expanded 220px card where viewport width permits.
- Allow normal page vertical scrolling on small screens rather than clipping nav, board, or actions to force a no-page-scroll invariant.

Retain the prototype's explicit `overflow-x`/`overflow-y` declarations to avoid browser auto-promotion creating spurious scrollbars.

## Drill behavior

Preserve current drill correctness before broadening the target model:

- `Start Drill` is enabled only when `OpeningRoots.get_root(selected_fen)` succeeds; pass that FEN and the selected perspective through the existing `/play` drill setup flow.
- Keep one action labeled `Start Drill`; do not add `Start Drill as White`, `Start Drill as Black`, or duplicate side-specific drill buttons. The action always inherits the global `Playing as` perspective.
- Intermediate/non-root and observed off-book nodes omit the action rather than silently drilling a different ancestor.
- Extending drills to arbitrary book/off-book positions is a separate task because the current API contract, metadata, and route validation require a named root.

## Loading, empty, and error behavior

- Initial load shows a board/workspace skeleton.
- No user evidence is not an empty page: render the reference book tree with no-data grades and null metrics.
- A perspective with no games still supports navigation and named opening lookup.
- Structural/API failure shows a page-level retry. Child-expansion failure is column-local.
- Missing eval is a normal null state, not an error.

## Sequencing and boundaries

1. `g-opening-score-v2` establishes continuous direct-position semantics and the Lichess horizon.
2. Add the position-score read model and tree API with route canonicalization.
3. Extract production card/tree components from the prototype and replace `/openings`.
4. Migrate existing opening links/helpers and preserve named-root drill actions.
5. Remove obsolete page-grid code and, after parity review, the standalone prototype route.

Out of scope: multiple simultaneously expanded branches, editing/saving repertoires, arbitrary legal move exploration, engine-eval sorting, browsing full games beyond the opening boundary, and arbitrary-position drill targets.
acceptance_criteria:
## Behavior

- `/openings` renders the production horizontal selected-branch tree and synchronized board; only the deepest selected node is expanded.
- The URL stores `color` and the exact repeated UCI `move` line; reload, browser history, and copied links restore the same position.
- Invalid or stale lines are truncated to a backend-returned canonical line, and legacy `opening` links resolve to a deterministic book path.
- A single global segmented control labeled `Playing as: White | Black` switches perspective; it preserves the shared line where valid, flips board orientation, and changes side-specific metrics without combining both sides.
- Board drops select only API-listed structural moves; unlisted legal moves cannot desynchronize the board and tree.

## Graph domain

- Columns contain reference-book edges plus phase-valid observed off-book edges, not every legal move.
- Observed and reference-only branches terminate at the Lichess opening-to-middlegame horizon defined by `g-opening-score-v2`; the move entering the boundary remains visible as a terminal node.
- A no-evidence user still sees and can navigate the structural opening book with no-data metrics.
- Transposed routes share normalized-FEN metrics while retaining their distinct UCI navigation lines.

## Metrics and sorting

- Every returned node has direct position score fields with null representing no evidence; the API does not run one full score calculation per visible child.
- Compact cards show SAN, score, grade, opening name, and nullable selected-player-relative eval on two lines.
- Expanded cards show score/grade, eval, coverage, distinct game count, confidence, and terminal status for only the active global perspective, without an embedded board or a second perspective's score.
- A/B/C/D/F/no-data states have distinct accessible grade text and visual tokens; color is not the only signal.
- Games is backed by a distinct-session count, not `sample_size` relabeled as games.
- Each move-node eval comes from `analysis_cache` using `(parent_fen, move_uci)`, prefers `played_eval_mate` over `played_eval`, and is rendered from the selected perspective. Exact full-FEN matches win; normalized-FEN transposition fallback is indexed and deterministic. The starting root uses a cached `best_eval` only when a complete best-move row exists. Missing cache eval renders as an em dash and does not trigger per-column browser engine analysis or duplicate eval storage.
- User-turn and opponent-turn columns follow the documented relevance sort with deterministic tie-breaking; engine eval does not affect default ordering.
- Selected connectors encode grade, observed/book-only state, and clamped encounter-count thickness as documented.

## Drill and integration

- One action labeled `Start Drill` appears only for positions accepted by the existing named-root drill contract and starts with the global `Playing as` perspective; there are no side-specific drill button labels or duplicate White/Black actions.
- Existing named opening links and session-opening links continue to work during migration.
- The compact card body is reusable outside the tree without nesting interactive controls.

## Resilience and layout

- Initial load, no-data, page-level failure, missing eval, and child-column retry states are distinct.
- Stale async responses cannot replace a newer selected line or perspective.
- Desktop uses a viewport-bounded board/tree workspace with independent vertical column scrolling and horizontal tree scrolling.
- At `<=720px`, board and tree stack, the tree remains horizontally navigable, and page content is not clipped to enforce a no-scroll layout.

## Tests and quality gates

- Backend tests cover graph inclusion/exclusion, phase-boundary terminals, observed off-book edges, transpositions, canonical URL lines, direct position metrics, null evidence, sorting, exact and normalized analysis-cache lookup, cp/mate perspective conversion, cache-miss handling, and drill-root flags.
- Frontend behavior tests cover node selection/truncation, board-to-tree sync, URL restoration/canonicalization, perspective switching, compact/expanded states, loading/error recovery, no-data navigation, and drill navigation.
- Tests avoid exact connector coordinates, cosmetic copy, and pixel-level layout assertions.
- Focused backend tests, frontend test suite, and production build pass; SPEC.md is updated to describe the implemented tree and route/API contracts.

title: Align blunders page with Ghost-ready priority
description: Expand the Blunders page/API from a sorting-only change into a gameplay-aligned priority surface. The page should make its primary count, filter, and ordering match what Ghost gameplay can reasonably deliver, using Ghost-ready / practice-priority signals rather than broad SRS Due or recency. SRS due remains available as secondary metadata, but should not imply a target is steerable.
design:
Data flow and implementation plan:

1. Relationship to g-ghost-srs-policy
- This issue implements the accepted direction from g-ghost-srs-policy for the Blunders page and /api/blunder list endpoint.
- Scope is UI/API alignment, not a new gameplay steering policy.
- Actual in-game steerability remains position-dependent and owned by /api/game find_ghost_move.
- This issue depends on g-ghost-srs-policy so the policy decision lands before implementation.

2. Shared policy helpers
- Extract the durable ghost eligibility and durable scoring pieces from backend/app/api/game.py into a shared backend module such as app.srs_policy or app.srs_opportunity.
- Shared helpers should cover:
  - srs_due / due_priority from existing SRS semantics.
  - ghost_eligible using the same persistent eligibility rule as find_ghost_move.
  - practice_priority_score as a position-independent approximation of Ghost selection priority.
- /api/game should use the shared ghost_eligible helper so gameplay and the library cannot drift.
- /api/blunder should use the same helper for list fields, filtering, and ordering.

3. Preserve existing SRS meaning
- Keep srs_priority as the existing SRS due value. Do not repurpose it as the new sort score.
- Add explicit fields instead of overloading existing ones:
  - srs_due: boolean, derived from srs_priority > 1.0.
  - ghost_eligible: boolean, based on shared gameplay-aligned eligibility.
  - practice_priority_score: global approximation used for default ordering.
  - reached_since_review: expose if useful for backend tests and detail UI explanation; otherwise keep API-only/internal.
- Existing opportunity counters remain available: opportunities_since_review, opportunities_30d, reached_30d.

4. Practice priority score
- Sort by practice_priority_score descending by default.
- The score should mirror durable parts of GhostMoveCandidate.score:
  - urgency based on exact-reach policy for opportunity-tracked targets, or time fallback when no opportunity events exist.
  - severity using the same log-scaled eval loss normalizer.
  - reach_weight using smoothed p_reach when opportunity events exist.
- Explicitly omit current-position/session factors:
  - distance from current FEN.
  - first-move grouping and aggregation.
  - repeat penalties for recently repeated moves from the same FEN.
  - current opening-family match.
  - weighted random seed/session behavior.
- Recency should be used only as a deterministic tiebreaker.

5. /api/blunder behavior
- Normal mode should load/enrich/sort by practice_priority_score before pagination.
- due=true can be retained for compatibility, but it remains SRS-due semantics and should not be the primary UI path.
- Add a gameplay-aligned filter option such as ghost_ready=true or practice_ready=true if the UI needs a primary filter.
- If both due and ghost-ready filters exist, response fields and docs must make their difference explicit.
- Preserve total/due_total semantics for existing due=true behavior unless deliberately replaced with a new response field.

6. Blunders page UX
- Replace the primary Due count/toggle with a gameplay-aligned primary state.
- Default list order follows practice_priority_score from the API.
- SRS Due, last seen, streak, and opportunity/reach data become secondary details on cards or the detail pane.
- Avoid UI text that implies every SRS-due target is steerable in normal gameplay.
- The library page should describe a global practice signal, not exact current-game ghost selection.

7. Implementation choices carried from g-ghost-srs-policy
- Final label choice is an implementation decision. Prefer Ghost-ready if emphasizing live gameplay, or Practice-ready if emphasizing study/library usage. Use Practice priority for the ordering concept.
- Decide whether to keep a visible Due-only filter. If kept, demote it behind the gameplay-aligned filter and label it as SRS due / due for review, not ghost-ready.
- Prefer exposing srs_due explicitly from the API for clarity, even though it can be derived from srs_priority. This makes client code and tests less dependent on the exact threshold expression.
- Decide whether reached_since_review is visible in detail UI or API/test-only. It is useful for explaining why a broad SRS-due target is not Ghost-ready.
- Pick one primary filter/query name during implementation: ghost_ready=true if using Ghost-ready copy, or practice_ready=true if using Practice-ready copy. Avoid supporting both unless there is a compatibility reason.

8. Tests
Backend:
- Shared helper tests cover exact reach eligibility, broad opportunity with zero reach, low p_reach suppression, no-opportunity fallback, and threshold boundaries.
- /api/game tests prove find_ghost_move uses shared eligibility and still suppresses high-opportunity zero-reach targets.
- /api/blunder tests prove normal ordering uses practice_priority_score, not recency or raw srs_priority.
- /api/blunder tests prove Ghost-ready/practice-ready filtering can differ from SRS due filtering.
- /api/blunder tests preserve srs_priority as the due/filtering value.

Frontend:
- API fixtures/types include new fields.
- Blunders page tests assert the primary count/filter uses ghost_eligible or practice-ready data.
- Tests should focus on behavior/data flow, not exact copy/layout.

Out of scope:
- Changing the fundamental in-game steering policy beyond extracting and reusing the current helper.
- Claiming exact current-position Ghost selection likelihood on the generic Blunders page.
- Large DB/materialized-score optimization unless current library size makes Python-side enrichment impractical.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-04 (pending review).

CHOICES MADE:
- Labels: Practice-ready copy + Practice priority ordering. Primary filter query name: practice_ready=true.
- Kept due=true filter for compatibility, demoted to secondary (SRS-due semantics, recency order).
- Exposed srs_due, ghost_eligible, practice_priority_score, reached_since_review explicitly on list items.

SHARED MODULE (app/srs_opportunity.py):

title: show a couple of rows below selection in MoveList
description:
When navigating down the MoveList, either with the keyboard or the navigation buttons, keep the focused item visible with a scroll margin so there are 2 items below it.

design:
# Plan: show a couple of rows below selection in MoveList (g-dfmz)

## Goal
When navigating the MoveList (keyboard ← / → or the nav buttons), keep ~2 rows of
context visible *below* the focused move/ply. Currently a selection that scrolls
to the bottom edge sits flush against the viewport bottom. We want a bottom
scroll margin of 2 target-heights — but size-aware: if the viewport is too short
to fit the margin, the selected item's own visibility wins over the margin.

## Where the logic lives
All scroll math is in `src/components/MoveList.tsx`:
- `scrollMoveListTargetIntoView(container, target, stickyInset, behavior)`
  (~lines 88-115) is the shared chokepoint, called from THREE effects:
  1. move auto-scroll (~268) — target = selected move button → **wants margin**
  2. variation-ply auto-scroll (~291) — target = `.variation-ply--selected`,
     navigated with the same keys/buttons → **wants margin**
  3. message auto-scroll (~312) — target = last `.move-bubble` → **NO margin**
     (a bubble is not a navigated target and can be much taller than a row;
     applying 2× its height would cause a large smooth-scroll jump).

Because the three callers need different behavior, the margin must be a
**parameter of the helper**, not unconditional logic inside it.

## Target-height interpretation
"2 rows below" is interpreted as `2 * targetRect.height` of the *current target*.
- For the move path, `selectedMoveRef` is the move button (`src/components/MoveRow.tsx:176`),
  whose height we read directly via `targetRect.height` (`.move-button` is
  styled at App.css:3245 and has no explicit min-height; its height comes from
  content/grid row), so this is effectively "2 move rows below".
- For the variation path the target is the selected ply span, so it is "2 ply
  heights below" — close enough and self-consistent; we do not try to measure a
  canonical row height. This nuance is intentional and acceptable.

## Implementation

### 1. Add a constant (near lines 58-61)
`const MOVE_LIST_ROWS_BELOW_SELECTION = 2;`

### 2. Parameterize the helper
Add an optional `rowsBelow = 0` parameter:
```
const scrollMoveListTargetIntoView = (
  container, target, stickyInset, behavior, rowsBelow = 0,
) => {
  ...existing rect math...
  const visibleHeight = Math.max(0, container.clientHeight - stickyInset);

  if (targetRect.height > visibleHeight) {            // oversized: top-align, no margin
    setMoveListScrollTop(container, targetTop - stickyInset, behavior);
    return;
  }

  if (targetTop < visibleTop) {                        // top-clip: unchanged (asymmetric)
    setMoveListScrollTop(container, targetTop - stickyInset, behavior);
    return;
  }

  // bottom-clip: apply size-aware margin
  const desiredMargin = targetRect.height * rowsBelow;
  const margin = Math.min(desiredMargin, Math.max(0, visibleHeight - targetRect.height));
  if (targetBottom + margin > visibleBottom) {
    setMoveListScrollTop(container, targetBottom + margin - container.clientHeight, behavior);
  }
};
```
- `rowsBelow = 0` reproduces today's exact behavior (margin term is 0).
- Size-aware clamp: `min(desiredMargin, visibleHeight - targetHeight)` ensures the
  margin can never push the target's top above the visible top — implements the
  issue's "visibility of the selected item takes priority" rule. On a very short
  viewport the clamp drives margin → 0.
- `setMoveListScrollTop` already clamps to `>= 0`, so no top over-scroll.

### 3. Update the three call sites
- Move effect (~280): pass `MOVE_LIST_ROWS_BELOW_SELECTION`.
- Variation effect (~298): pass `MOVE_LIST_ROWS_BELOW_SELECTION`.
- Message effect (~328): pass `0` (or omit) — message scroll behavior unchanged.

### Upward scroll — left asymmetric (out of scope)
Top-clip stays aligned just below the sticky header; the issue only asks for rows
*below* the selection. Navigating *up* into a top-clipped row already exposes rows
below it, so the intent is naturally met in that direction.

## Tests (`src/components/MoveList.test.tsx`)
Reuse the existing harness (`setMoveListScrollMetrics`, `mockTargetRect`,
`installAnimationFrameQueue`).

Expectations that WILL change with this plan:
- **Variation ply test (line ~346, currently asserts `top: 54`)**: now gets the
  margin, so the expected `scrollTo` top increases by the clamped margin. Update
  the expected value to match `targetBottom + margin - clientHeight` for that
  fixture (clientHeight 120, header 32 → visibleHeight 88; ply height 24 →
  desiredMargin 48; clamp max = 88-24 = 64 → margin 48). Recompute and update.

Expectations that must STAY unchanged:
- **Message bubble test (line ~381)**: message path passes `rowsBelow = 0`, so
  its assertion must remain exactly as today. Verify it still passes — this is
  the regression guard for finding #1.
- **Top-clip move test (~line 315)**: unchanged (top-clip branch untouched).

New cases to add under `describe('MoveList auto-scroll')`:
1. **Move margin applied when room exists**: tall viewport, select a move whose
   row is just below the visible bottom; assert `scrollTo` top ==
   `targetBottom + 2*rowHeight - clientHeight`.
2. **Move margin clamped on short viewport**: clientHeight ≈ 1.5 rows; assert the
   selected row is fully visible (top >= sticky inset) and margin collapses
   toward 0 (selection visibility prioritized).
3. **Oversized target**: target taller than visibleHeight → top-aligned, no
   margin (early return path).

## Files touched
- `src/components/MoveList.tsx` — constant, `rowsBelow` param on the helper,
  pass-throughs at the move + variation call sites (message site passes 0).
- `src/components/MoveList.test.tsx` — update variation assertion, keep message
  assertion, add the new move-margin cases.

## Risk / notes
- Pure scroll-offset math; no DOM/CSS change.
- Default `rowsBelow = 0` keeps the message path and any future caller safe.
- Only the bottom-clip branch changes; top-clip and oversized paths preserved.
close_reason: Implemented size-aware bottom scroll margin (2 rows) below MoveList selection

description:
In analysis board use the same eval icons as the MoveList to label the moves on the board. Place the icon in a circle at the top right of the square where the piece was moved to but somehwat ooutside the boundary of the square.

If the board's square is 100x100px then the icon circle's diameter should be 40px and it's center point would be 8x8 pixels from the top right.

design:
# Plan: g-q810 — Move eval icons on analysis board

## Context
The analysis board's MoveList already shows classification icons (⭐ ! ?! ? ??) next to each move. The feature request is to also render those icons directly on the board as circular badges at the destination square of the currently displayed move. The issue spec defines exact sizing and edge-case rules.

## What we're building
A non-interactive overlay inside the board frame that shows a single icon badge for the current move's classification (skipping "good" moves and skipping when in a variation).

---

## Implementation

### 1. Position math (pure, no DOM measurement needed)

The board fills 100% × 100% of `.analysis-board__board-frame`. Each square is 12.5% of board width/height.

```
file: a=0, b=1, …, h=7   (from square name: charCode - 97)
rank: 1–8                 (from square name: parseInt char 1)
```

**White orientation:**
- squareLeft = file × 12.5%
- squareTop  = (8 − rank) × 12.5%

**Black orientation:**
- squareLeft = (7 − file) × 12.5%
- squareTop  = (rank − 1) × 12.5%

**Icon sizing (issue spec at 100px squares = 40% of square = 5% of board):**
- diameter = 5%,  radius = 2.5%
- "8×8 pixels from the top right" = center is 8px inward from the square's top-right corner; the 40px badge then protrudes ~12px past the corner ("somewhat outside")
- Default center: `squareLeft + 11.5%`, `squareTop + 1%`  (12.5% - 1% = 11.5% from square's left; 1% from square's top — both in board-% units where 1% ≈ 8px at a 100px square)
- Right-edge column (visual right): mirror to top-left — `squareLeft + 1%`, `squareTop + 1%`
- Top-edge row (visual top): center Y clamped to `max(top, 2.5%)` so icon stays inside board

Edge detection:
- `isRightEdge`: white → file === 7; black → file === 0
- `isTopEdge`:   white → rank === 8; black → rank === 1

### 2. Source data

**Destination square**: reuse `mainLineMoveDetails[effectiveIndex]?.playedSquares?.to` (line 938 pattern in AnalysisBoard.tsx). This already uses `sanToSquares` + the correct FEN-before; do not recompute.

**Icon data**: `CLASSIFICATION_ICON` in `MoveRow.tsx` (line 39) is not currently exported. Before importing it in AnalysisBoard.tsx, export it:
```ts
// MoveRow.tsx
export const CLASSIFICATION_ICON: Partial<...> = { ... };
```
Then import in AnalysisBoard.tsx.

Skip rendering if:
- `isInVariation` is true (variations lack classification)
- `effectiveIndex < 0` or out of bounds
- `classification` is null, "good", or not in `CLASSIFICATION_ICON`

### 3. Files to change

**`src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`**
- Add a `boardEvalIcon` useMemo that returns `{ square: string; icon: string; title: string } | null`
- Render a `<div className="board-eval-icons">` as a sibling after `<Chessboard>` inside `.analysis-board__board-frame`, containing a single icon circle div with inline `left`/`top` styles

**`src/App.css`**
- Add `position: relative` to `.analysis-board__board-frame`
- Add `.board-eval-icons` (absolute, inset 0, pointer-events none, z-index 5)
- Add `.board-eval-icon` (absolute, circle shape, centered via `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)`, small bold text, background matching the classification color from existing `move-icon--*` palette)

### 4. Icon styling

Reuse classification color tokens already defined for `.move-icon--blunder`, `.move-icon--mistake`, etc. in App.css. The board badge will use the same background/color mapping via a `data-classification` attribute or class modifier.

Diameter: 5% of board container (responds to board resize automatically).  
Font-size: ~2% of board (scales with badge).  
Background/color: match existing move-icon palette.

### 5. No show for "good"

The `CLASSIFICATION_ICON` map includes "good" with `✓`. We explicitly exclude `classification === "good"` before rendering.

---

## Verification

### Unit tests (`src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx`)
Add focused tests for the `boardEvalIcon` logic (extract as a pure helper to make it testable):
- Renders badge for non-good classifications (blunder, mistake, inaccuracy, best, excellent)
- Skips badge when `classification === "good"` or null
- Skips badge when `isInVariation === true`
- Correct `left`/`top` for default position (center protrudes past top-right corner)
- Correct `left`/`top` for right-edge (file h white / file a black) — mirrors to top-left
- Correct `top` clamped to radius for top-edge rank (rank 8 white / rank 1 black)
- Correct coordinates flip when `boardOrientation === "black"`

### Browser smoke check
1. Open analysis board on any reviewed game
2. Navigate moves — each blunder/mistake/inaccuracy/best/excellent move should show the badge at its destination square, protruding past the corner
3. Good moves: no badge
4. h-file moves (white) or a-file moves (black): badge appears at top-left corner instead
5. Top-rank moves: badge stays within board, not clipped
6. Flip board: badges update immediately
7. Enter a variation: badge disappears; return to main line: reappears
close_reason: Implemented move eval icon badges on analysis board

title: Playwright screenshot tests
description: Create Playwright tests that generate screenshots of app pages across 3 viewports (mobile/tablet/desktop). First pass covers a FIXED inventory of states per page (loading/error/empty/populated plus the seeded review-warning toast on /play) — see design field for the exact per-page state list and API mocks. Output is a reviewable contact-sheet gallery, not pixel-diff assertions. Harder live-game overlays and visual-regression diffing are tracked as follow-up beads.
design:
# Plan: Playwright screenshot tests for all pages/states (g-tsyy)

## Goal
A dedicated Playwright suite that captures deterministic screenshots of every app page across
3 viewports, in a FIXED first-pass inventory of UI states. Output is a reviewable gallery
(contact sheet), NOT pixel-diff assertions. Hard live-game states are scoped out to follow-up beads.

## Approach: screenshot gallery (not snapshot assertions)
- New spec dir `e2e/screenshots/`. Suite runs SERIAL (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })`)
  because playwright.config.ts has `fullyParallel: true` — parallel workers would race on the
  shared output dir / index generation.
- Each test: `page.screenshot({ path: output/<viewport>/<page>-<state>.png })` AND
  `testInfo.attach(...)` the PNG so it shows in the Playwright HTML report (raw path screenshots
  do NOT auto-appear in the report otherwise).
- A generated `output/index.html` contact sheet is the explicit human-review artifact, written
  ONCE in a final `afterAll` (or a separate ordered last test) — not per-test, to avoid the race.
- No `toHaveScreenshot()` pixel-diffing this pass (board/graphs/dates non-deterministic).
- Add `e2e/screenshots/output/` to .gitignore (currently only report/test-results/blob-report
  are ignored at .gitignore:37).

## Viewports (confirmed)
Six viewports, chosen to exercise the app's actual breakpoints (App.css:1305/2941/4999/5036/5067/5567),
not just generic device buckets. Iterate via `page.setViewportSize`.
- 390x844  — primary mobile (hits <=720, <=767)
- 360x640  — narrow + short mobile (hits <=720, <=767, <=760h, <=680h: mobile warning stack + short-screen chrome)
- 740x900  — KEY mixed band: /play game is mobile (<=767) but nav/analysis are desktop (>720)
- 820x1180 — tablet
- 1024x640 — tablet/desktop SHORT height (hits <=1099 intermediate game layout + history/analysis max-height:640 rule)
- 1440x900 — desktop
Note: not every page needs all 6 — pages with no responsive variance in a band can reuse one capture.
Helper exposes per-page viewport subsets to avoid redundant shots (e.g. auth/landing don't need 1024x640).

## Determinism controls
- Freeze clock via `addInitScript` (due-dates, stats windows, rating graph depend on it).
- Disable animations: inject `*{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}` before snap.
- Seeded accounts (e2e/fixtures/accounts.ts): due / stable / empty for populated vs empty states.
- Wait on explicit state locators (below) — no fixed sleeps.
- AUTH INIT: with no token, AuthContext.tsx:249 auto-registers an ANONYMOUS account; AppNav.tsx:106
  branches on `user.isAnonymous`. So "logged-out" is really the ANONYMOUS/default state — wait for
  auth initialization to settle before capturing nav.

## Per-page API mocks (exact)
Error states are forced with `page.route('**/api/...', r => r.fulfill({ status, body }))`.
- /game (GameAnalysisPage): requires id — GameAnalysisPage.tsx:101 redirects to /play when missing.
  Use `/game?id=<seeded session_id>` (or mock analysis). Error needs a NON-RETRYABLE response:
  GameAnalysisPage.tsx:53 polls on retryable errors, so a plain 500 won't show error. Fulfill with
  a 4xx ApiError-non-retryable shape (e.g. 403/404) to hit the terminal error branch.
- /stats: mock BOTH `/api/stats/summary` (StatsPage.tsx:77) AND rating history
  (RatingGraph.tsx:195 `fetchRatingHistory`) as a PAIR per state, else summary can be populated
  while the graph still loads/errors.
- /history, /blunders, /openings: seed-user driven for empty/populated; route-500 for error;
  route-delay for loading.

## Page + state inventory (FIXED first pass)

| Route | States |
|-------|--------|
| `/` | anonymous/default (Register/Login nav), authed (seed user) |
| `/login` | empty form, validation error (`.auth-form__error`) |
| `/register` | empty form, password-mismatch error |
| `/history` | loading, empty (empty user), populated + selected analysis, error |
| `/blunders` | loading, empty, populated (due user), due-only filter, selected+analysis, error |
| `/openings` | loading, no-evidence empty, computed-snapshot empty, populated tree, structural-leaf empty, error |
| `/stats` | loading, empty-window, populated, error (both mocks) |
| `/game?id=` | loading, processing, populated, terminal error (non-retryable), missing-color error |
| `/play` | fresh board, mid-game live + review-warning toast (FIRST PASS) |

### Play overlay states — explicit drivers
- review-warning toast / live board: reachable via real moves, reuse helpers from
  mobile-game-layout.spec.ts:51 (seeded review path). INCLUDE in first pass.
- promotion picker: `requiresPromotion` branch at ChessGame.tsx:986 — needs a real pawn-promotion
  move sequence or backend mock. SCOPED OUT to follow-up bead (g-tsyy-play-overlays).
- review-fail modal + spotlight: ChessGame.tsx:1316 `handleRevealSrsFail` — separate branch needing
  a failed SRS drill. SCOPED OUT to follow-up bead.
- game-end banner, drill overlay: SCOPED OUT to follow-up bead (require longer live-game scripting).

## State-locator reference (in code)
- history: `.history-shell__error`, `.history-shell__empty`, `No games played yet`
- blunders: `Blunder Library` heading, `Blunder library` listbox, `No blunders recorded yet`, `.blunders-shell__error`
- openings: `.openings-state--loading/--error`, `No opening evidence...`, `No scored openings...`
- stats: `.stats-shell__error`, `.stats-shell__empty`, window buttons
- gameAnalysis: `.history-shell__error`, processing indicator, missing-color text
- auth: `.auth-form__error`
- play: `.game-status-badge--live`, `.review-warning-toast`

## File structure
```
e2e/screenshots/
  pages.screens.spec.ts   # serial; describe per page, parametrized over states
  helpers.ts              # viewports[], freezeClock(), killAnimations(), captureState(), buildIndex()
  output/                 # gitignored PNGs + index.html
```

## Output / review

title: Add ghost move selection variability
description: Ghost targeting became overly concentrated after opportunity-aware SRS scoring. Add player-volume-neutral variability so repeated games do not collapse into the same line while preserving opportunity-aware prioritization.
design:
# g-ghost-variety Plan

## Summary
Add player-volume-neutral variety to backend ghost move selection in backend/app/api/game.py by changing selection from top-k individual blunders to weighted first-move lottery, then weighted target lottery. Preserve the existing due gate and opportunity-aware scoring. Implement the same-FEN repeat penalty using existing uploaded session_moves history with a bounded best-effort scan, not a migration.

## Key Changes
- Keep the current recursive CTE and GhostMoveCandidate.score() inputs: SRS priority, opportunity overdue, severity, distance, reach probability, and opening-family weighting remain unchanged.
- After filtering to due candidates (priority >= 1.0), dedupe repeated path rows by (first_move, blunder_id) before grouping. If duplicate rows exist from transpositions, keep the row with the highest computed score; use stable tie-breaks so duplicates cannot inflate secondary aggregate score.
- Group deduped scored candidates by first_move.
- For each first-move group, compute an aggregate score as max(candidate_score) plus a small secondary contribution from distinct remaining candidates, e.g. 0.15 * sum(other_scores).
- Apply score flattening before random choice: weight = sqrt(max(score, 0)) for first-move selection and for final target selection inside the chosen first-move group.
- Replace current TOP_K behavior with first-move top-k: sort first-move groups by penalized aggregate score, sample among the top TOP_K first moves, then sample among candidates for the selected first move.
- Add small pure helper functions in game.py for path-row dedupe, grouping, aggregate scoring, weight flattening, repeat penalties, and deterministic weighted choice.

## Same-FEN Repeat Penalty
- Reuse existing session_moves plus game_sessions; do not add a migration.
- Because session_moves has no fen_before or decision_source index, do not scan unbounded user history. Query only a bounded number of recent uploaded ghost decisions for the user, e.g. REPEAT_HISTORY_SCAN_LIMIT = 200, where session_moves.decision_source = 'ghost_path' and fen_before is not null, joined through game_sessions.user_id.
- Order the bounded scan by recent sessions and move order, e.g. game_sessions.started_at desc, session_moves.id desc or equivalent stable recency ordering available in the model.
- Normalize matching in Python with existing fen_hash(): compare fen_hash(session_moves.fen_before) to fen_hash(current_fen).
- Skip invalid stored fen_before values by catching ValueError from fen_hash(), matching the defensive pattern in _compute_blunder_opportunity_events(). A legacy bad row must not break ghost selection.
- From the bounded recent scan, collect only the first REPEAT_PENALTY_LOOKBACK matching decisions for the exact normalized FEN, e.g. REPEAT_PENALTY_LOOKBACK = 3.
- Penalize repeated first moves multiplicatively with factors such as 0.35x for the most recent same-FEN repeat, then 0.60x and 0.80x for older repeats. Multiple appearances use a deterministic rule, preferably multiplying applicable factors in recency order.
- This is explicitly best-effort: if the last few exact normalized-FEN decisions are older than the bounded scan window, no repeat penalty applies. Do not use wall-clock windows, last N games, or global recent history as the penalty definition.

## Determinism and Fallbacks
- Preserve seeded deterministic behavior by sorting before every seeded random. First-move groups use stable tie-breaks such as (-penalized_score, first_move). Candidates inside a chosen group use stable tie-breaks such as (-score, depth, -eval_loss_cp, -blunder_id, first_move).
- If all flattened first-move weights are zero, choose the first item from the stable first-move ordering.
- If all flattened target-candidate weights inside the chosen group are zero, choose the first item from the stable candidate ordering.
- Keep existing _rng_seed/session_id seed behavior so identical inputs and repeat-history rows produce identical choices.

## Public Interfaces
- No frontend API or response shape changes.
- No database migration.
- find_ghost_move() keeps the same return type.
- Internal constants may be added in backend/app/api/game.py: FIRST_MOVE_SECONDARY_WEIGHT, SELECTION_WEIGHT_POWER, REPEAT_HISTORY_SCAN_LIMIT, REPEAT_PENALTY_LOOKBACK, REPEAT_PENALTY_FACTORS.

## Test Plan
- Add backend unit tests around find_ghost_move() and helper functions in backend/test_game_api.py.
- Cover candidate grouping and dedupe: multiple due blunders behind one first move and one due blunder behind another first move produce one lottery slot per first move; duplicate (first_move, blunder_id) rows from transpositions do not increase aggregate score.
- Cover aggregate scoring: distinct duplicate downstream targets help slightly but do not dominate.
- Cover flattened weights: verify selection uses sqrt(score) or helper output equivalent, not raw scores.
- Cover same-FEN repeat penalty: prior uploaded ghost_path decisions from the same normalized FEN reduce that first move's selection weight; decisions from a different FEN do not; FENs differing only in halfmove/fullmove counters still match.
- Cover bounded best-effort behavior: decisions outside REPEAT_HISTORY_SCAN_LIMIT are ignored, and the query is bounded.
- Cover invalid history rows: invalid stored fen_before values are skipped and do not raise out of find_ghost_move().
- Cover deterministic ordering and zero-weight fallback for both first-move and target-candidate lotteries.
- Preserve existing opportunity-aware SRS, deterministic seed, and due-gate tests.
acceptance_criteria: Ghost selection groups candidates by first_move before weighted random choice. Weighted selection uses flattened weights rather than raw scores. A same-normalized-FEN repeat penalty reduces recently chosen first moves for that FEN without using wall-clock windows. Tests cover multiple blunders pointing to one move, score flattening/selection inputs, and same-FEN repeat penalty behavior. Existing opportunity-aware SRS tests continue to pass.
notes: Implemented first-move grouped ghost selection with path-row dedupe, sqrt-flattened weighted lotteries, bounded same-FEN repeat penalties from uploaded ghost_path session_moves, and focused backend coverage. Validation: cd backend && mkdir -p .tmp && source .venv/bin/activate && TMPDIR=/Users/mvargas/src/ghostreplay/backend/.tmp PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 pytest -p no:cacheprovider test_game_api.py test_srs_priority.py test_srs_opportunity.py test_opening_cache.py test_session_api.py test_analysis_cache_api.py -q => 139 passed.
close_reason: Implemented first-move grouped ghost selection variability with flattened weighted lotteries, same-FEN repeat penalties, and backend coverage.

Summary
Add a tiered, CSS-driven fire treatment to the existing PerfectStreakBadge in GameInfoPanel. The badge layout box stays stable, but the fire uses a larger aura that can visibly extend beyond the pill so the effect reads clearly at long streaks.

Key Changes
- Add a typed intensity helper from perfectStreak.current: none <3, ember 3-4, flame 5-7, hot 8-11, inferno >=12.
- Derive intensity only from the existing frontend streak state already passed into GameInfoPanel.
- Render data-fire-intensity on .perfect-streak-badge.
- Add internal aria-hidden aura/flame and ember/spark layers, plus a foreground content wrapper for the current star, Streak, and count.
- Preserve the accessible label: Perfect streak current, best personalBest.

Layout And Visual Rules
- Badge layout dimensions must not change when tiers change.
- Use position: relative, isolation: isolate, and visible overflow on the badge.
- Desktop flame/aura may extend about 14-22px above and 8-14px horizontally. Mobile caps extension to about 10-14px above and 6-8px horizontally.
- Keep the mobile badge flex basis at 4.4rem; fire must not increase row height or push matchup text.
- Use z-index only inside the badge; no toast, board, or modal z-index changes.
- Animation uses only transform, opacity, and filter/drop-shadow.
- prefers-reduced-motion disables continuous flame/spark motion and leaves a static glow/color treatment.

Styling Approach
- Tiers tune CSS custom properties for aura size/opacity, flame height/scale, ember visibility, animation duration, and glow intensity.
- Ember is mostly glow plus tiny drift; flame adds visible flame licks; hot increases height/glow/embers; inferno adds a brighter yellow/white core and occasional sparks.

Tests
