title: create drill mode epic
description:
Drill mode allows users to practice openings by playing an opening until they make a mistake. Drill mode has the following features:

- To start user selects a color, an opening, an engine difficulty, and strictness.

- When selecting the opening they specify the exact root position.

- The strictness defines what is considered a mistake at which point the drill ends. The user can specify how many centipawns below the best move is allowed. This is a slider that goes from perfect to -50 centipawns.

- Drill mode ends when either the user fails to cooperate with the ghost to reach the desired opening position or if they make a mistake.

- The ghost first steers to the selected opening, if the user's moves prevents ghost steering from reaching the selected opening it ends and shows the user the right move. 

- When they make a mistake, by playing a move below their selected strictness, the drill stops and it shows what would have been the correct moves using multiple arrows on the board, similar to analysis board's multiple arrows, but in green and also showing the wrong move arrow in red like the blunder arrow.

- After the user reaches the desired opening the SRS stuff works the same as in regular games, meaning either the ghost steers or the selected engine makes a move. the same SRS warning and info boxes are shown in the panel and MoveList. SRS success/failure is recorded the same as regular games. 

- When drill mode ends the user get to decide to do another drill or to continue the current game. If they go to another drill the opening, engine, and strictness selection is sticky from the previous drill but they can change them. If they want to continue the current game it proceeds as a normal game.
 
- Drill mode does not affect the user's elo rating. But if they continue playing the game then it will be rated as usual.

- Drills are not shown in history or analysis unless the user continues it as a normal game.
design: Parent epic for drill mode. Implementation is split into nine independently reviewable phase beads: product policy, backend contract, setup UX, pre-opening steering, post-opening continuation, strictness detection, end flow, history/rating/analysis policy enforcement, and focused tests. Each child bead should keep changes scoped to its phase and preserve the acceptance criteria captured here.
notes:
Patched drill strictness bug: active drills now fail on analyzed player move upload when eval_delta exceeds strictness, session move upload reports drill failure state, and frontend stops active drills on both analysis resolution and upload-confirmed failure. Verified with test_drill_api.py, GameAnalysisCoordinator.test.ts, and npm run build.
Code review follow-up: hoisted drill strictness threshold resolver into session_contracts.py, stored the started drill strictness_cp in Zustand, changed analysis-resolution checks to use captured session threshold, added stale/revert guards, hardened upload-response handling against non-active drills/missing terminal reason, and replaced the single analysis callback with add/remove listeners. Re-verified drill API, coordinator/api vitest, ChessGame vitest, and npm build.
Second review follow-up: simplified redundant move UCI expression in the ChessGame drill accuracy listener and added a focused ChessGame test asserting that an active drill stops when resolved player analysis exceeds the captured strictness threshold. Re-verified ChessGame vitest and npm build.
Policy amendment 2026-06-01: continued drills should be treated as one full normal game. Do not require drill-prefix demarcation for history, analysis summaries, CPL, blunder counts, stats, achievements, comparable user metrics, or PGN/export. Pre-continue drill uploads and analyses should feed regular opening evidence, passive blunder opportunities, blunder/SRS creation, analysis-cache side effects, streaks, and achievements. Uncontinued drills remain unrated and hidden from history/session-analysis lists.

title: MoveList navigation bugs
description: in MoveList, when there is a long list of moves and I click 'Go to starting postion' it doesn't scroll to make the first move cell visible. Also, When at the starting position it highlights a nonexistent cell above row 1. Also, when navigating to the top visible row it doesn't scroll the cell into view because half of it is covere up by the label row 'You | Engine'.
design: Revised plan for g-x1fg: do not assume the start-position bug comes from a fake selected row, because current main-line selection is already bounded to real move buttons via whiteIdx/blackIdx === effectiveIndex in MoveList and the selected ref/class only land on actual MoveRow buttons. Step 1 is to verify the exact browser symptom in the ConnectedMoveList/game-mode path and identify whether the reported highlight above row 1 is a true selected-state bug, a sticky-header overlap artifact, or the player-column tint/sticky grid presenting as a phantom cell. Scope: the user-facing bug here is the game MoveList path used by ConnectedMoveList, where no variation props are passed, so currentIndex = -1 means plain starting position with no start-variation rows above move 1. Implementation plan: keep currentIndex/viewIndex = -1 as the start sentinel, and fix the missing scroll by handling the no-target case explicitly when navigation lands on -1. For game mode, that means scrolling .move-list-scroll to its top content position so the first move row is visible. Separately, replace raw scrollIntoView(nearest) for selected move rows with header-aware scrolling that measures the sticky occlusion zone from the rendered .move-list-header cells inside .move-list-scroll and ensures a target row sitting at the top edge is repositioned below that inset plus a small gutter. title: Add request/response logging middleware
description: Add ASGI middleware that logs HTTP requests and responses in a controlled, redacted way.
design:
## HTTP Logging Middleware Plan

### Files
- NEW: backend/app/http_logging.py — pure ASGI middleware class
- NEW: backend/test_http_logging.py — tests
- EDIT: backend/app/main.py — register HTTPLoggingMiddleware as outermost middleware

### Middleware registration order
Add HTTPLoggingMiddleware last in main.py (making it outermost):

  app.add_middleware(AuthMiddleware, ...)      # innermost
  app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...)
  app.add_middleware(HTTPLoggingMiddleware)    # outermost — sees final status + user

Execution order: HTTPLoggingMiddleware → CORSMiddleware → AuthMiddleware → ExceptionMiddleware → routes.

---

### http_logging.py

Class: HTTPLoggingMiddleware — pure ASGI (__call__(scope, receive, send)), NOT BaseHTTPMiddleware.

#### Logging output
Configure a dedicated _JsonFormatter on the ghostreplay.http logger at module level with propagate=False:

  class _JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
      def format(self, record):
          return json.dumps({'level': record.levelname, **getattr(record, 'http', {})})

  _handler = logging.StreamHandler()
  _handler.setFormatter(_JsonFormatter())
  logger = logging.getLogger('ghostreplay.http')
  logger.addHandler(_handler)
  logger.propagate = False

caplog does not hook propagate=False loggers. Tests use a dedicated http_log fixture (see below).

#### Per-request fields always logged (via extra={'http': {...}}):
  request_id (uuid4), method, path, query (redacted), status_code, duration_ms, user_id

#### Query string redaction
Do NOT log raw query strings. Parse with urllib.parse.parse_qsl, redact values for keys whose
lowercase name contains password/token/secret/jwt, then re-encode. Log the redacted result.

#### State access in raw ASGI
AuthMiddleware writes request.state.user = payload, which stores to scope['state']['user']
(scope['state'] is a plain dict). Correct access:

  user = scope.get('state', {}).get('user')
  user_id = getattr(user, 'user_id', None)

#### send_wrapper — always active, body accumulation conditional
The send_wrapper MUST be active on every request regardless of LOG_HTTP_BODY. Capturing
status_code requires inspecting http.response.start, which only arrives via send. If send
is passed through unmodified when LOG_HTTP_BODY=false, all normal 200/401/422 responses
have no captured status and acceptance criterion 1 fails.

Structure:

  res_status = [None]
  res_body_chunks = []
  body_truncated = False
  body_byte_total = 0

  async def send_wrapper(message):
      nonlocal body_truncated, body_byte_total
      if message['type'] == 'http.response.start':
          res_status[0] = message['status']          # always
      elif message['type'] == 'http.response.body' and log_body:
          chunk = message.get('body', b'')
          body_byte_total += len(chunk)
          if body_byte_total <= BODY_BUFFER_CAP:     # only when body logging enabled
              res_body_chunks.append(chunk)
          else:
              body_truncated = True
      await send(message)                            # always forward

send_wrapper is always installed. Body accumulation (the elif branch) only runs when log_body=True.

#### receive_wrapper — only installed when log_body=True
When body logging is disabled, pass receive through unmodified (no wrapping needed since
we do not need request body and receive has no role in status capture).

#### Unhandled 500 handling
If an exception propagates out of await self.app(...), our finally block runs but res_status[0]
is None (send was never called). Treat None as 500:

  status_code = res_status[0] if res_status[0] is not None else 500

#### Body logging (opt-in via LOG_HTTP_BODY=true)
Read os.environ.get('LOG_HTTP_BODY') inside __call__, NOT __init__, so monkeypatch works
without a fresh app instance.

Memory safety — two-tier cap:
  BODY_BUFFER_CAP = 4096   # hard limit: bytes held in memory
  BODY_LOG_CAP = 1024      # cosmetic limit: chars in final logged string

If body_truncated: emit '[body too large to log]', skip JSON parse.

If within cap, redact then truncate:
  1. Parse full JSON from accumulated bytes (no pre-truncation)
  2. Redact values for keys whose lowercase name contains: password, token, secret, jwt
  3. Re-serialize to string
  4. Truncate serialized string to BODY_LOG_CAP chars

For text/* bodies: decode then truncate to BODY_LOG_CAP.
For binary / non-text: emit '[binary]'.

Headers are NOT logged at all. The Authorization token value must never appear in any log field.

---

### Test strategy

http_log fixture attaches caplog.handler directly to ghostreplay.http (propagate=False means
caplog's root-logger hook would miss these records otherwise):

  @pytest.fixture
  def http_log(caplog):
      target = logging.getLogger('ghostreplay.http')
      target.addHandler(caplog.handler)
      with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO, logger='ghostreplay.http'):
          yield caplog
      target.removeHandler(caplog.handler)

### test_unhandled_500_logged
Uses a minimal local app with no exception handlers and raise_server_exceptions=False.
The shared client fixture uses raise_server_exceptions=True, which would re-raise the exception
to the test instead of producing a loggable 500:

  def test_unhandled_500_logged(http_log):
      crash_app = FastAPI()
      crash_app.add_middleware(HTTPLoggingMiddleware)

      @crash_app.get('/crash')
      def crash():
          raise RuntimeError('boom')

      with TestClient(crash_app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as c:
          c.get('/crash')

      record = next(r for r in http_log.records if r.http.get('path') == '/crash')
      assert record.http['status_code'] == 500

### Test matrix

| Test | Notes |
|---|---|
| test_logs_metadata_on_success | GET /health → method, path, status_code=200, duration_ms>=0, request_id |
| test_logs_user_id_when_authenticated | authenticated POST → user_id matches token's user_id |
| test_logs_unauthenticated_request | no token → status_code=401, user_id=None, still logs |
| test_request_id_unique_per_request | two requests → two distinct request_id values |
| test_query_param_secret_redacted | GET with ?token=abc → logged query shows token=[REDACTED] |
| test_body_logging_disabled_by_default | LOG_HTTP_BODY unset → no request_body/response_body keys |
| test_body_logged_when_env_enabled | monkeypatch LOG_HTTP_BODY=true → request_body present |
| test_request_body_password_redacted | POST {'password': 's3cr3t'} + LOG_HTTP_BODY=true → '[REDACTED]' |
| test_response_body_token_redacted | POST /api/auth/login + LOG_HTTP_BODY=true → token field is '[REDACTED]' |
| test_body_truncated_at_cap | serialized body > BODY_LOG_CAP → logged string <= cap chars |
| test_large_body_buffer_ceiling | body > BODY_BUFFER_CAP → '[body too large to log]' sentinel |
| test_binary_body_skipped | content-type application/octet-stream → '[binary]' |
| test_unhandled_500_logged | minimal crash_app + raise_server_exceptions=False → status_code=500 |
| test_authorization_header_never_logged | Bearer token value absent from all record.http values |
acceptance_criteria: 1. Middleware logs request and response metadata for successful and failed requests. 2. Full body logging is disabled by default and can be enabled via env flag. 3. Sensitive headers and common secret fields are redacted. 4. Large bodies are truncated and binary/streaming responses are handled safely. 5. Tests cover the logging contract without asserting cosmetic log formatting.

title: Handle overlapping unresolved SRS reviews
description: Consecutive Review Position moments can overlap before the earlier analysis resolves. The current single pendingSrsReviewRef model only tracks one in-flight review, so a later review move can overwrite the earlier one and drop its grading/UI outcome. Redesign review tracking to preserve multiple pending review grades by move identity, keep backend review submission correct for each review move, and make the behavior explicit in tests.
design:
<proposed_plan>
# Fix Overlapping Unresolved SRS Reviews

## Summary
Replace the single pending SRS review ref with a multi-entry registry so every targeted player move keeps its own grading metadata until that move analysis resolves. Each pending entry captures the session at answer time, so backend submission uses the original `session_id` even if the live game state changes before analysis resolves.

## Key Changes
- Change pending review state to a registry such as `Map<string, PendingSrsReview>`, keyed by `analysisId`.
- Define each entry as `{ sessionId, analysisId, blunderId, moveIndex, userMoveSan, srs }`; `sessionId` is captured from `useGameStore.getState().sessionId` in `useChessGameController` when the targeted player move is committed.
- If a targeted review move somehow has no `sessionId`, clear the armed review target and do not enqueue an SRS submission entry; this avoids posting against later live session state.
- In `AnalysisEffects`, process SRS review grading from an `analysisStoreApi.subscribe` listener, not only `useEffect([lastAnalysis])`, so same-tick/cache-hit back-to-back `resolveAnalysis` updates are all observed.
- For each resolved analysis, look up the pending entry by `analysis.id`, confirm `moveIndex` matches, delete only that entry, then grade and submit using `pendingReview.sessionId`.
- Keep visible `resolvedReview` latest-active only: update the toast to pass/fail only if it still references the same `analysisId`; older late resolutions still append move-list messages and submit to the backend.

## Data Flow
1. Ghost opponent returns a `target_blunder_id` and target FEN, arming review state for the next player decision.
2. Player move from that target FEN calls `analyzeMove`, receives an `analysisId`, captures the current `sessionId`, and stores the pending review entry in the registry.
3. Analysis results may resolve out of order or in the same React tick. The Zustand subscription sees every `lastAnalysis` transition and routes each result to its matching registry entry.
4. Resolution computes `evalLossCp`, pass/fail via existing `isRecordableFailure`, appends the correct move-list SRS message at that `moveIndex`, conditionally updates the current toast, and posts `/api/srs/review` with the stored `sessionId` and stored `blunderId`.

## Cleanup Rules
- Clear the whole registry on hard reset, explicit new game start, and abandoned-session replacement before starting a new session.
- Preserve the registry through normal terminal game end/inactive state so terminal review analysis can still submit after `finishLocalGame`.
- On revert/rewind, prune entries whose `moveIndex` is removed by the rewind; keep entries for still-present earlier moves. Also clear the visible armed review/resolved toast as today.
- Unknown `analysisId` results and `moveIndex` mismatches must leave the registry untouched.

## Tests
- Update controller tests to assert targeted review capture includes `sessionId` and multiple targeted review moves accumulate entries instead of overwriting.
- Add `AnalysisEffects` subscription tests for two pending reviews resolving out of order and for two cache-like resolutions fired in the same `act`: both backend submissions use their own stored `sessionId`, `blunderId`, and `userMoveSan`, and both move messages target the correct move indexes.
- Add stale/unmatched tests proving unknown `analysisId` and mismatched `moveIndex` do not delete pending entries.
- Keep the existing inactive-game terminal review test and update it to the registry shape, proving normal game end does not drop a pending terminal review.
- Add lifecycle coverage for revert pruning removed move indexes and reset/new-game clearing the registry.
- Run focused frontend tests: `npx vitest run src/hooks/useChessGameController.test.ts src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.test.tsx src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx`.

## Assumptions
- `analysisId` is the primary identity because it is the analysis request identity already used by `resolvedReview`; `moveIndex` remains a stale-result guard.
- Backend schema and `/api/srs/review` stay unchanged; they already support independent immutable review rows.
- Keep this as a local ref-backed registry for now, not a Zustand store, because the data is transient and only needed by controller/effects/lifecycle cleanup.
</proposed_plan>
close_reason: Closed

title: Grade terminal SRS review moves
description:
Terminal Review Position moves can miss SRS grading when the move ends the game. The current SRS grading effect depends on isGameActive, so a checkmate/stalemate/draw-ending review move can flip the game inactive before the analysis result arrives. When that happens, the pending pass/fail review may never be submitted to /api/srs/review, and the review UI may never resolve from pending to pass/fail.

Fix terminal review grading so matching pendingSrsReviewRef reviews are graded and submitted even after local game finalization. Preserve the intended post-move outcome handling for game end, but do not let game inactivity suppress a review that was already armed and matched to the terminal user move.
design:
Plan:

1. Authorize SRS review grading from the pending review token rather than active game state.
- In AnalysisEffects, remove isGameActive from the SRS review grading early return and dependency list.
- Keep the existing guards for sessionId, isPracticeContinuation, lastAnalysis, lastAnalysis.moveIndex, and the strict pendingSrsReviewRef match on analysisId + moveIndex.
- This keeps ordinary inactive-game analyses from grading while allowing an already-armed terminal review move to resolve after local game finalization.

2. Preserve pending and resolved review UI through terminal game finalization.
- Do not clear resolvedReview from finishLocalGame. The terminal review toast should be able to remain pending, then transition to pass/fail after the game result is set.
- Keep resolvedReview cleanup in new-game, revert, reset, and next-move flows where the review context is intentionally abandoned or replaced.
- Do not rely only on pendingSrsReviewRef.current as the preservation condition: analysis may resolve before endGame/finishLocalGame returns, clearing the pending ref while resolvedReview already contains pass/fail.

3. Add deterministic terminal-position analysis synthesis.
- In the analysis worker pipeline, detect when applying the played move or best move produces a terminal position. Because chess.js flags terminal conditions immediately after applying a move, short-circuit the Stockfish post-move search for terminal positions instead of asking the engine for a score that may be null or wasteful.
- Synthesize post-move score objects in the exact format expected by the existing delta computation logic, then feed those objects through the same computeAnalysisResult path. Checkmate should be represented as a mate score in favor of the mating side, such as { type: "mate", value: 1 } from the mating side's perspective or an equivalent high-centipawn score that normalizes identically. Drawn terminal positions should be represented as { type: "cp", value: 0 }.
- For non-terminal post-move positions, continue to use Stockfish scores. For terminal played and best lines, compute delta from the synthesized played and best post-move scores with the existing player/mover perspective rules.
- A played terminal checkmate is not automatically a failure just because it differs from Stockfish's pre-move best move; alternate mating moves should pass when their synthesized eval is equivalent or better. Losing terminal outcomes and inferior draw conversions should fail deterministically when the computed loss reaches the SRS threshold.

4. Add targeted coverage.
- AnalysisEffects test: an armed pendingSrsReviewRef submits /api/srs/review even after isGameActive becomes false.
- Lifecycle/controller test: finishLocalGame preserves an existing pending or pass/fail resolvedReview while reset/new-game/revert/next-move cleanup still clears it.
- Analysis worker/util tests: terminal mate by the played move returns a non-null delta/classification, alternate mating moves are not forced to fail, and terminal draw/checkmate positions no longer skip SRS submission because delta is null.
notes: Addressed code review findings: mate-0 win chance now treats the score POV as checkmated so black terminal mates classify from the correct perspective; finishLocalGame now preserves resolvedReview only when it matches an explicitly preserved final move index and clears unrelated stale review overlays. Added black alternate-mate and unrelated-review finalization tests. Verification: targeted vitest, npm run build, and npm run test:run passed.
close_reason: Implemented terminal SRS review grading fix, terminal analysis synthesis, review-finalization cleanup, and tests.

title: analysis performance
description: When navigating moves using Analysis Board's MoveList there are occasional pauses where the UI becomes unresponsive. This happens even when Engine Lines is disabled.
design: Proposed fix: move displayedFen engine cleanup out of render into effects; stop/clear engine immediately when showEngineArrows becomes false; guard cachedBest/searchmoves/mergedEngineLines/engineLinesDisplay/engineArrows behind showEngineArrows so disabled mode does no engine-only chess.js work; consider making useStockfishEngine lazy/enabled so the Stockfish worker terminates while engine lines are off; optionally change MoveList navigation auto-scroll to instant/conditional behavior if profiling still shows layout jank.
notes:

AnalysisBoard still performs engine-related work when Engine lines is disabled: it calls stopSearch during render on every displayedFen change, computes cached-best restricted searchmoves with chess.js legal move generation regardless of showEngineArrows, and keeps the Stockfish hook/worker mounted. MoveList adds layout reads in requestAnimationFrame for smooth auto-scroll, which may amplify visible stalls but does not explain disabled-engine CPU by itself. Focused tests pass: npm run test:run -- AnalysisBoard MoveList.
Implementation 2026-04-27: moved AnalysisBoard engine stop/clear work out of render and into effects/unchecked handler; gated searchmoves, merged lines, line display, live eval, and engine arrows behind Engine lines; added useStockfishEngine({ enabled }) so the Stockfish worker is not created while disabled and is terminated when disabled. title: clicking blunders takes you to blunders
description:
In the stats pane in the /history analysis board, when clicking on blunders, mistakes or
inaccuracies it should select the corresponding move itself in the graph and MoveList.

When there are multiple moves of each type, repeatedly clicking on the category should cycle
chronologically through the moves of that type, starting with the first occurrence. The cycle
state should not reset if the user manually navigates to other moves in between clicks. No
extra UI indicator is needed for the cycle.

This navigation behavior is in addition to the existing highlight/pinning behavior: clicking
a category still pins all highlights for that type, while additionally jumping the current
move selection.

This works in both the You column and Ghost column, selecting the player's or ghost's corresponding
moves.
design:
# Implementation Plan: g-ve6m (Clicking blunders navigates to move)

## Objective
Enable clicking on "blunders", "mistakes", or "inaccuracies" in the `GameReviewStats` pane to automatically navigate the `AnalysisBoard` to the corresponding move. Repeated clicks on the same category should cycle chronologically through the moves of that type.

## Scope & Impact
- **Components:** `HistoryPage`, `AnalysisBoard`, `GameReviewStats`.
- **Hooks:** `useGameReviewStats`.
- **Impact:** Enhances the post-game review UX by making stats actionable. Does not affect game recording or engine analysis logic.

## Proposed Solution: Imperative Ref
We will expose an imperative handle (`jumpToMove`) from `AnalysisBoard` and manage the cycling state within the `useGameReviewStats` hook.

### Key Files & Context
- `src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx`: Manages the current move index (`currentIndex`). Needs to expose `jumpToMove` via `forwardRef`.
- `src/hooks/useGameReviewStats.ts`: Manages the interaction state of the stats pane. Needs to track the cycle index for each category and call the imperative handle.
- `src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx`: Glues `GameReviewStats` and `AnalysisBoard` together. Needs to create the ref and pass the `jumpToMove` callback to `useGameReviewStats`.

### Implementation Steps

1.  **Refactor `AnalysisBoard` to support `forwardRef`:**
    *   Update `AnalysisBoard` export to use `forwardRef`.
    *   Define an interface `AnalysisBoardRef` with `jumpToMove(index: number): void`.
    *   Implement `useImperativeHandle` inside `AnalysisBoard` to call `handleNavigate(index)`.
    *   *Note:* Ensure the component remains wrapped in `memo`.

2.  **Update `useGameReviewStats` to track cycle state:**
    *   Add an argument `onJumpToMove?: (index: number) => void` to the hook.
    *   Add state to track the current cycle index for the pinned stat: `cycleIndex: number`.
    *   Modify `handleStatClick`:
        *   If clicking a *new* category: Set it as pinned, reset `cycleIndex` to 0, and jump to the first move of that category.
        *   If clicking the *already pinned* category: Increment `cycleIndex` (modulo the number of moves in that category), and jump to the new move.
    *   Modify `handleGraphMoveClick`: Reset the pinned stat and cycle index.

3.  **Wire everything together in `HistoryPage`:**
    *   Create a `useRef<AnalysisBoardRef>(null)`.
    *   Pass `ref={boardRef}` to `AnalysisBoard`.
    *   Pass an `onJumpToMove` callback to `useGameReviewStats` that calls `boardRef.current?.jumpToMove(index)`.

## Verification & Testing
1.  **Unit Tests:** Update `HistoryPage.test.tsx` (if applicable) or manually verify the behavior. We should ensure that `forwardRef` and `memo` play nicely together.
2.  **Manual Verification:**
    *   Go to History -> Analysis.
    *   Click "Blunders". Verify it pins the highlight AND navigates to the first blunder.
    *   Click "Blunders" again. Verify it navigates to the second blunder.
    *   Manually click a different move in the MoveList. Click "Blunders" again. Verify it continues cycling from the last blunder it was on.
    *   Click "Mistakes". Verify it pins mistakes and navigates to the first mistake.

## Migration & Rollback
No database migrations required. If issues occur, revert the UI changes.

design:
Mobile portrait gameplay layout plan

Goal
- Make /play usable on narrow portrait screens by prioritizing board width and vertical density while preserving the desktop/tablet layout.
- Scope game-specific spacing changes to the game route and narrow breakpoints so history/openings/stats layouts are not accidentally reshaped.

Current data and layout flow
- GamePage renders <main className="app-shell game-page"> with AppNav and ChessGame.
- ChessGame renders .chess-section -> .chess-layout containing GameInfoPanel in grid-area panel, .chessboard-wrapper in grid-area board, .chess-graph-area in grid-area graph, and .moves-column in grid-area moves.
- Board width is limited by .chessboard-wrapper max-width: var(--game-board-max-width). On mobile .chess-layout is one column, but the board still pays for .app-shell padding, .chess-section padding/border, .chess-layout gap, and the eval bar width/gap inside .chessboard-board-with-eval.
- Eval data comes from ConnectedEvalBar, which reads analysisMap, moveHistory, viewIndex, and boardOrientation. Hiding it on mobile is a presentation-only change; it should not affect analysis state, move list annotations, or graph evals.
- Start/new-game dialogs are overlays inside .chessboard-board-area, so centering should be relative to the actual board area. Board area gets shifted right when the eval bar is present, and mobile outer padding compounds the visible offset.
- GameInfoPanel currently renders one aria-live panel with status text, badges, player Elo line, opponent line with 70px avatar, warning stack, and an Opening line only while isGameActive. Any compact mobile treatment must avoid duplicate announced content inside that aria-live region.
- ConnectedAnalysisGraph returns null until eval/pending data exists. Its height is controlled by .chess-graph-area .analysis-graph > svg: desktop var(--game-graph-height)=220px, mobile currently has an unscoped 330px override near the top of App.css, which is the source of the tall graph.
- AppNav currently renders all route/user actions inline in .nav-bar__actions; at <=720px CSS stacks brand and wrapping actions, causing two-row action overflow below the brand.

Implementation steps
1. Establish mobile game breakpoint and width math
- Use a focused game breakpoint around max-width: 767px, matching the existing game layout collapse.
- In .game-page, reduce outer padding to 0 on the inline axis, with a small top/bottom padding only if needed for breathing room.
- In .game-page .chess-section, remove border radius/border on mobile and set inline padding to 0 so the board can reach viewport edges.
- In .game-page .chess-layout, set width: 100%, gap to a compact value such as 0.5rem, and ensure min-width: 0 on the board/moves/graph tracks.
- In .game-page .chessboard-wrapper, set max-width: 100vw and width: 100%; with the eval bar removed, react-chessboard should resolve to a square close to viewport width.

2. Hide the eval bar only for mobile gameplay
- Add a mobile-only rule for .game-page .eval-bar { display: none; } and collapse .game-page .chessboard-board-with-eval gap to 0.
- Keep ConnectedEvalBar mounted unless a render-cost issue appears. CSS hiding avoids changing analysis subscriptions or desktop behavior.
- Verify that overlays and promotion picker still anchor to .chessboard-board-area, now full board width, so the start panel centers visually.

3. Recenter and constrain board overlays/dialogs
- For .chessboard-overlay, keep inset: 0 and center with flex, but add mobile padding using max(0.5rem, env(safe-area-inset-* where useful)) so dialogs do not touch screen edges.
- For .chess-start-panel and .revert-warning-dialog on mobile, set width: min(calc(100vw - 2rem), 22rem), box-sizing: border-box, and smaller padding/gaps.
- For .chess-start-options, keep wrapping but allow buttons to use compact padding; do not let the dialog exceed board width.

4. Replace narrow nav action overflow with a hamburger menu
- Refactor AppNav so route/auth actions are rendered from one shared action model or helper, preventing desktop/mobile drift from duplicating hardcoded links.
- AppNav keeps local isMenuOpen state and exposes a mobile menu button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- Keep desktop markup visually equivalent: brand plus inline .nav-bar__actions.
- On narrow viewports, hide/collapse inline actions behind the hamburger button and render the same route/auth actions in a fixed side drawer or panel.
- Hidden desktop actions must not remain tabbable when the mobile drawer is the active nav surface. Use CSS/markup that removes hidden action groups from the accessibility and tab order at the relevant state, or render one active action group per viewport.
- Drawer accessibility contract: open with the hamburger button; close on nav link click, logout click, close button, backdrop/overlay click, and Escape; return focus to the hamburger button when the drawer closes; expose an accessible drawer label; keep focus outlines visible.
- Use a button with a familiar menu icon drawn in CSS or simple markup, because there is no icon dependency in package.json. Add accessible label text via aria-label, not visible helper copy.

5. Compact GameInfoPanel for mobile active games
- Prefer one semantic markup path styled responsively where practical. If duplicate desktop/mobile rows are introduced, the hidden row must use display: none at the relevant breakpoint and aria-hidden where needed so the aria-live panel does not announce duplicate status/Elo/opponent content.
- For active games on mobile, present a compact matchup row: You <rating?> vs <avatar> <opponent label/Elo/name>, plus status badge and unrated/practice badge.
- Hide the verbose status text on mobile active games, but leave gameStatusBadge visible as requested.
- Hide the Opening line on mobile active games. Do not add new post-game Opening behavior as part of this issue; the current code only renders Opening while isGameActive.
- Remove visible labels Your Elo and Opponent from the mobile active summary. Preserve desktop copy to avoid changing existing desktop behavior unnecessarily.
- Reduce opponent avatar size in the mobile summary to about 32-40px. Desktop can continue using the 70px avatar.
- Keep ghost info, review warning, and rehook toasts accessible. If the ghost info button remains in the opponent row, size it to fit beside the compact summary; otherwise move it into the warning/ghost controls row without losing callbacks.
- Use stable classes such as .chess-panel__desktop-line and .chess-panel__mobile-matchup only if needed, so tests can assert rendered data without depending on CSS pixels.

6. Shorten game analysis graph on mobile
- Remove the existing unscoped @media (max-width: 767px) graph height of 330px, or override it later with a more specific .game-page selector placed after the existing rule.
- Set .game-page .chess-graph-area .analysis-graph > svg to a compact mobile height, likely 120-160px.
- Keep history page graph rules separate; existing .history-page mobile graph height can remain unless the same issue is observed there.
- Reduce .chess-graph-area gap/margins on mobile so the MoveList starts sooner.

7. Moves column visibility and vertical sizing
- Keep .moves-column after graph in mobile grid, but ensure max-height allows a useful scrollable list, for example clamp(220px, 34dvh, 360px), once graph height is reduced.
- Confirm MaterialDisplay and turn labels do not consume excessive height; if needed, shrink their min-height/padding only under .game-page mobile.
- Do not change move-list data flow: ConnectedMoveList continues reading useGameStore and analysisStore as today.

8. Verification and tests
- AppNav test harness: mock ../contexts/useAuth and wrap AppNav in MemoryRouter because AppNav calls useAuth and renders react-router Links.
- AppNav tests should cover menu state and behavior, not CSS breakpoint visibility: hamburger opens/closes the drawer, route actions render from the shared action set, link click closes the drawer, logout calls the mocked logout and closes the drawer, Escape/backdrop close the drawer, aria-expanded reflects state, and focus returns to the menu button on close.
- GameInfoPanel tests should cover compact matchup data if new markup is added, and should guard against duplicate visible semantic content where feasible without asserting pixel layout.
- BoardStage overlay tests should continue to cover start-overlay actions and can add a contract assertion for dialog containment only if exposed via markup/classes, not exact mobile measurements.
- Existing targeted tests to run: npx vitest run src/components/chess-game/ui/GameInfoPanel.test.tsx src/components/chess-game/ui/BoardStage.test.tsx src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx plus any new AppNav test.
- Build gate: npm run build.
- Visual verification: run the Vite app and inspect /play at 390x844 and 430x932 portrait. Check board width is viewport-edge or near-edge, eval bar hidden, new-game panel centered, nav hamburger does not wrap, active game panel is one compact row where possible, graph is short enough that the top of MoveList is visible after moves exist, and desktop width still has the side panel/eval bar/full nav.

Risks and constraints
- react-chessboard sizes from its container, so the main risk is an ancestor retaining padding/max-width. Validate with computed widths in browser, not only CSS review.
- Hiding the eval bar with CSS preserves state but may leave any parent gap if .chessboard-board-with-eval is not also collapsed.
- AppNav is shared across pages; mobile hamburger should improve all narrow pages, but game-page spacing should remain scoped to .game-page to avoid changing home/history layout unexpectedly.
- The issue asks to get the panel down to one line without overflowing. Treat that as best effort with nowrap where possible and allow controlled wrapping/ellipsis for long ghost/opponent names instead of letting text overlap.
notes: Review follow-up: addressed AppNav drawer accessibility by moving focus to the drawer close button on open, removing backdrop from tab order, and trapping Tab/Shift+Tab within the drawer until close. Re-ran focused Vitest: AppNav, GameInfoPanel, BoardStage, ChessGame all pass. Left pre-existing unrelated src/components/chess-game/config.ts and work changes untouched.
close_reason: Implemented mobile gameplay layout fixes, nav drawer accessibility follow-up, tests and visual smoke checks completed; build blocker filed separately as g-fix-build-unused.

title: End game effect
description: At the end of game add a sound corresponding to win/loss/draw. Play a random sound from public/audio/win on a win and one from public/audio/lose on a loss. No sound for a draw.
design:
Plan: Add guarded one-shot end-game audio with Vite glob-discovered clips.

Summary:
  Add session-aware one-shot end-game audio:

  - Win: random clip from src/assets/audio/win
  - Competitive loss: random clip from src/assets/audio/lose
  - Draw and “Practice ended.”: no sound

- Use Vite build-time import.meta.glob URL imports so adding a new audio file only requires rebuilding the app, not editing code.
- Trigger audio only for finalized competitive results: checkmate_win plays a random win clip; checkmate_loss and actual resignation play a random loss clip; draw and practice-ended stay silent.

Implementation details:
- Add a helper/module that builds clip URL arrays from import.meta.glob over src/assets/audio/win/* and src/assets/audio/lose/*, including mp3/wav/m4a extensions. The glob is build-time discovery, not runtime filesystem access.
- Add playEndGameAudio(result: GameResult) near the existing audio utilities/lifecycle helpers. It maps checkmate_win -> win clips, checkmate_loss/resign -> loss clips, draw -> no-op, chooses Math.floor(Math.random() * clips.length), and ignores Audio/play failures.
- Make the one-shot guard explicitly session-aware: track playedEndGameAudioSessionIdRef as string | null, pass/capture the finalizing sessionId into finishLocalGame, and play only when current useGameStore.getState().sessionId still equals that finalizing sessionId and playedEndGameAudioSessionIdRef.current !== finalizingSessionId. Set the ref to finalizingSessionId before invoking Audio.
- Reset playedEndGameAudioSessionIdRef on successful new game and hard reset for clarity, but correctness must come from the current-session equality check and stored played session id, so stale endGame promises after reset/session replacement cannot play.
- Extend finishLocalGame options with playEndGameAudio?: boolean defaulting to true and finalizingSessionId?: string | null. Use playEndGameAudio: false for the practice-continuation resignation path that produces “Practice ended.”
- Invoke the audio helper from finishLocalGame only after store.setGameResult(result), only when playEndGameAudio is true, and only when the session-aware guard allows it, so failed endGame calls never play premature audio.
- Update handleResign dependencies to include finishLocalGame.

Tests:
- Add focused unit coverage for the glob-backed clip helper if it is factored out, mocking/stubbing the clip URL arrays rather than asserting exact build output.
- Add lifecycle tests with Audio and Math.random stubs: terminal checkmate_win selects a win URL and plays; terminal checkmate_loss selects a loss URL and plays; draw does not construct/play Audio.
- Add duplicate/stale finalization coverage: two handleGameEnd calls for the same unresolved session play at most once; if a pending endGame resolves after reset/new game changes sessionId, it must not play audio.
- Add resignation coverage: actual resignation success plays a loss clip; failed resignation does not play; practice-continuation “Practice ended.” remains silent.
- Preserve existing blunder/best-move audio tests.
- Run npm run test:run -- src/hooks/useChessGameLifecycle.test.ts src/components/ChessGame.test.tsx, npm run lint, and npm run build.

Assumptions:
- import.meta.glob discovery happens at build/dev-server time; adding audio files requires restarting/rebuilding as needed, not a runtime directory scan.
- Resignation of an active competitive game is treated as a loss for audio.
- Ending practice continuation is not treated as a loss for audio.
- No UI, layout, API, schema, or backend changes are needed.
notes: Second review fix applied: terminal endGame and resign paths now re-check current session immediately after await endGame and before applying ratingChange, scoreChanges, or rating score updates. Strengthened stale game-end coverage with non-null rating data and added stale resignation rating-side-effect coverage. Verification: focused test run passed (71 tests); build passed; touched-file eslint has no errors, only existing hook dependency warnings.
close_reason: Implemented guarded end-game audio with session-safe stale-finalization handling and tests

title: Add glicko score
description:
Add two types of Glicko scores, one that simulates chess.com's score and one that uses lichess's Glicko-2 system. 

Display all three scores (including the existing ELO score) in the rating graph in /stats. Add checkboxes that allows the user to control which of the 3 scores to show in the graph.

For the in-game user rating add a mini gear icon that opens a settings  popup that allows the user to choose which of the three scores they'd like to display.

Implementation direction:

Prefer extending the existing rating pipeline rather than introducing a separate game-data read path.

Option A: add Glicko fields to rating_history alongside existing Elo fields, e.g. glicko_rating,
glicko_rd, and optionally glicko_volatility if using Glicko-2. This keeps the current rating
graph/history query shape close to existing code and lets old Elo behavior coexist during transition.
Option B: create a parallel glicko_rating_history table with user_id, game_session_id, rating, rd,
volatility, games_played, is_provisional/derived status, recorded_at. This is cleaner if both Elo
and Glicko must be displayed independently or compared.

Update backend/app/rating.py or a new backend/app/glicko.py with deterministic Glicko/Glicko-2
calculation. Inputs should be current Glicko state, session.engine_elo, fixed engine opponent RD
policy, result score, and elapsed rating period if we decide to age RD by time.

Update POST /api/game/end so rated outcomes write Glicko data in the same transaction as the
existing session end/rating update. No session_moves or PGN parsing should be required.
Add a historical backfill script that scans existing rated ended game_sessions ordered by ended_at
(or started_at fallback if needed), skips abandon/unrated games, and reconstructs Glicko history
from session.engine_elo + result. The backfill should be idempotent and avoid duplicating
rows/fields for sessions already processed.

API/UI choice still needed: either keep current endpoints returning Elo fields and add Glicko-
specific fields/endpoints, or migrate current rating endpoints to expose Glicko while preserving
frontend compatibility.
design:
# g-lqrj: Add Glicko Ratings

## Summary
Add Chess.com-style Glicko-1 and Lichess-style Glicko-2 tracks alongside existing Elo. Elo remains the compatibility/default rating and the sole driver for opponent sampling. /stats, the in-game rating label, and the post-game rating delta can display the selected score when data exists.

## Backend Changes
- Extend rating_history with nullable Glicko columns only: chesscom_rating, chesscom_rd, lichess_rating, lichess_rd, lichess_volatility.
- Preserve existing Elo history during backfill:
  - Existing rating, games_played, and is_provisional values are never rewritten.
  - Backfill overwrites/recomputes only Glicko columns deterministically on every rerun, so reruns are idempotent and converge if Glicko math changes before release.
  - If a rated session has no rating_history row, create one with recomputed Elo plus both Glicko tracks because there is no legacy Elo value to preserve.
- Make latest rating reads deterministic everywhere with recorded_at DESC, games_played DESC, id DESC.
- Add game_session_id uniqueness only after a preflight/dedupe step:
  - Detect duplicates before creating the constraint/index.
  - Keep the deterministic winner by the same ordering.
  - Prefer failing with a clear cleanup command unless implementation explicitly logs/archives duplicate ids before deletion.
- Add backend/app/glicko.py:
  - Chess.com-style Glicko-1: initial 1200, RD 350, engine RD 75, RD clamp 30..350.
  - Lichess-style Glicko-2: initial 1500, RD 350, volatility 0.06, tau 0.5, engine RD 75.
  - No inactivity aging in v1; abandon/unrated games do not update ratings.
- Preserve API compatibility:
  - Legacy Elo fields remain aliases.
  - Add scores, score_changes, and scores_after objects with explicit shape { elo: RatingScore, chesscom: RatingScore | null, lichess: RatingScore | null }. Elo is never nullable; non-Elo tracks are nullable before backfill or for legacy unfilled rows.
- Rollout: migrate nullable columns, run duplicate preflight/dedupe, add uniqueness, deploy null-gated API/new-row writes, run backfill.
- Update backend/conftest.py manual SQLite schema.

## Frontend Changes
- Add typed score shapes in src/utils/api.ts while preserving legacy Elo fields:
  - RatingScoreKey = elo | chesscom | lichess.
  - RatingScore = { rating: number, rd?: number, volatility?: number, is_provisional: boolean }.
  - RatingScores = { elo: RatingScore, chesscom: RatingScore | null, lichess: RatingScore | null }.
  - Call sites must treat only chesscom/lichess as nullable; Elo access stays direct.
- Update useGameStore:
  - Keep playerRating as Elo for sampleEloBin.
  - Add ratingScores and helpers to write all API score tracks.
  - fetchCurrentRating and every game-end path update all available scores but keep Elo as the source for matchmaking.
- Add local preference store persisted at ghostreplay_rating_display_type, default elo; selected non-Elo scores fall back to Elo when null.
- Update GameInfoPanel with selected rating label/value and a 24px settings popup.
- Update PostGameBanner so the visible delta follows the selected score via score_changes; fall back to legacy Elo when selected score data is null/absent, and label non-Elo deltas.
- Update RatingGraph:
  - Series checkboxes for Elo, Chess.com, and Lichess.
  - Skip null points per series.
  - All tracks share existing games_played provisional behavior in v1.
  - Preserve existing no-rated-games/no-stable-ratings states.
  - Add selected-series-empty state: "No data for the selected rating series yet."
  - Add all-series-unchecked empty state prompting selection.

## Test Plan
- Backend tests for Glicko math, API compatibility, nullable pre-backfill fields, game-end writes, deterministic latest ordering, duplicate preflight, uniqueness, and backfill preserving existing Elo while overwriting Glicko columns deterministically on rerun.
- Frontend tests for non-null Elo score typing/usage, multi-score storage, selected display behavior, Elo-only sampling, post-game selected-score deltas, null Glicko graph states, and settings persistence.
- Quality gates:
  - cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && TMPDIR=/Users/mvargas/src/ghostreplay/backend/.tmp pytest -p no:cacheprovider test_glicko_rating.py test_rating_api.py test_game_api.py test_rating_backfill.py -q
  - Broader backend suite if time allows.
  - npm run test:run
  - npm run build

## Assumptions
- Chess.com score means deterministic Glicko-1 approximation, not exact private-platform parity.
- Display preference and post-game delta display are browser-local and display-only.
- Existing Elo history is never rewritten except for creating rows that are currently missing.
- Backfill reruns may overwrite Glicko columns, but never legacy Elo columns.
- No session moves, PGN parsing, external API, or engine analysis data is needed.
notes: Code review fixes applied: legacy rows with null Glicko now keep non-Elo scores null on subsequent game-end writes until backfill; backfill ordering uses coalesce(ended_at, started_at); RatingGraph current footer renders current visible series values/labels. Added regression tests for legacy-null game-end behavior and null-ended backfill ordering. Verification: focused backend pytest 18 passed; RatingGraph tests 12 passed; npm build passed.
close_reason: Implemented Glicko rating tracks, API/UI display controls, backfill, migration, and review fixes.

title: Add root-level opening score and hero stats
description: Add an overall opening score for the root starting position and show the currently selected route's stats in the openings hero. The top-level openings page should use the same hero stats pattern as drill-down pages instead of being structurally special.
design:
Backend
- Extend `/api/openings/children` to return one canonical current-branch stats object alongside `children`, instead of deriving hero values in the page.
- Keep the new branch-stats response shape tight: only include the fields the hero and empty-state logic actually consume, rather than mirroring the full drill-down/root payload.
- Compute that stats object after `canonicalize_children_route`, so hero stats always match the canonical route used for breadcrumbs and drill-down content.
- For the top-level Start route (`parent_key=None`), aggregate across all cached opening-score rows to expose the repertoire-wide stats introduced by this task.
- For drill pages (`parent_key=<opening>`), aggregate the selected opening row plus all descendant rows, deduped through the same DAG-aware descendant handling already used for subtree child aggregation.
- Refactor the existing subtree aggregation math in `build_opening_children` into a shared helper so score/confidence/coverage/sample-size/root-count/last-practiced values are computed the same way for hero stats and child cards.
- Return null hero metrics when the branch has no scored rows, so the frontend can render placeholders without inventing values.
- Add explicit backend coverage that the new hero aggregate does not double-count shared descendants in DAG drill-down routes, mirroring the existing shared-node child aggregation risk.

Frontend behavior
- Extend `ChildrenResponse` in `src/utils/api.ts` with the new current-branch stats field and keep `getOpeningChildren` request behavior unchanged.
- In `src/pages/OpeningsPage.tsx`, derive hero content from that new field so both Start and named-opening routes use the same hero stats pattern.
- Top-level hero should show the repertoire-wide score/coverage/games/confidence values from the new backend aggregate.
- Drill-page hero should show the selected opening branch's stats, not the currently listed child card summary.
- Preserve the existing canonicalization flow: invalid colors/paths should still rewrite the URL, and the hero must update from the canonical response rather than the requested params.
- Change the page empty-state gates to use the new current-branch aggregate/root-count instead of the child-card-only checks. A branch with scored current stats and unscored children must keep its hero stats and content state instead of falling into the “no scored openings” empty state.
- Keep the existing empty-state messaging copy where it still applies, but drive it from branch-level emptiness: true-no-evidence when `computed_at` is null and the current branch aggregate has zero scored roots, snapshot-empty when `computed_at` is non-null and the current branch aggregate has zero scored roots.
- Render hero metrics as placeholders (`—`) when the current branch has no scored data.

Layout
- Update the openings hero markup so the current direct-child flex layout becomes: copy block plus a dedicated `.openings-shell__hero-rail` wrapper.
- Place the new stats card and the existing parent card inside that rail so they stack intentionally instead of wrapping opportunistically as separate flex children.
- Give the rail concrete sizing rules in `src/App.css`: `flex: 0 1 320px`, `min-width: min(100%, 280px)`, column layout, and consistent internal gap.

title: Push best-move feedback to a more dramatic sparkly treatment
description: Push the new best-move feedback beyond the current pop-and-bling treatment. Make the visual animation more dramatic and the audio more sparkly so best-move feedback reads as a celebratory moment rather than a subtle notification.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Keep the trigger on the existing best-move paths, but distinguish audio from visual lifecycle explicitly.
- Audio continues to ride the existing `resolveAnalysis` -> `lastAnalysis` subscription path in `AnalysisEffects.tsx`, where best-move sound is already gated to player moves only.
- Visual celebration is a different path and must be described separately: `resolveAnalysis` updates `freshlyResolved` in `AnalysisConnectors.tsx`, `MoveList.tsx` passes that through as `freshWhite` / `freshBlack`, and `MoveRow.tsx` turns `fresh && classification === "best"` into the best-only animation classes.
- The dramatic treatment must stay scoped to `fresh && best`, not plain `best`, so historical best moves in the move list do not light up when revisited or re-rendered.

2. Define teardown ownership before expanding the animation into multiple layers.
- Today fresh-state cleanup happens from the icon span `onAnimationEnd` in `MoveRow.tsx`, which calls back through `onFreshAnimationDone` to clear the resolved index in `AnalysisConnectors.tsx`.
- Once the best-move effect becomes multi-part, we need an explicit invariant: cleanup happens exactly once, on the final best-animation layer, not on the first nested animation event.
- Implement the best treatment so there is one authoritative completion signal for fresh-state teardown. If multiple animated descendants or pseudo-layers exist, intermediate animation-end events must be ignored.
- The plan should preserve the existing non-best cleanup behavior while making best-move teardown deterministic, so the class neither disappears before the glow tail finishes nor sticks forever.

3. Reshape the visual effect around a three-stage celebration: anticipation, burst, settle.
- The current best treatment is only `move-icon--pop-best` on the icon span created in `MoveRow.tsx`. Extend that DOM hook so the icon, SAN text, and the containing move button can participate independently.
- Replace the single pop keyframe with a sequence that starts with a slight compress/backshift, then a larger overshoot, then a smaller rebound settle.
- Add a lingering afterglow layer such as a shimmer ring, starburst, or sparkle halo that fades after the main motion.

4. Let the celebration extend beyond the icon without breaking move-list layout.
- The move list uses a tight three-column grid and `.move-button` currently has `overflow: hidden`, so any larger halo or ring will clip unless we contain it deliberately.
- Prefer an internal absolutely positioned FX layer or best-only pseudo-elements with `pointer-events: none` rather than changing row sizing.
- Keep the motion transform/opacity driven so row height, auto-scroll behavior, and neighboring rows stay stable.
- Briefly tint or brighten the containing best-move button and SAN text, but do not animate padding, border width, or font-size because those would cause reflow in the move grid.

5. Reserve the dramatic treatment for best moves and keep other classifications restrained.
- `excellent` and below should keep the current simpler pop so the hierarchy remains clear.
- Build the new best-move treatment as a best-only class path in `MoveRow.tsx` and `App.css`, not as a global animation change for all move icons.

6. Replace the current bling with a short layered chime.
- `blingSound.ts` currently plays a simple two-sine C6 to E6 beep. Replace it with a more celebratory patch using: a bright attack partial, a bell-like upper partial, a filtered noise burst for sparkle, and slight pitch motion or a short arpeggio.
- Keep the existing unlocked shared `AudioContext` flow so browser gesture gating still works.
- Keep total duration short and gain conservative so repeated best moves do not become harsh.
- Structure the synthesis so we can tune mild / medium / bold variants later, even if medium is the only shipped default initially.

7. Tune against the actual move-list sizing constraints.
- The player column is wider than the engine column, and the move list can render on narrower mobile widths, so the glow/ring has to read cleanly in both wide and tight cells.
- Confirm the lingering sparkle does not get clipped by the move-list scroll container and does not interfere with selection styling or message bubbles.
- Keep the total best-move effect roughly under one second, with the glow tail slightly longer than the scale motion so it reads as celebratory but not fatiguing.

8. Test behavior contracts rather than cosmetic specifics, with explicit coverage for the new risk points.
- Extend `AnalysisEffects.test.tsx` to keep proving audio only fires for player best moves and stays silent for engine best moves and non-best classifications. Add the missing black-player parity case so the gating is verified for both player colors.
- Extend `MoveRow.test.tsx` to verify fresh best moves receive the new best-only wrapper/classes while non-best fresh moves keep the simpler animation path.
- Add a best-path cleanup test that proves the fresh-state callback is tied to the final best animation completion rule, not any intermediate animation-end event.
- Avoid brittle assertions about exact keyframes, DOM geometry, or styling minutiae. Focus on trigger rules, class wiring, fresh-state teardown, and best-vs-non-best separation.

## Execution order

1. Document and preserve the current split lifecycle: audio via `lastAnalysis`, visuals via `freshlyResolved`.
2. Add new best-only DOM hooks plus a single authoritative best-animation teardown point in `MoveRow.tsx`.
3. Implement the CSS motion system, glow layer, and overflow containment in `App.css`.
4. Replace `playBling()` with the layered chime in `blingSound.ts`.
5. Update focused tests for player-color audio gating and final-best-animation cleanup.
6. Manually tune the effect against repetition fatigue, using mild / medium / bold variants if needed, with medium as the default.

title: Make a perfect move streak achievement
description:
Each time the user makes the best move show a streak counter. The longer the perfect move streak the more dramatic the display of the streak counter, maybe showing some kind of fire animation when the streak is long. Also keep track of the personal best streak, to be shown in /stats. When breaking the personal record it should also be displayed during the game.

Reuse the ⭐ icon in some way to tie the streak to the best move icon in MoveList.

When the counter>0 put the live streak as a compact badge in the GameInfoPanel, near “Your Elo” / opponent info.
  Desktop: in the left panel, after the rating or before the opening line.

  Mobile: in the top game header row as a small fixed-width badge, e.g. 🔥 4 or Best 4, so it does not create a
  new vertical row.

  Why this is probably right: it keeps the board clean, avoids competing with blunder/review toasts, and gives the
  streak persistent visibility without stealing focus every move.

  Dramatic Moments
  Use a temporary board-area toast only for milestones or personal bests.

  - Streak 3: subtle pulse on the panel badge.
  - Streak 5: brief “5 best moves” toast.
  - New personal best: stronger toast, maybe New record: 8.
  - Long streak: add fire animation to the persistent badge, not a permanent board overlay.

This should reuse the existing board toast pattern carefully. The bottom-right board area is already used
  by .blunder-toast and .review-pass-toast, so streak toast should not appear there at the same time as blunder/
  review feedback. Personal-best can queue after those or be suppressed if a blunder/review message is active.

  Avoid
  I would avoid placing the streak permanently over the board. The board already has:

  - blunder flash overlay
  - promotion picker
  - start/revert/resign overlays
  - arrows and square highlights
  - blunder/review pass toasts at bottom-right

  A permanent board overlay would add visual noise during calculation-heavy moments. It also risks mobile
  crowding.

  Desktop Options

  1. Left panel badge, recommended
     Add a compact row:
     Perfect streak 4
     Best 7

     It fits the existing status/meta pattern and can grow more dramatic with classes like streak--hot.
  2. Moves column header
     Good if the streak is treated as move-quality analytics. Less good because the moves column is already dense
     and may scroll.
  3. Below opening line
     Quietest option, but probably too buried for an achievement-style feature.

  Mobile Options

  1. Inline top header badge, recommended
     Keep it short: 🔥 4 / Best 7.
     Needs stable width or tabular nums so it does not shift the opponent label.
  2. Dedicated notice row
     Only for personal-best or milestone bursts. Mobile already has a notices grid area for warning stack messages
     below the board, so a streak milestone could share that pattern if it is transient.
  3. Board corner badge
     Use only for celebration bursts, not persistent state


  Interaction With Existing Messaging
  Priority should be:

  1. Critical blocking overlays: start, promotion, revert, resign.
  2. Review/blunder feedback: review warning, fail/pass, blunder toast.
  3. Ghost rehook notice.
  4. Streak milestone / personal best.
  5. Passive persistent streak badge.

  So the persistent badge can always exist in the panel/header, but animated celebratory messages should yield to
  blunder/review messaging. A “new personal best” can still update the badge immediately, then show a toast later
  if the message lane is busy.

  My recommendation: implement a persistent PerfectStreakBadge in GameInfoPanel, with desktop full text and mobile
  compact text, then add a separate transient StreakToast only for milestones and personal records. This gives the
  feature presence without competing with the instructional/error messaging that already matters during play..
design:
## Summary
Implement perfect-move streaks as a derived achievement backed by existing analyzed SessionMove.classification data. The game UI recomputes the live player-only streak by move order from retained moveHistory + analysisMap, shows a compact persistent badge in GameInfoPanel, and emits idempotent transient celebrations only when the derived state crosses milestone or all-time record thresholds. /stats shows the all-time personal best streak independent of the selected stats window.

## Key Changes
- Backend stats: add an Achievement/PerfectStreak summary to /api/stats/summary with all-time personal_best, derived from existing SessionMove rows joined to GameSession. Do not use the summary window's session_ids/cutoff for this achievement; compute from all sessions for the authenticated user. Compute max streak per session, resetting to 0 at every session boundary before scanning that session's player moves in move_number/color order. Count only moves where SessionMove.color == GameSession.player_color; increment on classification == best, reset on any other classified player move, and ignore null/unclassified moves so partial analysis uploads do not destroy streaks.
- Backend lightweight game support: add GET /api/stats/achievements returning the same all-time perfect_streak object so ChessGame can initialize personal best without loading the full stats summary. Reuse one helper for both endpoints.
- Frontend API/types: add StatsAchievementsSummary and PerfectStreakSummary types, extend StatsSummaryResponse, and add getStatsAchievements().
- Ordered live streak recompute: create a perfectStreak.ts domain helper that takes moveHistory, analysisMap, playerColor, previousPersonalBest, previousDerivedState/event state, and the live history boundary. It iterates move indices from 0 through moveHistory.length - 1 in move order, only considering player moves whose analysis.move matches moveHistory[index].uci, ignoring missing/unclassified/stale analyses, incrementing on classification === best and resetting on other classified player analyses. It returns current streak, best observed in retained live history, personal best, and an optional celebration event.
- Celebration idempotence: do not emit events merely because recompute sees an existing streak. Emit only when the derived state crosses a milestone/record from the previous derived state, or when the event key has not been celebrated in this game. ChessGame should keep lastCelebratedEventKey/lastCelebratedStreak refs, clear them on new game/reset, and trim/recompute them on revert so opponent analysis resolution, remount, or unrelated analysisMap changes do not replay streak 5/new-record toasts. Event keys should include event type plus streak value, e.g. milestone:5 or record:8.
- Async safety: do not update streak counters from lastAnalysis resolution order. Instead, subscribe to analysis-store changes and recompute from the full ordered retained history whenever analysisMap changes or moveHistory/playerColor changes. Ignore analyses outside current history or with mismatched UCI to avoid stale coordinator results after revert/remount.
- Revert/remount handling: derive displayed streak from recompute, not local event increments. On revert/reset/new game/remount, recompute against retained moveHistory and current analysisMap. Existing extra analysisMap entries for trimmed moves are harmless because the helper enforces the live boundary and UCI match; celebration refs prevent harmless recomputes from replaying toasts.
- Game UI: add PerfectStreakBadge to GameInfoPanel. Desktop displays after rating/opponent metadata and before opening as compact text using the existing ⭐ icon plus Best N. Mobile displays a fixed-width single-line badge in the top header row so it does not add a row. Badge is hidden when current streak is 0 unless personal best is shown post-game/inactive. Add hot/fire styling at long streak thresholds on the badge, not as a permanent board overlay.
- Board toast integration: extend BoardStage props with an optional streakToast object and render it inside .chessboard-board-area before the Chessboard, using a new .streak-toast style compatible with .blunder-toast absolute bottom-right positioning. ChessGame owns the transient toast timer and passes null when any higher-priority lane is active: start/revert/resign/promotion overlays, blunderAlert, isReviewMomentActive/resolvedReview, or showRehookToast. Drop suppressed streak toasts rather than queueing them; the badge still updates immediately. Streak 3 uses badge pulse only; streak 5+ and new personal best can show toast, with new record copy taking precedence.
- Stats page: add an Achievements or Move Quality card showing ⭐ Perfect streak / Best N. Label it All-time so it is clear it is not controlled by the window picker.

## Test Plan
- Backend pytest: stats summary empty data returns personal_best 0; mixed sessions compute only player-color best streaks; cross-session best streaks do not combine; non-best classified player moves reset; opponent best moves do not count; null classification rows are ignored; /api/stats/achievements matches the summary helper.
- Backend all-time/window regression: create a best streak outside window_days=30 and a lower/no streak inside the window; assert /api/stats/summary?window_days=30 achievements.perfect_streak.personal_best equals /api/stats/summary?window_days=0 and the achievements endpoint.
- Frontend unit tests: perfectStreak helper recomputes by move order, handles out-of-order analysis resolution, ignores stale UCI mismatches and indices outside moveHistory, resets on classified non-best moves, ignores unclassified results, detects milestone 3/5 and new records only on threshold crossing/uncelebrated event keys, and does not replay events on no-op recompute, opponent analysis resolution, or remount-like recompute.
- Component tests: GameInfoPanel renders compact desktop/mobile badge props without opening a new mobile row; BoardStage renders streakToast only when prop is present; StatsPage renders all-time perfect streak from summary.
- Integration/regression tests: ChessGame increments badge after best player analysis even if analyses resolve out of order, resets after later mistake/blunder, recomputes correctly after revert/remount, does not repeat streak toasts on harmless recomputes, shows new-record toast only when review/blunder/overlay messaging is inactive, and clears/recomputes celebration refs on new game/reset.
- Quality gates: npm run test:run; backend pytest for test_stats_api.py plus any new focused stats test module.

## Assumptions
- Perfect move means analysis classification exactly best, matching the existing MoveList ⭐.
- Personal best is all-time maximum single-session streak across uploaded session moves, independent of the selected stats window.
- No new DB table or migration is needed for v1; deriving from session_moves keeps historical data correct and avoids sync bugs.
- Unclassified moves are ignored rather than treated as streak breaks because analysis can upload incrementally or be incomplete.
notes: Addressed repeated-local-record review finding: record eligibility now compares against an effective known best that includes locally advanced previousPersonalBest after the baseline is known, while preserving delayed baseline-load record emission. Added regression: baseline 0 emits record 3, after reset reaching 3 again does not produce a record event. Verification: focused perfectStreak/ChessGame tests passed (51 tests); npm run build passed.

# g-ly5m: Linear Engine Analysis Progress

## Summary
Replace the circular engine depth spinner in AnalysisBoard with a 3px horizontal progress bar pinned to the top edge of .analysis-board__engine-header. The bar appears after Stockfish reports the first depth for the displayed FEN, fills determinately toward depth 21, and shows an animated shimmer inside the filled portion while thinking.

## Implementation Plan
- Add ENGINE_SEARCH_DEPTH = 21 in src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx and use it for Stockfish evaluatePosition calls and progress calculations.
- Derive cappedEngineDepth = Math.min(activeEngineDepth, ENGINE_SEARCH_DEPTH), use it for aria-valuenow and fill width, and keep the visible label as raw d{activeEngineDepth}.
- Render a non-focusable progressbar only when showEngineArrows && activeEngineDepth > 0, relying on activeEngineLines so stale engineInfoFen data remains hidden.
- Keep the depth text label, remove the circular .analysis-board__engine-spinner, and remove @keyframes engine-spin if no longer used.
- Make .analysis-board__engine-header position: relative and pin a 3px bar to top: 0; left: 0; right: 0 without changing header layout.
- Use a full-width track and a filled child with inline width cappedEngineDepth / ENGINE_SEARCH_DEPTH * 100; keep the shimmer inside the filled child with overflow hidden.
- Apply the animated class only while engineThinking is true.
- Update AnalysisBoard tests for depth progress, over-depth capping, disabled/stale visibility, and thinking animation state.

## Tests
Run npm run test:run -- src/components/AnalysisBoard.test.tsx and npm run build.
