description:
Rollup of the smaller findings from the 2026-07-02 CPL/accuracy audit (see also g-1l4p, g-hs78, g-no51). Each item is independently small; split out if any grows.

1. Avg CPL has no unknown state: contract is a non-nullable int defaulting to 0 (backend/app/api/history.py:138, pinned in test_history_api.py:165), so an unanalyzed game displays 0 — indistinguishable from perfect play — and a partially analyzed game averages whatever subset resolved. Accuracy got a None contract and a completeness gate; CPL got neither. Consider average_centipawn_loss: int | None plus frontend em-dash rendering.

2. Surface inconsistency: GameAnalysisPage runs projectExactBest (rewrites promoted moves to delta 0 / classification best) before computing side stats; HistoryPage feeds raw moves (src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx:201). Same game can show different Avg CPL and classification counts on /history vs the game-analysis page, and both can differ from the backend summary number. Either project on both surfaces or on neither.

3. Stuck computing indicator: after POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS, HistoryPage leaves analysisProcessing true forever (src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx:100-102) even though nothing server-side will ever complete a row-incomplete game — accuracy shows computing… indefinitely. Should fall back to the em-dash state.

4. /stats population mixing (backend/app/api/stats.py): quality_distribution counts player moves from ALL sessions in window including in-progress games, while accuracy_pct and mistake_free_game_rate use ended games only — same card, different denominators. Also accuracy_pct is an unweighted mean of per-game INTEGER accuracies (double rounding; a 10-move game weighs the same as a 60-move game). Defensible, but make it a documented decision.

5. Perf: accuracy is recomputed from raw move rows plus a python-chess PGN parse per game on every request — 50 parses per /history call, and ALL ended games ever on /stats?window_days=0. A persisted per-game accuracy column (recomputed on upload) removes the per-view cost and would also make g-hs78 backfill-able.

6. Nano: backend rounds ACPL with bankers rounding int(round(...)) while the frontend uses Math.round — ±1 divergence on exact halves. compute_game_accuracy derives the mover from index parity but eval perspective from move.color — safe today only behind the completeness gate; a cheap consistency assert would pin it.

title: Cheap/incremental opening-score freshness signal (replace O(evidence) row-hash digest)
description:
# Cheap/incremental opening-score freshness signal (replace the O(evidence) row-hash digest)

## Problem
`_is_batch_fresh` (`backend/app/opening_cache.py:380`) proves a cached opening-score batch is current
by recomputing `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` (`backend/app/opening_evidence.py:646`) and comparing it
to the fingerprint stored on the batch. That digest is **O(all of the user's evidence)**: it
full-scans + string-hashes every `session_moves` row, normalizes thousands of candidate FENs through
python-chess in a Python loop, and `IN`-queries `analysis_cache` / `position_analysis`. For a heavy
user (user 14: ~22k `session_moves`, ~9k distinct candidate FENs) it costs ~1.3s quiescent and up to
~3.2–9.6s under GIL contention with a running recompute.

This is the root cost behind every slow path that needs a freshness verdict:
- session/drill start baseline snapshot (`snapshot_opening_baseline`) — being moved OFF the hot path
  by Option 1 (sibling bead g-mxeo), but the digest still runs, just on a worker;
- the end-of-session delta poll `read_opening_score_delta` (`opening_score_delta.py:329`);
- the scheduler's own fast-path gate in `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed`.

Options 1 and 2 in g-mxeo only RELOCATE or WEAKEN the proof. This bead makes the proof itself cheap, so
freshness can be asserted in O(1)-ish for every caller — the principled fix.

## Direction (to be finalized in plan mode)
Replace the full-row-hash digest with a cheap, monotonic freshness signal that is equivalent for
"did any consumed evidence change?":

- **Watermark approach:** per `(user_id, player_color)`, a tuple of
  `max(updated_at)` + `row_count` over the exact tables/filters the overlay consumes (`session_moves`
  joined to in-scope `game_sessions`, the `analysis_cache` / `position_analysis` trusted subset,
  blunders, blunder_reviews). Store it on the batch alongside `inputs_fingerprint`; freshness =
  watermark matches. Needs an `updated_at` (or equivalent monotonic column) on every consumed table —
  audit which already have one; `session_moves` / `analysis_cache` may need one added + backfilled.
  Edge: row_count alone misses update-in-place; pairing with max(updated_at) covers it, but a
  delete+insert keeping count and an older max could alias — bound this by also tracking max(id) or a
  per-table change counter. Quantify alias risk before committing.
- **Maintained running digest approach:** keep an incrementally-updated digest/counter per
  `(user,color)` advanced wherever evidence is written (the `/moves` evidence txn, SRS review writes,
  blunder recording), stored and compared in O(1). More invasive (every writer must bump it) but
  exact and immune to the watermark aliasing edge.

Either way: keep `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` as the SLOW-PATH oracle used to (a) seed/repair the
cheap signal and (b) cover semantic-only changes already folded in via
`OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION`. The cheap signal is the fast gate; the full digest remains the
source of truth on a cheap-signal miss or version bump.

## Blast radius
Touches `_is_batch_fresh` and every caller (`proven_fresh_opening_scores`, `read_opening_score_delta`,
`recompute_opening_scores_if_needed`, the Option-1 background baseline job), the batch schema
(new stored signal column(s) + alembic + conftest `_create_test_schema`), and possibly an
`updated_at`/counter column + backfill on `session_moves` and `analysis_cache`. Larger and
higher-risk than g-mxeo — do it as its own epic-sized effort after Option 1 lands.

## Acceptance criteria
A freshness verdict for an already-built batch is computed without scanning/hashing all of a user's
evidence (no `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` call on the fast path); freshness is provably equivalent to
the current digest (false-negatives allowed = unnecessary-but-correct rebuild; NO false-positives =
never serve a stale batch as fresh), verified by a property/differential test against the existing
digest across mutation scenarios (insert move, update eval, add review, registry/version bump).

## Relationship
Complementary to g-mxeo (Option 1), not a replacement. g-mxeo removes the digest from the START path
now; this bead removes its cost from ALL paths and can later simplify g-mxeo's background job back into
a cheap synchronous check.
design:
# g-jact — Cheap/incremental opening-score freshness signal

## Context

Every path that needs a "is this cached opening-score batch still current?" verdict pays
`opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` → `raw_evidence_inputs_digest`
(`backend/app/opening_evidence.py:956`), which is **O(all of a user's evidence)**: it full-scans +
string-hashes ~22k `session_moves` rows, normalizes ~9k candidate FENs through python-chess in a
Python loop (the dominant CPU cost), and `IN`-queries `analysis_cache` / `position_analysis`. It
costs ~1.3s quiescent and 3–10s under GIL contention. Callers: the async start-baseline snapshot
(`proven_fresh_opening_scores`), the end-of-session delta poll (`read_opening_score_delta`), and the
scheduler's fast-path gate (`recompute_opening_scores_if_needed`). g-mxeo moved these off the request
thread but the cost still burns worker time.

Goal: prove freshness in ~O(1) on the common path, provably equivalent to the current digest —
**false-negatives OK (harmless rebuild), NO false-positives (never serve stale as fresh)** — verified
by a differential test against the existing digest.

## What the digest actually consumes (verified)

The digest reads six evidence surfaces. They split by attributability:

| # | Surface | Table(s) | Scope | Write mode | Monotonic col? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | session moves | `session_moves` ⋈ `game_sessions` (eligibility) | **per-user** | UPDATE-IN-PLACE (post-end eval backfill) + INSERT, both inside `upsert_session_moves` (see S1 bump site for the two commit paths) | none (id not bumped on update) |
| S2 | eligibility | `game_sessions.status/drill_state/drill_terminal_reason` | **per-user** | UPDATE-IN-PLACE | `ended_at` set on end, **but NOT on accuracy-fail** |
| S3 | move-grain cache | `analysis_cache` at candidate `fen_before` | **shared, FEN-keyed** | UPDATE-IN-PLACE replace (`_apply_update`) + INSERT | `created_at` insert-only; no `updated_at` |
| S4 | position-grain cache | `analysis_cache` at candidate `normalized_fen_before` + `position_analysis` at norm | **shared, FEN-keyed** | UPDATE-IN-PLACE + INSERT | `position_analysis.updated_at` yes; `analysis_cache` no |
| S5 | ghost targets | `blunders` ⋈ `positions` ⋈ `game_sessions` | **per-user** | INSERT-only content (eligibility via S2) | `created_at` |
| S6 | reviews | `blunder_reviews` ⋈ `blunders` | **per-user** | INSERT-only (re-review = new row) | `reviewed_at` |

**Why neither "pure" option in the bead works:**
- A maintained **per-user counter** cannot cover S3/S4: analysis writes are FEN-keyed and shared, and
  no FEN→user index exists (confirmed — the writers never map a FEN back to affected users).
- A **max(updated_at)+count watermark** cannot cover S1 (in-place eval backfill, no timestamp), S3
  (in-place replace, no `updated_at`), or the accuracy-failed-drill eligibility flip in S2 (no
  timestamp at all) — and it still needs the candidate-FEN normalize loop it's trying to avoid.

So we **partition** the surfaces and use the right mechanism for each.

## Design — partitioned freshness signal (chosen)

Store three things on each batch at build time, then check them in order:

1. **Per-user surfaces (S1,S2,S5,S6) → maintained counter `evidence_seq(user, player_color)`.**
   A durable per-(user,color) integer bumped in every transaction that mutates a per-user surface
   (see *Writer bump sites*). Immune to the in-place/no-timestamp problem because a counter bump does
   not depend on any row timestamp. Home: add an `evidence_seq` column to the existing
   `opening_score_cursors` table (already keyed `(user_id, player_color)`); bumping upserts the row so
   it works before any batch exists.

2. **Shared surfaces (S3,S4) → global counter `cache_epoch` + per-batch scoped shared digest.**
   - `cache_epoch`: a single global integer advanced by **mandatory DB triggers** on `analysis_cache`
     and `position_analysis` (AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE — no app-level bump calls; see *Writer bump
     sites* for why triggers are the sole mechanism). Decision outcomes that issue no SQL (KEEP /
     INVALID / no-op merges — and ORM setattrs that change nothing) naturally fire no trigger, so
     "only genuine writes bump" falls out for free. Home: new 1-row table `evidence_epoch`.
   - **Scoped shared digest**: at build time, capture this batch's shared-FEN scope — the raw
     candidate `fen_before` set (for exact S3 move-grain lookups) and the normalized-FEN set (for S4
     `position_analysis` + legacy `analysis_cache` position lookups) — and store a hash over *only*
     the shared lines (`AC|`, `PA|`, `ACP|`) computed over that scope. This lets a `cache_epoch` drift
     be resolved by re-hashing just this batch's positions, **without** re-scanning session moves or
     re-running the normalize loop.

3. **Registry/semantics → `registry_fingerprint`, now made all-inclusive.** Today
   `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` is folded only into the *raw* fingerprint
   (`opening_cache.py:157`), NOT into `registry_fingerprint` (`opening_score_inputs_fingerprint`,
   `opening_cache.py:115`). Once the fast path stops computing the raw fingerprint, a future
   `raw-v5→raw-v6` semantic bump would be invisible to `cheap_fresh` on already-stamped batches — a
   **false-positive**. Fix: fold **`OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION`** *and* a new
   **`FRESHNESS_CONTRACT_VERSION`** (bumped whenever the cheap-signal semantics — scope definition,
   scoped-digest formatting — change) into `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint`, so the O(1)
   `registry_fingerprint` comparison covers every version/semantic surface. Drop the now-redundant
   explicit fold in the raw fingerprint (it inherits both transitively via `registry_fp`).

**The full `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` is retained ONLY as (a) the differential-test reference and
(b) the source-of-truth digest still computed on the *rebuild* branch (stored as `inputs_fingerprint`).
It is NOT on the normal freshness path, and there is no "seed a NULL-signal batch from the oracle"
machinery** — see the REPAIR note below for why that half was cut.

### Freshness algorithm (replaces `_is_batch_fresh`)

```
cheap_fresh(batch, rows) -> bool:
    if registry_fingerprint != batch.registry_fingerprint:            return False   # registry+evidence-inputs+contract versions (all O(1))
    if batch.evidence_seq is None or batch.cache_epoch is None:       return False   # pre-migration / unstamped → treat as stale → rebuild (see REPAIR note)
    epoch = current_cache_epoch()  # SELECT value FROM evidence_epoch WHERE id=1
    if epoch is None:                                                 return False   # singleton row missing → cannot prove → rebuild
    if current_evidence_seq(user,color) != batch.evidence_seq:        return False   # S1/S2/S5/S6 changed → candidate scope may differ → rebuild
    if _batch_has_stale_branch_keys(rows):                            return False   # (existing check, kept)
    if epoch == batch.cache_epoch:                                   return True    # O(1) FAST ACCEPT
    # cache_epoch drifted: some shared write happened SOMEWHERE.
    scoped = scoped_shared_digest(db, batch.shared_scope)   # re-hash AC|/PA|/ACP| over STORED scope (sample epoch BEFORE this read)
    if scoped == batch.scoped_shared_digest:
        best_effort_rearm(batch, epoch)                    # mark caught-up so next check is O(1) again
        return True
    return False                                            # a shared row AT THIS BATCH'S POSITIONS changed → rebuild
```

Note: `evidence_seq` mismatch goes straight to rebuild (not the scoped path) — because a per-user
change can add/remove candidate FENs, so the stored scope is no longer valid. This matches today's
behavior (any per-user change already forces a full digest mismatch → rebuild).

**REPAIR = "treat as stale → rebuild" (no separate oracle-reseed code path).** An earlier draft had a
distinct REPAIR outcome that seeded a NULL-signal batch from the full oracle. **That machinery is dead
on arrival and is cut:** rollout folds `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` (`raw-v4→raw-v5`) into
`registry_fingerprint`, so *every* pre-migration batch fails the **first** check (registry) and
rebuilds — control never reaches the NULL-`evidence_seq` line during rollout. Post-migration the writer
*always* stamps the signals, so a NULL there means a genuinely corrupt/partial batch, which we also
want to just rebuild. So the two "unstamped/missing-singleton" lines simply `return False`; they are a
defensive belt-and-suspenders, not a separate code path. The full digest survives only as the rebuild
digest + the differential-test reference. Net: **less code, identical behavior.**

**`best_effort_rearm` discipline (it is a WRITE on read paths — Finding 7).** The scoped-fresh branch
calls `best_effort_rearm(batch, epoch)` from callers that are logically reads: `read_opening_score_delta`
is a GET, and the baseline job holds its own session. The rearm `UPDATE opening_score_batches SET
cache_epoch = :epoch` MUST therefore:
- run in a **short, independent transaction/session** of its own — never the caller's — so it cannot
  leave the caller's transaction in a dirty or failed state;
- **swallow lock contention** (notably sqlite `"database is locked"`) and any error: a failed re-arm
  only costs one extra scoped re-check next time, so it must never propagate;
- **not** be required for correctness — it is a pure optimization that restores the O(1) fast-accept.

Concurrent re-arms racing on the same batch are **safe**: each stamps an `epoch` value it sampled
*before its own scoped read*, so even a "stale" writer's stamp is a valid lower bound — the worst case
is one extra re-check on the next call, never a false accept. (Same lower-bound discipline as build;
see below.)

### Sampling/ordering invariant (critical for no-false-positive)

`evidence_seq` and `cache_epoch` must be sampled **BEFORE** the evidence read they describe — both at
batch build and at scoped re-arm — so the stamped value is a **lower bound** on the read. Then any
write landing during/after the read advances the live counter *above* the stamp → future check sees a
mismatch → harmless rebuild. (This is the **opposite** of `computed_at`, which g-mxeo samples *after*
the read as an upper bound for time-decay. Document both.) A write that lands mid-read but is included
in the batch only causes an unnecessary rebuild (allowed), never a false accept.

### Soundness (no false-positive)

`cheap_fresh` returns True only when registry + version match, **and** `evidence_seq` matches (⇒ no
S1/S2/S5/S6 change since build ⇒ candidate scope unchanged), **and** either `cache_epoch` matches (⇒
no shared write anywhere) or the scoped shared digest over the (unchanged) scope matches (⇒ no shared
change at this batch's positions). Every input to `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` is therefore unchanged
⇒ digest identical ⇒ overlay identical ⇒ scores identical. The only residual hazard is a writer that
mutates a surface without bumping its counter — mitigated by centralizing bumps at the choke-points
below and by the differential test that mutates every surface.

## Schema changes (models + alembic + conftest `_create_test_schema` — all three, per repo rule)

- `opening_score_cursors`: add `evidence_seq BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (per-(user,color) counter).
  **Add a model-column comment** stating the out-of-band-writer contract (any migration/script mutating
  `session_moves`/`game_sessions`/`blunders`/`blunder_reviews` must bump `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION`
  or advance the affected cursors — see Risks). Note `reserve_opening_score_generation` also upserts this
  row; its DO-UPDATE `set_` must stay single-column (`latest_generation`) so it never clobbers
  `evidence_seq` (see *Writer bump sites* / Finding 1).
- `opening_score_batches`: add `evidence_seq BIGINT NULL`, `cache_epoch BIGINT NULL`,
  `scoped_shared_digest TEXT NULL` (NULL on pre-migration batches → `cheap_fresh` returns False → rebuild
  re-stamps them; see the REPAIR note — no separate reseed path).
- New table `evidence_epoch (id INT PK CHECK(id=1), value BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)` — global
  shared-cache epoch (single row). **The migration AND conftest MUST seed the singleton row**
  (`INSERT INTO evidence_epoch(id, value) VALUES (1, 0)`): the triggers do `UPDATE ... WHERE id=1`,
  which silently no-ops if the row is missing → epoch never advances → false-positives. **Mandatory**
  `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` triggers on `analysis_cache` and `position_analysis` increment
  `evidence_epoch.value` (dialect-specific DDL in models-comment/alembic/conftest; Postgres
  statement-level, sqlite row-level) — see *Writer bump sites*.
- No new version constant lives in the DB: `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` and the new
  `FRESHNESS_CONTRACT_VERSION` are code constants folded into `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint`, so
  they ride in the existing `registry_fingerprint` column (no schema change for versioning).
- New child table `opening_score_batch_shared_scope (id PK, batch_id FK→opening_score_batches
  ON DELETE CASCADE, fen TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT CHECK kind IN ('raw','norm'))`, indexed on
  `batch_id`. Stores this batch's raw candidate `fen_before` set and normalized-FEN set. Matches the
  existing per-batch child-table idiom (`user_opening_scores`, `opening_position_scores`) and cascades
  on retention prune. (Alt: two JSON `Text` columns on the batch — simpler but ~1 MB/batch and less
  idiomatic.)

Files: `backend/app/models.py`, a new `backend/alembic/versions/2026xxxx_*.py`
(pattern: `20260625_01_add_opening_score_baseline.py`), and `backend/conftest.py` `_create_test_schema`.

## Writer bump sites

Add a Python helper `session_is_evidence_eligible(session) -> bool` mirroring
`SESSION_EVIDENCE_ELIGIBLE_SQL` exactly: `status == 'ended' OR (drill_state == 'failed' AND
drill_terminal_reason == 'accuracy')`. (Note: the existing `_should_run_session_move_evidence`,
`session.py:811`, is NOT this gate — it permits live/active sessions and only excludes
abandoned/ended-unconverted drills.)

`bump_evidence_seq(db, user_id, player_color)` — advances the per-(user,color) counter on
`opening_score_cursors`, in the **same txn** as the write it accounts for (it executes the upsert
statement but does **not** commit; the caller's commit flushes it — so the bump and the evidence write
are atomic together, and a rolled-back write rolls back its bump).

**MANDATORY: the increment MUST be an atomic in-DB column expression, never a read-modify-write.** A
Python read (`SELECT evidence_seq`) → `+1` → `UPDATE` loses bumps under concurrency: two transactions
that both read `seq=5` and write `6` collapse two changes into one advance — the exact false-positive
this bead forbids (if a batch build samples `seq=6` between their commits, it misses the second change
yet matches forever). Mirror `reserve_opening_score_generation` (`opening_cache.py:294-313`) **per
dialect**:
- sqlite: `sqlite_insert(...).on_conflict_do_update(index_elements=[user_id, player_color],
  set_={"evidence_seq": OpeningScoreCursor.evidence_seq + 1})`
- postgresql: the `postgresql_insert` equivalent.
- generic fallback (last branch of `reserve`, non-sqlite/pg — unused in practice): the same
  read-modify-write `reserve` uses is acceptable there, since those dialects aren't run.

The DB evaluating `evidence_seq + 1` as a column expression under the ON-CONFLICT row lock is what
makes concurrent bumps compose (`+1` applied twice ⇒ `+2`, no lost bump) — the atomicity is at the SQL
statement / row-lock level, independent of transaction isolation.

**Both `bump_evidence_seq` and `reserve_opening_score_generation` write the SAME composite-PK row
`(user_id, player_color)` of `opening_score_cursors` from independent transactions.** To avoid one
clobbering the other's column, each upsert's `set_` must touch **exactly one** column:
`bump_evidence_seq`'s `set_` = `{evidence_seq: evidence_seq + 1}` only; `reserve`'s `set_` =
`{latest_generation: latest_generation + 1}` only (it already does — leave it). The `.values(...)`
insert branch of each still supplies both columns (falling back to the schema default for the one it
doesn't own), but the DO-UPDATE branch that fires on the existing row must be single-column.

Call `bump_evidence_seq` wherever a per-user surface changes, **gated so a bump fires only
when the write actually changes the digest's evidence set** (else per-move live-game writes would
recreate the recompute churn the eligibility exclusion was built to avoid — the digest excludes active
sessions, `opening_evidence.py:83/1001`):
- **S1** `session_moves`: inside `upsert_session_moves`, **before commit**, gated on
  **`session_is_evidence_eligible(game_session)`**. `upsert_session_moves` has **two** mutation-and-commit
  paths and a single bump at this level covers **both**: (a) the generic-dialect read/UPDATE-or-INSERT
  loop with `db.commit()` (`session.py:1116-1130`, commit at `:1134`), and (b) the Postgres/SQLite
  `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` path (`session.py:1168-1198`, `db.execute(statement); db.commit()`).
  Do **not** try to bump only "on the backfill UPDATE branch" — the ON-CONFLICT path is a single
  statement that inserts-or-updates without telling us which, so bump once per eligible upload
  regardless. (`session.py:1042` is the analytics-emit helper `_emit_session_moves_uploaded`, **not** a
  session_moves mutation — do not hook there.) A live/active session's per-move uploads do NOT bump
  (fails the eligibility gate); the eligibility transition (below) folds all its moves in with one bump.
  A post-end eval-backfill upload (session already `ended`) DOES bump.
- **S2** eligibility transitions (flip already-uploaded moves eligible/ineligible without touching S1):
  status→'ended' (`api/game.py:715`, `api/drills.py:498`, `api/drills.py:527`); the accuracy-fail path
  `drill_state='failed' + drill_terminal_reason='accuracy'` (`api/drills.py:333`); **and the
  drill→converted path** `continue_drill` (`api/drills.py:363-370`) — converting an eligible
  `failed+accuracy` drill to `drill_state='converted'` REMOVES it from the evidence set (a
  digest-visible change), and it also calls `resegment_session_moves`. **Rule: bump iff
  `session_is_evidence_eligible(session)` changes truth value across the transition** — capture it
  before and after and bump only on a flip. A literal "any write to `status`/`drill_state`/
  `drill_terminal_reason`" would over-bump on transitions that leave eligibility unchanged — e.g.
  `active → root_reached` (`api/game.py:927`, and the additional `drill_state → 'root_reached'` writes
  at `api/game.py:936` and `api/drills.py:416` that agents surfaced) or `failed + off_route`
  (`api/drills.py:444`), all still ineligible per `opening_evidence.py:95` — reintroducing the perf churn
  (a false-negative, not a stale-data bug). **The extra `root_reached` sites need no special handling:
  the truth-value rule already covers them — `root_reached` is ineligible both before and after, so
  eligibility doesn't flip → no bump.** Concrete flip sites (the only ones that bump): end (F→T),
  accuracy-fail (F→T), natural-end fail (F→T via `status='ended'`), convert (T→F). `started_at` is confirmed **immutable** (set only at insert: `game.py:642`,
  `drills.py:269`; no UPDATE anywhere) so it needs no coverage; `segment` (what `resegment` rewrites)
  is not read by the digest, so the convert bump is driven by the eligibility flip, not resegment.
- **S5** `blunders`: new-row insert in `_upsert_blunder_target` (`api/blunder.py:247`, called from
  `_record_target` with `source_session_id=session.id` during gameplay, `blunder.py:309-317`). **Gate:
  bump only if `source_session_id IS NULL` (manual blunder — always a ghost target) OR the source
  session is currently `session_is_evidence_eligible`.** A live-game blunder whose source session is
  still active is not yet a ghost target (`opening_evidence.py:1168` join), so its later session
  eligibility transition carries the bump.
  **Which `player_color` to bump (getting this wrong is a false positive):** the digest scopes ghost
  targets by the *source session's* `player_color`, falling back to `positions.active_color` for
  sessionless blunders (`opening_evidence.py:1173-1176`). At the `_record_target` site the source
  session is in hand → bump `session.player_color`. For any manual/sessionless insert path
  (`source_session_id IS NULL`) bump `positions.active_color` of the blunder's position. (Both cases
  are exactly `_get_blunder_player_color`'s rule, `srs.py:55` — reuse it if a single site covers both.)
- **S6** `blunder_reviews`: new-row insert in the SRS path (`api/srs.py:156`, next to the existing
  `request_recompute` at `:189`). Bump unconditionally *w.r.t. eligibility* — reviews are low-frequency
  user actions (no per-move churn concern), so gating is unnecessary; at worst a review of a
  not-yet-eligible blunder triggers one harmless rebuild.
  **Which `player_color` to bump:** the digest scopes reviews the same way as S5 — source session's
  `player_color`, else `positions.active_color` (`opening_evidence.py:1187-1195`). **Use the existing
  `_get_blunder_player_color(db, blunder)` helper (`srs.py:55`), which encodes exactly this rule, and
  skip the bump when it returns `None`.** A `None` result provably corresponds to a blunder whose
  review is excluded from *both* colors' digests (no source session AND no position active_color match),
  so no digest consumes it → skipping the bump is correct, not a gap.
  **Do NOT add a bump for the SRS path's in-place writes to `blunders.pass_streak` /
  `blunders.last_reviewed_at`** (also on `api/srs.py`): the digest consumes only the *review rows*
  (`blunder_reviews.passed/reviewed_at`) and the ghost-target `fen_raw`, never `pass_streak` or
  `last_reviewed_at` (see the S6 SQL, `opening_evidence.py:1185-1197`). A future author might reflexively
  "also bump on the streak update" — that would be harmless-but-wasteful over-bumping; the single
  new-review-row bump is complete and correct coverage for S6.

`cache_epoch` — **DB triggers are the sole, mandatory mechanism (no app-level bump calls).** The
shared tables are global (no per-user attribution needed) and their writers are irreducibly scattered
across independent transactions: `write_analysis_cache_rows` opens its own isolated session/engine and
owns the txn (`analysis_cache_repo.py:582-621` — a bump bolted onto the public caller would be in the
wrong transaction), `repair_analysis_cache.apply_invalidation` DELETEs rows directly outside the writer
(`scripts/repair_analysis_cache.py:127`), and `position_analysis_backfill._upsert_winner` writes via
plain ORM (`position_analysis_backfill.py:260`). An `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` trigger on
`analysis_cache` and on `position_analysis`, incrementing `evidence_epoch.value`, fires for *every*
writer (present and future) including deletes — closing the repair-delete false-positive gap and the
forgotten-bump hazard uniformly, without touching any writer's code. DDL goes in the alembic migration
and the hand-written conftest schema (Postgres `FOR EACH STATEMENT`; sqlite `FOR EACH ROW`). Row-level
bumping N times per batch is harmless (magnitude is irrelevant — only change matters).
(`evidence_seq` stays app-level: it needs per-(user,color) attribution the FEN-keyed triggers can't
provide, and it needs the eligibility gate above.)

## Reader / caller changes (`backend/app/opening_cache.py`, `opening_score_delta.py`)

- Fold `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` + new `FRESHNESS_CONTRACT_VERSION` into
  `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint` (`opening_cache.py:115`); drop the redundant explicit fold in
  `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` (`opening_cache.py:157`). Now `registry_fingerprint` carries
  every version surface, so `cheap_fresh`'s O(1) registry check catches semantic bumps.
- Rewrite `_is_batch_fresh` (`opening_cache.py:395`) to the algorithm above. Add helpers
  `current_evidence_seq`, `current_cache_epoch`, `scoped_shared_digest`, `best_effort_rearm`,
  `session_is_evidence_eligible`.
- Refactor `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` (`opening_evidence.py:956`) to build lines in two labeled
  groups (per-user: `SM|`/`GT|`/`BR|`; shared: `AC|`/`PA|`/`ACP|`) so `scoped_shared_digest` reuses
  the exact shared-line SQL/formatting over a *supplied* FEN scope (guarantees scoped == full-slice by
  construction). **The stored scope MUST be the digest's own BROAD candidate set** — the
  `candidate_fens`/`norm_keys` derived at `opening_evidence.py:1035-1059` (every eligible player-color
  move lacking a primary eval), **NOT** the overlay's narrower `_apply_cache_fallbacks` candidates
  (opening-interval premoves only). Capturing from the digest derivation is what makes scoped ==
  full-slice; a narrower scope would let `cheap_fresh` accept while the full digest changed at a
  non-opening candidate FEN (a false-positive). Capture the scope inside this function and persist it.
- `recompute_opening_scores_if_needed` (`opening_cache.py:1116`): replace the unconditional
  `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` fast-gate with `cheap_fresh`. Compute the full digest only on
  the **rebuild** branch (stored as `inputs_fingerprint`, retained as the source-of-truth digest + the
  differential-test reference — not for any oracle-reseed path, which was cut per the REPAIR note); stamp
  `evidence_seq`, `cache_epoch`, scope rows, and `scoped_shared_digest` on the new batch (sampled
  before the evidence read).
- `recompute_opening_scores` writer (`opening_cache.py:874`): accept + persist the new signal fields +
  scope rows alongside `inputs_fingerprint`. **Extend the existing "prebuilt overlay requires matching
  fingerprint" invariant (`opening_cache.py:884-901`) to the whole freshness bundle**: pass
  `(inputs_fingerprint, evidence_seq, cache_epoch, shared_scope, scoped_shared_digest)` as one required
  `FreshnessSnapshot` object, sampled **before** the overlay evidence read (same lower-bound discipline
  as the fingerprint today); when `overlay` is supplied the snapshot must be supplied too (raise
  otherwise, before the generation reservation). This prevents stamping a newer signal onto an older
  overlay — the exact hazard the current guard exists to prevent.
- `proven_fresh_opening_scores` (`:434`) and the delta poll now get the cheap verdict for free. **Leave
  each caller's scheduler gate exactly as it is — they are NOT uniform, so do not "restore" one that
  never existed:**
  - `proven_fresh_opening_scores` has **no scheduler gate at all** (its docstring: "NEVER touches the
    scheduler"). Keep it gate-free.
  - `read_opening_score_delta` uses `is_recompute_scheduled` (`opening_score_delta.py:547-550`). Keep.
  - `_capture_baseline_json` uses the narrower `is_recompute_inflight` (`opening_score_delta.py:136-138`),
    **not** `is_recompute_scheduled`. Keep.
  This change swaps only *how freshness is proven* (`cheap_fresh` in place of the raw digest); it does
  not add, remove, or move any scheduler gate.

## Rollout / self-heal

Bump `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` (`opening_evidence.py:77`, `raw-v4`→`raw-v5`) and add
`FRESHNESS_CONTRACT_VERSION = "fresh-v1"`. Both now ride in `registry_fingerprint`, so every existing
batch mismatches on the **first (registry) check** → `return False` → rebuild → stamps the new signals.
(The NULL-`evidence_seq`/`cache_epoch` lines never even execute during rollout, since the registry check
short-circuits first — they only guard genuinely-corrupt post-migration batches; see the REPAIR note.)
**No data backfill script needed** (a key advantage over watermark columns, which would require
backfilling 22k `session_moves` rows). The migration seeds `evidence_epoch(1, 0)`; new instances start
clean.

## Testing (acceptance criteria)

New `backend/test_opening_freshness_signal.py`, reusing `test_opening_evidence.py` helpers
(`_insert_user/_insert_session/_insert_move/_insert_blunder/_insert_position`) and the mutation-test
style at `test_opening_evidence.py:804-912`.

- **Core no-false-positive property** — for each scenario: build a batch, mutate, assert
  `cheap_fresh(batch) == True ⟹ raw digest unchanged`:
  1. insert eligible session_move → seq bumps → stale
  2. **backfill eval on existing move in place** → seq bumps → stale *(watermark would miss)*
  3. end a session (active→ended) → eligibility flip → seq bumps → stale
  4. **fail a drill on accuracy** (no timestamp) → seq bumps → stale *(watermark would miss)*
  5. insert `analysis_cache` at a **candidate** fen → epoch bumps, scoped digest changes → stale
  6. **replace `analysis_cache` in place** at a candidate fen → epoch bumps, scoped changes → stale *(watermark would miss)*
  7. insert/replace `analysis_cache` at a **non-candidate** fen → epoch bumps, scoped **unchanged** →
     **fresh** (re-arm) — assert full digest also unchanged *(the whole point: unrelated shared churn ≠ rebuild)*
  8. add `position_analysis` winner at a candidate norm → epoch bumps, scoped changes → stale
  9. **DELETE an `analysis_cache` row at a candidate fen** (repair-invalidation path) → epoch bumps,
     scoped changes → stale *(the direct-delete gap; false-positives without the epoch bump/trigger)*
  10. **convert an eligible accuracy-failed drill** (`continue_drill`) → seq bumps → stale
  11. add ghost-target blunder → seq bumps → stale
  12. add blunder_review → seq bumps → stale
  13. bump `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` **or** `FRESHNESS_CONTRACT_VERSION` → `registry_fingerprint`
      changes → stale, and assert the raw digest was NOT called **on the verdict path**
      (`cheap_fresh`/`_is_batch_fresh`) — O(1) version coverage. (The subsequent *rebuild*
      still computes the full digest to stamp the new batch — that's expected and out of scope for this
      assertion.)
  14. registry/graph change → stale
  15. no-op → fresh
- **No-churn (eligibility-gating) scenarios** — assert a bump does NOT fire and `cheap_fresh` stays
  **fresh** with the full digest **also unchanged** (parity with the active-session exclusion):
  16. upload a move to a **live/active** session → no seq bump → fresh *(the churn guard)*
  17. record a blunder whose **source session is still active** → no seq bump → fresh; then end that
      session → seq bumps → stale *(S5 source-eligibility gate)*
  18. a **non-eligibility-changing** transition (`active → root_reached`, or `failed + off_route`) →
      eligibility truth value unchanged → no seq bump → fresh, digest unchanged *(S2 truth-value rule)*
- **Broad-scope regression** *(digest-scope-not-overlay-scope)*: mutate the `analysis_cache` row of a **non-opening**
  candidate FEN (an eligible player-color move lacking a primary eval that is NOT an opening premove)
  → epoch bumps, scoped digest changes → stale. Guards against capturing only the overlay's narrower
  fallback candidates.
- **Atomic-increment / concurrency** *(this review's Finding 1)*: two `bump_evidence_seq(u, c)` calls in
  independent sessions that both start from `seq=N` must leave `seq == N+2` (no lost bump). Assert the
  implementation uses the ON-CONFLICT column-expression form, not a Python read-modify-write. Also assert
  a `bump_evidence_seq` interleaved with a `reserve_opening_score_generation` on the same
  `(user,color)` row leaves **both** `evidence_seq` and `latest_generation` correctly advanced (neither
  clobbers the other's column). Under sqlite's serialized writer this is deterministic; a thread/txn
  interleaving test is sufficient.
- **Player-color scoping** *(this review's Finding 2)*: a bump attributed to one color must not mark the
  other color's batch stale.
  - build fresh batches for both `(u, white)` and `(u, black)`; add a ghost-target blunder whose source
    session is `black` → **only** the black batch goes stale; white stays fresh (assert full digest for
    white also unchanged).
  - S6 `None`-skip: a review of a blunder with no source session AND a `positions.active_color` that
    matches neither color's digest → `_get_blunder_player_color` returns `None` → **no** bump for either
    color, and the full digest for both colors is unchanged (proves skip-on-None is not a false-fresh).
- **Randomized differential loop**: apply a random sequence of the above; after each, assert
  `cheap_fresh ⟹ digest_unchanged`. Strongest guarantee against false-positives.
- **Re-arm test**: scenario 7 twice — second check is O(1) (epoch caught up), asserted via a spy that
  `scoped_shared_digest` is not recomputed.
- **Expected fallout in existing tests (update these, don't just "rerun the suite").** Folding the
  version(s) into `registry_fingerprint` and dropping the explicit fold in
  `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint` changes the hash *composition*, so tests that patch
  `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` or assert a computed `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint`/
  `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint` value will move and must be updated in this change:
  - `test_drill_api.py:1674` — patches/asserts around `raw_evidence_inputs_digest`.
  - `test_game_api.py:2023` — same.
  - `test_opening_cache.py` — fingerprint-composition expectations.
  - `test_opening_score_delta.py` — fingerprint / freshness expectations.
  Grep `raw_evidence_inputs_digest`, `opening_score_raw_inputs_fingerprint`,
  `opening_score_inputs_fingerprint`, and `_is_batch_fresh` across `backend/test_*.py` before landing to
  catch any others. These are *expected* churn, not regressions.
- Regression: full backend suite (`opening_cache`, `opening_evidence`, `opening_score_delta`,
  baseline scheduler). Note the flaky-under-parallel-load pre-push hook — rerun named files in
  isolation before trusting a failure.

## Verification (end-to-end)

Boot uvicorn on a throwaway sqlite `DATABASE_URL` (per repo note; never touch `.opening_graph_cache`),
seed a heavy user, and confirm via the timing logs that a warm freshness check no longer calls
`raw_evidence_inputs_digest` on the fast path (add a debug counter/log around the digest) and that the
start-baseline / delta-poll worker timings drop from ~1.3s to ~O(1) on the fast path.

**Read the timing logs correctly — the "O(1) fast accept" holds only when the shared cache is
quiescent.** The three-tier cost of a warm check:
- shared cache quiescent (`epoch == batch.cache_epoch`): genuinely **O(1)** — two integer reads
  (`evidence_seq`, `evidence_epoch`) plus the existing branch-key check. This is the steady-state win.
- shared cache drifting (a recompute wave is actively writing `analysis_cache`, so `evidence_epoch`
  advances continuously and the fast-accept never hits): every check falls to the **scoped shared
  digest** — the AC/PA/ACP `IN`-queries over this batch's *stored* ~9k-FEN scope. That still skips the
  session-move full-scan AND the python-chess normalize loop (the digest's dominant cost), so it's
  likely **low hundreds of ms**, not the ~1.3s full digest — but it is NOT O(1). Expect the timing logs
  to show this tier during/right after a recompute wave.
- The always-avoided cost regardless of tier: the ~22k-row `session_moves` scan + normalize loop, which
  `raw_evidence_inputs_digest` runs and neither warm tier does.

So the claim is: **O(1) when quiescent; scoped-digest (still a large win, no scan/normalize) under
active analysis churn; full digest only on an actual rebuild.** Don't misread a churn-window
scoped-digest timing as a regression.

## Risks / non-goals

- **Forgotten bump** = false-positive risk. For the **shared** surface it is *fully* eliminated: the
  mandatory triggers fire for any INSERT/UPDATE/**DELETE** by any writer (repo internal txn, repair
  delete, backfill, future scripts). For **`evidence_seq`** it remains app-level discipline at the
  enumerated per-user choke-points; the differential test exercises every surface (incl. delete,
  drill-convert, and the eligibility-gated no-churn cases) to catch a missed or mis-gated site. This
  is the one thing to get right.
- **Out-of-band writers to the per-user tables are invisible to `evidence_seq`** (the shared tables are
  covered by triggers; `session_moves`/`game_sessions`/`blunders`/`blunder_reviews` are bumped only at
  app-level choke-points). There is precedent for alembic data migrations doing raw `UPDATE`s on these
  tables (e.g. `20260615_02_add_normalized_fen_before.py:55`). A future migration or maintenance script
  that mutates a per-user evidence table **without** bumping `evidence_seq` → **permanent false-fresh**
  (a stale batch served forever, since no counter ever advances). **Discipline (make it explicit):**
  - Any migration/script that mutates `session_moves`, `game_sessions` (eligibility columns), `blunders`,
    or `blunder_reviews` MUST either bump `OPENING_EVIDENCE_INPUTS_VERSION` (globally invalidates every
    batch via `registry_fingerprint` — the simplest, safest hammer) or advance **all** affected cursors'
    `evidence_seq` in the same migration.
  - Add a **comment on the `OpeningScoreCursor.evidence_seq` model column** (and mirrored in the
    conftest DDL) stating this contract, so the next author of such a migration sees it.
  This is a discipline note, not new runtime code — the shared-table trigger approach was chosen
  precisely because it does NOT rely on this kind of discipline; `evidence_seq` can't be made trigger-
  driven (it needs per-(user,color) attribution + the eligibility gate), so it inherits the caveat.
- **Over-bump churn** (opposite failure) = false-negative/perf risk: bumping `evidence_seq` on live
  per-move writes would reintroduce the recompute churn the active-session exclusion avoids. Mitigated
  by the `session_is_evidence_eligible` gate on S1/S5 + the no-churn tests (16–17).
- **Postgres hot-row contention** on the single `evidence_epoch` row under many concurrent analysis
  writers (mitigated by `FOR EACH STATEMENT` on Postgres). Acceptable at current (single-active-user)
  scale; could shard/advisory-lock later.
- **Non-goal**: simplifying g-mxeo's async baseline job back to a synchronous check (the bead notes
  this becomes possible afterward) — follow-up, not in this change.
- **Non-goal**: watermark `updated_at` columns on `session_moves`/`analysis_cache` — explicitly
  deferred.
acceptance_criteria: A freshness verdict for an already-built batch is computed without scanning/hashing all of a user's evidence (no raw_evidence_inputs_digest on the fast path); provably equivalent to the current digest (false-negatives = harmless rebuild, NO false-positives) verified by a differential test against the digest across mutation scenarios.

title: Debug overlay: capture request/response bodies (redaction-gated)
description: Follow-up to g-l8t2 (metadata-only network capture). Extend the in-app debug overlay's fetch capture to also record request and response BODIES, gated behind redaction. Blocked by the RELEASE BLOCKER privacy note in src/utils/debugLog.ts: bodies + Authorization headers would be persisted to localStorage. Requires: (1) Response.clone() before reading body so the app's stream is untouched; (2) size cap reusing ARG_TRUNCATE; (3) Authorization-header + token/PII redaction in the serializer; (4) an opt-in gate (?debugbody=1 or a constant) since body capture is heavier and higher-risk. Do NOT start before the redaction work the debugLog.ts header flags.
design:
# g-bsg9 — Debug overlay: capture request/response bodies (redaction-gated)

## Context

The in-app debug overlay (`src/utils/debugLog.ts` + `src/components/DebugOverlay.tsx`)
captures `console.*`, uncaught errors, and — since **g-l8t2** — network request **metadata**
(method/URL/status/duration/request-id) via a `window.fetch` monkeypatch. Metadata alone often
isn't enough to debug an API bug on-device (mobile / devtools closed): you can't see the payload
that was sent or the error envelope that came back, which is why `.har` hand-exports are still
needed (`tmp/*.har`).

This bead extends the existing fetch wrapper to also record **request and response bodies**. The
reason it was split out of g-l8t2 and gated is privacy: bodies + the `Authorization` header would
be persisted to `localStorage` (see the RELEASE BLOCKER header at `debugLog.ts:8`). Login/register
request bodies carry `{username, password}` (`AuthContext`/`api.ts`), and login/register **response**
bodies return a JWT — raw secrets we must never write to disk. So body capture must be (a) opt-in,
(b) redacted, (c) size-capped, and (d) must never disturb the app's own response stream.

Intended outcome: with an explicit opt-in, each net row in the overlay also shows the (redacted,
truncated) request and response body, making on-device API debugging self-contained. Scope of the
redaction guarantee: **captured fetch bodies** never persist a password / JWT / bearer token. This
does **not** cover the pre-existing `console.*` capture path (`serializeArg`, `debugLog.ts:66`),
which still persists arbitrary args unredacted — that broader hardening belongs to the RELEASE
BLOCKER follow-up, not this bead (see Privacy note).

## Scope decisions (defaults; user was away when asked — revisit if wrong)

1. **Bodies only, no header capture.** We never read or persist request/response headers. The
   safest handling of the `Authorization` header is to not capture it at all. Redaction targets
   token/PII *inside bodies* (the JWT still leaks via login/register response bodies, so body
   redaction is mandatory regardless).
2. **Gate = `?debugbody=1` + persistent `localStorage` flag + an overlay "Bodies" toggle**, checked
   **per-request** so a runtime toggle takes effect immediately. On-device control is the overlay's
   whole purpose.
3. **Redact passwords, tokens, emails; keep `username`.** Username is the primary debugging
   identifier and lower-risk than a password/JWT.

## Design

### 1. Data model (`src/utils/debugLog.ts`)
Extend `NetMeta` with two optional, already-redacted strings (no new entry type; overlay renders by
`level` and reads `args`, unchanged):

```ts
export interface NetMeta {
  // …existing fields…
  reqBody?: string   // redacted + truncated; present only when gate on AND a request body existed
  resBody?: string   // redacted + truncated; attached asynchronously after the response resolves
}
```

Both are **forward/backward compatible** with persisted blobs (`hydrate()` filters on
`typeof e.args === 'string'`; older rows simply lack `reqBody`/`resBody`, and the overlay reads
`args`).

### 2. Opt-in gate (module state, checked per-request)
```ts
const BODY_STORAGE_KEY = 'gr.debugBody'
let bodyCaptureOn = false

function initBodyGate(): void {          // called from installFetchCapture()
  try {
    const p = typeof window !== 'undefined'
      ? new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('debugbody') : null
    if (p === '1')      { bodyCaptureOn = true;  localStorage.setItem(BODY_STORAGE_KEY, '1') }
    else if (p === '0') { bodyCaptureOn = false; localStorage.removeItem(BODY_STORAGE_KEY) }
    else                { bodyCaptureOn = localStorage.getItem(BODY_STORAGE_KEY) === '1' }
  } catch { bodyCaptureOn = false }
}
export function isBodyCaptureEnabled(): boolean { return bodyCaptureOn }
export function setBodyCapture(on: boolean): void {   // overlay toggle calls this
  bodyCaptureOn = on
  try { on ? localStorage.setItem(BODY_STORAGE_KEY, '1') : localStorage.removeItem(BODY_STORAGE_KEY) }
  catch { /* ignore */ }
}
```
`uninstallFetchCapture()` resets `bodyCaptureOn = false` for test isolation. The wrapper reads
`bodyCaptureOn` at request time (not install time) so the toggle works without reinstalling.

### 3. Redaction serializer (the security core)
`redactAndTruncate(text: string): string` — **redact first, truncate last** (a token must never
survive by landing across the *display* truncation boundary). Reuses `ARG_TRUNCATE` (2000) via the
existing `truncate()`. It is an alias of the shared `redactCompleteText` primitive (below); the
streamed-response path wraps that with `redactCappedBody` (§5) to also handle *read-cap* truncation.

Shared key predicate used by **every** structural path (JSON *and* URL-encoded):
```ts
const SENSITIVE_KEYS = ['password','new_password','current_password','token','access_token',
  'refresh_token','authorization','secret','api_key','apikey','email']       // 'username' kept
const isSensitiveKey = (k: string): boolean => {
  const s = k.toLowerCase()
  return SENSITIVE_KEYS.some((d) => s === d || s.includes('password') || s.includes('token'))
}
```

Also a **text-level sensitive-key detector** (built from the same list) for the conservative
fallback below:
```ts
// word-ish match so game FEN/PGN never trips it, but password=/token=/"secret": do
const SENSITIVE_KEY_RE = /(?:^|[^a-z])(password|new_password|current_password|token|access_token|
  refresh_token|authorization|secret|api_?key|email)\b/i     // (single line in code)
const hasSensitiveKeyText = (s: string): boolean => SENSITIVE_KEY_RE.test(s)
```

`scrubText(s)` — always-applied token regex backstop:
- JWT: `/\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\b/g` → `[redacted-jwt]`
- Bearer: `/Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]+/gi` → `Bearer [redacted]`

**One shared primitive — `redactCompleteText(str)` — handles any *complete* body** (used by the
request string path §4 and the not-cap-hit response path §5), in order:
1. `JSON.parse` succeeds → walk the parsed value, replace every `isSensitiveKey(key)` value with
   `'[redacted]'`, re-stringify, `scrubText`, `truncate`. (The common case: our JSON API bodies.)
2. Parse fails **and** `hasSensitiveKeyText(str)` → we cannot structurally key-redact a non-JSON
   blob, and `scrubText` only knows JWT/Bearer, so a raw `password=secret` or `{secret: sk-…}` could
   slip through → return the generic note `'[body with sensitive keys, not shown]'`. **Never display
   the raw string.** (This closes the global-`fetch` risk: the wrapper patches *all* callers, not
   just our JSON auth ones, so we must not assume a string body is safe.)
3. Parse fails and no sensitive-key marker → benign non-JSON (PostHog egress, plain text) →
   `truncate(scrubText(str))`.

`redactAndTruncate(text)` is just `redactCompleteText(text)`. Everything wraps in try/catch → on any
failure return `'[unserializable]'` (mirrors `serializeArg`), so redaction can never throw inside the
fetch path. This is the same "when unsure, drop the payload" stance used for the read-cap case (§5).

### 4. Request body extraction (synchronous, from `init.body` only)
`captureRequestBody(init?: RequestInit): string | undefined`
- `undefined`/no body → `undefined`.
- `string` → `redactCompleteText(body)` (§3: JSON-structural, or the `[…sensitive keys…]` note for a
  non-JSON string like `"password=secret"`, or scrubbed benign text — so a global-`fetch` caller that
  posts a raw form-encoded string cannot leak).
- `URLSearchParams` → **structural** redaction (NOT `toString()` → text path): iterate entries into a
  new `URLSearchParams`, replacing values where `isSensitiveKey(key)` with `[redacted]`, then
  `truncate(scrubText(out.toString()))`. Keeps `password=secret` sent as an *object* readable-but-safe
  (`password=[redacted]`).
- anything else (`Blob`/`FormData`/`ArrayBuffer`/`ReadableStream`) → `'[' + (ctor name) + ']'`
  placeholder — **never consumed**. (Our app always sends JSON strings; this is just a safety net.)

We read `init.body` only — never `input.body`. **Documented scope limitation (open question,
resolved as app-call-scoped):** request-body capture covers `fetch(url, { body })` — how this app
issues *every* request (`api.ts` `requestJson`, `AuthContext.tsx:195`, `openingBook.ts`). It does
**not** capture the body of `fetch(new Request(url, { body }))`, because reading `input.body` would
consume the app's own request stream (metadata + response body are still captured for such calls).
The app never uses that form; if it ever does, a separate `input.clone()` path would be needed.
`init.body` is available synchronously, so `reqBody` is computed at request start (§5) and passed to
`pushNet`.

### 5. Response body capture (async, on a CLONE, never blocks the caller)
Critical correctness: (a) **snapshot the gate at request start** so an in-flight toggle can't make a
request half-captured; (b) `res.clone()` **before** the app reads the stream; (c) never `await` the
read before returning `res`; (d) capture `reqBody` on the **error path** too (a failed request's
payload is exactly what you want to see).

```ts
window.fetch = async (input, init) => {
  const captureBodies = bodyCaptureOn                       // ← snapshot ONCE at request start
  const method = …; const rawUrl = …
  const reqBody = captureBodies ? captureRequestBody(init) : undefined   // computed pre-send
  const start = performance.now()
  try {
    const res = await originalFetch!.call(window, input, init)
    const id = pushNet({ …metadata…, reqBody })
    if (captureBodies) {                                    // ← same snapshot, not a re-read
      const clone = safeClone(res)                          // try/catch; null if no .clone (doubles)
      if (clone) void readBodyCapped(clone).then((t) => setNetResBody(id, t))
    }
    return res                                              // returned immediately; body reads async
  } catch (err) {
    pushNet({ …metadata…, status: 0, ok: false, errorKind: classifyFetchError(err), reqBody })
    throw err
  }
}
```
- `safeClone(res)`: `typeof res.clone === 'function' ? res.clone() : null` in try/catch.
- `readBodyCapped(clone)` — **stream-read with a hard cap, independent of `content-length`** (a
  missing or lying `content-length` must not let a chunked body buffer unbounded):
  1. Fast-path early-out: if `content-length` is present and `> BODY_READ_CAP`, return
     `'[large body ' + n + ' bytes, not captured]'` without reading.
  2. If `clone.body?.getReader` exists: pull chunks and, for each chunk, **byte-slice to the
     remaining capacity before decoding** — `value.subarray(0, min(value.byteLength, remaining))`
     through a `TextDecoder({stream:true})` — so even a single chunk far larger than the cap only
     decodes/allocates `remaining` bytes. When a chunk is sliced (or `readBytes` reaches
     `BODY_READ_CAP`) set `hitCap = true`, **break, and `reader.cancel()`**. This makes the cap a
     *hard* bound regardless of chunk size or a missing/lying `content-length`. Cancelling the
     *clone's* stream is safe (the app holds its own copy).
  3. Fallback (test doubles / no `body`): `buffer = await clone.text()` (complete body → `hitCap`
     stays false; still capped by the final `truncate`).
  4. Return `redactCappedBody(buffer, hitCap)` (below). On any throw → `'[unreadable]'`.

  `BODY_READ_CAP` need only exceed the display cap enough to keep redaction reliable (a JWT is
  short) — e.g. `ARG_TRUNCATE * 4` (~8 KB). We never read megabytes just to show 2 KB, and typical
  API JSON responses (< 8 KB) are read in full and structurally redacted.

- **`redactCappedBody(buffer, hitCap)` — the "redact before truncate" guarantee under a read cap.**
  The read cap is itself a truncation *before* redaction, so a secret can be sliced mid-value
  (`{"token":"eyJlong…` cut off): `JSON.parse` then fails (structural walker skipped) **and** the
  JWT/Bearer regex misses the incomplete token (no closing segment / word boundary), which would
  persist the raw prefix. So:
  - **`hitCap` and the buffer does NOT `JSON.parse`** → return the generic note
    `'[large body truncated before safe redaction]'`. **Never display the raw prefix.** (An
    incomplete document may hold a split secret we cannot reliably scrub.)
  - **otherwise** → `redactCompleteText(buffer)` (§3): if it parses, structural redaction is safe
    even when `hitCap` (the whole parsed object is walked before display truncation); if it's a
    complete non-JSON body, §3 already routes sensitive-key text to a note and benign text through
    `scrubText`.

`pushNet` returns the new entry `id` (currently returns void). New internal
`setNetResBody(id, resBody)`: locate the entry by id in `entries`; if found and it has `.net`,
publish a **new** array with `net: { …net, resBody }` and `args` rebuilt via `formatNetArgs`
(so the overlay/Copy/filter see the body), `notify()`, then persist with the **same immediate policy
as `pushNet`**: `schedulePersist(!entry.net.ok && entry.net.errorKind !== 'abort')`. This matters —
a `500` row flushes its *metadata* immediately at push, but the error **envelope** attaches later;
debouncing it would drop the response body from `localStorage` if the page closes before the 500 ms
timer (exactly when you most want the envelope). Successful/aborted rows stay debounced.
If the entry was already evicted from the 500-cap ring buffer, drop silently.

### 6. Rendering — zero overlay-render changes (bodies ride in `args`)
Consistent with g-l8t2's philosophy (everything human-readable lives in `args`, so text-filter and
Copy-all work for free). Extend `formatNetArgs(meta)` to append body lines when present:
```
GET /api/openings/tree?player_color=white 200 (143ms) #a1b2c3
  → {"session_id":"…","fen":"…"}          (reqBody, when present)
  ← {"token":"[redacted-jwt]","user":{…}} (resBody, when present)
```
`.debug-entry__args` is a `<pre>` with `white-space: pre-wrap`, so multi-line renders correctly with
no CSS change. `copyAll` already serializes `e.args` → captured bodies land in copied bug reports.

### 7. Overlay "Bodies" toggle (`DebugOverlay.tsx` + `.css`)
Add a header button next to Copy/Clear (`DebugOverlay.tsx:77` region):
```tsx
const [bodiesOn, setBodiesOn] = useState(isBodyCaptureEnabled)
// onClick: const next = !bodiesOn; setBodiesOn(next); setBodyCapture(next)
<button
  type="button"
  aria-pressed={bodiesOn}                       // ← binary state; tests assert on this, not styling
  className={'debug-toggle' + (bodiesOn ? ' is-active' : '')}
  onClick={…}
>Bodies</button>
```
Reuse the existing `.debug-overlay__header button` styling; add a small `.debug-toggle.is-active`
accent rule (e.g. teal border, mirroring `.debug-chip--net.is-active`). No change to
`LEVELS`/filters (bodies aren't a level).

### 8. Privacy / RELEASE BLOCKER note
Update the header comment at `debugLog.ts:8`: body capture is now available but **opt-in and
redacted** (denylist + JWT/Bearer regex, `Authorization` header never captured). State the residual
risks explicitly so the guarantee isn't overclaimed:
- Redaction covers **captured fetch bodies only**. The `console.*`/error path (`serializeArg`,
  `debugLog.ts:66`) still persists arbitrary args unredacted — a `console.log(token)` would leak.
  Applying redaction there (or clear-on-logout, or PROD gating) is the broader RELEASE BLOCKER work,
  **out of scope for g-bsg9**; call it out as the recommended companion follow-up.
- Even within bodies, `username` and non-denylisted fields are still persisted when the gate is on;
  redaction is best-effort.

## Files touched
- `src/utils/debugLog.ts` — `NetMeta.reqBody/resBody`; gate (`BODY_STORAGE_KEY`, `bodyCaptureOn`,
  `initBodyGate`, `isBodyCaptureEnabled`, `setBodyCapture`); redaction (`SENSITIVE_KEYS`,
  `isSensitiveKey`, `SENSITIVE_KEY_RE`/`hasSensitiveKeyText`, `scrubText`, JSON walker,
  `redactCompleteText` [= `redactAndTruncate`], `redactCappedBody`); `captureRequestBody`
  (+ structural `URLSearchParams` path); `safeClone`/`readBodyCapped` (byte-sliced hard cap,
  `hitCap`-aware fallback) + `BODY_READ_CAP`; `pushNet` returns id + accepts `reqBody`;
  `setNetResBody` (immediate persist for failed rows); `formatNetArgs` appends bodies; wrapper
  snapshots `captureBodies` at request start + records `reqBody` on the error path; wire into
  `installFetchCapture`/`uninstall…` (reset `bodyCaptureOn`); header comment.
- `src/test/setup.ts` — the global `afterEach` (`:25`) also `localStorage.removeItem('gr.debugBody')`
  so the persisted gate can't leak body capture into a later test's install.
- `src/components/DebugOverlay.tsx` — Bodies toggle button + local state.
- `src/components/DebugOverlay.css` — `.debug-toggle.is-active` accent.
- `src/utils/debugLog.test.ts` — new `describe('body capture')`.
- `src/components/DebugOverlay.test.tsx` — toggle renders + flips `isBodyCaptureEnabled`.
- No `main.tsx` change (install site unchanged).

## Test coverage (`debugLog.test.ts` → `describe('body capture')`)
Mirror the existing `fetch capture` block's stubbing (`window.fetch = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(...)`,
`installConsoleCapture()`, restore in `afterEach`). Call `setBodyCapture(false)` **and**
`localStorage.removeItem('gr.debugBody')` in `afterEach` so neither the in-memory flag nor the
persisted gate leaks into later tests (the global teardown at `src/test/setup.ts:25` clears the key
too, as a backstop).

- **Gate off by default:** no `?debugbody`, POST with a body → net entry has no `reqBody`/`resBody`;
  `args` has no `→`/`←` lines.
- **Request body redacted:** `setBodyCapture(true)`; POST `body: JSON.stringify({username:'a',
  password:'secret'})` → `net.reqBody` contains `username` + `[redacted]`, does **not** contain
  `secret`.
- **Response captured on a clone, caller stream intact:** stub returns
  `new Response('{"token":"eyJa.eyJb.cccc"}')`; after the wrapped call `await res.text()` still
  yields the original body (proves clone, not consume); after a microtask flush `net.resBody` has
  `[redacted-jwt]` and no raw token.
- **Async attach:** immediately after the call `resBody` may be undefined; after
  `await Promise.resolve()` / `await vi.runAllTimersAsync()` it's set and `args` includes the `←`
  line.
- **Persisted secret guarantee (the security assertion):** with bodies on, run a login-shaped
  request/response, flush persistence, then assert `localStorage['gr.debugLog']` does **not**
  include `'secret'` or the raw JWT.
- **Truncation:** body > `ARG_TRUNCATE` → `reqBody`/`resBody` ends with `…[truncated]`.
- **Size guard via content-length:** response with `content-length` > `BODY_READ_CAP` → `resBody` is
  the `[large body …]` note, body never read.
- **Size guard WITHOUT content-length (review fix #1):** a `Response` whose body is a
  `ReadableStream` emitting > `BODY_READ_CAP` of data and **no** `content-length` header → `resBody`
  is bounded (length ≤ ~`BODY_READ_CAP`); assert the reader was cancelled / not fully drained (spy
  the stream's `cancel`, or emit far more than the cap and assert the captured length stays bounded).
- **Sensitive value crossing the read cap (the redact-before-truncate hole):** a
  no-`content-length` `ReadableStream` emitting `{"token":"<JWT/long secret>…"}` where the token
  value straddles `BODY_READ_CAP` so the buffer is cut mid-value → `resBody` is exactly
  `'[large body truncated before safe redaction]'`, and — the key assertion —
  `localStorage['gr.debugLog']` contains **no** substring of the raw token prefix. Complement with a
  small (< cap) `{"token":"eyJ…"}` that DOES parse → `[redacted]`/`[redacted-jwt]`, proving only the
  cap-truncated case falls back to the note.
- **Single chunk larger than the cap (hard-bound fix):** a `ReadableStream` that emits **one** chunk
  of `BODY_READ_CAP * 10` bytes → captured `resBody` length stays ~`BODY_READ_CAP`-bounded (the chunk
  was byte-sliced before decode, not fully allocated), and the reader's `cancel` was called.
- **Raw form-encoded string body leaks nothing (global-fetch fix):** direct
  `window.fetch(url, { method:'POST', body:'password=secret&x=1' })` with bodies on → `reqBody` is
  `'[body with sensitive keys, not shown]'` and neither `reqBody` nor `localStorage` contains
  `secret`. Contrast: the same fields via `new URLSearchParams({password:'secret'})` →
  `password=[redacted]` (readable, safe). And a benign string `'ping'` → shown scrubbed.
- **Failed-row response body flushes immediately (persist-policy fix):** a `500` response with a body
  → after the async attach resolves, `localStorage['gr.debugLog']` already holds `net.resBody`
  **without advancing the debounce timer** (mirror the existing immediate-flush test at
  `debugLog.test.ts:242`). A `200`'s `resBody` stays debounced until the timer advances.
- **URLSearchParams request body redaction (the review fix):**
  `body: new URLSearchParams({username:'a', password:'secret', access_token:'x'})` →
  `reqBody` shows `username=a`, `password=[redacted]`, `access_token=[redacted]`, contains neither
  `secret` nor `x`.
- **Mid-flight toggle snapshot (the review fix):** start a request with bodies **on**, call
  `setBodyCapture(false)` before the stubbed fetch resolves → the resolved entry STILL has
  `reqBody`/`resBody` (captured per the start-of-request snapshot); and the reverse (start off →
  toggle on mid-flight) captures nothing.
- **Non-JSON scrub:** response text `'auth Bearer eyJa.eyJb.cccc done'` → scrubbed
  (`Bearer [redacted]`, no raw token), no crash.
- **Clone-less double:** stub `Response` without `.clone` → no throw; `resBody` absent or
  `[unreadable]`.
- **Non-string request body:** `body: new Blob(['x'])` → `reqBody` is `'[Blob]'`, blob not consumed.
- **reqBody on failure:** a rejected/500 request with bodies on still records `reqBody`.
- **Toggle persistence:** `setBodyCapture(true)` sets `gr.debugBody`; `false` removes it.
- Existing metadata tests must stay green (bodies are additive; gate defaults off).

`DebugOverlay.test.tsx`: Bodies button renders with `aria-pressed="false"`; clicking flips
`aria-pressed` to `"true"` and toggles `isBodyCaptureEnabled()` on/off.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run src/utils/debugLog.test.ts src/components/DebugOverlay.test.tsx` (rerun any flaky
  file in isolation — the pre-push suite is flaky under parallel load).
- `npx tsc -b` — the pre-push gate builds the whole tree; the `'net'` typing split from g-l8t2 stays
  intact and `pushNet`'s new return type must not break call sites.
- Manual: `npm run dev`, open a page with `?debug=1&debugbody=1`, log in, trigger an API call →
  confirm net rows show `→`/`←` body lines, the password/JWT read `[redacted]`/`[redacted-jwt]`, and
  the app still works (response stream intact). Toggle "Bodies" off → new rows have no body lines.
  Inspect `localStorage['gr.debugLog']` in devtools → no raw secret present.
notes: Implementation complete + 2 review fixes applied. (P1) content-length>cap fast path moved BEFORE res.clone() into new captureResponseBody() — an unread tee branch buffers everything the app reads, so a known-large response is now never cloned (clone-spy test). (P2) redaction widened: isSensitiveKey now marker-substring matches on separator-stripped keys (client_secret/secretKey/X-Api-Key/apiToken/credential all caught; username+session_id kept); JSON string VALUES with assignment-shaped secrets (password=…, token: …) suppressed while bare mentions ('Invalid username or password') stay visible; email-address regex added to the always-on scrub backstop. Verified: vitest 64/64 green, tsc -b clean, Playwright live run 14/14 (401 envelope still fully visible in overlay, password [redacted], no secrets in localStorage). Awaiting user review before commit.

title: Reconcile exact-best on game-review AnalysisBoard path (GameAnalysisPage)
description:
## Problem

The finished-game review screen (`GameAnalysisPage` → `AnalysisBoard`) renders move classifications straight from the backend session export without running the existing `reconcileTrustedBest` exact-best projection. This is the one remaining consumer where a played move that equals the trusted position best can disagree with its own displayed classification.

`GameAnalysisPage.tsx` fetches `SessionAnalysis` via `fetchAnalysis(id)` and passes `moves={analysis.moves}` and `positionAnalysis={analysis.position_analysis}` directly to `AnalysisBoard`. `AnalysisBoard` reads `m.classification` verbatim (`AnalysisBoard.tsx:385` for the move list, `:1029` for the on-board badge). The `useMoveAnalysis` hook it calls (`AnalysisBoard.tsx:258`) only provides `analyzeMove` for new interactive variation moves — it never re-projects the seeded review moves, so the `reconcileTrustedBest` call inside that hook (`useMoveAnalysis.ts:225`) does not apply here.

Result: when `position_analysis[fen_before].best_move_uci == played move uci` but the stored `classification != "best"` (e.g. the stored row came from a weaker/earlier run than the trusted position best the backend now serves), the board shows the blue best-arrow on the destination square but no gold "best" star/badge on the move — a visible contradiction on the same square while reviewing a finished game.

## Why this is the narrowed scope

The two other interactive consumers already self-correct via the shipped `reconcileTrustedBest` helper:
- Live ChessGame / MoveList: `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1471`
- Post-game interactive AnalysisBoard via the hook: `useMoveAnalysis.ts:225`

Drill review (`DrillAnalysisPage` → `buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot`) is internally coherent (classification and best come from the same local worker run). So `GameAnalysisPage` (game review) is the only path with the visible gap. This bead closes that gap by reusing the existing client-side helper instead of doing the full backend contract rework tracked in g-backend-best-proj (now deferred to P4).

## Fix

Re-join `moves` to `position_analysis` by `fen_before` and apply the existing `reconcileTrustedBest` projection (or an equivalent that reuses its PROMOTION rule) before the data reaches `AnalysisBoard`. No backend change, no new wire fields, no mate-score rule, no SPEC churn.
design:
## Target

Apply the exact-best projection to the game-review payload before it reaches `AnalysisBoard`, mirroring what the live and interactive paths already do, using the shipped `reconcileTrustedBest` helper (`src/workers/analysisUtils.ts:431`).

## Where to apply it

Project once, after the fetch, in `GameAnalysisPage.tsx` (or a small pure adapter it calls). Do NOT push it into `AnalysisBoard` itself — `AnalysisBoard` is shared with the interactive path that is already reconciled, and double-applying would be redundant. Keep the projection at the seam where the backend session export is adapted into props.

## Algorithm

For each move in `analysis.moves`:
1. Look up `analysis.position_analysis[move.fen_before]`.
2. Gate strictly on trusted position truth — mirror `isTrustedExactBestHit`: project ONLY when the entry exists, `position_trusted === true`, and `best_move_uci != null`. This preserves the g-position-analysis invariant that untrusted legacy-seed bests (`position_trusted === false`, set at `backend/app/api/session.py:1268`) cannot define exact-best.
3. If the played move's UCI equals that trusted `best_move_uci`, run the PROMOTION branch of `reconcileTrustedBest`: classification -> `best`, delta/loss -> 0, repoint bestMove/bestLine at the trusted best. Leave genuinely non-best moves untouched (do NOT promote, and the helper's DEMOTION branch is not needed here since the export does not over-grade).

## Shape adaptation (the one real wrinkle)

`reconcileTrustedBest` takes/returns the worker `AnalysisResult` shape (`move`, `classification`, `bestMove`, `bestLine`, `bestEval`, `playedEval`, `delta`, ...). The session export move (`SessionAnalysis.moves[]`) is a different shape (`m.classification`, `m.uci`, etc.). Two options:
- (A) Adapt each session move to the reconcile input shape, run the helper, map the result back onto the session move (only `classification` and the best-* fields actually feed the AnalysisBoard render at `AnalysisBoard.tsx:385/1029` and the arrow source).
- (B) Write a thin session-grain projection that reuses the same equality rule and PROMOTION outcome.
Prefer (A) so the rule stays single-sourced in `reconcileTrustedBest`. Pull the played UCI from the session move; trusted best from the position entry.

## Tests

- Trusted position best == played move but stored `classification: "good"` -> projected to `best`, board shows the star and the badge matches the arrow.
- `position_trusted === false` (untrusted legacy seed) with best == played move -> NOT promoted (invariant preserved).
- Genuinely non-best move (played != trusted best) -> classification unchanged.
- Move with no `position_analysis` entry for its `fen_before` -> unchanged.
- Keep the projection out of the interactive AnalysisBoard path so it is not double-applied (regression guard).

## Out of scope

Backend wire-contract changes, new trust flags (`derived_exact_best`), mate-score loss rules, and consumer cutover across `analysis.py`/`session.py` all remain in g-backend-best-proj (deferred, P4). This bead is purely a client-side mirror of an already-shipped helper onto one render path.
acceptance_criteria: GameAnalysisPage game-review render projects a played move whose UCI equals a trusted (position_trusted===true) position best_move_uci to classification 'best' with loss 0, so the move's star/badge matches the on-board best-arrow. Untrusted legacy-seed positions (position_trusted===false) are NOT promoted. Genuinely non-best moves and moves without a position_analysis entry are unchanged. Projection reuses reconcileTrustedBest and is not double-applied on the interactive AnalysisBoard path. Tests cover all four cases.
close_reason: Mirror reconcileTrustedBest exact-best promotion onto the game-review AnalysisBoard path via projectExactBest adapter in GameAnalysisPage
