title: Play overlay screenshot states
description: Follow-up to g-tsyy. Capture screenshot states for the harder /play overlays scoped out of the first pass: promotion picker (requiresPromotion, ChessGame.tsx:986), review-fail modal + spotlight (handleRevealSrsFail, ChessGame.tsx:1316), game-end banner, and drill overlay. Requires real move scripting or backend mocks to reach each branch.
design:
# Plan: Play overlay screenshot states (g-yr3a)

Follow-up to g-tsyy. Add the four hard /play overlays scoped out of the first pass to the
screenshot gallery suite (`e2e/screenshots/pages.screens.spec.ts`): promotion picker,
review-fail spotlight, game-end banner, and the drill setup overlay. Same contract as g-tsyy —
reviewable contact-sheet PNGs across viewports, NOT pixel-diff assertions.

## Where these render (verified, line numbers drifted from the bead title)
- Promotion picker: `BoardStage.tsx:377` renders `<PromotionPicker>` when
  `pendingPromotion && !showRevertWarning && !showResignWarning`. Classes:
  `.promotion-picker-backdrop`, `.promotion-picker-square` (aria-label `Promote to <piece>`).
  `pendingPromotion` is set in `ChessGame.tsx:1352` / `:1062` when `handleDrop`/`applyPlayerMove`
  returns `requiresPromotion` — i.e. chess.js detects a pawn reaching the last rank with no
  promotion piece supplied. This is computed from the LOCAL `chess` instance, so the real board
  must actually have a pawn on the 7th rank.
- Review-fail spotlight: `BoardStage.tsx:405` renders `<SrsFailSpotlight>`; visible only while
  `trigger` (srsFailTrigger nonce) is non-null. Classes: `.srs-fail-scrim`, `.srs-fail-content`,
  `.srs-fail-content__inner`. Trigger path: `AnalysisEffects.processSrsReview` (AnalysisEffects.tsx:200-204)
  calls `onSrsFail` → `triggerSrsFailSpotlight` (ChessGame.tsx:1411) when a SEEDED SRS review move
  is replayed and FAILS (`isRecordableFailure(evalLossCp)` true, i.e. delta exceeds threshold).
  Auto-dismisses: hold `SRS_FAIL_HOLD_MS` then shrink then `onDone` (SrsFailSpotlight.tsx:78,94).
  The manual-reveal variant is `reviewFailModal`/`handleRevealSrsFail` via the MoveList (no scrim);
  the full-screen artifact we want is the spotlight scrim.
- Game-end banner: `PostGameBanner.tsx:59` / `:97` render `.game-end-banner` when
  `showPostGamePrompt && gameResult`. Reached deterministically by RESIGNING (no long game needed):
  `handleResignClick` → resign warning (`BoardStage.tsx:337`, button name "Resign") →
  `executeResign` sets gameResult + showPostGamePrompt. Two banner shapes: normal game (rating
  delta) and stopped-drill (`isStoppedDrill`).
- Drill overlay: the start overlay in drill mode. `showStartOverlay` defaults true
  (ChessGame.tsx:153); `isDrillMode` toggled by `handleSwitchToDrillMode` (:1538). When
  `showStartOverlay && isDrillMode` the DrillSetupPanel renders (opening picker / color / strictness).
  Fully deterministic for the `due` seed user (has openings) — NO game scripting.

## Approach per state (ordered easiest → hardest)

### 1. Game-end banner — resign path (deterministic, MANDATORY end mock)
Reuse `startGameAsWhite` from the existing spec. Then:
- play one move so resign is enabled, click the "Resign" CONTROL, which opens the resign warning
  `alertdialog` (`BoardStage.tsx:337`, `aria-labelledby="resign-warning-title"`).
- DISAMBIGUATE the confirm click: both the underlying control and the modal button are named
  "Resign", so strict mode will match two nodes. Scope the confirm through the dialog, e.g.
  `page.getByRole("alertdialog").getByRole("button", { name: "Resign" })` →
  `onResignAnyway`/executeResign.
- `executeResign` calls `endGame` → `POST /api/game/end` (api.ts:589), whose `EndGameResponse`
  drives the banner's rating delta. This is NON-deterministic, so MOCK `**/api/game/end` with a
  fixed `EndGameResponse` (stable rating_before/after, scoreChanges) — mandatory for a stable
  banner, not optional. Wait on `.game-end-banner` / `.game-end-banner-message`.
- Capture state `game-end-banner` across `viewportsFor("play")` (all 6 — banner lives in
  `.chess-graph-area`, layout differs in the mixed/short bands).

### 2. Drill overlay — drill setup panel (deterministic, no mocks)
- `loginAs(page, "due")`, goto `/play`. The start overlay is already shown on load
  (`showStartOverlay` default true). Click the Drill mode toggle (`handleSwitchToDrillMode`,
  button in the start overlay — confirm exact name in BoardStage start-overlay JSX).
- DO NOT wait on a panel root: `DrillSetupPanel` returns a FRAGMENT, no root element
  (`DrillSetupPanel.tsx:63`). And `.opening-picker` (`OpeningPicker.tsx:277`) renders WHILE openings
  are still loading. So wait for the picker trigger label to flip from the loading state to
  `"Select opening"` (`OpeningPicker.tsx:268-274`, `triggerLabel` is "loading…"/"Select opening"
  depending on `isLoading`/`openingFamilies`). Allow a wide timeout — the openings graph is a
  process-wide singleton (reuse g-tsyy warm-up note).
- Capture `drill-setup` across all play viewports. Optionally a second shot with an opening selected.

### 3. Review-fail spotlight — fail the seeded SRS review (real moves, no mocks)
- Build on the existing `play` seeded-review sequence (`playToSeededReviewPosition`: e2/e4, Ng1/f3,
  Bf1/c4) that reaches the review-warning toast for the `due` user. The seeded blunder is `Nxe5`
  (`game-blunder-ghost-srs.spec.ts:148`).
- DO NOT invent a "sufficiently bad" move. The pending SRS review is keyed by `analysis.id` AND a
  `moveIndex` equality check (`AnalysisEffects.tsx:133`), so reuse the ALREADY-PROVEN deterministic
  failure move from `game-blunder-ghost-srs.spec.ts:153`: at the review moment play `e1`→`e2`
  (the king move), which is the recorded fail path. This drives `delta` past threshold,
  `isRecordableFailure` true → `onSrsFail` → spotlight. Assert `.review-warning-toast` first.
- TIMING (corrected): `page.clock.setFixedTime` does NOT pause timers — `SRS_FAIL_HOLD_MS` →
  `setPhase("shrink")` and then `SRS_FAIL_SHRINK_MS` → unmount (`SrsFailSpotlight.tsx:78,94`) will
  still fire and the scrim can vanish mid-capture across 6 viewports. Mitigation:
  PAUSE the clock (`page.clock.pauseAt(FIXED_TIME)` / install-then-pause) so the hold/shrink timers
  do not advance during captures, and re-measure correctly per viewport.
- rAF RE-MEASURE (corrected): the scrim's clip-path hole is measured from `targetRef` and re-measured
  on `resize`/`scroll` via `requestAnimationFrame` (`SrsFailSpotlight.tsx:70-76`). Under a paused
  clock rAF will not auto-fire, so after each `setViewportSize` the hole would be stale. After every
  viewport resize, tick exactly ONE controlled frame (e.g. `page.clock.runFor(16)` or a single rAF
  flush) so `measure()` re-runs against the new board rect before screenshotting. This likely needs a
  small spotlight-specific capture variant rather than the shared `captureAcrossViewports`.
- Capture `review-fail-spotlight` across all play viewports (full-screen; board placement differs).

### 4. Promotion picker — mock the opponent endpoint to script a promotion line (HARDEST)
The picker fires only when the LOCAL chess board has a pawn one step from the last rank, so we must
genuinely advance a pawn there. Real ghost play won't cooperate. Plan: mock the single opponent
endpoint and script an EXACT, asserted legal line.
- Opponent replies come from one endpoint: `POST /api/game/next-opponent-move`
  (`getNextOpponentMove`, api.ts:871). The applied reply is `chess.move(sanMove)` in the controller
  (`useChessGameController.ts:368`), which THROWS "Ghost returned illegal move" on illegal SAN — so
  every mocked reply must be legal in the exact position we will have produced.
- EXACT scripted line (White escorts the a-pawn, Black shuffles the g8 knight):
  `a2-a4 / Nf6`, `a4-a5 / Ng8`, `a5-a6 / Nf6`, `a6xb7 / Ng8`, then `b7xc8` — White's b7 pawn
  captures on c8 and reaches the last rank with NO promotion piece supplied → `requiresPromotion`.
  We control both colours via the mock, so each Black reply (`Nf6`/`Ng8` alternation) is legal and
  never touches the advancing pawn.
- The mock must return the FULL `NextOpponentMoveResponse` contract (api.ts:413), not a partial:
  `{ mode: "engine", move: { uci, san }, target_blunder_id: null, target_blunder_srs: null,
  target_fen: null, decision_source: "backend_engine", drill_route: null }`. NOTE `move` carries
  BOTH `uci` and `san` (the plan previously named only `san`); supply both, matching SAN to the
  position.
- USE `mode: "engine"`, NOT `"ghost"`: an `engine`→`ghost` mode transition fires the rehook toast
  (`ChessGame.tsx:1094`, `setShowRehookToast(true)`), which would pollute the promotion screenshot.
  Keeping every reply `engine` means no transition and no toast.
- Play the final `b7xc8` capture so `handleDropPiece` → `requiresPromotion` (ChessGame.tsx:1351).
  Existing `playMove` is click-click (routes through `applyPlayerMove`/`handleSquareClick` :1103);
  confirm click-click yields `requiresPromotion`, else use `page.dragAndDrop`.
- Wait on `.promotion-picker-square` (or `.promotion-picker-backdrop`). Capture `promotion-picker`.
- RISK: if scripting proves flaky, fallback is a tiny dev-guarded test seam (query param to start
  from a near-promotion FEN). Prefer the mock-opponent line first; document whichever is used.

## Suite integration
- Add the four captures inside the existing `test.describe("play", ...)` block in
  `e2e/screenshots/pages.screens.spec.ts` (serial mode already configured). Each new overlay gets its
  OWN `test(...)` with a fresh game (mirrors the existing "fresh board" vs "mid-game" split) so one
  overlay's dismissal/toasts can't bleed into another.
- Three of the four states (game-end banner, drill overlay, promotion picker) reuse the existing
  `captureAcrossViewports`/`captureState` helpers unchanged — they have no per-viewport timing
  dependency — and land in `output/index.html` under the `play` section automatically (buildIndex
  groups by page/state).
- The SPOTLIGHT state is the exception: it needs a dedicated capture loop (paused clock + a one-frame
  rAF tick after each `setViewportSize` so the clip-path hole re-measures — see state #3). Implement
  this as a small spotlight-specific variant of the viewport loop in the spec (or a thin
  `captureSpotlightAcrossViewports` helper); do NOT route it through the shared
  `captureAcrossViewports`, which resizes-then-shoots with no frame tick.
- Reuse `prepareDeterministicPage`, `viewportsFor("play")`, `failRoute`/route mocks throughout. Keep
  all mock/route blocks scoped + `page.unrouteAll()` after each, matching the suite's discipline.

## State-locator reference to add
- promotion: `.promotion-picker-square`, `.promotion-picker-backdrop`
- spotlight: `.srs-fail-scrim`, `.srs-fail-content`
- game-end: `.game-end-banner`, `.game-end-banner-message`
- drill overlay: the OpeningPicker trigger label `"Select opening"` (NOT a panel root — DrillSetupPanel
  is a fragment; `.opening-picker` is present while still loading, so gate on the label flip)

## Verification / test coverage
- Run `npm run test:e2e:screens -- --grep play` and eyeball the four new entries in
  `output/index.html` across all play viewports.
- Confirm determinism: re-run twice. The spotlight needs the PAUSED clock (not just setFixedTime)
  plus a one-frame tick after each resize to survive all 6 captures; the resign banner needs the
  `/api/game/end` mock for a stable rating delta. Note the suite is serial — do not parallelize.
- Pre-push vitest suite is flaky under parallel load (project memory); these are Playwright e2e, run
  them in isolation.

## Resolved facts (confirmed in code)
- Drill mode toggle button label is literally `Drill` (`BoardStage.tsx:192`,
  `getByRole("button", { name: "Drill" })`). DrillSetupPanel is a fragment (no root) — gate on the
  OpeningPicker `"Select opening"` trigger label.
- Click-click DOES reach `requiresPromotion`: `handleSquareClick` → `applyPlayerMoveAndAdvance`
  (ChessGame.tsx:1121) → `applyPlayerMove`, which sets `pendingPromotion` on the
  `requiresPromotion` result (ChessGame.tsx:1062). No drag needed.
- `/api/game/end` mock payload — concrete `EndGameResponse` (api.ts:306):
  `{ session_id: "<id>", result: "resign", ended_at: "2026-06-01T12:00:00Z",
  rating: { rating_before: 1200, rating_after: 1188, is_provisional: false, ... },
  score_changes: { elo: { rating: -12, ... }, chesscom: null, lichess: null } }`.
  Fill `rating` (RatingChange) and `score_changes` (RatingScores) with the exact field shapes from
  api.ts so the banner's `rating-delta` renders a fixed value; `scores`/`scores_after` optional.
close_reason: Implemented four /play overlay screenshot states (game-end banner, drill setup, review-fail spotlight, promotion picker) in e2e/screenshots/pages.screens.spec.ts; verified across all play viewports

title: Lazy continuation fallback for legacy cached best lines (no stored PV)
description: Follow-up to g-engine-line-pv. For sessions analyzed before best_line_uci was persisted, the cached best line still renders only one move. Add a lazy fallback: when the user opens the AnalysisBoard cached best popup and the cached PV length is 1, run a single-PV continuation search from the position AFTER the cached best move, prepend the cached best move, and surface that as the line. Higher regression risk: needs separate worker orchestration so it does not clobber the active engine-lines search.
design: Constraints discovered during g-engine-line-pv review: evaluatePosition clears shared info/infoFen and supersedes pending searches (src/hooks/useStockfishEngine.ts:249), and stockfishWorker stops the running search when a new eval arrives (src/workers/stockfishWorker.ts:190). A naive evaluatePosition call would clobber the live engine-lines search. Fallback therefore needs EITHER a separate non-disruptive worker/channel OR an explicit background/non-superseding request mode in the hook+worker, PLUS a moves param so the continuation searches the position after the cached best move. Cache the UI continuation result separately (keyed by position+bestmove) so it is not confused with live search info. Validate the returned continuation PV before rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Opening cached best popup on a legacy position (cached PV length 1) shows a multi-move SAN line after continuation completes. The live engine-lines search is not interrupted/clobbered while the continuation runs. Continuation result is cached and not recomputed on reopen. Continuation PV is validated before render.
notes: Investigation found a distinct new-session path: /api/analysis/lookup may return legacy/precomputed rows without best_line_uci, and current cache-hit gating accepts them as complete. That cancels the worker and uploads null PV into the new session. g-cjik remains the lazy UI fallback for already-stored one-move/null lines.

title: Backend: Opportunity-aware SRS scoring
description:
Implement opportunity-aware scoring to reduce overweighting of rare branches.

Scope:
- Define and persist opportunity counters needed for scoring:
  opportunities_since_review, opportunities_30d, reached_30d
- Compute smoothed reach probability:
  p_reach = (reached_30d + 2) / (opportunities_30d + 4)
- Add opportunity overdue term:
  opp_overdue = opportunities_since_review / expected_opportunities(pass_streak)
- Integrate with score:
  score = opp_overdue * severity * distance_weight * (p_reach ^ 1.5) * opening_weight
- Keep opening_weight in baseline weighted form from g-eo1 notes (no separate optional opening-family gating mode).

Validation:
- Data-layer tests for counter updates and rolling-window logic
- Integration tests ensuring rarely encountered branches are downweighted vs frequently reached branches
- Backfill/compatibility behavior for existing blunders without counters
design:
## Revised Plan: Opportunity-Aware SRS Scoring

### Core Signal
- **reached**: session contains the exact blunder position FEN (user arrived at the trap)
- **opportunity**: session reaches an ancestor position (within OPPORTUNITY_ANCESTOR_RADIUS_PLY = 8 ply reverse walk) from which the blunder position is reachable via moves graph. Exclude the blunder position itself. Use **only** ancestors where Position.active_color == player_color for opportunity matching — opponent-turn ancestors are context, not branch-choice opportunity.

Invariant: **reached implies denominator eligibility**. Opportunity = opportunity_only OR reached. This prevents reached_30d > opp_30d (which would make p_reach > 1).

### Data Model

**New table: blunder_opportunity_events**
- id (BigInt PK, autoincrement)
- blunder_id (BigInt FK → blunders.id, CASCADE)
- session_id (UUID FK → game_sessions.id)
- occurred_at (DateTime TZ, nullable) — use COALESCE(session.started_at, session.ended_at), NOT ended_at alone
- opportunity (Boolean) — session reached blunder ancestor (with active_color == player_color) OR exact blunder position
- reached (Boolean) — session reached blunder position exactly
- Unique constraint: (session_id, blunder_id)

**No cached columns on blunders table.** Derive all counters from events at query time. This avoids staleness of rolling 30-day counters when no new uploads occur.

### Source of Truth
1. moves, positions, blunders, blunder_opportunity_events (all tables)
2. Counters derived from events at query time (ghost scoring, blunder listing)

### Query Derived Counters

**opportunities_since_review** = COUNT(1) FROM blunder_opportunity_events WHERE blunder_id = X AND opportunity = true AND COALESCE(occurred_at, created_at) > last_reviewed_at

**opportunities_30d** = COUNT(1) FROM blunder_opportunity_events WHERE blunder_id = X AND opportunity = true AND occurred_at >= NOW - INTERVAL 30 DAYS

**reached_30d** = COUNT(1) FROM blunder_opportunity_events WHERE blunder_id = X AND reached = true AND occurred_at >= NOW - INTERVAL 30 DAYS

**p_reach** = (reached_30d + 2) / (opportunities_30d + 4)  — Laplace smoothing. By invariant, reached_30d <= opportunities_30d always.

### Session Upload Logic (backend/app/api/session.py)

After upsert:

1. **Collect session position_ids**: from session_moves, collect all position_ids via fen_hash lookup on fen_before/fen_after. Track player_color and started_at.

2. **For each candidate blunder for this user**: compute reverse ancestors from blunder.position_id via moves graph, bounded by OPPORTUNITY_ANCESTOR_RADIUS_PLY (8 ply). Exclude the blunder position itself. Filter to ancestors where Position.active_color == player_color (branch-choice opportunity).

3. **Match**: if any session position_id matches blunder ancestor → opportunity_only = true. If any session position_id matches blunder position_id → reached = true. Set opportunity = opportunity_only OR reached (invariant).

4. **Upsert event row**: for each matching blunder, upsert into blunder_opportunity_events(session_id, blunder_id, opportunity, reached, occurred_at = COALESCE(session.started_at, session.ended_at)).

No precomputed ancestors — on-the-fly walk at upload time. Ghost scoring reads only events, no graph traversal.

### Score Formula
- OPPORTUNITY_POWER = 1.5
- Due gate: opp_overdue >= 1.0 (consistent with old > 1.0 threshold)
- GhostMoveCandidate.score(now, current_opening_family) — accept param
- opening_weight: 1.0 for same family, 0.1 for different (weighted form from g-eo1 notes)
- Opening family: handle frozenset nondeterminism — deterministic sort by opening_key

### Files to Modify

1. **backend/alembic/versions/20260508_01_add_opportunity_tracking.py** (new) — create blunder_opportunity_events table
2. **backend/app/models.py** — add BlunderOpportunityEvent model (no new columns on Blunder)
3. **backend/conftest.py** — add blunder_opportunity_events table DDL
4. **backend/app/srs_math.py** — add:
   - OPPORTUNITY_POWER = 1.5
   - OPPORTUNITY_ANCESTOR_RADIUS_PLY = 8
   - expected_opportunities(pass_streak)
   - compute_p_reach(reached_30d, opp_30d)
   - calculate_opportunity_overdue(opp_since_review, pass_streak)
5. **backend/app/api/game.py**:
   - GhostMoveCandidate: no new fields — scoring function queries events at call time or accepts precomputed counters
   - Alternative approach: keep minimal fields (opp_30d, reached_30d, opening_family) passed through from find_ghost_move's CTE which joins events to derive counters inline
   - score(now, current_opening_family): accept param, opp_overdue >= 1.0 gate, OPPORTUNITY_POWER
   - find_ghost_move CTE: add event-derived counters via LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY, add opening_family, detect current opening family via _detect_opening_family()
   - due-threshold: use opp_overdue >= 1.0 when event count > 0, old calculate_priority() >= 1.0 otherwise
   - TargetBlunderSrs: add opp_since_review, opp_30d, reached_30d, p_reach fields
6. **backend/app/api/blunder.py**:
   - Add _detect_opening_family(fen_raw) — deterministic frozenset handling
   - Call from _record_target when is_new=True
   - Modify list_blunders: query events to derive counters, compute priority
   - Add opp_since_review, opp_30d, reached_30d, p_reach to BlunderListItem
7. **backend/app/api/session.py**:
   - Add _compute_blunder_opportunity_events(session_id, user_id, player_color)
   - For each blunder: walk ancestors bounded by OPPORTUNITY_ANCESTOR_RADIUS_PLY, check session positions, upsert events
   - Call after existing post-upload functions (line 311)
8. **backend/app/api/srs.py** (~line 92): Set blunder.last_reviewed_at on review — event-derived queries naturally filter by COALESCE(occurred_at, created_at) > last_reviewed_at. To handle upload-after-review in same session: exclude events from the same session as latest review when deriving opp_since_review (if latest review session_id == current session_id, skip that event for opp_since_review).

### Backfill / Compatibility
- Existing blunders: no events → all derived counters = 0, fallback to old urgency formula
- When all counters == 0: fall back to old urgency-based score
- opening_family: if NULL, opening_weight = 1.0
- No historical backfill needed

### Test Plan
- Repeated session upload: events upsert, no double-counting
- Changed/replayed upload: event row updates correctly
- Review resets opportunities_since_review (derive from events after last_reviewed_at)
- Upload-after-review in same session: event excluded from opp_since_review derivation
- True 1/100 rare-branch: ancestor reached 100 times, exact position reached once → p_reach ≈ 3/102 ≈ 0.03
- Multi-root opening-family: frozenset resolved deterministically
- Ghost move favors high-opportunity over high-severity-only
- Ancestor walk excludes blunder position itself
- Opposite-color ancestors not counted (active_color != player_color)
- Invariant: reached_30d <= opportunities_30d always (reached implies opportunity)
- p_reach bounded to (0, 1] even with Laplace smoothing and zero data
- Event table: foreign key cascade delete on blunder
notes: Review fixes applied: replayed uploads with zero parseable FENs now still delete stale opportunity events; opportunity counters now use grouped SQL aggregation with latest-review windowing instead of loading all events into Python; ghost scoring uses compute_p_reach() for the same bounded/clamped p_reach as API responses. Verification: focused review-path gate passed (82 passed); full backend pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q passed (495 passed, 1 sqlite datetime warning).
close_reason: Implemented opportunity-aware SRS scoring, reviewed, tested, and approved.

title: Fullscreen repeat-mistake warning shrinks after 5 seconds
description:
When the user repeats a mistake, show the "You made this mistake again!" warning as a full-screen overlay for 5 seconds, then animate/shrink it back into its normal in-place warning UI.

Also add a bad buzzer sound.
design:
# Design: Fullscreen repeat-mistake warning that shrinks after 5s + buzzer

## Goal
When the user repeats a known mistake (SRS review fail), the existing inline
"You made this mistake again!" srs-fail bubble is easy to miss. Promote it to a
full-screen overlay for ~5s, play a "bad buzzer" sound, then animate it shrinking
down into its existing in-place warning UI.

## Current flow (unchanged trigger point)
- `AnalysisEffects.processSrsReview` (src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.tsx:170)
  detects `!passed` and calls `appendMoveMessage(moveIndex, { variant: "srs-fail",
  text: "You made this mistake again!", srsFailDetail, srsStats })`.
- That message renders inline as `.move-bubble--srs-fail` in MoveRow.tsx:252.
- This inline bubble stays as the permanent "in-place warning UI" — we do NOT remove it.

## New: fullscreen overlay state
1. New state in ChessGame.tsx alongside showFlash (line ~153):
   `const [srsFailOverlay, setSrsFailOverlay] = useState<SrsFailDetail | null>(null)`.
   Pass `setSrsFailOverlay` into AnalysisEffects props (mirror setShowFlash wiring at
   AnalysisEffects.tsx:46/66 and ChessGame.tsx:611/1670).
2. In processSrsReview `!passed` branch, after appendMoveMessage, call
   `setSrsFailOverlay({ userMoveSan, bestMoveSan, userMoveUci, bestMoveUci })` and
   `playBuzzerAudio()`.

## Overlay lifecycle (two-phase: hold then shrink)
Mirror the showFlash timer pattern (ChessGame.tsx:1159).
- Phase A "hold": overlay mounts at full size, fade/scale-in (200ms), holds ~4.8s.
- Phase B "shrink": after 5s total, add `.srs-fail-overlay--shrink` class which runs a
  500ms scale-down + translate + fade keyframe, then unmount (`setSrsFailOverlay(null)`).
- Implement with a small effect: on overlay set, `setTimeout(()=>setPhase('shrink'),4500)`
  and a second `setTimeout(()=>setSrsFailOverlay(null), 5000)`; clear both on cleanup.
  Track phase via a sibling state `srsFailPhase: 'hold' | 'shrink'`.

## Rendering location
Render a new `<SrsFailOverlay detail phase />` inside BoardStage, in the
`.chessboard-board-area` container next to `{showFlash && <div className="blunder-flash"/>}`
(BoardStage.tsx:369), so it overlays the board (the visually dominant area) and the
shrink target (bottom move panel) sits below it. z-index above streakToast (z 8) -> use z 12.

Overlay content: large centered card — warning glyph (reuse ! / WarningTriangleIcon),
headline "You made this mistake again!", and the played-vs-best line
("You played <userMoveSan>" / "Best was <bestMoveSan>") reusing srs-fail-body styles.

## Shrink-into-place animation (App.css)
Keep it pragmatic — no cross-DOM FLIP measurement. The shrink keyframe scales the card
from 1 -> 0.15, fades opacity 1 -> 0, and translateY toward the bottom panel where the
inline bubble lives (translateY(40vh)), transform-origin bottom center. Add
`@keyframes srs-fail-overlay-in` (200ms) and `@keyframes srs-fail-overlay-shrink` (500ms
ease-in forwards). Backdrop: semi-opaque scrim (rgba(0,0,0,.55)) that fades with the card.
respect prefers-reduced-motion: skip scale/translate, just fade.

## Buzzer sound
- Add asset `public/audio/buzzer.mp3` (a short harsh error buzzer). README in public/audio.
- New util `src/utils/buzzerSound.ts` mirroring blingSound.ts: lazy `new Audio('/audio/buzzer.mp3')`,
  `preload='auto'`, `playBuzzer()` resets currentTime and `void audio.play().catch(()=>{})`.
  Guard `typeof Audio === 'undefined'` for tests/SSR.
- Call from processSrsReview `!passed` branch (best-effort, never throws).

## Tests
- AnalysisEffects/ChessGame test: on srs review fail, `.srs-fail-overlay` appears; after
  advancing timers 5000ms (vi.useFakeTimers) it unmounts; inline `.move-bubble--srs-fail`
  remains. Assert buzzer play() invoked (mock Audio). On srs pass, no overlay.
- Reduced-motion path: just assert class present; animation is CSS-only.

## Files touched
- src/components/chess-game/AnalysisEffects.tsx (trigger + buzzer + new prop)
- src/components/ChessGame.tsx (state, timers, prop wiring, pass to BoardStage)
- src/components/chess-game/ui/BoardStage.tsx (render SrsFailOverlay)
- src/components/chess-game/ui/SrsFailOverlay.tsx (new)
- src/utils/buzzerSound.ts (new) + public/audio/buzzer.mp3 (new asset)
- src/App.css (overlay + keyframes)

## Decisions (2026-06-03)
- Dismiss: click/tap-to-skip. Overlay (and scrim) is a button/clickable; onClick sets
  phase='shrink' immediately and schedules the 500ms unmount. Auto 5s path still applies
  if untouched. Clear the original 4.5s hold timer on manual skip to avoid double-trigger.
- Buzzer asset supplied by user at public/audio/buzzer.mp3. Code wires to that path now;
  if the file 404s, play() rejects and is swallowed by .catch() — no breakage.

## REVISION (2026-06-03): Spotlight the board, do not cover it
Goal correction: the 5s window is to make the user STUDY the blunder move. The board
with red (played) / green (best) arrows must stay fully visible. So the overlay is a
SPOTLIGHT, not a cover.

### Auto-reveal arrows (reuse existing reveal path)
On SRS fail, automatically perform the same state change as handleRevealSrsFail
(ChessGame.tsx:1292): setReviewFailModal({userMoveSan,bestMoveSan,userMoveUci,
bestMoveUci,evalLoss:0,moveIndex}) and setViewIndex(moveIndex-1), plus
clearBlunderBoardOverride()/setBlunderAlert(null). This drives deriveBlunderArrows
(ChessGame.tsx:295) to render red user-move + green best-move arrows and shows the
position before the mistake. It also auto-reveals the inline srs-fail bubble detail
(revealedSrsFailIndex = reviewFailModal.moveIndex, ChessGame.tsx:1647).
- Factor the body of handleRevealSrsFail into a callable (e.g. revealSrsFail(detail,
  moveIndex)) so AnalysisEffects can trigger it without a click. Pass it down (or expose
  via the same connectors that already pass onRevealSrsFail).
- Do NOT clear reviewFailModal when the overlay shrinks — arrows + revealed bubble persist
  afterward, matching today's click-to-reveal behavior. (handleNavigate already clears it
  when the user navigates away.)

### Spotlight rendering (z-index lift, no rect measuring)
Replace the "cover the board" plan:
- Fixed full-viewport scrim div `.srs-fail-scrim` at z-index 11, rgba(0,0,0,.55), fades
  in 200ms / out during shrink.
- While overlay active, add class `.chessboard-board-area--spotlit` to the board area
  container: `position: relative; z-index: 12;` plus a soft glow ring
  (box-shadow / outline) so the board sits ABOVE the scrim and stays fully lit with arrows.
  Toggle via a prop/state passed into BoardStage.
- Warning card `.srs-fail-overlay` at z-index 13, position fixed, anchored top-center
  (translateX(-50%), top: ~4vh) so it sits in the dimmed margin and never overlaps squares.
  Card content unchanged (glyph + headline + played/best line).

### Card lifecycle unchanged
Hold ~4.5s -> shrink keyframe (scale 1->0.15, translateY toward bottom panel, fade) ->
unmount at 5s. Click/tap on scrim OR card => jump to shrink early (clear hold timer).
Scrim fades out together with card; board z-lift class removed on unmount.

### Files touched (updated)
- ChessGame.tsx: extract revealSrsFail(); on overlay open set spotlight state; pass
  `isBoardSpotlit` to BoardStage; render scrim + card (or keep card in BoardStage but
  scrim/card must be fixed/full-viewport, so render at ChessGame root for safe stacking).
- BoardStage.tsx: apply `--spotlit` class to .chessboard-board-area when isBoardSpotlit.
- AnalysisEffects.tsx: on !passed call revealSrsFail(detail, moveIndex) + open overlay +
  playBuzzer().
- App.css: .srs-fail-scrim, .srs-fail-overlay, .chessboard-board-area--spotlit glow,
  keyframes (in/shrink), prefers-reduced-motion fade-only.
- SrsFailOverlay.tsx (card), buzzerSound.ts, public/audio/buzzer.mp3 (user-supplied).

### Test additions
- On srs fail: arrows present (reviewFailModal set), `.srs-fail-scrim` + `.srs-fail-overlay`
  present, `.chessboard-board-area--spotlit` applied; advance 5000ms => overlay+scrim gone,
  spotlight class gone, BUT arrows/reviewFailModal + inline bubble still present.
- Click scrim => shrink starts before 5s.

## REVISION 2 (2026-06-03): Viewport robustness — measured cutout, NOT z-index lift
The z-index spotlight from REVISION 1 is NOT viewport-safe. The board sits deep inside
the CSS grid (.chess-layout > .chessboard-board-with-eval > .chessboard-board-area). A
root-level scrim at z-index 11 paints above the entire .chess-layout subtree (which has
no z-index), so `position:relative; z-index:12` on .chessboard-board-area cannot climb
above it — the board would get dimmed too. Behavior would also vary by which ancestors
form stacking contexts => flaky across breakpoints. DISCARD the z-lift.

### Robust spotlight: measured cutout in a body portal
- Add a ref to the board element (.chessboard-board-area or the inner board square) and
  read getBoundingClientRect().
- Render scrim + card via React portal to document.body (avoids all stacking-context and
  overflow:hidden traps in the grid).
- Scrim: position:fixed; inset:0; rgba(0,0,0,.55); with a rectangle HOLE over the board
  rect via clip-path (e.g. clip-path polygon punching the board rect, or an SVG mask /
  four edge rects). Board shows through fully lit with red/green arrows.
- Recompute hole on resize + scroll via ResizeObserver + listeners; only active during the
  <=5s window so cost is negligible. Throttle with rAF.

### Card placement (responsive, from the measured rect)
- Card portal'd to body, position:fixed, horizontally centered. Compute "above vs below"
  the board hole from the rect: place above if rect.top has room, else below — so it never
  covers squares on short mobile screens.
- Pointer: scrim+card clickable for click-to-skip; the hole area is pointer-events:none so
  board stays inspectable (no interaction needed during review anyway).

### Shrink target across viewports (accepted approximate)
Inline srs-fail bubble is in the right moves column on desktop but below the board on
mobile — one translate vector can't hit both pixel-perfectly. Shrink collapses toward the
board hole's bottom edge (scale 1->0.15 + fade + translateY downward), which reads as
"folding back down" in both layouts. Pixel-perfect FLIP onto the bubble is explicitly out
of scope.

### Net: works mobile->desktop ONLY via this measured-portal-cutout approach.
Files: add SrsFailSpotlight.tsx (portal: scrim cutout + card, takes board ref/rect),
remove the BoardStage `--spotlit` class plan and the board z-lift. Keep buzzer + reveal +
lifecycle (hold 4.5s / shrink / click-skip) unchanged.

## FINAL DECISION (2026-06-03) — approved via prototype
Reference prototype kept at repo root: `prototype-spotlight.html` (open in browser,
click "Trigger"). The implementation should match its look/behavior. Chosen design:

### Visual
- Scrim cutout: position:fixed full-viewport scrim (rgba(0,0,0,~.6)) portal'd to
  document.body, with a clip-path rectangle HOLE measured over the board's live
  getBoundingClientRect() (+~8px pad). Board stays fully lit so red/green arrows read.
  Re-track the hole on resize + scroll (capture) while active; throttle with rAF.
- Content: ONLY a red "!" glyph + headline "You made this mistake again!". NO background
  tint over the board, NO played/best line, NO helper text. Legibility from a strong
  text-shadow on the headline (0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.95), 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,.9)) and a
  drop-shadow on the glyph. Glyph+headline pinned to the TOP of the board, centered
  (left = rect.left+rect.width/2, translateX(-50%), top ≈ rect.top + min(18px, 4% height)).
  Also portal'd to body, z above the scrim. Sizes use clamp() so it scales mobile→desktop.
- Discard earlier alternatives: the on-board translucent-tint card (REVISION) and the
  z-index board lift (REVISION 1) are both rejected.

### Behavior / lifecycle
- Hold ~4.5s, then shrink: scrim fades out (.5s) and content scales to ~0.12 + fades
  (transform-origin top center). Unmount ~520ms later. Total ≈5s.
- Click anywhere on the scrim OR the content => skip straight to shrink (clear hold timer).
- prefers-reduced-motion: fade only, no scale.

### Arrows (auto-reveal so the move is visible under the spotlight)
On SRS fail, auto-trigger the existing reveal path (factor body of handleRevealSrsFail at
ChessGame.tsx:1292 into a reusable fn): setReviewFailModal({...}) + setViewIndex(moveIndex-1)
+ clearBlunderBoardOverride() + setBlunderAlert(null). Drives deriveBlunderArrows
(ChessGame.tsx:295) to show red played + green best arrows and parks the board on the
pre-mistake position. Do NOT clear reviewFailModal when the spotlight closes (handleNavigate
clears it when the user moves away).

### Buzzer
buzzerSound.ts modeled on blingSound.ts; play() from processSrsReview !passed branch,
best-effort. Asset public/audio/buzzer.mp3 supplied by user; missing file just no-ops.

### Wiring sketch
- New component src/components/chess-game/ui/SrsFailSpotlight.tsx: props { active,
  targetRef (board element), onDone }. Owns phase state + hold/shrink timers + click-skip +
  resize/scroll re-measure; renders scrim+content via createPortal(document.body).
- BoardStage.tsx: add ref to .chessboard-board-area; render <SrsFailSpotlight
  active={srsFailActive} targetRef={boardAreaRef} onDone={onDismissSrsFail} />. New props
  srsFailActive + onDismissSrsFail threaded from ChessGame.
- ChessGame.tsx: state srsFailActive; reusable revealSrsFail(detail,moveIndex); pass
  setSrsFailActive + revealSrsFail into AnalysisEffects.
- AnalysisEffects.tsx processSrsReview !passed: revealSrsFail(detail,moveIndex) +
  setSrsFailActive(true) + playBuzzer().

### Tests
- srs fail: arrows present (reviewFailModal set), scrim + content present; advance 5000ms =>
  gone, but reviewFailModal/arrows + inline bubble persist. Click scrim => early shrink.
  Buzzer play() mocked. srs pass: nothing. Reduced-motion: class present (CSS-only anim).

## PLAN CORRECTIONS (2026-06-03, from review)
1. Retrigger (was: srsFailActive:boolean). A boolean won't re-fire while already
   active, but AnalysisEffects can process multiple/out-of-order/same-tick SRS
   resolutions (AnalysisEffects.tsx:125; AnalysisEffects.test.tsx:259). REPLACE the
   boolean with a nonce trigger: ChessGame holds
   `srsFailTrigger: { id: number; moveIndex: number } | null` (bump id each fail).
   SrsFailSpotlight takes the trigger as a prop and resets phase + hold/shrink timers
   in an effect keyed on trigger.id (clear prior timers first). A new fail mid-display
   restarts the 5s cleanly. onDone clears only if id matches the current trigger.

2. Measure the actual board square, NOT .chessboard-board-area. .chessboard-board-area
   is just a flex container (BoardStage.tsx:142; App.css:584) and the prototype measures
   the square board (prototype-spotlight.html:60,83). Add a dedicated ref on the
   Chessboard's square root (wrap <Chessboard> in a div with ref, or ref the board
   wrapper) and measure THAT for the clip-path hole + content top placement.

3. Timing constants (avoid flaky tests). Export shared constants, e.g.
   SRS_FAIL_HOLD_MS and SRS_FAIL_SHRINK_MS, used by the component AND tests. Either make
   hold+shrink total exactly 5000ms, or have tests advance past hold+shrink (e.g. >5020ms)
   / advance by the constants. Do not assert "gone at exactly 5000ms" against a
   4500+520ms timeline.

4. Click-to-skip contract — DECISION: clicking the dimmed scrim skips; the board hole is
   pointer-events:none so clicks there fall through to the board and do NOT skip (board
   stays inspectable). The content (glyph+headline) also skips on click. Document this and
   test "click dimmed scrim => early shrink" (not clicks on the board hole).
notes: Implemented per FINAL DECISION + PLAN CORRECTIONS. Files: buzzerSound.ts (new), SrsFailSpotlight.tsx (new portal: scrim cutout via clip-path + glyph/headline, nonce trigger, hold 4500ms/shrink 520ms, click-scrim-skip, resize/scroll re-measure), BoardStage.tsx (wrapper ref .chessboard-square-measure + render spotlight), ChessGame.tsx (srsFailTrigger nonce state, triggerSrsFailSpotlight reusing handleRevealSrsFail, handleSrsFailDone), AnalysisEffects.tsx (onSrsFail prop + playBuzzer in !passed branch), App.css (scrim/content + keyframes + reduced-motion). Tests: SrsFailSpotlight.test.tsx (3) + AnalysisEffects fail-path test (buzzer+onSrsFail). Full suite 783 pass, tsc+build clean. Buzzer asset public/audio/buzzer.mp3 user-supplied (missing=no-op). NOT committed pending review.
close_reason: Implemented full-screen repeat-mistake spotlight + buzzer; tests green, build clean

title: Add sounds
description: Add sounds for chess moves. The audio file public/audio/move.m4a is for a regularmove and public/audio/take.m4a for a capture move.
design:
# Plan: Add move/capture sounds (g-a6wi)

## Context
The board currently plays audio for blunders, best moves, the SRS buzzer, and
end-game results, but ordinary moves are silent. We want tactile feedback on
every move: a soft "move" sound for regular moves and a distinct "take" sound
for captures. The two clips already exist: `public/audio/move.m4a` and
`public/audio/take.m4a`. Sounds should play for **all** moves (player, opponent/
engine, and ghost), matching Lichess/Chess.com behavior.

## Approach

### 1. New util: `src/utils/moveSound.ts`
Mirror the existing singleton pattern in `src/utils/buzzerSound.ts`. Cache two
`HTMLAudioElement`s (lazy, guarded by `typeof Audio === "undefined"` for the
test/SSR environment), and export:

```ts
export function playMoveSound(isCapture: boolean): void
```

It selects `/audio/move.m4a` or `/audio/take.m4a`, then resets
`currentTime = 0` and calls `.play()`. **Fully best-effort**: wrap the entire
body in `try/catch` (mirroring `endGameAudio.ts:62`) so a synchronous throw from
`new Audio(...)`, `currentTime`, or `play()` can never bubble into the move
commit path, and also swallow the async rejection via `.play()?.catch?.(() => {})`.

Note on autoplay: the first async engine/ghost sound may be blocked by the
browser until a user gesture unlocks audio. This is acceptable best-effort
behavior — no special unlock handling.

### 2. Hook into the single move chokepoint
All three move paths (`applyPlayerMove`, `applyEngineMove`, `applyGhostMove`)
funnel through `commitAppliedMove` in
`src/hooks/useChessGameController.ts` (line ~114). Add a `playMoveSound(...)`
call there. The chess.js `AppliedMove` exposes `appliedMove.captured`
(`string | undefined`) — use `Boolean(appliedMove.captured)` to pick the clip.
Place the call near the top of `commitAppliedMove`, before/after `chess.fen()`.

Note: history scrubbing/replay uses a separate Chess instance (`ChessGame.tsx`
line 96 `replayed.move(...)`) and does **not** go through `commitAppliedMove`,
so rewinding won't trigger sounds. Good.

Intentional overlap: best/blunder moves will now play an immediate move/capture
sound **plus** the existing delayed analysis audio (best-move bling / blunder
clip). This is intended — move feedback is immediate, analysis feedback follows.

### 3. Update docs: `public/audio/README.md`
Add a short section documenting `move.m4a` (regular move) and `take.m4a`
(capture), and that `commitAppliedMove` picks based on `move.captured`. While
here, fix the existing mismatch: the README lists `bestmove.mp3`, but
`src/utils/blingSound.ts:1` actually plays `/audio/bestmove2.wav` — correct the
doc to match.

### 4. Tests
**`src/utils/moveSound.test.ts`** — vitest. Because the util caches singleton
`HTMLAudioElement`s, isolate each test with `vi.resetModules()` + dynamic
`import()` of the module, stub `Audio` via `vi.stubGlobal`, and clean up with
`vi.unstubAllGlobals()`. Assert:
- `playMoveSound(false)` plays the `move.m4a` clip; `playMoveSound(true)` plays
  `take.m4a`
- no throw when `Audio` is undefined
- no throw when the `Audio` constructor / `play()` throws **synchronously**
- async `.play()` rejection is swallowed

**Controller integration** (`src/hooks/useChessGameController.test.ts`) — mock
`playMoveSound` and assert it fires once per move with the correct `isCapture`
arg across the player, engine, and ghost paths, plus at least one capture case.
This is the real behavioral guarantee since `commitAppliedMove` is the chokepoint.

## Files
- `src/utils/moveSound.ts` (new)
- `src/utils/moveSound.test.ts` (new)
- `src/hooks/useChessGameController.ts` (add one call in `commitAppliedMove`)
- `src/hooks/useChessGameController.test.ts` (integration coverage)
- `public/audio/README.md` (docs + bestmove2.wav fix)

## Reuse
- `src/utils/buzzerSound.ts` — singleton Audio pattern to copy.
- `src/components/chess-game/endGameAudio.ts:62` — try/catch best-effort style.
- `AppliedMove.captured` — already available, no new move-parsing needed.

## Verification
- `npm test` — new `moveSound.test.ts` + controller tests pass; existing tests stay green.
- Manual (`npm run dev`): make a non-capturing move → hear `move.m4a`; make a
  capture → hear `take.m4a`; confirm opponent/engine and ghost moves also play;
  confirm scrubbing back through history is silent.
notes:
- For the capture integration test, use an actual capture sequence so chess.js
    sets appliedMove.captured, for example e4, d5, then exd5.

  - Reset the mocked playMoveSound in beforeEach, matching the existing test
    style.

title: Define deployment architecture
description:
No deployment strategy is specified.

## Components to Deploy

1. **Frontend** - Static React app
2. **Backend** - Python FastAPI server
3. **Database** - PostgreSQL

## Options

### Option A: Simple VPS (MVP)
- Single DigitalOcean/Linode droplet
- Docker Compose for all services
- Nginx reverse proxy
- Let's Encrypt SSL

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports: ['3000:3000']
  
  backend:
    build: ./backend
    ports: ['8000:8000']
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://...
  
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  
  nginx:
    image: nginx
    ports: ['80:80', '443:443']
```

- Pros: Simple, cheap (~$10/mo), full control
- Cons: Manual scaling, single point of failure

### Option B: Platform as a Service
- **Frontend**: Vercel or Netlify (free tier)
- **Backend**: Railway, Render, or Fly.io
- **Database**: Managed Postgres (Supabase, Neon, Railway)

- Pros: No ops, auto-scaling, easy deploys
- Cons: Can get expensive, less control

### Option C: Cloud Native (Future)
- AWS/GCP with Terraform
- ECS or Cloud Run for backend
- RDS for database
- CloudFront for frontend

- Pros: Production-grade, scalable
- Cons: Complex, expensive, overkill for MVP

## Recommendation
**Option B for MVP**:
- Vercel for frontend (free, great DX)
- Railway or Fly.io for backend
- Neon or Supabase for Postgres

## CI/CD Pipeline
```yaml
# GitHub Actions
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm test
      - run: pytest
  
  deploy-frontend:
    needs: test
    # Vercel auto-deploys from GitHub
  
  deploy-backend:
    needs: test
    steps:
      - uses: railway/deploy-action
```

## Environment Management
- Development: Local Docker Compose
- Staging: Separate deployment (optional for MVP)
- Production: Main deployment

## Secrets Management
- Use platform's env var management
- Never commit secrets
- Document required env vars

title: Add time control options for games
description:
The spec doesn't mention time controls for games.

## Questions

### Is Time Control Needed for MVP?
Arguments for:
- More realistic game experience
- Prevents endless thinking
- Adds pressure (blunders more likely under time)

Arguments against:
- Adds complexity
- Training app, not competitive
- Users might want unlimited time to think

### Options

1. **No time control (MVP)**
   - Unlimited thinking time
   - Simplest implementation
   - Focus on learning, not speed

2. **Optional time control**
   - User chooses: None, 5+0, 10+0, 15+10, etc.
   - Engine also plays on clock
   - Clock UI component needed

3. **Per-move time limit**
   - Not a full clock, but max time per move
   - e.g., 60 seconds per move
   - Simpler than full clock

## Implementation (if adding)

### Frontend
- Clock component (two clocks, user + engine)
- Time selector in game setup
- Visual/audio warning when low on time
- Game ends on timeout

### Backend
- Store time control in game session
- Track time used per move
- Validate move timestamps

### Engine Consideration
- Stockfish needs time management
- `go wtime X btime Y` command
- Different from unlimited `go depth 20`

## Recommendation
**No time control for MVP**. Add as enhancement later if users request it.

## Future Enhancement
- Track 'thinking time' per move even without clock
- Analytics: 'You blunder more when thinking > 30 seconds'

title: Address graph scalability and pruning strategy
description:
The position graph could grow very large. Common opening positions (e4, d4, Nf3) will be traversed constantly.

## Scale Concerns

### Position Growth
- Every unique position = new row
- Opening positions shared across all users (if not per-user)
- Endgame positions less likely to repeat

### Query Performance
- Recursive CTE for path finding
- Worse as graph grows
- Need indexes on fen_hash, is_blunder, srs_due_date

## Architecture Questions

### Per-User vs Shared Positions?

**Option A: Shared positions table**
```sql
-- positions table is global
-- blunders table is per-user, references positions
```
- Pros: Deduplication, smaller DB
- Cons: Queries need user filter

**Option B: Per-user positions**
```sql
-- Each user has their own position nodes
-- No sharing between users
```
- Pros: Simpler queries, user isolation
- Cons: Massive duplication of common positions

**Recommendation**: Shared positions, per-user blunders

### Pruning Strategies

1. **Orphan cleanup**
   - Positions with no blunders and no edges = delete
   - Run as scheduled job

2. **Old position archival**
   - Positions not accessed in 1 year -> cold storage
   - Unlikely for active blunders

3. **Graph compaction**
   - Merge linear chains of positions (no branches)
   - Complex, maybe not worth it

## Index Strategy
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_positions_fen_hash ON positions(fen_hash);
CREATE INDEX idx_blunders_user_due ON blunders(user_id, srs_due_date) WHERE srs_due_date IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_moves_from ON moves(from_position_id);
```

## Monitoring
- Track table sizes over time
- Monitor query latency for path-finding
- Alert if growth exceeds projections

title: Handle concurrent sessions (multi-tab play)
description:
What happens if a user opens multiple browser tabs and plays simultaneous games?

## Scenarios

1. **Tab A and Tab B both playing**
   - Both legitimate games
   - Both should track blunders independently
   - Each has own session_id

2. **Tab A playing, Tab B opens same game**
   - User refreshes or duplicates tab
   - Should resume same session, not create new one

3. **Ghost mode conflicts**
   - Tab A triggers ghost mode for blunder X
   - Tab B independently reaches blunder X
   - Both valid, no conflict

## Implementation Options

### Option A: Allow freely
- Each tab = independent session
- No special handling needed
- Pros: Simple
- Cons: User could 'cheat' by practicing same blunder in parallel

### Option B: Single active session
- Only one game allowed at a time
- New tab shows 'Game in progress in another tab'
- Pros: Cleaner UX, no cheating
- Cons: More complex, needs websocket or polling

### Option C: Session recovery
- Store session_id in localStorage
- New tab checks for active session
- Option to 'resume' or 'abandon and start new'

## Recommendation
Option A for MVP (simplest). Revisit if cheating becomes a concern.

## Notes
- Document expected behavior
- Consider adding session metadata to blunder records for debugging

title: Frequency-weight opponent book branches in opening score & coverage (DEFERRED: needs data volume)
description: Opponent-node weights in the opening scorer are currently UNIFORM over book replies (backend/app/opening_rootcalc.py:406 in _base_weights). For the 'ready in real games' framing, being unprepared for a high-popularity mainline should cost more than a rare sideline. Weight opponent branches by real-game popularity so both the score AND coverage track actual risk. Intended source: aggregate frequency from our own players' games. Alternative to consider that could unblock earlier: an external book/popularity source (e.g. Lichess opening explorer) instead of internal player data. Related to g-zc3p (readiness score, which establishes the opponent-breadth handling this refines).
