title: v2-deprecation Phase 2: migrate canonical writer (precompute) off v2 to grain contracts
description: precompute_openings.py still stamps resolver-complete-v2 on every canonical row. Migrate it to write position_analysis (position-complete-v1) + analysis_cache move rows (move-complete-v1) directly. BLOCKED by g-6xc3.
design:
Migrate the canonical writer off v2 so it produces grain-specific contracts directly.
BLOCKED by g-6xc3 (cross-grain replacement policy) — do not start until g-6xc3 lands with
the asymmetric replacement tests.

`backend/scripts/precompute_openings.py` — stop producing v2; produce both grains:
- `_result_row` (~706): stop hardcoding `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2`. Move rows go to
  `analysis_cache` stamped via `select_canonical_move_contract(data)` -> `move-complete-v1`.
  Fail-closed: a `None` return (row does not satisfy move-complete) is a hard write FAILURE
  that fails the run manifest for that position — a canonical producer that cannot emit valid
  move evidence aborts the position; it is NOT silently dropped.
- Add a position write: emit one `position_analysis` row per `normalize_fen(fen_before)` via
  `app.position_analysis_repo.write_position_analysis_row` (position-complete-v1), routed
  through the existing position dominance policy. Replaces "precompute writes v2 -> backfill
  projects to storage" with a direct write.
- Dual-write transaction boundary: `write_position_analysis_row` stages + `flush()`es on the
  CALLER session (caller owns the txn); `write_analysis_cache_rows` REFUSES an in-transaction
  caller and opens its own isolated txn. They cannot share one open transaction. Required
  order per batch: (1) write AND COMMIT the position_analysis rows on the caller session so it
  is clean; (2) call `write_analysis_cache_rows` for the move batch (its own txn);
  (3) post-write verification re-reads both stores. Treat the pair as NON-atomic: a position
  counts written only when both grains verify, so a partial success self-heals — the next run
  re-processes any position missing either verified grain. Document this; do not assume atomic.
- Resume gate (`filter_unstored_positions` ~798-814 and `_verify_stored` ~755-781): preserve
  today's VERIFIED gate, never weaken to row presence. Today: done only when the stored row
  passes `_identity_verified` + `contract_satisfied(v2)`. Migrated: done only when BOTH
  (a) the move row is `_identity_verified` + `contract_satisfied(MOVE_COMPLETE)`, AND
  (b) a `position_analysis` winner for `normalize_fen(fen_before)` is identity-verified +
  `contract_satisfied(POSITION_COMPLETE)`. Malformed/partial rows are re-analyzed.
- `assert_can_produce_target_contract` default (~673) and run manifest (~1077): target the
  grain contracts, asserting capability to produce both the played-eval (move) and
  best-move+PV+eval (position) evidence.
- `eval_delta` on the move row becomes a documented canonical-run snapshot (move-complete does
  not validate the cross-grain invariant) — used by blunder/SRS/display only.

Hard dependency g-6xc3 (asymmetric on authority, NOT contract supersession — move-complete-v1
is deliberately not a v2 superset). g-6xc3 must land with tests pinning BOTH directions:
  - canonical AUTHORITATIVE move-complete-v1 MAY replace a NON-authoritative browser
    resolver-complete-v2 row for the same (fen_before, move_uci) key; and
  - an arbitrary / NON-authoritative move-complete-v1 row MUST NOT replace an AUTHORITATIVE
    resolver-complete-v2 row.

Verify: `pytest backend/test_precompute_*.py backend/test_analysis_cache_policy.py`; scratch-DB
precompute run asserting no new v2 rows, populated `position_analysis`, the verified-both-grains
resume gate, and a partial-write rerun that completes the missing grain.
acceptance_criteria: Precompute writes no new v2 rows; move rows stamped move-complete-v1 (fail-closed on None -> manifest failure); position_analysis written directly; dual-write ordered (commit positions, then move rows, then verify) and treated as non-atomic/self-healing; resume gate requires BOTH a contract_satisfied(MOVE_COMPLETE) move row AND a verified position_analysis winner; precompute + cache-policy tests green.

title: Background-worker opportunity recompute scales with whole user graph (heavy-blunder users)
description:
Background-worker optimization (DOWNGRADED): _compute_blunder_opportunity_events
scales with the user's ENTIRE blunder/position graph, not the current session.
Real inefficiency, but the original /moves-latency premise no longer holds.

STATUS — premise largely mitigated after this bead was filed (2026-06-23):
- g-yjtn (2026-06-27, "defer /moves graph+SRS evidence side effects to background
  worker"): the whole evidence pipeline (advisory lock + ghost-graph upsert +
  opportunity recompute + commit + analysis-cache write + recompute enqueue) now
  runs on the single daemon worker in app/session_evidence_scheduler.py, NOT on
  the /moves request path. The 2-4s is no longer user-visible latency.
- g-y90g (2026-06-28, "recompute opportunity once at finalize, not per increment"):
  the opportunity recompute is gated by run_opportunity / recompute_opportunity.
  Mid-game incremental uploads SKIP it; it runs once per session at finalize. The
  original "cost multiplies if /moves fires per-batch" concern is gone.

So the title's "2-4s residual on /moves" no longer describes a user-facing bug.
What remains is a background-thread CPU/DB inefficiency, not a latency bug.

The inefficiency itself still exists (verified 2026-06-29, line numbers current):
1. db.query(Blunder).filter(Blunder.user_id == user_id).all() loads ALL ~628
   blunders every recompute (backend/app/api/session.py:615).
2. _forward_reachable_position_ids(...) runs an 8-level forward BFS over the
   user's whole position graph (session.py:612, fn at 294-338).
3. Python loop over every blunder (session.py:616).
This is a flat ~2-4s per finalize for a many-blunder user, scaling with the
user's total graph rather than the session.

Residual real-world risk (narrow): app/session_evidence_scheduler.py uses a
SINGLE daemon worker that serializes ALL users' evidence runs. Under concurrent
finalize load, a few 2-4s recomputes for heavy-blunder users could back the queue
up. This is a worker-throughput edge case for heavy users only — not correctness,
not request latency.

Original measurement (server.log, many-blunder user 14, session
9a09bcb2-659c-453c-bf3d-2092de51f2dc) — these were per-/moves-call BEFORE g-yjtn/
g-y90g, retained for context:
- opportunity_events: n=28, avg=2872.7ms, max=4824.9ms
- ghost_graph_upsert:   avg=237.2ms, max=670.9ms
- analysis_cache_write: avg=158.2ms, max=376.1ms
- analytics:            avg=30.8ms
- session_moves_upsert: avg=51.8ms
- evidence_commit:      avg=43.7ms

Proposed fixes (if/when this becomes a worker bottleneck):
- Scope the blunder query to positions relevant to this session rather than
  loading the full per-user set.
- Cache or incrementally maintain the forward-reachable BFS instead of
  recomputing per finalize.
- Confirm finalize concurrency / worker-queue depth in prod before investing.

How to check timing logs:
- Backend logs via StreamHandler to stderr (backend/app/logging_config.py) — no
  file handler; backend/server.log only populated if uvicorn output is tee'd.
- Run: cd backend && .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000 --host
  0.0.0.0 --env-file .env 2>&1 | tee server.log
- Then: grep 'side_effect=opportunity_events' backend/server.log | sed -E
  's/.*elapsed_ms=([0-9.]+).*/\1/'
acceptance_criteria: If pursued: opportunity_events recompute is sub-second (target <1000ms, ideally <500ms) for a many-blunder user (user 14, ~628 blunders) measured via the side_effect=opportunity_events timing line on the evidence worker; no regression in opportunity-event correctness (g-8y63 forward-BFS unit tests still pass). NOTE: no longer a /moves request-latency criterion — measured on the background worker (g-yjtn) at session finalize (g-y90g).
notes:
Discovered during g-w2ex manual verification on 2026-06-22. Epic g-zuym hypothesized _upsert_analysis_cache as the slow side effect; instrumentation disproved that and pointed at opportunity_events instead.
2026-06-29: downgraded P2->P3 and reframed. Original /moves-latency premise mitigated by g-yjtn (deferred to background worker) + g-y90g (once-per-finalize, not per-batch). Underlying O(all-blunders + full-graph-BFS) inefficiency confirmed still present in code but now off the request path; residual is worker-throughput only.

title: Backend exact-best projection for lookup/session payloads
description:
## Problem

The live drill MoveList issue was fixed in the frontend by promoting a published AnalysisResult when request-bound trusted position truth says the played move equals the trusted best move. That is correct for the live ChessGame path, but it leaves the resolver contract split across consumers: /api/analysis/lookup can still return a flattened payload where position truth says the played move is best while move-grain evidence is untrusted or worker fallback later under-rates the move.

A backend resolver projection would make trusted exact-best results a single source of truth for all consumers. When a requested played move equals the trusted position grain's best_move_uci, the backend can derive coherent exact-best move facts from the position grain instead of requiring separate trusted move-grain evidence for the classification. This should also address similar seed/display issues in AnalysisBoard and session-review payloads if the same projection helper is used there.

Important constraint: do not silently redefine raw browser-game move rows as trusted canonical move evidence. The backend should distinguish derived exact-best facts from independently trusted move-grain evidence.
design:
## Target Design

Add a backend response projection for trusted exact-best requests, shared by /api/analysis/lookup and session/AnalysisBoard payload production where applicable.

When the resolver has trusted position evidence and the requested played move equals trusted position.best_move_uci, derive a coherent exact-best result:

- classification: best
- best_move_uci / best_move_san: the trusted position best move
- best_line_uci: the trusted position PV when available
- position_eval_loss_cp: 0
- eval_delta: 0 only if the contract explicitly allows exact-best zero loss for this response surface
- played_eval / played_eval_mate: derived from the trusted position best_eval / best_eval_mate only under a documented derived-exact-best contract, or left as unavailable with an explicit exact-best flag if mate/CP semantics make derivation unsafe
- source/provenance fields should identify the value as position-derived exact-best, not raw move-row evidence

Do not simply stamp move_trusted: true on an untrusted browser-game move row without changing the contract. Prefer one of these explicit approaches:

1. Add fields such as derived_exact_best: true and classification_source: trusted-position-exact-best while leaving move_trusted to mean independent move-grain trust.
2. Add a grain-specific evidence contract such as move-derived-best-v1 and make move_trusted true only for that derived response contract, not for the underlying AnalysisCache row.
3. Split response metadata so independent move trust and derived classification trust are separate booleans.

The chosen contract must prevent consumers from assuming a canonical played-eval move row exists when the backend only derived exact-best from position truth.

## Consumer Cutover

Use the same backend helper in all payload-producing paths that flatten position and move facts:

- /api/analysis/lookup
- session drill-review export used by AnalysisBoard/sessionUpload paths
- any compatibility adapter that still returns old CachedAnalysis-shaped fields

This is expected to supersede or reduce the frontend-only promotion in GameAnalysisCoordinator once all relevant consumers receive the backend-derived exact-best projection.

## Tradeoffs

Pros:
- Backend becomes the single source of truth for exact-best projection.
- Fix applies to AnalysisBoard/session review and not only the live ChessGame coordinator.
- Frontend cache guards can remain simple if the response explicitly says the classification was trusted/derived.
- Session uploads and display consumers receive coherent best-move evidence without waiting for local worker fallback.

Risks:
- Overloading move_trusted would erode the position-vs-move grain split.
- Emitting eval_delta: 0 for mate-bearing rows needs an explicit rule because current threshold-loss migration is CP-only.
- If only classification changes but move_trusted/hasCpEvalLoss gates remain false, frontend published paths may still fall back to worker and miss the projection.
- Multiple backend consumers may each have their own flattening logic; the fix should be centralized to avoid drift.

## Relationship To Existing Work

The frontend g-move-best-icon fix remains a narrow live-path safeguard. This backend bead is the long-term contract cleanup. It should preserve the g-position-analysis invariant that browser-game rows cannot define strict position truth; only trusted position rows may produce derived exact-best facts.
acceptance_criteria:
- /api/analysis/lookup returns a coherent derived exact-best payload when requested move_uci equals trusted position best_move_uci even if independent move-grain evidence is absent or untrusted.
- The response explicitly distinguishes derived exact-best facts from independently trusted move-grain evidence; raw browser-game rows are not silently treated as canonical move evidence.
- AnalysisBoard/session-review payload production uses the same projection helper or has an explicitly tested equivalent path.
- Non-best moves such as Bf4 at the g-ul4p position retain their original non-best classification/evidence and do not get promoted.
- Exact-best CP rows expose loss 0 consistently for drill/display consumers.
- Mate-bearing exact-best behavior is explicitly documented and tested: either safe loss-0 projection is supported or numeric threshold loss remains unavailable with a separate exact-best flag.
- Frontend fallback/published-path behavior is audited so the backend projection is actually consumed instead of being bypassed by move_trusted/hasCpEvalLoss gates.
- Tests cover the g-ul4p sibling-row case: Bf4 remains excellent/non-best, c4 returns derived best from trusted position truth despite untrusted move evidence.
- Tests cover session/AnalysisBoard payloads receiving the same derived exact-best classification/trust metadata.
- SPEC.md is updated if the wire contract or trust flag semantics change.
notes:
## DEFERRED (P4) — cleanup, not an active bug

Downgraded from P2 to P4 on 2026-06-29 after auditing the actual consumers. This is an architectural single-source-of-truth cleanup, not a user-visible bug. No related bug is currently observable in normal play/review.

### Why it is currently unnecessary

The exact-best projection already exists and is applied client-side by the shipped `reconcileTrustedBest` helper (`src/workers/analysisUtils.ts:431`), which covers every interactive consumer:
- Live ChessGame / MoveList — `GameAnalysisCoordinator.ts:1471`.
- Post-game interactive AnalysisBoard — `useMoveAnalysis.ts:225`.
- Drill review (`DrillAnalysisPage` -> `buildDrillAnalysisSnapshot`) is internally coherent: classification and best both come from the same local worker run, so the two grains cannot disagree.

The only remaining consumer with a visible gap is the finished-game review path (`GameAnalysisPage` -> `AnalysisBoard`), which renders the backend session export verbatim (`AnalysisBoard.tsx:385/1029`) without reconciliation. That gap is now tracked narrowly in g-kfxj as a client-side mirror of the existing helper — no backend wire-contract change required. Note the session export already exposes `position_trusted` per position (`api.ts:1137`, set at `session.py:1260/1268`), so the client can gate the projection on trusted positions without backend help.

So the full backend rework here buys only "single source of truth" tidiness; it does not fix any user-facing symptom that g-kfxj won't already cover.

### What would revive this as a more important issue

Raise priority and prefer the backend projection over more client-side mirrors if any of these become true:
1. A NON-JS or non-self-correcting consumer appears that flattens position+move facts and cannot run `reconcileTrustedBest` client-side — e.g. a server-rendered page, a public/3rd-party API surface, email/share/embed/PGN export, or a native/mobile client. Those can only get coherent exact-best from the backend.
2. Client-side patching drifts: the reconcile rule starts getting duplicated/forked across paths (currently the helper is single-sourced; g-kfxj adds a third call site). If keeping them in sync becomes error-prone, centralizing in the backend is worth the contract risk.
3. A consumer needs coherent classification BEFORE the client can post-process (e.g. server-side accuracy/summary stats, or filtering/sorting by "best" on the server).
4. We need mate-aware exact-best loss semantics or a documented `derived_exact_best` wire contract for external consumers — the CP-only client shortcut is not sufficient there.
5. g-kfxj's client mirror proves insufficient or itself becomes a maintenance burden.

Until one of those holds, prefer the narrow client fix (g-kfxj) and keep this deferred. Preserve the g-position-analysis invariant in any future work: only trusted position rows may produce derived exact-best facts; untrusted/browser-game rows must not be silently treated as canonical move evidence.

title: Deprecate legacy resolver-complete-v2 semantics after position-analysis cutover
description: Follow-up from g-position-analysis.7. Once position_analysis read paths are fully cut over and backfill is verified, retire the legacy mixed-grain resolver-complete-v2 projection semantics. Scope: audit remaining trusted_for_resolution readers, remove or quarantine frontend/backend compatibility fields, update evidence contract helpers/tests, and ensure post-split move writes never rely on v2.
design:
# Plan: g-v2-deprecation — Retire legacy `resolver-complete-v2` semantics

## Context

`g-position-analysis` split position-level best-move truth (`position_analysis`,
`normalized_fen`) from move-level evidence (`analysis_cache`, `(fen_before, move_uci)`)
and replaced the single `trusted_for_resolution` flag with grain-specific
`position_trusted` / `move_trusted`. All 8 phases are closed. `g-v2-deprecation` is the
scheduled follow-up to retire the legacy mixed-grain `resolver-complete-v2` projection
that was deliberately kept alive during the migration.

**Grounding reality (verified in code, not assumed):** the bead's precondition —
"position_analysis read paths fully cut over and backfill verified" — is only half true.

- **Reads ARE cut over.** `resolve_trusted_positions` (position_analysis_repo.py) reads
  storage first and only falls back to a trusted v2 cache row; `analysis.py` emits
  `position_trusted`/`move_trusted`; the frontend reads only those (api.ts, AnalysisBoard,
  analysisUtils).
- **Writes are NOT.** `backend/scripts/precompute_openings.py:706` still stamps
  `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2` on every canonical row. `select_canonical_move_contract`
  (evidence_contracts.py:299) exists but is **never called in production**.
- **Legacy v2 projection is load-bearing for trust.** `move_trust_flags`
  (analysis_trust.py:77-90) grants `move_trusted` to *all* canonical move evidence via
  `legacy_v2_satisfies_move`; `position_trust_flags` and the repo fallback grant position
  trust via `legacy_v2_satisfies_position`. Removing the projection today would
  mass-untrust every canonical row — exactly the hazard the migration design warned about.
- **`trusted_for_resolution` is already dead on the frontend** (api.ts marks it
  `@deprecated`, zero reads) but the backend still computes/emits it.

So the core deprecation is **hard-blocked** on first migrating the canonical writer and
re-stamping existing v2 rows. Only the `trusted_for_resolution` wire-field removal is
unblocked.

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

1. **Promote `g-v2-deprecation` to an epic** with sequenced sub-beads; existing `g-6xc3`
   becomes a dependency of the writer-migration sub-bead.
2. **Ship the `trusted_for_resolution` removal now** as its own slice (zero live consumers).
3. **Keep `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2` registered as a historical, no-trust contract** at the
   end — preserve its `supersedes` chain (`RESOLVER_COMPLETE`/`MINIMAL_*` → v2) and audit
   readability; it simply stops conferring any position/move trust.

## Trust-flow being dismantled

```
canonical precompute ──writes──▶ analysis_cache row stamped resolver-complete-v2
                                   │ (carries BOTH best_* and played_* today)
        ┌──────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
   position grain                                          move grain
   backfill projects v2 → position_analysis            move_trust_flags grants
   (position-complete-v1)         AND                  move_trusted via
   resolve_trusted_positions      legacy_v2_satisfies_move (declared-id gate)
   v2-cache fallback tier
```
Target end-state: precompute writes `position_analysis` (position-complete-v1) + move
rows (move-complete-v1) directly; trust comes only from the grain contracts; v2 confers
nothing.

## Epic decomposition (5 sub-beads + g-6xc3)

DAG:  `.1` ships independently in parallel with  `g-6xc3 → .2 → .3 → .4 → .5`.

---

### g-v2-deprecation.1 — Remove `trusted_for_resolution` wire field  (UNBLOCKED — ship now)

Backend `backend/app/api/analysis.py`:
- **Do not delete `_trust_flags()` wholesale** — its `authoritative` and `contract_satisfied`
  return values still populate the diagnostic response fields at lines 268-269. Replace it
  with a two-value helper returning `(authoritative, contract_satisfied)`: keep
  `_is_authoritative(row)` + `contract_satisfied(row.evidence_contract_id, _row_contract_data(row))`,
  drop only the third `trusted` computation (and with it the `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2` gate at
  133-137). Update the call site (~247) to the two-value form; keep emitting `authoritative=`
  and `contract_satisfied=`.
- Remove only the `trusted_for_resolution=` lines from both emit sites (~270 computed value,
  ~307 position-only `False`) and the field from the `CachedAnalysisResult` model.
- Keep the `contract_satisfied` import — still needed for the `authoritative`/`contract_satisfied`
  diagnostics (not because `move_trust_flags` uses it internally). Drop the
  `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2` import (line 18); it was used only by the removed `trusted` computation.

Frontend:
- `src/utils/api.ts`: delete the `@deprecated trusted_for_resolution?: boolean` field (~957).
- Confirm via grep that nothing reads `.trusted_for_resolution` / `.trustedForResolution`
  (already verified zero reads).

Docs/tests:
- SPEC.md: drop the parenthetical "(`trusted_for_resolution` is retained only as a
  deprecated, unread field)" at ~2483 and the "...that replace the old
  `trusted_for_resolution`" phrasing at ~2571 (reword to past tense / removed).
- Migrate assertions in `backend/test_analysis_cache_api.py` (7 refs) and
  `backend/test_analysis_outcome_stability.py` (2 refs) to `position_trusted`/`move_trusted`.

Verify: `pytest backend/test_analysis_cache_api.py backend/test_analysis_outcome_stability.py`;
`tsc -b` + `vitest run` on touched frontend.

---

### g-v2-deprecation.2 — Migrate canonical writer off v2  (BLOCKED by g-6xc3)

`backend/scripts/precompute_openings.py` — stop producing v2; produce both grains:
- `_result_row` (~706): stop hardcoding `RESOLVER_COMPLETE_V2`. Move rows go to
  `analysis_cache` stamped via `select_canonical_move_contract(data)` → `move-complete-v1`.
  **Fail-closed:** a `None` return (row does not satisfy move-complete) is a hard **write
  failure that fails the run manifest** for that position — a canonical producer that cannot
  emit valid move evidence aborts the position; it is NOT silently dropped.
- Add a position write: emit one `position_analysis` row per `normalize_fen(fen_before)`
  through `app.position_analysis_repo.write_position_analysis_row` (position-complete-v1),
  routed through the existing position dominance policy. This replaces "precompute writes
  v2 → backfill projects to storage" with a direct write.
- **Dual-write transaction boundary (finding 3).** `write_position_analysis_row` stages +
  `flush()`es on the *caller* session (caller owns the transaction); `write_analysis_cache_rows`
  *refuses* a caller session that is `in_transaction()` and opens its own isolated
  transaction. They therefore cannot share one open transaction. Required order per batch:
  (1) write **and commit** the `position_analysis` rows on the caller session so it is clean;
  (2) call `write_analysis_cache_rows` for the move batch (its own transaction);
  (3) **post-write verification** re-reads both stores. Treat the two stores as
  non-atomic: a position counts as written only when *both* grains verify, so a partial
  success (one store committed, the other failed) self-heals — the next run re-processes any
  position missing either verified grain. Document this; do not assume atomic dual-write.
- Resume/idempotency (`filter_unstored_positions` ~798-814 and `_verify_stored` ~755-781):
  preserve today's **verified** gate, do not weaken to row presence. Currently a position is
  "done" only when the stored row passes `_identity_verified` + `contract_satisfied(v2)`.
  Migrated gate: done only when **both** (a) the move row is `_identity_verified` +
  `contract_satisfied(MOVE_COMPLETE)`, **and** (b) a `position_analysis` winner for
  `normalize_fen(fen_before)` is identity-verified + `contract_satisfied(POSITION_COMPLETE)`.
  Malformed/partial rows are re-analyzed, never short-circuited to `status: ok`.
- `assert_can_produce_target_contract` default (~673) and run manifest (~1077): target the
  grain contracts, asserting capability to produce both the played-eval (move) and
  best-move+PV+eval (position) evidence.
- `eval_delta` on the move row becomes a documented canonical-run snapshot (move-complete
  does not validate the cross-grain invariant) — used by blunder/SRS/display only.

Hard dependency **g-6xc3** (cross-grain replacement). `decide_analysis_cache_replacement`
(analysis_cache_policy.py Rule 5) must let a canonical `move-complete-v1` row replace a
stored browser-analysis v2 row, but the rule is **asymmetric on authority, not contract
supersession** (move-complete-v1 is deliberately *not* a v2 superset, so supersession alone
points the wrong way). g-6xc3 cannot unblock `.2` until it lands with tests pinning **both**
directions:
  - canonical **authoritative** `move-complete-v1` MAY replace a **non-authoritative**
    browser `resolver-complete-v2` row for the same `(fen_before, move_uci)` key; and
  - an arbitrary / **non-authoritative** `move-complete-v1` row MUST NOT replace an
    **authoritative** `resolver-complete-v2` row.

Verify: `pytest backend/test_precompute_*.py backend/test_analysis_cache_policy.py`; run
precompute against a scratch DB and assert no new v2 rows, populated `position_analysis`,
the verified-both-grains resume gate, and a partial-write rerun that completes the missing grain.

---

### g-v2-deprecation.3 — Re-stamp existing production v2 rows  (BLOCKED by .2)

One-time, idempotent migration script (`backend/scripts/`):
- **Move grain:** re-stamp *authoritative canonical* `analysis_cache` rows declaring v2 →
  `move-complete-v1` in place. Safe by construction: every valid v2 row already satisfies
  move-complete (v2 validation required finite `played_eval` + enum-valid `classification`).
  Non-authoritative/browser v2 rows are left as historical — they never conferred trust
  (`move_trust_flags` gates on `authoritative`), so re-stamping them is unnecessary.
- **Position grain:** verify/complete `position_analysis` backfill coverage for every
  trusted `normalized_fen` the v2 cache-fallback tier currently serves, so storage fully
  replaces that fallback. (Backfill already projects v2 → position-complete-v1; this just
  confirms completeness and records any `position_analysis_conflicts`.)
- Record before/after counts; rerunnable (skips rows already on grain contracts).

Must land *after* .2 — re-stamping before the writer flip would fight precompute's v2
resume filter and churn rows.

Verify: post-run query shows zero authoritative v2 `analysis_cache` rows and full storage
coverage; spot-check that `move_trust_flags`/`position_trust_flags` still return trusted for
the migrated rows via the *grain* branch (not the legacy branch).

---

### g-v2-deprecation.4 — Remove legacy v2 projection semantics  (BLOCKED by .2 + .3) — the deprecation

title: Persist stronger analysis-board evals
description:
## Problem
In-game Stockfish WASM analysis currently uses a weaker depth-17 single-PV search, while the analysis board runs a stronger depth-21 MultiPV search. Analysis-board results are transient, so stronger evidence cannot improve analysis_cache and weaker game evaluations may remain the durable value. More generally, the application needs reusable profile ordering so convenient weaker searches can populate missing keys without preventing later stronger compatible searches from upgrading them.

## Objective
Allow complete, compatible analysis evidence produced on the analysis board or by future stronger searches to be persisted through the shared analysis-cache writer and replace weaker compatible evidence according to explicit profile dominance.

## Scope
- Define exact immutable browser search profiles for in-game depth-17 analysis and analysis-board depth-21 MultiPV analysis, including pinned WASM/build identity, search settings, and analyzer protocol.
- Extend profile comparison to express explicit stronger/weaker relationships without inferring a universal ordering from raw depth.
- Separate trusted replacement eligibility from canonical trusted-hit/legacy-reclamation authority so a stronger browser profile can replace a weaker browser profile without becoming equivalent to native canonical precompute.
- Add an authenticated batch endpoint for writing approved analysis evidence through write_analysis_cache_rows; the backend validates or stamps the allowed producer profile rather than trusting arbitrary client authority claims.
- Convert completed unrestricted analysis-board searches into complete evidence rows and persist them.
- When the played move is not represented by the unrestricted MultiPV result, run the required targeted search so played_eval, best_eval, eval_delta, classification, best move, and best PV come from a coherent profile and satisfy the evidence contract.
- Preserve the canonical depth-24 profile over browser depth-21 evidence.
- Keep incompatible engine builds, networks, search-limit types, protocols, and restricted/hybrid searches unordered and unable to overwrite one another.
- Add diagnostics for accepted/rejected upgrades and tests for profile ordering, endpoint validation, evidence construction, and analysis-board persistence.

## Important Edge Case
AnalysisBoard currently may exclude the cached best move with searchmoves and merge the old cached line into live depth-21 lines for display. That hybrid result must not be stamped as a coherent depth-21 profile or persisted as replacement evidence. Cache-producing analysis must use an unrestricted search to establish the best line and a compatible targeted played-move search when needed.

## Non-Goals
- Do not rewrite historical session_moves when cache evidence improves.
- Do not treat numeric depth alone as a cross-engine quality score.
- Do not allow browser evidence to replace the native canonical depth-24 profile or reclaim unidentified legacy rows merely because its depth is higher than another browser search.
- Do not change live indexed-move source arbitration owned by g-cache-first-resolve.

## Existing Foundation
g-guard-cache-writes is complete and already provides analysis profile metadata, evidence contracts, the deterministic comparator, and the shared transaction-safe writer. This issue extends that foundation; it is not blocked on the completed bead.
design:
# Design: Persist stronger analysis-board evals (g-cache-stronger-evals)

## Goal
Persist complete depth-21 analysis-board evidence through `write_analysis_cache_rows` so it can replace a weaker depth-17 `browser-game-v1` row when the stored key resolves to the same exact `(fen_before, move_uci)` bytes. The new evidence uses the same post-move analyzer protocol as the existing browser-game producer, only at a deeper search depth.

The key match is an implementation assumption that must be made explicit. The FEN half is byte-identical because `SessionMove.fen_before` is stored from the same client value that browser-game cache writes use. The UCI half is a second derivation: browser-game rows used `SessionMoveInput.move_uci` uploaded by the frontend chess.js path, while session analysis rows do not store `move_uci`, so the new endpoint derives it from `SessionMove.fen_before + move_san` via python-chess. For standard legal chess moves these derivations should agree, including castling, promotion suffixes, and en passant. If they do not agree, the failure mode is graceful but noisy: the writer takes the `NEW_KEY` insert path for a near-duplicate `browser-analysis` row and leaves the original `browser-game` row untouched. The design therefore targets exact replacement, not corruption prevention through normalized matching.

The feature is storage-side by design. `browser-analysis-v1` stays `authoritative=False`, so it does not become a trusted `/lookup` hit, does not publish through the frontend trusted-cache path, does not reclaim unidentified legacy rows, and cannot overwrite canonical depth-24 evidence. Read-time trust for stronger browser rows is a separate follow-up (`g-v21l`).

The only intentional read-path effect in this bead is narrow: rows stamped `source="analysis"` rank above `source="game"` in `tree_eval.lookup_move_evals` tier-4 untrusted normalized-transposition fallback. Tier 3 exact untrusted rows still win before source ranking is considered, and position-grain resolution is unaffected because `position_analysis_repo.resolve_trusted_positions` filters to trusted rows before sorting.

## Core Invariants
- Search quality is ordered only by explicit profile compatibility and `dominates` edges, never by raw numeric depth as a generic comparator.
- Dominance completeness is core-field completeness: the optional mate annotation fields (`played_eval_mate`, `best_eval_mate`) never veto an otherwise-dominant replacement. A stronger search that resolves a shallow mate claim into a CP score is better evidence, not less complete evidence.
- Browser-analysis evidence is coherent single-PV post-move analyzer evidence, not display MultiPV output and not a restricted/hybrid `searchmoves` display result.
- Replacement eligibility is split from canonical authority: browser-analysis may replace browser-game, but it is not canonical, not read-trusted, and not allowed to reclaim legacy rows.
- Cache writes are scoped to an authenticated session the user owns, and only exact mainline moves from that session can be submitted. Sessions that are not evidence-eligible (hidden/abandoned drills) are rejected server-side, not just left un-wired client-side.
- The write key must be the exact `SessionMove.fen_before` string plus server-derived `move_uci`; normalized matching is not enough because it can hide halfmove/fullmove-clock drift and create near-duplicate cache rows. Because browser-game used a client-derived UCI, the plan must test the independent SAN->UCI derivation at the known divergence points.
- The backend stamps all profile identity and provenance fields. The client never submits profile, authority, source, or SAN claims.

## Existing Facts And Constraints
- `g-guard-cache-writes` already provides analysis profile metadata, evidence contracts, the deterministic comparator, and the shared transaction-safe writer. This issue extends that foundation.
- `analysis_cache_policy.decide_analysis_cache_replacement` already orders by authority, explicit `dominates` edges, and completeness masks. It must continue to avoid raw-depth ordering.
- `EVIDENCE_FIELDS` in `analysis_cache_policy.py` includes the optional `played_eval_mate` and `best_eval_mate`, and Rule 5's replacement condition requires `incoming.populated_fields >= existing.populated_fields` over ALL of those fields. Without a change, a complete CP-only depth-21 row cannot replace a depth-17 row that stored a raw mate count (`INCOMING_LESS_COMPLETE_KEEP`). This bead fixes that for dominance (Rule 5); see Replacement Policy.
- `Profile.authoritative` currently conflates read trust, legacy reclamation, cross-family replacement eligibility, same-profile merge rights, and `resolve_profile` stamping. This bead separates replacement eligibility from authority.
- `resolve_profile` stamps only active authoritative profiles. Browser-analysis must therefore be stamped by the new endpoint rather than accepted from arbitrary client identity claims.
- Existing `browser-game-v1` rows are non-authoritative and have all identity fields set to `None`, so they identity-verify trivially against the inline `browser-game-v1` profile. That lets an explicit `browser-analysis-v1 -> browser-game-v1` `dominates` edge apply to existing depth-17 rows.
- Identity verification compares stored row columns against the 12 `IDENTITY_FIELDS`: engine name/version/build, full `eval_file_id` and `eval_file_small_id`, search limit, threads, hash, multipv, analyzer protocol, and manifest digest. It does not compare `RESOLUTION_FIELDS`-only runtime filenames (`eval_file`, `eval_file_small`). Those names participate in canonical write-time `resolve_profile`, but browser-analysis rows must verify by the stored full identities.
- `analysis_profiles.stamp_identity(profile_id)` already exists and returns the four manifest-derived fields canonical writers cannot observe at runtime: `eval_file_id`, `eval_file_small_id`, `analyzer_protocol_version`, and `profile_manifest_digest`. Canonical rows get the other identity columns from the observed profile-resolution payload. Browser-analysis has no `resolve_profile` path, so its endpoint needs a full identity stamp that writes every `IDENTITY_FIELDS` column from the registered profile; otherwise `identity_verified` is false and `is_replacement_eligible()` silently fails.
- Canonical `dominates` edges are excluded from the manifest digest.
- Browser-game evidence semantics are the required evidence semantics here: `analysisWorker.ts` runs a root best-move search, then post-played and post-best searches (`position fen ... moves <move>`), and `computeAnalysisResult` derives played/best/delta from those post-move scores. `classifyMoveAdvanced` produces `canonical=true`. Mate scores are stored both as mate-to-CP finite evals and as raw mate counts. Canonical precompute uses the same semantic shape.
- The worker's `message.delta` is mover-relative `bestEval - playedEval` and is not clamped. Independent WASM searches can produce a negative value. `resolver-complete-v2` requires `eval_delta >= 0` and requires it to equal the contract formula computed from white-relative `best_eval` and `played_eval`.
- The worker emits `canonical=true` only from the `classifyMoveAdvanced` branch where both post-move scores exist. Legacy delta-band fallback can emit a non-null classification with `canonical=false`, and the no-bestmove path emits `canonical=false` with null fields. Only `canonical===true` rows are compatible with `browser-analyzer-v1`.
- `analysisWorker.ts` currently hardcodes `go depth 17` in `runSearch` and posts structured fields: `bestMove`, `bestLine`, `bestEval`, `playedEval`, mate fields, `delta`, `classification`, and `canonical`.
- The evidence producer is `analysisWorker.ts`, which configures Hash 128 and MultiPV 1. The display worker `stockfishWorker.ts` uses different settings and is not reused for evidence.
- `stockfish-18-lite-single.wasm` from npm `stockfish@18.0.7` embeds the single lite net `nn-9067e33176e8.nnue`, SHA-256 `9067e33176e8c5edb7aa8db6a3aedd012f84a1f39872e86357c6c2d0993f314d`. The first 12 hex match the filename and the content was verified against the Stockfish network host. This differs from canonical SF18's big net `nn-c288c895ea92.nnue`; browser-analysis is network-incompatible with canonical and must never dominate it. The lite build has no small net.
- The compiled browser engine artifact is `node_modules/stockfish/bin/stockfish-18-lite-single.wasm`, SHA-256 `a8fbc05ec6920b56d7485826dcb02c5ffd2826bcbf751cf973046f237a9096f1`. The JS loader `stockfish-18-lite-single.js` is SHA-256 `2278005057f381491f1c9bb3e44c9f5920b3a00bef9759e33cc6582769a1f1fe`, from npm `stockfish@18.0.7` with integrity `sha512-tJ+bfMAHs4fV7QYiLcHUicx1RzKOQwj8twx/z0iUTauMG+SE3l1rEtRSg+WER81ke3bc5tqKBWEWntUbydkgZg==`.
- In this repo, `engine_version` is the second token of the engine UCI `id name` line captured by canonical precompute. Canonical SF18 stores `"18"`, and the WASM reports `id name Stockfish 18 Lite WASM`, so browser-analysis also pins `engine_version="18"`. The npm package version `18.0.7` is only surrounding provenance.
- Rule 3 in `analysis_cache_policy.py` is the replacement-eligibility gate: a non-replacement-eligible incoming row keeps the existing row there and never reaches Rule 5. `INCOMPATIBLE_KEEP` belongs only to Rule 5, after an incoming row is replacement-eligible or authoritative but does not dominate the existing profile.
- `resolver-complete-v2` requires finite integer `played_eval` and `best_eval`; mate-only evidence fails. It validates `eval_delta` from white-relative evals and the active color. Its `required_fields` do NOT include the mate fields — two v2-satisfying rows can legitimately differ in population only on `played_eval_mate` / `best_eval_mate` (and SAN, which both producers always populate).
- `AnalysisBoard` is rendered by four surfaces: `GameAnalysisPage` (`src/pages/GameAnalysisPage.tsx:175`), `HistoryPage` (`src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx:253`), `BlundersPage` (`src/pages/BlundersPage.tsx:511`) — all saved-game boards backed by `fetchAnalysis(sessionId)` — and `DrillAnalysisPage`, which renders an ephemeral local snapshot ("Drill review — not saved") with no server session analysis.
- `backend/app/api/session.py` already has `_should_run_session_move_evidence(game_session)`: browser-game evidence is skipped for abandoned drills and for ended, unconverted drills (hidden, unrated, unrecoverable). The new endpoint reuses this exact predicate as its server-side eligibility gate.
- `SessionMoveInput.move_uci` is accepted by the browser-game upload path and used by `_upsert_analysis_cache`, but `SessionMove` does not persist a `move_uci` column. Any session-analysis wire field or endpoint membership check must re-derive UCI from stored SAN and FEN.
- `buildMainLineMoveDetails` (`src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx:194`) reconstructs `fenBefore` from `startingFen` / previous `fen_after`, and `projectExactBest` (`src/utils/projectExactBest.ts:57`) does the same and derives played UCI from SAN via `sanToUci`. Both are migrated to the new wire fields (see Exact Keys).
- `API_ROUTE_TEMPLATES` in `src/utils/api.ts:75` maps concrete dynamic paths to exact backend route templates for analytics; unlisted routes fall back to generic `{id}` normalization and fail to join server route labels. The new endpoint must be registered there.
- `chess` / python-chess is already a backend dependency. No `analysis_cache` schema change, alembic migration, or conftest change is needed. `position_analysis` storage is out of scope.

## Evidence Semantics
Depth-21 browser-analysis evidence is produced by reusing `analysisWorker.ts` with a parameterized depth. The worker must run the same protocol as browser-game:

1. Root best-move search at depth 21.
2. Post-played search at depth 21.
3. Post-best search at depth 21.
4. `computeAnalysisResult` on those post-move scores.
5. `classifyMoveAdvanced` classification, accepted only when the returned message has `canonical===true`.

Display `stockfishWorker` / `useStockfishEngine` remains responsible only for analysis-board arrows and visible MultiPV lines. Any display result that used `searchmoves`, excluded a cached best move, or merged a cached line into live depth-21 display data is a hybrid UI artifact and must never be stamped as `browser-analysis-v1` evidence.

Mate handling preserves both representations:
- `played_eval` and `best_eval` store the finite mate-to-CP converted values required by `resolver-complete-v2`.
- `played_eval_mate` and `best_eval_mate` store the raw mate counts.

The analyzer returns values from the mover's perspective. The frontend maps them to the endpoint's white-relative contract:

```ts
const turn = getSideToMove(fen) // 'w' | 'b'
const moverColor = turn === 'w' ? 'white' : 'black'
const whiteBest = playerToWhite(message.bestEval, moverColor)
const whitePlayed = playerToWhite(message.playedEval, moverColor)
const evalDelta = Math.max(
  turn === 'w' ? whiteBest - whitePlayed : whitePlayed - whiteBest,
  0,
)
```

Do not submit `message.delta`. Algebraically the recomputed value is `max(message.delta, 0)`, but recomputing from the exact white-relative integers being submitted makes the row self-consistent with the server contract. Drop the row if either white eval is null. Also drop before upload unless `message.canonical === true`, `bestMove`, `classification`, `bestEval`, `playedEval` are non-null, and `bestLine.length > 1`. A canonical worker result with a one-move PV would fail the v2 `len(line) > 1` check anyway; surfacing it as a rejection is acceptable, but the driver can avoid the upload.

The worker's `canonical` flag is consumed only as a submission gate. It is not stored in `analysis_cache`.

## Profile Registry
In `backend/app/analysis_profiles.py`:

1. Add `replacement_eligible: bool = False` to `Profile`.
2. In manifest loading, set `replacement_eligible = m.get("replacement_eligible", m["authoritative"])` so canonical profiles keep their existing behavior.
3. Keep `browser-game-v1` otherwise unchanged. Because `replacement_eligible` defaults from `authoritative=False`, depth-17 browser-game rows cannot replace depth-21 browser-analysis rows.
4. Add constants `BROWSER_ANALYSIS_PROFILE_ID` and `BROWSER_ANALYZER_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.
5. Add inline profile `browser-analysis-v1`:
   - `engine_name="Stockfish"`
   - `engine_version="18"`
   - `engine_build="a8fbc05ec6920b56d7485826dcb02c5ffd2826bcbf751cf973046f237a9096f1"`
   - `search_limit_type="depth"`
   - `search_limit_value=21`
   - `multipv=1`
   - `threads=1`
   - `hash_mb=128`
   - `eval_file="nn-9067e33176e8.nnue"`
   - `eval_file_small=None`
   - `eval_file_id="nn-9067e33176e8.nnue:9067e33176e8c5edb7aa8db6a3aedd012f84a1f39872e86357c6c2d0993f314d"`
   - `eval_file_small_id=None`
   - `analyzer_protocol_version="browser-analyzer-v1"`
   - `profile_manifest_digest=_manifest_digest(...)` over `_DIGEST_FIELDS`, not `None`
   - `authoritative=False`
   - `replacement_eligible=True`
   - `active=True`
   - `dominates=frozenset({"browser-game-v1"})`
6. Define `browser-analyzer-v1` as the Stockfish 18 lite-single browser analyzer protocol: root best-move plus post-played plus post-best depth-N searches, `computeAnalysisResult`, and `classifyMoveAdvanced` classification (`canonical===true`).
7. Add a profile-side comment recording the JS loader hash, npm package version, and npm integrity as surrounding provenance. `engine_build` itself is the SHA-256 of the compiled WASM artifact, matching canonical executable-hash semantics.
8. Add `stamp_profile_full(profile_id) -> dict` for browser-analysis endpoint stamping. It returns exactly `{field: getattr(profile, field) for field in IDENTITY_FIELDS}`: the full 12-column read-time identity set. It complements, or can internally reuse, the existing narrower `stamp_identity(profile_id)` helper. Do not include `eval_file` or `eval_file_small` in this stamp because they are `RESOLUTION_FIELDS`, not `IDENTITY_FIELDS`, and adding them to digest/identity verification would change the contract.
9. Add `"browser-analysis-v1"` to `dominates` in both canonical manifests so current canonical depth-24 v2 writes dominate browser-analysis.

`_assert_fully_pinned` does not run for non-authoritative profiles, but the browser-analysis profile still pins the full net hash and engine artifact hash for honest provenance and stable identity verification.

## Replacement Policy
In `backend/app/analysis_cache_policy.py`, add `CacheRow.is_replacement_eligible()`:

```py
identity_verified and active and profile.replacement_eligible
```

Keep `is_effectively_authoritative()` for true authority. The comparator changes are:

- Rule 2 same-profile MERGE requires both rows to be replacement-eligible. This is a real behavior change for non-authoritative rows: two `browser-analysis-v1` writes for the same key may now merge when fields agree and the incoming row contributes a missing field or contract successor. `browser-game-v1` remains first-wins because it is not replacement-eligible.
- Rule 3 keeps existing rows when `incoming.is_replacement_eligible()` is false.
- Rule 4 legacy reclamation still requires true authority. This check must be independent of Rule 3 after Rule 3 is loosened; a replacement-eligible but non-authoritative incoming row against legacy or unverified existing evidence returns `KEEP, LEGACY_KEEP_NON_AUTH`.
- Rule 5 uses explicit `dominates` edges and existing completeness/superset checks. No raw-depth comparison is introduced.

The Rule 3 -> Rule 4 edit is the riskiest comparator change. Today a non-authoritative incoming row never reaches Rule 4. After this bead, `browser-analysis-v1` must pass Rule 3 so it can reach Rule 5 dominance against `browser-game-v1`, but it must still be stopped by Rule 4 for legacy/unidentified existing rows. Treat that as a surgical invariant and test it directly.

### Mate fields must not veto dominance
Add `OPTIONAL_MATE_FIELDS = frozenset({"played_eval_mate", "best_eval_mate"})` and change Rule 5's completeness check to compare mate-stripped masks:

```py
superset_ok = (incoming.populated_fields - OPTIONAL_MATE_FIELDS) >= (
    existing.populated_fields - OPTIONAL_MATE_FIELDS
)
```

Rationale: the mate fields are engine annotations of the position, optional under every registered contract (`resolver-complete-v2.required_fields` excludes them), not a measure of evidence richness. A depth-21 search that resolves a shallow depth-17 "mate" claim into a CP-only score is stronger evidence; the old row's raw mate count must not block the replacement with `INCOMING_LESS_COMPLETE_KEEP`. The exclusion is symmetric and applies to every Rule 5 dominance decision, which also hardens the canonical guarantee: a CP-only canonical v2 write replaces a browser-analysis row that had stored mate counts.

Scope of the exclusion:
- Rule 5 only. `contract_ok` (superset-or-successor contract) is still required, so replacement never drops contract-required fields.
- Rule 2 mate-field handling is unchanged even though Rule 2 eligibility is broadened above: mate fields still participate in `_fields_agree` overlap agreement and in the superset-merge "contributes a missing field" test, where they are genuinely additive.
- Rule 4 legacy reclamation keeps the full-field superset deliberately: it protects unidentified evidence of unknown provenance, browser-analysis never reaches Rule 4 as a replacer (it requires true authority), and loosening it is out of scope here.

Expected matrix:
- Browser-analysis incoming vs browser-game existing: Rule 5 dominance -> `REPLACE, DOMINATES_REPLACE`.
- Browser-analysis CP-only incoming vs browser-game existing WITH populated mate fields: still `REPLACE, DOMINATES_REPLACE` (mate exclusion).
- Browser-game incoming vs browser-analysis existing: Rule 3 eligibility gate -> `KEEP`; the gate reason is `NON_AUTHORITATIVE_KEEP` when the existing row is identified. Do not assert `INCOMPATIBLE_KEEP` for this case because it never reaches Rule 5.
- Browser-analysis incoming vs canonical existing: Rule 5 sees canonical is not in browser-analysis `dominates` -> `KEEP, INCOMPATIBLE_KEEP`.
- Browser-analysis incoming vs legacy or unidentified existing: Rule 4 true-authority check -> `KEEP, LEGACY_KEEP_NON_AUTH`.
- Current canonical v2 incoming vs browser-analysis existing: canonical dominates browser-analysis, equal `resolver-complete-v2` contract, mate-stripped superset passes -> `REPLACE, DOMINATES_REPLACE`, including when only the browser row carried mate counts.
- Current canonical v2 CP-only incoming vs browser-game existing WITH populated mate fields: canonical dominance still replaces; the mate-field exclusion is global to Rule 5, not special-cased to browser-analysis.
- Same-profile browser-analysis vs browser-analysis: exact duplicate -> `SAME_PROFILE_IDEMPOTENT`; agreed incoming superset -> `SAME_PROFILE_SUPERSET_MERGE`; overlapping disagreement -> `MERGE_CONFLICT_KEEP`.

The canonical replacement guarantee is intentionally scoped to current canonical `resolver-complete-v2` writes. If canonical move-grain writes migrate to `move-complete-v1`, Rule 5's contract/superset checks would keep an existing browser-analysis v2 row because `move-complete-v1` drops `best_*` fields and is not a successor of `resolver-complete-v2`. That cross-grain replacement gap is tracked separately in `g-6xc3`.

## Source Ranking
In `backend/app/analysis_trust.py`, rank the new source between precomputed and game:

```py
_SOURCE_RANK = {"precomputed": 0, "analysis": 1, "game": 2}
_OTHER_SOURCE_RANK = 3
```

Rows written by this endpoint stamp `source="analysis"`.

This ranking has a narrow functional effect. `tree_eval.lookup_move_evals` uses source rank only in tier 4, the normalized untrusted transposition fallback. Tier 3 exact untrusted rows are checked first, so an exact `source="game"` row still wins over a normalized `source="analysis"` transposition hit. The ranking only makes a normalized analysis row outrank a normalized game row when no exact untrusted row exists for the queried `(fen, move_uci)`.

The `_SOURCE_RANK` helper is also shared by position-grain legacy sorting. The sorting consumers are `resolve_trusted_positions` and `_legacy_position_sort_key` in `backend/app/position_analysis_repo.py`; `source_rank` itself lives in `backend/app/analysis_trust.py`. Browser-analysis is non-authoritative and `resolve_trusted_positions` pre-filters to trusted rows before sorting, so the `"analysis"` tier is inert for position-grain resolution.

The existing relative order of precomputed, game, and other is preserved, and there are no existing `"analysis"` rows today.

Accepted cross-user blast radius: `analysis_cache` is global, so a client-supplied `source="analysis"` row written from one user's owned session can outrank a `source="game"` row in the tier-4 normalized untrusted fallback rendered to OTHER users. This is deliberately accepted: it is the same broad trust tier as existing browser-game rows, which are also client-supplied, unverified, and already globally visible through tiers 3–4; browser-analysis adds stricter legality validation before writing. The new source only reorders two untrusted advisory tiers relative to each other; it cannot cross into trusted `/lookup` hits, drill grading, frontend trusted publication, or position-grain resolution. Documented in SPEC.md.

## Evidence Contract
The endpoint accepts only complete `resolver-complete-v2` evidence. There is no sparse fallback for analysis-board writes and no change required in `backend/app/evidence_contracts.py` beyond using the existing validator from the endpoint.

## Session-Scoped Endpoint
Add `POST /api/session/{session_id}/analysis-evidence` on the session router (`prefix="/api/session"`). It depends on `get_current_user`, loads the session with `_get_session_or_404`, and enforces `_ensure_session_owned_by_user`, mirroring `upsert_session_moves`.

Keep the route thin by moving cache-write preparation into a small unit-testable helper.

Request body: a list capped around 60 rows, each containing:
- `fen`
- `move_uci`
- `best_move_uci`
- `best_line_uci: list[str]`
- `played_eval`
- `played_eval_mate`
- `best_eval`
- `best_eval_mate`
- `eval_delta`
- `classification`

The request intentionally has no SAN, profile, authority, source, or evidence-contract fields. Evals are white-relative and `eval_delta` is recomputed by the client from those white-relative evals.

Endpoint processing:

1. After ownership passes, gate on session evidence eligibility by reusing `_should_run_session_move_evidence(game_session)`. When it returns false (abandoned drills; ended, unconverted drills — hidden, unrated, unrecoverable), short-circuit: return every submitted row with reason `session_not_evidence_eligible` and never touch membership, validation, or the writer. This is the server-side backstop for the client-side rule that drill boards never pass `sessionId`, and it reuses the exact predicate that already gates browser-game evidence in `upsert_session_moves` — normal sessions and visible/converted drills pass, matching the existing browser-game trust shape.
2. Build the exact session membership set once. For each `SessionMove` in the session with non-null `fen_before`, derive `played_uci` from `fen_before` plus `move_san` via python-chess and collect the exact `(fen_before, played_uci)` strings. The FEN half is the same byte string browser-game rows used. The UCI half is intentionally re-derived because `SessionMove` lacks a stored `move_uci`; it is expected to match the browser-game upload's chess.js-derived `SessionMoveInput.move_uci`, but that agreement is an assumption covered by targeted tests.
3. For each submitted row, if `(fen, move_uci)` is not in that exact set, record `not_in_session` and drop it. Do not normalize here; normalization would reintroduce the key-drift bug this design fixes.
4. Dedupe surviving request rows by key in request order. The first occurrence of each `(fen, move_uci)` is primary. Later occurrences get `duplicate_request_key` and are not sent to the writer. Because the writer only receives unique keys, its own duplicate-conflict path should not fire for this endpoint.
5. Validate legality for each primary row with python-chess: FEN parses, `move_uci` is legal, `best_move_uci` is legal, and `best_line_uci` is a legal sequence from `fen`. This is stricter than the browser-game upload path, which does not validate full-PV legality. On failure, record `invalid_legality` or a more specific reason and drop it; this degrades to a missed upgrade, not a bad write.
6. Derive SAN server-side from validated UCI: `move_san = board.san(move)` and `best_move_san = board.san(best_move)`. The stored row uses these server-derived SAN values.
7. Require `resolver-complete-v2` using the existing validator. This revalidates `eval_delta` from white-relative evals as a server-side backstop. On failure, record `contract_unsatisfied` and drop it.
8. For survivors, stamp `analysis_profile_id="browser-analysis-v1"`, all fields from `stamp_profile_full("browser-analysis-v1")`, `source="analysis"`, and `evidence_contract_id="resolver-complete-v2"`. Set `fen_before=fen` and `move_uci=move_uci`, attach server-derived SAN, and encode `best_line_uci`.
9. Call `db.commit()` immediately before `write_analysis_cache_rows(db, survivors)` so the writer receives a clean session with no open transaction. Skip the writer when there are no survivors.
10. Return a list parallel to the request. Every submitted row appears exactly once, in request order, with either its endpoint rejection/duplicate reason or the writer `Reason` for its unique key.

The endpoint emits its own diagnostics for rows rejected before the writer because `write_analysis_cache_rows` only returns reasons for rows it receives. Valid survivors are still written even when other rows in the same request are rejected. The 60-row cap and duplicate-key response are defensive: the planned frontend driver submits one dwelled move at a time in normal operation, so duplicate multi-row batches should not dominate implementation or test effort.

Trust model: the endpoint accepts client-supplied evals and classifications for moves in a session the authenticated user owns; it does not server-verify the evals. This is the same broad trust tier as browser-game evidence, with one stricter validation caveat: browser-analysis also checks FEN/move/PV legality before writing. The blast radius is bounded because browser-analysis is non-authoritative, cannot drive `/lookup` trusted move analysis, drill grading, frontend trusted publication, or position-grain resolution, and can only affect advisory move-grain tier-4 untrusted transposition fallback for exact mainline moves in an owned session. The cross-user reach of that tier-4 effect is explicitly accepted (see Source Ranking). Canonical/authoritative rows remain protected by the replacement policy. If the threat model tightens later, server-side eval verification should be a separate issue.

## Exact Keys On Session Analysis Moves
Add `fen_before: str | None` and `move_uci: str | None` to the `SessionAnalysisMove` backend model and the TypeScript `AnalysisMove` type. They are null only for legacy moves whose `SessionMove.fen_before` is null (or whose SAN fails to parse); such moves are omitted from evidence eligibility.

Populate those fields where session analysis responses are built:
- `fen_before = SessionMove.fen_before`
- `move_uci = chess.Board(fen_before).parse_san(move_san).uci()`

This does not prove the key is byte-identical to the historical browser-game row by construction; it proves the server can produce the intended key from durable session data. Browser-game wrote `SessionMoveInput.move_uci` from the client. Session analysis exposes a python-chess SAN->UCI derivation from the stored SAN. Tests must cover castling, promotion, and en passant to prove the two practical derivations agree for the realistic edge cases.

The analysis board, evidence driver, and move-analysis lookup consume `move.fen_before` and `move.move_uci` directly. They must not reconstruct `fen_before` from the previous move's `fen_after` chain and must not derive played UCI client-side from SAN.

Two existing helpers currently do exactly that reconstruction and must be migrated, not just new code:
- `buildMainLineMoveDetails` (`src/components/AnalysisBoard.tsx:194`) derives `fenBefore` as `index === 0 ? startingFen : moves[index - 1]?.fen_after`. Change it to prefer `move.fen_before` and fall back to the chain reconstruction only when the wire field is null (legacy sessions).
- `projectExactBest` (`src/utils/projectExactBest.ts:57`) derives `fenBefore` the same way and then derives played UCI from SAN via `sanToUci`. Change it to prefer `move.fen_before` and `move.move_uci`, with the same null-only fallback for both.

Fallback policy is split by purpose: display rendering (arrows, exact-best projection) keeps the reconstruction fallback so legacy sessions still render, but the evidence driver has NO fallback — a move with null `fen_before` or `move_uci` is skipped for evidence, never reconstructed. Tests must prove both helpers prefer the wire values when present (see Tests).

This retires the earlier client-reconstruction idea. A normalized membership check could pass while the exact FEN string differed from the browser-game cache key, especially in halfmove/fullmove clocks. The exact wire fields make replacement land on the existing browser-game row when the independently derived UCI matches. If a derivation mismatch is ever found, the outcome is a `NEW_KEY` browser-analysis insert beside the old browser-game row; that is acceptable as a graceful fallback but not the desired upgrade.

## Frontend Evidence Driver
In `analysisWorker.ts`, thread an optional `depth` from `AnalyzeMoveMessage` into `runSearch`. Replace the hardcoded `go depth 17` with `go depth ${depth ?? 17}`. In-game callers continue to omit depth and therefore use 17; the evidence driver passes 21. `runSearch` is the single choke point for the root, post-played, and post-best internal searches, so `analyzeMove` must pass the selected depth into all three calls, not just the root search.

Add a dedicated evidence driver, for example `src/services/analysisEvidence.ts` plus a small hook such as `useAnalysisEvidence`. It owns its own analyzer-worker instance, separate from the display `stockfishWorker`.

The driver runs only when `sessionId` is present. Add `sessionId?: string` to `AnalysisBoardProps`. All three saved-game analysis surfaces pass it, not just `/game`:
- `GameAnalysisPage` (`src/pages/GameAnalysisPage.tsx:175`) passes the page's saved-game session `id`.
- `HistoryPage` (`src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx:253`) passes `selectedGame.session_id`.
- `BlundersPage` (`src/pages/BlundersPage.tsx:511`) passes `selectedAnalysisSessionId` (`selected.source_session_id ?? selected.last_session_id`), the same session whose `fetchAnalysis` result the board is rendering. Blunder source sessions can be converted drills; those are evidence-eligible and pass the server gate.
- `DrillAnalysisPage` renders an ephemeral local snapshot ("Drill review — not saved") and passes no `sessionId`. Ephemeral and drill boards never write evidence client-side; the endpoint's `_should_run_session_move_evidence` gate backstops hidden/abandoned drill sessions server-side regardless.

For the viewed mainline position, use the next mainline move `nextMove = moves[effectiveIndex + 1]` and its exact wire fields:
- `fen = nextMove.fen_before`
- `move = nextMove.move_uci`
- `playerColor = sideToMove(nextMove.fen_before)`
- worker message: `{ fen, move, playerColor, depth: 21 }`

Skip the move entirely when `nextMove.fen_before` or `nextMove.move_uci` is null (legacy session); the driver never reconstructs them.

Map the worker result to the endpoint row:
- Require `canonical===true`.
- Require non-null `bestMove`, `classification`, `bestEval`, `playedEval`, and `bestLine.length > 1`.
- Send `best_move_uci = bestMove` and `best_line_uci = bestLine`; do not send SAN.
- Convert `played_eval`, `best_eval`, `played_eval_mate`, and `best_eval_mate` from mover-relative to white-relative.
- Recompute `eval_delta` from the white-relative evals; do not forward `message.delta`.
- Include `classification`.

Trigger policy in `AnalysisBoard`:
- mainline only (`!isInVariation`)
- a real next move exists (`effectiveIndex` in `[-1 .. moves.length - 2]`)
- dwell debounce on the displayed position
- dedupe by submitted `(fen, move_uci)`
- cancel on navigation using the worker's existing cancel protocol, so interrupted searches never submit
- run one evidence search at a time and schedule it as low-priority/idle work after the dwell delay; if the display engine exposes an "active search" signal, wait for the current display search to settle before starting evidence
- no `!trustedBest` gate

Do not gate on position-grain `trustedBest`. That value comes from trusted normalized-FEN position evidence and is not proof that the exact `(fen, move_uci)` row is canonical or strong. A canonical position best can coexist with a weak browser-game exact move row, and skipping evidence would miss the intended upgrade. Correctness comes from the write policy preserving canonical rows. An optional future optimization can skip work when exact move trust is exposed cheaply (`g-v21l`), but it is not required here.

Performance tradeoff: the evidence driver owns a second Stockfish WASM instance and can run three depth-21 searches for a dwelled move while the display `stockfishWorker` is also searching MultiPV lines. Debounce, dedupe, cancellation, one-at-a-time scheduling, and idle/display-settled gating bound the worst case, but remaining analysis-board jank from competing engines is an accepted UX cost for this storage-only bead. Reducing that cost through exact trusted-row read gating belongs with `g-v21l`.

Add `submitAnalysisEvidence(sessionId, rows)` to the API client. It posts to `/api/session/{sessionId}/analysis-evidence` with auth headers and treats failures as best-effort, like lookup.

Register the route for client analytics: add to `API_ROUTE_TEMPLATES` in `src/utils/api.ts`:

```ts
[new RegExp(`^/api/session/${UUID_SOURCE}/analysis-evidence$`, 'i'), '/api/session/{session_id}/analysis-evidence'],
```

Without this, `normalizeApiPath` degrades the path to `{id}` segments and client `api_request_client.route` events fail to join the server `api_request.route` labels.

## Tests
Backend tests:
- Profile registry: `browser-analysis-v1` exists with the pinned identity values, `engine_version=="18"`, `engine_build` equal to the WASM SHA-256, `eval_file_id` present and content-addressed, digest non-null and stable, `dominates={"browser-game-v1"}`, canonical manifests dominate browser-analysis, and `stamp_profile_full` stamps every `IDENTITY_FIELDS` column. Also assert the relationship with existing `stamp_identity`: it remains the narrower four-field manifest stamp, while `stamp_profile_full` omits `RESOLUTION_FIELDS`-only `eval_file`/`eval_file_small`.
- Replacement policy: browser-analysis replaces browser-game with `DOMINATES_REPLACE`; browser-game cannot replace browser-analysis and is stopped at the Rule 3 eligibility gate; browser-analysis cannot replace canonical and returns `KEEP, INCOMPATIBLE_KEEP`; browser-analysis cannot reclaim legacy/unidentified rows and returns `KEEP, LEGACY_KEEP_NON_AUTH`; current canonical v2 replaces browser-analysis; a test or explicit doc assertion captures that future canonical `move-complete-v1` would not replace browser-analysis v2 under current superset checks (`g-6xc3` gap); browser-analysis same-profile idempotent, superset-merge, and `MERGE_CONFLICT_KEEP` cases are covered; no raw-depth comparator is used.

- Source ranking: `source_rank("analysis")==1`, between precomputed and game, with existing precomputed/game/other order preserved; normalized untrusted `analysis` outranks normalized `game` in `tree_eval` tier 4; an exact `game` row still wins via tier 3 when present; browser-analysis is filtered out before position-grain sorting, so source rank is inert for `position_analysis_repo.resolve_trusted_positions` / `_legacy_position_sort_key`.
- Endpoint authorization and membership: 404 for missing session, 403 for non-owner, `not_in_session` for any exact `(fen_before, move_uci)` not in the owned session mainline, legacy null-`fen_before` rows are not evidence-eligible.

The gate is asserted to be the same predicate as `upsert_session_moves` (call `_should_run_session_move_evidence`, not a re-implementation).

Add a defensive mismatch test where an existing browser-game row has a divergent UCI for the same real move: the analysis write inserts `NEW_KEY` and does not corrupt or replace the old row.

The illegal-PV case documents that this endpoint is stricter than browser-game and may drop otherwise-uploaded browser-game evidence as a missed upgrade.

Keep duplicate/cap tests light because normal frontend operation submits single-row dwelled moves.

Include targeted SAN->UCI fixtures for castling (`e1g1`/`e8g8` as applicable), promotion with piece suffix (`e7e8q`), and en passant (`e5d6`-style capture) to prove python-chess derivation agrees with the browser-stored UCI convention.

Frontend tests:

## Documentation
Update `SPEC.md` because this changes durable cache semantics. Document:
- Browser profile ordering: `browser-game-v1 < browser-analysis-v1 < canonical-24`.
- `authoritative` vs `replacement_eligible`.
- `browser-analyzer-v1` as the analysisWorker `classifyMoveAdvanced` post-move protocol at depth 21, using the same method as browser-game but deeper.
- The exact-key model: `SessionAnalysisMove` carries `fen_before` and `move_uci`, and evidence writes use those values to match browser-game cache keys; display helpers (`buildMainLineMoveDetails`, `projectExactBest`) prefer the wire fields with a legacy-only reconstruction fallback, and the evidence driver never falls back.
- White-relative eval storage, mate-to-CP plus raw mate fields, and delta recomputation/clamping from white evals.
- Dominance completeness excludes the optional mate annotation fields: a dominant CP-only row replaces a weaker row that stored raw mate counts; mate fields still participate in same-profile merge agreement.
- Browser network identity `nn-9067e33176e8.nnue` with full hash, distinct from canonical's net.
- `engine_build` pinned to the `stockfish-18-lite-single.wasm` SHA-256; JS loader hash, npm package version, and package integrity as surrounding provenance.
- `engine_version="18"` as the UCI id-name token; npm `18.0.7` is provenance only.
- Canonical-to-browser replacement is guaranteed for current canonical `resolver-complete-v2` writes; the future `move-complete-v1` cross-grain gap is deferred to `g-6xc3`.
- Browser-analysis rows are not read-trusted on `/lookup` or frontend trusted publication paths; read-time trust is `g-v21l`.
- Source ranking `precomputed < analysis < game < other` and its effect limited to move-grain tier-4 normalized untrusted fallback with no exact untrusted row; position-grain resolution is unaffected.
- The exact-key caveat: FEN bytes come from durable `SessionMove.fen_before`, while UCI bytes are server-derived from SAN because `SessionMove` has no `move_uci`; derivation mismatches degrade to a near-duplicate `NEW_KEY` insert rather than corruption.
- The accepted cross-user blast radius: client-supplied `source="analysis"` rows from one user's owned session can outrank `source="game"` rows in other users' tier-4 untrusted fallback — same broad trust tier as existing browser-game rows, with stricter full-PV legality validation, never crossing into trusted paths.
- SAN is server-derived from UCI and never trusted from the client.
- The endpoint is session-scoped, owner-only, guarded by exact mainline membership, gated on `_should_run_session_move_evidence` (hidden/abandoned drills rejected with `session_not_evidence_eligible`), and only runs from boards with a `sessionId`.
- Evidence-writing surfaces: `GameAnalysisPage`, `HistoryPage`, and `BlundersPage` saved-game boards; `DrillAnalysisPage` and ephemeral boards never write.
- The response is per submitted row and includes `duplicate_request_key` handling.
- Evidence is not gated on position-grain `trustedBest`; write policy protects canonical rows.
- Evidence uses a second Stockfish WASM worker and may compete with display analysis; debounce/dedupe/cancel/idle scheduling bound the cost, and deeper read-time skip logic is deferred to `g-v21l`.
- The trust model: owned-session client evals are accepted unverified, matching browser-game, with blast radius limited to non-authoritative advisory fallback.

## Out Of Scope
- Do not rewrite historical `session_moves` when cache evidence improves.
- Do not change live indexed-move source arbitration owned by `g-cache-first-resolve`.
- Do not touch `position_analysis` storage.
- Do not treat numeric depth as a cross-engine quality score.
- Do not let browser evidence replace canonical depth-24 evidence or reclaim unidentified legacy rows.
- Do not add read-time trust or worker-usage reduction for browser-analysis rows; that is `g-v21l`.
- Do not solve canonical `move-complete-v1` replacing browser-analysis v2 rows here; that is `g-6xc3`.
- Do not add server-side engine re-verification of browser-analysis evals in this bead.
- Do not loosen Rule 4 legacy-reclamation completeness (mate-field exclusion is Rule 5 only).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A complete approved depth-21 analysis-board profile replaces a complete depth-17 browser-game row for the same (fen_before, move_uci).
2. Depth-17 browser evidence cannot replace depth-21 analysis-board evidence.
3. Neither browser profile replaces an active canonical depth-24 row.
4. Incompatible or unidentified profiles remain unordered and cannot overwrite trusted evidence.
5. Numeric depth is never used as a generic cross-profile comparator; ordering is explicit and deterministic.
6. Browser profile metadata is validated or stamped by the backend; clients cannot claim arbitrary canonical or authoritative identities; and evidence writes are scoped to a game session the authenticated user owns, accepting only moves played in that session's mainline.
7. Only coherent completed analysis is persisted; restricted searchmoves plus a merged cached line is rejected as cache-producing evidence.
8. Persisted rows satisfy the complete evidence contract, including best move/PV, played and best evaluations, eval_delta, and classification.
9. Every persisted played move is evaluated by the single-PV post-move analyzer protocol (root best-move + post-played + post-best searches at depth 21, the same method as browser-game but deeper), never from a display MultiPV snapshot; played_eval, best_eval, eval_delta, and classification come from one coherent profile.
10. All writes route through write_analysis_cache_rows and expose accepted/rejected reason diagnostics.
11. Tests cover upgrade/downgrade/canonical/incompatible ordering, endpoint validation (including session ownership and mainline-membership rejection), score perspective and mate handling, single-PV post-move played evaluation, interrupted searches, and duplicate submissions.
12. SPEC.md documents browser profile ordering and analysis-board cache persistence.
